It is the work of architect Luis Xavier (1965-67) and based on the earlier design plans of his father Raul Xavier.  I enjoy viewing this statue of the Patron Saint Vincente who is standing in a decorative robe and holding a caravel with two ravens which is the Coat of Arms of the city of Lisbon. It is a neat statue to see while visiting this viewpoint. || Saint Vicente is the true patron saint of Lisbon. The statue holds the caravel with two crows, symbol of the city of Lisbon. According to legend, the saint's dead body was brought back home and the 2 crows accompanied it. || Some great views over the old town near the statue. || Great view, sit back have a beer! Cool breezes. || One of many sculptures in the city. St Vincent is the patron saint of Lisbon. The sculpture of the saint is holding a boat with 2 common ravens on top. It is a symbol of the city.  Nearby is a viewpoint terrace from which you can overlook the city.  The area is a tourist hotspot.  Follow here and on IG for more travel and food and drink tips, ideas and reviews @one.more.step.along.the.world || Nice statue in the middle of a plaza with great view over Lisbon east part and the river. || Great views of the city and river! || Best viewpoint of Alfama || so picturesque and accommodates many people not to feel too crowded. There’s a restroom but it closes at 1700. || A space with a very beautiful and romantic vibe.I recommend dining here at night || Nice square. More expensive for food/drinks as near the port || Very nice art.lovely place.

place_name: Mosteiro de São Vicente de Fora
reviews_content: For €8 this has to be great value for money. We were lucky to see a tile exhibition within the building too. The church is a spectacular surprise after wandering around the cloisters, and the 360 degree view from the roof is amazing. || Thank you for your wonderful feedback! We are glad to hear that you enjoyed the experience. The atmosphere of the Monastery is truly unique. To fully appreciate it, one must step inside and take the time to relax and absorb its beauty. We hope to welcome you back soon to explore even more! || Amazing historical place to visit there are 2 parts of this building, the church and the museum. The ticket cost 8€ for adult of 3€ if you’re student. Full of historical learning and amazing rooftop for 360 degree city view. || Thank you so much for your visit and kind words! We’re delighted to know you enjoyed exploring both the church and the museum, as well as the rooftop with its panoramic views over Lisbon. We hope to welcome you again soon! || Was on a cruise and our ship docked at Lisbon seaport. Decided to do the 2.5 hours private Tuk-Tuk ride to explore the various monuments and landmarks, and we stopped briefly at this place. Beautiful coloured tiled walls and high ceilings.. lit  a candle at 50 cents which was a nice touch. Went to the flower garden nearby. Very beautiful 😍 🤩 👌🏾 || Thank you so much for sharing your experience! We're so glad to hear you enjoyed the Tuk-Tuk ride and had a chance to visit our space. || Fantastic. Gorgeous views from the top, lovely collections, and the tile work is incredible. The craftsmanship is just wow. || Thank you so much for this wonderful review! We’re thrilled that you enjoyed the gorgeous views from the top and took time to appreciate the collections and the incredible tile work. We hope to welcome you back again soon! || Amazing place—I loved my experience here! It’s hard to believe that, given how popular Lisbon is a tourist destination, it would still have “hidden gems,” but this is very much that. Some great things about it:  TONS of Portuguese azulejos ✅  Fascinating architectural detail ✅  Spacious, with tons to explore ✅  Friendly staff ✅  Lots of history + interesting artifacts ✅  Beautiful views over the city ✅  Reasonably priced ✅  No crowds, so you can actually enjoy at your own pace! ✅  Highly recommended! || Dear Tomas, First of all we would like to thank you for your visit to the Monastery and then for the kind comment. We are very happy to know that you had a pleasant experience in our spaces and we thank you very much for sharing such a complete review with the various aspects that led you to gratify this experience. || A large collection of porcelain murals, religious artifacts, paintings and church items. Hold onto your ticket until you leave because you will need it to use the bathroom and to exit. || Thank you for your kind words and for highlighting the richness of our collection. We look forward to welcoming you again soon! || This was a wonderful surprise. I had never visited this Monastery before and loved every bit. The monastery itself is very beautiful, inside and out, and every wall, every staircase, every room is covered in  beautiful tiles. I don't think I have ever seen so many tiles on a building before. There is even an exhibition of La Fontaine's fables painted in tiles on the upper level. The Bragança Pantheon is unique and deserves a visit! There is also the cardinals pantheon inside. The view from the upper level is gorgeous over the hills of Lisbon. The gentleman at the entrance was super nice and explained us a lot before we entered. || Thank you very much for your visit and kind comment about the Monastery. Wow! Fantastic description of the monastery with all essential details and information. Thank you very much for sharing your positive experience and promotion to our monastery. About the tiles there are more than 100.000 tiles in the whole building, which corresponds to more or less 222 panels. It is the second monument in the world with the most baroque tiles in their original place. Muito obrigado! || We found this place by accident, and I daresay I enjoyed it  more than St. Jeronimo's - no lines, not crowded and so much more to see . || Thank you for your kind words! We're glad you enjoyed your visit and the peaceful atmosphere. We hope to welcome you back soon! || Worth every Euro entry fee! The monastery is beautiful inside and out with a large collection of antiques. The view from the roof is stunning and you can spend hours there without getting bored. || That's wonderful! Thank you so much for the feedback. Until next time! || Very underrated. We visited on a Saturday and it was nearly empty… it would seem that the tourists all skip it for some reason. Just go and you’ll see that it’s a great place to get away from the crowds all swarming the “influencer spots” || Thank you very much for your visit and your kind words about the Monastery. We are delighted that you chose to explore it—it's still one of Lisbon's hidden gems, and we're so glad you discovered it. We look forward to welcoming you again!

place_name: Church of St. Vincent de Fora
reviews_content: A beautiful and tranquil church. Few visitors on a weekday in December. Time and space to appreciate wonderful monastic chanting playing in the background. The multi-lingual signs direct you towards the amazing collection of blue and white tiles (azulejo) which decorate the cloisters, walls, and stairs. These are simply stunning. Many depict rural scenes and the pursuits of the gentry, while others capture funny parables and fables. The latter are very well presented for visitors, with written summaries of each one in Portuguese and English. In total there are over 200 tiled panels so some you might want to study carefully and others you might spend less time on, depending on your schedule. Another highlight for us is the 360 degree panoramic view from the roof, well worth the climb. A fascinating good-value  visit. Seems to be overlooked by many tourists. || Thank you so much for this wonderful and thoughtful review! We’re truly delighted to hear that you enjoyed the calm atmosphere of the church and had the time and space to fully appreciate the monastic chanting and the remarkable azulejo collection.  It’s especially rewarding to know that the multilingual interpretation and the presentation of the tile panels helped bring the stories to life for you. With more than 200 panels, it’s lovely to hear you took the time to explore them at your own pace.  We’re also very glad you enjoyed the panoramic rooftop view, it really is a special perspective over Lisbon and a highlight for many of our visitors.  Thank you for highlighting the tranquility and value of the visit, and for helping bring attention to a place that often remains a hidden gem. We hope to welcome you back again in the future! || A beautiful and peaceful church with impressive architecture and stunning tile work. It’s less crowded than other Lisbon landmarks, which makes it a nice spot to explore in a calm atmosphere. The cloisters and the rooftop view are definitely worth seeing || Thank you so much for your kind words and thoughtful review! We're truly happy to hear that you enjoyed the peaceful atmosphere and took the time to appreciate the architecture and tile work. The cloisters and rooftop views are indeed special, and we're glad they made an impression on you. We always strive to offer a calm and meaningful experience for our visitors—thank you for being part of it! || Such an underrated gem! My friends and I spent nearly two hours exploring the beautiful rooms, the church, cloisters, and vast collection of religious artifacts with great explanations. The rooftop views are stunning, and best of all, it’s not crowded. || Thank you so much for your comment! We're happy to hear that you enjoyed the visit, the explanations, and the views from the terrace. We hope to welcome you back soon! || Not to be missed, really enjoyed our visit here. Think we got lucky as we arrived quite later but it was open because it was Sunday. Nice place to walk around with loads of interesting large blue and white tiles. Great views at the top too. || Thank you so much for your visit and kind words! We are very happy to know that you enjoyed the monastery, the tiles, and the views. || This is amazing place! Not crowded, cheap entrance tickets. I highly recommend you to visit it. Very underrated, unfortunately. || Thank you so much for your kind review! We’re really happy to hear that you enjoyed the place and appreciated the peaceful atmosphere and affordable tickets. Your recommendation truly means a lot to us. We agree, it’s a hidden gem, and we’re glad you discovered it! || Marvellous.  The complex as a whole is one of the best religious buildings we have visited in Lisbon. The museum is beautifully laid out with some fantastic items. The two cloisters are an oasis of serenity  - plain simple white but with a series of beautiful tiled scenes/panels (65 in total). The actual church is massive with a series of beautifully decorated side chapels. The highlight has to be the views over Lisbon from the roof. We spent well over a hour just wondering around enjoying its serenity and elegant beauty. || Thank you so much for your visit and for your kind words! We are delighted to know that you enjoyed exploring the Monastery of São Vicente de Fora and that you appreciated the serenity of the cloisters, the richness of the museum, and the beauty of the church—especially the view over Lisbon. Comments like yours are a great motivation for us to continue preserving this very special place. We hope to welcome you back soon! || Beautiful and peaceful spot in Alfama. The church is stunning inside and the cloisters with the blue azulejos are incredible. The rooftop view over Lisbon is worth the visit alone.  Quiet, historical, and full of charm. One of Lisbon’s hidden gems. || Thank you so much for your feedback!  We are very pleased to know that you enjoyed the church, the cloisters with their tiles, and the view from the terrace.  It's always a pleasure to welcome those who appreciate the history and tranquility of this special place.  We hope you will visit us again! || What a treasure in the middle of Lisbon.  Not far from the port. Definitely worth the time. Climb the bell tower if you can for amazing views of Lisbon. || Thank you so much for your comment!  We're glad to hear you enjoyed your visit and the view from the terrace. || I absolutely love the Mannerist complex – the simplicity and symmetry are just perfect! It’s also a very quiet spot, so you can really take your time and enjoy every detail. The exhibition offers a thorough look at the history from the medieval period, though most of it is in Portuguese. The architectural elements are definitely worth the visit, especially the cloisters and the rooftop terrace, which offer stunning views of Lisbon. The admission fee for adults is €8, and you get a discount with the Lisboa Card! || Thank you very much for your visit and kind comment about the Monastery. Wow! Fantastic description of the monastery with all essential details and information. Thank you very much for sharing your positive experience and promotion to our monastery. || An absolutely stunning church! The Church of St. Vincent de Fora is a hidden gem in Lisbon, offering breathtaking architecture and rich history. The interior is beautifully adorned, with intricate details and a peaceful atmosphere. The view from the rooftop is also incredible, providing a unique perspective of the city. The staff were welcoming and informative, making the visit even more enjoyable. A must-see for anyone in Lisbon – truly a remarkable experience! || Thank you very much for your visit and kind comment about the monastery. We are very glad to know that you enjoyed your time here and we are grateful for the magnificent description of your very positive experience. It is very rewarding for us that you not only enjoyed the monument itself which is stunning, but also appreciated the assistance provided by our staff. Hope to see you again in the future!

A beautiful park where you can spend a few hours. It has a path that goes around it and which I recommend to walk. Beautiful trees and ponds ideal for a pause after a busy day. There's a café which is usually busy and a table is hard to find. On Sundays there's a small marketplace and so you can encounter locals mixed up with tourists. Just across the street you'll find the admirable Basílica da Estrela which is worth the visit. || I met some friends at Jardim da Estrela and it was a very nice experience. The park has lots of trees and open space, so it felt calm and relaxing. We enjoyed walking and sitting by the small lake together. || This is a gorgeous park — perfect for people-watching or for families with kids who just want to escape the hustle and bustle of Lisbon. It’s a peaceful spot to unwind and enjoy a slower pace in the middle of the city, and it even has restrooms (although I wouldn't call them clean but they were free), which is always a plus when exploring! || This place is heaven! One of the most beautiful parks I've seen by far. It's full of nature and also some animals, mostly birds. The place is perfect for a weekend picnic, a chilly eventing, yoga, hangouts and more. Thank you Lisbon for this amazing green gem! || Stunning park in the heart of Lisbon. Absolutely stunning. Full of beautiful plants and flowers, ponds and statues. Benches everywhere and the wonderful Banana Cafe inside which sells burgers and sandwiches, drinks and other refreshments where you can dine alfresco || 🌿 A Peaceful Oasis in the Middle of Lisbon ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5) We stumbled upon Jardim da Estrela on a warm afternoon, and it turned out to be one of the most peaceful and refreshing places we visited in Lisbon. It’s more than just a public park — it feels like a little urban sanctuary. The garden is beautifully maintained, filled with exotic plants, huge trees offering generous shade, and winding paths that invite you to slow down. What really stood out for me was the birdsong — there were so many birds, and their constant, melodic chirping made the whole place feel like a live sound bath. It’s incredibly soothing. If you have the time, don’t just walk through. Find a quiet corner, sit down, breathe, and maybe even meditate. This place is perfect for that. It’s not just visually calming, it actually sounds calming too. There are also benches, fountains, a lovely gazebo, and a charming little café nearby if you want to sit and sip something while watching the world go by. Families, joggers, solo readers, and locals chatting on benches all seem to coexist naturally here. It has a very authentic Lisbon energy — not overly touristy, just real life unfolding in a gorgeous setting.  Quick Ratings: Atmosphere: 10/10 Birdsong & Nature Vibe: 10/10 Relaxation Potential: 11/10 Accessibility: 10/10 Instagram View: 8.5/10 Highly recommend making time for it — especially if you’re feeling overstimulated by the city. It’s the kind of place that quietly resets your mood.  If this helped, I’d love a 👍 — and don’t forget to breathe deeply when you visit. 🌿✨ || I recently spent a peaceful afternoon at Jardim da Estrela in Lisbon, and it quickly became one of my favorite spots in the city. Located directly across from the grand Basílica da Estrela, this romantic-style park was inaugurated in 1852 and offers a refreshing blend of history, nature, and community life. The park spans 4.6 hectares and features winding paths shaded by exotic trees like jacarandas and ginkgoes, as well as beautifully maintained flower beds and small lakes with ducks and turtles. One of the standout features is the wrought-iron bandstand, originally built in 1884 and relocated here in 1936, which adds a touch of old-world charm. Families and locals gather here, especially on weekends, to enjoy the playgrounds, picnic areas, and the café with outdoor seating that serves light meals and drinks. The park is free to enter and open daily from 7 am to midnight, making it an accessible and welcoming space for everyone. Whether you're looking to relax, take a leisurely stroll, or immerse yourself in a bit of Lisbon's history, Jardim da Estrela offers a serene and delightful escape from the city's hustle and bustle. || I have a 5 year old and a 2 year old. This is hands down my favorite park to take them to in Lisbon. Great playground. Lots of space to run. A cute little library with little tables the kids can draw and color at. Birds walking about. Cafes for a quick coffee or juice. Plus it’s super safe because it’s all gated. || Definitely one of the most loveliest gardens in Lisbon, if you come here for a few days, I would strongly recommend to see this place. Very cool for pet owners and children hence the park has playgrounds and a huge space  for dogs to enjoy. Also, it’s a very good place just to meet and chill or enjoy your day in serenity. || A beautiful park with ancient trees. Ideal for sitting in peace. || The garden is truly magnificent. For the past several months, we have spent an hour here every afternoon, strolling and unwinding. The vibrant colors of the flowers, the soothing rustle of the leaves, and the gentle warmth of the sun create an atmosphere of pure serenity. || Beautiful park with many interesting plants in it. Great for spending a few calm moments during sightseeing or for lunch break || Beautiful park with a wide variety of trees and different areas for either working out or doing a picnic, reading and relaxing. Is rather small for a jog yet early mornings or later in the evenings is really peaceful and perfect for a walk. || Probably the best part of Lisbon. Quiet, peaceful, and with a lovely café that has plenty of tables where you can sit, have a bite, and rest. Thankfully, the usual loud and disrespectful tourists haven’t discovered this spot yet (and I hope my review won’t attract them, lol). Surrounded by lots of greenery, it’s such a beautiful, relaxing park — right across from the basilica. Love it! || Im so happy I found this place! Beautiful trees, very dog and children friendly. Banana cafe serves great coffee and pastel da nata ❤️ || I feel so blessed and lucky to be a short walk from this beautiful oasis. The care and thoughtfulness the Portuguese put into public spaces with a care for community is beautiful to experience. || 2€ Banana Bread under quiet Palmtrees in the middle of a bustling Metropolis, what more can one wish for? Fantastic, quiet place to have a beer, run or just have a chat near the pond. Especially beautiful at night! || Lovely park, plenty of benches dotted around to sit and enjoy the greenery and tranquility.  2 cafes with good selection of food and drinks. || I must admit that it is a very very nice park. I liked a tree in particular, they have a liberty-style gazebo, toilets and a couple of cafè, a small artificial lake with ducks, an exhibition building and statues scattered here and there. It is right in front of Estrela cathedral. || A beautiful and well maintained garden. This was built in 1852 as first public park of Lisbon. It has many old and beautiful trees. Worth spending some time and walking when you are free.

Perfect place to bring children and pets! The view is stunning, you can both enjoy the Pantheon and the river at the same time. Given that there’s a dog park within, lots of people bring their dogs every day. There’s also a kiosk if you would like to have something. || Very nice park with great views of the water. There is a playground and dog park within and it is near the flea market which makes for a nice escape from the busy shopping stalls! || Nice little park with the a great view of the bay  Park has a dog park inside along with various exercise equipment to use. The park also has a great view to enjoy the mini cafe restaurant inside it. || Stumbled upon this park after wandering from Feira da Ladra. It has a nice hut stand that serves drinks and small bites. Not much to the park, a lil play area for kids and trees and benches. Nothing to go out of your way for. || Beautiful garden with amazing view of the river. There’s also a great place there to have a coffee or a beer. Great for kids and dogs as well. || Beautiful urban park in the Alfama. There is also a little dog park located inside. A great place to take a break, grab a coffee, and enjoy the view. || Very nice park with great views. Not crowded and with plenty places to sit and relax. || Nice garden.. hoping to see the jacaranda trees... No flowering yet in end of March. || Beautiful park . Great to be with family and friends and walk the dog || Great place to exercise in the morning and the coffee shop open at 10

More educational than entertaining. An old monastery and church repurposed as a museum. The museum has an impressive exposition on history of organized Christianity in Portugal. The architecture is impressive and the tile panels are exquisite. The church towers are worth visiting too as the views from there are even better than those from the National Pantheon (and it’s easier to take pictures from there). The entry fee is reasonable. || This building was  18th century Igreja (church) very gothic and recorded so many historical events. The building is very pretty and my favorite part is the 360 degree point of view at the roof top. Even though some of the part a bit scary and feels draining to climb up. || Went here after a recommendation from one of our friend, and it was honestly just amazing. There's a bit of culture, much to see and it's quite impressive. And on top of that you end the trip with a spectacular view. All that for 5€ per adult. Would recommend. || Fantastic roof top views of Lisbon, beautiful courtyard, friendly staff and peaceful cloisters decorated with stunning blue tiles. || Coffee shop people were very inconsiderate || Guy behind the counter is rude and arrogant we used the toilets and he gave very bad attitude  Court yard is nice  He obviously has the same problem over and over but np need to be rude in a church || Built in 1147, this monastery suffered the ravages of the 1755 earthquake. It was rebuilt. Walking through its doors, you'll feel like you've stepped back in time. We simply loved this visit.  The church is simply incredible, as is the double cloister. As you wander through some of the rooms, you'll discover superb azulejo frescoes. As a bonus, the tour gives you access to the monastery's rooftops, which offer a beautiful 360-degree view of the city.  Finally, the second floor of the building is dedicated to the fables of Jean de la Fontaine. A great way to (re)discover them, especially with children. Allow about three hours for the tour at your own pace.  Admission: 8 euros per adult (6 euros with the Lisboa Card) and 4 euros for those under 25. || A very worthwhile visit to the monastery and its church. The highlight is the panoramic view from the church rooftops. Also not to be missed is the Royal Pantheon of Bragança. The azulejos (tiles) are also worth seeing, especially the series depicting La Fontaine's fables. Allow at least two hours for a complete visit. || I absolutely recommend purchasing a ticket to visit the entire church and the monastery. There's no waiting (unlike the Jeronimos Monastery), and the spaces you visit are diverse and rewarding. The tour also includes a climb to the top of the monastery (beautiful views), a couple of exhibitions, the majolica cloister, and the cisterns. || Less publicized than other museums and historical/religious buildings in the city, I think it's the best value for money. You'll spend more than an hour, even two if you like, visiting every room and floor of this museum. Everything is described in detail, even in English, so you'll have no problem learning all the information and curiosities.  It's easily accessible by taking the historic tram 28, but if climbing a lot isn't a problem for you, given its proximity to the city center (the Rua Augusta Arch, for example), it won't take you long to reach your destination on foot. || A little-known gem! You can see the monastery from the viewpoint at the foot of the mountain, and it's a short walk up to find the museum entrance. At first glance, it might seem like there's not much to see, but almost all the spaces are open, and the courtyard and church are magnificent. You can even go to the second-floor altar for a panoramic view of the church – the scenery is absolutely stunning, offering a better view of Lisbon than from the viewpoint below. The interior's floral tile decorations are very characteristic of Lisbon and definitely worth photographing.  The historical section is explained in detail, and the layout is well-planned, making it a commendable museum.  The rooftop is a bit hidden. After following the path and seeing most of the rooms, follow the signs up the stairs at the last entrance. You'll first reach a platform, and then a small door on the right leads to the bell tower. It's not difficult to get there.  Many people give up here, but you need to go up the stairs through the small door to reach the main platform. || We found it by chance and were amazed by how much there is to see and how many wonderful religious and non-religious artifacts of inestimable value. In gold and silver. Stunning workmanship. Remains of papal robes and slippers, among many other things. Stunning paintings and frescoes. So much history and art. A tour that lasted at least an hour, thoroughly enjoyed, for a very fair price: 5 euros per person. Truly worth a visit. Elisabetta || Fantastic visit! I can confirm that the tour will take between 2 and 3 hours! Several rooms to discover, as well as the panoramic view, which is a beautiful way to end the visit 🌟 || Lovers of religious art and azulejos will love this place. For everyone else, the monastery's bell tower offers a fantastic view of Lisbon. At €5 admission, it's not too expensive, pleasantly cool on hot days, and located right next to the E28 tram stop. || It's worth a visit. The prices are reasonable (under 25 it's €4, over 25 it's €8, and kids are free). Almost everything is available with English information, and there's a beautiful 360-degree view from the roof. || Worth the detour for the diversity of what there is to see and the superb view of Lisbon. Perfect signage! Pretty garden with bougainvillea. All this a little away from the most visited sites || Excellent guided tour and excellent work by the guide and the choir. I recommend it! Prior booking is required. || Discovered by chance during our walks in Lisbon. A magical place with its flowers in the inner courtyard. || A chance visit that was absolutely worth it. As always, the kindness of the people who greet you is unparalleled.

A small, quiet  and hidden little perch that provides great views of the city. There are a few benches and some trees to take in the city. Feels safe and clean here. A great place to see the sunrise over Lisbon if you're up early! || Worth to walk all the way up with stairs or options to have the cable car. Church is beautiful inside too. || Decent night view after a rainy day, absolutely empty here when we reached around 7pm on a Monday night - definitely one of those quiet terrace (also has 3 chairs), for folks to chill and enjoy the scenery 👍🏻 || Very cosy place. It is a bar with terrace near and you can have a drink above Lisbon. The church is very old wit a lot of mosaics. || Nice spot to relax and enjoy an amazing view! || There are a handful of very nice viewpoints in the Alfama neighbourhood providing really good views of the neighbourhood's many orange/rust coloured rooftops down below.  One such place that seems to be off the beaten path is the elevated platform in front of Igreja de Santo Estevao. Here you find just a handful of people enjoying the views, which is rather nice compared to the massive crowds at more popular spots like Miradouro de Santa Lucia and Miradouro das Portas do Sol. || Great view, not too busy, quite messy and dirty on weekend mornings || Great views. This is one of those places that is a great “cooling off” resting point when traveling around town. Bring a drink (or you can buy one nearby) and have a seat. Lots of seats available actually. If you have a dog with you, this is also a good spot for them to relax as well. || This belvedere is a hidden gem in Lisbon! This lesser-known viewpoint offers stunning, panoramic views of the city and the Tagus River. It's a peaceful spot, away from the usual tourist crowds, making it perfect for a relaxing break.

One of the best view points over the magnificent city of Lisbon. Enter through the gates of the playground and walk to the end. You will have a lot of place to sit and just enjoy the view.  Magnificent place to just turn off your mind and live in the moment, because it's not as crowded as other miradouros. || Nice visit and beautiful grounds. Good views, but can not see the cruise ships. Only €6 and a free drink at the top with seating etc. || Great view of the city and a bit of the port. Best viewing spot is through the playground and to the left. || Views from this park of the east side of Lisbon. Not as nice as the other viewpoints at the castello o even farther, but still it is nice and it is free. The park is not too big or worthwhile though. || Great view but if you’re looking for a sunset don’t go here. The west is blocked so probably best to come here for sunrise.  If you want to get a good sunset view, go to Miradouro da Graça. || A quiet place to take a break ❤ || Lovely little view point with small play area for kids. Just below the castle. Worth a visit when you come out the castle and walk your way down || 100% recommend, this might be the best view in Lisbon. || Good view point over Lisbon. Just tends to be windy in winter and to get there on foot you have to go through an  narrow street with cars constantly passing bye || Cute little park with some fitness tools & a small playground – the view from here towards Alfama neighborhood and the bay is beautiful! Great place to relax, picnic or a romantic date. Park has opening hours! In the summer it closes after 7pm. || First stop during my Miradouro tour through Lisboa - nice view, not gonna lie. || Beautiful view. There is nothing else to do but enjoy the view and rest a bit. || Hidden gem near the castle, if you are looking for a place that is not too touristy go inside the children park to get to this amazing view, you get to see the river and enjoy the old buildings from above with a free place to sit at and soak up some sun and views. || Great views, and cool breeze (great for the hot summer weather). Definitely worth it to go to the lower level, as there are significantly less tourists and the view is the exact same. || Nice and quiet Small bench that you can eat something on good viewpoint || A little park in Lisbon up just to have a beautifull view of the town and the TAJO river. || Quite steep and narrow stairs but the views were stunning. Paid 5€ but included a drink of your choice. || The spot is a bit hidden but very beautiful once you find it. Just walk through the playground and you will get there!! || This area had many amazing spots, for example, the beautiful sea view, artist workout, and sometimes you would meet musician who sing nice song songs. You may need to replenish more energy as you would walk upstairs and downstairs all the time in this area. || Nice view on top of the town

This is one of the most beautiful sunset spots in Lisbon. The view over the city and the river is truly stunning, and the atmosphere becomes magical as the sky turns warm shades of orange and pink. … || Another stunning viewpoint with a beautiful church as a backdrop. We went for a sunset and it didn’t disappoint. There were tons of people but we didn’t have a problem getting pictures and enjoying the view! || *IMPORTANT*: Beautiful view and it’s the same view from which charges 15€. Just avoid the path of picture 4 where the stairs are steep and there are a lot of hobos living in tents, they are harmless but the steps are their toilets so just imagine… || Best spot in Lisbon to watch the sunset. Easy to reach by foot, tram or cable car and the views are exceptional. || A wonderful viewpoint in Lisbon! Miradouro de Santa Luzia is absolutely worth a visit. The views over Alfama’s rooftops and the Tagus River are genuinely beautiful, and for the price of free, you really can’t complain.  ￼  It was a bit crowded when we went, but that’s expected given how popular this spot is. Even so, it’s still a memorable place to slow down for a few minutes, take photos, and enjoy the scenery. The viewpoint itself is part of the charm too, with a small landscaped terrace, shaded areas, and classic blue-and-white azulejo panels that make it feel distinctly Lisbon.  ￼  One detail I appreciated is that the tile panels aren’t just decorative, they depict historical scenes, including Lisbon’s Praça do Comércio before the 1755 earthquake and the 1147 conquest of the castle (a cool touch if you like history).  ￼  That said, I wouldn’t call the views “to die for.” You can get comparable viewpoints nearby, and this is more of a “quick, classic Lisbon stop” than a once-in-a-lifetime moment. It’s also conveniently located in Alfama at Largo de Santa Luzia, right by the Church of Santa Luzia, making it an easy stop while exploring the neighborhood.  ￼  Overall, crowded or not, it’s still definitely worth a visit and an easy, memorable addition to a Lisbon walking day. || Miradouro de Santa Luzia offers some of the most impressive views in Lisbon. place_name: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
reviews_content: You get a fantastic view of the historic centre of this beautiful city from here. You could stay and enjoy the well kept gardens and the views all day. There's so much to look at. Enjoy the full chaos of colours and sounds that envelope your senses. You'll have so many photos when you leave this place, but it is the experience itself that will stay with you. || Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara offers one of the most beautiful panoramic views in Lisbon. The terrace overlooks the historic center, the castle, and the river, making it an ideal place to pause and take in the city’s landscape. The garden is well kept, and the atmosphere is relaxed despite being a popular spot.  It’s especially impressive at sunset, when the light over the city becomes warm and golden. A must-see viewpoint if you want a classic Lisbon panorama in a pleasant, accessible setting. || A nice panoramic view of the city center and part of the coast. It’s adjacent to a busy street and is easy to access locates at the city center. It’s very spacious there currently hosting a Christmas bazaar making it loads of festive feels. There are different direction to arrive the view point, including one very steep pebble street as in the picture. Will recommend if you are nearby, but not necessarily worth to travel across the city for it as there are a number of other Miradouro in the city. || One of the most beautiful viewpoints in Lisbon! It offers a fantastic panoramic view over the city, especially at sunset when the light is golden. There’s a small park with benches, trees, and even a kiosk for coffee or drinks. It can get a bit crowded, but the atmosphere is lively and pleasant. A must-visit spot for anyone exploring Lisbon || We took the funicular up to this little park for the views, and it was not disappointing! The 270 degree views of the city and surrounding mountains were breathtaking. There are two levels to this park, and plenty of park benches to relax on. There is a small cafe here, if you need a drink or a snack. I would definitely recommend visiting here, especially if you want some really great photos! || Great view of the City from the nearby Bairro Alto. We were fortunate to visit during the New Year's market. Excellent choice of Portuguese specialties (think serrano sandwich with sheep cheese) and Porto. || Lisbon is a city that pretends to be humble while casually seducing you at every corner. I left the house planning “just a short walk,” which, in this city, is the most unrealistic expectation you can possibly set. Five minutes in and you’re already climbing some Biblical staircase, questioning gravity, God, and your shoe choices. But then Lisbon apologizes. It always does. Usually with light. I wandered through streets that smelled like roasted chestnuts and mild chaos, past tiled façades that look like somebody finally let a poet design buildings. People spilled into cafés, dogs trotted around like they owned the place, and the whole city glowed in that gentle, old-European way — like a postcard that refuses to retire. Eventually I drifted uphill to Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara, which is the kind of viewpoint that doesn’t just offer a view — it offers perspective. The kind that makes you remember you still have a pulse. Up there, under a tree that had definitely lived through several empires, I found an artist named Anne Laidam, casually painting like she had all the time in the world. Her works were neon daydreams of Lisbon — trams, rooftops, broken sunlight — the whole city filtered through someone’s kindness. I wasn’t planning to buy art. (I never plan to buy art. Art plans to buy me.) But one of her trams looked at me with the exact attitude of a Lisbon cat: unimpressed, slightly judgmental, irresistibly charming. So, of course, I adopted it. And carried it home alongside a copy of Saramago — because every reckless purchase deserves a companion in philosophy. If you ever want a walk that feels like a conversation with a city that knows it’s beautiful but doesn’t brag: just start walking. Lisbon will take care of the rest. || Fantastic views of the city and the boats sailing past on the ocean. Plenty of food and drink stalls. || Amazing view, very nice vibe with bars and good street food around (a bit overpriced). Definitely worth checking if you're is Lisbon, specially near sunset hours. I'd recommend for couples who want a romantic vibe. || Best spot in Lisbon to stop and see the whole city. It has a dog park below and a nice spot in the back with a cat box that was tended by some retirees. Great place for photos, food, music and just relaxing. || This is one of Lisbon’s finest viewpoints, offering sweeping views over the red rooftops of Alfama and the Tagus River. Created in 1864, the viewpoint is laid out over two levels. The upper terrace features traditional Portuguese landscaping, while the lower terrace includes classical statues and a central fountain—creating a peaceful garden atmosphere in the heart of the city. A unique feature here is the azulejo tile map installed in 1952, which helps visitors identify Lisbon’s main landmarks visible from the terrace. || Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara is one of those viewpoints that instantly makes you slow down and appreciate Lisbon, especially from a Canadian tourist’s perspective. The garden setting is peaceful and well-kept, the terrace is spacious, and the panoramic view across the city toward the castle and the hills beyond is simply stunning. It’s an easy place to linger, whether you’re snapping photos, enjoying a quiet moment, or just soaking in the atmosphere with a coffee in hand. There’s a relaxed, welcoming vibe that makes it feel less rushed than other viewpoints, and it offers a perfect balance of beauty, comfort, and classic Lisbon charm. || Visited on June 13th during the annual festival, and the atmosphere was electric! The viewpoint was buzzing with lively stalls selling refreshing drinks and delicious fast food. While I couldn’t stay for the evening concert, the daytime energy alone was worth the trip. The panoramic views of Lisbon are breathtaking—you can see the entire city stretched out below, just as pictured. The charming fountain area offers plenty of seating, making it a perfect spot to relax with coffee or even enjoy a leisurely lunch. With ample benches and easy access via Tram 51E or local buses, this miradouro is both convenient and unforgettable. A must-visit for the views, vibes, and vibrant local culture! || Unbelievable view of the city and river and the castle. Best place to take in the beautiful charm of Lisboa! || Having seen amazing viewpoints all over the world, from the mountains of Greece to the fjords of New Zealand, I know a good view when I see one. Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara is a beautiful high viewpoint of Lisbon city. From here, you can see the castle across the city, the sea on one side, and even watch planes landing on the other.  We walked uphill for about 15 minutes to get there, which was a bit tiring. I was surprised to find food trucks once we arrived. There wasn't a lot of variety, but you can grab a drink and a snack. Just know they are tourist prices, like 10 Euros for a small cocktail and 15 Euros for a sandwich. Small hack: stop at a convenience store before you go up and grab your drinks there to save money.  Even with those prices, this spot is a must-visit if you go to Lisbon. The views are worth it. || An elevated terrace overlooking historic Lisbon. This large area is very popular for photos with a remarkable view. (Note that the streetcar which serviced this location experienced a tragic accident earlier in 2025. While still weighing heavily on the hearts of locals, the park is open and accessible.) || A great view which you can see all across lisbon. While we were sitting and enjoying the view there was live music which made the experience better and more relaxing. The choice of food around is good as there were plenty of bakeries around, the amount of seats were good so we didn't have to wait for sit and have some lunch. || A must see point of view if you’re visiting the city. The view is wonderful and the park is very well maintained with bench and a fountain. Highly recommended to everyone || Great spot for the sunrise and close to a couple cafe for some espresso and sweets for your reward for seeing the beautiful view of the harbor and city. || One of the best view point from this side of Lisbon. The Castelo de San jorge and the other lookouts on the other side can be seen, as well as the port. The park in this side is also very nice. It is not as high as the other but totally worth it to take some pictures of the landscape.

Regarding Largo da Graça, it is still undergoing requalification by the Lisbon City Council and the contractor, and we would also like to inform you that, due to the ongoing work, cleaning can only be carried out after the pavement has settled. Best regards. || This letter serves to bring to your attention matters that seem to me to be important and easily resolved. These are the lighting and cleanliness of the Feira da Ladra area.  Lighting - In recent days/weeks, it has been observed that the aforementioned area has had its public lighting cut off, more precisely in the fair area, next to the old Navy Hospital and at the beginning of Rua do Paraíso, leaving it completely dark and providing what I have witnessed on numerous occasions: individuals who stop their vehicles and urinate in that area. Naturally, the non-existent or scarce lighting further encourages this occurrence. Also in Largo Dr. Bernardino A. Gomes (father), on the street that has no trees and where the waste deposits are located, the lamp of the public lighting has been inactive for a long time. In this regard, I appeal to the Parish Council to take the necessary steps to resolve the aforementioned situation;  Cleanliness - The waste containers located in Largo Dr. Bernardino A. Gomes (father) in front of numbers 176 and 176A are frequently littered with trash, providing a degrading spectacle for passersby. Furthermore, they are situated in the only area of ​​the street/square where one can see the river, a situation that is unfortunately not conducive to aesthetics. The proximity to the Feira da Ladra flea market encourages passersby to urinate there, contributing to the lack of cleanliness and nauseating smell that is felt daily in that location, also not helping those who want to appreciate the view from there. Of course, these factors, combined with the fact that the public lighting pole located there is deactivated, mean that the aforementioned situation continues without any sign of resolution.  In light of the situations observed and mentioned, I propose that the necessary steps be taken with the competent authorities to reactivate the public lighting and that the waste containers be placed approximately 30 meters downstream, on Rua do Mirante, in a location that does not interfere with traffic, the view of the river, or anyone's residences, as there are no windows or doors in that area that could be damaged by this change. || The small square with the garden in the middle between Rua de São Tomé and Travessa do Açougue is a complete mess! Besides the lack of maintenance of the garden, if you can call it that, it's full of trash such as beer bottles and such. Judging by its condition, it seems like it hasn't been cleaned or maintained since the last popular saints' festivals?! Is that possible?  It would be so easy and simple to have this garden beautiful and clean. What is the council doing?  Thank you.  António Reis || It is regrettable that the Parish Council of São Vicente was asked to sweep and wash Angelina Vidal Street, from beginning to end, because since the Popular Saints' festivities, this street has been disgusting and filthy, full of garbage that has never been collected. They do nothing and don't even pay attention to what the residents of this street say and write. || Having gone to the council headquarters today seeking information about the possibility of starting a tourism project in the Graça area, I hereby inform you that the service provided by the lady responsible for concessions/authorizations was nonexistent. She didn't even bother to get up from her desk to find out what it was about, instead telling her colleague at reception that there was nothing available at the moment and that I should keep checking back because they were currently carrying out a lot of construction work. (I think the lady in question must be overwhelmed by her position or lack the qualifications to perform it properly). It pains me to pay taxes to support these unqualified individuals who are personally in charge of serving the public. Kind regards || Good afternoon. I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with the attitude of an employee of the São Vicente parish council, of which I am a voter.  On the evening of Wednesday, June 22, 2016, a gentleman parked his van in the Quinta de Ferro parking lot next to his residence and left a rear window open.  Then a gentleman who works for the parish council passed by, opened the car door, folded down the seats, and removed four plastic bottles (I believe they were wine bottles) and a large Pingo Doce bag full of lemons from the trunk. He then took the bottles and the bag of lemons in the van.  Without further ado, here is my complaint regarding the gentleman who committed this cowardly act.  Without further ado,  Here is my complaint. || Unfortunately, they are very active when it comes to doing personal side jobs. Providing trash bins and planning trash collection in the shelters of Stac Apolonoa takes months. || This parish council is a disgrace, from the president to the assistant, Natália Vinagre, who is a big liar and irresponsible. They meddle in people's lives and don't use the council's funds to help those in need and those they recommend. || An insufficient Parish Council, which only organizes parties, excursions and lunches, when it could be truly useful and make a difference in supporting the community, especially the elderly and needy of the parish, has closed its offices and its website is unavailable. || I'd like to know why whoever does the lawn maintenance in the parking lots doesn't bother to put up a barrier for the stones. Today my van got all scratched up. I'll call first thing tomorrow morning, because by 6:05 PM nobody answered. || I live at number 90 on Rua do Vale de Santo Antonio, first left. My 84-year-old father earns around €500 and pays almost €90 in rent. No repairs have ever been done, nor have inspections been carried out by the Santa Casa (a charitable institution), the City Council, or anyone else. Who can help? || Why has there been no street lighting in the sappers' area for over a week? || When distributing masks, please follow the example of the Santa Maria Maior Parish Council. || What types of services are available to the public?

Superb panoramic view of Lisbon with a very chill bar and nice people to share the view with || Not exactly what I expected... The view was great but there were lots of garbage thrown all around the place. And the alleys trough it was also a bit dirty. I absolutely understand the street art which is great but are plenty of bottles and papers and other plastic materials trown there || A good place to see the city. People start to come here two hours before sunset and thus if you want to secure a front spot you may need to arrive early.  Most people bring wine and stay for several hours. This is one of the few viewpoints that have a bar on-site which makes it very convenient. No entry fee || Great viewpoint, perhaps one of the less “well-known” spots not ruined by TikTok trends / videos. Nice bar there too (which is closed on Mondays). Overall would highly recommend, despite the steep walk there! || Great vibes, beautiful views (especially to watch the sunset). There is a really nice kiosk to get beers, wines and snacks. || Top place to watch sunset, a lot of young people hanginf, drinking and listening music. || Nice viewpoint, but not as scenic as others. More ordinary rooftops and scenery, except for the 25 do abril bridge and the Christo Rei statue in the distance. Plain setting at the top, but it does have an information board, a water closet, some tables and a small cafe building. || Awesome look out point, little bar at the top and great vibes around sunset! || I call it „the least touristy miradouro“ It’s lovely alternative to all the central ones. || My friends and I passed by this viewpoint by chance. This place is simple but tranquil and not crowded with tourists. We had to climb a long flight of uneven stairs to reach this place, but all of the tiredness went behind us when we saw this beautiful sunset 🤍 || Nice spot with a little café/drinks/snacks with local vibes. Avoid week ends and evenings as it can become quickly crowded. Good exposure so it catches the sun from morning to evening. || A great point to watch the sunset go down over Lisbon. The place it was busier when I have visited. There is a small kiosk selling drinks and snacks. If you do have time is worth the visit there. || Beautiful view with lots of seating areas, or strip of grass under the trees for more nature loving. But for why the heck did you destroy such a nice place with a ray of trash cans? To the Lisbon authorities - please move them out of the miradouro’s main observing point - makes the view quite icky. Perhaps people can learn to throw their trash as they leave, not trash the place itself? Thanks || Well worth the walk and less busy than other vantage points in the city. Added bonus was the little coffee kiosk with good, inexpensive coffee. Entrance was a bit tricky to locate. || Second stop during my Miradouro tour through Lisboa - nice view, not gonna lie. || Breathtaking views. But remember it's Lisbon, so be ready to walk uphill. || The best place to smoke a joint and enjoy the sunset 🌅 || I found this viewpoint by lucky and found it quite attractive. Easy access and a small place to have a drink. The day was cloudy but it did not detract from its charm. || Simple neighborhood viewpoint. Enjoy the sunset with the locals. Chairs and benches available as well as a bar serving drinks and snacks. || Absolutely beautiful view! The sunset here is amazing! Very clean and there is a lovely little cafe at your disposal. There is also a little shop not far from this view point. People having the best time! Take some wine, cheese and bread and enjoy the view, or maybe go with some friends and some beer and enjoy the ambiance and your friends company. :)

This little bar in Alfama is just perfect! 🍷 We had such a lovely time having wine and a great chat with the owner. He let us sample a few wines before we picked one. The cheese platter was also delightful. 🧀 Totally recommend! ✨ … || We had fun at the tipsy turtle! I had a glass of delicious red wine, and my husband tried a few of the beers. Ronny was super helpful with selecting local wines, letting me taste a few to see which ones i liked. They are super knowledgeable and friendly! Will return. || We rounded out a great stay in Lisbon with an evening drink at the Tipsy Turtle. The drinks and cheese board were great, and the best part was the owner / manager / barman. He was really knowledgeable, lots of good advice about wine, port … || We had the best time at the Tipsy Turtle! Ronny is an amazing bartender.  The charcuterie and cocktails were amazing.  Fantastic local atmosphere.  If you visit Lisbon, go here! || So lucky we found this wine bar- amazing service, wine and cheese. Met a new friend, Mary, who said the beer was great. Bartender Dillon’s recommendations were excellent- we tried so many wines we loved with tastes before we decided on a … || Perfect spot to take a drink. Highly recommended. Some of the best drinks we’ve had. Ronny and the crew were simply amazing. A must if you’re in Lisbon. || If you’re looking for a place with good music and great Portuguese wine don’t hesitate to check out this space! Our server let us try out the wines before purchasing and was very knowledgeable, he even gave us a couple free samples. A perfect place to grab a drink or two while discovering the Alfama neighbourhood. || What a hidden(?) gem! Stumbled upon this place looking for a quick glass of wine and little did we know that Ronny was our guy. Super friendly, attentive, and great wine. He let us try a wide variety of drinks and even hooked us up with … || Ronnie was a great host, a very knowledgeable bartender. Cocktails were amazing, Mojito & Pastel De Nata we would recommend. The music was fun & upbeat, great vibes! … || Beautiful bar with the best bar staff. Bar staff are so knowledgeable with fantastic wine recommendations and so knowledgeable. Had the best wine, cheese board, and shots. Literally couldn't ask for a better bar to stumble upon. || If I could give this place more than 5 stars then I absolutely would! The drinks were perfect, the recommendations were incredible, the service from Ronnie was perfect! Absolutely gutted we discovered this place on our last night in Lisbon … || We  had some very nice wine and port. The owner, Ronnie knows a lot about wines and was fun to get to know. It has a very inviting feel and atmosphere. We might go back before we leave Lisbon. || Stopped in for a cocktail. A lovely, quirky bar. Excellent Aperol Spritz and Mojito. So good we may come back at night. Staff very friendly. || Nice place but the bartender did not shut up! We popped in for a "quick n quiet" drink before our final walk round Lisboa. He just didn't get the message that we only wanted 1 drink each no food, gave my husband a large beer when we asked … || Ronnie and his staff really make this shy and small place huge. Their knowledge about wines, brandies and genuine interest in understanding the customer preferences makes this a hidden gem, unsung song amidst many mild options out there. … || Great bar with fantastic cocktails! We highly recommend the Pastel de Nata Liquor, it was delicious! The owner is really passionate and you can feel that he loves what he does. We had a great time! || Great advice on selecting the wine. The table games were also fun. Friendly service! || Great selection of wines and our server was very knowledgeable! He was able to recommend wines according to our preference. You can tell this place is all about the quality of the wine they serve. If you love wine and want to try some authentic Portuguese wine, you MUST visit! || Charming, under-the-radar bar in the hipster area. The owner greeted us warmly and introduced us to some real local treasures—smooth yet punchy Aguardente and beautifully aged Madeira wines you rarely see outside Portugal. || A must-visit gem in Alfama!  Tipsy Turtle is the perfect spot to unwind in the heart of Alfama. The …

This downtown cosy wine bar offers a fusion petisco menu with an extensive wine offer at fair prices with informal service in a minimalistic ambiance.  We were 3 for dinner who chose the couvert, fresh goat cheese, escabeche de coelho, a delicious lascas de bacalhau, the ox tail with salad, all with waters, a few glasses of wine and a coffee for €40/pax.  IT is a favourite ✨💫 || Truly the best wine bar in Lisbon ♥️ We had the loveliest time — the staff and the owner were so welcoming, and the atmosphere was warm and inviting. They were incredibly helpful in helping us choose a wine, and the Dois Carvalhos Reserva was absolutely excellent. A bottle of that, paired with goat cheese and sourdough, made our evening truly wonderful. Highly recommend! || The best way to spend a last afternoon with friends Seriously. It’s a wine bar, and they’ve got great munchies. And, even more importantly, they’ll happily spend all the time in the world with you figuring out what you want to drink - anything from pairings to “just a glass of wine” Seriously, just an awesome place! || We had an amazing night at Nova. After a long day walking the hills of Lisbon their concept "you choose the food and we choose the wine" is a perfect way to relax. Every bite, paired with a perfect wine ... and a beautiful reflection of Portuguese grapes. The bread and olive oil was so good I could drink a glass of the olive oil. The oysters, fresh and paired perfectly with a white wine. Fish cakes were tasty. Above all, the friendly and fun service the staff provided was outstanding.  Do go see this quaint lil wine bar in Lisbon! || I never give full 5 stars, but I had to make an exception. The experience starts from your first step inside, the place is built perfectly. The staff is more skilled in wine then most sommelier I've met even in michlen restaurants. The food is not only great but with precision. Everything about the place is precise and any little detail in the place was given sophisticated thought. If you like wine, and are in Lisbon, you must pass through. || Yonara is great! She helped us so much!! I loved the food, the atmosphere, the wine! It was a superb experience. Save some room and taste the drunk pear for a dessert || Wow, Pedro thank you! We stumbled across this gem and I’m so glad we did! The food and wine were incredible - even my picky eater parents agreed. I’ve been a little scared to try sardines but tried it here and it was SO delightful. Each of the food/wine pairing went so well with each other and Pedro gave us explanations to put it all into context. Highly highly recommend!! || Wow, this wine bar and restaurant is just absolutely incredible. Our first night in Lisbon, we went here after dinner and were blown away by how intimate and personally curated the experience was. João helped us pick a couple dishes and suggested wines to pair each with. He explained why each wine would pair well, along with an explanation of where in Portugal each wine came from.  Our experience was so good that we came back for our last night in Lisbon for a full dinner, along with wine pairing. Our second visit was even better than the first, with both the hostess and João remembering us and taking incredible care of us.  Some Google ratings in Lisbon seem artificially inflated, but Nova Wine Bar has absolutely earned its 4.9 stars as of September 2025. || I came to Lisbon in search of a true culinary experience, and this was easily one of the best meals of the entire trip. The owner, Pedro, personally welcomed me as soon as I sat down, which immediately set the tone for the evening. I told him I was open to anything, and he curated a six-tapas tasting, each thoughtfully paired with a different wine.  Every pairing was beautifully balanced and clearly intentional, elevating each dish without overpowering it. The progression felt effortless, refined, and deeply satisfying from start to finish. If you are looking for an exceptional, memorable culinary experience in Lisbon, go to Nova. You will not be disappointed. || Loved this spot! We tried two cheeses and the ham — all perfectly curated — and Pedro gave us great wine pairing tips. Every choice was spot on for the four of us. Cozy, elegant and delicious!

place_name: Red Nose Natural Wine Bar and Shop
reviews_content: A hidden gem in the heart of Campo de Ourique.  On a hot summer’s day, we stepped into this cozy little wine shop and were warmly welcomed by the owner, who served us natural wines at a small table inside. The air conditioning was a big plus, making it the perfect escape from the heat.  We spent a wonderful afternoon learning about Portuguese wines and their origins, while enjoying delicious food that paired beautifully with each glass. We left feeling not only a bit more knowledgeable, but also a bit happier than when we arrived.  A true local treasure — highly recommended! || Red Nose Bar is the spot if you’re into wine and good times. They’ve got an awesome selection— sip whatever and everything they suggest, tastes good, you’ll find something special.  staff? super friendly, know their stuff, and will make you feel like a wine pro in no time.  Oh, and the vibe? Chill but classy, perfect for a date or just a night out with friends. || Very cosy wine bar, we had our first natural wine here thanks to the kind staff! || Very groovy wine bar. No wine menu, so you tell the host what wine you are after, they give you a few to try and you chose the one you want - loved it! The wine glasses are really nice too - which always makes the wine taste better 😅 || Great selection of European wines. I tried Portuguese wines and got excellent recommendations. Unfortunately, I didn’t get a chance to try the food. || Thank a lot! We are refreshing our tapas menu soon and hope you will back to try with cool wines! || Gorgeous natural wine bar in the charming Campo de Ourique area of Lisboa! I loved the choice of wines — including excellent non-alcoholic options — and the relaxed, welcoming atmosphere created by the team. The sommelier will help you choose the perfect wine according to your mood, taste, and preferences, making the experience even more personal. The place isn’t too big, but the tables outside add a lovely touch to the vibe. The food dishes vary according to the guest chef, who personally explains all the ingredients and inspiration behind each plate. Perfect for meeting friends, a date, or simply enjoying a glass of whatever suits your mood. || Very nice wine bar (natural wines mostly). Good choose of the different wines, which you could try and choose the better for you. Also good small plates of food, great pairing to your wine. || Thank you so much for your wonderful review! We're thrilled that you enjoyed our selection of natural wines and the food pairings. Wishing you all the best and hope to see you again soon! || It's always a good idea to pick one glass or bottle of natural wine here. Friendly staff, good vibe and any kind of taste could be satisfied || Top notch service, not only incredibly knowledgeable and professional, but also relax and extremely generous, with an impressive offer and fair and clear prices. Relax environment and very enjoyable experience. Highly recommended if you are looking to try good quality wines from all over the world! || Thank you for your kind words! We're thrilled to hear that you enjoyed our relaxed environment and global wine selection, and we can't wait to welcome you back! || The staff is very lovely and they have a great selection of good wines! I cannot recommend this place enough🙌🏻

Came here for my birthday meal based on the excellent reviews and proximity to the apartment we were staying in. So glad we came. Delicious cheeses and meats to start and excellent steak. The waiter was very helpful in finding us a wine … || Thank so for your kind words, Maisie. || Personal experience. The owner helped us pick a wine and allowed us to try until we found one we loved. The charcuterie board with insane. The owner went through what meat and cheese was from which region. Highly recommend || What a treasure! My friend and I stumbled across this charming little restaurant this week and are so glad that we did. The owner is a one-man show; he works so hard to keep the food and wine flowing, it's really impressive. He has a very … || Lovely little wine bar in Lisbon! The owner is very nice and welcoming, creating a relaxed and friendly atmosphere. Great selection of wines and tasty food to go with them — all at very good prices. A perfect spot to enjoy an authentic local experience. Highly recommended! || I was a little hesitant when we arrived but I’m so glad we stayed. It’s a one man show (there is help with the  food) and so much fun. … || Thank you Heike. Best regards || What an absolute gem of a place . The owner clearly a connoisseur of wine and an amazing chef. Exceptional food and great value for money, particularly given the quality of the fresh produce and service. Bookings essential but don’t miss this place if you are in the area. || Private dining at its best without the price tag ! Ridiculous amount of wine selection and the food is sublime . I would like to keep  this a secret but corkscrew deserve the recognition ! || Really good wine&food and the host was very attentive. || Amazing place! This wine bar won us over from the very first moment. Great atmosphere, excellent wine selection, and truly outstanding service — attentive, professional, and welcoming. We had a wonderful evening. Highly recommended! || Our experience was unique...we knew the moment we spoke with the orner, we knew this would be out kind of resto. Personalised service, a sensé of humour, passionnante about his work and his région, this award Winning sommelier  , took the …

We booked Lisbon Winery based upon the strong recommendation of travel author Rick Steves. Unfortunately, our experience fell short of what we usually expect from Rick's suggestions. Our disappointment was not with the charcuterie board or the wines poured for us, which were all delicious and generously served. Instead, we felt that the service we received was cool and unfriendly to an unacceptable degree. The food and wine were all presented with a well-rehearsed script, but we found it difficult to ask questions or learn more about what was given to us. Our server seemed disinterested and tried to disengage with us at the earliest opportunity. We believe that we were friendly and relaxed, so I'm not sure why we were treated this way. We simply wanted to learn a little more and expected that the staff would be happy to share their love of Portuguese food and wine. Our visit was in the afternoon and there were only a few other customers present, so it was hardly a busy environment. In fact, our server seemed to enjoy chatting with another couple and he spent far more time with them. We also experienced a woman come into the Winery about half-way through our visit who brought a barking dog with them into the space where we were eating and drinking. The staff seemed to know her, and they chatted with her for about 10 or 15 minutes before the woman and her dog left. By the time we finished, we left feeling that the staff of Lisbon Winery couldn't have cared less about our experience and wishing we had spent our time differently. || Thank you, Kenneth, for taking the time to share your feedback.  My name is Alex, and I am the co-owner of Lisbon Winery. I’m truly sorry that your experience didn’t meet the high expectations you had. If a guest leaves less than delighted, it means we still have room to grow, and I sincerely appreciate the chance to reflect and improve.  That said, I’d like to clarify a few points about your visit:  1. Regarding the presentation and “script”: Our wine and charcuterie selection changes daily — sometimes even during the day — depending on availability, temperature, pairings and guest's preferences. Because of that, no two tastings are ever the same, and there is certainly no pre-established “script.” Our sommeliers speak from knowledge and passion, not memorization. I’m sorry if it felt otherwise during your experience. Sharing the stories of small, independent Portuguese producers is at the heart of what we do and has been the foundation of our more than 2,000 five-star reviews.  2. About the service and attention: I was present during your tasting and observed our sommelier presenting your wines, grapes, wine regions, olive oils, and pairings with his usual enthusiasm and professionalism. From my perspective, he was not unfriendly and was attentive. Of course, every table and tasting is unique — for example, the other couple you mentioned was experiencing a Port tasting, which naturally follows a different rhythm and pacing. Counting minutes of interaction isn’t really the spirit of hospitality we believe in; instead, our focus is on quality, not quantity, of engagement.  3. Regarding the dog: It’s true that a customer briefly came to the deck with a small dog, which is permitted under Portuguese law. The dog remained on the deck, a specific area completely separate from the food and wine area, as per our internal rules. The barking lasted just a few moments, and I personally went to calm the animal. It was me, the owner, and not the staff, that spent some time talking with the lady, who is a customer, like you and came to buy wine. So, once again, not giving more attention to this customer than to you as our sommelier was available in exclusive for both tables in the room.  We understand that every guest has different expectations and sensitivities, and we take all feedback seriously. Our team will keep working hard to offer great experiences. We’ll continue to improve and to stand by the warmth and authenticity that define Lisbon Winery. || Ironically, the low-rated reviews made me want to visit this place. The premium wine tasting costs €85 with an online reservation, but walking in was €95. I assume the extra charge was because I wasn’t part of a group, but paying the additional €10 ended up feeling worth it. They offered three types of local olive oil, a wide range of regional ham and cheese, and small-batch local wines. I hadn’t eaten dinner beforehand, but the amount of food they served was more than enough. The portions of cheese and ham were so generous that I regretted leaving some behind. My companion doesn’t enjoy Port wine, so we asked to switch to red wine, and they kindly accommodated the request. The only minor downside was that English isn’t my first language, and after the third glass, the alcohol made it harder to follow the explanations. Obviously, that’s not the venue’s fault. If you want a solid introduction to premium Portuguese wine, I recommend visiting this place. || Thank you, Luna, for reviewing us. We are really glad you have trusted us. We have a score of 4,9 on Google, so we have thousands of very happy customers and are really happy to know you are one of them. We hope to see you back one of these days. || Thiago is the best I want to adopt him. His knowledge of the Portuguese wine region is beyond words I'm already ready organizing a family trip to come back and feast on Thiago's knowledge of wines. Please if you find yourself in Lisbon come to this wine tasting with Thiago. Thiago is the best I consider him as though he is my son! 😂 || Thank you, Daniel, for your amazing review. It is just beautiful to see that we end the tastings with new friends. We had the best time!! We hope to see you back soon. || Tiago was excellent!, it was an amazing  experience totally recommend it, we learned a couple of things and we have been to wineries everywhere in the USA, Canada, Mexico, New Zealand, Spain. Thank you Tiago for your time and knowledge. || Thank you, Deborah, for your kind review. It was an absolute pleasure to welcome you at the Lisbon Winery and to share our passion for the Portuguese wines with you. We hope to see you again one of these days. || What a lovely place! It’s stylish but relaxed, and the staff is super friendly and speak great English. They explain everything clearly and can choose wines for you based on your preferences — and the recommendations were spot on for me.  Do yourself a favour and get the cheese/meat platter. It’s huge — listed for 2 people, but perfect for 3, and you could even share it with 4 if you’re on a budget. The wines were reasonably priced and the recommended ones didn’t break the bank.  I’ll definitely return the next time I’m in Lisbon. Thank you, and all the best to your business — it’s clear you take pride in what you do. || Thank you, Samu, for taking the time to review us. We had a great time too. We hope to see you back one of these days. || Tiago was our host for the evening.  Starting with bread and olive oil.  Then the wines and cheese and meat board.  Finishing with a 35YO port.  Greedy,  we asked for something to knock oursocks off. A 43YO port.  Echoing back to that first night,  "I don't want the evening to end..." Amazing... || Thank you, John, for your kind review. It was a great pleasure to welcome you at the Lisbon Winery and we are really happy to know you enjoyed the wine tasting and the special Ports served. || The wine tasting is truly excellent. We were brought some nice wines that represented different areas of Portugal that were not mass produced and good quality. The cheese and charcuterie platter was also very tasty. Our sommelier was Thiago who used to take part in the World Cup of wine tasting. He was very friendly and informative. Highly recommended. || Thank you for your generous review. We are really happy to know you enjoyed our wine tasting and your time with Tiago. It was a fun afternoon. || My husband and I were part of a small group wine tasting on Nov. 26th and had an amazing experience! The Sommier was incredibly passionate about the wines and we learned so much, including our liking of “Green Wine” and  Tawny Port. The only criticism we have is that there wasn’t an opportunity (that we noticed) to note ahead of time that we’re vegetarian so the Charcuterie was in the same board as the cheese. We ate most of the cheese that was not in direct contact with the meat, but felt bad about the food waste! || Hi, Lindsay. Thank you for your kind review. We are really happy to know you had a nice experience with us. Regarding your point about food restrictions, actually that is one of the questions we ask in our booking form. We ask for name, contact and also: “Do you have any food restrictions or allergies?” We have a lot of people doing our tastings with food restrictions and allergies and that is where we ask for that information so we can be ready for all situations. We were surprised to see all the meat untouched and it actually something we commented, but without that information we just did our normal premium board, cheese and charcuterie included. || Thank you so much to Tiago for a wonderful and very educational tasting! Great wine and even better conversation. Lisbon Winery is a  wonderful ambassador for Portuguese wine. We had a great time and I highly recommend a visit! || Thank you, Amie, for your review. We are so happy to read that you had a fun experience and are really excited to meet people as passionate as we are for great wine. || A group of 4 of us reserved a wine tasting and we were fortunate that Diago was our sommelier! We had a wonderful time and enjoyed the finest wines of different parts of the Portugal region. Went above and above and beyond, Very attentive and answered all of our questions. || Thank you for your kind words, Elizabeth. It was great meeting you and your group. What a fun afternoon! We hope to see you again soon.

Gutted that we only tried Wine Not on our last evening in Lisbon. Aside from an extensive selection of wines, all of the food we ordered were absolutely outstanding. The restaurant interior was lovely with the option of dining outside as well. Customer service was great, would absolutely come back if we return to Lisbon! || We had a great “small meal” here while sampling several of their absolutely amazing local wines! The manager spent a good amount of time explaining their large selection of wines to us, and telling us about how each one was produced and bottled, as well as the subtle differences in the varieties. We were really impressed by the quality of the wines, and the really surprisingly low prices. We even bought two bottles to take home because it was just too good of a deal to pass up! They have very comfortable indoor seating, and also a small deck outside, if you prefer. Definitely put this place on your list if you want to learn about and sample some really great local wines! They have a great food menu, also, and some vegetarian options. || Came here twice because I enjoyed the wines and service that much. Andre and Felipe were very knowledgeable about Portuguese wines so I was able to learn quite a bit. A lot of the other wine bars I visited in Lisbon just served you wine and walked away. Being from the San Francisco bay area with Napa and Sonoma counties nearby, I consider myself a bit of a wine snob. While this vineyard is on the larger production side  (I generally prefer smaller wineries), they only pivoted to this model the past some years ago. They have been around for over 100 years and know what they are doing. Seating inside was very comfortable.
