Cheese smelled so good, every bite of the guanciale tasted like heaven. The pasta came quick as well. The guy who welcomed us and took our order explained their specialty, treated us kindly. He offered us “spicy olive oil” or something like that, which tbh the first time i tried and it was the perfect touch to add kicks to the other pasta we ordered (couldn’t remember what it’s called). The place is rather small but its clean. I would definitely come back for the carbonara☺️ || I don't get the hype. The pasta was undercooked, we needed a lot of salt to just make it taste like anything, and the flavors didn't quite go.... Would not return, especially for the price. I think people who don't know good pasta come here, like a tourist trap or for expats who are looking for something trendy. The staff was very kind and attentive. || Food: I tried the Pasta Carbonara here, which was very good, delicious. It really is a specialized pasta place. Try it The people were helpful, smiling, and the food came very quickly. The locatian actually is a little small, but we can say its cozy. || My favourite pasta spot in Lisbon!  The pasta is made fresh and you can really taste the difference. My go-to is the carbonara and it never disappoints. The service makes the whole experience even better – friendly, welcoming, and fun. You really feel taken care of, which makes me come back every time I’m in town.  The atmosphere is relaxed and comfortable, the kind of place you can enjoy whether you’re stopping in for a quick dinner or having a nice evening with friends. || Very good fresh pasta, home made, excellent service made by super kind staff! Highly suggested!

So delicious and exactly what I needed from my first meal in Portugal. I had the orange + almond salad, mushroom rice, and garlic prawns. Service was quick and food was so fresh and balanced. The door was closed when I walked up and so I … || Although the food tasted good, we felt very scammed by the portion, we ordered the MAIN dish of garlic shirmp for 16 euros and it contained only seven shrimp!!? No bread on the side or frites no nothing ? How is this a main dish ? If it was … || Came here for lunch with a reservation. Small establishment so I would highly recommend making a reservation. … || Pls make a reservation- it seems like it’s always fully booked. Cute little place with best Sangria! Fried baby squid was good n savory. Fries decent- saffron rice was tangy- and pork cheeks with tomato migas was not my cup of tea… very tender tho- wanna try other dishes next time if I get a chance. || This is a fantastic restaurant with mouthwatering dishes! We tried the roasted cheese with honey (literally was amazing) and bread, beef cheeks (super tender and fell apart as soon as you put your fork in it), octopus with sweet potatoes … || Advisable to book 2-3 days in advance, because this quaint space have very limited seats with too amazing food. We're so lucky to still secure a spot being second on the waitlist at 8pm, on our final night in Lisbon. FOH is super charming … || Food was well done and flavourful , small dishes but filling . My favourite was the octopus with sweet potato. Staff were polite but aloof. Room was cozy and comfortable. Recommended to make reservations ahead of time || amazing food, lovely atmosphere. Aubergine is out of this world as are all of the puddings❤️ Thank you we had a lovely time and the waiter was friendly too. || The taste of the food is amazing. I went there on my own and ordered in total 3 main dishes and 1 starter. That speaks volumes. However is difficult to get a reservation because it’s a tiny restaurant so it’s … || Pros: The place is a bit off the busy streets and quite quiet. The food is delicious, but the portions are not too big. …

Really good, authentic, inexpensive family run Portuguese restaurant. The garlic butter shrimps were really good and we even used as dipping sauce for the bread! Octupus rice was average but the grilled pork is really juicy but not oily and all of us enjoyed it. Finally the house special dessert which was biscuit, whipped cream and chocolate could be so amazing put together. It's delicious yet not overly sweet. Nothing we have eaten in Portugal. Must try! || Had a solo dinner here and everything was fantastic. The family running the restaurant is very nice and the food is so so delicious. I had a codfish cake, the arroz de polvo (octopus rice), and a baba de camelo for dessert. The octopus rice was so soupy, savoury, and comforting -- the octopus very tender. || This was out favorite spot to eat! We had some other Portuguese restaurants while visiting Lisbon, but this, by far was the best! The food was so fresh, the owners were so kind and hospitable. Please visit this restaurant, it is tucked away and has the coolest interior! We will be back again my friends! || This review does not correspond to this establishment. We would appreciate it if you could remove it to avoid inconveniencing customers who may arrive here mistakenly. Thank you. || Superb food! Ordered both the octopus rice  and grilled fish. It feels like grandma cooking. Very satisfying and comforting. This was one of my best meals in Lisbon. The octopus was soft, rice was flavourful and the fish, perfectly done! Truly a gem, small but shining bright! Will recommend to anyone ard the area or after the visit to the Museu Nacional do Azulejo! || We have black pork, shrimp with garlic, fried chicken sticks and desserts.  The sticks is not oily and still juicy. Shrimp is tasty. Gill black pork is just perfect. All meals present not too salty. || Service, sooooooo gooooood, food, best. We loved it so much. Thank you for wonderful dishes 😋💗 || I think the one of the best food in Lisbon. We tried lot of places but this one is a hidden jem. We ordered sardines, an octopus salad and seafood rice. The food is delicious. Also, the service is a top notch! || I was searching far and wide for the small fired sardines. Delicious! We also got the sea bass which was as equally fantastic. Worth the trek. Don’t skip the dessert :) || Absolutely wonderful! Food: authentic and delicious. Service: excellent. Ambiance: unbeatable. Far superior to the very popular but disappointing "Sol" place nearby. My lunch featured fresh gezpatco, and calamari. It was so good I came back for dinner which featured the grilled bream and house vinho tinto. Don't miss the cave inside or this place! || This place is a hidden gem that should not be missed in Lisboa! Filled with friendly locals and great authentic food. The octopus was so tender, and both the grilled sardines and fried sardines were excellent dishes. Seafood was very fresh and cooked very well. I really want to point out the amazing service here as well. Our server was so kind, friendly, and we had great conversations with her. If you want to have a delicious dinner at a local spot (not touristy) in Lisboa, definitely come here!

We love trying cocktail rooms wherever we go, tried this one and it REALLY hit the spot. Best owners, very kind, great vibes - extremely relaxed. The drinks were solid - will hold their own against any cocktail room anywhere. We had the smoky margarita, negroni, a Caribbean inspired drink (forgot the name) and the Black Forest.  Shout out to the Black Forest, that was one VERY well made drink! Completely recommend. Host made us taste her favorite drink - I think it was called the Nikkei Milk Punch and I must say that one was extremely well balanced and beautiful as well.  Best part of the space for us were all the 🐶s visiting, completely made our evening! || Atmosphere: 8/10 Located in Lisbon’s Graça district. Very chill, home-style vibe—cozy, comfortable, music at a good level. Backbar is okay. Seating is limited: no bar counter, a few indoor tables, plus some patio seats.  Drinks: 8.5/10 Recommendation: Black Forrest, Pineapple Express Menu is simple. Selection is decent. Flavors are good. Coasters are nice; glassware is average; garnish is nice. Presentation is okay overall, with unique ice on select serves.  Service: 8.5/10 Water on arrival. Team is friendly, professional, and attentive. Prices are average for Lisbon. Reservations not needed. || Proper crafted cocktails in a small, cozy and we'll appointed space. Joanna and Peter create lovely drinks and provide personal service. I had a lovely milk punch which was perfectly balanced.  Its a good idea to make reservations. We will definitely go again. || Booked Onda to grab a quick pre-dinner drink and we ended up going a bit early and I’m so happy we did!  We got to try four different cocktails and they were so good and so creative! The space was also really cool - loved the decor and the owners were really sweet. || Had an amazing time here and really enjoyed getting to know the owners and hearing their stories and recommendations.  We loved it so much we closed out both of our nights in Lisbon here.  If you are looking for a great cocktail and a relaxing chill atmosphere this is the place to go! || This was hands-down our favorite cocktail bar in the city. It’s a laid back atmosphere where the husband/wife owners attend to the customers with passion and dedication. It’s clear that they love what they do. In my opinion, this establishment is better than Red Frog. The Nikkei Milk Punch was my favorite. You won’t find anything like it elsewhere; it’s one-of-a-kind. Don’t pass up the opportunity to visit, but do make a reservation. || What do you know about cocktails? 🍸✨ Forget everything you think you know! 😎 Because here, a whole new world will open up to you — a world of amazing flavors, aromas, adventures, and people who are truly in love with what they do! 💫🌍💃  Every sip is a little journey 🌴🍹 — through taste, through passion, through creativity! 💥 Whether you’re into something classic, bold, or totally unexpected, they’ll create the perfect cocktail just for you! 🍒🍍🍋  This place isn’t just about drinks — it’s about emotions, art, and pure joy! 💖✨ So dive in, explore, and let yourself be amazed by this ocean of cocktails! 🌊🍸🔥  Cheers to unforgettable moments! 🥂😄🍹 || Thank you so much for your visit and review. We hope you can come by this week for the tasting experience before you go home. 🍸🍸🍸 … || I’ve gone to Onda multiple times, and have always had a nice time.  I lived here as a student (American so do take that into account with my opinions on prices) for about a year and visited multiple times throughout my stay. A few times I went for drinks (sometimes alcoholic and sometimes not, they have amazing options for both) and once for a cocktail making class which was a super fun experience!  It’s a place to go if you want nice cocktails. They’re well made and super unique, so though they aren’t the cheapest, the prices  are by no means unreasonable and are on par with a lot of other places I’ve been to. I loved the smoky margarita, as well as the Thai infused alcohol (I don’t remember the name) which was one of the best cocktails I’ve had.  Would recommend and planning on going again soon as I’m visiting for the holidays! || I can't speak too much to the food but I can speak to the lovely couple who own the place and took us on a journey of many cocktails. Easily a true highlight of Lisbon and something I would recommend anyone who enjoys the finer spirits and what magic they might contain. Do yourself a favor take a friend or six to the cocktail flight, and if you enjoy whiskey talk to Peter the owner into giving you a master class in Whiskeys around the world. || Drinks are crafted with perfection. Flavor explosion balanced with eased shoulders. Cheers for the memorable experience.

Definitely worth a Visit. We popped in for a quick Cocktail before dinner and it certainly didn't disappoint. Cocktail waiter was super friendly and attentive. He made us fabulous cocktails and you can see from the menu, these are not your standard classic cocktails. If you want something different, this is the place for you! || My cousins and I had such a great experience! Marcus (the bartender) was extremely welcoming and created some drinks based on our interests/personalities. We came here to end our night and will definitely be coming back here in the days to come! Appreciated the vibe and ambiance of this place. || Good music and atmosphere. You need to ring the bell to get in. Had the server recommended two drinks. The first one in the first picture is amazing. The second one is just average. It is a little bit expensive comparing to other bars in Lisbon. But you may find it worthwhile. || We totally recommend stopping by Corksey’s! Super well-made cocktails and a team that’s clearly passionate about what they do.  We came in with high expectations and they were not just met, but exceeded. Tried the Cherry Blossom and Coffee & Coconut.  The Cherry Blossom tasted like a summer dream—full of cherry flavor and really smooth and well-balanced.  Coffee & Coconut was kind of a play on an espresso martini, but also something completely different. The combo of coffee and coconut was just perfect. Great choice for a pre-dinner drink or a relaxed afternoon break.  As tourists, we really appreciated how the bartender took the time to chat with us and even gave some great tips on places to see in Lisbon and other bars worth checking out. || Marcus made us some delicious drinks, was super knowledgeable and even gave us tips on where to eat in the area late at night since most places were closed.  I’d recommend checking this place out it was a treat! || What a charming, cosy little gem! I was planning on heading to the Peruvian spot on this street, but it was too busy so we kept walking and came across this (fairly new?) hole in the wall cocktail bar.  It's basically a one man show, with a single bartender and a server to help him out. (I don't know if there's food? But there are a few complimentary snacks.) The space is not large at all. It maybe seats about 12. Which is perfect for the experience.  Service was prompt and helpful.  I started with the Terracotta which the bartender mentioned was one of his favourites. It was smooth and exceptionally well-balanced. The hints of cheese and pumpkin shrub really held up against the tequila. The apricot was a bit too present for me, but it was a tasty and sophisticated little drink. And considering it was Jose Cuervo (my most hated tequila and usually awful), I have to give kudos to the bartender for making it so drinkable.  We tried some others as well, but the superstar of the night was the Madeirese. What a fantastic cocktail! I was in love at the first sip. I could drink these forever.  What's wild is that on paper, it seems exceptionally sweet and almost none of these ingredients appeal to me! But I saw "banana" and, for some reason, decided, "Hey, why not lol?"  I am so glad I did. Now, it is sweet. But not in a cloying or cringey way. Somehow, it's beautifully balanced with the rich, deep flavour of actual Madeira banana puree (which are not as sweet as the common Cavendish banana). The honey is only used as an accent and the Madeira wine rounds out and softens the rum.  I can still taste it when I think about it and I hope next time, it's still on the menu when in back in Lisbon.  The cocktails are minimalistic in presentation and complex in flavour. But most of all, they are delightful to drink! A very crisp, classy, unique and modern menu with memorable drinks. Amazing job.  This bar is such a welcome addition to the cocktail scene here and I can't wait to come back.  EDIT: I have now been here multiple times -- always for the Madeirese, and even on the days they don't have it, they've made other excellent drinks! And the staff is still super welcoming and top notch. Truly one of my favourite bars. || Thank you very much Vee :)   New menu comming, and Madeirense, from the 1st menu, will be back !   See you soon.   Cheers Vasco || A great spot with a chill atmosphere but what really made the night was the Biswash the bartender — incredibly friendly and attentive. He took the time to ask what kind of flavours we liked and then crafted custom drinks that were absolutely perfect. The spicy marg was class.  You can tell they really know their stuff and love what they do. Highly recommend if you’re looking for a place with great vibes and top-notch, personalised cocktails! || A Tiny bit hard to find the entrance, but THE best drinks in Lisbon.  Ring the Bell, pray for a open slot and let them work their magic.  Ask for Bis-special, life-changing. || Ring the bell and you're in. What can I say about the service? It's one of the best I've experienced anywhere, tied with another speakeasy in Lisbon.  Amazing cocktails. I went off the menu to let him work his magic, and he did. || What a cool experience!  Great spot with exceptional service.  My server Marcus was professional, friendly, and made me a fantastic custom-made drink from my preferences! || Firstly, I believe his name was Marcus (sorry if I'm wrong) was an unbelievable host and mixologist - I have never made such an friendly connection with a server before and he is unbelievable at his job, he spoke so highly of the business and its progression, as well as making us feel like friends. The cocktail 'it's so corny' was the best cocktail I have ever had. I couldn't recommend this place more, Marcus - you made our evening amazing and your talent is impeccable! Thank you so much, we can't wait to return on our next future trip to Lisbon. Ps the banana cocktail and their twist on the dirty martini was also amazing! || If I can give this a 10/5 I would… amazing drinks, relaxing atmosphere and unbelievable menu. The mixologist is a mad scientist… the menu it incredible and if you don’t like it he will go above and beyond to make you a drink that you WON’T forget! Also, you won’t forget Marcus, beautiful personality and genuine. Just a good person! || A beautiful and intimate speakeasy cocktail bar, hidden in plain sight. It’s visible from the cobblestone steps, but only if you look carefully (blink and you’ll miss it) and you have to ring the doorbell to get in, which is a nice touch. Makes it feel exclusive and similar to old speakeasy bars.  The drinks that we tried were amazing, especially the ‘Peppers’ and ‘Pera Santa’ cocktails. Great little place, highly recommended! || Awesome speakeasy with an awesome bartender. I will be cheering for Cape Verde in the World Cup thanks to the great chats with our bartender. Safe travels on your US trip! || Really cool speakeasy style bar with inventive and interesting cocktails. There is a large variety of different styles of drinks with local and south american ingredients as well as some asian touches. The staff were very helpful and professional as well! Note that the entrance is very unassuming and you need to ring the doorbell. We arrived at around 21:00 on a Monday and the place was empty which felt awkward but not much later another couple entered. || We tried couple of cocktails from their new menu and they were absolutely amazing! The highlight for me was definitley coffee & coconuts, yet the one with berries was also very delicious and sour. Service is very attentive and they offered to do a completely new cocktail based on our taste preference as well. Would come here again! || Charming hidden speakeasy with amazing cocktails that are well balanced. The ambiance is vibey with great beats playing in the background. The best part of this bar however, is the service. After making reservations for two they kindly accommodated 4 of our friends who did not have reservations. The host even sat us all together. With that being said if you do have a big group or not please still make reservations as the bar can only sit about 12 people comfortably. To the host and bartender obrigada!!! Appreciate your service so much! || Thank you very much Isa :) || Found this little haven in the city away from the busy drunken crowds. What a GEM!! Drinks were fantastic and the staff were super friendly, highly recommend. Delicious cocktails around €12 each. Intimate venue but perfect for a couple || Biswas was amazing with the cocktails. Had a really great conversation with him. He made a very interesting negroni unlike any I’ve had before. Highly recommend! || Very interesting cocktails.  You can always let the bartender know what you prefer in taste and he will make you a drink that custom to that. Very happy with our drinks

Atmosphere: 7/10 Monarch sits in one of Lisbon’s popular nightlife areas. The vibe is casual yet accented with cool design elements that give it character. Music volume is good. The backbar looks nice, though seating at the counter is awkwardly split by a column. There are many tables available for groups.  Drinks: 7.5/10 Recommendation: Rub-A-Dub-Anana The menu is simple in design with a decent selection. Flavors are good and generally well balanced. Glassware is average, garnishes basic, and presentation minimal with little focus on ice or details. No coasters provided.  Service: 8/10 Water is served on arrival. The team is friendly and attentive, though professionalism could be sharper. Reservations aren’t needed. Prices run slightly above average for Lisbon. || Thank you so much for your review, Anton! We're glad you enjoyed the atmosphere, the drinks, and the service. We also appreciate your detailed comments, which are important for us to continue improving. It will always be a pleasure to welcome you back! || A very cozy place with a warm, personal and friendly service. The atmosphere makes you feel right at home. The cocktails are absolutely amazing, and the staff gives excellent recommendations based on your taste. Highly recommended! || Thank you, Alvaro! We're so glad to hear you enjoyed the welcoming atmosphere and friendly service. We're delighted to know that the cocktails and the team's suggestions suited your taste. We greatly appreciate the recommendation and hope to welcome you back soon! || Cocktails are delicious and the staff really know their stuff. Recommended us cocktails based on our tastes and they didn’t disappoint! || Thank you so much for your review, Matt!  We're delighted to hear you enjoyed the cocktails and that the team managed to choose the perfect cocktails to suit your taste. Knowing that the food, service, and atmosphere met your expectations is very important to us.  We hope to welcome you back soon for another great experience. || An amazing place! We came off season on a Saturday night. Right away the staff was super nice and recommended us cocktails to our liking. 11/10 recommend. I felt very welcome and the place looked cozy and nice :) || Thank you so much for your review, Kadi! We're so happy to hear that you felt welcome, enjoyed the cocktails, the cozy atmosphere, and the service. We appreciate the recommendation and hope to welcome you back soon. || Short story: this is probably the best cocktail bar in the city. You must go. Long story: I stumbled upon this place after a surprise cancelation of a dinner reservation down the street (another story) and what an amazing turn of events! Tamara made me one of the best cocktails I’ve ever had and they recommended another restaurant to me and called to make sure I could get a seat and the food was incredible! Great drinks and but even better people here. Tamara, they took great care of me at Gunpowder thank you for turning my night around :) || Thank you for your feedback, Amber! We are so glad you enjoyed the experience and that the service made a difference to your evening. Tamara greatly appreciates your recognition and kind words. We hope to see you again soon. || My favorite bar in Lisbon hands down.  Friendly place and welcoming to English speakers.  The place is a clean, upscale, trendy establishment with comfortable seating.  The service was professional and friendly and the establishment really cared about the customer experience.  The drinks were artful and unique combinations, involving some different ingredients like rhubarb.  There was skilled mixology, care, pride, and passion that went into the cocktails.  The owner even helped us with researching and finding a restaurant.  I would frequent this place if I was a local. || Thank you so much for your review, Jason! We're glad you enjoyed the atmosphere, the cocktails, and the service from our team. It will always be a pleasure to welcome you back whenever you return to Lisbon! || Delicious cocktails with refined flavors. The bartender was incredibly friendly and welcoming, and the atmosphere was just perfect. Highly recommended! || Thank you so much for your review, Josephine! We're so glad you enjoyed the cocktails, the friendly service, and the atmosphere. Your recommendation is very important to us. || Monarch Bar in Lisbon was such a fun surprise. I came in expecting to order a Last Word, but Tamara suggested something off-menu—the Back Door Bandit—and it ended up being exactly what I didn’t know I wanted. It had the perfect balance of kick and spice, with just enough sour. The chipotle and habanero flavors were bold but smooth, and yes, the mix is homemade. WOW to the expert mixologist!!  Even their water was thoughtful—infused with macaron tea, light and floral without being sweet. The whole experience felt considered but totally unpretentious. The vibe was cool without trying too hard, and the service was warm and welcoming from the start. I’ll definitely be back to see what else Tamara has up her sleeve. || Maryam, thank you for the feedback! We work every day to create special moments, and knowing that it worked makes us happy.  Best regards, The Monarch Cocktail Bar || Monarch is a must-visit for anyone who truly appreciates top-quality cocktails. Every drink is beautifully balanced, made with great ingredients and real attention to detail — you can tell there’s serious craft behind each glass. The atmosphere is cozy and relaxed, and the service is amazing. Definitely a place worth coming back to! || Thank you so much for your review, Luis! We're delighted to know you appreciated the quality of the cocktails, the attention to detail, and the atmosphere of the place. We appreciate your kind words and hope to see you again soon. || We stepped inside and the bartender invited us in. You can sit at a cozy private table. We chose to sit at the bar and have fun conversation with other patrons and the owner. Was not crowded early on a weeknight during off peak season. We each enjoyed 2 cocktails that were priced as expected between 11-13 euros each for high quality crafted drinks. Our favorite drink was Backdoor Bandit. Would happily return and explore the menu more. || Thank you for your review, Emily! We are delighted to hear that you enjoyed the cocktails, the atmosphere, and the interaction with the staff and other customers. We appreciate your feedback and hope to welcome you back soon to explore more of our menu. || TL;DR: This is hands-down the best cocktail bar in Lisbon. Bigger review: Oddly enough I don't want you to know about this bar. I want to keep it all for myself... but since I'm not in Lisbon all the time, I don't mind sharing it that much. Excellent cocktails, amazing people and lovely atmosphere. If you're ever in the neighbourhood, dive in, and your tastebuds will thank you for it. Enjoy! || Thank you for your review, Bas! It's great to know that you consider our place one of the best cocktail bars in Lisbon and that you enjoyed both the drinks and the atmosphere. We really appreciate your kind words and hope to see you again whenever you're in the area. || A classy little cocktail bar that is tucked away just a short walk from the hustle and bustle of the Time Out Market and all the bars and restaurants in Cais do Sodre.  We came here on a recommendation from another Lisbon bartender, and it was a pleasant experience. Despite being a sophisticated looking place, it has a casual, relaxed feeling that invites you in. There's no pretentiousness here.  The day we tried, they were out of some of the menu due to a really busy night before, and I understand that happens at these small, independent bars that make their own infusions and batches. It was okay, because they have a decent backbar and were able to get all the classics we asked for. The cocktails we tried from the menu were good and solid, but didn't exactly wow. But they're definitely better than a lot of cocktail bars I've been to in Europe. Simple and classy, but with a flavour complexity that is still interesting. You'll find creations here that are very unique.  All were made well, and service was good. Definitely a strong choice for a place to come for a nice drink and chat with friends. If you want to avoid the packed, loud, stuffy bars in town and have a creative drink or classic cocktail made exactly how you like it, I'd recommend this spot. || Thank you for your positive review, Vee. We look forward to your next visit!  Best regards, The Monarch Cocktail Bar || These are some of the best cocktails we’ve ever had—absolutely spectacular! My number one from now on is “Blast from the Past”, but honestly, every drink we tried was incredible. On top of that, the place itself is beautiful, with a cozy, intimate vibe and great music. The owner, Ze, is such an awesome person and really makes the whole experience even better. We’re not from Lisbon, and we already know we’re really going to miss this spot. || Hi Silvija! Thank you very much for your words. It was a pleasure to meet you and Nerius. You guys are amazing! The kind we wont forget.  I hope to see you guys soon! Cheers || Joao and his team of bar staff(mixologists probably a far more correct phrase), were simply amazing on the multiple nights I returned there. Magic/laughter/style/honesty, its all comes from the staff and the great atmosphere/drinks they create. || Thank you for your review, Vinny! We're really happy to hear that João and the team made your evenings so enjoyable, with a great atmosphere and excellent drinks. It's always great to receive this feedback. We hope to see you again soon for more good times! || These were hands down the best cocktails we had ever had. The bar master (Freddie) is a true craftsman - he clearly delights in creating and choosing recipes that his guests will love, and he is a true master of his craft. He actually sits down with you to learn what you enjoy before bringing out samples to see if they resonate, and then takes your order. The atmosphere is relaxed and intimate. Highly, highly recommend the Monarch! || Thank you for your positive review, Kevin Loechl. We look forward to your next visit!  Best regards, The Monarch Cocktail Bar || Highly recommend! Expert cocktails, enthusiastic, knowledgeable and passionate bartender. Warm welcome when we stumbled in from the rain. We each tried a different cocktail and every one was a banger. This place should have been packed but I’m glad it wasn’t! Hidden gem! || Thank you for your positive review, Lindsay Eckert. We look forward to your next visit!  Best regards, The Monarch Cocktail Bar || Daniel, Zé and Yasmine are cocktail geniuses! Every cocktail we tasted was incredible. They take unconventional tastes and enhance them into a drink. Seriously amazing works of art. My favourite is the Romeu et Julietta, but having tasted almost every drink on their list, you can’t go wrong with any of them! || Thank you so much for sharing, Victoria G! It's a joy to know you enjoyed the experience. We look forward to your visit again!  Best regards, The Monarch Cocktail Bar || Great drinks and very friendly staff - not too loud atmosphere and funky decor . I’ll be coming back - it was a great stop after a Japanese Portuguese infused meal || Thank you very much for your review, Lucas Wilker Souza e Silva! We are pleased to know that you enjoyed the drinks, the relaxed atmosphere, and the friendliness of our team. We appreciate your patronage and hope to see you again soon. || This place is a hidden gem. In any other city it would be a must-go. The bartender is knowledgeable and friendly, as is the waiter. Casual place but with high quality spirits and cocktails to an agreeable price given the effort made into every cocktail. Took very good care of me and my parents 🙏 Rare to find people so genuinely nice and committed to their art. Do drop-by this place, you won't be disappointed! || Thank you for your positive review, Markus. We look forward to your next visit!  Best regards, The Monarch Cocktail Bar || One of Lisbons hidden secrets! Such an amazing cocktail. || Thank you so much for your review, Kay! We're so glad to hear you enjoyed our space and cocktails. We hope to welcome you back soon!

place_name: Pink Bar - The smallest bar in town
reviews_content: Sweet super tiny bar in Lisbon. Fortunately got here early and didn’t have to wait in any crazy lines like they had later on. Unsure if I ordered wrong both times but the drinks were quite rough || Great bar one of the best in town Best cocktails And the shots Great recommendation || They do not ask you what exchange rate you want to pay and force you to pay the 5% markup if you're using USD. || We recommend customer to pay in EUR,and its the customer who choose the currency . || Good drinks, owners, talkings. Good central area to stay. || Beautiful buildings in the daylight. It is located on the main road of Lisbon city center. The entrance is accessible for wheelchairs. It might be difficult to find parking nearby. || Seems okay. If you are extreme fan of hygine and luxury, this won't suit you but if are a traveller and need a decent place at the epicenter of hustle and bustle of Lisbon, go for it. || Great location, nice rooms, breakfast selection good. || Looks awesome at night, great achitecture! || Art deco icon building of Lisbon.  Designed by Cassiano Branco and Carlo Florencio Dias and built in 1931. Unfortunately only the facade was left and hides these days a hotel. || There are many things to see and do.  If you have time, this is a great experience.

The apartment is very clean and furnished nicely, but the swimming pool was very cold and not clean. || A Choir makes any place shine ♥️ || The best thing that has happened in the Lopes neighborhood in the last 20 years was the emergence of this cultural space.  The space is modest, yes, but with a welcoming atmosphere, devoid of pretension or any other "isms" that pollute certain spaces linked to the artistic world. It is, without a doubt, "family friendly"!  The prices for events are affordable, usually ranging from €6 to €10.  The small size of the place contrasts with the great proximity it allows between the public and the artists, making each event a very intimate and enriching experience.  Despite the limitations of the space, its versatility is reflected in a diverse program. Jazz, Classical, Dance, Theater, talks or film previews... Everything fits in there!  It's a real "house of surprises," or it wouldn't be packed! || A pleasant place, although a bit small for the number of people who attended the show. || I love the space! I'm so happy to see a project like this being born in a neighborhood like Bairro Lopes; it's extremely important. || A very cozy and intimate night of stand-up comedy... || Very cozy and cheerful.

Beautiful, historic theatre and concert venue.  Situated just off Restauradores Square. || It was the best experience of my life! Seeing Alcione was a life long dream and been it such an iconic house in such an amazing company was everything ❤️❤️ || Came here to see King Gizzard three nights in a row, initially thought I missed it as an entrance is up a slope not on the main street but think that there are actually a few ways in. The bar has a system of ordering a drink round the far side as you come in and then have to go collect from the other side, there are other bars up stairs that looked quieter (although I just drank at the restaurant over the road before which done cheap beers you could drink in the street). The actual concert hall is pretty cool, large standing bit in the middle which has a good gradient on, then around this is some benches. On upper levels there are small rooms that had seats then a standing terrace right at the top, not sure how these worked as I just stood each night. Sound and lights were impressive. || Nice old theatre. Was there for the concert of MEUTE, which was incredible by the way. I didn't expect that there were such good acoustics here. Everything was well organized. The staff was friendly and informative. Enough toilets everywhere. Next time I will bring something to sit on as the benches were a bit hard when sitting some time. Can recommend a visit. || History and location alone make it a cool venue. Acoustics were fine in the GA pit and there looked to be plenty of seating around the bowl. Beverage lines are sparse and a mess due to an unnecessary ordering system they have. Also there is quite literally no security search to get in which is concerning. || I went for a Ferxxo concert and it was very good the concert, with a good light show. In the entrance was a bit of confusion but the security sorted it out. When arriving inside it look a bit old and made me remember for a sec that i was in the middle of a circus where they do shows, but it had space still and i could enjoy the concert. Now to go to the toillet in mens side is a pain, since the stairs that lead there are full of people queueing at the bar. Talking about the bar, it was the moat ridicculous thing, because i doesn't say anywhere that is a pre-pay line and you there queueing at the bar and when you get to the counter the bartender says you have to order on the other line, besides this they charge you 1.50eur for a cup and if you return it intact they won't give you money back, although everywhere else they do return the money. I remember having a guy asking for a manager because he wanted is money back for the cups since he had 15euros worth of empty cups. Another stupid thing my girlfriend wasn't feeling well and i bought a bottle of water for her so she could sip it throughout the concert and those weirdos removed the cap in front of me, and i says no because i didn't want to spill the water, and the bartender said it was their policy, so i had to put my finger inside the concert so it wouldn't spill all over. These people need their brains checked, and i don't recomend going to the bar in these coliseu || We saw the Christmas Circus and it was a great show, several different groupa of top notch performers, perfect for Kids and longer than we expected. Go to the earlier shows as the evening show has extremely long lines. || Beautiful theater.  The theater employees were all fantastic folks. No alcohol was served for our show (no sure if that is true of all shows), and fair warning: get in line early for 'The Loo' at break time.  Jethro Tull rocked the house! || Amazing concert, better still, the venue is a piece of history and art. A must visit. || The experience with the Swan Lake was beautiful, the sound quality was impeccable, you could almost feel the orchestra was right in front of you. However, the seatings are very unfortunate - I barely saw the stage and were sitting in a prime row, I can’t even imagine what the others could see. The event was in the afternoon, with hundreds of of children, and there was no booster or anything that could allow them to see the show. If it’s an experience you want to savor, or if it’s your first experience (as it certainly was for 90% of those kids), this is not a minor detail. || This review isn't about the show that I saw because it was brilliant but the place lack of renovations. It is an old venue, we get it but the lack of comfort on the seats and the too warm place make it way uncomfortable experience.  The rest is small so pretty much you see pretty well from almost every place except the ones besides the palco because that's too close and you will need to be looking to the side (weird) || The place itself is good for concerts and DJ parties. I’ve been to see Rivo and Marten Lu and was a blast. Was well organized, even the crowded. I hope to be there for more concerts. || Amazing venue!!! One of the best I ever visited. || Have watched two circuses here. Both quite grand. Can get quite crowded. Maybe management could look at limiting entry beyond a certain number. Food choices are rather limited. || I went there more recently to see John Cleese on his "Last time to see me" tour and, again, it was a great feeling. It's a large hall, very popular, in a building that shows its age but that it's still the place to go for every performer coming to Lisbon, rather than more modern and fancy venues. || Lovely wood antique-ish vibe, looks nice overall, it has a little coffee station with drinks and snack.. only things I would change are those super tiny uncomfy hard thin wooded seats!! Also, the audio they need more speakers. || Incredible concert by Cesaria Evora - wonderful orchestra in the concert hall and an experience to remember….The performers and musicians from Cape Verde were just fantastic! || Nice place for shows, great location, surrounded by restaurants and bars. Great atmosphere and service. Loved it! || We went there for the Gentleman concert. It's not really big but not too small either. The sound was not the best but got better at the end. || The space is well organised and it’s easy to find your seat. The place is beautiful and quite big. The only downside is that it has no AC. It was a 26C degrees night, crowded and both public and presenters were drenched. It takes a bit off the experience.
I once saw a play here… We even drank wine… || My favorite theater in Portugal. || It's a unique performance venue.

place_name: Fado em Tons de RGB - Ozearv
reviews_content: Beautiful street mural by Lisbon artist, Oze Arv. || Nice and colorful Murals 🤩  Instagram - panameri_blog … || This is a fantastic mural that was just finished this Summer. There is a little park across the elevated street to have a glass of wine while you contemplate the scene. || This is one of the prettiest street art walls I've ever seen 😍🎨 || Simply beautiful!! A must see!! || This impressive mural is located on Rua Natália Correia in Graça, Lisbon. It is one of three artworks in Lisbon included in the online community Street Art Cities' list of the 100 best artworks of 2021. Ozearv describes the work on his Instagram as "the fado of the alleys and new timbres." It's a remix of fado, where each animal takes and leaves a little of itself. This artwork also serves as a reminder of how ephemeral street art can be. Before 2014, the same wall adorned Violant's mural "The Tree of Knowledge," dedicated to the poet Florbela Espanca. || Street art in its purest form 🖼️🎭 || A work by artist OzeArv, completed in August 2021, that blends hyperrealism with geometric shapes.  It's located between the Graça and Penha da França neighborhoods. Simply beautiful 😍 || Visionary and colorful work

They allowed the auditorium to be available for my son's school Christmas concert. Overall it was all very organized and neat. Obly problem is there's not a lot of room between rows of seats so, whenever someone needed to get up, the whole row would have to stand to let them pass. Amazing sound travel and spacious stage, one you can see clearly through all the seats. || A good venue for a wide range of different event types.  Good acoustics. || Nice place for big events || A perfectly brewed coffee, a consistently fresh pastry, and the perfect break in the heart of the Olaias metro station. Cafeteria Furtas21 is the right flavor at the right time. || Beautiful performance hall. || An event that went very well.  It's a shame there's so little space to stretch your legs between the rows. || A central venue in the city for events and conventions, the amphitheater is spacious and the seating is comfortable, but logistics are challenging and parking is difficult. There's also a small café that offers day passes! || Excellent venue for congresses and similar events. || Many excellent conditions for hosting events.

Amazing experience to do whilst you’re in Lisbon. We absolutely loved it.  We were slightly hesitant to book with the film not being one we’d typically choose, but the atmosphere made it 10x better.  The film was shown inside the courtyard of a church which added to the atmosphere. As you walk up to the church you pass the Miradouro De Graca viewpoint which was insane.  The food inside was a pizza vendor, which was so good. The bar inside had loads of options too.  We’d 100% go back again! || We knew we wanted to include a Black Cat Cinema screening during our July visit to Lisbon—and it did not disappoint! Watching Momento at Palácio Grilo made for a truly memorable evening. We arrived early and enjoyed great music and a glass of wine before the film. The setting was beautiful, the atmosphere was relaxed, and the entire experience felt like the perfect summer night in a historic Lisbon landmark. Highly recommend! || Great experience overall. Location is great and it was a fun experience. Improvements are on food alternatives and pricing: we waited a lot for the pizzas and the Brazilian sushi was expensive for the quantity of food - the promise was plenty of food options when you have just two. The sound for the movie was not great but prefer this experience rather the headphone ones. || Black cat cinema never misses. I’ve been multiple times, at different locations, and every time is a pleasure. I especially loved when Kebab Station partnered to provide their delicious pulled pork wraps.  For anyone going, I’d recommend getting there for the music, we saw Via Torta last night and they were amazing. Also, make sure to ask for a complementary blanket to borrow early on (as they can run out) at the bar, if you didn’t accurately assess how cold it’d be (especially towards the end of the films)  Overall: - arrive for the music (usually 8pm) - enjoy the beautiful venues & timeless movies - ask for a blanket early on if wearing short sleeves or shorts (and have no jumper etc) || Thank you so much Gus!!!! And we're so glad you enjoy the food from our partners and our musical guests! Can't wait to see you soon (and we'll have the blankets ready!) || We went to a Moonrise Kingdom showing and it was magical! An impromptu event we found for our first night in Lisbon and it felt like being a part of the city. The chosen place was stunning and fit the movie perfectly. We also had a delicious smash burger! It got a bit chilly because we didn’t have enough layers on, but the blankets really helped. Such a wonderful evening, thank you for the magic! || This makes us sooo happy! Thank you so much for your kind words and hope you enjoy your days in Lisbon :) || Four ladies night out to see Black Cat Cinemas showing of Lost in Translation Tuesday night at Igreja Paroquial Largo da Graça Lisboa and it was magical. Before the show began great food options, some of us had the Shawarma from LKS and others the sushi from Cultivate…Tão delicioso !! We couldn’t resist the cinnamon gelato from Chantilly. The opening began with the resonating music of Orange Moon, the perfect sounds to start the show while relaxing in comfy seats. The host was vibrant and inviting…and the show began under a open cool sky with mood lighting surrounding us, I felt like I was in a movie.. I could go on and on..it was extraordinary! I look forward to my next visits. || This review gave me GOOSEBUMPS!! I am sooo happy you gals had such a lovely night at Black Cat. Can't wait to see you all again soon :) || Beautiful open-air cinema with a truly special atmosphere! I went with my sisters on the last night of our city trip to Lisbon, and we watched Roman Holiday – the perfect ending to our vacation. Comfy seating, live music and a super friendly team. Everything was so thoughtfully arranged, with great snacks and drinks. Highly recommended! 🤍 || Thank you so much for your kind words, Sophie!! 🤍 … || I had a great time last night at Black Cat Cinema. The organisation was excellent: foods and drinks were available for purchase and they even provided blankets. || We have been following BlackCat from afar and we now live in Lisbon - booked opening night 2025!  The experience exceeded expectations and highly recommend it. Amazing venue, setup and hosts.  Great to chat with Sergio, @ImmigrantFoodie, (they introduced us to BlackCat), and enjoyed the great food, beer, and popcorn. We will be back a few more times this summer, thank you all. || Ahhh thank you so much for your words, Michael!! Can't wait to see you soon :) || Wonderful experience in Lisboa ! A nice food selection and a wonderful scenery for an outdoor cinema ! I would do it again and recommend it without a doubt to any travelers coming to the city!

Fantastic venue and accoustics. Easy to get to and well marshalled. Visited for a Nena concert which was amazing! || Great concert hall and only €5 a pint. Came to watch Happy Mondays || Sagres Campo Pequeno is very good for multi-purposes, particularly for concerts, and the organization is good in terms of entry’s. The building is very beautiful on the outside, especially at Christmas time, and is also located in the center of Lisbon with plenty of bars and restaurants around it. The only thing that is not so good, so to speak, is the seats inside which don't have much legroom, otherwise it is a good building. || Amazing place for a concert. Not too big so that is not far away from the stage but still big enough for big crowds and warm atmosphere.  The architecture is very detailed and elaborate. Very well kept too. Friendly personnel made it easy to find the spot...  Great shows. Chair are not very comfortable and the VIP area is not the best to watch the shows, especially for small people and kids that can't see the stage and the actors/ singers. || Visited Sagres Campo Pequeno in August 2024 for a Simple Minds concert. Impressive building, pretty dead during the daytime but comes alive in the evening with the bar / restaurants getting busy. You can get drinks from the restaurants but for concert goers it is better to get your drinks within the complex. Prices are not bad at around 4.50 Euro a pint (in plastic cups) Also be warned that in August it gets very very warm in there. || I wouldn’t recommend attending music concerts here. People smoke heavily inside despite the ban, and the staff ignores it. The sound quality was poor. The single cloakroom window caused a 20-minute queue, and it wasn’t free. || Attended a concert there and had a great experience. Easy to access with helpful and friendly staff on hand. There were bars in the standing area which were well staffed and easy to access during the show. Really nice venue, good beer and good sound. Can't ask for anything more then that || Nice place and really good for the variety of restaurants from sea foods , sushi and traditional Portuguese foods || Great spacs for concerts.  Good acoustics and staff. || Beautiful, historic venue in heart of Lisbon. Outside lit up for holidays. Several eateries and bars in area. Inside cozy and intimate. Some partially obstructed seats for our show, a rendition of Pink Floyd The Wall. Acoustics are excellent. All in all, just a great evening. || I like the Normal store here. The movie theatre is also nice. || Concerts at campo pequeno are ok, musicals are awful. The sound at the venue is quite bad and the seats are really uncomfortable, even if you're at the front row. || Just saw Phantom there. Loved the performance but the venue itself was subpar. I know the venue is old but the seating is very uncomfortable especially for someone tall like me. The heat and humidity were crazy especially for late October. || Very interesting place, there is a theatre and many restaurants. || Interesting concept with a mini shopping mall in the lower levels, a concert type hall in the main area  and surrounded by outdoor and indoor restaurants. Easy access to the Metro as well. || Fantastic. It's an incredible building. Standing since 1890, The bull ring has been adapted to be able to function as a theater and concert house.we saw a magnificent of Phantom of the opera. || This is a good for multi-purpose venue. However, at the end of the show we saw I don't know if people were standing up because they really liked the show or because the leg room was really tight - and I'm not tall. Maybe the expensive seats are better, but tall people need to think about getting an aisle seat! || Awesome and variety of dinning places at the venue, great Italian restaurant. All in all a great experience and enjoyable night out. || A massive building with lots of restaurants a theatre and underground shopping centre and supermarket.  Used to very a bulk ring n would loved to hv seen a theatre production there. V interesting building to just walk round the outside.

A wonderful example of a well-maintained and carefully renovated Gothic cathedral. The Sé de Lisboa dates back to 1147, with construction completed around the 13th century, making it the oldest church in Lisbon.  You can really feel the history here, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic elements shaped over centuries. It’s not overly grand or touristy, just authentic and atmospheric.  Definitely worth taking some time to visit when you’re in the city — a quiet, impressive place right in the heart of Lisbon. || Oldest church in the city (1147). Gorgeous catholic cathedral and a must visit. Very cool to be able to go up in the old choir loft  and especially outside by the large stained glass window on the front of the cathedral. There was a short line when I went on a weekday, so you may want to buy tickets in advance for a weekend, cruise ship port day, or high season. I was disappointed that the cloisters were closed when I went. || Beautiful and historic place in the heart of Alfama. The cathedral feels ancient and peaceful inside, with thick stone walls and soft light coming through the windows. I loved seeing the mix of old architecture and history all around. Even from the outside, it’s impressive — especially when the tram passes by. Definitely worth a short visit while exploring Lisbon. || The cathedral was absolutely breathtaking. There is still an admission fee, but you get a discount with the Lisboa Card, which helps. As you enter, you go up the stairs to the treasure room. On the way up, make sure to notice the carved cross on the stairs, said to have been made by Saint Anthony to repel the devil during his studies.  The artifacts in the treasure room are beautifully detailed and very well preserved. From there, you can access the interior balcony, which offers a great view of the main church below and a close look at the stunning stained glass centerpiece. There’s also a small passage leading to an exterior balcony overlooking the front of the cathedral, though it’s quite narrow and can get crowded. It’s a tight squeeze, one-way, and very high up, so just take care if you’re not great with heights.  The main cathedral itself is massive, with chapels dedicated to different saints along the back. The whole place feels grand and full of history.  Overall, an incredible experience and definitely a must-see when visiting Lisbon. || The oldest and most iconic church in Lisbon, full of history and charm. The architecture is impressive, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. Inside it’s peaceful and beautifully lit, offering a quiet break from the busy streets. Climb up to see the cloisters and enjoy the view of Alfama. A must-visit for history and architecture lovers || We took the classic yellow #28 tram and got off at the Se. The area is very cute with many great photo opportunities. We also had brunch at a sidewalk cafe in the small square right before the Se. It’s worth a visit for the views. || ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Lisbon's spiritual heavyweight champion since 1147 ⛪ Plot twist: you absolutely should go inside this magnificent cathedral, and here's the best part - it's completely free! No tickets, no queues, just walk right in like you own the place (which, in a way, we all do). The Sé de Lisboa isn't just "a church like all the churches" - it's THE church, Lisbon's oldest and most historically significant. The Romanesque fortress-like exterior might look a bit stern and businesslike, but step inside and you're hit with centuries of Portuguese history. The Gothic cloisters are genuinely stunning, and if you're lucky enough to catch evening light streaming through those rose windows, you'll understand why people have been coming here to feel something greater for nearly 900 years. The treasury and archaeological remains are worth exploring if you have time, but honestly, just sitting quietly in the main nave for a few minutes costs nothing and gives you everything. The acoustics are incredible if you catch a service or choir practice. Pro tip: Combine with a wander through Alfama afterwards - you're perfectly positioned for the neighbourhood's winding charm. Historic, free, and utterly peaceful. What's not to love? 🕊️✨ || Dear Tom, thank you for visiting, and we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience. We hope you can return one day to visit the museum and other corners of the monument. || The architecture is impressive, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. The treasury upstairs is interesting. Paintings are fabulous. The views from the top are spectacular! || Well worth the ticket price and the time to explore. Don’t miss the area upstairs where the vestments are- I’m fascinated by the detailed stitching even on the shoes! The cathedral is beautiful and there is information on its history available even if you elect not to get the audio guide. || Santa Maria Maior is the kind of place that makes you fall in love with Lisbon almost instantly. It’s the heart of the city — full of charm, history, and little surprises around every corner. Wandering through its narrow streets, you go from lively plazas to quiet alleyways, all wrapped in that classic Lisbon mix of energy and old-world beauty.  You’ve got iconic Lisbon landmarks all within a short walk — the Sé Cathedral, the viewpoints in Alfama, Praça do Comércio, and the buzzing streets of Baixa and Chiado. But what really sticks with you is the atmosphere: the tiled facades, the sound of trams passing by, and the tiny cafés where you can stop for a pastel de nata and just soak it all in.  It’s vibrant without being overwhelming, historic without feeling like a museum, and genuinely one of the best areas to explore if you want to experience Lisbon’s soul up close. || What a gem of a place that I walked into while taking the tram 28 route. Such great architecture inside the church and the tile work was very intricate and unique which truly identifies Lisbon || We went on a Saturday and they happen to be holding a mass, which was a great time to visit. The ticket counter was closed due to the mass so they were not selling tickets but allowed access. Pretty neat to see a full functioning catholic cathedral in action with all of its ornate architecture and items. || The Lisbon Cathedral is the oldest church in the city and a prominent symbol of Portugal's history, showcasing a blend of Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque architectural styles. It's free for the visit of the Cathedral but you need to pay for the museum tour. || The cathedral is a worth seeing part of the historic landmarks in Lisbon. I've been to a lot similar sights all across Europe and I can't say that it is amongst the most spectacular but it is still very interesting, also one of the oldest. It is also sometimes open to the public for free and during the weekend. || Beautiful cathedral with a long history. Also, the turn outside the church is a perfect spot to take pictures of tram 28. || This is an amazing church to check out. I would recommend paying the small entrance fee of $7 euros I believe. You get to see so much more and it is so worth it. I am always memorized by the architecture. I am not religious and I truly enjoyed this powerful place. || The Lisbon Cathedral is absolutely worth a visit. It’s one of the oldest and most important landmarks in the city, with a mix of Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles that really tell the story of Lisbon’s history. The outside is impressive, but the inside feels even more special – calm, quiet, and filled with beautiful details. If you have time, go into the cloisters as well, where you can see layers of history all in one place. It’s right in the Alfama district, so you can easily walk around the old streets after your visit. Definitely recommend stopping by, even if just for a short visit. || A must visit place in Lisbon. You can enter freely as a prayer (stopping by the entrance) or go for a ticket to explore the entire church, including the museum in the first floor and the terrace in front of the plaza. It is a wonderful mixup of different styles, from Romanic to Gothic, with several additions in the following centuries. || The tower was unfortunately closed off, so we could not go up. You can still go outside on a short passageway, just under the central stained glass window, and the views of the city is beautiful. Overall, it was worth paying the entrance fee to go upstairs, see the museum section. More information in English would be helpful for visitors who don't speak Portuguese. By pure coincidence, while visiting the church, two man started playing/practicing the organ, it was beautiful. || Exactly what we expected before coming. We can feel the power of Jesus Christ covering the church. Something reminds us of Dark Souls, the game that we played together, its inspired by ancient Europeans civilization. || Dear Daud, we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience and that it brought back fond memories. Thank you very much for your feedback.

place_name: Church of Our Lady of the Rosary of Fatima
reviews_content: I had the privilege of visiting the Church of Our Lady of the Rosary of Fatima, and it was truly a transcendent experience. The moment I stepped inside, I felt enveloped in serenity and peace.  The stunning stained-glass windows stole my heart - exquisite craftsmanship and vibrant colors that seem to dance with the light, illuminating the sacred space.  Every aspect, from the intricate architecture to the reverent ambiance, resonates deeply. This beautiful church is a testament to faith, hope, and devotion.  A must-visit sanctuary for those seeking solace, inspiration, or simply a moment of connection.🤩🌟🌟 || Church of Our Lady the Rosary of Fatima in Lisbon was consecrated in 1938. It's a mixture of modern and traditional architecture. Inside are mosaics and colorful stained glass windows. Especially the stained windows behind the choir are quite impressive, with depictions of saints and angels. The church is still in use as such, but respectful visitors are welcomed. There is no charge. reviews_content: The experience is great. The monastery is only accessible by visiting the Tile Museum.  The main church is much more beautiful and spectacular that the museum.  We only went in because we read a note saying "don't forget the church". The church has loads of tiles too. Monster Madre de Dios. Completely worth it. Museum is free with the Lisbon card || The convent—meaning Convent of the Mother of God—was founded in 1509 by Queen D. Leonor, wife of King Manuel I of Portugal. The architecture reflects a harmonious blend of Manueline, Baroque, and Mannerist styles, with the interiors showcasing exquisite gilded woodwork, classic paintings, and traditional blue-and-white azulejos. Remarkably, the convent suffered little damage during the 1755 Lisbon earthquake and remains one of the best-preserved religious buildings from that era. It functioned as a convent until the mid-20th century and was converted into the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (National Tile Museum) in 1965. Note: Many parts of the original convent, including the Igreja (church), can be visited during specific hours of the day via the museum. || The monastery is only accessible by visiting the Tile Museum.  The cloisters and main church are beautiful and worth paying the ticket price for the museum (which is also spectacular).  I have attached a couple of images of the monasteries church and upper cloister. || Very nice tile museum and church. To wait bus in weekend was little long time. || Love this place, worth the visit || Marvellous. Inside the tiles museum. Very small museum . The church was part of the convent. It deserves a visit || The convent was expanded over the centuries, with significant interventions during the reign of D. João III and baroque decorations added between the late 17th and mid-18th centuries. The convent church, known for its Portuguese baroque style, has a single nave adorned with 18th-century Dutch azulejos by Willem van der Kloet. || The Monastery of Madre de Deus, founded in 1509 by Queen Leonor, underwent several construction campaigns, notably after the 1755 earthquake, resulting in a blend of styles: Mudéjar (ceiling of Queen Leonor's chapel); Manueline (ground floor of the cloister and bell tower); Mannerist (structure of the church and cloister); Baroque (church decoration); and Revivalist (portal, second floor of the cloister, and two rooms). Its very simple façade features a striking 19th-century Neo-Manueline portal, providing lateral access to the church, which is classified as a National Monument. The interior, with a single nave, is lined with 18th-century historical tiles depicting the life of St. Francis of Assisi. The chancel and upper choir feature 16th-century paintings framed in carved wood. The National Tile Museum is located in this building. || The Mosteiro de Madre de Deus Monastery is part of the Tile Museum. We enter the monastery from the museum's first floor. The main hall is impressive, intricately crafted 😀. The amount of detail is immense. A plaque describing each element suggests that you could spend hours here familiarizing yourself with this place. Sometimes, you might come here on a school trip, where children are challenged to find some of these details on cards. If you're interested in sacred art, this part of the Tile Museum is especially for you. You can't miss it 👍. Every inch of the ceiling and walls is worth taking a look at and taking photos of. In the second, smaller hall, a film is being shown on a TV. Opposite the TV, against the wall, is a bench where you can sit and watch the film quietly. Before entering the museum, it's worth installing the official MNAz – Museu do Azulejo app 👌 on your smartphone. It's an audio guide with the ability to play the content as you please, even outside the museum. I highly recommend installing this app. It's worth getting there before opening time, as it's less crowded and allows for easy photo taking. If there's a tour after a tour, it might be difficult to take photos. reviews_content: A stunning church, from the outside it looks quite simple, but inside it’s full of gold, marble, and detailed artwork. Each chapel has unique decorations worth seeing. It’s calm and not too crowded, perfect for a quiet visit. Definitely worth stopping by. || Our private tour guide brought us here after learning that I enjoy visiting churches when we travel. He compared it to the Sistine Chapel, which seemed like a stretch—especially given how unassuming the exterior is. Honestly, it’s probably not a church I would have bothered climbing the steps to visit on my own.  Inside, however, it was a different story entirely. The painted ceiling and the opulence of the altar and artwork throughout were the most impressive of any church I visited in Portugal. The craftsmanship is extraordinary.  What made it truly special, though, was the feeling inside. There was a deep sense of goodness and calming peace that I rarely experience in many of the churches I visit. Feeling that kind of holiness is uncommon for me, which made this visit especially meaningful.  Saint Roque, the church’s namesake, is the patron saint against the plague. He devoted his life to caring for plague victims before ultimately contracting the disease himself—adding another layer of depth and reverence to this remarkable place. || One of my favorite churches while living in Lisbon. The Church of Saint Roch is incredibly well-preserved, and the gold detailing from top to bottom, especially across each of the 14 Stations of the Cross, is just breathtaking. It’s truly an amazing experience.  I 100% recommend visiting the museum too. It’s around €8, and they offer a student discount, no proof needed if you look young enough (like me!). Walking through it, you can really imagine how people back then must have felt in awe. The gold, the grandeur, it all ties in with Portugal’s historic campaigns abroad. It just makes sense.  Pro tip: Be respectful and keep quiet while inside. It’s a sacred and peaceful space. || From the outside, the Church of Saint Roch looks quite plain, but once I stepped inside I was amazed. The chapels are beautifully decorated, and the Chapel of St. John the Baptist really stood out for me with its richness and detail. It felt peaceful to walk around and just take it all in. || The Church of Saint Roch (Igreja de São Roque) is one of the most beautiful and decorative churches ever seen. The lavish Chapel of St. John the Baptist, made from precious materials, is a masterpiece of European art. This church reflects immense faith, vision, and artistic labor, making it a true gem of Lisbon’s heritage and one of the most impressive religious buildings in Portugal. || The Igreja de São Roque is special because of its stark exterior that contrasts with an incredibly ornate and lavishly decorated interior, housing what is considered one of Europe's most expensive chapels, the Chapel of St. John the Baptist. This chapel was built in Rome with precious materials like gold, marbles, and mosaics, then shipped and reassembled in Lisbon, showcasing impressive Italian Baroque art. || Very nice church, not as know as others in the city but totally worth it. reviews_content: A beautiful and tranquil church. Few visitors on a weekday in December. Time and space to appreciate wonderful monastic chanting playing in the background. You can feel here 'the breath of history on your neck'. || It was closed to the public when I visited || A very beautiful place of worship and religious service. Splendid images of Our Lady of Penha de França. I enjoyed visiting this church and attending Mass. || The Church of Our Lady of Penha de França, built on one of the highest points in the city known as Cabeço de Alperce, is one of Lisbon's most original churches. Its construction began in 1597-98. In 1601 it was given to the Augustinian hermits. Between 1625 and 1635 a new temple was built to replace the previous one. In the 18th century, the church underwent further renovations, completed in 1754, which were severely damaged by the earthquake the following year, and subsequently rebuilt with the support of the Marquis of Marialva. In the 20th century it became a parish church. The cult of Our Lady of Penha de França originated from a legend about a lizard that spread throughout Brazil and the East through Portuguese navigators. Notable features of the church include the atrium, staircase, octagonal interior, marble cladding in various colors, the altarpiece, images, and the sacristy with its 18th-century tilework. Cinema São Jorge is a beautiful, historic cinema that every film lover should have on their radar. Housed in an old building, it constantly hosts screenings and is regularly featured in film festivals and cultural events.  If you're into the film scene, this place is a must. It's super easy to get to, right by the Avenida metro station (blue line) and also well-connected by bus. It’s located right on one of the main roads in Lisbon.  The ticket booth is outside, on the left, and the staff speak English, so no worries if you're visiting. They accept both cash and card.  The theater itself is grand, spacious, and atmospheric, you really feel like you're part of something special when watching a movie here. Most foreign films come with subtitles in both English and Portuguese, and in some cases, they’ll even display subtitles on a separate bar screen if the event organizer provides them.  The only downside is the men's toilet, which feels a bit old, like something out of Harry Potter (charming for some, inconvenient for others). But that’s part of the vintage charm, I guess.  There’s also a lovely balcony on the second floor, and during some events at night, they even offer free drinks. Overall, it’s an iconic venue that mixes cinematic culture with Lisbon’s classic charm. || THE main stage of most lx film fest. The place is central and kind of iconic. || Went to a comedy show and left amazed by the venue. It preserves a lot of the original elements of the cinema including the restrooms (I did not expect to ever say this, but tres cool urinals!). And has a little balcony overlooking the avenue. || I went into this cinema accidentally and absolutely fell in love with it! Beautiful vintage  spacious cinema with multiple halls, comfortable seats. Fine bar with tap beer. I am very glad that places like this still exist. Thank you for the excellent evening of Fado music. || @dreams - ode to the Cranberries @Ti Maria @Cruzada Humano || It was wonderful... everything was meticulously planned.
