I had a lot of fun! || A very good room, which, although not very large, is excellent. Good acoustics and lighting, a great show dedicated to Saramago. || Very bad. The person in charge of opening the door arrived 1 hour and 40 minutes late. The place is completely unmanaged. Everything is chaotic. I don't know who runs this place, but whoever does should be ashamed! || A very comfortable and pleasant space. A performance venue I was unfamiliar with, but I became a fan.  I recommend it.

Uma sala de cinema que nunca deveria deixar de existir. Uma sala verdadeiramente dedicada ao cinema (I am sorry if people want to eat popcorns and they are frustrated; or wish to enter the session after it has started and they are not allowed; or feel the chairs unconfortables - they are recently designed chairs, confortable enough for the time you spend there watching a movie - they aren't couchs 'tho and they have no  extra space for drinks...). || It’s very downtown but it’s very small and the chairs, for a marathon specially (of movies) is really uncomfortable also the sound is not great  The service is amazing || Worst theater ever!  Tried to see Spike Lee’s Black Klansman, and they would not let me in.  The film was on several minutes into the showing but because they were more concerned with closing their registers they would not sell me a ticket.  I would recommend to anyone considering this cinema to consider the many other options.  Their commitment to customer satisfaction and customer service seems to be at an all time low! || Run down place and uncomfortable chairs..Incredible rude and arrogant staff..Prices not justified. No wonder nobody seems to want to go there.. || I absolutely love this independent cinema and proudly support it. It’s a unique place that always offers a rich and diverse selection of high-quality arthouse and independent films. Every visit is a true cinematic experience, showcasing original works that are often underrated but always impactful.  This cinema has soul, far removed from the impersonal feel of multiplexes. The atmosphere is warm and authentic, and the passionate staff make every screening special. If you enjoy films that break away from the mainstream, this is the place for you. Highly recommended! || Cinema Ideal is a great cinema, where we can/see find good movies, that many times are not available in those big cinemas multiplexes.. Which I dont like as usually they almost have only commercial movies. Its very causy and has a good location. The seats are quite uncomnfortable, which is a pity. And I love that its forbiden drinking and eating. If I go to the cinema is to watch quietly a movie not to eat and drink! Keep on with your exibitions!! || Great films at the city centre. || Has a small library of one of the best films of all times. || I love small cinemas with great selection of films. Plus they have some selection of movies with English subtitles- very useful! || It's a small cinema. You are not allowed to eat inside, which is a problem for a big popcorn fan like me. Also the staff only told us that after we purchased the ticket. They should at least advise people before they buy the ticket.  Also, before the movie, the queue for entering the room was huge and went around the corner.  The movies choice is good and lots of alternative movies, but in general I would not go back.

Popcorn-Lovers take care, the big bucket is unusual big, I didn’t even manage half of it as an experienced popcorn-eater. Great experience, cinema was very clean and super friendly staff! || Staff were friendly. We were in Sala 6, very well organised and clean but sound system could have been better. It was lower than expected and we could clearly hear the person talking beside and behind us, which created a problem for us to focus on the movie. || This was always my favourite mainstream cinema in Lisbon, no scratch that, anywhere!  There was nothing to fault it. Comfortable - nonsense to state there is no a/c. No sound inteference from areas outside. Faultless peojections. Good programming. Great prices. But was prompted to comment by the quick and gracious way they dealt with us not wanting to watch what we mistakenly thought was an English language film. Full marks to them! || Good cinema and convenient seats. They apparently don’t accept foreign credit card but you can buy the ticket online at cheaper price. ( 6.3€ online vs 6.6€ at box office ). There are few movies that are displayed in the original language so better check before buying. || I think this is the best place to watch a movie in Lisbon. The cinema is very comfortable, the prices are really affordable and the quality of the projection is good. Besides that, the audience behaves very well, so this is a very good extra point. || Just returned from a Sunday afternoon trip to the movies. The theater was clean, popcorn freshly prepared. Unfortunately the studio 11 where our film was showing got really warm a quarter of the way through the film even though it was nearly empty. By the end of the film I was almost in a full sweat. I did not find anyone after the movie to let them know of this condition. Also the screen had a few water marks at the top Centre which was a bit annoying. || Large selection of movies through the entire year. Food and drinks are big and expensive. || I had an inconvenience in my first attempt to watch a movie and it was so well solved. I had really a good experience. I got Yorn discount for the ticket and also for the popcorn menu. So I spent just 8€. || Some movies are not in English even though the theatre is in El Corte Ingles. “VP” is shown next to the Portuguese movies but who would know what VP is supposed to mean? Website does say “double session in Portuguese” in the description for VP but it’s not a good translation. What does double session mean? All they had to do was say “Language: __” next to the movie. The fact that all movies have the word ingles next to them is very confusing. There are very simple ways to make it clear which language the movie is shown in and they fail to do so by using random acronyms. (Edit: Changed star rating since they did refund me) || The lack of air conditioning killed the mood. Great movies, comfortable seats,  however unbearably hot during a summer night

As students of film heritage, we had access to  not just the cinemas and the museum but the documentation centre as well.  Cinemateca Portuguesa is the state institution responsible of preserving and protecting film heritage of Portugal and beyond.  It also boasts of a rooftop restaurant and a curated book and antique media shop.  It’s worth visiting! || Thank you so much, Emmanuel! || The Cinemateca Portuguesa offers not only cinema and cinematic history but also a cinematography museum, a wonderful rooftop restaurant, and an exquisitely curated book and antique media shop. || Thank you so much, Alvaro. || Went to the restaurant here, good food and friendly service. Something went wrong with our booking for 11 but they accommodated us well regardless. Really interesting building, and loads of cool film projection memorabilia everywhere. || This place is a gem! Highly recommend a visit to their cafe bar (with terrace). The staff are super helpful and the food is great. A lovely place to hang out. Apparently,  they show films outside in the Summer.  One of the most beautiful art cinemas I've been to. They've got a book shop and a quiet library.  Lots of English language films. Using proper film rather than digital.  I'll be back. || Hidden gem for film lovers. Founded in 1948 and set in a magnificently restored 19th-century building, it’s a space where moorish arches, tiled walls, and a grand staircase meet vintage projectors, rare posters, and screenings of timeless films. It feels less like stepping inside cinema’s living memory. Beyond the films, the bookshop is great with cinephile’s gems, and the café terrace “39 Degraus” is perfect for a coffee break. || Great ambience, didn’t know what to expect of it. But the food was great! And the movie was so nostalgic (high quality). || This place is heaven! There are old European and American movies playing everyday and you can get a list of them at the front desk. The museum isn’t very large, you might want to check it out while waiting for the movies. Make sure you pay a visit the bookstore! Plenty of vintage magazines in Portuguese. So precious. || That was an amazing cultural place. The building also is very beautiful. Fantastic people. Great snack bar too! || Unbelievable place! It's an old cinema in the city centre where you can feel being 60 years back and watch the old movies. Incredible experience!  They show some world classics in original language, not only Portuguese, but also French, Italian, Spanish, and of course American.  Really stunning decoration with old video cameras, old cinema chairs, and posters on the wall. Even if you don't want to see a movie, just drop by for a coffee or a cocktail in the rofttop restaurant || Thank you, Alexandra. || Nice building, the museum exhibit is small but interesting. There's a very nice terrace with great lunch deals, the food was really nice.

Nice sound and image quality. However, the seats are a bit inconfortable.  Accessible via public transportation and well-organized. Nice place overall. || What an amazing space! I frequented here for 2 weeks for DocLisboa. || I attended TEDxLisboa there and it was an amazing experience The location is very good Near transport Well maintained The team working there are very friendly and do speak several languages || This is one of the most unique buildings in Lisbon. I'd suggest visiting it at dusk or just after sunset. It's a truly majestic piece of art. || A home for culture in lisbon. Great programme of performances, music, cinema and talks. || The most elitist and dystopian but at least people that work that are really nice always.  Good cinema rooms WITH 4K and updated Dolby atmos (which rare in comercial cinemas and independent cinemas in Portugal) || Stunning modernist architecture and interior design, world class theater, sound system & performance program👌 … || Really amazing exhibition spaces and great shows! || One of the most beautiful buildings in Lisbon, it's architecture is magnificent. || Good vibe, captivating doc film festival.

Great museum that was an unexpected highlight for me in Lisbon. I went in with low expectations because puppetry is not an interest for me. But by the time I left, this museum gave me an appreciation for the artistry of puppets from across the world and across the centuries.  The museum is much larger than you might expect, which means there's lots of room for the huge amount of puppets they showcase. The displays offer excellent close-up views.  Really a lovely place that I recommend you visit. || Loved this museum. So unusual and fun! A wide range of puppets from different countries and time periods. If you're looking for something a bit different to do I'd highly recommend. We went on a weekday morning and it was nice and quiet. 5 Euro entry, which we just paid on the door. Nice gift shop, not overly priced. || Wonderful museum with tons of portuguese marionettes, including puppets and props from movies - one you can see in the museum and one is on YouTube. Seeing backstage of this art certainly adds to experience and appreciation. In addition there are many interesting collection from rest of the world: german and chinese were fascinating and there are incredible african one too. Highly recommended!!! || Titally in love with this exposition! It was the best way to leave Lisbon, I had a great time. Also, since I'm an animation student, it made the exposition 10x interesting. || Excellent museum looking at the history of puppets across different regions of the world. It has some interesting displays showing the characters used in stop motion videos and the results that can be achieved. Well worth the visit. || Totally worths a visit! A great collection of puppets from different cultures. Very well organised! We really enjoyed it! || Amazing, fascinating museum! Great place for all ages, we truly loved it! Puppets and masks are very interesting and well presented.  Also, there is interactive bit to it - you can try to move the puppets, there are memory games and colouring. Exhibition of miniatures was fantastic!!! I think my both daughters liked it the most... 😀 we couldn't believe how precisely everything was done, every little detail... Don't hesitate to visit this museum,  to us is one of the best in Lisbon! || I didn’t think that I will like it so much. It is a small but nice museum, where you can see characters from some movies, all the work behind the scenes. I was really impressed. || The puppet show was great, truly fun for the whole family- and I have a 7 month old and a 7 year old. We all were entertained. There were children of all ages in the audience. The staff at the museum was very friendly and helpful (English speaking). There's a lift entrance on the right side of the building by the way. || Amazing museum! Very entertaining and good for kids and adults! Not too long which keeps things more interesting so you can pay attention to all the details without having to spend a day there. Very good price for the tickets as well || Really fun museum collection of puppets, marionettes, and international masks.  Especially good sections about traditional puppet theater in Portugal and Mali animal masks.  Items are very well displayed.  Our visit was less than an hour.  Note that access from street level involves one flight of stairs outside and more than a flight inside.  We felt like we were the only ones in the museum on a summer Saturday. || Nice little museum with good collection of puppets from around the world. Well worth visiting. || Great museum to visit. They have very beautiful puppets with some interactive games for children. A must stop in Lisbon. In addition, it is cheap. Also, the Bulding itself is nice to visit. || Different but well worth a visit || Perfect place for both children and adults! Been there three times, also with excursion and workshop for student of my school -- Architectural Thinking School. All is just great! The collection of puppets from around the world is amazing! Bravo! || A great museum that takes you on a trip around the world. The world of puppetry in Portugal but also from far away. Mixed with stop motion and how this art is evolving. A great collection which is worth the visit || Honestly one of the best museums I’ve been to. Actually interesting and fun and comical. There are several rooms with marionettes from all over the world, as well as some interactive exhibits. The gift shop is also wonderful. || Such a cool museum! Loved seeing the diversity of puppets from around the world and learning about the history with info cards in English and Portuguese. Would have loved a little theater area with seating to see process videos and puppet shows. || Well-thought permanent exposition. Should be interesting both for kids and adults. Temporary exposition was very different (modern puppet animation) and smaller (one big hall) but no worse in any sense || If you’re a puppet nerd, don’t miss out on this one. There’s great variety of puppets from Portugal, Europe, Southeast Asia, South America, and Africa, with some videos to see them in action on actual shows. I take my time in museums and this place took me an hour and a half.

This is a stunning building. I did not find the tombs nearly as interesting as the building itself. Climbing the stairs (181 to get to the very top) was worth the effort. There are viewing balconies at each level and then you can go outside at the top and look over the city. There was an interesting display on the Mexican custom of Day of the Dead also, though I wasn’t quite sure why it was there. We had no wait to get in on a Wednesday morning. || American Traveler here. We stumbled upon this place as we were at a Saturday flea market. I thought the outside architecture was beautiful. I loved the curves and sharpness. Even on a Saturday the wait time was a little long. They only allowed a certain amount of people in at a time. The gift shop was closed at the time. Absolutely beautiful inside and if you go upstairs you have a great view of the city. A must see! || Lovely building. There are some runs of well known people. . The best views 360 degrees is you go up to around 200 steps. || Even though I have the utmost respect for this place, I cannot shake the feeling that there’s something wrong. It does honor important Portuguese figures who shouldered the foundations of the country and state next to a soccer player. Weren’t there more people to celebrate for their courage against state enemies? Artists that created lasting cultural shifts like fado (there's one)? The history of the place is where it hits home, and I recommend you read about it and visit it for its charm rather than for most of the resting souls it hosts. The terrace is also a thing, if you like stunning views of roofs and the port. || Beautiful! Heads up, if the weather is shitty you can’t go outside on the Terrence. So I would recommended buying tickets when you get there so you know if it is open or not. Still beautiful inside but same price. In November we had no line ups. || Definitely not the most interesting place in Lisbon. The rooftop area is decent, but there’s no particularly beautiful view. || This is a must see in Lisbon. Great views of the city and amazing architecture. Even if your not religious or interested in burial chambers, the views and inside of this building are beautiful. Student discount available and no waiting times || The building itself is magnificent, there are a lot of small rooms, old narrow stairs and tombs, a bit scary. But the rooftop has a great view over the Tagus river || With the Lisboa card, the entrance is free! Go straight up to the top and enjoy the view of the pantheon from the top and also view of Lisbon. || Though smaller than other national pantheons I’ve visited, Lisbon’s National Pantheon is exceptionally well-maintained and offers a distinct charm all its own. What stood out most was the integration of contemporary artistic collaborations, which breathe new life into the space without overshadowing its historical weight.  The structure itself is elegant and serene, and the modern touches serve as a powerful reminder of how history and memory continue to evolve. It’s a quiet, reflective place—less grandiose, but deeply intentional in its presentation.  A meaningful stop for those who appreciate heritage spaces that honour the past while embracing the present.

Nice market with a big selection of things to buy. Even though many people visit, it doesn’t feel too crowded, and it’s easy to walk around. Prices are quite reasonable. Worth a visit for shopping and picking up souvenirs. || Meh. Fine to stroll around to pass some time but not really worth the hype it’s given. A mix between junk which would be difficult for a tourist to take home, or tat which can be found all over the city. There are a few unique stalls, mainly the art prints and posters which were nice.  The best part was a smoothie brought from inside the permanent market area, it was really yummy and healthy. || Definitely liked the Feira da Lada; nice mix of people and the items on sale were quite diverse. Nice location in the Afalma district with some good restaurants right there. || Fun mix of art, handmade, vintage, antique, and junk - dispersed over a few streets. The building in the middle hosts amazing artist and makers - we bought beautiful one-of-a-kind sun prints and handmade soap. Great place to buy unique Lisbon gifts like canned chocolate sardines or cork accessories.  Restaurants available around the market too for lunch, coffee or drinks. || An interesting place, I think it's more for locals, just because I don't find anything useful I can take home. It's a good experience to go and explore what locals tend to buy in these kinds of places. There were a lot of antiques, books, vinyls, movies, souvenirs and many more things. || It’s a great and very big flea market in a good location, but as some other reviews have mentioned, some stalls can look very very similar so you’re not sure if you’re getting quality pieces… but if you look hard enough you can find some nice trinkets to have as a souvenir || It's nice to walk around but there's nothing you can't find cheaper in other places of the city || My husband really wanted to come to this market as it reminded him from description of the ones in London when he was in grad school that he loved.  So, we walked over from our hotel (about 25 minutes) and we were not disappointed.  This is mostly vintage and antiques but there are some vendors with ceramics, clothing, and art and handmade items.  Prices were fair and we were able to find many things to take home to friends and family as well as a few choice finds for our daughter and ourselves.  A few vendors were selling snacks and drinks inside the main building. || A great way to spend a morning… lots of vendors to look at. 4/5 because we didn’t end up finding as many desirable things as we would have liked given the size of it! || Sis and I started off super excited to check it out cause of tiktok. You feel awkward and uninvited going into the booths cause is all layed out on the ground. Barely any tables have prices, so it discourages you from asking and leaves you just looking.  Found a table with vintage mcdonalds pins. Super cute, very unique. I turn out to be pretty discouraged when at least 10 other booths have the same exact selection. The first mcdonald pin table was truly trying to tell me they were old, assuming I'm a dumb american.. Quick google search, and they're just mass-produced "vintage"..  All camera  and electronic tables have a very small sign stating just for parts.  There were really cool vintage looking lighters shaped like all sorts of things. Super unique Super cool until you see literally 10 other tables with the same variety..  Perfect place for girlies that dont have their frontal lobe yet. If i came here 10 years ago i would've bought the whole place. I'm sure there are truly vintage items lost in there, but there are a lot of suspicious "vintage" items, along with TONS of forgotten about garbage || Maybe the best flea market of Lisbon. Great setting, accomodating & chill vendors, fine variety of vintage, heirloom, & modern craft items. || Lovely market on Saturday and Tuesday! And today the weather was perfect! I love the craft shops indoor with unique earrings and necklaces! Great to support local artists. There’s also clothing shops, antiques and everything in between. || Feira da Ladra is definitely worth visiting, though if you go to it expecting quality items offered for sale, you may be disappointed. Quite a bit of what's on display falls on the side of the line denoting tawdry tat rather than quality knick-knacks, and much of it is overpriced. What's offered inside the Santa Clara Market in the middle of the flea market is much more worth looking at and buying – quality handcrafted items tastefully displayed, with home-baked goods also offered for sale.  That said, we spent an enjoyable pre-Christmas Saturday morning strolling through the market after we finally found our way there up winding streets, with three stops to ask for directions along the way. It's not an easy place to find, as one walks from the Santa Apolónia metro station uphill. || Great market with plenty of stands! Watch out as some stands are way overpriced for what it is but in general the stands were very cool. I loved the indoor market portion with food and handmade art and jewelry and other trinkets. Definitely worth a stop! || Well worthwhile if you are in the Alfamma district. The weather was very mild, sun was shining. We thoroughly enjoyed strolling through the marked. We'll layer out. We started at the top & worked our way to the end, stopping along the way for a beer. We found the prices overall to be expensive, not many bargains to be had, most prices were retail. The market has a good police presence, you feel safe. There are public toilets, 50cents, spotless. || I liked this flea market! It is actually pretty big and many people sell their stuff. There‘s always a black sheep and some people want to sell things for high prices but there are also many good people that also help you to pick something and tell you if it suits you or not.  Be sure to bring enough water and a hat, it‘s burning in the sun!  You could find good things, there are also some more professional sellers for boho style clothes. Very big! But if you like searching and looking for stuff, then you’ll love it! || Big market full of antiques and souvenirs. Prices are cheap for many items. It closes at 5p.m even on a Saturday because most of the vendors were packing at 5 and here it says it closes at 7. || The location is on the hill. We went on a Saturday and mostly got souvenirs at an affordable price. Highly recommend to buy new items -bags, jewelry, totes, and etc. Walk around first before you decide on something since you might find a cheaper price at a different store. We didn’t get any used items. Most vendors were so nice. || Ive been coming to lisbon for over 10 years and ive really seen the market change alot. There are much less antiques at the bottom of the hill, but still a fantastic trip. Make sure to say hello to Nuno, selling records near the fish mural || Market with a lot of different things; cameras, furniture, clothes, jewelry, sunglasses, food, you name it. Make sure to bring cash with you.

Miradouro de Santa Luzia is absolutely worth a visit. The views over Alfama’s rooftops and the Tagus River are genuinely beautiful, and for the price of free, you really can’t complain.  ￼  It was a bit crowded when we went, but that’s expected given how popular this spot is. Even so, it’s still a memorable place to slow down for a few minutes, take photos, and enjoy the scenery. The viewpoint itself is part of the charm too, with a small landscaped terrace, shaded areas, and classic blue-and-white azulejo panels that make it feel distinctly Lisbon.  ￼  One detail I appreciated is that the tile panels aren’t just decorative, they depict historical scenes, including Lisbon’s Praça do Comércio before the 1755 earthquake and the 1147 conquest of the castle (a cool touch if you like history).  ￼  That said, I wouldn’t call the views “to die for.” You can get comparable viewpoints nearby, and this is more of a “quick, classic Lisbon stop” than a once-in-a-lifetime moment. It’s also conveniently located in Alfama at Largo de Santa Luzia, right by the Church of Santa Luzia, making it an easy stop while exploring the neighborhood.  ￼  Overall, crowded or not, it’s still definitely worth a visit and an easy, memorable addition to a Lisbon walking day. || Miradouro de Santa Luzia offers some of the most impressive views in Lisbon. From here you can see the Alfama district and the river in a truly beautiful setting. The terrace is elegantly decorated with plants and traditional blue and white azulejos, making it even more special. It is one of those places you simply cannot miss when visiting the city. || I visited Miradouro de Santa Luzia on a rainy day and the view was absolutely worth it! One of the most beautiful viewpoints in Lisbon. charming tiles, peaceful vibes, and a perfect spot to take in the city from above.  Perched on the hills of Alfama, Lisbon’s oldest district, this viewpoint sits beside the small Igreja de Santa Luzia one of the most breathtaking views in the city. || Miradouro de Santa Luzia is pure magic. The moment you reach the terrace, Lisbon unfolds beneath you — red rooftops tumbling toward the sparkling Tagus River, narrow streets weaving through the Alfama district, and sunlight dancing on every tile. The bougainvillea and azulejos add a splash of color that feels almost unreal. It’s the kind of spot where you just want to sit, breathe, and let the city’s charm wash over you, maybe with a coffee in hand or a camera tucked away, because some moments are just for feeling, not snapping || Beautiful viewpoint. Probably the most beautiful viewpoint of lisbon. Just soak in the surroundings and immerse yourself. The tram to the hill is generally full at the base. Suggest take bolt in case you struggle to do the hike. But don't miss this point. || Miradouro de Santa luzia  Visited around 3 PM and the view was just beautiful — calm, sunny, and full of charm. You can see the red rooftops and the Tagus River stretching into the distance. I only stayed about 10 minutes, but it was completely worth it. Such a peaceful spot in the middle of Lisbon. || Miradouro de Santa Luzia is a beautiful viewpoint with stunning views over Alfama’s rooftops and the Tagus River. The terrace is very charming, with flowers, shaded areas, and traditional Portuguese tiles that add to the atmosphere. It’s a great spot for photos and a short rest while exploring the area. It can get busy with tourists, but the view and vibe make it well worth a visit || A must-see viewpoint in the city. The view is essential, overlooking the sea and the rooftops below, but it is more decorated with azulejos tiles and a very cute little square than its neighbor, Portas do Sol ... and crowded as well most of the time ! || A very lovely patio with a great view! And it is free! Could be a bit crowded but would recommend to take a visit on your way down from the castle, as the view will not disappoint you for sure! || Beautiful view — especially stunning at sunrise or sunset. The lighting is amazing, but there are usually more people at sunset.

place_name: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
reviews_content: You get a fantastic view of the historic centre of this beautiful city from here. You could stay and enjoy the well kept gardens and the views all day. There's so much to look at. Enjoy the full chaos of colours and sounds that envelope … || Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara offers one of the most beautiful panoramic views in Lisbon. The terrace overlooks the historic center, the castle, and the river, making it an ideal place to pause and take in the city’s landscape. The … || A nice panoramic view of the city center and part of the coast. It’s adjacent to a busy street and is easy to access locates at the city center. It’s very spacious there currently hosting a Christmas bazaar making it loads of festive feels. … || One of the most beautiful viewpoints in Lisbon! It offers a fantastic panoramic view over the city, especially at sunset when the light is golden. There’s a small park with benches, trees, and even a kiosk for coffee or drinks. It can get a … || We took the funicular up to this little park for the views, and it was not disappointing! The 270 degree views of the city and surrounding mountains were breathtaking. … || Great view of the City from the nearby Bairro Alto. We were fortunate to visit during the New Year's market. Excellent choice of Portuguese specialties (think serrano sandwich with sheep cheese) and Porto. || Lisbon is a city that pretends to be humble while casually seducing you at every corner. I left the house planning “just a short walk,” which, in this city, is the most unrealistic expectation you can possibly set. Five minutes in and … || Fantastic views of the city and the boats sailing past on the ocean. Plenty of food and drink stalls. || Amazing view, very nice vibe with bars and good street food around (a bit overpriced). Definitely worth checking if you're is Lisbon, specially near sunset hours. I'd recommend for couples who want a romantic vibe. || Best spot in Lisbon to stop and see the whole city. It has a dog park below and a nice spot in the back with a cat box that was tended by some retirees. Great place for photos, food, music and just relaxing. || This is one of Lisbon’s finest viewpoints, offering sweeping views over the red rooftops of Alfama and the Tagus River. Created in 1864, the viewpoint is laid out over two levels. The upper terrace features traditional Portuguese … || Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara is one of those viewpoints that instantly makes you slow down and appreciate Lisbon, especially from a Canadian tourist’s perspective. The garden setting is peaceful and well-kept, the terrace is … || Visited on June 13th during the annual festival, and the atmosphere was electric! The viewpoint was buzzing with lively stalls selling refreshing drinks and delicious fast food. While I couldn’t stay for the evening concert, the daytime … || Unbelievable view of the city and river and the castle. Best place to take in the beautiful charm of Lisboa! || Having seen amazing viewpoints all over the world, from the mountains of Greece to the fjords of New Zealand, I know a good view when I see one. Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara is a beautiful high viewpoint of Lisbon city. From here, … || An elevated terrace overlooking historic Lisbon. This large area is very popular for photos with a remarkable view. (Note that the streetcar which serviced this location experienced a tragic accident earlier in 2025. While still weighing heavily on the hearts of locals, the park is open and accessible.) || A great view which you can see all across lisbon. While we were sitting and enjoying the view there was live music which made the experience better and more relaxing. The choice of food around is good as there were plenty of bakeries around, the amount of seats were good so we didn't have to wait for sit and have some lunch. || A must see point of view if you’re visiting the city. The view is wonderful and the park is very well maintained with bench and a fountain. Highly recommended to everyone || Great spot for the sunrise and close to a couple cafe for some espresso and sweets for your reward for seeing the beautiful view of the harbor and city. || One of the best view point from this side of Lisbon. It is a wonderful mixup of different styles, from Romanic to Gothic, with several additions in the following centuries. || The tower was unfortunately closed off, so we could not go up. You can still go outside on a short passageway, just under the central stained glass window, and the views of the city is beautiful. Overall, it was worth paying the entrance fee to go upstairs, see the museum section. More information in English would be helpful for visitors who don't speak Portuguese. By pure coincidence, while visiting the church, two man started playing/practicing the organ, it was beautiful. || Exactly what we expected before coming. We can feel the power of Jesus Christ covering the church. Something reminds us of Dark Souls, the game that we played together, its inspired by ancient Europeans civilization. || Dear Daud, we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience and that it brought back fond memories. Thank you very much for your feedback.

The viewpoint at Parque Eduardo VII offers a wide, open panorama over the city, stretching from the park’s geometric gardens down to Avenida da Liberdade and the river. It’s a peaceful spot, especially in the early morning or late afternoon, and the elevated position gives a great sense of Lisbon’s layout.  The area around the viewpoint is spacious and easy to access, though not as atmospheric as some of the older miradouros in the historic districts. Still, it’s a worthwhile stop if you’re already exploring the park or want a less crowded viewpoint with a clear, unobstructed city view. || Great location and view,  plenty of seating spaces too.  Great scenic view of the city and theres a handy cicktsil bar on hand where ypu can relax in a bit of style and comfort,  failing that there is an icecream stall too,  the hike from the river front can be a bit daunting at tines but worth the climb || A peaceful spot with views over Lisbon. Perfect for photos or just relaxing in the sun. The walk up is easy, and the park itself is well-kept. Best visited at sunset for amazing colors and a calm atmosphere. || Some peace and tranquility from the city hustle & bustle! Theres a sweet high spot where u can take photos of the city touching the sea with the LISBOA sign. Get here early to avoid the crowds as they wanna get images etc. || Perfect View of Lisbon!!! Very nice place and quite romantic as you walk through the parc! || Worth the walk and it is very beautiful. I hear it is even better in the spring with the florals. The Lisboa sign is here too, much less crowded than other areas. || Great observation deck with beautiful views over the city and the river. A nice place to relax and enjoy the scenery. || I was looking for a spot to do a bit of jogging and ended up here. The area has a nice elevation, perfect for a more engaging run, and I wasn’t the only one enjoying it — there were other joggers, a few tourists, and locals relaxing in the garden with their dogs. The combination of activity and friendly atmosphere gave the place a warm and welcoming touch. || Very nice place, nice walk too. Good for picnics and watching a majestic view || Awesome view- both sunset and sunrise are amazing- great place to visit at any time of the day. || Large open area at the top of the park with view all the way to the river. Also a monument to the Lisbon earthquake. Well worth the walk for the view. If walking up from Restauradores you can stroll Av da Liberdade and window shop all the high end stores on the way || The view is nothing but speculation! Super easy to come here; either the blue or yellow metro line is fine. Sometimes there is live music, it fits with the chill vibes here. With a clear sky, one can spot some of the main historical landmarks of Lisboa over this observation point. || This location offers a spectacular vista for all to enjoy.  The park grounds are well-maintained and inviting.  There's always something happening, with events scheduled throughout the year.  A literary celebration is commencing soon, promising a delightful experience. It's a wonderful place to spend an afternoon. || What a great hidden gem in Lisbon. The views from this spot is gorgeous and the city down there can be seen from above in a clear day. It is a bit far from the main attractions, but I totally recommend coming here if you have time. || Beautiful view of Lisbon. We had coffee in the terrace of El Corte Inglés then had a short walk to the Mirador. || Beautiful place. Perfect for a break in your exhausting sightseeing schedule. Features great views over a park, the city, and the river in the distance. Seems to be not only for the tourists, but also the locals. || A beautiful water fountain and garden viewpoint on the top of the hill at Lisbon.   The fountain looks like a ruin but it's what the designer wanted it to look.   The garden is well manicured and beautiful.   Overall, a good experience. || A nice observation platform adjacent to monuments with an expansive view of a huge park and far away water body.  You can get a photo with Lisboa sign. || Its a great view and a fantastic walk from top of the park and all the way straight down to the river . || Beautiful vista point to the city With gorgeous landscape!!!

We were in Lisbon for a few days before our cruise so we signed up for a walking tour of Alfama. The guide pointed out lots of history in this square and all around  Alfama.  We saw the Fado museum, the Jewish Quarter, quaint narrow streets and the old lady selling cherry alcohol in chocolate cups. All educational and lots of fun.  A must see area of Lisbon. || Lovely Spot for Breakfast with Great Service and Local Tours  A great place to sit down and enjoy breakfast — the service is excellent, and the atmosphere is relaxed with many tourists passing by. The area feels very safe and welcoming.  You can also catch a ride with tour buggies, which are parked nearby throughout the day and available for hire. The going rate is £100 for a 2-hour tour, making it a convenient spot to start your adventure. As we waited only for one day it was great option to visit all tourist places and take photos using buggy. || Very nice place day and night time. Can hear the fado in the street. Very romantic place. || Interesting place,historical Old part of Lisbon || This place is like a great gate to the old town of Lisbon with loads of cute tiny streets going up and down and gazillion of restaurants. Have some cash with you as some places don’t accept cards or only over €10 and make sure your camera is on 100% because you won’t be able to stop taking pictures 📸 … || Nice square. I love the grand mother sale the chocolate cup with cherry alcohol. 1€50 the cup. After small streat is so cute || We stayed near this square in a lovely AirBnB. Everyday we'd walk through this square on our way to see some more of Lisbon. Really cute square with some horse-head fountains. There's a few restaurants on either end and some locals selling wine as well. Usually saw a few tuk-tuks for rent near the street across from the Museu de Fado. || Your photo with the bike is not in Largo do Chafariz de Dentro! Stop misleading people || A lovely place to relax and enjoy a drink or two, lovely vibes..cocktail was €15, there iseating & drinking in it, made with Portugues rum, the inside of the pineapple & coconut cream... || Reminds me of alfalfa from penacony || Small square with antique romantic flavour || We visited the Castelo de S Jorge, then walked through the Alfama neighborhood on our way down to this square. I'd recommend that walk to everyone as there are many beautiful spots along the way. The square itself is quite pretty. It  was busy with people, and many great restaurants. || Another nice square to walk by during Alfama exploration || A bit small but I can confirm for the churros. Took the local Portuguese version and it was worth it! Highly recommend. || Authentic to the Lisbon culture and experience. Excellent food and wine.  Excellent Fado. Friendly neighbors. || Alfama is an old neighborhood and you will find lot of nice ppl walking its norrow streets. It is full of story. Be ready for the stairs hahahaha I loved it || Absolutely beautiful! Try to enjoy a shot of ginja in a chocolate cup! || Love tboz pmace and this region. Best place in Lisbon. Come here for  great experience || It is winter, so it was not as busy and filled with life. But we enjoyed the sun across from the Fado museum. || Small square with restaurants and coffee shops. || Only 2 stars?? What a ridiculous person you are! || Pretty underwhelming after seeing so much beauty in Lisbon. I’d keep it low on the list for your day.

Just a view point, good to capture cruise ships. There is a small bar and seating nr road. || It's an amazing view over Lisbon.  The square is lined with trees.  You can walk or get the tram up here.  This is a good stop off if you're walking up to the castle.  Follow here and on IG for more travel and food and drink tips, ideas and reviews @one.more.step.along.the.world || It’s amazing at 6Am very Calm Relax Lisbon view || Amazing view over Lisbon || Great viewpoint.  Lots of local people hanging out. || Smoke one right there || This is in front of the tram stop for tram number 28. It's easy to spot, as many people get off here first. The most common route is to get off here and then walk up and down the steep slopes of Sao Jorge and Alfama. The area is dotted with restaurants, cafes, and souvenir shops. || A beautiful place with a lovely view, especially at sunset. || Nice views and photo spot. || There is a beautiful view from this point. || Beautiful viewpoint over Alfama, Tram 28 and the cozy square with terraces with beautiful plants and trees.

Amazing experience to see the city Scape of Lisbon. You can go up by lift and then down by the stairs that's on the side near the church. Less crowded in the morning, passed through it in the afternoon and there was a huge line. || ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Tourist trap? Yes. Still worth it? Also yes (with conditions) 🛗  Let's be honest - Santa Justa Lift is absolutely crawling with tourists and you'll pay premium prices for what is essentially a very slow, very ornate elevator ride. But here's the thing: it's genuinely beautiful neo-Gothic ironwork, and those views from the top are properly spectacular. Sometimes tourist attractions become tourist attractions for good reason!  That said, here's your insider move: skip the lift queue entirely and take the stairs from Rua do Carmo. It's a surprisingly easy walk up through Carmo ruins area, costs nothing, gives you a decent leg stretch, and you'll still get those same panoramic views over Baixa and the river. Plus you'll feel smugly superior watching the queues below while you're already up there sipping coffee.  The lift itself is undeniably charming if you appreciate 19th-century engineering, and it does connect Baixa to Bairro Alto efficiently. Just don't expect it to be a hidden gem - embrace the tourist experience or take the stairs like a savvy local.  Either way, those views are absolutely worth it! 📸✨ || Took the side street and got amazing views of the city. Spare the tourist trap of taking the lift and walk the stairs to the top for this amazing views of the city. Recommended to go during sunset. || Worth a stop.  Only €6 to ride the lift, which is really a fun piece of history. Sure, it's a little slow but a fun experience.  If you don't want to pay, just keep walking, you will find the top.  If you do pay the lift, then you can go to the very top by stairs which has some even better views. || The elevator is a tourist trap that you'll pay over 6 € but you can climb the stairs for free or go to the old church for the same view ... The elevator was created to facilitate access between the Baixa and Bairro Alto districts. At the time, it was considered one of the most modern elevators of its era. Designed by the Portuguese engineer Raoul Mesnier du Ponsard, a disciple of Gustave Eiffel, which metal structure is reminiscent of the beloved Eiffel Tower ... || Go early in the morning or close to sunset to avoid long lines. Once you’re at the top, the view over the city and the Tagus River is breathtaking. You can also access the viewpoint from a nearby street without paying for the lift, if you’re just after the view. || The Santa Justa Lift is one of Lisbon’s most iconic landmarks — a striking neo-Gothic iron elevator that connects the lower Baixa district to the higher Largo do Carmo. Built in 1902 by a student of Gustave Eiffel, it showcases elegant metalwork and stunning views from the top terrace. The short ride itself is a charming glimpse into Lisbon’s history, but the real reward is the panoramic view over the city’s rooftops, the Tagus River, and São Jorge Castle. Especially beautiful at sunset, the Santa Justa Lift is both a functional piece of engineering and a romantic symbol of old Lisbon. || Very long queues to then get to the overcrowded top floor. There's another way to get there, a 5 minute walk around the elevator to the left, then right up some steps and there you get an even better view - open, as it's unobstructed. Better for photos too as there are less people in the way. Going this way gets 5 stars, the elevator the just the two. || It is ok for the view point but it is worth the wait or money, not so sure. But it is cool to ride the old elevator just money and time could be better spent elsewhere. It is always lined up. I wouldn’t do again especially going to other view points in the city that are better views. || Actually I did not take the lift, but I was at the upper level. I heard that the Santa Justa Lift free view was almost as good as the paid view, so I just stayed where I was instead of gong to the upper viewing platform (the stairs were closed off). I had to put my phone between the bars to get good photos, holding on tight in the wind, so be careful! All around there were great views so worth a quick visit! || During my visit, to Santa Justa Lift was unfortunately out of service, which was quite disappointing since I had really looked forward to experiencing the famous view from the top. However, the surrounding area made up for it  full of charm, energy, and plenty of great shops to explore. Even though I missed the ride itself, spending time in that part of the city still turned into a pleasant experience. I’d definitely love to come back once the lift is working again! || Super OLD & extremely SLOW wooden elevator going up about 5-6 floors :) The wait was long, because it was so slow.  I wanted to take the elevator after sundown for the cool atmosphere and amazing night view!! Visit during the day, under scorching sun wouldn’t have been a great experience in my opinion.  No ticket needed with Lisboa Card, which was a plus. I don’t think i would have gone for the ride if I had to pay 5euros. || It’s one of Lisbon’s most iconic landmarks and definitely worth a visit. The historic iron lift, with its beautiful neo-Gothic design, is both charming and impressive. The ride to the top is short but fun, and the viewing platform offers stunning panoramic views over the city, including Rossio Square, the castle, and the river. || Not worth it at all. Introductions on how to get passes is not clear at all. It made it sound like you got them in line. The sign at the entrance to the line says they take card only. There are card machines at the entrance to the lift but then the workers there state that they will only take cash. To get to the level that the lift takes you, you can actually walk up to for free from The other side. Once you get off the lift, you can pay to climb stairs to go to the next level and then pay again to get to the top. If you are able, just walk around to the other side and get to the view from the street. There are so many amazing views around Lisbon that you can get to by walking, tram or rickshaw. Don’t pay for this || Very long queues and poor organization, with only one staff member managing both the ascent and descent, which causes frustrating delays. The ticket price is €6.10 for a very short ride, and unfortunately the experience doesn’t quite match the cost. At the top, there are metal safety grilles all around, which completely block the possibility of taking clear, unobstructed photos of the view. While the architecture of the lift itself is beautiful and historic, the overall visit feels disappointing and not worth the long wait. || It’s free to if you Lisboa Card. There are lots of people lining up for the lift up in the afternoon. I went there in the morning when there were just around 6 people ahead of me. After going up, you could enjoy the beautiful views of Lisbon and Elevador da Bica funicular was not far away. || In my humble opinion, this is only worth it if you have a day pass or the Lisbon card, otherwise absolutely not worth the single ticket price. Long queues for a 30 second ride up in the elevator and some views of the city that you can have for free in other parts of the city. They are not even that great anyway, there are better points. || Long queues but the due to the funicular crash it is currently closed. Looks a bit glitchy though. Also you’re only paying for the elevator ride you can access the viewing platform from the back with a bridge for free when it’s open. || It’s a nice construction with quaint interiors of the lift. It is free for Navegante card members till the first viewing point. And then charged 5 Euros. I think first level is good enough. Exits on the other side to the museum. It’s a worthwhile visit || If you’re paying €6 to go up, you’re basically falling for marketing. From the other side (next to the Carmo Convent, which you’ll likely visit anyway), the entrance is free. The top is extremely crowded and honestly unpleasant, but at least if you want to check it out, do it for free.  As for the architecture — yes, the lift itself is unique and looks beautiful. But paying just to go up? That’s simply foolish.

place_name: Chafariz da Rua de O Século
reviews_content: Lisbon Story Centre is an excellent place to understand the history of Lisbon and Portugal. The staff were super helpful and welcoming from the start.  You are provided with headphones in your preferred language, and each interactive segment clearly explains different phases of Lisbon’s history in a very engaging way.  This is honestly one of the best ways to learn about Lisbon, especially if you’re visiting for the first time.  The storytelling, visuals, and audio guides make history easy to follow and enjoyable. A big bonus is that it’s free with the Lisboa Card, which makes it even more worth visiting.  The museum also has clean washrooms inside, which is very convenient. Overall, it’s a must-visit museum for first-time visitors and history lovers.  Highly recommended! || It was really interesting to hear all those great stories about Lisbon’s history. The tour was truly informative; however, clearer instructions could have been given about the audio guide. It was an automatic system, meaning that as we walked into different rooms, the guide would start explaining the story. The problem was that sometimes the audio began in the middle, causing some information to be missed. || We returned to Lisbon Story Centre at about 2pm where the crowd had more or less subsided. Here, we found that there was a need for crowd control because of the audio guide through the gallery. The audio guide is a very cool device. When you enter a certain section, it will trigger the audio to start for that particular section as you listen and see the exhibits. Probably RFID activated if we were to hazard a guess. This is also why the staff emphasised that we should not touch anything on the audio guide, maybe perhaps for the volume because everything is played automatically. The length of the audio is also fixed. This is also why, unlike a museum where you can skip exhibits, the guide leads you through each section with...  For the full review and details of our 5 months Round The World RTW travels, visit 2bearbear today! || Very interesting to hear the history of Lisbon. It was an audio guided tour and I loved the story telling aspect of it. The museum is quite small but provides a good atmosphere to set the history. With great visuals and designs, it provided a deeply emotional and exciting view of the history of Lisbon. Would recommend to tourists || If you are interested in history, this is the place. The exhibit is easy to follow with video projections to the props, which made you feel like you are brought back in time. It is not boring! It’s right at the square and has a nice cafe outside to have a light bite and cold imperial beers. || Great place to go and become educated on the history of Lisbon. The headsets are included in the entry fee and trigger automatically as you walk through the exhibits. No need to fiddle with controls etc. I found the exhibits interesting and the audio was clear and on point. Recommend you buy tickets in advance online to speed entry at peak times. || With the Lisboa card, the entrance is free. 40minutes are max to see around and learn the history. Open on Mondays. || This place should be on your list when visiting Lisbon. They have only audio guides but good triggers based on your position in the centre. It starts playing when you move. Entire exposition is interactive with sound, video, pictures, earthquake, and smells. Really, vanilla, cocoa, and other smells during the trading part of the exhibition. Come, explore Lisbon history. || The earthquake thing was fun. Probably don’t take your little kid in it there was a toddler in it when I was and that lil dude was freaked out. I’d rate it higher but there were several mentions of “discoveries” that were definitely places other people already lived. It was pretty uncritical for what’s mostly a history museum. But hey I guess it calls itself a story centers so it’s not dishonest about what it is. || Mildly interesting very small museum about the history of Lisbon. Worth having a look if you’re in the area but otherwise not worth travelling for. If you can get a discounted ticket do so as it doesn’t feel worth the ticket price.

During my recent visit to Lisbon, I had the pleasure of exploring the Chafariz das Necessidades, an enchanting historical site nestled in the heart of the city. As I stepped into the meticulously landscaped gardens surrounding the fountain, I was immediately captivated by the serene ambiance and the sense of tranquility that enveloped the area.  The Chafariz das Necessidades, dating back to the 18th century, boasts stunning Baroque architecture and intricate detailing, making it a true gem of Lisbon's cultural heritage. The central fountain, adorned with ornate sculptures and cascading water features, served as a picturesque focal point amidst the lush greenery and vibrant flowers that adorned the gardens.  Exploring the grounds, I couldn't help but feel transported back in time, imagining the aristocrats and nobles who once strolled through these very gardens centuries ago. The meticulously manicured pathways led me through a captivating array of flora, from vibrant azaleas to towering palm trees, creating a delightful sensory experience at every turn.  One of the highlights of my visit was ascending the grand staircase to the upper terrace, where I was treated to breathtaking panoramic views of Lisbon's skyline and the Tagus River beyond. It was the perfect spot to pause and soak in the beauty of the city, while reflecting on the rich history and cultural significance of this remarkable landmark.  Overall, my visit to the Chafariz das Necessidades was a truly memorable experience, offering a delightful blend of history, art, and natural beauty. Whether you're a history buff, a nature enthusiast, or simply seeking a peaceful retreat from the hustle and bustle of city life, this hidden gem is not to be missed during your time in Lisbon. || At the heart of the garden lies the Chafariz das Necessidades, an ornate fountain commissioned by King João V in 1747. This baroque masterpiece features a central obelisk surrounded by sculptures of dolphins and sea creatures, creating a captivating focal point. || I have visited there at night and no water in fountain.  Need more maintenance. Historic place. || Cute spot with a lookout towards the bridge. Interesting museum across the road too; pretty building. || Chafariz das Necessidades is a very beautiful water fountain in a park right in front of a government building. Is empty and it looks like it's a little rundown || Great spot for sunset || A viewpoint, with hidden a park. || Located in Largo das Necessidades, in front of the Palace of the same name, this fountain stands in the center of the Olavo Bilac Garden, named after the Brazilian writer and poet born in 1865.  It dates from 1747 and is part of the Palace complex, having resulted from a vow made by King João V to the Virgin Mary.  Its authorship is attributed to the architect Caetano Tomás de Sousa, author of the execution project of the Palace.  In the middle of a tank that receives water from four gargoyles of Baroque inspiration, rises an obelisk topped by a bronze cross that crowns a monstrance of thorns that accentuates the religious character of the monument.

Superb panoramic view of Lisbon with a very chill bar and nice people to share the view with || Not exactly what I expected... We’re really glad to hear you found our team welcoming. We’re sorry that the space didn’t fully meet your expectations regarding quiet areas and layout.
