We can’t wait to welcome you back for another great visit! … || Went in for a coffee and some pastries and was pleasantly surprised. Iced caramel latte was nice, pastries were amazing and the staff were very nice.  Prices are on the high side, but not uncommon for a nice looking brunch spot. Speaking off, the decoration is simple yet very tasteful and bright, the place is roomy and fresh even on a hot summer day. You can see behind the scenes into the kitchen (and some places used for storage that could probably be hidden).  The variety of pastries is unbelievable and they all look delicious. Overall, excellent place. || Hello Filipe,  Thank you so much for your thoughtful review! We’re delighted to hear you enjoyed the iced caramel latte, our pastries, and the atmosphere of the space. It’s great to know that the staff made a positive impression as well!  We also appreciate your feedback on the pricing – we aim to offer quality and experience, and we’re glad to hear it was worth it for you. As for the behind-the-scenes view, we’ll take note of your suggestion about storage areas to ensure everything is presented in the best way possible.  We’re thrilled to know you had a great time and look forward to welcoming you back soon for another round of delicious treats!  Best regards :) || This became one of our favourite breakfast spots while staying in Lisbon as it was close to our hotel. The staff were accommodating, easy to talk to and attentive. Food was very tasty with a vast menu. Coffee was 👌. Would recommend. || Hi Mrstruan1,  Thank you so much for your lovely words! We’re thrilled to hear we became one of your favorite breakfast spots during your stay in Lisbon. It’s great to know you enjoyed the food, coffee, and service — we’d be delighted to welcome you back anytime! || My partner brought me here on my birthday last week, since it’s one of her favourite pastry cafés — and she was absolutely right!  The pastry selection was so tempting I wanted to try at least four at once 🫠. I also went for the salted coconut iced latte, which was a completely new (and delicious) experience.  The staff were friendly, welcoming, and made the visit feel even more special. I’m already looking forward to coming back for more pastries and food. Highly recommend. || Hi Inga,  Thank you so much for celebrating your birthday with us! 🎉 We’re delighted you enjoyed the pastries and the salted coconut iced latte — it’s wonderful to hear it made your visit extra memorable. Our team will be very happy to know they helped make your day special. We look forward to welcoming you back soon for more pastries and good moments! :) || Best place in the neighborhood 💓 good coffe, delicious eggs and THE FRENCH TOAST is just the best. Caterina attended us the two days we went and she’s just the sweetest ✨ || Hi Maria,  Thank you so much for your lovely words! 💓 We’re thrilled you enjoyed the coffee, eggs and especially the French toast. Catarina will be so happy to know she made your visits even sweeter ✨ We can’t wait to welcome you back again soon! || DoBeco was definitely our favorite brunch spot in Lisbon. The food was great, the staff was friendly and helpful and the interior was very much aesthetically pleasing. I had the Egg & House-cured bacon bun, without the spicy honey. It was great. Not too heavy, not too light. The bacon was perfect. A little dry overall but still amazing. The matcha I had with this bun was also great :) My boyfriend had a DoBeco plate, he chose the tornado omlette. Every single ingredient in the plate tasted extremely high-quality, from the home-made jam to the wonderful artisanal ham. Pao de Deus matched the quality of the rest of the food. The lemonade he had with it was sour to his enjoyment, very refreshing. We also got some sourdough bread to take home. We used it for sanwiches later and we are convinced that it was some of the best bread we have ever had. || Hello Sasha!  Wow, thank you so much for such a thoughtful and detailed review! We’re absolutely delighted to hear that DoBeco was your favorite brunch spot in Lisbon — that truly means a lot to us.  It’s great to know you both enjoyed your meals so much. From the Egg & House-cured bacon bun to the DoBeco Plate with the tornado omelette — we're glad each element left a strong impression. And we’re extra happy to hear the sourdough bread made its way home and continued to bring joy at your table!  Thank you for taking the time to share your experience with us. We can’t wait to welcome you back next time you’re in Lisbon!  Warm regards :) || Had a great time at Do Beco Santos! The vibe is super nice and the service was excellent. Special thanks to Catarina – she was super friendly and really made the experience even better. Definitely recommend! || Hello Anne,  Thank you so much for your kind words! We’re delighted you enjoyed the vibe and service at Do Beco Santos. Catarina will be so happy to know she made your experience even better 🌟 We truly appreciate your recommendation and look forward to welcoming you back soon! || Superb pastries and nice coffee. The service was a bit hurried and a few mistakes happened - nothing major but forgetting a dish here and there. The main restaurant area is quite echo-y and can feel loud. Kids loved watching pastries being made right in front of them!  Would still recommend for a more upmarket coffee break! || Hello Jaana,  Thank you so much for the lovely review! We’re thrilled that you and your kids enjoyed our pastries and coffee. It's great to hear that the kids had fun watching the pastries being made – we love sharing that behind-the-scenes experience!  We also appreciate your feedback on the service and the atmosphere. We’re sorry for any small mistakes and will be sure to work on improving the flow of service to avoid any oversights. As for the acoustics, we’re looking into ways to make the space more comfortable for everyone.  Thanks again for the recommendation! We look forward to welcoming you back for another coffee break soon.  Best regards :) || Delicious and beautiful restaurant. All made in house and sooo yummy! || Hello Isaac,  Thank you so much! 😊 We’re thrilled you enjoyed the food and the restaurant. Everything is made in-house with love, and we can’t wait to welcome you back soon. … || Amazing brunch place. The turkish eggs are delicious and the view into the bakery a nice little plus for the ambiente. Good bakery/coffee place || Hi Michael,  Thank you so much for your kind words! We’re delighted you enjoyed the Turkish eggs and the cozy view into our bakery. It’s wonderful to hear you also appreciated the coffee and atmosphere. We hope to welcome you back soon for another brunch! || We had been to their other cafe in another area and stopped by this one, it was just as good as first one. We will be back 💯 || Hi Shan,  Thank you so much for coming back to visit us! 🌟 We’re thrilled to hear you enjoyed this location as much as the other one. We can’t wait to welcome you again soon! … || What the hell is this place Im not the kind of person to write reviews but like what the hell… the food and service was awful. The place it self looks cute/ pastries are nice/ coffee is nice but the food….. bland no flavour lowkey made our tummy unhappy and we were 5.  Took them 30 minutes to bring us a solid coffee and didn’t bring us the 2nd water that we ordered.  Really bad service. I get working in hospitality can be a pain… customers can be rude/ working lots of hours/ maybe having a bad day. God I know.  But genuinely everyone looked like they didn’t want to be there. Are they trying to ruin this business??  I’m not hating or trying to hurt anyone’s feelings but this place needs some proper managing.  Like I said pastries and coffee amazing. Food and service awful. || Hi Natasha,  Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback. We’re truly sorry to hear that your experience with the food and service didn’t meet your expectations — we take comments like these very seriously. We appreciate your understanding of the challenges in hospitality, and we’ll be reviewing our service and kitchen processes to ensure a smoother experience for all our guests.  We’re glad to hear you enjoyed the pastries and coffee, and we hope you might consider giving us another chance in the future to provide the quality of service and food we strive for. || I’ve been to this cafe several times since I live nearby. The bread is great! Pastries are okay and a tiny bit overpriced (but that's just my opinion, I obv don't know their costs). The service really depends on the day...Sometimes they’re nice, other times it feels like they’re annoyed you’re there, especially when you sit inside.  Today was the first time I got a coffee, though. €3.50 for a lukewarm small batch brew.  That's not OK. I mean stuff happens, but man, you know you brew it hours ago, you still decide to serve it...and then you do not even check the temp before doing so.  I don't know...I feel like the price–quality ratio is off but I kept on going back, as I was hoping that the mediocre experiences I had, were exceptions. But after today I am giving up, plenty of other great bakeries/cafes around. || Hi Leelo,  Thank you for taking the time to share your detailed feedback. We’re glad to hear you enjoy our bread, and we truly appreciate your honesty regarding pastries, coffee, and service. We understand your concerns about the coffee temperature and the overall price–quality perception — this is something we take seriously and will review internally.  We haven't experienced issues with the temperature of our batch brew before, our thermoses are designed to maintain it properly, and this hasn''t been a recurring concern for our guests.  if this had been mentioned during your visit, we should have gladly suggested an alternative that better suited your preferences.  Regarding the seating, we don’t have an outdoor space, which can sometimes make the flow and seating arrangements confusing, especially on busy days. We’re sorry this added to your frustration. Your feedback is very valuable to us and will help us improve. We hope you might consider giving us another chance in the future. || I really loved this place! We have something similar in Porto—Bicho—with great pastries, excellent coffee, and great service.  The people at the nearby tables were having such a good time enjoying their Saturday brunch—I love that weekend buzz of conversations and laughter.  Such a great atmosphere! || Thank you so much, Alyona!  We're so happy you had a good experience with us :)  We look forward to your next visit! || Great place. The quality of the beverages and food is outstanding. The service is very friendly and efficient. This is a true bakery. We were concerned with the high amount of reviews for such a new place but decided to give it a try. It was away beyond our expectations. We selected a simple choice: cappuccino with bread and butter. The perfect classic. The detox juice was super tasty. We are definitely going back soon. || Thank you so much for the review, E M!  We're thrilled you had a great experience :D  And thank you for the photos.  See you soon!

They’re all over Lisbon, and if you can’t make it to Pastéis de Belém in the Belém district, this bakery is a great alternative for enjoying the famous pastel de nata. The crust was flaky and perfectly complemented the soft, creamy custard filling.  We ended up buying several boxes to take home with us, and they made great gifts. Convenient, delicious, and a solid option when you’re craving a classic Portuguese treat. || The egg tarts were one of the best we had in Lisbon! You can even see the workers making the tarts which was very cool to see. The only issue is that this location doesn’t have much space to stand. But it is worth it since the pastel de natas are soo good || Hi Saloni. Thank you for your feedback. We would be delighted to welcome you to Manteigaria in Rua Augusta, Time Out Market, Alvalade, Belém, Campo de Ourique, Parque das Nações and Saldanha where you can sit and enjoy the pastel de nata on the terrace. We look forward to see you again soon. || Hands down, the best pastel de nata I’ve ever tried in Lisbon! It’s different from the egg tarts I’m used to from Asia, but the custard here is incredibly fresh, creamy, and perfectly balanced. The crust is delightfully crispy, and I love that you can sprinkle cinnamon powder on top or enjoy it as is—both ways are amazing! This is an absolute must-try spot for anyone visiting Lisbon. Highly recommend! || The best Paste de Nata in the whole Lisbon. The bakery is very tiny, but such a mesmerizing. You can watch the pastry chefs prepare these desserts live. The staff is very polite and pleasant – your mood is lifted after visiting. I definitely recommend it. || Really great, rich, custard filling. Could eat it all day. Unfortunately the crust was a bit soft and lacked any crunch.  Really convenient and cute place to stand at the counter and observe the magic happen from being the glass. || Hi Rui. Thank you for your feedback and we're sorry about what happened. Our customers' feedback is very important to us so that we can continually improve our service and provide unique experiences.  We look forward to seeing you again soon. || Such good Pan de Nata! Queue moves super fast, staff is friendly, card payment, practical packaging and multiple presentations (1 pan, 2, 6, etc). Price is €1.50 per Pan, they also have coffee, lemonade, etc. No place to seat, so 100% take away. || Title: Good in Small Doses  Manteigaria is one of those places you *have* to try in Lisbon, and yes—the pastel de nata lives up to the hype… but only to a point. The first one or two are lovely: crisp shell, creamy custard, that iconic warm comfort. But if you overindulge, the charm starts slipping. The more you pay attention to the flavor details, the more it shifts from “wow” to “hmm, maybe not as magical as I thought.”  Coffee was fine, nothing to write home about. I also tried their glühwein, which turned out both pricey and un-drinkable—one sip was more than enough.  The setup is convenient, though. They’ve got a stand where you can grab a pastel on the spot (probably the best way to enjoy it—fresh, hot, and fleeting), or place an order to take away.  Overall: worth trying, especially if you’re in Chiado/Baixa and want that Lisbon pastry experience. Just don’t get carried away—sometimes less really is more. || Hi Manja. We appreciate your feedback and visit. We hope to see you again soon. || Lovely pastel de nata — very creamy and delicious! Definitely worth the hype. As December is off-peak, I assumed there wouldn’t be a queue, but there was one. That said, it moved quickly and there was no real wait time; you go in and they serve you straight away. || Manteigaria is truly a temple of the famous Portuguese pastel de nata, and it’s easy to see why it’s a must-visit in Lisbon. The moment you step in, you’re greeted by the aroma of freshly baked custard tarts wafting from the open kitchen, where trays of golden-brown pastries are pulled straight from the ovens.  The pastel de nata here is perfection — warm, flaky, and buttery on the outside, with a silky custard that’s rich and just the right amount of sweet. The slight caramelized top adds a beautiful touch of bitterness that balances every bite. A light dusting of cinnamon and powdered sugar takes it to another level.  Watching the bakers at work behind the glass and seeing trays of these beauties coming out of the oven makes the experience even more special. The staff are friendly and efficient, ensuring everyone gets their tart fresh and hot.  Whether you’re grabbing one to go or standing at the counter with a bica (espresso), Manteigaria offers a bite of Lisbon’s heart — simple, authentic, and unforgettable. || Some of the tastiest pastéis de nata we had in Lisbon! Located in a lovely spot at the beginning of Bairro Alto, right across from the square. You can enjoy your pastéis de nata at a small stand or take them away with you. || A few doors down, we checked out Manteigaria where they served the Pastel de Nata – the famous Portuguese egg custard tart. There was only standing space inside this outlet and many people came in to have just the Pastel de Nata. We ordered 2 Pastel de Nata from Manteigaria (1.4 euro each) and also an iced Americano (2 euros).  In terms of the outer crust, it was the flaky and crisp version that we come to know even in Singapore. This we loved. As for the taste of the custard, it was more on the sweet side and less on the eggy side unlike what we tried in Singapore. Perhaps they have been tweaked to suit Singapore tastes? We probably have to try out a few more Portuguese egg custard tarts (Pastel de Nata) over the next few days to verify...  For the full review and details of our 5 months Round The World RTW travels, visit 2bearbear today! || After trying most of the popular and recommended places for pastel de natas, I would have to say this is better than the most by small margin. Most places in Lisbon makes good pastel de natas, and hard to tell which is better but this one had slightly richer custard and lingering pleasant flavour. Would definitely recommend but brace for a lineup as it gets really busy. Luckily the line moves pretty fast. || 🌍 Explore, Taste, and Travel with Us! We are explorers from Dubai, do follow our adventures and food journeys on Insta: vibrant_wanderer_rhythm  🥂 DM us for travel tips and insights for any destination ❤️  It is for a reason that this place is famous. Loved it a the sugar , cinnamon and creamy flavors wrapped with the flaky pastry will surely win your heart  We loved it , would highly recommend it || By far the best Pastéis de Nata I tasted. I would rank my top 3 as follows: 1. Manteigaria (only tried this location twice) 2. Pastéis de Belem 3. Piriquita (Located in Sintra) || When I came across this picture of this super delicious pastel de nata, I remembered that I actually took this picture to write a review.  So here we go …  For me this is where you go for the best pastel de nata in town. Without doubt I have been taking all my visitors over the years and no one has not liked them ever! They all want to go back and often I take a box back with me to the family when I visit my folks.  I am definitely missing one right now … || Some of the best pastries and pastel de nata in the area. Prices are decent and it’s a popular spot. Everything is made fresh, and it’s a real experience watching them make the pastel de nata. || Had only one quick Pastel de Nata at this Manteigaria branch in Lisbon on my way home after a long day exploring the city and seeing such a fresh, still-warm pastel being served in the evening almost made me cry. Undeniably amazing. Recommended! || The crust is buttery but not too greasy. It’s flaky and holds its structure shattee beautifully when you take a bite. The egg custard filling it a creamy smooth texture that is at the perfect sweetness. Don’t forget to douse the pastel de nata in cinnamon. It wouldn’t be properly without it 🤦‍♂️.  This is one do the big three and it’s worth wait.  Need I say more 😌? || It was very crunchy and caramelized on top but the pastry wasn’t as flakey as I would have liked. It was a little too sweet for me. I’d recommend people to eat at the store because there is an extra charge for takeout || Hi Linda. Thank you for your comment and for visiting. We hope to see you again soon. || Had a manteigari 3 mins walk away from where we were staying. Truly one of the best pastel de Natas in Lisbon!! Definitely sprinkle on some of the cinnamon they give you as it elevates the pastry to a whole other level!!!

The best pastries + brekkie! Love love love their almond croissants, bread, and little desserts. We got some to have for Christmas dinner and they were all delicious but the blueberry is our favorite … || This is a super exquisite French dessert shop with a truly French atmosphere. The small space is incredibly charming, and the owner is incredibly nice. 💐 We ordered two tarts—the 🍋Lemon Tart and the 🍮Fig Tart. … || Lovely French bakery in Anjos! The fig tart, raspberry cake, and croissant were all delicious especially the croissant, super flaky and buttery. Cozy atmosphere, perfect for coffee and desserts. 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 … || loved this place. The desserts are beautifully crafted, the apple tart isnt too sweet,  the canelé has a lovely caramelized crust and the cream puffs were light and flavorful. The coffee was rich and so smooth. Cozy space for afternoon treat ;) || Really lovely place and after living here for 3 years - I must say that this is one of my fav in Lisbon. It is hard to find a French bakery here, and the tastes of those sweets are very good. I recommend the chocolate bar. It is a very good experience to just sit there and enjoy some dessert in a lazy afternoon. || Real French pastry in Lisbon. What an Amazing place and beautiful taste. Staff is really welcoming and the food is great. Tiago is 5 stars || I came here with my friend for afternoon tea. The environment is lovely, the cream puffs are delicious, and we ordered a purple cake which also tasted amazing. It’s a great place to sit down and enjoy a nice afternoon tea || This historic bakery with its 1661 heritage delivers exceptional quality across every category. The croissants are perfectly golden and flaky, while their chocolate selection - from rich brownies to delicate pastries - looks incredible. I … || I was really surprised at Lully1661! The environment in the store is super atmospheric. Although it is not big, it is very exquisite. The lighting and furnishings are very careful, which is suitable for dating and sisters' afternoon time. || Very nice pastries with good viennoiseries. Everything looks appealing! The torsade and the flan were good. Service was quick. || This is my third time. 1st time I got baguettes. It was not very good quality from my experience in France or UK or Italy. 2nd time I got apple pie and simple croissant. It was also so so. I still want to give them chance because this place … || Hello Janet, we're so sorry that our products do not match your expectations and if there is any chance we get you to swing by again we'd love to discuss this with you in more details as every comment matters to us in our attempt to deliver quality and value for money to all in Lisbon. || I really really like this bakery, lully's French pastries are amazing. My favorite is the puff, every bite makes me feel better! || The croissants and puffs were very good, the shop was great and the cakes were beautifully presented like works of art! || Thank you and we look forward to having you again soon! || Lully 1661 has been a welcome addition to Anjos since its inception. It is simply fantastic, possibly the best bakery in Lisbon. They offer a great variety of breads and patisseries at a range of prices. The tomato and ricotta danish is a … || Such a cute tasty place . Great lunch deal . Sandwich, cake n drink €12 || True French pastry and deserts, delicious, freshly baked, flavours are gorgeous. A wonderful point to stop for your morning espresso. || A delicious french bakery, however quite pricey and not made comfortable to stay and enjoy your coffee. Almost €30 for a tiny cake of about 10cm in diameter. Only 4 seats inside the shop, their bar is bigger than the possible seating area. The staff could be much friendlier.. || AMAZING bakery!! Sad we only discovered it on our last morning in Lisbon! Very friendly staff, you can get coffee to go and the pastries were fantastic - clearly freshly made and to a very high quality. Will definitely be back. || Ordered twice from uber: - sandwiches were done with the bread of the day before, it was really chewy. - size was half of what was pictured in Uber … || Lovely bakery in the heart of lisbon that sells just the BEST pasteries and bread in town! The staff are always welcoming and go the extra mile to make one feel at home. You won't find me at any other bakery while lully is around as no competitor comes close!

My new favorite spot in lisbon! Absolutely delicious sourdough pastries and delicious matcha! The pastel de nata was my favorite but try all of them. So cute on the top of a pretty and cute street too. Can’t wait to come back! || The slow bakery is simply perfect. The best pastries I’ve ever had and no animal get exploited for it. The service is very good and especially João is very kind and helpful. The store has a great atmosphere and beautiful timeless interior. Thank you for having a completely vegan pastries store 🙏🏼 we would love to have something like this back home. We’re looking forward to come back one day! || My second time here already. Love their pear tart so much! The almond croissant is loaded with filling, so moist and delicious. All of their pastries are also vegan. || I love this little corner of sunshine! The coffee and matcha were reallyyy good and the staff were so kind 💖 I love this space they got and you can even have pastries! Super pretty inside, I highly recommend dropping by! || i cannot put into words how highly i recommend this place to anyone visiting lisbon!! absolutely delicious. the owner of the bakery is very friendly and passionate, explaining each pastry in detail, making the experience so much better. my partner and i went back there almost everyday after we first discovered it, happy at the simple thought of trying something new from the various display of goods. it's the vegan pastries heaven!! must try: raspberry and pistachio cream danish 😍 || I personally think that they are one of the best pastries of Lisbon. The hill killed me because the pastry shop is located on top of a 3min hill, but it was worth! I enjoyed every bite, mostly of the Cinnamon Roll! I’m coming back for it! || My two favorite places in Lisbon now together… couldn’t be happier! I do highly recommend to pass by for a good coffee and amazing pastries 🥐💛 || Wow ! This place is such a vibe. The best vegan pastries I’ve ever had, delicious coffee, A/c , and great music. Do not hesitate to stop by and treat yourself! || We had some of the best pastries and coffees during our trip to Lisbon. The staff recommended the daily specials, and they were absolutely incredible - fresh, full of flavour, and beautifully made. The service was friendly and welcoming, and the atmosphere made it the perfect stop to enjoy some amazing pastries. Couldn’t recommend it more highly! || Collab of the Year in Lisbon! EleEla Café has truly outdone themselves by bringing together three powerhouses in one unforgettable experience.  You’ll find La Cabra’s legendary Danish coffee (yes, that La Cabra – rarely seen in Lisbon), silky Minor Figures oat milk, and baked goods by the iconic Slow Bakery – offering some of the best vegan, plant-based pastries and sourdough bread you’ll taste anywhere.  The vibe? Spot on. Minimalist and effortlessly cool design, a 90s classic hip-hop playlist setting the tone, and a team that welcomes you like an old friend – warm, genuine, and passionate.  I’m especially happy that Slow Bakery is finally within reach – no more trips to Costa da Caparica just to stock up on their baked goodness.  Highly recommend this spot to anyone who cares about top-tier coffee, great energy, and next-level craftsmanship. Wishing the team lots of success – Lisbon just got a little better.

place_name: PIM PAM Café - Specialty Coffee, Ceremonial Matcha, Sandwiches, and Pastries
reviews_content: Having lived in the Anjos neighborhood for a couple of years now I can confirm that Pim Pam has the best coffee around. Their food selection is limited but what they do serve is reliably tasty and fresh - the banana bread in particular is truly amazing. Oh and I almost forgot that it’s run by two of the sweetest guys you’ll find. What a delight for our vizinhança! || Cute small comfortable coffee shop with a tasty iced matcha latte! We ordered cappuccino and iced matcha latte, and we really liked two of them! Also, the croissant with ham and cheese was quite delicious. The croissant was very fresh and crusty and the ham was super delicious. || Awww Ekin we’re blushing ☺️ thanks so much for your kind words and we look forward to your next visit 🙌 … || Superb. Had the chicken salad, a banana bread and a latte. All amazing quality. Friendly staff, nice outdoor seating area. Simple, cheap enough and quick. I’ll be back. PS get the banana bread it’s amazing. || You're very kind, Chris. We're happy you had a good experience and we look forward to welcoming you again! || Happened upon this café and it was fantastic! The baristas were friendly, the coffee was superb, and they gave me cute cat sticker ❤️ a must visit in Lisbon! || Aww Gina we're so happy you enjoyed your visit (and the cat stickers :)) || Truly hidden gem in the specialty coffee map in Lisbon. Fresh, new place that’s really getting started very well. The owner - Edgar is great guy with nice vision and passion. Unfortunately they don’t have filter coffee yet but Edgar told me that it’s the matter of one month. Espresso was great and so the espresso tonic which was prepared excellent with great balance in the taste thanks good quality of tonic and espresso and especially used lemon. Good luck Edgar I’m rooting for you! || Thanks Jacob for your worlds🫶 I hope to see you soon  … || Pim Pam was pretty much where I started my day during my two weeks in Lisbon. Cozy yet gorgeous coffee shop with the best espresso. I appreciated the variety of drinks including iced and matcha options. Their croissant sandwiches and burritos were my favorite and the banana bread was amazing. Edgar, the owner, was really sweet and welcoming. I’ll definitely be back when I’m in Lisbon. Obrigado! || You're so kind- we look forward to seeing you again soon! || Cozy Vibes and Excellent Brews – 5/5  I recently visited PIM PAM café, and I have to say, I was thoroughly impressed. From the moment I walked in, the ambiance was warm and inviting. Soft lighting, comfortable  with a great terrace.  The coffee? Absolutely fantastic. I tried their signature espresso, and it was rich, smooth, and perfectly balanced—no bitter aftertaste, which is a rare find. Their pour-over was equally impressive, with a delicate, flavorful profile that showed off the beans’ true character. The owner and the barista were super friendly.  If you’re in the area and looking for a coffee shop with both great drinks and a chill vibe, PIM PAM Café is definitely worth a visit. I’ll be back for sure! || Thanks for your visit Bruno 🫶 … || This place is beyond a 5-star rating! The flat white and cappuccino here in Lisbon are simply unbeatable. The service is not just friendly; it's like a warm hug on a rainy day. The wall tiles remind you of the exquisite patterns at the Museu Nacional do Azulejo. I highly recommend it, and there's no doubt I'll be back with a skip in my step. It's the go-to spot for local coffee enthusiasts. || We're blushing! Tank you so much for your kind words- we're looking forward to seeing you again! || Pim Pam is a hidden gem located in Anjos just below the "secret" viewpoint of Monte Agudo in Lisbon’s picturesque Penha de França neighborhood. This spot is ideal for indulging in delicious, freshly prepared food while enjoying a break from the bustling city center.  The staff are incredibly welcoming and friendly, not only to humans but also to furry companions, with dog treats conveniently available for our four-legged friends.  I was particularly amazed by the explosion of flavors in the carrot cake—it truly caught me by surprise! If you’re in the area, make sure to visit Pim Pam for an extraordinary culinary experience in great company. || Best Latte in Lisbon! If you love coffee this is a hidden gem. The owner (Edgar) is very welcoming. :)  P.S: the place is pets friendly.

place_name: Fábrica da Nata - Pastéis de Nata
reviews_content: Here’s the deal. I saw the line at the famous pastel de nata place in Belém and was like, life is too short for that. A friend recommended this place and it didn’t disappoint. They got super tasty pastel de natas, fresh out the oven along with a bunch of other stuff. Unfortunately, I had to wait for my plate, which I received after my family was done eating…. || A fantastic place with awesome costumer service, good atmosphere and a very friendly staff. Definitely one of the best bakeries to have an breakfast in the region, the red berries crepe had the perfect level of sweetness and the pastel de nata had a super delicious filling. Can't wait to have another snack there once i visit Lisbon again. || Coeliac heaven! I would consider moving from England to Lisbon just for the pastries. By far the very best gluten free pastries I have had anywhere in the world 🥲🥐💖💕😋 || UNBELIEVABLE. As a gluten intolerant I feel like a kid in a toy shop. The amount of different foods they have is staggering. The two items I had were both delicious, too, so no reason to suspect the rest of the menu wouldn’t be just as amazing! Service was also incredible, the server was very friendly and prices were agreeable too. The decor/aesthetic is also super nice and feels very posh, it’s clear a lot of effort has been put into making it look nice. I would give 6 stars if I could! || Wonderful gluten free bakery/ cafe in central Lisbon. Pastries and panini’s of an excellent quality. A coeliac can feel like a normal human being. And the showstoppers being the GF pastéis de nata‘s. || Nice place. They do a good gluten free pastel de nata and the ham & cheese filled pastry was really good (ask them to heat it). The cinnamon role and pain au chocolates were okay. || Awesome place with so many allergy friendly options (on top of everything being gluten free). A must stop for the gluten free folks! || So awesome to find a fully gluten free place! We got the carrot soup (really good), tapicoa with cheese (not great, a little dry and bland - have had better), pain au chocolat (6/10, probably would be better if it was warm but the chocolate was hard and pastry wasn't flaky), pastel de nata (filling was super yummy but pastry wasn't flaky), and toast with apple/peanut butter/coconut (really good flavor combo and toast was quite good). Love the variety of options || Portuguese pastries (pastel de nata, chicken pie) and croissants were amazing! There was surprisingly so many options so i couldn't even decide and ordered a takeaway. I wish i stayed longer in Lisbon and pop by again 💖 …

In a city known for its high-quality brunch spots and cafés, this establishment no longer holds its place. Despite its history dating back to the 1930s, it’s unclear how it has survived. The pastel de nata, priced at €1.50—above average—reflects the overall quality of the café. Served cold with an overcooked exterior, it was disappointing. The barista, an older gentleman who may be the owner, was friendly, but the café itself feels like a fading relic, slowly dying and suffering . The interior is outdated and lacks cleanliness, creating a sense of neglect. Overall, it’s not worth a visit—more of a forgotten space than a thriving café. || Amazing and traditional spot to have breakfast with a view of the tram. The owner and employees are very friendly and always try to make an effort to understand what you are saying, despite only speaking Portuguese. If you come a couple days in a row the people in the neighborhood will welcome you with kindness. Ideal spot to get a pastel de nata! || Truly a gem and a favorite among locals. This is a cozy small cafe and bakery run by a lovely old couple. I came here on a morning walk and got myself treated to sweet and fresh aromas of pastries and coffee beans. Thank you for making my day. || Hidden gem down a little backstreet. Way cheaper than the tourist traps, everything is so delicious and fresh. Great spot for a coffee sat on the tables outside. Recommend the palmier and all of the pastries.. || Cute neighborhood bakery where the locals go for coffee.  Great for early risers since it opens at 7am while the other coffee shops/bakeries in the area open at 8:30.  Very friendly service, English speaking.  Their plain brioche roll as well as the rustic roll were both fresh.  And the croissant filled with cream was soooo good!!  More like brioche, not flaky, and the filling reminds me of Korean cream custard with a hint of orange flavor?  And coffee was excellent and strong, great value for 75 cents!  And you can get it to go. || Lovely little bakery, and place to have an authentic Portuguese experience. Prices are extremely reasonable and great value. The place is clean and inviting. Delicious treats and coffee. Loved the Pastel de Nata. || Lovely quaint bakery. The owners are a lovely pair who only speak Portuguese. They were patient with me fast and efficient went two days  in a row. This is an ideal palce for early risers. || What a gem of a place. Clean, friendly, and affordable. Gorgeous selection of pastries and delicious coffee. Way better than the over-priced newer establishments further up the road. We will be back! || Excellent service. The man at the counter was very friendly and even though my Portuguese isn’t great he still made the effort to understand and was very polite and well-mannered. The pastries are good and reasonably priced. I recommend the freshly-squeezed orange juice. 5* || Lovely little bakery run by a very nice couple. Excellent food with pastries, cookies, sandwiches and more. The coffee is top notch with expert espresso pulls by the owners. Paninis are fresh and cooked to order. Limited English but didn’t affect order or experience. Highly recommended.

Absolutely incredible spot in the heart of Alfama! 🌟 Padaria Doce Mila is everything you dream of when you imagine authentic Lisbon food. Every single morning the locals are there cooking up fresh food right in front of you — from perfectly … || What a hidden gem (literally). Great service, the owners are very nice and understanding of travellers. Served with a smile. Highly recommend 5*. This place is off the beaten path in a little Courtyard, take a break and visit them. 🤗 … || A hidden gem - in house bakery. You can taste the care and tradition in the sweet treats. … || Sweet Portuguese bakery in a backyard. There are lots of different pastries to choose from. Everything I tried tasted very good and was also very reasonably priced. The waiter was very nice, even if he unfortunately only spoke Portuguese. || Lovely local place to get nata! Espresso was divine so a welcome morning combination upon arriving in Lisbon! Staff were warm and welcoming, definitely an underrated place! Easy to miss the entry on the road so watch out for the shop board sign. || For me the best Pastel de nata in Lisbon. Very good coffee and atmosphere. Very good prices. It is a gem in whole city. Highly recommended. || Delicious food with excellent coffee! Great for breakfast/lunch with reasonable prices :) And in my opinion - best Pastel de Nata in Portugal! ❤️ || We came here for breakfast.  I’m in love with with the Pastéis natas.  They are a good size and after my big breakfast of chicken on toast, I could barely finish it. Which was  a panini with chicken and tomato and cheese. Highly recommend. || Owner and staff were very friendly. Menu is simple, food is good, but nothing to write home about. Very neighborhood vibes which is a nice experience. Coffee is good. || This cafe is such a lovely hidden gem! The owner is so kind and his pastries are delicious. There is a little courtyard with tables in the shade, perfect place to relax and enjoy. I love coming here ❤️❤️ || Delicious food served by the kindest woman! Great local place. Love it || Really nice Pastelaria, definitely recommend, the owner of the place is the nicest, really friendly. All of his pastries are delicious. And the terrace outside makes the all difference too to eat in a cosy settings. We are coming almost every morning for breakfast. || Absolutely delicious pasteis de nata! And such a friendly beautiful couple who own the place. || Really really great hole in the wall pastry and espresso place!!  Best breakfast place to go in Lisbon || Perfect and tasty breakfast 👌 … || We were introduced to this place on a walking tour. Delicious pastry and espresso! || A lovely local bakery with very friendly staff and delicious traditional pastries at a very reasonable price. It’s conveniently located in a small square just off the main street. Perfect for a quick breakfast—highly recommend! || We were a group of nine eating here for two mornings. It was an amazing and authentic experience. Very cheap but still high quality! || Very traditional. The host is really sweet and the pasteis de nata are absolutely amazing. Also, the small garden is really lovely and can give you a break from the caos of the city || An authentic Portuguese, family run restaurant near the historic center. Great value - good food at a reasonable price. Tucked away in a little alley, away from the overpriced tourist area.

Well equipped, clean and entertaining playground. Plenty of slides, swings and play structures for smaller kids plus more challenging play structures for bigger kids. Note gravel surface was fine for 1 kid with no shoes but bothered the other one who kept her sandals on. Toilets strictly for kids only - attendant monitors adherence to the signs! Nice bar nearby - in common with plenty of playgrounds in Lisbon. || We were in Lisbon for vacation. I was riding the tram 28 with my toddler son and we decided to jump off the tram to go to the nearest playground.  It turned out it was a fun playground with little stones on the floor. Kids can play with the stones for a long time.  The playground is situated in a nice green park.  The slides are giraffe and lion shape. There are few swings. There isn’t much shades so it could be hot and sunny during summer days. || The best playground! The animal shaped structures are so cute! This is my first time seeing little pebbles as the playground floor, and my daughter loved it. There are decent swing sets for babies and older kids, and also a climbing structure in another area. The surrounding park is beautiful and busy, and parents can have a drink at the nearby quiosque. || Very good park perfect do go with children because it has a lot to do for kids in a Jung age || Excellent playground for children to play but be cautious going during work hours as the lady who works there will yell at any adult that attempts to climb or sit on a swing and threatens to call the cops on you. I advise visiting after 17:00 when she’s no longer there (plus it’s cooler with the sun going down) || The playground itself is very nice. But the lady who takes care of the toilets next to it is very bossy and kinda mean. The playground was almost completely empty and I just wanted to swing a little bit on the swings. I was not bothering anyone. The lady came out and said I was not allowed in there and needed to leave. Apparently it is forbidden to enjoy a swing set in peace when you're not a little kid anymore. For the rest the playground is nice with cool slides and climbing stuff || Not sure why this playground gets such high marks (aside from the lovely surroundings). The equipment is not actually very kid friendly. Younger children absolutely need assistance climbing, and the rocks are difficult to walk on. || Nice playground. Restrooms are just for kids. There are benches and water fountain closeby. || This is our favorite playground and park in Lisbon. There are two play areas…  The first is quite large with super small, smooth rocks for the surface and enclosed by a wooden fence. There you can find swings, slides, teeter totter, benches for parents, and all sorts of other fun. My kids love the rocks and spend half the time scooping and burying themselves. Bring sand toys and trucks for the ultimate rock experience.  The second play area is a giant rope pyramid! It’s awesome. I’ve even climbed up as far as my old body would allow. This is a kid favorite too.  Next to the play areas is a kiosk/cafe serving up everything you want - tostas, pastries, snacks, ice cream, wine, beer, cocktails. The kiosk has one small bathroom.  There’s a children’s only bathroom that is attended by a park worker to ensure the kid’s space remains safe and clean. There are water fountains around too.  The park has many shaded areas perfect for a picnic or birthday party. There’s another cafe on the other side of the park that is more calm and typically has fewer kids.  There are also peacocks that live there and they wander about and are a fun surprise for the kids. || Great for having coffee seating in nearby coffee place and watching your kids playing on the playground. Just warning.. don't put best clothes on them. They will end up a bit dirty from the flooring which are small stones. But what a fun for them... || My kids liked it. It’s unpleasant for 3 reasons. First, there is an attendant who forbids adults from using equipment. An adult cannot swing or even sit on a swing, even when no child is present. Second, the ground is covered with pebbles that are covered in dust and grime. Finally, the pest count is high: flies, pigeons, and rodents abound. || The best play park outside of the centre of Lisbon. Never too busy, and just really well designed and thought through. Side note: there is a black board (double sided) so always a good idea to take some chalk if you have any. || It's one of the most famous parks of the city. Great for picnics, walks or just laying on the grass. Kids love it and if you're lucky there's a live concert going on || Nice little playground with slides, swings and other things. Benches on the shadows for parents. || Great place for the kids to unwind. Clean.

reviews_content: This children's playground has the usual toys that can be found elsewhere. There are 4 rocker toys, a slide and a climbing structure. Overall, it's a fantastic place for a fun-filled day out with the family. || One of the best free public children's playgrounds in Lisbon with well maintained, interactive and engaging games and equipment for kids (ideally aged 2-8?). The Fernando Pessoa Garden, located in the Areeiro district of Lisbon, is a tranquil green space dedicated to one of Portugal’s most celebrated literary figures. Nestled among the urban surroundings, the garden offers a peaceful retreat with neatly landscaped paths, benches, and shaded areas ideal for quiet reflection or reading. Named after the iconic poet and writer, the garden subtly pays homage to Pessoa’s legacy, often drawing locals and tourists alike who are seeking a moment of calm amid the city’s rhythm. Its central location in Areeiro makes it easily accessible, serving both as a community gathering spot and a small cultural landmark. || One of the best playgrounds that I have found so far in Lisbon in terms of amenities, shade, other kids to play with, and safety from streets. We go all of the time. || Nice park. Clean and green. Kid friendly playground. And there is also a football cage. || Very welcoming place. Pleasant. However, the playground only has attractions for children up to 3 or 4 years old. They should do something similar to the Campo Pequeno park, with a lot of variety for different age groups. || This garden, for the long-time residents, is the Roma garden. It has always been known by that name. It was given the name Fernando Peça because he would occasionally go for a bike ride there early in the morning, even though he lived on a different block. || A well-kept garden near our house, where I often go with my grandchildren. Fitness and exercise circuit. Tables available. || This garden is very peaceful; I usually spend my lunch break here. It's a very beautiful space. || A beautiful garden, very well laid out, and with the advantage of being suitable for children, dogs, and people of all ages. || A very pleasant place to take children for a walk. Or for those who have pets. || One of the few gardens in Lisbon without the noise of traffic. Well-frequented, well-located and maintained. || A pleasant place, with a playground offering many attractions to keep the children entertained. || Pleasant park, but a bit neglected in terms of upkeep. || Nice garden for children, could be cleaner. || The somewhat neglected park needs more maintenance. || Nice places to spend an afternoon with family. || Great for the grandchildren. A lovely small children’s play area. There’s a children’s climb on tram with slide, seesaw, swings and a ride on car.  We found the play area to be too close to people smoking by the open cafe. Nonetheless, the play area kept our little one entertained for a short time while visiting the area. || Very neat location next to historical aqueducts. Cafe next door was fantastic although quite a number of smokers (to be expected in Portugal but were very close to the playground & children) || Nice playground with a large toy tram. There is a nice little cafe next to it as well so you can spend a longer time. There are lots of trees for shades || It's a playground in the garden. It's quite popular with children, so many people use it. || I really enjoyed going to the park, and the baby did too! But the tram was a bit dirty and the baby swing needed a little repair. But otherwise it's very pleasant. || A wonderful family daycare. A playground for children and a café for parents in a quiet and comfortable location. || It's right next to an outdoor seating area, which makes it a good location for both children and parents. || Few toy options. Pleasant environment.

place_name: Parque Infantil da Praça José Fontana
reviews_content: This is a small playground with two areas: one for younger children and another for older kids. Unfortunately, there are not many suitable play options for toddlers, such as seesaws or swings. There are seating areas for parents, but the play areas have limited shade. The metal slide gets very hot due to direct sunlight all day. The ground is covered with small pebbles, which do a decent job of cushioning falls, but there is still a risk of scraped knees. There are no restrooms available, but there's a café right next door where you can grab drinks and snacks, which is a nice perk. || Great little park and playground. If you have kids and have to wait in the long queues in the nearby city administrative centre, then on a sunny day this is a glorious respite. The atmosphere is slightly cosmopolitan, which again is a pleasant change if you’ve just been dealing with all that bureaucracy has to offer. || Nice outdoor spot. Coffee shop in the middle of the park is convenient. Clean. Lots of places to sit on the park. || Great park for kids located right next to a bar. Win win! || Clean but a bit hard for very young children. No protection from the sun so can get very hot here at times. || Small playground with two play areas. One area is geared toward younger children, and the other toward older children. Unfortunately, there aren't any good play options for very young children. There are no seesaws or swings. There are seating areas for parents. There's little shade in the play areas. The metal slide gets very hot because it's in the sun all day. The ground is made of small pebbles. Overall, the ground cushions children's jumps well. However, there is still a risk of injury, such as scraped knees. Unfortunately, there are no restrooms. It's good that there's a café right next door, so you can stock up on drinks and snacks. || There are two play structures, one suitable for younger children and a second one with more difficulty. There are benches for parents, both inside and outside, and being next to the café is great for relaxing a bit while the children play. We loved it! || It's a nice park, but besides needing repairs, the kids from the school across from it are always there smoking things they shouldn't be smoking... || A nice, pleasant little green park as a refreshment in the surroundings of concrete buildings and busy streets. It has a nice little vaulted and elevated pavilion ideal for summer concerts, if they are held there, otherwise it would be a shame. || a small selection of attractions for children

Filipe is an amazing host and a really kind person; something really rare in the hospitality business nowadays because is passion is genuine. We went there 3 days in a row for the oysters (so fresh and tasted incredible) and the sparkling wine was really really good. We spent Christmas Eve there and the food and wine pairing was outstanding (the octopus and the linguine with clams were wow)! We had the chance to order a bottle of 1998 and it was a true discovery. Thank you so much for taking great care of us Filipe and team, you deserve all the success in the world! || Dear Kira Ghidoni,  Thank you so much for your kind words! We are extremely happy to know that you enjoyed our establishment and, of course, Filipe and the team. It's a pleasure to welcome customers like you. The octopus salad was flavorful but too finely diced to enjoy the real octopus texture. The dessert Pera Bêbada com Gelado de Limão —  drunk pear with lemon sorbet — was simply unforgettable.  On top of that, Filipe’s warm, attentive service made the dinner exceptional.
