We do our best to keep our 'moto' alive: #happymusic #happypeople! || The staff at the door are beyond rude. They treat you like you were beging to enter the place when actually you are paying to go in. No good at all || We are sorry for any behavior that was less than friendly and polite. We will try to find out what happened. Cheers! || Great club! Really nice atmosphere. DJ playing some classic rock songs. Not that mainstream radio songs. Really great experience! || Many thanks! We try our best! || On Facebook said was open on Sunday I did confirmed had the reply said yes then I went there on Sunday was closed 😡😢 … || Hello! It was open on Sunday. From 22:30 to 04:00. Are you sure you are referring to Roterdão Club on Pink Street? || My friend got roofed by some guys in the bathroom but the music is nice.. || Dear Vanessa, if something happened that threatened your Security, we are very worried. Are You sure that it was at Roterdão? Nothing was reported to our security team. Best wishes! || Honest and fun. Not fancy but it provides great fun, filtered crowd and cheap big drinks || It makes us happy to know you enjoyed your time :-)

place_name: The Lisbon Pub Crawl- Discover Lisbon
reviews_content: Leo is the man to do the Pub Crawl in Lisbon with. It was so much fun. Super cool group, stack cup game, dance, karaoke and drinks. Everything was awesome. || Joined the pub crawl twice whilst I was in Lisbon. The MOST fun, such a great way to meet people as I was travelling alone. Leo, Nicholas & Phelps were the BEST 🩷🩷🩷 || Met some cool people I wouldn’t have otherwise. VIP access at the bars. Good times waiting to happen.. Cheers🍻 || First pub crawl experience and definitely a very good one! The bars they brought us to were very nice, good music and space wasn’t a problem since the night was warm so some of us stayed outside. The alcohol included is nice, you get shots and an open bar. I don’t think you can get wasted but a bit tipsy maybe! The guides of the tour, especially Ana and Victoria especially, are nice and organised! I highly recommend 🤘🏻 || Hi Estelle, Thank you very much for  leaving such an amazing review. Lovely that you enjoyed our experiences. We look forward to seeing you again in the near future and party like we never did before.  Best regards, Discover Lisbon team || We had an amazing time with our tour guide Thomas!!! The free shots were trash though from the bars they tasted like juice! It overall was a fantastic time. Highly recommend :) || Phelps he is the best guy ever he is so friendly and funny I think I will try it just because of this. They are friendly and they know how to have fun they are the best || Lovely guide called tiago kept the group together and energetic. Definitely a recommendation. Lots of people and good communication and friendliness! || this was so fun and so safe and all tour guides were amazing!! had fun with us and made sure everyone was having a good time and accounted for. Anna T specifically was amazing and does deserve a raise! please do go on Portugal pub crawl || The pubcrawl was really nice  will sure we will recommend my friends, our tour guide MANNUUUUUU did a great job || Ton was such an amazing guide would definitely recommend if in Portugal for the night.

We had reserved a VIP table weeks in advance. When we arrived, they had given our table away. Then, they tried to set up a table in the exit hallway. It was hysterical. We refused that, so they set up half a table where only 2 people could sit blocking the walkway to the dance floor. It was fine, there was not much need for a table. There was hardly anyone there so it didn’t matter much. Eventually another table left and they moved us there. The bottle of vodka was a ridiculously cheap brand and the “OJ” was some type of orange drink. It was a funny experience. It’s fun  it you’re with fun, light-hearted people, and the place is very cool to walk around. Just don’t take it too seriously! The server at the table was hospitable.  UPDATE: Since the club has responded that my review is not true, please see attached pictures. The exit area is where they tried to set up our “VIP” area, the table is where they put us in the middle of the walkway, and you can see whatever orange-aid drink and cheap vodka they gave us. So….yeah….it is true. And now that I know you’re liars, you go down from two stars to one. ✌🏻 || Not true! Thank you!.... Thats not the exit area... actually thats the artists area... joy is a standard orange juice in night clubs... its not a white brand... the same about the vodka eristoff... its a well known brand... better go out more often or if you need attention get a boyfriend instead... || Amazing experience! Great bars, fun people, and the guides were top-notch. The open bar at the start was a huge plus. Perfect way to meet people if you're traveling solo. I’d definitely do it again — 100% recommend...!!!♥️♥️♥️ || Had an amazing night at Temple Club Lisbon! As a gay club, it delivered everything I was hoping for — fun, energy, and most importantly, a space where I felt totally safe and welcomed. The drag queens were absolutely fabulous and brought so much life to the stage! Great music, good drinks, and a crowd full of good vibes. Can’t wait to come back next time I’m in Lisbon! 🌈💃🍸 || Great vibes and atmosphere and the music too! One of the only clubs here in Lisbon us girls really felt safe. Good value for money and very nice staff! Would go again! || My favorite club in Lisbon. It’s cozy, nice people looking to have a good time, the music is special, not your typical rave but more on the synthpop, darkwave, indie, disco. You get a drink for your entry fee, good ventilation, and friendly staff. || Temple Night Club is absolutely amazing! The DJ played nonstop hits, and the energy in the crowd was insane. Definitely the best place to party in the city! || This club is incredible! From the moment you walk in, you feel the excitement. Great service, fun crowd, and unbeatable music...!!! || Night club with amazing techno events, some of the best Hardtechno/Darktech I have heard in Lisbon. Theres even food (burgers&fries) for the hungry, and it's really tasty :)  Both dancefloors have a great atmosphere and you can smoke outside, the only downside is that they only accept card payment || Visited this club loads of time for some major international acts, they bring some great artists, whom I have grown up listening and to add on the staff is great. This place has an underground vibe to it, drinks are economically priced… || Nice place to dance. It takes time to get used to Lisabon's DJs but after that it goes smoothly.🥰🥰🥰

Went in August after 2am. No lines, 10€ for females that comes with a drink. Was super sceptical bc of the terrible reviews but music is INCREDIBLE for all Baile Funk lovers (even as a gringa). Partied non-stop till 6 am, best night of my life at a club!!! || Went on a Friday and it felt like a middle school party. No one was on the dance floor and everyone was standing on the edges. I think this club is meant for young kids. 18-20 years old. Good music though. Lots of Portuguese, Spanish and English songs. My friend lost the card that they gave her and had to pay €100. || Absolutely terrible. Please don’t go here. It’s a massive scam, always empty, music is dead and the workers are horrible, they started physically pushing us and don’t clearly explain how the club works. The bouncers make you feel unsafe when it’s literally their jobs to make it safe. Complete scam. Save your coin. || Do not let anyone you know attend this disgusting venue.  The doormen are extortionists why violently attack innocent young people to steal their money.  My friend was violently assaulted by 3 security staff.  He has a broken arm and is physically and mentally shattered.  We will be taking legal and criminal action but we urge you to avoid this place. || Force you to spend 10 euro on a card they give you but then don't tell you how much the drinks are when you swipe your card so you have to ask to even know how much you're spending. The shots are 4 euro. Got there earlier in the night but then it just did not get better throughout the night. Also if you lose the card they give you, you have to pay 100 euro. || Genuinely the worst club I've ever been to. Some random English guy spilled a drink at the bar, the bar staff was so angry and was intentionally refusing to serve other English people. Petty and racist || I was attacked by three bouncers at this club completely unprovoked.  I did not order anything from this club but was charged a Euro fee of 100 via my debit card to leave the club.  I was punched multiple times by security for no reason.  Multiple witnesses who are not affiliated with me can confirm my attack was completely unprovoked.  They are locals who have stated that going to the police will do no good.  AVOID THIS CLUB AT ALL COSTS.  (As an aside, I am in the ER awaiting treatment and a CT Scan….see other reviews:  this club should not be allowed to operate)  Next day update:  One of the three bouncers who attacked me (punching me 10-15 times according to bystanders who tried to intervene and can confirm I did nothing to deserve the attack) took my wallet and stole my credit card.  They charged over $450 to my credit card after I left.  I did not realize they stole my card until this morning.  Thankfully my credit card company declined the charges and is investigating them for fraud. Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
reviews_content: You get a fantastic view of the historic centre of this beautiful city from here. You could stay and enjoy the well kept gardens and the views all day. There's so much to look at. Enjoy the full chaos of colours and sounds that envelope your senses. You'll have so many photos when you leave this place, but it is the experience itself that will stay with you. || Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara offers one of the most beautiful panoramic views in Lisbon. The terrace overlooks the historic center, the castle, and the river, making it an ideal place to pause and take in the city’s landscape. The garden is well kept, and the atmosphere is relaxed despite being a popular spot.  It’s especially impressive at sunset, when the light over the city becomes warm and golden. A must-see viewpoint if you want a classic Lisbon panorama in a pleasant, accessible setting. || A nice panoramic view of the city center and part of the coast. It’s adjacent to a busy street and is easy to access locates at the city center. It’s very spacious there currently hosting a Christmas bazaar making it loads of festive feels. There are different direction to arrive the view point, including one very steep pebble street as in the picture. Will recommend if you are nearby, but not necessarily worth to travel across the city for it as there are a number of other Miradouro in the city. || One of the most beautiful viewpoints in Lisbon! It offers a fantastic panoramic view over the city, especially at sunset when the light is golden. There’s a small park with benches, trees, and even a kiosk for coffee or drinks. It can get a bit crowded, but the atmosphere is lively and pleasant. A must-visit spot for anyone exploring Lisbon || We took the funicular up to this little park for the views, and it was not disappointing! The 270 degree views of the city and surrounding mountains were breathtaking. There are two levels to this park, and plenty of park benches to relax on. There is a small cafe here, if you need a drink or a snack. I would definitely recommend visiting here, especially if you want some really great photos! || Great view of the City from the nearby Bairro Alto. We were fortunate to visit during the New Year's market. Excellent choice of Portuguese specialties (think serrano sandwich with sheep cheese) and Porto. || Lisbon is a city that pretends to be humble while casually seducing you at every corner. I left the house planning “just a short walk,” which, in this city, is the most unrealistic expectation you can possibly set. Five minutes in and you’re already climbing some Biblical staircase, questioning gravity, God, and your shoe choices. But then Lisbon apologizes. It always does. Usually with light. I wandered through streets that smelled like roasted chestnuts and mild chaos, past tiled façades that look like somebody finally let a poet design buildings. People spilled into cafés, dogs trotted around like they owned the place, and the whole city glowed in that gentle, old-European way — like a postcard that refuses to retire. Eventually I drifted uphill to Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara, which is the kind of viewpoint that doesn’t just offer a view — it offers perspective. The kind that makes you remember you still have a pulse. Up there, under a tree that had definitely lived through several empires, I found an artist named Anne Laidam, casually painting like she had all the time in the world. Her works were neon daydreams of Lisbon — trams, rooftops, broken sunlight — the whole city filtered through someone’s kindness. I wasn’t planning to buy art. (I never plan to buy art. Art plans to buy me.) But one of her trams looked at me with the exact attitude of a Lisbon cat: unimpressed, slightly judgmental, irresistibly charming. So, of course, I adopted it. And carried it home alongside a copy of Saramago — because every reckless purchase deserves a companion in philosophy. If you ever want a walk that feels like a conversation with a city that knows it’s beautiful but doesn’t brag: just start walking. Lisbon will take care of the rest. || Fantastic views of the city and the boats sailing past on the ocean. Plenty of food and drink stalls. || Amazing view, very nice vibe with bars and good street food around (a bit overpriced). Definitely worth checking if you're is Lisbon, specially near sunset hours. I'd recommend for couples who want a romantic vibe. || Best spot in Lisbon to stop and see the whole city. It has a dog park below and a nice spot in the back with a cat box that was tended by some retirees. Great place for photos, food, music and just relaxing. || This is one of Lisbon’s finest viewpoints, offering sweeping views over the red rooftops of Alfama and the Tagus River. Created in 1864, the viewpoint is laid out over two levels. The upper terrace features traditional Portuguese landscaping, while the lower terrace includes classical statues and a central fountain—creating a peaceful garden atmosphere in the heart of the city. A unique feature here is the azulejo tile map installed in 1952, which helps visitors identify Lisbon’s main landmarks visible from the terrace. || Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara is one of those viewpoints that instantly makes you slow down and appreciate Lisbon, especially from a Canadian tourist’s perspective. The garden setting is peaceful and well-kept, the terrace is spacious, and the panoramic view across the city toward the castle and the hills beyond is simply stunning. It’s an easy place to linger, whether you’re snapping photos, enjoying a quiet moment, or just soaking in the atmosphere with a coffee in hand. There’s a relaxed, welcoming vibe that makes it feel less rushed than other viewpoints, and it offers a perfect balance of beauty, comfort, and classic Lisbon charm. || Visited on June 13th during the annual festival, and the atmosphere was electric! The viewpoint was buzzing with lively stalls selling refreshing drinks and delicious fast food. While I couldn’t stay for the evening concert, the daytime energy alone was worth the trip. The panoramic views of Lisbon are breathtaking—you can see the entire city stretched out below, just as pictured. The charming fountain area offers plenty of seating, making it a perfect spot to relax with coffee or even enjoy a leisurely lunch. With ample benches and easy access via Tram 51E or local buses, this miradouro is both convenient and unforgettable. A must-visit for the views, vibes, and vibrant local culture! || Unbelievable view of the city and river and the castle. Best place to take in the beautiful charm of Lisboa! || Having seen amazing viewpoints all over the world, from the mountains of Greece to the fjords of New Zealand, I know a good view when I see one. Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara is a beautiful high viewpoint of Lisbon city. From here, you can see the castle across the city, the sea on one side, and even watch planes landing on the other.  We walked uphill for about 15 minutes to get there, which was a bit tiring. I was surprised to find food trucks once we arrived. There wasn't a lot of variety, but you can grab a drink and a snack. Just know they are tourist prices, like 10 Euros for a small cocktail and 15 Euros for a sandwich. Small hack: stop at a convenience store before you go up and grab your drinks there to save money.  Even with those prices, this spot is a must-visit if you go to Lisbon. The views are worth it. || An elevated terrace overlooking historic Lisbon. This large area is very popular for photos with a remarkable view. (Note that the streetcar which serviced this location experienced a tragic accident earlier in 2025. While still weighing heavily on the hearts of locals, the park is open and accessible.) || A great view which you can see all across lisbon. While we were sitting and enjoying the view there was live music which made the experience better and more relaxing. The choice of food around is good as there were plenty of bakeries around, the amount of seats were good so we didn't have to wait for sit and have some lunch. || A must see point of view if you’re visiting the city. The view is wonderful and the park is very well maintained with bench and a fountain. Highly recommended to everyone || Great spot for the sunrise and close to a couple cafe for some espresso and sweets for your reward for seeing the beautiful view of the harbor and city. || One of the best view point from this side of Lisbon. The Castelo de San jorge and the other lookouts on the other side can be seen, as well as the port. The park in this side is also very nice. It is not as high as the other but totally worth it to take some pictures of the landscape.

Eduardo VII Park is one of the most beautiful and relaxing green spaces in Lisbon. The park offers stunning panoramic views over the city and the Tagus River, making it a perfect spot for photos, walks, or simply enjoying the scenery. The wide paths are ideal for walking or jogging, and the well-maintained gardens add a peaceful atmosphere away from the busy city streets. One of the highlights is the impressive geometric garden design and the viewpoint at the top of the park, which provides a breathtaking perspective of Lisbon. The park is also very spacious, so it never feels overcrowded, even during busy hours. There are benches throughout the area, perfect for resting and enjoying the surroundings. Eduardo VII Park is great for families, couples, and solo travelers alike. It’s close to the city center and easy to access, making it a must-visit for anyone exploring Lisbon. Whether you’re looking for a quiet place to relax, take a walk, or admire the city from above, this park is definitely worth a visit. || We were in Lisbon for several days while waiting to start a cruise with NCL.  We stopped at the north end of this magnificent park and walk all the way to the southern end.  Lots of great views and spots for wonderful pics.  Several monuments along the way. || Parque Eduardo VII is a beautiful park with stunning views of the city and the river. It's beautifully maintained, with plenty of greenery and spacious walkways. It's a great place to escape the hustle and bustle of the city, take beautiful photos, and simply enjoy the atmosphere. A must-see if you're in Lisbon. || It's quite an amazing space. Jardim da Parada in Campo de Ourique is one of those rare places in Lisbon that feels genuinely local—quiet, shaded, and full of character. The garden is beautifully maintained, surrounded by big, old trees like sequoias and plane trees, with a small pond in the center where ducks and turtles paddle around peacefully. There’s a traditional bandstand, a nice playground for kids, and a charming little kiosk café that serves good coffee, light meals, and has plenty of outdoor seating under the trees. The vibe is calm and neighborly. People of all ages hang out here—seniors playing cards or reading, parents with strollers, kids running around, people walking their dogs, and others just sitting quietly enjoying the shade. One lovely touch is the old red phone booth that’s been turned into a tiny free library. It’s things like this that make the park feel alive and loved. The space isn’t huge, but it’s got everything it needs. Flower beds are always fresh, paths are clean, and there are benches everywhere. There are also two important statues tucked inside the garden—Maria da Fonte and Professor Ferreira de Macedo—which give it a bit of historical personality. But what really stood out this time was the buzz around the new underground development being planned. The city has announced a project to build a large underground parking garage beneath the garden. While I understand the need to ease traffic and create more parking in Campo de Ourique, I can’t help but feel concerned about the long-term impact this might have on such a delicate green space. There’s a real fear among locals that the construction will disturb the ecosystem of the garden—the roots of these beautiful old trees, the peace and quiet, and possibly the safety of the pond and wildlife. Right now, the garden feels timeless and balanced, and people are naturally worried that digging beneath it could change that. It’s a bit of a crossroads moment for Jardim da Parada. As it stands today, it’s one of the most welcoming and peaceful little parks in the city—loved by the neighborhood and full of everyday life. I hope that whatever happens with the development plans, the soul of the garden is preserved. If you're in Lisbon and want to experience a bit of calm, community, and natural charm, this place is well worth a visit. And if you’re a local—keep an eye on what’s planned beneath your feet. || Jardim da Parada is a compact, well-kept square that does the fundamentals right: plenty of shade, ample benches, smooth paths, a small playground, and a kiosk for quick coffee. Benches everywhere and the wonderful Banana Cafe inside which sells burgers and sandwiches, drinks and other refreshments where you can dine alfresco || 🌿 A Peaceful Oasis in the Middle of Lisbon ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5) We stumbled upon Jardim da Estrela on a warm afternoon, and it turned out to be one of the most peaceful and refreshing places we visited in Lisbon. It’s more than just a public park — it feels like a little urban sanctuary. The garden is beautifully maintained, filled with exotic plants, huge trees offering generous shade, and winding paths that invite you to slow down. What really stood out for me was the birdsong — there were so many birds, and their constant, melodic chirping made the whole place feel like a live sound bath. It’s incredibly soothing. If you have the time, don’t just walk through. Find a quiet corner, sit down, breathe, and maybe even meditate. This place is perfect for that. It’s not just visually calming, it actually sounds calming too. There are also benches, fountains, a lovely gazebo, and a charming little café nearby if you want to sit and sip something while watching the world go by. Families, joggers, solo readers, and locals chatting on benches all seem to coexist naturally here. It has a very authentic Lisbon energy — not overly touristy, just real life unfolding in a gorgeous setting.  Quick Ratings: Atmosphere: 10/10 Birdsong & Nature Vibe: 10/10 Relaxation Potential: 11/10 Accessibility: 10/10 Instagram View: 8.5/10 Highly recommend making time for it — especially if you’re feeling overstimulated by the city. It’s the kind of place that quietly resets your mood.  If this helped, I’d love a 👍 — and don’t forget to breathe deeply when you visit. 🌿✨ || I recently spent a peaceful afternoon at Jardim da Estrela in Lisbon, and it quickly became one of my favorite spots in the city. Located directly across from the grand Basílica da Estrela, this romantic-style park was inaugurated in 1852 and offers a refreshing blend of history, nature, and community life. The park spans 4.6 hectares and features winding paths shaded by exotic trees like jacarandas and ginkgoes, as well as beautifully maintained flower beds and small lakes with ducks and turtles. One of the standout features is the wrought-iron bandstand, originally built in 1884 and relocated here in 1936, which adds a touch of old-world charm. Families and locals gather here, especially on weekends, to enjoy the playgrounds, picnic areas, and the café with outdoor seating that serves light meals and drinks. The park is free to enter and open daily from 7 am to midnight, making it an accessible and welcoming space for everyone. Whether you're looking to relax, take a leisurely stroll, or immerse yourself in a bit of Lisbon's history, Jardim da Estrela offers a serene and delightful escape from the city's hustle and bustle. || I have a 5 year old and a 2 year old.
