Most invested money seems to go exclusively to gentrification related activities like high (over) priced luxury apartments, and international branded boring stores, and not into much improvement or upkeep of public facilities. || One of the most beautiful gardens in Lisbon. An excellent place to rest and every month you'll find new blossom || Beautiful spacious garden with lots of clean benches you can rest or have a picnic, or just read a book. It’s also a great place to people and dog watch. Lots of interesting dogs walk passed us. The trees are huge and stunning and there are stone sculptures around too. || So soothing place in Lisbon to sit and relax in lush green surrounding. Its facing iconic landmark church. The setup of garden is beautiful with amount of seating. It's pets friendly place. There is a small pond. I saw multiple people doing yoga and training which also add life to this place

Eduardo VII Park is one of the most beautiful and relaxing green spaces in Lisbon. The park offers stunning panoramic views over the city and the Tagus River, making it a perfect spot for photos, walks, or simply enjoying the scenery. The wide paths are ideal for walking or jogging, and the well-maintained gardens add a peaceful atmosphere away from the busy city streets. One of the highlights is the impressive geometric garden design and the viewpoint at the top of the park, which provides a breathtaking perspective of Lisbon. The park is also very spacious, so it never feels overcrowded, even during busy hours. There are benches throughout the area, perfect for resting and enjoying the surroundings. Eduardo VII Park is great for families, couples, and solo travelers alike. It’s close to the city center and easy to access, making it a must-visit for anyone exploring Lisbon. Whether you’re looking for a quiet place to relax, take a walk, or admire the city from above, this park is definitely worth a visit. || We were in Lisbon for several days while waiting to start a cruise with NCL.  We stopped at the north end of this magnificent park and walk all the way to the southern end.  Lots of great views and spots for wonderful pics.  Several monuments along the way. || Parque Eduardo VII is a beautiful park with stunning views of the city and the river. It's beautifully maintained, with plenty of greenery and spacious walkways. It's a great place to escape the hustle and bustle of the city, take beautiful photos, and simply enjoy the atmosphere. A must-see if you're in Lisbon. || It's quite an amazing space. Whether it's chilling, or events, or testing your photographic prowess, it fits the bill. There are usually tourists and residents generally around, and it's more lively during celebrations like Christmas. || It's a very beautiful and large park, perfect for a peaceful walk surrounded by nature. The view from the top of the park is spectacular. Depending on the time of year, there may be more or fewer tourists. On a sunny day with good weather, it's well worth a visit. || A great view of Lisbon from here, you can see the whole layout and scale looking down towards the river. Relaxed and friendly atmosphere as you view the scenery and monuments. You also get an excellent view of the planes coming into Lisbon. || A beautiful public park in Lisbon, Portugal with great views over the city. The top is great for photos. Good for a walk, sit and have lunch or a drink, or have your dog play around. || Wonderful Christmas Atmosphere! We visited Parque Eduardo VII during the Christmas season, and it was a fantastic experience. The Christmas market (Wonderland Lisboa) created such a pleasant and fun atmosphere. It’s a great spot, especially for young people and families, with plenty of amusement park rides, games, and festive food stalls. The park itself is beautiful, and the view from the top is breathtaking. Highly recommended if you are in Lisbon during the holidays! || Parque Eduardo VII is one of the best spots in Lisbon to enjoy a peaceful walk and take in a great view of the city. From the top of the park, you can see all the way down to the river and the Praça Marquês de Pombal. It’s a lovely place to relax, especially at sunset. The park is also very close to El Corte Inglés, so it’s easy to combine a visit with some shopping or a coffee break nearby. || What a great parque / jardim in central Lisbon. Plenty of spaces to walk and sit with many great restaurants, cafes , and quiosques nearby to enjoy the warm Lisbon sun

place_name: Garden of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation
reviews_content: Such a lovely garden full of paths and little bridges and loads of seating in the shade and great fun to explore and some statues too and we saw a heron and lots of ducks.  The amphitheatre was a real surprise too || Beautiful garden with long bamboo passage ways, a pond with lots of cute ducks, a small area to eat ice cream or coffee and a large area great for dogs. This is a great place to go on a walk with friends or go on a study session. Everything is full of vegetation and butterflies. Like an actual 'secret garden'. If you like fantasy books this is your place to go because it looks like a place in a fairytale. I cannot recommend this garden enough, especially for outdoor lovers. My description doesn't give this place enough justice. || This place is part of a foundation started by Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil tycoon and art lover. You can really feel his belief that “art is for everyone, and beauty means more when it’s shared.”  Right in the middle of the city, there’s this peaceful garden with tall trees, calm ponds, and quiet paths. I could take my time and enjoy the art without any rush. The way nature and art come together here left such a strong impression. || A very lovely garden, located in the center of the city. It’s super convenient to visit either by metro or different bus networks. Here, it’s more like a combination of different gardens, so there are lots of options to enjoy the sun, green, and overall atmosphere. Totally recommended to visit, including the museum inside. || Gorgeous space for all to enjoy for free - lots of areas to picnic, hang with friends, for kids to run around or bike, easy for strollers to get around. There are also two cafes and an ice cream shop - you can spend a whole day enjoying this beautifully maintained space. There must be a mighty team of gardeners tending to all the plants! What a valuable space for residents and visitors alike in this otherwise very densely developed city. || Gulbenkian always had beautiful gardens, around the museums buildings. Landscaping as Portuguese know how ! Now that the renovation of the modern museum is achieved, there is a new setting of this side of the gardens to discover, mix of Japanese zen design, existing garden style and a monumental, yet perfectly integrated awning. Inspiring place where to wander, with cafe and sometimes outdoor activities at the amphitheatre. Just mind the rush hours and some week-end can be crowded, as this place is since long praized by Portuguese and tourists ! || My primary objective was to visit the museum; however, due to renovations, the collection had been relocated.  I was disappointed by the limited number of items, particularly paintings, compared to my expectations. Nonetheless, the collection was aesthetically pleasing and unique.  The garden, however, was unappealing.  Perhaps I mistakenly visited the incorrect park, as signage was inadequate, requiring extensive navigation to locate the proper entrance. || Big enough to wander around. The noise of the city suddenly stops and everything becomes cooler. Part of it is like a jungle. Lots of people either solo or couples and a lot of families with small children. It is a really special place || Designed in the 1960s by Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles and António Viana Barreto, the garden is a beautifully landscaped urban oasis in the heart of Lisbon. The space features a harmonious blend of lakes, streams, terraced lawns, and forested paths—creating a tranquil environment for relaxation and reflection. The garden connects seamlessly with the main Gulbenkian Foundation building and museum, allowing visitors to experience art, architecture, and nature in one integrated setting. || Quiet, cozy park perfect for rest, private conversation with a friend or relaxation!

Genuinely, the hidden gem of Lisbon. Worth the climb up from the coast and my word, what an attraction!  We had no queue and a very chill inside experience.  Explore (and I do mean explore) the exotic meandering paths through the foliage, it's great to spend an hour or so.  A really nice bio diversity to look at and enjoy. Particularly enjoyed the banana tree 🍌  Really fairly priced and a fantastic cultural excursion.  HUGE recommend✌️ || Estufa Fria is a true oasis of tranquility in the heart of Lisbon. A wonderful place to escape the hustle and bustle of the city and enjoy the beauty of exotic plants, waterfalls, and cozy paths. The atmosphere is truly peaceful, with everything well-kept and thoughtfully designed down to the last detail. A wonderful place for a leisurely stroll, meditation, or a romantic date. A must-see for anyone who loves nature and wants to see a different, greener side of Lisbon. One of the most pleasant and inspiring places in the city! || Nature, garden, and park lovers will enjoy this spot. It offers about 30–45 minutes of peaceful walking surrounded by greenery and a small artificial lake.  Entrance costs less than €4 per person — a very reasonable price for the experience.  There’s also a café with a lovely terrace nearby, though it’s not directly accessible through the greenhouse area. || Verry beautiful, if you are traveling to Lisbon or just live here, I would recommend coming here. It’s very beautiful nature in the middle of the city come here and relax and enjoy your day. also, if you are a student or a younger person, you can get tickets for way cheaper. You just need to show your student card confirmation that you are a student and we paid our tickets for five euros the two of us so that’s amazing. || Really nice and super cheap. Cool plants and I saw baby ducks! there are so many rooms and pathways, despite it not being the biggest building in the world you really feel like you can get lost in there. Very thoughtfully and beautifully designed. || If you’re in Lisbon on a Sunday and want a peaceful escape from the city buzz, Estufa Fria is absolutely perfect. Hidden inside Parque Eduardo VII, this lush greenhouse feels like stepping into another world — calm, green, and full of life. 🌴  You’ll walk through tropical plants, waterfalls, and quiet pathways where time slows down. It’s beautifully maintained, not crowded, and filled with natural light filtering through the glass roof — ideal for a relaxed stroll or quiet reflection.  💚 Perfect for: •	A slow Sunday morning or afternoon •	Nature lovers, photographers, and couples •	Escaping the heat or city noise  Tip: Grab a coffee nearby afterward and enjoy the view over Avenida da Liberdade — it completes the perfect Sunday in Lisbon. || This is a great area to stroll through while enjoying beautiful flora and fauna. It is located at the far end of Eduardo VII Park. We spent 45 minutes there. || This botanical garden is my favourite hidden gem in Lisbon! Lots of great spots inside for photography and well maintained. Very affordable too! 🌿 || Most beautiful garden i have ever seen. So lush and green with the most monstera i have ever seen. So peaceful and relaxing. Toilets inside. Sat with goslings and ducklings and saw chickens and peacocks as well. Student tickets were €1.80! Highly recommend || This botanical garden is a true gem, offering a diverse collection of plants.  The layout is well-designed, creating a tranquil and relaxing atmosphere.  There are numerous benches and open spaces, perfect for enjoying a picnic lunch.  The affordable 3 euro entrance fee makes it an exceptional value.  A visit here is highly recommended for anyone seeking a peaceful escape.  The variety of flora provides something of interest for every visitor.  It's a wonderful place to spend a few hours immersed in nature.

My fav Lisbon park! Such a wonderful green space full of amazing trees and plants away from busy streets. The park used to be the garden of a wonderful Palace and is littered with beautiful old buildings and statues surrounded by nature and teaming with birds including chickens, geese peacocks and parakeets plus lots of stray cats. Set on a hill looking down to the river this parc is like stepping back in time. Never too busy and space to sit and just connect with nature. || Pretty neglected for the potential it has.  From dry vegetation that amounts, to destroyed/eroded pathways and all the buildings collapsing or ruined.  Among those a beautiful circular building with a greenhouse like glass roof, that by itself is worth the visit.  Just judge it too harshly by its state for it is in my opinion appealing as a rui ed site.  Can’t help to feel like patrimony is being lost without any concern or attempt to save it.  OVERALL IT IS FREE, so can’t really complain on the ticket price 😂  Therefore the relation price to quality of experience is actually juicy better than the Belém Botanical garden.  Also quite awesome if one is into urban ruin exploring! || I really liked this park, it is located a little away from the city center, therefore, there are very few people here and it is clean. There are several picnic tables, peacocks and ducks are walking, a beautiful view of the bridge, a lot of exotic plants and it's just nice to walk here. || A very wonderful and beautiful park.  - Diverse plants, interesting landscape, lots of greenery, and a fairly large area for walking. - There are buildings and fountains. They are partially abandoned but very atmospheric. - There is a lawn where people sunbathe in good weather. - Chickens, geese, peacocks, and cats roam freely around the area. - The park also has a restroom and an enclosed area for dog walking || A beautiful, tranquil space with magnificent cactuses. The chickens run wild, and it feels like a place from a different era. The views of the bay, framed by the plants are something you don't get in many other places either. || It’s a beautiful park with a rare tree that it’s worth spending some time with. Although it’s not for those with walking difficulties as it has elevations and unevenness. Love that there are chickens, peacocks and geese roaming freely. And there are benches for those who wants a place to chill and have their meals. || It has the potential to be the best park in the city if anyone would invest in it.  It has: In the central part is a big lawn, great for picnics and enjoying the peace and quiet (ducks, peacocks, gees and chickens excluded). To the west of the lawn there is a dog or children park, i was not sure, but it is fenced so they don't bother those that are allergic to them. On the other side to the east of the lawn there is a pond with ducks. Further east from the lawn there are staircases that lead to the closed section unfortunately, with a garden done in french style, with a symmetrical pattern of short hedges outlining the flowers planted there. And by looking at it on google maps it is apparent that on the other side of it there are staircases again leading to another similar area that is also closed off. To the north of the lawn there are buildings. First up right next to the lawn there is a glass dome that looks like a theater of some sort, although small and half the glass roof is shattered, then behind it there are buildings that look like maybe they were coops for the birds that are now running around. Coming right behind that is a plato with a big circular water feature that isn't working and half around it is a wall with a (closed) gate that leads into a (overgrown) corridor that leads to some sort of i guess important building. Next to the corridor starts a cactus garden that has been left unchecked for far too long. Even though cactuses are thriving, the paths through it are bit harder to navigate so caution is advised. || Absolutely got surprised by this little park in a quite busy city district. I was expecting an average garden park in the middle of a concrete jungle, but when I entered I got a real different feeling. Being used to Lisbon's buzziness, I am often missing the nature. This park has a very wild feeling to it. Even though it still offers the clean open grass area to lie down and enjoy a picnic with friends and family, you feel like in the middle of untouched nature just a few steps away from the central grass area. The cactus garden offers exactly what you expect and more. There are wild plants and of course 🌵🌵 but there are also free running chicken and even peacocks with beautiful feathers. Feels very untouched, and has even a great view to the bridge. The constant airplane crossing still remind you that you are almost in central Lisbon. Definitely worth a visit if you like wild nature and peace just around the corner. || Very calm space - the perfect get away from the busy touristy areas. Some visitors are sunbathing on the grass. The cactus garden impressed me with the size of the cactuses - some of them were twice my height. There are many happy birds but mostly roosters, crowing non-stop. It’s probably a way to prove their masculinity in front of the chicks… actually I don’t know - it’s not my business :) There are several neglected structures that are still quite beautiful. || What a beautiful, interesting little park! Off the beaten track, loads of ducks, geese, chickens, and pea-fowl. The cactus garden area was where the chickens were plotting to take over the world lol. So glad we happened upon it. || The park could be beautiful as I believe once was, but today it is very poorly maintained with destroyed paths, overgrown bushes and sad abandoned buildings. It probably wouldn't even be expensive to restore it, so I'm confused how they could let this happen. || A nice park to have a picnic. The few features are the peacocks and the geese’s. And the Dragoeiro plant at the south entrance. I read that it’s rare and only a few hundreds left. The park did have a lot of variations of flora, maybe it’s winter time. Oh.. the white roosters seems to monopolised the north entrance. They are cute and naturally roaming. Just an easy part to walk. Nearby is Jardim Estrella which is smaller but probably more family friendly. You could see my other  review there. || This park is extremely underrated!! LOOK AT ALL THESE CHICKENS!!! I was so surprised and tickled to walk through….chickens, cats, many differently types of cactus (and mature too), and a fantastic view of 25 of April Bridge!!! If I lived here I would come often to the park. Peaceful and a jungle of endless exploration. || This a beautiful park that is located off the beaten path. It is quite hilly but there is plenty of shade. The main reason to go is to see all the species of native birds. I saw chickens, geese, pigeons, and peacocks. Just make sure to not step in the animal dung! || We were lucky to find this place. It's very authentic and very beautiful in terms of authentic landscape design. Just have a look at my photos. We could see many photographers that make photo sessions there. There are many white chickens, colorful peacocks, ducks, gooses, etc. There is big walking area and also some field where you can take sun bath or sit at the tables and have a picknick. || There's a hidden gem in the park - a collection of one of the oldest cacti on the planet. It's a free admission to the park except for the restroom, you'll have to pay for adults. There's a water fountain in the park, so you can fill your bottle with it. We visited during Easter holiday, and it was very nice to see that someone was sweet and thoughtful to "hide" some candies in trees and bushes for kids. || I love this garden: feels so wild with all the wonderful animals! Peacocks, chickens, cats, geese and more.  Highly recommend the cactus garden 🌵 the only downside for me is there’s no like little place for refreshments or drinks (I couldn’t find a water tap either). So come prepared!!! || It's the perfect spot for a picnic, to enjoy a sunny day, or simply for a walk. The park offers a calm setting for outdoor activities and relaxation. || Beautiful calm park with a nice cactus garden, free chicken and peacocks. Very nice. || A peaceful park in Lisbon with quiet paths winding around ponds and towering cacti, plus the occasional rooster to hear or peacock to spot. Perfect for a lunchtime break or a change of scenery. It offers ancient trees and impressive views of the Ponte 25 de Abril. A must-see hidden gem.

On September 7, I visited Jardim Amália Rodrigues and witnessed a partial blood moon eclipse under a cloudy sky. The park, with its wide open spaces and elevated views, was a perfect place to capture the moment in photos. Even with the clouds, the experience was memorable and unique. || Lovely park and bar with a pool to cool your feet after a long day walking..cycling and generally getting about. The drink prices are reasonable. Definitely call in here if your in Lisbon. It's beautiful. || It is a delightful urban oasis at the northern edge of Parque Eduardo VII. Whether you’re after a peaceful retreat, a picturesque spot for photos, or simply want to enjoy sweeping views of Lisbon, this hidden gem is definitely worth a visit. || Somehow hidden from turistic path, a small part of the parc is dedicated to famous singer. || Designed by Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles and opened in 1996, the garden was named in 2000 in tribute to Amália Rodrigues, Portugal’s legendary fado singer. The garden features a variety of trees and plants, with quiet walking paths and benches that make it ideal for rest, reflection, or a peaceful stroll. || Lovely setting, but the garden is boring and very disappointing. Fans of Amalia Rodrigues must be very disappointed. Like the rest of the area, very poorly maintained and pedestrian access is dreadful. A missed opportunity, big time. || Great views and perfect location to see sunset over Lisbon with some live music in the background || Park with a great view of central Lisbon 💚 The shade of the trees makes for a great place to sit down and relax a bit. The sun beats down quite mercilessly at around midday. The many benches are a welcome addition for weary travelers. || What a beautiful park. With a nice a cosy bar to hang out and have a drink while enjoying the fresh atmosphere. || This little garden looked like part of the Parque Eduardo VII. The statue at the entrance was interesting.

Very interesting local park where multiple varieties of poultry roam free! There’s also good to great dining options in and around the park, such as the Italian restaurant in the middle of the park that offers indoor and outdoor seating. || It made my day! To see all these animals in sp urban place🐔🐥🐤  Gives some special rural energy!! … || Lisbon is a busy city. You wouldn't expect a bunch of chickens and roosters chilling in tiny garden right in the city center... and yet, here, you do.  It's a gorgeous spot. Come and enjoy! || Small peaceful park with chickens & ducks 🐔 … || Review of Campo dos Mártires da Pátria – 5 Stars  If you’re looking for a peaceful, green escape in the heart of Lisbon that also offers a quirky and heartwarming surprise, Campo dos Mártires da Pátria is an absolute gem. This urban park blends history, nature, and charm in a way that makes you want to stay for hours. It’s one of those rare places that feels alive—quiet yet full of character.  The park is beautifully maintained with wide paths, benches under tall trees, and a calm atmosphere perfect for walking, reading, or simply breathing in the serenity. It’s surrounded by elegant buildings and steeped in historical importance, making it more than just a green space—it’s a cultural landmark.  But what truly stole my heart and made me give this park a glowing 5-star rating were the chickens and roosters. Yes, you read that right. Real, free-roaming gallinas y gallos live here, wandering through the grass and greeting visitors with cheerful clucks and crowing. It’s such a unique and unexpected detail that adds life and magic to the place. They’re charming, friendly, and seem completely at home—bringing joy to kids and adults alike. I absolutely love them. They’re the soul of the park for me.  If you’re in Lisbon and want a quiet spot full of life, history, and the sweet company of feathered friends, don’t miss Campo dos Mártires da Pátria. It’s a small paradise with a big heart. || Great central park in Lisbon that is quite family friendly. With an outdoor beverage place and loads of friendly animals such ducks and chickens about to keep you and your kids eye's busy.  Campo dos Mártires da Pátria, commonly known by its former name Campo de Santana, is a street in the parish of Arroios in Lisbon.  It occupies the upper part of the trough that separates the two converging valleys in the city center, which correspond to Avenida da Liberdade and Avenida Almirante Reis. It is a space full of history, located in the central area of ​​Lisbon, which served as a slaughterhouse in the 16th century and which has known many uses over the last two centuries, such as a bullring, from 1831 to 1889, the realization of the Feira da  From 1835 to 1882 and still a vegetable market in the mid-19th century. || Cutest park with ducks, chickens, roosters, and a little water feature. The restaurant at the park is also great and opened all day serving food (unlike many local places that stop serving real food in the afternoon).  We love this park for the kids to run around and climb trees.  Great for a stroll with stroller and kids. Safe and clean.  Sometimes some homeless people are on the benches but that’s city life so doesn’t bother me. || we were there when they were feeding the ducks, geese, roosters, and pigeons. They take care of all the birds here with ponds and even a coop. We just sat and watched for an hour or something and it was so entertaining || Very peculiar place to relax. || Lisboa was one of the cities I had the most fun exploring on a skateboard. Everyone is very friendly and the food is just fantastic. As long as you don't fall into the tourist traps you will be fine. You'll find that the more you explore this city the more the culture gets to you.

place_name: Parque Urbano do Vale da Montanha
reviews_content: Beautiful park with so many spaces to let your dog run free, to picnic, or to exercise (lots of big hills!). My dog and I love it. || Great place to enjoy some nature inside the city, great walks, enjoy the sun. || Lovely view and very nice atmosphere || I planted a tree here! || Very ample and great for walks. || Very cosy... In the middle of the city. || A pleasant park for strolling or exercising, in the center of Lisbon. It's a very large park, connected to Bela Vista park. It has a kiosk at the entrance and limited parking spaces. || A huge space with several spots to enjoy the sunrise or sunset. The view of the moon is also beautiful. Views of Olaias, the Tagus River, Areeiro, Boa Vista, and Chelas. There's space for picnics, plenty of shade, and a drinking fountain. || I really liked this park, it was a pleasant surprise! 😀 It has a kiosk with friendly people and live music (we went on a Saturday) and a wide variety of food and drinks. The park is spacious, has a very fun and challenging playground, is served by a bike path, and parking is easy but paid during the week. I recommend a visit; you can spend a very pleasant afternoon here. || Excellent place for a walk or a run. Plenty of green space, well-marked paths, although in winter it can be a bit difficult to do in some areas closer to the perimeter due to lack of lighting. Bonus points for the new (excellent) cycle path that runs through it and allows you to enjoy the route in a way that is semi-isolated from pedestrians. || Pleasant urban park, good for basic physical exercise. Excellent place to observe the various train compositions that serve the capital with arrivals and departures from Santa Apolónia Station or Gare do Oriente. Unfortunately, there are no functioning drinking fountains (either they have been removed or are disconnected from the public network), probably to increase the sale of bottled water at the kiosk. It is equally regrettable to note that the vast majority of dog owners, in total disregard for current regulations, walk their dogs without a leash, without a muzzle for potentially dangerous breeds, and do not pick up their droppings. || A very nice park for children, extremely clean and well-maintained. The park has a kiosk with an outdoor seating area; the girls who run it are very friendly, they have delicious homemade popsicles and toasties that are just as good! The place gets sun all day! Great for a lunch break if you work nearby, for an after-work coffee, or even as a family since you can always keep an eye on the children. I recommend it. || I love this kiosk in the park.  Natural juices, homemade popsicles, good coffee, and a lot of friendliness that we're not used to. The variety of cakes and savory snacks isn't huge, but what they have is good quality. They always have fresh water for the dogs after a walk in the park. They also have a playground with accessories for children. I go whenever I can. || A pleasant place to relax, even in a busy city like Lisbon. || Excellent place for walking, running, skateboarding, rollerblading, and cycling. I just think the stone interruptions between the bike paths are very poorly done because if you're skateboarding or rollerblading, it's almost mandatory to stop to avoid falling. And the lack of drinking fountains is also a drawback. || A very pleasant park, good for children, for walks, etc…  But I think it lacks some playground equipment for younger children. || Great place for walking or running. || I was there in December and it was quiet; it seems to be busier in the summer. And the kiosk there is an excellent idea; you can have a snack, enjoy the view, and if you have children, they'll be entertained and under your supervision. || An urban park that integrates perfectly into the city, allowing you to experience nature. It connects to Bela Vista Park and Olaias. It offers spaces for various types of recreation, a kiosk, and a landscaped vegetation plan adapted to the climate, featuring native species. Very good! || A great place to stretch your legs and relax. In a decade, if it continues to be cared for and maintained, it will be a new green lung for the city, with plenty of shade inviting relaxation and picnics. || Very good! Well frequented. The girls at the kiosk are very friendly. I like being there in contact with nature. There should be more trees, because on very sunny days there is little shade. || A park that added area to Bela Vista Park, with only one drawback: there are quite a few dogs roaming around, and they leave their droppings in the green areas. Otherwise, it's a good place for a walk. || A free, unobstructed natural space, a balm in the middle of the city. Cars are not allowed, only pedestrians, cyclists, etc. || Peace, nature, and fresh air – great for relaxing in the city. Plenty of space for walking and many hidden corners to discover. Good for family outings, with the dog, cycling, or running. || This park is amazing! Perfect for a walk, a picnic, or strolling with our four-legged friends. (It has dog water fountains.) || Excellent for walking and spending time, the only thing it lacks is a little more lighting; there are paths that are difficult to walk on after dark. || Nice green space, a very pleasant kiosk, great for walking, taking children for a run, playing or cycling. Also good for taking animals for a run.

Jardim da Parada in Campo de Ourique is one of those rare places in Lisbon that feels genuinely local—quiet, shaded, and full of character. The garden is beautifully maintained, surrounded by big, old trees like sequoias and plane trees, with a small pond in the center where ducks and turtles paddle around peacefully. There’s a traditional bandstand, a nice playground for kids, and a charming little kiosk café that serves good coffee, light meals, and has plenty of outdoor seating under the trees. The vibe is calm and neighborly. People of all ages hang out here—seniors playing cards or reading, parents with strollers, kids running around, people walking their dogs, and others just sitting quietly enjoying the shade. One lovely touch is the old red phone booth that’s been turned into a tiny free library. It’s things like this that make the park feel alive and loved. The space isn’t huge, but it’s got everything it needs. Flower beds are always fresh, paths are clean, and there are benches everywhere. There are also two important statues tucked inside the garden—Maria da Fonte and Professor Ferreira de Macedo—which give it a bit of historical personality. But what really stood out this time was the buzz around the new underground development being planned. The city has announced a project to build a large underground parking garage beneath the garden. While I understand the need to ease traffic and create more parking in Campo de Ourique, I can’t help but feel concerned about the long-term impact this might have on such a delicate green space. There’s a real fear among locals that the construction will disturb the ecosystem of the garden—the roots of these beautiful old trees, the peace and quiet, and possibly the safety of the pond and wildlife. Right now, the garden feels timeless and balanced, and people are naturally worried that digging beneath it could change that. It’s a bit of a crossroads moment for Jardim da Parada. As it stands today, it’s one of the most welcoming and peaceful little parks in the city—loved by the neighborhood and full of everyday life. I hope that whatever happens with the development plans, the soul of the garden is preserved. If you're in Lisbon and want to experience a bit of calm, community, and natural charm, this place is well worth a visit. And if you’re a local—keep an eye on what’s planned beneath your feet. || Jardim da Parada is a compact, well-kept square that does the fundamentals right: plenty of shade, ample benches, smooth paths, a small playground, and a kiosk for quick coffee. Central location, steady footfall from locals, and a calm, family-friendly atmosphere throughout the day. Clean, safe, and predictable—ideal for short breaks or reading in the open air. É um dos melhores sítios de Campo de Ourique. || Without question this is one of my favorite parks! The quiosque has one of the best burger-fry combos you can get anywhere.  I'm here a few times a week, finding it to be peaceful, grounding, and a place to be with community. || A nice garden in the fancy zone of Campo  Grande. Lots of people during the sunny weekends of the autumn. Sometimes also market with handicrafts. Good for a walk with the family. || Nice place to take a break when doing the shopping in Campo area. Little playground for kids is good touch. || Well kept. A little oasis in the city with local artisans offering handmade items (maybe that is just on the weekends). || One of my favourite Parks in Lisboa. Perfect for young children and dog walks. There's also a kiosk next to the play park that serves drinks and snacks || great place to take young children for a playful time and nice hangout for a coffee or tea || I love it here! The trees are gorgeous and provide shadows and beauty to the square. Always lively with kids, doggies, and elderly playing chess. Loads of restaurants and shops  in the adjacent streets, including Arcádia (chocolate), A Padaria Portuguesa, and a good Italian restaurant called Memoria. One cannot go wrong! 🙂 || Beautiful park to walk through. Lots of kids playing and laughing. Pond with ducks and turtles. Beautiful trees

Pleasant green space with coffee shops and bars as well as a children’s play area. One of the bars has live entertainment. At one end of the park, stunning view of Lisbon and the river. || One of the best gardens in Lisbon!! Very chill and relatively less crowded than the other famous parks here, so if you’re looking for a serenity, this might be a good spot. Easy to come here by tram or metro after walking a bit. || Great place for a hanging out - beautiful scenery, centrally located near the bairro alto - I can totally recommend || Bistro/restaurant in the park, perfect for a timeout from sightseeing in the shade, there was a singer singing fado, the food was just es expected, warm, tasty, and the whole experience was just perfect || It’s a good place to sit for some time. There is free access to drinking water and also a place where the public can charge their phones for free. However, you need to bring your own charger. || Lovely park to rest the knackered feet after walking up and down hills all day || A wonderful garden with some lovely plants and flowers to view.  On a hot day, this is a great garden to visit. With many trees to provide some shade, you can enjoy the suns rays as well as keeping chilled.  It's quite a small garden, but with a small fee of 5 Euro it is worth a visit (if you like gardens). There are some cool art displays within the gardens also, which fit into the space nicely.  Overall these gardens offer good value fro money and is lovely to walk around and explore new and interesting plants. || Even at afternoon heat a good place to relax. With small cafe and sometimes live music. Nice! || My neighborhood park. It's awesome. Beautiful trees. Farmer's market on Saturdays. Friendly kiosks for a cold beer or fresh pastry. It's golden! || Wonderful spot to relax after walking all day, or go for a stroll and grab a snack and/or drink at one of two kiosks or the small restaurant. Playground is brand new and has something for all ages. Statues and artwork are a treat to discover and contemplate. Plenty of seating and grass around the park for lounging around.

Nice park outside the botanical garden with peacocks 🦚 … || Amazing place to have a rest a watch a birds || It was a Beautiful lake || The lake is fenced off for the animals; but surrounding it are wooded areas with lawns, great for picnics and leisure time with friends and family. I did that today, the view is beautiful. || Very beautiful and peaceful, in this place you can enjoy a moment of calm while appreciating different species of birds. || Poor ducks, the water is so dirty. || Beautiful, and the upstairs bar was fantastic; I loved it. I was there, peacefully enjoying a drink, when suddenly I found myself surrounded by these wonderful birds, the peacocks, minding their own business, not bothering anyone. The waiter eventually shooed them away, but I enjoyed the experience. || A very beautiful park where you can simply relax in the sun. Highly recommended as a rest stop on the way to the botanical gardens. || Really nice for a short walk, unfortunately many places in the greenhouse are blocked, a shame || Absolutely beautiful. Very well maintained. I highly recommend it to anyone who loves botany.

A rare find in Lisbon it seems, a quiet shaded park. It had picnic benches with tables, benches in the shade, grass to lie on, a cafe and is very peaceful.  Having said that it does feel like it needs some attention as much of it is run down and the prevailing smell of urine is not so appealing with your lunch || While the view of Lisbon from here is undeniably beautiful, the park itself has sadly declined. It’s often not clean and no longer feels safe, especially after the evening. The presence of homeless people can be unsettling. It's best to visit during the day for the vista and avoid it after dark. No nearby toilets. || Jardim da Cerca da Graça is a hidden gem with an absolutely fabulous view. It’s pretty simple to get there by bus, but just a heads-up, it does involve walking a fair bit downhill after you get off. Still, totally worth it. || It’s the perfect spot to relax, enjoy a picnic, or simply take in the lovely views over Lisbon. The atmosphere is calm, with plenty of shade, open green spaces, and a small café to grab a drink. A wonderful place to unwind and escape the city’s busy streets for a while. || Having just arrived in Lisbon, we dropped off our bags and got our hike on. We ended up at this great park to relax in, and one of the few that had a playground. We thoroughly enjoyed listening to the dogs playing in the wide-open green space above the playground, one even sounded like a turkey gobbling along. || Very cute little park with stunning views. There is a wee cafe/bar in it with a toilet, a children’s play area and plenty of green space to lie down and relax. Also has amazing views || It’s nice to have a park, but the many many dogs leave behind a lot of dog poop. Even if picked up, this makes your clothes and blanket dirty, and I mean really dirty. Even worse, millions of flies. || Nice little park - an oasis in Graca. There’s a big grassy bit where dogs run around. Be careful of the dog poo though! There’s also a little kiosk for drinks and snacks too || One of the best parks in Lisbon. The view is great, the atmosphere is chill and cool. There’s always a lot of cute dogs running around. You can also get a coffee at the small roundy there :) || A bit abandoned park with full of ugly graffitis. City view is nice but we were really disappointed about no way out anywhere except the entrance (don't believe google maps, there is no direct "green" trail). || Nice park. There is open space for doing some sporty activities. I also enjoyed staircase with street art near the park. One of my favorite spots in Lisbon || The day I passed through this park it was all quiet. Nice view all the same. || This park is some what hidden. Most people come here to sun bath, read a book, smoke weed, you play with there dog. Lots of trees around to stay cool. || I got to this park kind of by accident, but it became one of my favorite spots in Lisboa. Surrounded by buildings and unfolding paths, it's a dreamy spatial experience. The great view to the castle doesn't hurt. Ideal for a picnic, beers with friends, play ball, walk the dog, even a date. || It’s a gorgeous place with so much potential. Lots squatters, make sure to watch your children. Suggest the português government gives them a better home! || This guy and his two dogs have lived in the dog park for 4 months straight with all their nasty equipment spread out like they own the place. What is wrong with this city? || DO NOT BRING CHILDREN HERE. While the space is beautiful, unfortunately it’s now full of homeless people and off leash dogs, including in the children’s play equipment. Avoid. || A nice relaxing park where you can enjoy, rest, read, have a picnic or spend time with you friends. Seems to be a dog friendly place 🐕. … || i did not mean to come here, my friend must have sent the wrong location💔💔 … || The garden was well designed for kids and dogs. But unfortunately it has not been maintained and it's now very dangerous for both kids and dogs. People with drug addiction have taken over the dog and kid park and there is litter, ash, and even syringes left about. Whoever is responsible for maintaining the park, you need to step up. Clean this park up and properly maintain it. Get the addicts to move elsewhere. I can't believe anyone would treat a kids playground this way. It's very sad.

The viewpoint at Parque Eduardo VII offers a wide, open panorama over the city, stretching from the park’s geometric gardens down to Avenida da Liberdade and the river. It’s a peaceful spot, especially in the early morning or late afternoon, and the elevated position gives a great sense of Lisbon’s layout.  The area around the viewpoint is spacious and easy to access, though not as atmospheric as some of the older miradouros in the historic districts. Still, it’s a worthwhile stop if you’re already exploring the park or want a less crowded viewpoint with a clear, unobstructed city view. || Great location and view,  plenty of seating spaces too.  Great scenic view of the city and theres a handy cicktsil bar on hand where ypu can relax in a bit of style and comfort,  failing that there is an icecream stall too,  the hike from the river front can be a bit daunting at tines but worth the climb || A peaceful spot with views over Lisbon. Perfect for photos or just relaxing in the sun. The walk up is easy, and the park itself is well-kept. Best visited at sunset for amazing colors and a calm atmosphere. || Some peace and tranquility from the city hustle & bustle! Theres a sweet high spot where u can take photos of the city touching the sea with the LISBOA sign. Get here early to avoid the crowds as they wanna get images etc. || Perfect View of Lisbon!!! Very nice place and quite romantic as you walk through the parc! || Worth the walk and it is very beautiful. I hear it is even better in the spring with the florals. The Lisboa sign is here too, much less crowded than other areas. || Great observation deck with beautiful views over the city and the river. A nice place to relax and enjoy the scenery. || I was looking for a spot to do a bit of jogging and ended up here. The area has a nice elevation, perfect for a more engaging run, and I wasn’t the only one enjoying it — there were other joggers, a few tourists, and locals relaxing in the garden with their dogs. The combination of activity and friendly atmosphere gave the place a warm and welcoming touch. || Very nice place, nice walk too. Good for picnics and watching a majestic view || Awesome view- both sunset and sunrise are amazing- great place to visit at any time of the day.

place_name: Garden of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation
reviews_content: Such a lovely garden full of paths and little bridges and loads of seating in the shade and great fun to explore and some statues too and we saw a heron and lots of ducks.  The amphitheatre was a real surprise too || Beautiful garden with long bamboo passage ways, a pond with lots of cute ducks, a small area to eat ice cream or coffee and a large area great for dogs. This is a great place to go on a walk with friends or go on a study session. Everything is full of vegetation and butterflies. Like an actual 'secret garden'. If you like fantasy books this is your place to go because it looks like a place in a fairytale. I cannot recommend this garden enough, especially for outdoor lovers. My description doesn't give this place enough justice. || This place is part of a foundation started by Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil tycoon and art lover. You can really feel his belief that “art is for everyone, and beauty means more when it’s shared.”  Right in the middle of the city, there’s this peaceful garden with tall trees, calm ponds, and quiet paths. I could take my time and enjoy the art without any rush. The way nature and art come together here left such a strong impression. || A very lovely garden, located in the center of the city. It’s super convenient to visit either by metro or different bus networks. Here, it’s more like a combination of different gardens, so there are lots of options to enjoy the sun, green, and overall atmosphere. Totally recommended to visit, including the museum inside. || Gorgeous space for all to enjoy for free - lots of areas to picnic, hang with friends, for kids to run around or bike, easy for strollers to get around. There are also two cafes and an ice cream shop - you can spend a whole day enjoying this beautifully maintained space. There must be a mighty team of gardeners tending to all the plants! What a valuable space for residents and visitors alike in this otherwise very densely developed city. || Gulbenkian always had beautiful gardens, around the museums buildings. Landscaping as Portuguese know how ! Now that the renovation of the modern museum is achieved, there is a new setting of this side of the gardens to discover, mix of Japanese zen design, existing garden style and a monumental, yet perfectly integrated awning. Inspiring place where to wander, with cafe and sometimes outdoor activities at the amphitheatre. Just mind the rush hours and some week-end can be crowded, as this place is since long praized by Portuguese and tourists ! || My primary objective was to visit the museum; however, due to renovations, the collection had been relocated.  I was disappointed by the limited number of items, particularly paintings, compared to my expectations. Nonetheless, the collection was aesthetically pleasing and unique.  The garden, however, was unappealing.  Perhaps I mistakenly visited the incorrect park, as signage was inadequate, requiring extensive navigation to locate the proper entrance. || Big enough to wander around. The noise of the city suddenly stops and everything becomes cooler. Part of it is like a jungle. Lots of people either solo or couples and a lot of families with small children. It is a really special place || Designed in the 1960s by Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles and António Viana Barreto, the garden is a beautifully landscaped urban oasis in the heart of Lisbon. The space features a harmonious blend of lakes, streams, terraced lawns, and forested paths—creating a tranquil environment for relaxation and reflection. The garden connects seamlessly with the main Gulbenkian Foundation building and museum, allowing visitors to experience art, architecture, and nature in one integrated setting. || Quiet, cozy park perfect for rest, private conversation with a friend or relaxation! || Best place to hide when it is very hot. There are lots of nice shaded banks to sit and rest under the trees. || Lovely place to escape the bustle of Lisbon for some hours, still in the middle of the city. Grab a picnic towel, a book and sunscreen and lay down for the afternoon. The grass field in the garden is lovely to get some sun light. Even in winter. || one of the most eye-relaxing places seen during my life. An intellectual and thoughtful place , where you can nurture your mind and abandon  everyday tortuosity. the place I’ve been missing the most since my departure from Lisbon. || A really nice place to wander around, there's lots of corners tucked away if you want to sit by yourself or have a conversation. And they have ducks! || Well-known park in Lisbon where people go to just hang-out, relax, create, work and have a love/get out of here relationship with all the ducks! The museum offers a lot of commodities as well and many times have free entry events :) || So relaxing to walk the grounds of the garden. There are shady as well as sunny areas depending on what you prefer and a cafe for your meals. The ducks and the water areas make it even more attractive. Unfortunately a large part of the grounds are under renovation, so we couldn’t walk there. Still, the air is crisp and the garden is well maintained for visitors. || One of the most gorgeous public gardens I've been to with stunning art, landscaping, plants and wildlife. They are doing extensive renovation in a section of it so it's blocked off (and will be incredible once done) but there's still plenty of areas to wander on paths, sit on benches, grab something at cafe and sit outside and enjoy the birds. I brought my camera and had so much fun capturing images of the Spring babies. Truly a remarkable place for all to enjoy. || A perl in the city of Lisbon. Strongly suggested if you have any minimal appreciation for plants and greenery. They have three great greenhouses with a wide variety of plants from all-over the planet. It also looks like a sustainable place to support with a visit. Entrance tickets are cheap and discounts are available. || Beautiful place to go with time on a sunny day to enjoy yourself and/or friends. Lot's of benches to sit or grass to lay down if you want. Different areas to see and walk to. I really loved even though it was drizzling when I went there. I will come back tho. || My favorite park in Lisbon — full of artwork, exotic plants, winding paths, and little ponds. Despite all that, there’s still plenty of open space to sit or lie down and relax. My 10-year-old son loved it, too.

Huge park. Lost of places to sit and enjoy || Great space for music festivals. Nice environment. Lately a bit dry, causing some dust in the air,  but you gotta deal with it. Still ok. || It was amazing, I went there for the Rock in Rio festival, but the park is amazing. It has stunning views and lots of space. Perfect for picnics with family and friends! || Spacious but if it's windy it's awful.. Super dusty that you will need to use a scarf to cover your face like you're in the desert. Needless to say that it's not a good place for a festival either || Very nice place to walk, jogging and just take a rest. Very quiet, big enough. Has picnic tables, also comfortable for reading and study. || Super large park, great for running! But careful, its very hilly. || Lovely neighborhood park, off leash dogs galore, nice view of the city and a few trails to escape the tourist trap of downtown without having to travel too far. || Nice park with trails to walk, jog or ride a bike. However, there is not much shade. || Well organised and run festival. Relaxed setting and crowd. Great to see top bads like Pet Shop Boys live. || We loved this festival! Great bands and the park's hills allowed us to see the main stage from far. Lots of stepped viewing points also available where u could sit and have a drink when not dancing! Toilets were well-organised and staff helpful. Fun, free activities and photo/ video souvenirs also included in price. Would recommend!

Very interesting local park where multiple varieties of poultry roam free! There’s also good to great dining options in and around the park, such as the Italian restaurant in the middle of the park that offers indoor and outdoor seating. || It made my day! To see all these animals in sp urban place🐔🐥🐤  Gives some special rural energy!! … || Lisbon is a busy city. You wouldn't expect a bunch of chickens and roosters chilling in tiny garden right in the city center... and yet, here, you do.  It's a gorgeous spot. Come and enjoy! || Small peaceful park with chickens & ducks 🐔 … || Review of Campo dos Mártires da Pátria – 5 Stars  If you’re looking for a peaceful, green escape in the heart of Lisbon that also offers a quirky and heartwarming surprise, Campo dos Mártires da Pátria is an absolute gem. This urban park blends history, nature, and charm in a way that makes you want to stay for hours. It’s one of those rare places that feels alive—quiet yet full of character.  The park is beautifully maintained with wide paths, benches under tall trees, and a calm atmosphere perfect for walking, reading, or simply breathing in the serenity. It’s surrounded by elegant buildings and steeped in historical importance, making it more than just a green space—it’s a cultural landmark.  But what truly stole my heart and made me give this park a glowing 5-star rating were the chickens and roosters. Yes, you read that right. Real, free-roaming gallinas y gallos live here, wandering through the grass and greeting visitors with cheerful clucks and crowing. It’s such a unique and unexpected detail that adds life and magic to the place. They’re charming, friendly, and seem completely at home—bringing joy to kids and adults alike. I absolutely love them. They’re the soul of the park for me.  If you’re in Lisbon and want a quiet spot full of life, history, and the sweet company of feathered friends, don’t miss Campo dos Mártires da Pátria. It’s a small paradise with a big heart. || Great central park in Lisbon that is quite family friendly. With an outdoor beverage place and loads of friendly animals such ducks and chickens about to keep you and your kids eye's busy.  Campo dos Mártires da Pátria, commonly known by its former name Campo de Santana, is a street in the parish of Arroios in Lisbon.  It occupies the upper part of the trough that separates the two converging valleys in the city center, which correspond to Avenida da Liberdade and Avenida Almirante Reis. It is a space full of history, located in the central area of ​​Lisbon, which served as a slaughterhouse in the 16th century and which has known many uses over the last two centuries, such as a bullring, from 1831 to 1889, the realization of the Feira da  From 1835 to 1882 and still a vegetable market in the mid-19th century. || Cutest park with ducks, chickens, roosters, and a little water feature. The restaurant at the park is also great and opened all day serving food (unlike many local places that stop serving real food in the afternoon).  We love this park for the kids to run around and climb trees.  Great for a stroll with stroller and kids. Safe and clean.  Sometimes some homeless people are on the benches but that’s city life so doesn’t bother me. || we were there when they were feeding the ducks, geese, roosters, and pigeons. They take care of all the birds here with ponds and even a coop. We just sat and watched for an hour or something and it was so entertaining || Very peculiar place to relax. || Lisboa was one of the cities I had the most fun exploring on a skateboard. Everyone is very friendly and the food is just fantastic. As long as you don't fall into the tourist traps you will be fine. You'll find that the more you explore this city the more the culture gets to you. || Great central park in Lisbon that is quite family friendly. With an outdoor beverage place and loads of friendly animals such ducks and chickens about to keep you and your kids eye's busy. || Nice park for getting away from busy Lisboa. Well maintained pathways makes it easy and safe for strollers and runners. || Offering park with free birds (geese, ducks, chickens, etc.) a fun park for dogs and spots to train. || Campo dos Mártires da Pátria, commonly known by its former name Campo de Santana, is a street in the parish of Arroios in Lisbon.  It occupies the upper part of the trough that separates the two converging valleys in the city center, which correspond to Avenida da Liberdade and Avenida Almirante Reis. It is a space full of history, located in the central area of ​​Lisbon, which served as a slaughterhouse in the 16th century and which has known many uses over the last two centuries, such as a bullring, from 1831 to 1889, the realization of the Feira da  From 1835 to 1882 and still a vegetable market in the mid-19th century. || It's a mix of things that make this place interesting. A monument with many stone plates thanking a doctor/saint for the graces achieved (something common in the Catholic religion), small and big birds around cristalline pools, including cocks and chickens sleeping by the sun. Green places like these are rare in Lisbon, so I treasure them as much as I can when I come across one. || Cozy park. Ideal to lie on the ground and relax for a while. The place has a little lake with lots of ducks. The surrounding is very quiet and residential. || Crazy, there are lots of birds! So cool || Greenery around small pond park chicken 🐔 and Dock and its doculings walking swimming entertaining free of cost. … || A tranquille garden where you can relax and watch the ducks.  If you want to have a good sight of the city you should walk a little bit further. || I have never seen such place like this! Chicken in the middle of capital city? A very nice idea! Respect the animals.

A beautiful park where you can spend a few hours. It has a path that goes around it and which I recommend to walk. Beautiful trees and ponds ideal for a pause after a busy day. There's a café which is usually busy and a table is hard to find. On Sundays there's a small marketplace and so you can encounter locals mixed up with tourists. Just across the street you'll find the admirable Basílica da Estrela which is worth the visit. || I met some friends at Jardim da Estrela and it was a very nice experience. The park has lots of trees and open space, so it felt calm and relaxing. We enjoyed walking and sitting by the small lake together. || This is a gorgeous park — perfect for people-watching or for families with kids who just want to escape the hustle and bustle of Lisbon. It’s a peaceful spot to unwind and enjoy a slower pace in the middle of the city, and it even has restrooms (although I wouldn't call them clean but they were free), which is always a plus when exploring! || This place is heaven! One of the most beautiful parks I've seen by far. It's full of nature and also some animals, mostly birds. The place is perfect for a weekend picnic, a chilly eventing, yoga, hangouts and more. Thank you Lisbon for this amazing green gem! || Stunning park in the heart of Lisbon. Absolutely stunning. Full of beautiful plants and flowers, ponds and statues. Benches everywhere and the wonderful Banana Cafe inside which sells burgers and sandwiches, drinks and other refreshments where you can dine alfresco || 🌿 A Peaceful Oasis in the Middle of Lisbon ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5) We stumbled upon Jardim da Estrela on a warm afternoon, and it turned out to be one of the most peaceful and refreshing places we visited in Lisbon. It’s more than just a public park — it feels like a little urban sanctuary. The garden is beautifully maintained, filled with exotic plants, huge trees offering generous shade, and winding paths that invite you to slow down. What really stood out for me was the birdsong — there were so many birds, and their constant, melodic chirping made the whole place feel like a live sound bath. It’s incredibly soothing. If you have the time, don’t just walk through. Find a quiet corner, sit down, breathe, and maybe even meditate. This place is perfect for that. It’s not just visually calming, it actually sounds calming too. There are also benches, fountains, a lovely gazebo, and a charming little café nearby if you want to sit and sip something while watching the world go by. Families, joggers, solo readers, and locals chatting on benches all seem to coexist naturally here. It has a very authentic Lisbon energy — not overly touristy, just real life unfolding in a gorgeous setting.  Quick Ratings: Atmosphere: 10/10 Birdsong & Nature Vibe: 10/10 Relaxation Potential: 11/10 Accessibility: 10/10 Instagram View: 8.5/10 Highly recommend making time for it — especially if you’re feeling overstimulated by the city. It’s the kind of place that quietly resets your mood.  If this helped, I’d love a 👍 — and don’t forget to breathe deeply when you visit. 🌿✨ || I recently spent a peaceful afternoon at Jardim da Estrela in Lisbon, and it quickly became one of my favorite spots in the city. Located directly across from the grand Basílica da Estrela, this romantic-style park was inaugurated in 1852 and offers a refreshing blend of history, nature, and community life. The park spans 4.6 hectares and features winding paths shaded by exotic trees like jacarandas and ginkgoes, as well as beautifully maintained flower beds and small lakes with ducks and turtles. One of the standout features is the wrought-iron bandstand, originally built in 1884 and relocated here in 1936, which adds a touch of old-world charm. Families and locals gather here, especially on weekends, to enjoy the playgrounds, picnic areas, and the café with outdoor seating that serves light meals and drinks. The park is free to enter and open daily from 7 am to midnight, making it an accessible and welcoming space for everyone. Whether you're looking to relax, take a leisurely stroll, or immerse yourself in a bit of Lisbon's history, Jardim da Estrela offers a serene and delightful escape from the city's hustle and bustle. || I have a 5 year old and a 2 year old. This is hands down my favorite park to take them to in Lisbon. Great playground. Lots of space to run. A cute little library with little tables the kids can draw and color at. Birds walking about. Cafes for a quick coffee or juice. Plus it’s super safe because it’s all gated. || Definitely one of the most loveliest gardens in Lisbon, if you come here for a few days, I would strongly recommend to see this place. Very cool for pet owners and children hence the park has playgrounds and a huge space  for dogs to enjoy. Also, it’s a very good place just to meet and chill or enjoy your day in serenity. || A beautiful park with ancient trees. Ideal for sitting in peace.

On September 7, I visited Jardim Amália Rodrigues and witnessed a partial blood moon eclipse under a cloudy sky. The park, with its wide open spaces and elevated views, was a perfect place to capture the moment in photos. Even with the clouds, the experience was memorable and unique. || Lovely park and bar with a pool to cool your feet after a long day walking..cycling and generally getting about. The drink prices are reasonable. Definitely call in here if your in Lisbon. It's beautiful. || It is a delightful urban oasis at the northern edge of Parque Eduardo VII. Whether you’re after a peaceful retreat, a picturesque spot for photos, or simply want to enjoy sweeping views of Lisbon, this hidden gem is definitely worth a visit. || Somehow hidden from turistic path, a small part of the parc is dedicated to famous singer. || Designed by Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles and opened in 1996, the garden was named in 2000 in tribute to Amália Rodrigues, Portugal’s legendary fado singer. The garden features a variety of trees and plants, with quiet walking paths and benches that make it ideal for rest, reflection, or a peaceful stroll. || Lovely setting, but the garden is boring and very disappointing. Fans of Amalia Rodrigues must be very disappointed. Like the rest of the area, very poorly maintained and pedestrian access is dreadful. A missed opportunity, big time. || Great views and perfect location to see sunset over Lisbon with some live music in the background || Park with a great view of central Lisbon 💚 The shade of the trees makes for a great place to sit down and relax a bit. The sun beats down quite mercilessly at around midday. The many benches are a welcome addition for weary travelers. || What a beautiful park. With a nice a cosy bar to hang out and have a drink while enjoying the fresh atmosphere. || This little garden looked like part of the Parque Eduardo VII. The statue at the entrance was interesting. || Good place to relax and meditation... Also your dog will be more than happy to play into the little lake... A coffee on the side also will be great || Amazing views, beautiful gardens, and a perfect place to read a book. || Not to much illumination by night but it’s a cute place || Everywhere I go in the world I always look for a sculptor from the maestro Botero 🫀🫶.  So glad I saw that they have a piece of his in Lisboa.  🇨🇴🇨🇴🫶🫶 … || I love it. You can find fresh corners to cool off in summer while enjoying a green calm environment. A nice pond with fish, turtles and beautiful lilies. Visit it if you are in the area. || Beautiful green space and a lovely photo opportunity || Chilled park that catches the sun perfectly and usually there is a bit of a breeze and if that's not the case you may find some shade from the nearby trees. Close proximity to cafe for some drinks or a nearby lidl that also sells cold drinks. Sunset can be pretty incredible from this place as well if you're lucky || This was very pretty. Worth seeing if you're in the area. My family, though, was under the mistaken impression that this was a fountain that young children could frolic in. To be clear, once we realized it wasn't, we made another plan. People seemed to be letting their dogs run in. So there's that.  Nearby ice cream stand only takes cash. || A great place to stop for a drink, a bite or both. The round, shallow pool is perfect for dogs to play in. || Beautiful clean park. Really loved it. Jardim da Parada in Campo de Ourique is one of those rare places in Lisbon that feels genuinely local—quiet, shaded, and full of character. The garden is beautifully maintained, surrounded by big, old trees like sequoias and plane trees, with a small pond in the center where ducks and turtles paddle around peacefully. There’s a traditional bandstand, a nice playground for kids, and a charming little kiosk café that serves good coffee, light meals, and has plenty of outdoor seating under the trees. The vibe is calm and neighborly. People of all ages hang out here—seniors playing cards or reading, parents with strollers, kids running around, people walking their dogs, and others just sitting quietly enjoying the shade. One lovely touch is the old red phone booth that’s been turned into a tiny free library. It’s things like this that make the park feel alive and loved. The space isn’t huge, but it’s got everything it needs. Flower beds are always fresh, paths are clean, and there are benches everywhere. There are also two important statues tucked inside the garden—Maria da Fonte and Professor Ferreira de Macedo—which give it a bit of historical personality. But what really stood out this time was the buzz around the new underground development being planned. The city has announced a project to build a large underground parking garage beneath the garden. While I understand the need to ease traffic and create more parking in Campo de Ourique, I can’t help but feel concerned about the long-term impact this might have on such a delicate green space. There’s a real fear among locals that the construction will disturb the ecosystem of the garden—the roots of these beautiful old trees, the peace and quiet, and possibly the safety of the pond and wildlife. Right now, the garden feels timeless and balanced, and people are naturally worried that digging beneath it could change that. It’s a bit of a crossroads moment for Jardim da Parada. As it stands today, it’s one of the most welcoming and peaceful little parks in the city—loved by the neighborhood and full of everyday life. I hope that whatever happens with the development plans, the soul of the garden is preserved. If you're in Lisbon and want to experience a bit of calm, community, and natural charm, this place is well worth a visit. And if you’re a local—keep an eye on what’s planned beneath your feet. || Jardim da Parada is a compact, well-kept square that does the fundamentals right: plenty of shade, ample benches, smooth paths, a small playground, and a kiosk for quick coffee. reviews_content: Miradouro de Santa Luzia is absolutely worth a visit. The views over Alfama’s rooftops and the Tagus River are genuinely beautiful, and for the price of free, you really can’t complain.  ￼  It was a bit crowded when we went, but that’s expected given how popular this spot is. Even so, it’s still a memorable place to slow down for a few minutes, take photos, and enjoy the scenery. The viewpoint itself is part of the charm too, with a small landscaped terrace, shaded areas, and classic blue-and-white azulejo panels that make it feel distinctly Lisbon.  ￼  One detail I appreciated is that the tile panels aren’t just decorative, they depict historical scenes, including Lisbon’s Praça do Comércio before the 1755 earthquake and the 1147 conquest of the castle (a cool touch if you like history).  ￼  That said, I wouldn’t call the views “to die for.” You can get comparable viewpoints nearby, and this is more of a “quick, classic Lisbon stop” than a once-in-a-lifetime moment. It’s also conveniently located in Alfama at Largo de Santa Luzia, right by the Church of Santa Luzia, making it an easy stop while exploring the neighborhood.  ￼  Overall, crowded or not, it’s still definitely worth a visit and an easy, memorable addition to a Lisbon walking day. || Miradouro de Santa Luzia offers some of the most impressive views in Lisbon. From here you can see the Alfama district and the river in a truly beautiful setting. The terrace is elegantly decorated with plants and traditional blue and white azulejos, making it even more special. It is one of those places you simply cannot miss when visiting the city. || I visited Miradouro de Santa Luzia on a rainy day and the view was absolutely worth it! One of the most beautiful viewpoints in Lisbon. charming tiles, peaceful vibes, and a perfect spot to take in the city from above.  Perched on the hills of Alfama, Lisbon’s oldest district, this viewpoint sits beside the small Igreja de Santa Luzia one of the most breathtaking views in the city. || Miradouro de Santa Luzia is pure magic. The moment you reach the terrace, Lisbon unfolds beneath you — red rooftops tumbling toward the sparkling Tagus River, narrow streets weaving through the Alfama district, and sunlight dancing on every tile. It’s the kind of spot where you just want to sit, breathe, and let the city’s charm wash over you, maybe with a coffee in hand or a camera tucked away, because some moments are just for feeling, not snapping || Beautiful viewpoint. Probably the most beautiful viewpoint of lisbon. Just soak in the surroundings and immerse yourself. The tram to the hill is generally full at the base. The small museum inside is interesting and gives some insight into the history of the castle, including who built it, what it was used for, and a look at some of the pottery and tiles found on site. Beautiful old town 💕 || Castelo de São Jorge is a stunning medieval fortress situated on one of Lisbon’s highest hills, providing visitors with magnificent panoramic views of the city, including the Alfama district, the Baixa area, the Tagus River, and the iconic 25 de Abril Bridge.  The castle itself has a rich history, originally serving as a Moorish citadel before becoming a royal palace and later a military stronghold.  Visitors can explore vast ramparts, eleven towers, archaeological sites, and remnants of the former royal palace, all set within beautiful gardens that are home to roaming peacocks, adding a unique and charming touch to the experience.  The castle's grounds feel like a living museum where one can marvel at medieval defensive architecture, walk along ancient walls, and enjoy peaceful spaces shaded by olive trees and dotted with historical artifacts.  Surrounding the castle, the neighborhood of Alfama offers a vibrant yet authentic atmosphere with narrow, winding streets, traditional tiled houses, cozy cafes, and small shops steeped in local culture.  The area is known for its lively yet intimate vibe, enriched by the sounds of Fado music and the daily rhythms of local residents.  Travelers often find themselves enchanted by the blend of history, culture, and scenic beauty, making the approach to the castle a meaningful journey in itself.  The castle’s elevated position allows for stunning sunrise and sunset views across Lisbon, creating memorable photo opportunities and moments of reflection against the backdrop of terracotta rooftops and the sparkling river below.  Visitors are recommended to arrive early to avoid crowds, as the castle tour, including its museum and archaeological areas, can take one to two hours. The pathway includes some steep climbs, but the well-preserved structures and the sweeping city vistas make the effort worthwhile.  There are also small cafes within the castle grounds where visitors can pause and enjoy refreshments while taking in the scenic surroundings.  Overall, Castelo de São Jorge offers a rich, immersive experience of historical, cultural, and natural heritage, making it a must-visit landmark for anyone exploring Lisbon’s fascinating past and vibrant present.  The castle’s majesty, along with the lively charm of its surroundings, creates an unforgettable visit that reflects both the resilience and spirit of Lisbon. || What an awesome experience this was! A great space for high quality productions. Will see other theater performances here again! Recommended! || We went to see Comédia a la Carte, the show itself is 5 star, the Tivoli is good, good sound, pretty buiding, but the chairs could use an update, too small and stiff, and they go all the way to the sides which leaves you with a side ways view to the stage, not the best. But to enjoy in such a fine way the view and sound of the show in the last row of the building has a lot to say about this great venue. || It was not exceptional, but worth the experience. || Nice place for any kind of show. From more traditional to the more futuristic. Nice acoustics and very helpful personnel. It's well located in the center of the city which then it's easy to move anywhere.  I went to a magician show by Luis de Matos and then went to eat and a walk in parque Eduardo VII where I saw some of the people that were in the show. || A great venue. Even up on the third tier, the view was very good. We enjoyed the show immensely.  The only complaint I might have is how long it took to vacate after the show ended. || Entry was well organised (staff at the entrance was quick in directing people to their doors; overall, staff is quite efficient); however, the seats are not leveled well enough to enjoy a comfortable view if the person in front of you is as tall as you.
