place_name: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
reviews_content: Great night at this bar two nights in a row by witnessing awesome "wako kungu" band group of amazing artists and dance social the following evening!  Oh and social meet up was a fun and unique experience as well.  Make sure to check their event schedule for details. || There are these couple of guys one tall and healthy with a trench coat and one south asian guy, trying to dance forcefully with people. They looked usuals at the place because everyone knew them including the DJ but no one is bothered about their way of indulging with people until a lady got pissed and had a strong word with him and asked to stop it. The place needs to take this into account or this could escalate really quickly one day into something big. || The cocktails were very good and tasty. The band was really good but sadly in room with limited seating so could not watch unless reserved or very early. || Or “O Bom O Mau e O Vilão” Great signatures drinks and great bartenders. We were here mid-week, even then they had live blues band. Nice atmosphere. Highly recommend! || This isn’t your typical bar—it feels like being invited to a private event. The vibe is cozy and inviting. A special shoutout to Lauretti, who crafted two refreshing cocktails for us. || Fantastic vibey spot. Amazing interior design, great drinks, friendly staff. Came early in the evening so had our choice of several rooms. Should be a bustling bop later at night. || Great cocktails, great atmosphere and fantastic decor. || Without doubt the best bar I’ve ever been to globally for live music. Amazing jazz vibe. Genuinely was happy to give them a tip. || If you're looking for an unforgettable night out with great music, fantastic drinks, and a lively atmosphere || live music was phenomenal, the best part, one of the best live music experiences I’ve seen, with a great space for everyone to dance along — the atmosphere was wonderful that night, and the space itself contributed to it 🎷  great bartenders, and attentive service: made me a really good espresso martini 🍸  really nice space/decor: some small intimate space, bigger open spaces, great lighting & decoration: really nice to stay at 🪞 || Bar with dancefloor, open late and with mix of tourists, expats (mostly) and locals. || Excellent  bar in Lisboa. The atmosphere is so good. || The cocktails were good and the live concert was great! And the staff were very kind. It was my last night in Lisbon, so i really wanted to see the concert but when I get there it was 7 30 pm and the concert was scheduled at 10 30, so the staff made a reservation for me so that I could come back at that time, even I was alone. If I can visit Lisbon again someday, I will definitely visit this place again! With friends :-) || This review is just because a single bar tender girl that was in the back bar dressed in black with an hard eye liner that was really aggressive and unprofessional and made all my friends leave the place. Next time I’ll do an official complaint. || Fun Monday night cover band and delicious shaken cocktails || great dj, played great music. however the drinks were not as good as we read in reviews. || You have to go on the live Jazz evening. They have their itinerary on the door or their website. || Funky unique djs, not too crowded or sweaty and good for dancing or lounging || The best one in Lisbon

This is such a cozy and comfortable place in Alfama! Great vibe, MUSIC IS AMAZING and the owner is absolutely very kind 😊 A good choice to hangout with friends. Will definitely come back again || thank you very much, you are welcome any time:) || Absolutely amazing service, handsome bartender/owner who prioritized our needs. Great pricing. Highly highly recommend for a great experience. I tried so many bars and had a bad time. Come here. You will have fun and can trust the owner, he’s not trying to take advantage of anyone. Intimate experience with games and so friendly || thank you very much:) || My apartment is down the street. This bar is the only bar that is not a tourist trap in the area and is worth hanging out in. Arguably one of maybe 3 bars worth going to in the entire neighborhood of Alfama.  Why?  1. The myth, the man, the legend, Zoltan himself. Charismatic and charming bartender / owner / life coach / magician. 2. The drinks are fairly priced, no frills, standard issue. 3. There are usually nice people inside, both locals and random travelers. Because the bar is rather small, people talk to each other, unlike most drinking establishments. || The bar is really nice and the owner is super welcoming! It’s a really nice place to enjoy the night with friends in Lisbon 💃🏼🥰 || thank you very much, this is a big help for us:) || A nice place with a relaxed, kind owner. Good prices and you can get unicum! ;) || “the name of Lisbon could originate from a supposed ancient Phoenician term Alis-Ubbo, meaning "safe harbour" or "pleasant haven".” I think these two terms: ‘safe harbour’ and ‘pleasant haven’ are both true for Este Bar. thank you, Zoltan for the unique and friendly experience we’ve had here : ) highly recommended || :,) thank you very much || They call it a bar, but that’s generous. It has bottles, yes. A counter. A door that closes most of the way. A bathroom that doubles as a confessional booth for lost souls.  Really it’s more like a holding cell for men who once had potential. I say this without judgment. I say this while finishing my third gin and tonic, poured by a man named Zoltan. A man not so much tending bar as standing trial in a place without laws. He doesn’t pour drinks. He offers them, like penance, like saying a rosary you don’t remember learning.  The bar has no schedule. No rules. The light flickers. The furniture rearranges itself when you look away. Zoltan disappears for several minutes and no one notices—because maybe he never really arrives.  There is no menu. There is no bill. You pay what Zoltan says, or what you feel. He once charged me €7.20 for a drink and then €1.80 for “emotional labor.” I thanked him. Another time he charged me nothing, but made me write down the name of someone I miss and put it in a jar behind the bar.  The ceiling leaks when it doesn’t rain. The floor sticks to memory. The wine is imaginary but emotionally vivid. Locals say the bar is built on a fault line between remembrance and shame.  Five stars. Without irony. Without mercy. This bar is not recommended. It is inevitable. || Five stars, obviously. I don't know what this place is. A bar? A liminal space? A social experiment? I entered what I thought was an abandoned storefront in Alfama and immediately lost all sense of time. Inside: Zoltan. Or at least the idea of Zoltan. He may be several people stacked inside a trench coat. He may be a sentient fog bank wearing a flannel shirt. He handed me a drink that tasted like my parents' divorce and said, “This one’s on the house. The house is not real.”  The music was playing but it wasn’t coming from speakers. It came from under the floorboards, inside the light fixtures, from beneath my skin. Sad, soft music sung by bearded men who have definitely cried in a canoe. I asked if there was a jukebox. Zoltan said, “There was. It left.”  I went to the bathroom, or maybe I became the bathroom. It’s smaller than a thought. Covered in words I don’t remember writing. “WHO IS ZOLTAN” was carved into the mirror. The sink laughed at me. The toilet made an offer I refused. When I came back, the bar had moved two feet to the left and Zoltan was gently rotating.  We played chess without a board. I lost. He gave me a receipt that simply read “fate.” Five stars. I haven't left yet. I can't find the door. I think I might be Zoltan now. || :'D finally someone understood what the goals are.  million thank you || Cozy, small and very fun atmosphere.  Highly recommend! || thank you very much:) || Was a walk past and let's go back decision and glad we did! Was fun talking to Zoltan and talk about our common Hungarian thread! The drinks weren't half bad and thanks for the brain games to keep the others in our party busy! Highly suggest a visit! || thank you very much:)

Very nice experience, shared with 3 teens from 12 to 17 + 1 adult. They all enjoyed and used 59 minutes of the 60 allocated to the game. They were amazed by the quality of the scenery, enjoyed the enigmas. They all want to return ! We appreciated the welcome room, with sofas, coffee and water as courtesy drinks. The booking was amazingly easy online, the whole experience deserves 5 stars. || We done the saw room and it was really cool I get scared so it was a bit scary for me there’s a few jump scares. Our guide was Ricardo he was very informative and very attentive. I would definitely come back and try another theme next time || I really liked the room, we finally went to the room called Forbidden Temple of Montezuma. There were 5 of us, a pleasant environment, the decoration was very nice. Our game master Sergio was very nice and when we asked for help he always gave it clearly and precisely. We wanted to go to another room, but we overlooked the location so we had to change rooms. But we had a great time. With interactive tasks and everyone could take part in the tasks.  We definitely recommend the place! || I had such an amazing time at this escape room! The space was immersive, challenging, and so much fun from start to finish. The puzzles were clever and well-designed, and everything felt really well organized.  A very special thank you to Ricardo, he absolutely made the experience. He was friendly, enthusiastic, and incredibly helpful without giving too much away. His energy set the tone and made the whole visit even better. Ricardo genuinely deserves a raise! || Great place, the temple of Doom was challenging and very fun. Thank you even wiser for this great team building experience and Ricardo for being a skilled game master. || We did Jack the Ripper and found it very interesting. We had the help of Sergio along the way and was also very nice to deal with. We will definitely try another game again. It makes a fun night out :) || Amazing experience! I have been to three of their rooms, They were all really great. The atmosphere of them is amazing and top notch production value. The puzzles are very challenging but well thought out. Our host Joana was so nice and explained everything very well. One of the best escape room experiences, and I have been at many escape rooms in many countries. Highly recommend! || Really great puzzles and atmospheric rooms. The scenic design is incredible. I wasn't feeling very well so Salamay toned down the scare which I really appreciated, and I always felt safe. But you can get really scared if you want. Barbara also helped us with the first room that we did (which was the hardest) and she balanced giving us a challenge with helping us succeed on time. Would do Game Over rooms again! || Great escape room with fun, challenging puzzles and an awesome atmosphere. Special thanks to Maria for guiding us through the game she was super helpful and made the experience even better. Highly recommended! || We did the walking dead one and we had so much fun!! Terrified!!! But really good, and well thought out! Ricardo was our guide and he was amazing! Couldn’t have done it with out him! He was clear, cool and so helpful. Thank you Ricardo, you’re the best!

place_name: Escape Rooms Game Over - Santa Clara
reviews_content: It was incredibly interesting, very interactive, and extremely well designed. The special effects, the storyline, and the overall atmosphere were impressive and truly immersive. Everything was well explained and easy to follow, even though the challenges themselves are quite complex — in the best possible way.  The staff was fantastic: friendly, professional, and very attentive. A special thank you to our guide Luca, who helped us a lot and made the whole experience even more enjoyable.  I highly recommend this escape room to everyone — just make sure to choose the difficulty level wisely, as it can be quite challenging but incredibly fun. We will definitely come back and are already excited to try the other rooms.  Book in advance — it’s absolutely worth it! || Great place with a good variety of escape rooms. We had a lot of fun, the puzzles were engaging and the time flew by. Big thanks to Sara - she was welcoming and made the experience even better. We’ll definitely be back to try the other rooms. || We tried the Agrabah room this time and it was a lot of fun. The puzzles were more physical and we enjoyed the different kinds of challenges. Alexis  was our game master and she once again was very helpful. Her hints are just enough to lead you in the right direction. || We've tried multiple rooms and I only have good things to say. About the game masters, I had Luca and Rodrigo. The first one is the best and the latter I found a bit neutral and didn't help the experience itself. I would give 5 stars if all the game masters were at the same level. Apart from this I totally recommend if you like to challenge yourself. || My family and I were very impressed with this location and the number of rooms they offer. The design of the Atlantis room was really cool and the puzzles were decently hard! Alexis was very helpful throughout our adventure, offering small nudges when we looked lost or when we were going too far the wrong way. We're definitely coming back soon! Thank you! || What an amazing experience! I've played the scream of Agrabah with Bruna as Host and was amazing, she was a great host, helped only when is necessary! We are going to return very soon. || We did the haunted hotel and it was very fun and interesting. The rooms are big and more to explore. Alexia was very nice and helped us along the way. It makes a great day out. || Great experience, really amazing and great fun. Our gane master Vaz was very helpfull and accommodating.  Reccomend and if ever in Lisbon will come back. || We played Illuminati. The rooms are nicely done. The riddles are definitely challenging. The loudness of the sound was for us too much. The two of us didn’t solve it within one hour. Propably it’s better to ask more frequently for help if you get stuck. || Amazing experience! Very fun and challenging room for our first time. The host Rodrigo was very pleasant and explained and guided us very well. Will definitely come back to try another room

Amazing experience:) loved it! Thank you Carolina for the great job || It was a great experience; it was our first time playing, and we needed help from the staff to understand the game. The staff was wonderful and patient with us, being very attentive at every moment to help us progress. Definitely, when I return to the game, I hope to find the same level of support from the staff if I need assistance. || Thank you Alejandra! We're so glad you had a great first escape room experience! 🎉🔑 Our team is always happy to help, and it's great to hear that you felt supported throughout the game. We’ll be here whenever you're ready for your next challenge – hope to see you again soon! 🚪 … || I've experienced several escape rooms and this one is the best so far: the right level of difficulty and challenge that kept us engaged until its very  surprising end.  Carolina, our game master, did a fabulous job supporting us with the tricky parts while keeping the challenge unspoiled. Great job and a great addition  to the game itself. Thank you! || Paulo, thank you so much for your detailed and kind feedback! 😊 Carolina will be delighted to know her support enhanced your experience without compromising the challenge. We hope to see you again for more exciting adventures! 🔑✨ … || The staff is great and super nice, the puzzles are clever and new. We did the Ancient Egypt room. Of the many escape rooms I have done, I was only scared and my heart started racing only a few times, and this was one of them. || Thank you so much Miguel! We’re so happy to know that the Pharaoh's Tomb managed to surprise you and even get your heart racing a little — that’s always a good sign in an escape room! 😉 Our team loved having you here and we hope you’ll come back for a new adventure soon! … || Chose the Lost Island (Kids edition) and enjoyed ourselves quite a lot. It took us some time to get things done and move from one room to the next one (3 rooms total) seeing we could not solve some of the riddles. I would advise not taking anything with you, as you will be moving around quite a lot, but you can leave your belongings in locked chests located in the "lobby". You are not allowed to take pictures in the rooms. reviews_content: We had a great stay at this apartment in Lisbon. The location is superb – right in the center and within easy walking distance of restaurants, cafés, shops, and many major sights. The apartment was also a bit cold despite the electric heaters in each room. Towels were very limited—we each only had one for a 3-night stay. Additionally, one of the rooms is a family room, which might not be ideal for groups wanting full privacy. We made it work, but it meant our friend had to walk quietly through our room at night, and it’s something that would have been good to know in advance. place_name: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
reviews_content: You get a fantastic view of the historic centre of this beautiful city from here. You could stay and enjoy the well kept gardens and the views all day. There's so much to look at. Enjoy the full chaos of colours and sounds that envelope your senses. You'll have so many photos when you leave this place, but it is the experience itself that will stay with you. || Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara offers one of the most beautiful panoramic views in Lisbon. The terrace overlooks the historic center, the castle, and the river, making it an ideal place to pause and take in the city’s landscape. The garden is well kept, and the atmosphere is relaxed despite being a popular spot.  It’s especially impressive at sunset, when the light over the city becomes warm and golden. A must-see viewpoint if you want a classic Lisbon panorama in a pleasant, accessible setting. || A nice panoramic view of the city center and part of the coast. It’s adjacent to a busy street and is easy to access locates at the city center. It’s very spacious there currently hosting a Christmas bazaar making it loads of festive feels. There are different direction to arrive the view point, including one very steep pebble street as in the picture. Will recommend if you are nearby, but not necessarily worth to travel across the city for it as there are a number of other Miradouro in the city. || One of the most beautiful viewpoints in Lisbon! It offers a fantastic panoramic view over the city, especially at sunset when the light is golden. There’s a small park with benches, trees, and even a kiosk for coffee or drinks. It can get a bit crowded, but the atmosphere is lively and pleasant. A must-visit spot for anyone exploring Lisbon || We took the funicular up to this little park for the views, and it was not disappointing! The 270 degree views of the city and surrounding mountains were breathtaking. There are two levels to this park, and plenty of park benches to relax on. There is a small cafe here, if you need a drink or a snack. I would definitely recommend visiting here, especially if you want some really great photos! || Great view of the City from the nearby Bairro Alto. We were fortunate to visit during the New Year's market. Excellent choice of Portuguese specialties (think serrano sandwich with sheep cheese) and Porto. || Lisbon is a city that pretends to be humble while casually seducing you at every corner. I left the house planning “just a short walk,” which, in this city, is the most unrealistic expectation you can possibly set. Five minutes in and you’re already climbing some Biblical staircase, questioning gravity, God, and your shoe choices. But then Lisbon apologizes. It always does. Usually with light. I wandered through streets that smelled like roasted chestnuts and mild chaos, past tiled façades that look like somebody finally let a poet design buildings. People spilled into cafés, dogs trotted around like they owned the place, and the whole city glowed in that gentle, old-European way — like a postcard that refuses to retire. Eventually I drifted uphill to Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara, which is the kind of viewpoint that doesn’t just offer a view — it offers perspective. The kind that makes you remember you still have a pulse. Up there, under a tree that had definitely lived through several empires, I found an artist named Anne Laidam, casually painting like she had all the time in the world. Her works were neon daydreams of Lisbon — trams, rooftops, broken sunlight — the whole city filtered through someone’s kindness. I wasn’t planning to buy art. (I never plan to buy art. Art plans to buy me.) But one of her trams looked at me with the exact attitude of a Lisbon cat: unimpressed, slightly judgmental, irresistibly charming. So, of course, I adopted it. And carried it home alongside a copy of Saramago — because every reckless purchase deserves a companion in philosophy. If you ever want a walk that feels like a conversation with a city that knows it’s beautiful but doesn’t brag: just start walking. Lisbon will take care of the rest. || Fantastic views of the city and the boats sailing past on the ocean. Plenty of food and drink stalls. || Amazing view, very nice vibe with bars and good street food around (a bit overpriced). Definitely worth checking if you're is Lisbon, specially near sunset hours. I'd recommend for couples who want a romantic vibe. || Best spot in Lisbon to stop and see the whole city. It has a dog park below and a nice spot in the back with a cat box that was tended by some retirees. Great place for photos, food, music and just relaxing.
A tree of public interest. Great to climb 😌 …

During my recent visit to Lisbon, I had the pleasure of exploring the Chafariz das Necessidades, an enchanting historical site nestled in the heart of the city. As I stepped into the meticulously landscaped gardens surrounding the fountain, I was immediately captivated by the serene ambiance and the sense of tranquility that enveloped the area.  The Chafariz das Necessidades, dating back to the 18th century, boasts stunning Baroque architecture and intricate detailing, making it a true gem of Lisbon's cultural heritage. The central fountain, adorned with ornate sculptures and cascading water features, served as a picturesque focal point amidst the lush greenery and vibrant flowers that adorned the gardens.  Exploring the grounds, I couldn't help but feel transported back in time, imagining the aristocrats and nobles who once strolled through these very gardens centuries ago. The meticulously manicured pathways led me through a captivating array of flora, from vibrant azaleas to towering palm trees, creating a delightful sensory experience at every turn.  One of the highlights of my visit was ascending the grand staircase to the upper terrace, where I was treated to breathtaking panoramic views of Lisbon's skyline and the Tagus River beyond. It was the perfect spot to pause and soak in the beauty of the city, while reflecting on the rich history and cultural significance of this remarkable landmark.  Overall, my visit to the Chafariz das Necessidades was a truly memorable experience, offering a delightful blend of history, art, and natural beauty. Whether you're a history buff, a nature enthusiast, or simply seeking a peaceful retreat from the hustle and bustle of city life, this hidden gem is not to be missed during your time in Lisbon. || At the heart of the garden lies the Chafariz das Necessidades, an ornate fountain commissioned by King João V in 1747. This baroque masterpiece features a central obelisk surrounded by sculptures of dolphins and sea creatures, creating a captivating focal point. || I have visited there at night and no water in fountain.  Need more maintenance. Historic place. || Cute spot with a lookout towards the bridge. Interesting museum across the road too; pretty building. || Chafariz das Necessidades is a very beautiful water fountain in a park right in front of a government building. Is empty and it looks like it's a little rundown || Great spot for sunset || A viewpoint, with hidden a park. || Located in Largo das Necessidades, in front of the Palace of the same name, this fountain stands in the center of the Olavo Bilac Garden, named after the Brazilian writer and poet born in 1865.  It dates from 1747 and is part of the Palace complex, having resulted from a vow made by King João V to the Virgin Mary.  Its authorship is attributed to the architect Caetano Tomás de Sousa, author of the execution project of the Palace.  In the middle of a tank that receives water from four gargoyles of Baroque inspiration, rises an obelisk topped by a bronze cross that crowns a monstrance of thorns that accentuates the religious character of the monument.

Really wonderful tour by Beatriz!! She had such expansive knowledge about the history that’s informed local, cultural, and global history around Lisbon, and showed me some really beautiful spots. Based on our interests, we also stopped by places along the way that aligned with our hobbies/curiosities. Would totally recommend. || Lisbon Chill-out Walking Tour is the way to go! We love having a smaller group and it’s not commercialized. Jose was our guide and he was amazing!! He is knowledgeable and has a good sense of humour! My husband and I like him for his consideration for the locals while giving us a tour of Lisbon. We also like this tour for exploring the off-the-beaten-paths away from the regular touristy areas. We enjoyed learning the history of Lisbon, and the speed is great! The tour was longer than 3 hours and we hiked up to the top of the hill and got to see the sunset with the castle in the background! It was so magical.. Thank you, Jose!! I’d highly recommend this tour to anyone visiting Lisbon! || We had the pleasure of having José as our tour guide around Lisbon last week. I always preferred tours from locals since we get to see and feel the everyday sites and sounds of the city, from their point of view. This tour was thorough, touching on Lisbon’s history, meeting locals, and hearing about their stories, to seeing sites that were out of the books. The tour lasted about 3.5 hours, taking little rests along the way. We took the evening tour and we saw the most beautiful sunset in Lisbon at the end of the tour. Highly recommend and thank you Jose for this wonderful experience. || Beatriz was our expert and kind guide. In high detail, she explained information on the history, culture, and places in the neighborhoods we never could have known on our own. This tour is for adults who are eager for Portuguese knowledge and like to ask questions. My family walked talked and listened for 3 hours! Lots of walking and stopping at spots, so bring water with you and 50 cents for the bathrooms at the end of the tour. || I will never regret joining this tour on the first morning I arrived in Lisbon. My tour guide, Jose, was excellent at introducing the city in an engaging and captivating way. He started with a little brainstorming and he tried to personalise the tour according to our preferences, like history, architecture, and food.  He shared the history of Portugal and brought us to non-touristy places that I would call hidden gems.  I feel that if I had gone to the same places by myself, I wouldn’t have been able to fully capture or immerse myself in the rich Portuguese culture. The places he brought us to, such as Alfama, gave me a completely different perspective, and I wouldn’t have experienced them the same way on my own.  I have been on several walking tours, and this is one of the best. I really hope more people discover this Chill Out Lisbon tour and fall in love with the city  They're also so kind to provide a good list of restaurant recommendations that are mostly family-owned so you get to try authentic Portuguese cuisines :) || I absolutely loved this tour. José took us on a walk through his favourite parts of Lisbon,  skipping the main attractions that we can all find,  and leading us through the parts that still belong to the old inhabitants of Lisbon. You can see that he maintains good  respectful relationships with them,  and he reminds his guests of their behaviour as well. I loved the stories I got to listen to,  and capturing views that I would have missed if I were on my own.  100% can recommend! || My wife and I took a tour with José on the first day of our vacation and found this tour to be an excellent way to start our trip. We loved having a knowledgeable guide show us many places that we would not have otherwise known about and to provide a true local perspective.  Having done other walking tours in Lisbon, this is the best one we have found and would absolutely recommend it to anyone visiting! || We had a great walking tour with Nicole around Lisbon for a weekend visit on 15/08, showing us the main sights of the city centre and helping us navigate through the small streets in Alfama. As a first-time visitor to Portugal, she did a great job of briefing us on the country and the city's history, whilst also contextualising the facts into how locals view Lisbon today. It was great to have someone so enthusiastic to answer all of our questions, no matter what, and it was a great way to spend a few hours in the evening. I would highly recommend this free walking tour to any other first-time visitors and people who want to speak to enthusiastic locals about the history and culture of the city! || Our 10am tour guide Jose is very knowledgeable about local history and culture and thoughtful. It was a very nice 3 hours walking tour around old town of Lisbon. Plan to bring plenty water walking uphill in the hot summer. || Went on the 10am English tour with Jose on July 13, 2025.   I am typically reluctant to use words like fantastic, unbeatable, not to be missed, or awesome, but all of these apply to this experience. My wife and 12 year old walked with a small friendly group from all over the world and loved every minute of Jose’s tour.  Funny, informative, and proud of the city.  This is a thinking -persons foot tour. Jose is proud to avoid the usual monuments and tourist ‘traps’ and gives you an insiders view of the city.  It’s a lot of walking at a good pace. Good to know; wear comfortable shoes, bring water, and some cash. We felt like we received the local flavor of Lisbon and were able to see areas that tourists skip over. The tour gave us a perfect foundation for our vacation, and I highly recommend Chill-Out for any traveler to Lisbon. A great value even when a generous tip is given to the guide for an outstanding tour of the city. || Our tour guide was Rita aka Riri… Muito Obrigado! She did a good job, it was just my bf and I on the tour so it was nice to feel like we had a local very enthusiastic and honest on any questions we had. Its free but a tip is recommended so have cash or I think paypal/venmo forgot which is accepted. We just gave whatever euro cash we had available. We went around Barrio alto, Alfama, Baixa, etc. and learned about the interesting stories in history. End of the tour we also asked for a recommendation in where to eat and it was a great recommendation. Would recommend! Please note, there is a lot of walking so wear comfortable shoes! || I took one of these tours literally within hours of landing to Lisbon, as my hotel was offering one right when I checked in. It was a great way to hit the ground running after a red eye, so I could stay awake and get on local time, and acclimate to the city. Our guide was very knowledgeable, and interactive (it was a small group, so we could ask as many questions as we wanted). It's also nice to know you're supporting a local directly (the tour is free but be prepared to tip them in cash). || We really enjoyed this free walking tour! Our guide was Nicole & she was excellent! We learned a lot about the history of the city and local culture. Nicole was artful in her routing so that it was never obvious she was stopping to give us a chance to rest 😅 as we walked all the way to the castle at the top of the city. The walking tour was a great way to start our trip as we explored the city & learned in which areas we wanted to spend extra time. Highly recommend Chill-Out Lisbon Free Tours & also Nicole! || Did the walking tour at 10am with Jose. Jose is a born and raised Lisboeta whose love and passion for the city really shines through when he talks. His tour avoided the tourist traps and took us to the places he thought were important for us to see. He was always conscious of making sure his group didn't disrupt the lives of the people who live in the city. He shared a wealth of knowledge with us, so much so that we were able to fact check the tour guide of our evening wine cruise. Incredible experience, 12/10.

Painted rocks are placed on the beach, and visitors can participate by rearranging them into different sculptures. Haha It’s a form of participatory art. || Walking around the waterfront in Lisbon. Just off the main square, we found this wonderful artistic display of stacks of rocks all painted to create a smile on your face. Not a large area but very colorful and enjoyable. Please do not miss it if you are in this area of Lisbon. || This is a small slice of Lisboa that made us smile! Near the ferry station, the artist has created different features, very colorful! Thank you || Placa do Comercio Great sand sculptures by Brun. Don't miss it || very interesting great work || Adorable display of stacks of rocks painted to resemble different things. reviews_content: The Museu dos Azulejos in Lisbon is a hidden gem. It beautifully showcases Portugal’s history and culture through an incredible collection of hand-crafted tiles. The museum also features stunning sacred art, and the building itself is unbelievably gorgeous — truly a work of art on its own.  Don’t miss the large tile panel that depicts Lisbon before the Great Earthquake — it’s absolutely fascinating. I highly recommend visiting this museum; it’s one of the most unique and enriching experiences in the city. || Missed this great museum the first time I was in Lisbon, so promised myself a visit if I ever returned, and this summer I did. Tiles and  mosaics are so important to the culture of Portugal, so to learn some of the history and wander the beautiful gardens with a small cafe here is a real treat. 10/10 worth a visit. || I really enjoyed exploring the incredible collection of tiles, showcasing Portugal’s artistry through the centuries. The exhibits are well-organized with clear English explanations, and the building itself is stunning—especially the views from the upper floors. It’s peaceful, not crowded, and easy to walk through at your own pace. No wait to enter, and tickets can be bought right on site. Highly recommend spending a couple of hours here if you love history, art, or design! || A must to visit. The price of thd ticket is matching the spectacle you'll enjoy (I surely cannot say the same for other places in Lisbon). A church amazingly rich in decorations is an integral part of the museum. At the end of the visit you can enjoy the gigantic view of Lisbon reproduced on azulejo. Beautiful. || A fascinating museum that tells the story of Portugal’s famous azulejos — decorative tiles found all over the country. The collection is huge, with tiles from different centuries and styles, all beautifully displayed in a former convent. Don’t miss the panoramic Lisbon tile mural on the top floor. || Spectacular museum where you can see Portugal's history through the tiles.  Unique experience. The cloister and chapel or monastery were amazing too. 100% recommended visit. Free with the Lisbon card. || FANTASTIC ! I was truly impressed by this unique and fantastic museum, which includes an integrated monastery and the beautiful Madre Deus Church. It’s an incredibly diverse and one-of-a-kind place, where you can discover ancient and extraordinary tile-making techniques that take you on a fascinating journey through history.  The staff are very friendly and enjoy sharing the museum’s stories and anecdotes. The café offers delicious cakes, small bites, and excellent cappuccino, which you can enjoy in a wonderful patio filled with palm trees. || We were able to walk thru this at our own pace.  Unfortunately, the audio tour didn't work.  But the tiles were lovely and the building itself was truly beautiful!  The chapels and sanctuaries were pretty astounding. || A great museum to add to your list of places to visit in Lisbon. They have a huge collection of tile work from many different historical eras, as well as more modern works. There is a beautiful chapel that you can visit here, also, but check to see the hours that the chapel is open during the day to visitors before planning your trip. They have a nice cafe and covered courtyard to relax in after you spend about 1 1/2 to 2 hours going through every exhibit. We will definitely recommend this to friends! || amazingly curated museum with beautiful interior and works of art. There were a lot of informative texts which are not too long and not too short. The museum’s shop also had a great selection of things to buy from. I’d highly recommend visiting during the opening hours before noon since the line could get very long.

tonight, together with many other people, we waited for an hour outside the Academy of Sciences to attend the Guerra concert scheduled in the library, which until yesterday was certainly included in the program on the official website of the Theatre. It is shameful that an important musical institution suddenly cancels a concert, even if it is free, without replacing it or informing it in time and simply making it disappear from the site. the lack of attention and respect for the public (who could have done something else instead of wasting time, like us who came on purpose by train from Cascais) as well as minimal programming, make us evaluate this Theater as the poorest in Europe || Great old opera house, one of the oldest in Europe, with great company and nice repertoir. I've seen The rape of Lucretia by Benjamin Britten wich was a great show with outstanding voices like Maria Luisa de Freitas as Lucretia and Luis Rodrigues as Collatinus || Yo can have a guided tour of you coordinate via email. Maria is a friendly tour guide that takes to backstage, to the stage and shows to the balconies and the story of the theater. || Beautiful theater, built in just 6 months. There is not a bad seat here. || Very old authentic theatre with great condition. Beware, there’s no buffet there! The cabins on the second & third floor are really great! || Even with covid the organization is incredible. I stayed at a private cabin at 2nd rank, and when the show was over every cabin on that floor had an emergency door right on front open for you to leave. Good staff as well || Absolutely exquisite theater. Very special can't wait to go back for the opera tonight. || Founded in 1793, it was designed from the ground up to be a place for enjoying opera, choral and symphonic music. The building exhibits the neoclassical architectural style so trendy in Italy during the XXVIII century but said to have been influenced by the Russian Bolshoi Theatre. || Visited the open air ballett event. The atmosphere in the courtyard was remarkable. It was really funny, when during the performance the tram railway passed by. || Cozy theatre. Not too Big I would say Big enough. Polite and nice employees.

We were only passing by on a walk around Lisbon and stopped to take pictures. … || Lovely theatre, very cosy, the seats are comfortable and has homely feeling about it. La Feria does it again and again and again! 😊 … || I do recommend this show that is currently on exhibition in Politeama theatre. The last one I went to was Beauty and the Beast, it was great and I … || Beautiful building both outside and inside. The façade is worth a special attention. || The only theatre with musical productions in Portugal. Really good productions with really good voices and actors. Update, new show same quality! Great cast! || They have a loud speaker at the street playing songs from their shows constantly. They seem to have no respect for the public or their neighbors || Amazing performing talent! Would give the final star if there was air conditioning. || A magical theater! Know for its Portuguese musicals (a genre called Revista). It wasn’t what I expected at all. And even though I appreciated their interpretation of it, I feel that they needed more practice so they’d be more synchronized. Their movements, we’re not in sync with each other, or the music. They also seemed clunky, and not very graceful at times. The lack of costume changes, stage design, and lighting on their costumes made it feel like a missed opportunity. Several families stood up and left the show 10-15 minutes into it. The only negative is the single small entrance and exit door. || A very nice place for concerts and other live events. Quite central too. || Extremely poor experience. When the act finished they did a Q&A session with all the spectators. It was a wonderful moment. Great job, well done! You will make me come again to see A Verdade. || Very accommodating staff. My mother has mobility issues and everything was done to make sure she had a great experience at the theater || Very nice theater and, by the way, very nice restaurant in the theater || A well-equipped contemporary theatre house. || One of the best theaters in Lisbon || One of the great Portuguese theatre companies. HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE Absolutely inacceptable. I was sitting with friends, ready to enjoy the night and support a small theatre play created by a friend. I asked the staff if I could quickly step outside to my car to take a medication, literally a 3-minute thing. One nice hostess said yes, another repeated “quick”, but neither mentioned that I would not be able to re-enter the room afterwards.  When I returned, they refused to let me in. Zero explanation, zero empathy. Their decision was rude, unprofessional, and completely avoidable. The staff were unhelpful and behaved as if they took pleasure in making the situation worse, especially that security girl bullying everyone around her.  This is incredibly disappointing for a place that should value and respect the people who make the effort to come and support smaller, less commercial theatre. I would absolutely not recommend. || Hello! We are very sorry for the situation and the negative experience you describe. It is never our intention to cause discomfort or frustration to those who visit us — quite the opposite. We would just like to clarify that the rule of not allowing re-entry into the room after the start of the show is not an arbitrary decision by the team. It is an internal rule that also follows legal guidelines applied to cultural spaces, ensuring that: there are no interruptions for the audience already in the room; the actors are not distracted or harmed during the play; the artistic experience takes place with the necessary respect and concentration. We understand that, in your case, it was just a quick moment and we regret if this information was not clearly communicated to you at the beginning. We will reinforce this point internally to avoid similar situations in the future. Thank you for your feedback and we hope to welcome you again, providing a more positive experience. We are always working to improve. || My friend and I arrived 8 minutes late. We bought tickets 1 month ago but were not allowed to enter. It would be nice at least to have an announcement about these strict rules beforehand when the tickets are sold. Or to have some seats in the last row reserved for such cases. Very disappointing. || Hello! Thank you for your comment, and we regret that your experience was not positive. Regarding entry after the show has started, we would like to clarify that not admitting the public after the scheduled time is a common rule in theaters and is part of the safety and respect protocols for the artists and the audience already present in the room. Late interruptions can distract the actors and affect the experience of those watching. Even so, we understand the frustration, especially since you purchased your tickets in advance. We will reinforce the communication of this rule at the time of purchase to avoid similar situations in the future. Thank you for your feedback; it is very valuable for us to continue improving, and we hope to welcome you again on another occasion. || had the chance to catch a show at Teatro Ibérico, and it was such a great experience! The theater itself has a cozy, intimate vibe, which makes it feel like you’re part of the performance. The actors were incredibly talented, and the energy in the room was electric. I especially loved how diverse the performances were — from classic plays to modern productions, there’s always something interesting going on. If you’re ever in Lisbon and looking for a night out, this place is definitely worth checking out for some culture and entertainment! || Thank you so much for your kind words! This is an amazing place to check out if you are into the ruins and history of the sacred sites. Such a cool place. Plus you can buy a ticket that is good for 4 museums in the group. If you are checking out the free ruins across street ensure you pay the fee to check out the museum as it is worth it. || Museu de Lisboa - Teatro Romano: Where Romans Once Roared and Bluegrass Now Echoes  There’s something magical about watching live music in a Roman theatre, especially when it’s tucked into the winding streets of São Mamede and surrounded by the bones of Felicitas Iulia Olisipo, Lisbon’s ancient Roman self.  We arrived on a Thursday evening, just in time for the monthly performance held every last Thursday at 18H00 and were lucky enough to catch Stonebones and Bad Spaghetti, Portugal’s only bluegrass band. Yes, bluegrass. In a Roman ruin. And it worked.  The excavation site itself is awe-inspiring. You sit among the stones, imagining togas and sandals, while banjos and fiddles fill the air. The crowd was a mix of locals and curious wanderers, all drawn in by the music and the magic of the setting. After the show, we joined the happy throng for a glass of wine overlooking the river, because of course there’s wine. It’s Lisbon.  Then we wandered into the museum, where we met the charming Carlota, a bubbly art historian with a passion for living history and history in the making. She walked us through the scale of the original theatre, which could seat 4,000 patrons in the 1st century AD a fact made even more impressive when you see how modest the current excavation is.  The pottery displays are beautifully curated, and the guides know how to spin a story, turning shards and stones into tales of empire, entertainment, and everyday life.  Verdict: The Museu de Lisboa - Teatro Romano is a hidden gem where ancient history meets modern creativity, and where you can sip wine, hear bluegrass, and learn about Roman engineering all in one evening. Highly recommended for history buffs, music lovers, and anyone who enjoys a good story told in stone. || Outstanding indoor and outdoor spaces showing archeological remains, restoration, artifacts and renderings of what the Roman theater looked like. Excellent place to stop, scenic views and learn history || An absolute must see in Lisboa especially more if you happen to be lucky enough to attend a concert there. || We recently visited the Roman Theatre remains in Lisbon and were pleasantly surprised by how well done the site is. Although it’s quite small, it’s incredibly informative and thoughtfully presented, giving a real sense of the history and significance of the area.  One particularly lovely touch is that they host free concerts on Thursdays a beautiful way to keep the spirit of the theatre alive and open it up to the public in a meaningful way. It’s great to see such cultural heritage being celebrated like this.  We do hope there’s still more to be discovered and that future excavations might reveal even more of the site’s past. For now, though, it’s well worth a visit if you’re in Lisbon and interested in its layered history. || I love Ancient Rome. And this was a great little spot to visit. I love how accessible it was, just along the street but covered quite nicely. Loved it! || The remains of this ancient theater are a reminder of how long Lisbon has stood. The exhibit is very large, but does its job well. We get a sense of how much Lisbon has been through under Roman rule.  I walked away from the site wondering how much more history lies buried beneath the city. || This small but incredibly insightful museum reveals a hidden layer of Lisbon's deep past: the ruins of the Roman Theatre of ancient Olisipo. Originally built during the prosperous era under Emperor Augustus in the 1st century AD, the theatre was a major public building in Roman Lisbon. For centuries it lay buried and forgotten. ​Remarkably, its existence came to light following the devastation of the great earthquake of 1755, which unearthed parts of the structure. Excavations continued sporadically, revealing more over time. The museum itself does an excellent job presenting the archaeological finds (columns, pottery, everyday objects) and explaining the theatre's structure, history, and rediscovery through engaging displays. Seeing the actual ruins integrated into the museum space is a powerful experience. A must-visit for anyone interested in Roman history and the origins of Lisbon! || The main site of the theater ruins are viewable, free of charge, via the walkway constructed around the protected site. Like the museum across the lane (3€), the modern preservation and installations are minimal in style and use architectural outlines to provide the former scope and scale for visitors. The museum features excavation of the centuries of building and expansion over this site, while also housing artifacts spanning all the epocs of human settlement on the hills of Lisbon. || They have every last Thursday of every month a free live music show which was very nice. Expect shows to start at least 15 mins late — it’s Portugal, it’s a given.  The acoustics were decent but were nothing special. Seats were comfortable and ushering staff were polite. A great space for high quality productions. Will see other theater performances here again! Recommended! || We went to see Comédia a la Carte, the show itself is 5 star, the Tivoli is good, good sound, pretty buiding, but the chairs could use an update, too small and stiff, and they go all the way to the sides which leaves you with a side ways view to the stage, not the best. Small library without conditioning,  WiFi access, where you can borrow books, CD and DVDs. It's quiet and there are tables where you can work. There's a dedicated space for children. I must say it wasn't productive at all: - There's only a few tables and many of them don't have power plugs. I have no ideia how this is possible, but it makes absolutely no sense. People regularly come in and start talking out loud with the librarians. The librarians, not only accept this behaviour, but many time respond the same way! The answer to the final question was the clincher.......Will you be driving us?   Of course she would and what a great decision we made.  Tanya was knowledgeable, flexible, funny and honest. They showed my wife and I all the great spots, including one of the best local restaurants in Lisbon, and all this for a very reasonable price.  They are very friendly and knowledgeable.  I trust them with any recommendations. || Our guide was Victoria on a tuk tuk tour and she was fantastic. She pointed out interesting details in the streets as well as telling us the history of the city. She even knew about the hidden bathroom at the senic spot. || Thanks for your feedback || For the second time this year, we booked a tuk-tuk ride with Tanja and were once again completely thrilled 🤩 While we explored Alfama and its sights in May, this time Tanja drove us through the southern streets of Lisbon, with Belém and the Monument to the Discoveries as our final destination. It's a huge and beautiful plaza that has been decorated with a Christmas tree and surrounding lights. It's a must see in Lisbon and you can also see a gigantic arch and a middle statue in honor of someone important in Portuguese history. || Praça do Comércio considered a historical symbol of political power and manifestation of capitality in Portugal. It's a beautiful place to spend quality time with family, friends & special person. It's quite and welcome people who really wants to enjoy sunset. After the Revolution of 1910 the buildings were painted pink. However, they have recently returned to their original color, yellow. The south side, with its two square towers, is faced to the Tagus. || Lots of fun activities around. We saw street entertainment, vendors and restaurants and even a 360° video booth! Walk down to the water and sit of the steps to enjoy the waves. As long as you don’t feed the birds you’ll enjoy it || History at its best, even when it's busy it is possible just to stand in your own wee world and admire the architecture.  if you have a Lisbon travel card, you can climb the stairs to the top of the monument for fantastic views all for free.  Be sure to visit one or more of the wonderful restaurants round the sides.  Nightime is a completely different experience and one not to be missed. || 🌅 Where the City Opens to the River ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)  After walking down Rua Augusta on that bright June 2025 afternoon, we finally reached Praça do Comércio — Lisbon’s great stage by the Tagus River. Still with my friend, I remember stepping out from beneath the arch and feeling the city breathe wider, as if every street had been leading to this one golden moment.  The vast square, once home to Portugal’s royal palace before the 1755 earthquake, now stands as a symbol of rebirth. The yellow arcades glow under the sunlight, and the sound of waves blends with the hum of trams. In the middle, King José I’s bronze statue, mounted on his horse Gentil, looks forever toward the river — the same horizon that launched the Age of Discoveries. Standing there, I could almost imagine ships setting sail again.  We rested on the marble steps facing the Tagus, watching ferries and silhouettes cross the glittering water. It was hot — the kind of radiant, reflective heat only Lisbon can produce — but the breeze from the river made everything slow down, peaceful and cinematic.  Practical Notes  Visit near sunset for cooler air and golden light on the arcades.  Bring water; shade is limited.  Perfect spot for wide-angle photos or time-lapse videos.  Cafés under the arcades are pricier but worth it for the view.  Quick Ratings Historical & Cultural Value: 10/10 Atmosphere & River Views: 9.5/10 Accessibility: 9/10 📸 Photo & Video Potential: 10/10 Café & Rest Spots: 8.5/10  📝 If this glimpse of Lisbon resonated with you, hit 👍 and follow me — I share real impressions from Europe’s most curious corners. || Praça do Comércio is one of Lisbon’s most impressive and iconic squares. The wide open space, framed by historic yellow buildings and facing the river, creates a grand and welcoming atmosphere. It’s a beautiful place to walk through, especially in the late afternoon when the light reflects off the water and the arcades.  The square is lively but not overwhelming, with plenty of cafés and easy access to the surrounding streets of Baixa. A must-see landmark that perfectly captures the elegance and scale of Lisbon’s waterfront. || We were in Lisbon for a few days while waiting to join a cruise. We spent a lot of time walking around this area as there is a lot to see here. The plaza is magnificent. Beautiful big arch surrounded by beautiful buildings. Outdoor cafes, statues and lots of tourists all around. A must see if you visit Lisbon. || This is not a destination site but it is worth walking through just for the sheer size of it. It’s also on the water and has one of the Lisboa signs (great for touristy photos!) at the end near the water. You can also see the 25 Abril bridge from here. It was pretty at Christmas with a huge tree. || It’s a nice place, but there are too many touts. First, they will try to sell you sunglasses and then they all move onto other substances. I was bothered here at least five times in an unsolicited way. || Get a leg (or foot!) up and go to the top of the entrance to Lisbon! Beautiful views and we were able to appreciate an aerial view of the beautiful tile on the streets. We also saw the castle we were visiting next!

A beautiful and peaceful spot right by the Tagus River — perfect for a stroll, watching the sunset. You get a great view of the 25 de Abril Bridge and the passing ferries especially with Sunset.  It’s a simple place, but somehow feels magical — especially in the golden hour. A must-stop if you’re walking around Praça do Comércio. || Its a beautiful square on the beach of the river, with an amazing view and on calm days it is peaceful enough to just sit there or have a walk and enjoy the view of the river and Almada across the river. || We were walking around Lisbon for several days while waiting to join our cruise. By the river in front of Praça do Comercio, we observed two stone columns in the water. We were told by the guide that the columns were installed with a dock in 1755 after the earth quakes. It is a nice quiet spot by the water to relax. || Cais das Colunas is one of those places in Lisbon that just sticks with you. Tucked right next to Praça do Comércio, it’s a peaceful riverside spot with amazing views of the Tagus—especially at sunset. Whether you're passing through or looking for a place to unwind, this is a perfect stop.  The vibe here is really special. It’s calm but still full of life—locals lounging around, tourists soaking it all in, occasional street performers, and sometimes even live music playing in the background. It feels like a snapshot of Lisbon’s soul.  I love grabbing a coffee and just sitting on the stone steps, watching boats go by and the sky change colors as the city lights start to glow. It’s also a great spot for photos—between the water reflections and the beautiful architecture, everything looks picture-perfect.  It’s simple, free, and yet one of the most memorable parts of the city. I’ve been here multiple times and always end up staying longer than I planned.  If you’re visiting Lisbon, definitely carve out a little time to come here. You won’t regret it. || The view of the Tagus River, the 25th of April Bridge, and the view is simply breathtaking, especially at sunset. It’s a great spot to sit, take photos, and soak in the city’s atmosphere. A must-see for anyone exploring the Praça do Comércio area || Great area to visit and hang out with family and friends. A lot of restaurants and cafes,  beautiful view of the city and the river. || The place is amazing for walk at end of the day and or just sit and listen to sound of water and birds flying. I think both locals and tourists come here often just to sit enjoy the sunset views, the vibe and view of the other side of the city.  Best time to go there is when it is sunny at end of the day to get relaxed and enjoy the sunset, or in the morning for sunrise. During the day mostly when it is sunny it is quite crowded. || This is a historic riverside pier in Lisbon, easily recognized by its two marble columns rising from the Tagus River. Designed by Eugénio dos Santos as part of the city’s reconstruction after the 1755 earthquake, the columns are said to be inspired by those of Solomon’s Temple—symbolizing wisdom and devotion. For much of its history, this pier served as a key docking point for ferries and ships, connecting Lisbon with the southern bank of the Tagus and functioning as an important transport hub. The original columns were removed in the late 19th century, later restored in 1929, dismantled again during metro construction in 1997, and finally reinstalled in 2008. || As described, past historic entryway to the city. Some nice musicians, but wouldn’t recommend more then 15min here || It was a lovely day for a walk, and this was a lovely place to visit! There is only a small sandy beach area, but it was fairly clean and our little dog absolutely loved running around on the sand after walking on pavement all day! (we didn't see any signs saying that dogs are not allowed on the beach and we kept her on a leash). || Just sitting there is beautiful, you can take boat tour of tagus river next to it. || People come here to see the sunset by the river on the shore. You get a nice view of the 25 April Bridge whilst you sit or stand in contemplation. Worth coming down to visit no matter what time of day it might be.  It is next to the Praça do Comércio. Here important figures, including a head of state like Queen Elizabeth II arrived into Lisbon.  Sometimes there are musicians playing.  It gets very windy, so be careful! Watch any loose belongings.  Follow here and the IG link in profile for more travel and food and drink tips, ideas and reviews! || Such a beautiful place to sit and watch the water, with the street musicians creating impeccable vibes! || What a place to hang out before sunset. What I really enjoyed was the view and all the different people of all ethnicity and background just hanging out.  Nice breeze in the evenings and some guy was playing some music. I recommend coming here during your visit to Lisbon. Amazing atmosphere..... must visit places in Lisbon. Every tourist visits this place...❤️❤️❤️❤️ || Next to the main square of Lisbon. Possible to reach here by metro, bus, tram, and also boat. Also possible to sit and chill under the good weather here. || Lovely public square flanked by these massive columns at one end, from which the main street starts. Open 24 hours. We went there at 9 PM and walked around till almost midnight.  There are musicians playing lovely songs and lots of people, young and old, dancing under the columns. Really lovely atmosphere overall. || Loved this area o the centre! || This is a great place to hang out before sunset. What I really enjoyed was the view and all the different people of all ethnicity and background just hanging out.  Nice breeze in the evenings and some guy was playing some music. I recommend coming here during your visit to Lisbon. || A great place to just chill and relax for a bit. Especially on a nice day where you can just watch the waves and look out across the water. Soothing for the soul! || Near the middle and all the fast trouble of Lisboa you find a small place to relax. You will meet young people in mind and body, interpreting their level of art in different styles. They welcome you and you can do same. Enjoy it! Sometimes it’s hard to see a high proportion of homeless people and the coast isn’t that clean as it could be. Don’t find the tourist traps 🪤… there are many… (we know it, well) 😉

If you're looking for a peaceful spot to watch the sea and get lost in deep thoughts, this place is perfect. With tiered steps leading down to the water, you can choose just how close you want to be. The view is serene and shared with locals, travelers, seagulls, doves, and pigeons alike. It’s the kind of place that connects people to the heart of the city—creating a sense of soul and belonging. || Pretty and relaxing area, in a good location (close to the Cais do Sodré station, Terreiro do Paço and Praça do Comércio), and with a nice view of the Tejo and the 25 de Abril bridge. Really nice to spend some time. || Nice selection of food stands along the ocean view! 🌊 … || This place is very beautiful. Nice to sit here and relax. Has a few restaurants on the sea front and very good ice-cream shop. Also some great fresh juice vendors. || Beautiful view and great central location in Lisbon. Dirty and smelly due to the quality of people staying long in this place. Otherwise this area should’ve been wonderful and a highlight in Lisbon. If the city government will put more efforts to keep this place clean, it’s a top place to visit and enjoy || It’s a nice place to see beautiful views. But there are no chairs for people to sit. You either have to sit in the stone floor on the water bank or go to a restaurant or bar on the bank. || Great place to just chill and look at the water. Live band playing music when I was they || This place is very beautiful. Nice to sit here in the sun and relax. Has a few restaurants on the sea front. || Very cool place to hang out, especially in the evening in the summer time. There are food and drink stalls, with a DJ playing music. Everyone seems to be having a good time. A solo traveller, I met quite a few people there and had great conversations. If you're alone or even a couple and don't know what to do in the evening, this is a cool place to be at. || It is nice to have a rest and look at the ships, birds, bridge, statue on the other side, and for eating.

We were walking by and trying to decide where to eat when we met a lovely woman — maybe the owner, maybe not — but she was incredibly kind and welcoming. From the parc and the massive staircase it is the possible to have a very nice view. || A small viewpoint part of a hidden cute garden. The view is a bit blocked by the port, but it’s so calm and green, good place to spend some peace time. || The views are rather medium pretty. The purple tree are indeed amazing, but now (June) the flowers are ending and the park is beginning to look so so. Also kinda loins here due to the trains and cars. From there you can continue your journey by going down by the stairs and choosing between the directions to Cais do Sodré or Belém. || Sweet little view point outside the museu de arte antiga. Beautiful in the spring, with views of the river. place_name: Red Nose Natural Wine Bar and Shop
reviews_content: A hidden gem in the heart of Campo de Ourique.  On a hot summer’s day, we stepped into this cozy little wine shop and were warmly welcomed by the owner, who served us natural wines at a small table inside. The air conditioning was a big plus, making it the perfect escape from the heat.  We spent a wonderful afternoon learning about Portuguese wines and their origins, while enjoying delicious food that paired beautifully with each glass. We left feeling not only a bit more knowledgeable, but also a bit happier than when we arrived.  A true local treasure — highly recommended! || Red Nose Bar is the spot if you’re into wine and good times. They’ve got an awesome selection— sip whatever and everything they suggest, tastes good, you’ll find something special.  staff? super friendly, know their stuff, and will make you feel like a wine pro in no time.  Oh, and the vibe? Chill but classy, perfect for a date or just a night out with friends. || Very groovy wine bar. No wine menu, so you tell the host what wine you are after, they give you a few to try and you chose the one you want - loved it! The wine glasses are really nice too - which always makes the wine taste better 😅 || Very cosy wine bar, we had our first natural wine here thanks to the kind staff! || Great selection of European wines. I tried Portuguese wines and got excellent recommendations. Unfortunately, I didn’t get a chance to try the food. || Thank a lot! We are refreshing our tapas menu soon and hope you will back to try with cool wines! || Gorgeous natural wine bar in the charming Campo de Ourique area of Lisboa! I loved the choice of wines — including excellent non-alcoholic options — and the relaxed, welcoming atmosphere created by the team. The sommelier will help you choose the perfect wine according to your mood, taste, and preferences, making the experience even more personal. The place isn’t too big, but the tables outside add a lovely touch to the vibe. The food dishes vary according to the guest chef, who personally explains all the ingredients and inspiration behind each plate. Perfect for meeting friends, a date, or simply enjoying a glass of whatever suits your mood. || Very nice wine bar (natural wines mostly). Good choose of the different wines, which you could try and choose the better for you. Also good small plates of food, great pairing to your wine. || Thank you so much for your wonderful review! We're thrilled that you enjoyed our selection of natural wines and the food pairings. Wishing you all the best and hope to see you again soon! || It's always a good idea to pick one glass or bottle of natural wine here. Friendly staff, good vibe and any kind of taste could be satisfied || Top notch service, not only incredibly knowledgeable and professional, but also relax and extremely generous, with an impressive offer and fair and clear prices. Relax environment and very enjoyable experience. Highly recommended if you are looking to try good quality wines from all over the world! || Thank you for your kind words! We're thrilled to hear that you enjoyed our relaxed environment and global wine selection, and we can't wait to welcome you back! || The staff is very lovely and they have a great selection of good wines! I cannot recommend this place enough🙌🏻

A highlight of my visit in Lisbon! Great place to sit with friends and try different wines. Shout out to Coração who made great recommendations and was so kind. We loved everything we had! 10/10 recommend. || Thank you thank you thank you Caroline ❤️ || Great wine bar with a good selection of wines by the bottle. And our server recommended excellent options by the glass based on our preferred taste palette. It was a chill vibe and we really enjoyed the place so much that we even took a bottle of wine home. (We didn’t eat anything so that’s why I didn’t rate the food, but it smelt delicious.) || Amazing Tira. Hope to see you again soon ✌️ || We had a really great evening here! The sweet little bar belongs to Senhor Uva and the team has so many good wines on the list - we were surprised to find rather unknown gems like La Grange aux Belles. This is one of our favorite winemakers but it's very small and we don't see it often.  The team is super nice and friendly. They make you feel welcome right away. The place is in a great spot next to the park too.  We tried some of their small plates and they were all very good. The oysters were delicious and you can see they put effort into making everything nice. It's perfect for sharing while you drink wine.  What we also liked how easy it was to talk to other people there if you want to. It feels friendly and relaxed – a bit like a community approach, but you can also just sit quietly if you prefer. Not many places get this right.  Thank you to all the staff for such a nice evening. We will be back soon!  Katja & Sven || This makes us very happy Sven. Thank you so much for the support!!! || Amazing natural wine bar, with superb vegetarian small plates menu. The staff are super helpful and knowledgeable. Highly recommended and great value! || Thank you so much Graeme!! || We had two fantastic evenings here. Lovely and very knowledgeable staff, who recommended the perfect two wines to us. The bread and butter was just incredible. A real highlight of our stay in Lisbon. Highly recommend if you like natural wine and a relaxed atmosphere. || So amazing to read Ben. It was a pleasure meeting you and welcoming the crew. Have a great time in Lisboa ✌️ || We spent an incredible seven hours at this wine bar. The wine selection was top-notch, and the lovely terrace provided the perfect setting to enjoy it. The service was exceptional, with the owners themselves ensuring we had a wonderful time.  Though we hadn’t planned to eat, the food was too tempting to resist, and we ended up trying almost everything on the menu. Each dish was fantastic, perfectly complementing the wines.  such a fun memory —we can't wait to return! || Thank you Helena, it was great to meet you guys and we greatly appreciate your support. See you soon 🙏 … || Thank to Coração for an incredible experience! They are very knowledgeable of the wines and will help you find exactly what you're looking for. The food is also exceptional - you cannot go wrong with anything on offer ❤️ || Amazing Kelly, Thank you for the Love!!! || Came for a bottle of good natural red wine. Got an amazing recommendation and a delicious cheesecake magically packed for me even though they don’t do takeaway. The best! || Used to be one of my favorite places. Good wine. Great food. Unfortunately lately service has become very poor. Grumpy staff, poor to no advice when it comes to choosing wine. || Ola Alexandra. We appreciate that you enjoyed what we did and hopefully can continue doing. It does happen for us as well to go through challenging moments and difficult services. Maintaining consistency is one of the biggest quest in our industry and we will keep on doing our best as always. Hope to catch you for another visit in the future ✌️ || What a gem! This natural wine bar offers a truly original selection of superbly crafted wines. The atmosphere feels just as natural and welcoming as the wines themselves. Perfectly located next to the beautiful Estrela Park, it’s a spot that feels perfect in so many ways. || Awesome Hannes. Thank you for visiting us 🙏 …

Wow. 🤯 this Bar is AN EXPERIENCE! The 3 nights that we were in Lisbon, we had our dinner at Mae’s. That’ll indicate how much we enjoyed our dining experiences there. We didn’t manage to book the 1st 2 nights but because it’s just the 2 of us and we went in early at 7pm, we managed to get a table.  First and foremost, their service team were excellent and genuinely friendly. We felt so comfortable dining there. We had Lucas taking our orders all 3 nights and he’s become like a friend.  And the food? Every dish we ordered were superb and so flavourful.  Their breads are served with whipped butter and pumpkin jam. Just out of this world!! I love that they lightly toasted the lovely breads and how often does one get whipped butter!!  We loved the combination of the sardines and watermelon salad. There was some sprinkles of what we think as fried salted fish bites which elevated the flavours of the dish. Their duck croquettes were so good! Juicy shredded duck meat inside crispy thin shell.  The duck rice was to-die-for!! Succulent leg of duck with flavourful rice. So good. Their pork neck was another amazing dish. The pork was almost melt in the mouth and the jus was so good that we could lick every drop off the plate. We tried all 3 of their desserts as well and they were so good. Yet, arriving just as the doors opened, we managed to be seated without one - a small reminder that sometimes chance rewards the hungry. || This is a great restaurant in Lisbon, Portugal.
