However,  6,20 € for a tiny cup of cold coffee is too much ! || This is one of my favorite specialty coffee ☕️ shops in Lisbon. The coffee ☕️ is very delicious in all its varieties and the desserts 🧁 as well. … || Such a lovely place to take coffee. Lovely bright deep restaurant with nice zoned areas, Excellent selection of coffees & an inside coffee grinding wheel house. Service leg it down as well as dry cakes but as I say coffee & place is lovely. || From what we’ve tried in Lisbon, one of the best coffeehouse experiences. Very good coffee, coffee martini, breakfast, desserts, also friendly waiters and relaxing atmosphere. … || Real Portuguese coffee. Not for everyone. Snacks was really good.

One of the highlights of Estrela. One of the main Lisbon churches due to its size and beauty. You can visit for free but you'll need to pay to go to the rooftop. Beautiful paintings that contribute to the espiritual experience. Parking available just next to the church but it's usually quite full. You can also visit the park just across the street. A metro station is being built which will make it more accessible. || You can pay 5 € to walk up to the roof top. 20% off with Lisboa card and a million steps. The view is amazing. You also get to see inside of the basilica from the top- close to the dome. Also- Jesus dine with the 12 around a round table. || It is an absolute must see! One of the prettiest Basilicas we've visited. And we were able to access the roof and walk around the inside of the church from above and look down into the sanctuary. Absolutely gorgeous! || The interior is splendid. The ceiling, dome and floor are colorful. Paintings are fabulous. The ambience is serene. || The inside of the cathedral is free and breathtaking. there is a core beam of light that shines on you like a spot light for judgement of course.  For the bathroom. You need exact 0.50€ to use it and the post cards are exactly 0.50€ if you need change. I did the €5 climb which was not worth so buy the postcard instead and enjoy a clean private wc. The light goes off automatically but I just used my phone flashlight.  Update: I walked across the street to the Jardin and there is a free bathroom in the “casa de jardin estrella”. Do that. || Very ancient Basilica. It was indeed an Awesome Place, a must visit Place in Lisbon. It is a silent place to be with God. || After years of passing by outside, finally went in and was pleasantly surprised. It is not a giant cathedral, but it has enough of an imposing presence to allow one to appreciate the multiple altars and cruciform architecture. Also a pleasant surprise came in the form of the possibility of climbing to the rooftop from where you can have a look around the area at a very budget friendly price. Just be sure to be away from the belltowers when the full set goes off at, for example, 11:50 on a Sunday morning. || Known for its beautiful dome and interior, the Basílica da Estrela is one of Lisbon's most impressive monuments. The Basílica da Estrela in Lisbon was the first church in the world dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, built by Queen Maria I, and houses her tomb. It is also known for its large dome that dominates the Lisbon skyline, a remarkable baroque nativity scene, and its impressive neoclassical architecture. || I like to recommend everyone to visit this place it’s very peaceful n nice food with handmade dumpling thank u || Very beautiful and peaceful interior to the church. The floor of the church is particularly stunning in its design. We paid the 5 euros each to go to the rooftop. It was pleasant but for us, not worth the price.  Much prefer the pantheon rooftop.  The climb via a narrow spiral staircase is quite steep with just enough room to pass people - it is fun to go up. The view from the rooftop is nice and the dome is beautiful (you can see it close up from access from the rooftop terrace - mind your head going in 🤕) || Beautiful building and great to go up to the top to explore the roof and dome. || One of fav places in Lisbon. Very intricate details of the dome and arches. A must-visit spot for the  moment of peace and awe. Highly recommend spending time here to soak in serenity. || Sit down inside and settle your soul or admire the interior. || The beautiful colors of the church all come of different colors of marble. Blue, green, pink, yellow and grey marbles carefully carved for a harmonious result. The polished marbles shine like jewels. The interior is breathtaking. (Today's prices for blue marble is 2000e/m2), The rooftop  was nice, with the bells banging at five  a'clock and sun setting in the Atlantic ocean. || A basilica and a national heritage of Portugal. Built around 1780 this is the first church dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus. It is very good and the dome above the altar is wonderful. || It is a beautiful building inside and out, seen from below and above. Gorgeous decorations, works of art painted and carved in stone. The combination of natural light from the dome and the artificial lighting covers the interior in a special mix of colours. The roof offers great views of Lisbon in all directions. || Impressive creamy white late baroque church with a truly spectacular “terrace” on the roof of the nave, which is like something out of a movie set. Price to climb the spiral stairs is just 3€, and a small door in the dome also gives you a scary view straight down into the church itself—be mindful of the loooooow balustrade and also the electric wires running around the edge of the roof to keep the birds away ⚡️🐥⚡️ || The church, which was built in the Estrela neighborhood as a dedication by Queen Maria I of Portugal, whose wish for an heir was fulfilled, takes its name from this district. Since it is dedicated to the heart of Jesus, it is also known as the Convent of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus.  The church, which we can call the Baroque style, has a remarkable splendor and a beautiful architecture. The entrance is free, but I can say that the Bema section is viewed from a bit of a distance. There was a fee to access the terrace of the church. Since our visit was in the evening, we could not go to the roof, but I think the view is very beautiful with the Estrela park opposite.  I should also point out that the huge dome of the church, located in the hilly part of the neighborhood in the west of Lisbon, can be seen from many points in the surrounding area. If you take a nice route to the church, I think you can enjoy watching this dome until you get close. || Beautiful old church. When we visited the church, on a Monday around 11.30 in the morning, there was a service ongoing which ended around 12.30.  It’s a beautiful church but do not plan a whole afternoon for the visit, it’s not a very big church.  There’s an option to burn a candle for € 0,50.  Make sure to also visit the park behind the church, absolutely worth the visit. || It was a lot of fun to the climb 114 stairs to the roof. Some sections had no barriers 😫

place_name: Convento de São Pedro de Alcântara
reviews_content: This is a beautiful church to visit just across the street from the wildly popular Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara (viewpoint) in Bairro Alto.  The Chapel of the Lencastres just outside the main church entrance is very impressive. It is laid with marble and included a lovely altar.  The main church is equally attractive with Baroque features, a nice high altar and walls lined with azulejo (blue and white tile) panels that make for a most beautiful viewing of the church.  Well worth visiting for 10-20 minutes if you plan to spend time at Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara. || Beautiful blue tile work adorn the walls of this beautiful church. It’s quiet and a respite from the busy mirador right across the road. || Around 1:30pm I walked around the entire block twice and couldn't figure out how to get in. There were 2 iron gates but they were locked. I went across the street to a vendor and asked if they knew but they didn't. I went back an hour later and they were still closed. || Small church with huge beautiful paintings on the wall and the always present “azulejos” at eye level.  And the small Chappell  at its side is worth the view: walls, floor, ceiling, wow || A very nice church and chapel,  just beneath the tourist eyes,  and yet so ignored by them... || Special venue full of the typical blue tiles of Lisbon. || An amazing church in the heart of Lisbon. They also offer tours in 4 languages with a modest price around 2 or 3 euros. It was an unforgettable experience as for the first time I could walk straight until the end of the church standing beneath the statue of  Jesus Christ. || Great interior. I guess many people pass it by because the exterior is not so lavish. But it is beautiful inside. I was alone on 24th of december there, around 14h. || Churches and convents have particular visiting hours especially on Mondays, watch them before you go. || We are lucky we are so near to this peaceful heaven so relax inside , everyone should visit to get off the anxiety

Cathedral of Saint Paul of the Lusitanian Church (Anglican Church communion), which settled in a former Carmelite Convent built in the 17th century. || Beautiful church with a sweet garden inside. This church though is most of the time close. The rocks used to build this was very beautiful. Relaxing and numbing quiet inside even in the garden area. They have a WC. Lady staff that I met was grumpy and not welcoming || We were only able to see it from the outside on our way to a nearby museum. It was peaceful inside, where we entered the courtyard, and there's something like a dining room, so we respected the location and left. We would have liked to see the inside... || Despite the passing years, this old building remains standing. It's very beautiful from the outside, and upon entering, you find something very beautiful. The entire area is very nice to walk around. || The explanation of the history of this religious community, which we received from a very friendly lady, filled our hearts with joy. Very interesting. The garden behind the left door upstairs is a pleasant surprise. || St. Paul's Cathedral is the seat of the Portuguese Catholic Apostolic Evangelical Church, located in Lisbon. The cathedral stands on the site of a former Discalced Carmelite convent, founded in 1606 and completed in 1611. After the abolition of religious orders and the expulsion of the friars, the building was requisitioned and used from 1835 as barracks for the 17th Battalion of the National Guard, and from the following year also housed the police station. The building was then put up for sale at a public auction in 1872, and the property was purchased by the Scottish Presbyterian Church, a move that sparked considerable controversy. Since 1898, it has been owned by the Portuguese Catholic Apostolic Evangelical Church. || A different style than what I'm used to. Sobriety prevails above all else. It's not a typical Lisbon church. Although it's interesting to learn about other styles. Learn to compare. || I was very well received and the sermon was very edifying! It is a church in communion with the Anglican Church, with a very interesting history in Portugal.  I recommend it to everyone! || A place of prayer with a rich history. || It wasn't the most beautiful cathedral I've ever seen.

A wonderful example of a well-maintained and carefully renovated Gothic cathedral. The Sé de Lisboa dates back to 1147, with construction completed around the 13th century, making it the oldest church in Lisbon.  You can really feel the history here, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic elements shaped over centuries. It’s not overly grand or touristy, just authentic and atmospheric.  Definitely worth taking some time to visit when you’re in the city — a quiet, impressive place right in the heart of Lisbon. || Oldest church in the city (1147). Gorgeous catholic cathedral and a must visit. Very cool to be able to go up in the old choir loft  and especially outside by the large stained glass window on the front of the cathedral. There was a short line when I went on a weekday, so you may want to buy tickets in advance for a weekend, cruise ship port day, or high season. I was disappointed that the cloisters were closed when I went. || Beautiful and historic place in the heart of Alfama. The cathedral feels ancient and peaceful inside, with thick stone walls and soft light coming through the windows. I loved seeing the mix of old architecture and history all around. Even from the outside, it’s impressive — especially when the tram passes by. Definitely worth a short visit while exploring Lisbon. || The cathedral was absolutely breathtaking. There is still an admission fee, but you get a discount with the Lisboa Card, which helps. As you enter, you go up the stairs to the treasure room. On the way up, make sure to notice the carved cross on the stairs, said to have been made by Saint Anthony to repel the devil during his studies.  The artifacts in the treasure room are beautifully detailed and very well preserved. From there, you can access the interior balcony, which offers a great view of the main church below and a close look at the stunning stained glass centerpiece. There’s also a small passage leading to an exterior balcony overlooking the front of the cathedral, though it’s quite narrow and can get crowded. It’s a tight squeeze, one-way, and very high up, so just take care if you’re not great with heights.  The main cathedral itself is massive, with chapels dedicated to different saints along the back. The whole place feels grand and full of history.  Overall, an incredible experience and definitely a must-see when visiting Lisbon. || The oldest and most iconic church in Lisbon, full of history and charm. The architecture is impressive, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. Inside it’s peaceful and beautifully lit, offering a quiet break from the busy streets. Climb up to see the cloisters and enjoy the view of Alfama. A must-visit for history and architecture lovers || We took the classic yellow #28 tram and got off at the Se. The area is very cute with many great photo opportunities. We also had brunch at a sidewalk cafe in the small square right before the Se. It’s worth a visit for the views. || ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Lisbon's spiritual heavyweight champion since 1147 ⛪ Plot twist: you absolutely should go inside this magnificent cathedral, and here's the best part - it's completely free! No tickets, no queues, just walk right in like you own the place (which, in a way, we all do). The Sé de Lisboa isn't just "a church like all the churches" - it's THE church, Lisbon's oldest and most historically significant. The Romanesque fortress-like exterior might look a bit stern and businesslike, but step inside and you're hit with centuries of Portuguese history. The Gothic cloisters are genuinely stunning, and if you're lucky enough to catch evening light streaming through those rose windows, you'll understand why people have been coming here to feel something greater for nearly 900 years. The treasury and archaeological remains are worth exploring if you have time, but honestly, just sitting quietly in the main nave for a few minutes costs nothing and gives you everything. The acoustics are incredible if you catch a service or choir practice. Pro tip: Combine with a wander through Alfama afterwards - you're perfectly positioned for the neighbourhood's winding charm. Historic, free, and utterly peaceful. What's not to love? 🕊️✨ || Dear Tom, thank you for visiting, and we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience. We hope you can return one day to visit the museum and other corners of the monument. || The architecture is impressive, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. The treasury upstairs is interesting. Paintings are fabulous. The views from the top are spectacular! || Well worth the ticket price and the time to explore. Don’t miss the area upstairs where the vestments are- I’m fascinated by the detailed stitching even on the shoes! The cathedral is beautiful and there is information on its history available even if you elect not to get the audio guide. || Santa Maria Maior is the kind of place that makes you fall in love with Lisbon almost instantly. It’s the heart of the city — full of charm, history, and little surprises around every corner. Wandering through its narrow streets, you go from lively plazas to quiet alleyways, all wrapped in that classic Lisbon mix of energy and old-world beauty.  You’ve got iconic Lisbon landmarks all within a short walk — the Sé Cathedral, the viewpoints in Alfama, Praça do Comércio, and the buzzing streets of Baixa and Chiado. But what really sticks with you is the atmosphere: the tiled facades, the sound of trams passing by, and the tiny cafés where you can stop for a pastel de nata and just soak it all in.  It’s vibrant without being overwhelming, historic without feeling like a museum, and genuinely one of the best areas to explore if you want to experience Lisbon’s soul up close.

place_name: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
reviews_content: You get a fantastic view of the historic centre of this beautiful city from here. You could stay and enjoy the well kept gardens and the views all day. There's so much to look at. Enjoy the full chaos of colours and sounds that envelope your senses. You'll have so many photos when you leave this place, but it is the experience itself that will stay with you. || Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara offers one of the most beautiful panoramic views in Lisbon. The terrace overlooks the historic center, the castle, and the river, making it an ideal place to pause and take in the city’s landscape. The garden is well kept, and the atmosphere is relaxed despite being a popular spot.  It’s especially impressive at sunset, when the light over the city becomes warm and golden. A must-see viewpoint if you want a classic Lisbon panorama in a pleasant, accessible setting. || A nice panoramic view of the city center and part of the coast. It’s adjacent to a busy street and is easy to access locates at the city center. It’s very spacious there currently hosting a Christmas bazaar making it loads of festive feels. There are different direction to arrive the view point, including one very steep pebble street as in the picture. Will recommend if you are nearby, but not necessarily worth to travel across the city for it as there are a number of other Miradouro in the city. || One of the most beautiful viewpoints in Lisbon! It offers a fantastic panoramic view over the city, especially at sunset when the light is golden. There’s a small park with benches, trees, and even a kiosk for coffee or drinks. It can get a bit crowded, but the atmosphere is lively and pleasant. A must-visit spot for anyone exploring Lisbon || We took the funicular up to this little park for the views, and it was not disappointing! The 270 degree views of the city and surrounding mountains were breathtaking. There are two levels to this park, and plenty of park benches to relax on. There is a small cafe here, if you need a drink or a snack. I would definitely recommend visiting here, especially if you want some really great photos! || Great view of the City from the nearby Bairro Alto. We were fortunate to visit during the New Year's market. Excellent choice of Portuguese specialties (think serrano sandwich with sheep cheese) and Porto. || Lisbon is a city that pretends to be humble while casually seducing you at every corner. I left the house planning “just a short walk,” which, in this city, is the most unrealistic expectation you can possibly set. Five minutes in and you’re already climbing some Biblical staircase, questioning gravity, God, and your shoe choices. But then Lisbon apologizes. It always does. Usually with light. I wandered through streets that smelled like roasted chestnuts and mild chaos, past tiled façades that look like somebody finally let a poet design buildings. People spilled into cafés, dogs trotted around like they owned the place, and the whole city glowed in that gentle, old-European way — like a postcard that refuses to retire. Eventually I drifted uphill to Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara, which is the kind of viewpoint that doesn’t just offer a view — it offers perspective. The kind that makes you remember you still have a pulse. Up there, under a tree that had definitely lived through several empires, I found an artist named Anne Laidam, casually painting like she had all the time in the world. Her works were neon daydreams of Lisbon — trams, rooftops, broken sunlight — the whole city filtered through someone’s kindness. I wasn’t planning to buy art. (I never plan to buy art. Art plans to buy me.) But one of her trams looked at me with the exact attitude of a Lisbon cat: unimpressed, slightly judgmental, irresistibly charming. So, of course, I adopted it. And carried it home alongside a copy of Saramago — because every reckless purchase deserves a companion in philosophy. If you ever want a walk that feels like a conversation with a city that knows it’s beautiful but doesn’t brag: just start walking. Lisbon will take care of the rest. || Fantastic views of the city and the boats sailing past on the ocean. Plenty of food and drink stalls. || Amazing view, very nice vibe with bars and good street food around (a bit overpriced). Definitely worth checking if you're is Lisbon, specially near sunset hours. I'd recommend for couples who want a romantic vibe. || Best spot in Lisbon to stop and see the whole city. It has a dog park below and a nice spot in the back with a cat box that was tended by some retirees. Great place for photos, food, music and just relaxing.

They have an art center halfway down the street where they exhibit works by established artists who have worked with the gallery over the years. I love it! They also have an admirable collection in their reserve. The director, Rui Brito, always welcomes everyone with lots of stories and anecdotes. || Fabulous gallery, warmly welcomed by Rui, the owner, who also showed me around the backstage areas, which blew my mind! I feel so privileged to have seen some art that's not mainstream and for Rui's kindness in showing me around. My highlight of this trip 😀 || One of the most iconic galleries and art dealers in Portugal. It's always showcasing fresh artists and at affordable prices. Love the quaint tranquillity of the space. Trust me, it's worth going in. || Thank you, Yung! 👨‍🎨☺️ … || Very friendly and talented man! The paintings are beautiful! || This gallery is owned by Stepan Zaporozhan, the artist whose artwork is printed and sold everywhere in Lisbon (and maybe beyond). The shop has these prints and more that are not seen on the streets and in souvenir shops. He also sells the original water paintings and very beautiful acrylic paintings. Not very interesting to me personally. April 2022 visit. || Great exhibition and interesting program || I had the pleasure of visiting this Art Gallery on the occasion of David Claerbout's "Wildfire" exhibition on November 18, 2020. The space is fantastic for several reasons: 1. The entrance is quite intimate as it is located in a sunken tunnel and, upon entering the main room, the visitor has a feeling of immediate liberation; 2. We reiterate that we have no involvement in the negotiation or payment of the aforementioned artwork and that we do not condone practices that harm artists.  Stronddo remains focused on supporting the artists it works with in a transparent and professional manner. || Infinite variety at great prices. || Thank you for your review! || It is definitely not an art gallery, but rather a shop selling decorative and commercial paintings/pictures. || Hi Paul. Our physical space is indeed an art shop. But we're also a gallery where we promote art exhibitions. Besides, we run an international online art gallery at Stronddo.art. It would be best if you were informed prior to any evaluation. Thank you, and have an excellent week. || Without a doubt the best art gallery in Lisbon. || Thank you for your review! || An experience I highly recommend! || Thank you so much for your feedback and kind words :) || Dear Tamiris,  We regret if you had any less than successful experience at our gallery. Since we were unable to identify you as a client, partner, or supplier, we suggest you report the incident to hello@stronddo.art so we can assist you.  Thank you and see you soon!  Stronddo || Dear Thaís, we have registered your review, however we do not have any record relating to you, whether as a client, partner or artist. If you could provide more details, we would be happy to assist you. See you soon! || Thank you for your review! || Thank you for the 5 stars review ☀️ || Thank you for your feedback :) || Thank you for your feedback :) || Thank you so much for your feedback :) || Thank you for your feedback :) || Thank you for your feedback :) || Thank you for your review! || Thank you for your 5 stars review ☀️ || Thank you very much for the five stars :)

More educational than entertaining. An old monastery and church repurposed as a museum. The museum has an impressive exposition on history of organized Christianity in Portugal. The architecture is impressive and the tile panels are exquisite. The church towers are worth visiting too as the views from there are even better than those from the National Pantheon (and it’s easier to take pictures from there). The entry fee is reasonable. || This building was  18th century Igreja (church) very gothic and recorded so many historical events. The building is very pretty and my favorite part is the 360 degree point of view at the roof top. Even though some of the part a bit scary and feels draining to climb up. || Went here after a recommendation from one of our friend, and it was honestly just amazing. There's a bit of culture, much to see and it's quite impressive. And on top of that you end the trip with a spectacular view. All that for 5€ per adult. Would recommend. || Fantastic roof top views of Lisbon, beautiful courtyard, friendly staff and peaceful cloisters decorated with stunning blue tiles. || Coffee shop people were very inconsiderate || Guy behind the counter is rude and arrogant we used the toilets and he gave very bad attitude  Court yard is nice  He obviously has the same problem over and over but np need to be rude in a church || Built in 1147, this monastery suffered the ravages of the 1755 earthquake. It was rebuilt. Walking through its doors, you'll feel like you've stepped back in time. We simply loved this visit.  The church is simply incredible, as is the double cloister. As you wander through some of the rooms, you'll discover superb azulejo frescoes. As a bonus, the tour gives you access to the monastery's rooftops, which offer a beautiful 360-degree view of the city.  Finally, the second floor of the building is dedicated to the fables of Jean de la Fontaine. A great way to (re)discover them, especially with children. Allow about three hours for the tour at your own pace.  Admission: 8 euros per adult (6 euros with the Lisboa Card) and 4 euros for those under 25. || A very worthwhile visit to the monastery and its church. The highlight is the panoramic view from the church rooftops. Also not to be missed is the Royal Pantheon of Bragança. The azulejos (tiles) are also worth seeing, especially the series depicting La Fontaine's fables. Allow at least two hours for a complete visit. || I absolutely recommend purchasing a ticket to visit the entire church and the monastery. There's no waiting (unlike the Jeronimos Monastery), and the spaces you visit are diverse and rewarding. The tour also includes a climb to the top of the monastery (beautiful views), a couple of exhibitions, the majolica cloister, and the cisterns. || Less publicized than other museums and historical/religious buildings in the city, I think it's the best value for money. You'll spend more than an hour, even two if you like, visiting every room and floor of this museum. Everything is described in detail, even in English, so you'll have no problem learning all the information and curiosities.  It's easily accessible by taking the historic tram 28, but if climbing a lot isn't a problem for you, given its proximity to the city center (the Rua Augusta Arch, for example), it won't take you long to reach your destination on foot.

An amazing panoramic view over the coastline of the city from the terrace. So if you are looking around and exploring the city centre, its a good spot to have nice views of amazing photos. || Decent panorama over the city though the spot is dirty in some areas || The only thing that is uncomfortable about the area are the skaters who don't allow you to sit down or enjoy the view because they feel like they own the area. One of them threw his skateboard at me when I sat down in one of their play areas.  The police should have more control in this regard because there is also alcohol consumption. || It is located between the Pantheon and other more famous Miradouros here in Lisbon || A nice place to stop and enjoy the view while exploring the Alfama neighbourhood || Beautiful viewpoint. Because of the skaters, you cant sit down on the benches. || Meh, cannot see the sunset as other buildings obstructed || It's nice to go at night || The views are spectacular, but it's unbelievable how neglected and dirty the embankment is. With very little investment, it could be made beautiful. What a shame...

Lovely statue of Saint Vincent (Lisbon's patron saint), holding the boat and the ravens that are symbols of the city on one of the privileged balconies overlooking São Vicente Hill. One of Lisbon's best scenic viewpoints, the square sits atop one of the city's hills, which is why the viewpoint takes its name from an old gate in the Cerca Moura. In the labyrinthine old quarter of Alfama, with its streets, courtyards, and dead ends leading down to the Tagus River, near the Museum of Decorative Arts ... || A striking statue of St Vincent, who's seen holding a ship with two ravens, which pays tribute to the pair that accompanied and guarded his body throughout the journey from Sagres to Lisbon; and if you ever wondered where Lisbon got its coat of arms, look no further. || It is worth checking out statue if in the area. Too see the history always worth a few moments of time. || It is a beautiful monument, and the location is a great vantage point and resting place, one of the most beautiful stops of the city sightseeing trams no. 12 and 28, it is worth visiting both day and night. A great starting point for a walk to the castle. || The statue of St. Vicente of Saragossa is located at Miradouro das Portas do Sol. It is the work of architect Luis Xavier (1965-67) and based on the earlier design plans of his father Raul Xavier.  I enjoy viewing this statue of the Patron Saint Vincente who is standing in a decorative robe and holding a caravel with two ravens which is the Coat of Arms of the city of Lisbon. It is a neat statue to see while visiting this viewpoint. || Saint Vicente is the true patron saint of Lisbon. The statue holds the caravel with two crows, symbol of the city of Lisbon. According to legend, the saint's dead body was brought back home and the 2 crows accompanied it. || Some great views over the old town near the statue. || Great view, sit back have a beer! Cool breezes. || One of many sculptures in the city. St Vincent is the patron saint of Lisbon. The sculpture of the saint is holding a boat with 2 common ravens on top. It is a symbol of the city.  Nearby is a viewpoint terrace from which you can overlook the city.  The area is a tourist hotspot.  Follow here and on IG for more travel and food and drink tips, ideas and reviews @one.more.step.along.the.world || Nice statue in the middle of a plaza with great view over Lisbon east part and the river.

One of the most beautiful exhibitions to see in Lisbon. The building itself is also very good. It has a calming atmosphere. You can see a lot of different exhibitions and the staff is also very nice. Definitely “a must see” if you are visiting Lisbon.  After visiting the exhibitions, you can chill in the beautiful garden which is also very good designed. You feel like you are in another world:) I suggest you to go there a bit early and hang out with the ducks after your visit, there are restaurants/cafes you can sit at too. || Centro de Arte Moderna Gulbenkian - Where Wood, Light, and Art Collide in Quiet Elegance  Tucked into the leafy calm of Rua Marquês de Fronteira, the Centro de Arte Moderna (CAM) is a space that whispers rather than shouts. And the first thing that catches your eye - before the art, before the exhibitions - is that roof. Oh, that roof.  Inspired by Japanese design, the wooden canopy stretches out like a warm embrace, with natural open-grain beams that filter the light and soften the edges of the building. It’s minimalist without being cold, organic without being rustic, and it sets the tone for everything that follows. You feel like you’re entering a space that respects silence, celebrates craftsmanship, and invites reflection.  Inside, the layout is clean and considered, with natural materials and soft lighting that let the artworks breathe. Even without a blockbuster exhibition, it’s a place worth visiting just to experience the architecture, wander the serene spaces, and soak in the Gulbenkian calm.  We were lucky to catch the tail end of “Between Your Teeth”, a powerful exhibition featuring Paula Rego and Adriana Varejão. Though now closed, it left behind a lingering sense of bold storytelling and emotional depth, perfectly matched to the building’s quiet strength.  Verdict: CAM is a masterclass in architectural grace, where wood meets light, and art finds room to speak softly but powerfully. Highly recommended for design lovers, quiet wanderers, and anyone who believes that a roof can be a work of art. || I was out and about in the neighbourhood, they had a nice programme for the day, so i decided to check it out. It's been a while! The 1st time back since the renovation was completed. Highly recommend the guided visit to the exhibition. It's great and they also had a sign language guide translating which was also cool. || Building with a beautiful architecture and modern art inside very well organized and beautifully placed to do justice to the architecture. The best part is the garden that is magnificent with both animals and green areas and Japanese inspired pathways. || Boring and at that was shallow with very little meaning. Few pieces were actually worth seeing and the rest was derivative of Warhol and Pollack. The only interesting piece was the building itself and to see that is free of charge. Attached are the ONLY good pieces. || The museum buildings and the garden is absolutely worth seeing itself. Besides, current exhibition is also awesome. For a delightful experience, please visit the museum. It’s gorgeous. || My fav place in Lisbon. An oasis of calm in the middle of the city. Couldn’t recommend enough. G come to meditate read or lay in the sun and listen to the birds sing || Such a nice place with great architecture and surrounded by nature. The exposition was great, we enjoyed our visit. Good coffee outside the building also, from the little van. Nice place to just sit and enjoy nature. || I always have this interest in being around artistic spaces. Went there with a friend of mine. Right next to sao sebastiao station. Get off the station and will probably take 3 minutes walk ato reach there. It's best if you buy the full tour tickets. I think it was 12 euros each. I enjoyed the creation of small island and the rock and use the headphones for the sound and some background information. Also they usually have different exhibitions going on. So keep an eye on which one is going on at what time. Also one side of the museum is closed for now hopefully they will open soon. Loved the British collection gallery. It was fun and unique. They have a cafe or more like a rest pastelaria. Foods I have seen usually around 8 to 10 euros. Also there's some other cafes and restaurants with outdoor sitting. Great for a coffee and cigarette. Don't miss the tv room inside the British gallery collection. It's something I found really amazing. || Great exhibitions from beginning to end. And the facility is an art piece itself. Staff was exceptionally friendly. Go for the art then walk around the beautiful grounds.

While the museum is closed for renovations one can always visit the Centro de Arte Moderna (CAM) with a good collection and some amazing architecture The Museum has left a few expositions open and one can see Monet and other great pieces of art The gardens between the museums and CAM offer a nice stroll. There are concerts in the park || Unfortunately, the museum is temporarily closed. Yet, they have several exhibitions, including the main items like masterpieces from the main collections! Such as art pieces from Ottoman Empire, Iran, Asian arts, and European (mostly French in my opinion). The collection was amazing! I am so happy that they still offer temporary exhibitions even during the maintenance. || An amazing place with very helpful staff. We spent a good few hours here. It is an incredible collection with works by Monet, Turner and many more. I felt sorry for the staff who had to field strange enquiries from an American who asked things like "why do all the artworks have glass on them?" (They don't) And "why have these artworks been touched up by a modern artist?" (They haven't). Very patient staff! The grounds are really beautiful and free. We had a coffee in the cafe and the staff were great. Just a note that you cannot take water bottles with liquid in but there is a free cloakroom. I found the modern art very thought provoking and we only just saw all the artwork in the two buildings shortly before closing time. Unmissable if you love art. || Been wanting to go here for a while and finally did it last weekend. What a place, absolutely loved it. The collection is incredible and the spaces are stunning. We spent about 4 hours in the 2 buildings as they were closing up, but could have definitely been in there for longer. The grounds are really nice too. If you go on a Sunday afternoon, the queue isn’t that bad, it might take 30 mins. || Interesting museum with an older building and a brand new one. Architecture of both is interesting. The landscape/gardens surrounding the museum(s) is very inviting. Tranquil place in a bustling city. Gardens open to the public || Fantastic collection, curation and location. Quite an underrated museum with special Islamic and contemporary art pieces. A must see in Lisbon! The architecture is also interesting as well. || “One of Lisbon’s best museums! The Gulbenkian Museum houses an incredible art collection, from Egyptian artifacts to works by Rembrandt and Monet. The serene gardens add to the experience. Best visited in the morning for a quiet atmosphere. Entry is around €10, but free on Sundays after 2 PM. A must-see for art lovers looking for a mix of history, culture, and nature!” || A very beautiful art collection. It takes you through a couple of thousands years of art from Europe, Asia, and North Africa. The building is very spacious inside, and all objects are are displayed accordingly. For viewing the basic collection, I'd recommend spending three hours in the museum if you like to take time to absorb it all and go home with new inspiration. || Bit of a challenge finding the entrance. Ignore the signs and just make for the north of the park. Well laid out exhibits. Takes about an hour to go around. Bit of an eclectic mixture art from eras and parts of the world. A nice rest from the heat and steep walks around Lisbon. Very peaceful setting. Nice coffee shop on lower floor. || This place is an oasis in the middle of Lisbon. Besides the farm museums on the premises, they have incredibly well tended gardens, with streams, running across it, and a lake. Anybody can come and spend the day enjoying sunbathing, picnic king, talking to friends, enjoying the cafeteria and cafés and the incredibly well designed landscape. If you go to Lisbon, you must come see this place.

place_name: History of Lisbon Mural by Nuno Saraiva
reviews_content: Very cool comic mural about the history of Lisbon. It’s in an obscure tunnel that houses a public WC. The art is great and you can tell it’s loved cause it’s protected by plexiglass. We just happened upon it and I looked on the map to see if it’s here- sure enough loads of folks know about it! Also had a great view right above it. || There’s a comic mural near the toilet, but the smell of urine is quite strong. There are many murals in Lisbon that are far more beautiful. || Artwork is great but it’s small and uninteresting otherwise. The Miraduoro nearby is a better spot to visit. || Very nice place to explore the history and to take pictures. Completely free to see the mural as you walk around in Alfama || Nice place with very pleasing view but only problem are the people making you to buy stuff that we don't even want to look .very sad .these people should be removed from such place || Charming tunnel with a very pleasant artistic mural of the history of Lisboa. You're lucky if you find this remote spot in the winding streets of Lisboa. || A nice, short, and comical summary of the history of Lisbon, located under a viewpoint in a short tunnel down a few stairs. There's also a paid WC there. || Such a beautiful piece of art and some moron spray a graffiti on it. I hope someone will fix it soon || Experienced what I had read. Memorable visit. || We came here as part of a tour of the history of Lisbon, and it's easy to see why - the artist Nuno Saraiva has done a magnificent job of depicting the history of Lisbon in comic strip form, and the entire work is made more humorous in that there is a public bathroom right in the middle of it. || Very interesting depiction of the history of Lisbon. Like a comic book on a wall. Too bad it's next to the public toilet || It is a very nice place to visit and spend quality time with the friends and family. Very much recommended for tourists. || It was underwhelming for the time and effort to reach it. It’s an over sized comic book strip sitting over a public restroom. || Very cool and informative piece, located in an underpass walkway. I've noted other pieces by other artist around Lisbon and am very impressed by all his works. || Some idiot had wiped out 300 years of history and struggle with graffiti. But there’s a fantastic team who will fix it back right. Thanks for the humor and education. There’s nothing comics can’t do!!! || Breathtaking view and fun walk! || Great little cartoon under an arched walkway. Fun to have a quick look if you’re nearby. || There are no place in Lisbon  that I don't like but some are more amazing than others. || We came back to this mural 4 time, always when in Lisbon. It is a classic. || You can find a mural with the history of Lisbon. Unfortunately it has been vandalised... || Really cool viewpoint with nice historical images in a small tunnel. || Great place for a photo! || You can experience more infomation about History || Eye pleasant view form here || A very interesting mural that tells the story of Lisbon in a simple and illustrated way, with a humorous and immediate style. To see it, you have to go down a flight of steps, a detail worth keeping in mind … || Wandering from this point towards Alfama is a delight; follow the steps and you'll see a fantastic grapevine and meet Dora, who has a spectacular Ginja. || Much prettier than I imagined 🫶🏽 Come down the stairs, it's so cute!! …

Beautiful shop with very knowledgeable owner (Paulo). I'm very happy to have discovered this boutique on my Lisbon adventure. || Dear Alessandro, your kind words mean a lot to us. We're looking forward to receiving your next visit. || Exceptional friendliness and knowledge.

Excellent art gallery || A very pleasant space, with different exhibition rooms and a lovely outdoor patio where activities are also organized. || I visited the gallery to see the exhibition of photographs by Palestinian photographers about Gaza. In a simple and welcoming atmosphere, the gallery managed to create a space to show the reality of that people who have suffered so much. || It's worth a visit. It's a shame the garden is in such bad shape. || Top Gallery! With Top Exhibitions! Nasty Women PT Exhibition 2019 from March 8th to 10th! || Beautiful space with an interior garden where I have the pleasure of collecting my Ugly Fruit basket every week. || It's a good place to visit, but just to look around; the prices are geared towards upper-middle-class to upper-class families who can afford to shop in the stores there.

The National Museum of Ancient Art was the first museum I visited in Lisbon, and it left a lasting impression. Even before going in, the setting is beautiful. You can just hang out outside, enjoying the view of the harbor, the train tracks, and the museum itself.  Inside, it’s packed with incredible artwork. If you're into paintings and sculptures, especially those from pre-modern times, this is a must-visit. The restoration work on display is just stunning, and they even show the actual restoration room, which is fascinating to see.  The museum is clean, calm, and aesthetically pleasing. They accept cards for entry, and you can store your bag for free using a locker (you’ll need a coin, but you get it back). Overall, a fantastic museum experience. || The national museum of ancient art... I really enjoyed a lot.. they are represent the history of Portugal,Art works , painting... Must to go. When in Lisbon || With the Lisboa card, the entrance is free. They show diverse art works, objects, paintings which represent the history of Portugal. I enjoyed a lot each floor. || The museum is free every day right now because they are totally renovating the building and they've removed much of their collection. I only had an hour so I did not get to the first floor, but I enjoyed my short stay there. You'll see in my photos and videos what I was able to see. I'd say it's well worth it since it's free! || We came to the Nacional de Arte with high expectations, as we thought there would be as many paintings as the National Gallery in London. Despite the museum houses a collection of European & Portuguese art, jewelleries, furnitures, ceramics...etc, dating from the 14th to 19th centuries, I felt that there weren't many paintings from the well known artists. I expected to spend a few good hours in the museum but we managed to finish within an hour. Staffs were friendly & helpful throughout & the Gallery was almost empty on the day we visited. (Getting there wasn't easy, it's not closed to any metro station & unfortunately, we were not familiar with the train system - otherwise the closest train station would be "Santos". Anyhow, we decided to walk there from our hotel which took us 75 minutes & we were knackered by the time we got there. My advice is to take a taxi or Uber there) It's still worth a visit when you're in Lisbon. || This is so gorgeous monument. One of best in Lisbon. Here is very beautiful garden too and restaurant. || Much higher quality than I was expecting, with some big names in there, most significantly Bosch. There is a cool animated video based on the Japanese screens I really liked, plus I enjoyed encountering some top notch Portuguese artists I hadn't heard of before. || This is the country’s largest and most important museum of ancient art, showcasing works from the 14th to the 19th century. Its vast collection spans painting, sculpture, textiles, ceramics, furniture, metalwork, and decorative arts. The museum is housed in a former 17th-century palace—originally the Palácio de Alvor‑Pombal—which was built on the site of a 17th-century Carmelite monastery founded in 1683. The building was later rebuilt during the Pombaline era. The museum officially opened in 1884 as the National Museum of Fine Arts and Archaeology and received its current name in 1911. Out of more than 40,000 works in its holdings, around 5,000 are on permanent display—including Portuguese, European, African, and Asian masterpieces that reflect Portugal’s global connections during the Age of Discoveries. / ※ Included in the Lisboa Card. || It's a nice museum, but there aren't any special exhibits... || It's a great surprise for those who are not familiar with art environment. The building is amazing, beautiful architecture and very well organised. You can see different halls, from portuguese painting, European painting,  pottery, jewellery, etc. Only to see the painting of Bosch it's worthy the visit. Insane painting. || An excellent museum with a variety on display. From ceramics to jewellery to paintings, all wonderfully curated and well maintained exhibits.  Staff here are very helpful, informative and joyful. Lockers also available to store your backpack.  Minimum of 2hrs, ideally 3 needed to fully enjoy exhibits.  Highly recommend. Entry part of Lisboa pass. || The museum has many wonderful exhibits. Unfortunately when we were there on 28 Feb there was no access to the 3rd floor and we didn't get to see the whole collection. Therefore took 1 star off. The museum needs renovation, due to the rainy weather, it was even wet inside. The museum has amazing exhibits: gold, silver jewellery, paintings, furniture. I hope to visit it again after the renovation. || I hope I’m not being disrespectful, but honestly if you’re short on time you can easily skip this one. The picture that I shared is literally the only interesting part of the museum. And maybe it was under construction and that’s why but the inside didn’t have a lot if appeal, the outside is nice though! || Stepping into the National Museum of Ancient Art in Lisboa feels like stepping into a living time capsule. The walls here truly speak to you, telling stories of centuries past through breathtaking artwork and opulent decor. From intricate chandeliers that whisper of grand eras to paintings that capture the very soul of their subjects, every detail invites you to immerse yourself in history.  The collection is nothing short of spectacular, with masterpieces that span different styles, periods, and cultures. Whether it’s the mesmerizing portraits that seem to gaze into your soul, the detailed religious works that evoke awe, or the stunning decorative pieces, the museum offers an unparalleled journey through art and time.  The atmosphere is serene, and the beautifully preserved interiors make it easy to get lost in the grandeur. It’s more than a museum—it’s an experience that allows you to feel the heartbeat of history.  This is an absolute must-visit for art enthusiasts, history lovers, or anyone who appreciates the beauty of cultural heritage. If you’re in Lisbon, don’t miss the chance to let the walls of this extraordinary museum speak to you! || It's a fine museum. Just very very Christian faith based. I would have thought they would have more than just Christian based images and sculptures. Oh well... Still, time well spent. Takes about an hour to two, depending on how much you read and study each display. || Fantastic museum full of great antiques most of them related to Portugal empire and their colonies. Phenomenal collection of jewelry, furniture, pottery, sculpture and art works from several European countries. They have a really nice garden where we can sit and have coffee or lunch with superb view of river. Recommend!! || Nice museum to visit in Lisbon,  not crowded || The museum is so much better than I expected. Honestly, it's a must in Lisbon (for antique art of course). I would say it's very big - 4 floors with expositions, garden and an additional section (extremely beautiful as well) - and the art is as expected. Great selection, mainly religious but not exclusively, and most importantly, the very famous painting of Bosch. It was a nice experience and you'll probably be able to do the whole museum in 2-3 hours. || National Museum of Ancient Art located  in calm part of Lisbon with easy access by bus or walk distance. It's massive with 3 floors with extra exhibitions on ground floor-  this summer Barcelona Gothic. Perfect for Sacred Art fans as predominate throughout all exhibition. There is little shop, toilets  and lovely garden on the back. You will need to leave your bigger bag in the locker and any liquid containing alcohol also not allowed. Would recommend to buy combo tickets for museum + exhibition  for €8 || Although the weather was terrible on a Saturday morning, it’s incredible that hardly that many people visit this place. There are some significant historic Portuguese relics here. Gold, gem studded relics of the historic age. To painting by masters not probably cataloged correctly.  However amazing and fantastic the collection is, there is a lot that needs to be addressed. The museum needs an advertising push to get people through the door. A lot of the pieces need better explanation and the artists of the works in the collection need to be brought to the forefront. There is so much room for huge improvement and it will need a lot of backers to help that off the ground.

Absolutely insane experience. 10000/10 would definitely recommend to everyone. The guy that worked there was so nice and explained everything so good.The games were insanely fun. I felt so safe walking around the virtual world because everything was so well designed. Really a one of a kind experience and if I am in Lisbon again I will for sure come back!! || ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ We celebrated my son’s birthday here and it was fantastic! The kids had an amazing time, the games are super fun and the staff were great. Perfect place for birthdays. Why we’ll be back! || Super fun!!! We did Shmooter for our son’s 15th birthday. Great gameplay, no glitches, feels like you’re really there in a huge environment. It’s a really fun workout too. Do it!!! || What an experience! Even for my 2, 4, 6 year olds! Super friendly team, accommodating and engaging. He setup my kids perfectly, and as you can imagine, almost impossible to get them out there || Thank you so much Dawid! Your kids were amazing players and we totally get how hard it is to get them to leave. 😄 Hope to see you all again! 🚀  … || Possibly the coolest experience I have ever had!! Staff is super friendly, the games were so much fun (we booked one hour and got to play two games), definitely felt like a real life experience! The games were not only from simple to complex but also have so many different options where you can even play in teams with or against each other! I definitely would do this again!! Most definitely is the highlight of our holiday in Lisbon! || I love virtual games, so I was looking for a place to play in Lisbon. I signed up for a game during happy hour. I liked the location and service. The employee was friendly and kind and he helped me understand rules of games || Everyone should try it! We played 2 games - one was escape room, the other one was with zombies, both were really interesting and brought a lot of fun and suspense! The host was very passionate and kind. I truly recommend it to everyone! || Thank you all so much for making my son's birthday so special! The virtual reality experience was a huge hit—everyone had such a blast, and the kids couldn’t stop talking about it. We even went twice because it was that much fun! || I took my nephew to this experience, and was good fun, we went for half an hour to kill zombies. Nice people on site, tbh the graphics weren’t amazing but they supposed to do some game better, they also provide footage after the game, I will go again. || What an awesome family experience x definitely a great experience for friends and families wanting to have an awesome time together for beginners and experienced players || Thank you so much, Esther! 😊 We’re happy to hear your family had an amazing time. We hope to see you again for more VR fun soon! 🚀  … || Fantastic - my daughter was in heaven. The person in charge was  extremely helpful, friendly and professional. Such a delightful place. I would most definitely recommend it - it is worth a visit. More than once ! I had to play with her because she needed a team but I actually had a lot of fun myself and it was very nice to be aware of what VR is all about. || We did it two days in a row because it was so much fun!!! Our kids age 10 and 13 were absolutely flying high The instructor was great and helpful if we could give 10 stars ww would have || We hosted a kids birthday party here and the team was incredibly helpful from start to finish - and fantastic with the children on the day.  Highly recommend! || Was my first VR game in a room with my dear Portuguese family and although I didn’t win it was really good fun! One room, 8 people shooting eachother for 50 min! || So fun! The games were brilliant. Perfect for a big or small group. We played for 2 hours for a stag party and honestly we could have done double that. Everyone loved it. || Great place for a Ten Year old party!! || A great discovery, my 10 year old daughter and her friend experienced the virtual adventure. They had a great time and felt that the 60 minutes had passed as if it had been 20 minutes.  We'll be back for sure and we adults will too. || We had our son’s 13th birthday party here, and I think the adults had more fun than the kids. Great place for a party, and I see many more visits in our future based on the reaction from the kids. The owner is extremely helpful and kind! || We visited Another World in Lisbon and had an amazing time! We booked a 1-hour session for two people, which gave us the chance to play two different 30-minute games with a short break in between.  The staff was incredibly friendly and helpful, making the whole experience smooth and welcoming from start to finish.  The VR games were highly immersive and full of action. Nice athletics track for running but off-limits most of the day Saturday and Sunday due to football having priority. Most days you can use the track from 7.00 to 21.00 with 3€ fee for non members however on Saturday and Sunday, usually starting at 8.30 until midnight the track and fields are reserved for football. Eduardo VII Park is one of the most beautiful and relaxing green spaces in Lisbon. The park offers stunning panoramic views over the city and the Tagus River, making it a perfect spot for photos, walks, or simply enjoying the scenery. The wide paths are ideal for walking or jogging, and the well-maintained gardens add a peaceful atmosphere away from the busy city streets. One of the highlights is the impressive geometric garden design and the viewpoint at the top of the park, which provides a breathtaking perspective of Lisbon. The park is also very spacious, so it never feels overcrowded, even during busy hours. There are benches throughout the area, perfect for resting and enjoying the surroundings. Eduardo VII Park is great for families, couples, and solo travelers alike. It’s close to the city center and easy to access, making it a must-visit for anyone exploring Lisbon. Whether you’re looking for a quiet place to relax, take a walk, or admire the city from above, this park is definitely worth a visit. || We were in Lisbon for several days while waiting to start a cruise with NCL.  We stopped at the north end of this magnificent park and walk all the way to the southern end.  Lots of great views and spots for wonderful pics.  Several monuments along the way. || Parque Eduardo VII is a beautiful park with stunning views of the city and the river. It's beautifully maintained, with plenty of greenery and spacious walkways. Highly recommended if you are in Lisbon during the holidays! || Parque Eduardo VII is one of the best spots in Lisbon to enjoy a peaceful walk and take in a great view of the city. Well manicured lawns and hedges. The top of the park is a has the Monument to the Carnation Revolution, flanked by two sets of two obelisks. Car park nearby and easy walk to observation deck. Wear comfy shoes, take water, wear hat, sunscreen. Great place for photography || Very large sloping park mainly put over to trees and grass. Lovely view from the top across the city. The lighting is warm and low, the atmosphere inviting but charged, like something delicious is about to happen. And for us, it did—because Camila was our server.  Let me be clear: Camila wasn’t just good—she was a masterclass in service. Her confidence was quiet but magnetic, her knowledge of the menu as smooth as the bourbon behind the bar. She didn’t just take our order, she curated it. Every recommendation felt personal, like a whispered secret between old lovers.  We started with the nachos, and oh God—layered like a love letter, each chip holding a perfect balance of sharp cheddar, crema, and slow-braised meat that melted like velvet. It wasn’t just bar food—it was seduction on a plate.  The salmon sandwiches came next—decadent, sexy little things. The fish was silky and luscious, resting in a toasted roll with dill cream that made you want to close your eyes and just… feel. Every bite was a soft sigh of satisfaction.  And then—the shepherd’s pie. Rich, earthy, wrapped in whipped potatoes like a warm body under silk sheets. The flavors were deep and slow, the kind of dish that makes you lean back and smile at your date without needing words.  Throughout the night, Camila moved through the room like a poem—always there before we realized we needed her. She laughed easily, poured wine like it mattered, and treated us like we were the only people in the world.  Vitrine Bar doesn’t just serve food—it serves a vibe. And with Camila guiding your night, it becomes an experience that stays with you long after the last sip. || Thanks! The attention to the client is unmatched. Had a great night there having a drink with a friend, nibbling the fresh pop corns that they bring to the table and just vibing to the music they play. The decor is out of this world, because it's authentic nineteenth century (early twentieth, maybe). The cocktails are amazing and the service is on another level. Marcelo the bartender is the most attentive and next-level polite person you'll ever find at a bar. It's small, kind of dark and all amazing. || Terrible service and quite dirty. Such a shame because the place is cool! || Told them I was vegetarian and they were so helpful, and made me a vegetarian sandwich. Great dive style bar with fab music. Coming again tomorrow! || Unfortunately, when the waiter approached my table, he took my friend's order but ignored me entirely. I waited patiently for him to acknowledge me, but he didn’t. Eventually I had to leave my seat and approach the waiter to place my order. … || It is one of those pubs that are not common anymore. They keep that "old vibe" of service and cordiality. It seemed like "too much", but after my experience I would definitely come back! Fun, non expensive and really good vibe. It's not the … || Great atmosphere! Takes you back to the 80’s with lots of rock classics playing in background, but soft enough so you can talk clearly and comfortably. Good cocktails, and there’s a playing room. || I was really looking forward to this place. Little speakeasy in Lisbon. It looks wonderful, perfect lighting, plush banquettes, waiters dressed up like it's 1920. Smells of mothballs but you get used to it. … || Nice cozy place were we can talk without yelling at each other’s || this is a very cosy bar with a nice noir atmosphere and the staff which I presume was Vic himself was an old fashioned gentleman. one of the nicest experiences in Lisbon for us || Cozy place, not too crowded, very friendly staff and amazing drinks, highly recommend! The staff renewed our popcorn for hot new ones without we even order. || Great experience! Lovely staff, great drinks and awesome atmosphere. Plus: great snacks included!!! … || Great bar and atmosphere. A place to return and try more cocktails! || As a Portuguese player, I can say this bar is a kind of a pearl or jewel in the very heart of my city. Such a cozy and private little spot. They even have a snooker table  in the lower floor. … || Great bar a little hidden but with a great atmosphere,  the cocktails are amazing and there is a separate area with snooker tables that you can rent and play with friends || Very nice place for late and quiet drinks with friends. Our go-to place to end the night when the dinner ends too soon. Only let down is people can smoke inside, so the air has a lot of smoke and we end up smelling like it even if we're not smokers || What a great find shame we only found it on our last night or we would of been going every night. When we walked up we thought o we have to ring a bell but you don't the entrance is down the side where you are made very welcome service and price for drinks was great. Highly recommend || A place to see. The decoration of the bad is unusual and create a special and nice atmosphere. …

Thursday night visit on my own. Excellent. Got there at 9pm, and the band started at 9 15. And played till 11.  40% of seats taken by the time I got there; there are only about 30 seats, and limited standing area. Cover charge of €10 and … || Thank you very much, Ian! See you soon! || Small and cozy place. The band was fantastic, playing beautifully and creating such a relaxing, authentic jazz atmosphere. We didn’t make a reservation, we just showed up at 9pm sharp to find the best seating place, the band started at 10pm. A special shoutout to Edwardo & Rita their hospitality and kindness made the evening even more enjoyable. They made us feel truly welcome from the moment we arrived. || Thank you very much! See you soon! || Exquisite, small and intimate jazz club. Live music every night every day. Amazing service and atmosphere. But please be aware and respect the house rules - silence when musicians play. If you want to gossip with your friends with some background music this is not your place. If you enjoy music in it's deepest form, this is definitely your place! Card payments accepted and english spoken by staff so very easy for visitors in town to come and enjoy. Will definitely be back. || Thank you very much, Tuomas! See you soon! || Amazing cozy place for Jazz! Wonderful atmosphere. They serve some snacks, like pizza (which looked really nice) but the main thing is drinks and music of course. Highly recommend. Even if youre not a Jazz fan per se, you will love it. Staff is friendly! Go early cause seats are limmited. || Thank you very much, Isabel! See you soon! || Wonderful venue and even better music. We stopped here shortly before getting an early flight out. It’s small so if coming for a gig I recommend getting there close to doors opening. || Thank you so much, Wana! See you soon! || The place is beautiful and elegant. It was hidden in a quiet neighbourhood, in the beginning I was a bit hesitant but once they opened the door, Its like another world, a bit like speakeasy bar  The staff were very friendly. The minima expense for jazz gig is €10, which means if you order drinks more than €10 then the gig is free  The gig I had that night was very good, but was so late, 11pm-2am, I had to leave at 12 otherwise I almost fell asleep, can’t really enjoy the music , really wish they could start earlier || What a fabulous place! A gem! The owner is super friendly - answered my questions in advance and chatted to us when we were there to explain the background to the music (the night we went was a kind of Portuguese folk jazz fusion - which was beautiful and high quality). The place is small, packed full of locals with a really warm atmosphere. We had cocktails (great) and stayed for both sets. If you like intimate venues away from the tourist drags you’ll love it. || Thanks, David! See you soon! || All good very beautiful and they respect the moment for the musicians! The entry is 12,5€ plus what you want to drink. There are no tables just sits. The only thing is that the space is a little bit small and were full and more people was coming inside 🫣 you don’t need to do reservations 🙂 || Távola is easily the best place for live jazz in Lisbon! Excellent music, service and drinks. || Thank you so much, Liz! See you soon! || I'm not new to jazz, but new to the jazz scene here in Lisbon. Finally made it to Távola. The space is tight and the gig I saw was a trio...the musicians were fantastic and did not disappoint. There's an intimate setting where you are as close as possible to the musicians, so the audio quality is live and not being blasted through big speakers. €10 music cover €3 small beers, food: more bar style, simple (my next visit I will for sure eat before I go to hear jazz) || Thanks, Aaron! See you soon! || Hidden gem of a jazz club in Lisbon. The decor is 1970s the vibe is just perfect and musicianship out of this world. The hosts are friendly and on-point. Highly recommend a visit anytime you happen to be in Lisbon. || Thank you very much, Alastair! See you soon! || Top notch traditional jazz in an intimate environment.  I didn't try the food but the drinks etc were very good. || Thank you very much, MJ! See you soon! || What a great venue. Small and very friendly, Nuno his wife and daughter run the bar. Small intimate place, lots of character. A little hard to find at first, don’t give up just follow google. Music was really top class. Best jazz in Lisbon. So good I went back the next day, and it was even better! You won’t be disappointed. Starts really at 10.30, goes till 1. But go earlier and soak atmosphere. || Thank you very much, Jonathan! See you soon! || A very cozy place with a relaxing atmosphere even though it’s quite small and can be packed with people. The acoustics and setting while listening to live jazz is totally worth a visit. || Thank you very much! See you soon! || Great small jazz club with live music 5 nights each week. Tavola has a relaxed and welcoming vibe with lots of comfortable seating. If you enjoy jazz music, be sure to put Tavola on your list of places to visit in Lisbon! || Thank you very much, Dave! See you soon! || Really nice place to hang out and enjoy some live music,  The crew working and the people visiting the club are great.  There are some downsides.  1.  The club is super small.  2. It's not in a stand alone building.  3. It opens at 8 PM but be there by 6:45 or you probably won't get in.  4.  Being on the ground floor of a residential building they really want you to stand around outside and be very quiet. Probably due to local quiet hours laws.  For first timers, you will get a paper from the person at the door when you go in.  You take it with out to the bar and they mark your drinks. You pay when you leave the club by giving your paper to the bar tender where they add up your drinks and the $10 cover charge.  The system works for them.  Great atmosphere, good drinks and music, and great people and staff.  You will definitely enjoy it just now it will be an early evening and a long night. || Nice small club, the band was amazing today, I didnt expect it in Lisabon :) the only pitty is, that it is a bit far from my hotel 😀 || Thank you very much, Jirí! See you soon! || One of the most heartwarming places I’ve ever been to! Great music, amazing atmosphere, drinks were reasonable and great service || Thank you so much, Shamz! See you soon! || Prob the best Jazz club in Lisbon right now. Really cool atmosphere and good music, the pizzas are surprisingly good too. It's crazy they're able to do live jazz every day, I hope it keeps like that. There's a 10 euro cost to enter at the time of performance but it's worth it trust. || Thank you very much, Afonso! See you soon! || Great set up of an intimate jazz club. Good vibe. Cool crowd. Caught the last bit of a set on a Saturday night and the performance was great. Owner Nuno and his family were very hospitable. Great to see jazz alive and well in Lisbon. Not in city center but easy to reach by metro. || Thank you, J S! See you soon!

I’m afraid to rate this place, because I don’t want anyone else to know about this spot. Honestly I’ve lived in Portugal 2 years and hands down this is absolutely the best massage place I’ve been to. Now, if you don’t speak Portuguese, there might be a bit of a challenge with some of the therapists. But really, you’re not coming here to talk anyways, right? The ladies who work at the front are warm and welcoming. The facility is clean and comfortable. And the therapists are amazing. Definitely recommend! || Thank you very much for your kind words and for taking the time to share your experience. We’re truly happy to know that your visit was so memorable and that you felt well welcomed, from reception to the session itself.  Our focus is exactly that: to provide a clean, comfortable and professional environment where the body can fully relax — conversation naturally comes second 😉  Thank you for your trust and for the recommendation. It will always be a pleasure to welcome you again. || I had a session with Lavinia, a Brazilian therapist here, and it was great. She was friendly, attentive, and made me feel comfortable right away. The whole experience felt personal and unhurried, and she clearly knows what she’s doing. I left feeling relaxed and very satisfied with the visit. || Thank you for your visit, you will always be very welcome. || Wherever I travel — across East Asia or Europe — a good massage is something I always seek out. I know what makes it truly exceptional: cleanliness, skill, and that subtle touch of art. Nowhere have these three come together more beautifully than here.  What I received here not only relaxed my body and calmed my mind—it touched something deeper, as though my very soul had been gently held. || Thank you for your visit. We will always be looking to innovate, to surprise you. || Best experience I've had in a spa. The location is perfect and the staff is amazing.. definitely gonna come back! || Thank you so much for your lovely review! We’re delighted to know you had such a positive experience at Lennure Lux Spa. Our team is committed to providing a calm and welcoming environment for every guest. Very beautiful, clean and welcoming environment. Attentive and well-trained professionals who provide high-level service and true relaxation. It's a pleasure to know that you appreciated the atmosphere, the care, and the professionalism of our team. At Lennure Lux Spa, every detail is designed to ensure well-being, tranquility, and a truly revitalizing experience. Your recommendation means a lot to us. See you soon! || I went with my boyfriend and we were seen by therapist Luana. An excellent professional, the environment was calm and very welcoming. We left feeling totally relaxed. || Thank you so much for your testimonial! It's very gratifying to know that you enjoyed a relaxing and positive experience at our spa. Therapist Luana and the entire Lennure Lux Spa team are dedicated to providing moments of well-being, serenity, and harmony. You will always be very welcome. || My experience at O ​​Lennure Lux Spa was very pleasant, attended to by therapist Mia, and it provided me with an excellent moment of relaxation. || Thank you so much for your feedback. We are happy to know that we are on the right track to bringing satisfaction to you, our customer. || I loved the spa, excellent service from reception to the end. I had a treatment with my husband, with therapists Paul and Nina! I recommend it. || Thank you for visiting. You are always welcome. || I visited, the space is very pleasant. I was attended to by Lavinia, and she was a 5-star professional, kind, sweet, and very professional. A very pleasant experience to be repeated soon. || Thank you so much, Diogo. I'm very happy to know that you enjoyed our space and the service as well. You'll always be welcome! || We were seen by therapist Luana and I really enjoyed it.
