For me, this park goes on the Lisbon's top three, although playground needs some repairs, as it currently holds only 3 swings, 4 bouncy rockers, 2 short slides and little else that's working. || It's very special as it has beautiful trees: magnificent umbrella pines and cork oaks, and a wide variety of bird life: I have seen hoopoes in this park, part of what was once the estate of a manor house, before urban development reached this part of Lisbon about fifty years ago. Very few people come here, except for weekend picnickers at the specially provided tables, so it is a mini escape from the city. There is a training circuit, which nobody uses(!), and a small café. || Nice, quiet place to walk.  Lovely cork and eucalyptus trees.  Many benches to sit in the shade. Nice views from the top of the park. || Great place for families, picnics. Pros - you can bring your dogs there, the area with tables is covered by trees, there is also a playground for childrens. Cons - no WC || One of the great city parks in Lisbon. A good area with lots of trees and great for birds. It also features a playground for kids, a cafe stand with some live music on weekends. Goos for biking, walking or just enjoy the trees. Um dos poucos parquea a sério de Lisboa. Bem arborizado, tem circuito de manutenção,  parque infantil, zonas de picnic. Cafe com musica ao vico em alguns fins de semana || How nice it is to have such a park in the middle of the city. And the small bar "Esplanada da Mata" is worth visiting for a drink and a bite. || Amazing place for running, biking, etc || Nice place, but need maintenance in general. In the end nothing special there are several best parks in Lisbon

place_name: Garden of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation
reviews_content: Such a lovely garden full of paths and little bridges and loads of seating in the shade and great fun to explore and some statues too and we saw a heron and lots of ducks.  The amphitheatre was a real surprise too || Beautiful garden with long bamboo passage ways, a pond with lots of cute ducks, a small area to eat ice cream or coffee and a large area great for dogs. This is a great place to go on a walk with friends or go on a study session. Everything is full of vegetation and butterflies. Like an actual 'secret garden'. If you like fantasy books this is your place to go because it looks like a place in a fairytale. I cannot recommend this garden enough, especially for outdoor lovers. My description doesn't give this place enough justice. || This place is part of a foundation started by Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil tycoon and art lover. You can really feel his belief that “art is for everyone, and beauty means more when it’s shared.”  Right in the middle of the city, there’s this peaceful garden with tall trees, calm ponds, and quiet paths. I could take my time and enjoy the art without any rush. The way nature and art come together here left such a strong impression. || A very lovely garden, located in the center of the city. It’s super convenient to visit either by metro or different bus networks. Here, it’s more like a combination of different gardens, so there are lots of options to enjoy the sun, green, and overall atmosphere. Totally recommended to visit, including the museum inside. || Gorgeous space for all to enjoy for free - lots of areas to picnic, hang with friends, for kids to run around or bike, easy for strollers to get around. There are also two cafes and an ice cream shop - you can spend a whole day enjoying this beautifully maintained space. There must be a mighty team of gardeners tending to all the plants! What a valuable space for residents and visitors alike in this otherwise very densely developed city. || Gulbenkian always had beautiful gardens, around the museums buildings. Landscaping as Portuguese know how ! Now that the renovation of the modern museum is achieved, there is a new setting of this side of the gardens to discover, mix of Japanese zen design, existing garden style and a monumental, yet perfectly integrated awning. Inspiring place where to wander, with cafe and sometimes outdoor activities at the amphitheatre. Just mind the rush hours and some week-end can be crowded, as this place is since long praized by Portuguese and tourists ! || My primary objective was to visit the museum; however, due to renovations, the collection had been relocated.  I was disappointed by the limited number of items, particularly paintings, compared to my expectations. Nonetheless, the collection was aesthetically pleasing and unique.  The garden, however, was unappealing.  Perhaps I mistakenly visited the incorrect park, as signage was inadequate, requiring extensive navigation to locate the proper entrance. || Big enough to wander around. The noise of the city suddenly stops and everything becomes cooler. Part of it is like a jungle. Lots of people either solo or couples and a lot of families with small children. It is a really special place || Designed in the 1960s by Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles and António Viana Barreto, the garden is a beautifully landscaped urban oasis in the heart of Lisbon. The space features a harmonious blend of lakes, streams, terraced lawns, and forested paths—creating a tranquil environment for relaxation and reflection. The garden connects seamlessly with the main Gulbenkian Foundation building and museum, allowing visitors to experience art, architecture, and nature in one integrated setting. || Quiet, cozy park perfect for rest, private conversation with a friend or relaxation! || Best place to hide when it is very hot. There are lots of nice shaded banks to sit and rest under the trees. || Lovely place to escape the bustle of Lisbon for some hours, still in the middle of the city. Grab a picnic towel, a book and sunscreen and lay down for the afternoon. The grass field in the garden is lovely to get some sun light. Even in winter. || one of the most eye-relaxing places seen during my life. An intellectual and thoughtful place , where you can nurture your mind and abandon  everyday tortuosity. the place I’ve been missing the most since my departure from Lisbon. || A really nice place to wander around, there's lots of corners tucked away if you want to sit by yourself or have a conversation. And they have ducks! || Well-known park in Lisbon where people go to just hang-out, relax, create, work and have a love/get out of here relationship with all the ducks! The museum offers a lot of commodities as well and many times have free entry events :) || So relaxing to walk the grounds of the garden. There are shady as well as sunny areas depending on what you prefer and a cafe for your meals. The ducks and the water areas make it even more attractive. Unfortunately a large part of the grounds are under renovation, so we couldn’t walk there. Still, the air is crisp and the garden is well maintained for visitors. || One of the most gorgeous public gardens I've been to with stunning art, landscaping, plants and wildlife. They are doing extensive renovation in a section of it so it's blocked off (and will be incredible once done) but there's still plenty of areas to wander on paths, sit on benches, grab something at cafe and sit outside and enjoy the birds. I brought my camera and had so much fun capturing images of the Spring babies. Truly a remarkable place for all to enjoy. || A perl in the city of Lisbon. Strongly suggested if you have any minimal appreciation for plants and greenery. They have three great greenhouses with a wide variety of plants from all-over the planet. It also looks like a sustainable place to support with a visit. Entrance tickets are cheap and discounts are available. || Beautiful place to go with time on a sunny day to enjoy yourself and/or friends. Lot's of benches to sit or grass to lay down if you want. Different areas to see and walk to. I really loved even though it was drizzling when I went there. I will come back tho. || My favorite park in Lisbon — full of artwork, exotic plants, winding paths, and little ponds. Despite all that, there’s still plenty of open space to sit or lie down and relax. My 10-year-old son loved it, too.

A beautiful park where you can spend a few hours. It has a path that goes around it and which I recommend to walk. Beautiful trees and ponds ideal for a pause after a busy day. There's a café which is usually busy and a table is hard to find. On Sundays there's a small marketplace and so you can encounter locals mixed up with tourists. Just across the street you'll find the admirable Basílica da Estrela which is worth the visit. || I met some friends at Jardim da Estrela and it was a very nice experience. The park has lots of trees and open space, so it felt calm and relaxing. We enjoyed walking and sitting by the small lake together. || This is a gorgeous park — perfect for people-watching or for families with kids who just want to escape the hustle and bustle of Lisbon. It’s a peaceful spot to unwind and enjoy a slower pace in the middle of the city, and it even has restrooms (although I wouldn't call them clean but they were free), which is always a plus when exploring! || This place is heaven! One of the most beautiful parks I've seen by far. It's full of nature and also some animals, mostly birds. The place is perfect for a weekend picnic, a chilly eventing, yoga, hangouts and more. Thank you Lisbon for this amazing green gem! || Stunning park in the heart of Lisbon. Absolutely stunning. Full of beautiful plants and flowers, ponds and statues. Benches everywhere and the wonderful Banana Cafe inside which sells burgers and sandwiches, drinks and other refreshments where you can dine alfresco || 🌿 A Peaceful Oasis in the Middle of Lisbon ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5) We stumbled upon Jardim da Estrela on a warm afternoon, and it turned out to be one of the most peaceful and refreshing places we visited in Lisbon. It’s more than just a public park — it feels like a little urban sanctuary. The garden is beautifully maintained, filled with exotic plants, huge trees offering generous shade, and winding paths that invite you to slow down. What really stood out for me was the birdsong — there were so many birds, and their constant, melodic chirping made the whole place feel like a live sound bath. It’s incredibly soothing. If you have the time, don’t just walk through. Find a quiet corner, sit down, breathe, and maybe even meditate. This place is perfect for that. It’s not just visually calming, it actually sounds calming too. There are also benches, fountains, a lovely gazebo, and a charming little café nearby if you want to sit and sip something while watching the world go by. Families, joggers, solo readers, and locals chatting on benches all seem to coexist naturally here. It has a very authentic Lisbon energy — not overly touristy, just real life unfolding in a gorgeous setting.  Quick Ratings: Atmosphere: 10/10 Birdsong & Nature Vibe: 10/10 Relaxation Potential: 11/10 Accessibility: 10/10 Instagram View: 8.5/10 Highly recommend making time for it — especially if you’re feeling overstimulated by the city. It’s the kind of place that quietly resets your mood.  If this helped, I’d love a 👍 — and don’t forget to breathe deeply when you visit. 🌿✨ || I recently spent a peaceful afternoon at Jardim da Estrela in Lisbon, and it quickly became one of my favorite spots in the city. Located directly across from the grand Basílica da Estrela, this romantic-style park was inaugurated in 1852 and offers a refreshing blend of history, nature, and community life. The park spans 4.6 hectares and features winding paths shaded by exotic trees like jacarandas and ginkgoes, as well as beautifully maintained flower beds and small lakes with ducks and turtles. One of the standout features is the wrought-iron bandstand, originally built in 1884 and relocated here in 1936, which adds a touch of old-world charm. Families and locals gather here, especially on weekends, to enjoy the playgrounds, picnic areas, and the café with outdoor seating that serves light meals and drinks. The park is free to enter and open daily from 7 am to midnight, making it an accessible and welcoming space for everyone. Whether you're looking to relax, take a leisurely stroll, or immerse yourself in a bit of Lisbon's history, Jardim da Estrela offers a serene and delightful escape from the city's hustle and bustle. || I have a 5 year old and a 2 year old. This is hands down my favorite park to take them to in Lisbon. Great playground. Lots of space to run. A cute little library with little tables the kids can draw and color at. Birds walking about. Cafes for a quick coffee or juice. Plus it’s super safe because it’s all gated. || Definitely one of the most loveliest gardens in Lisbon, if you come here for a few days, I would strongly recommend to see this place. Very cool for pet owners and children hence the park has playgrounds and a huge space  for dogs to enjoy. Also, it’s a very good place just to meet and chill or enjoy your day in serenity. || A beautiful park with ancient trees. Ideal for sitting in peace. || The garden is truly magnificent. For the past several months, we have spent an hour here every afternoon, strolling and unwinding. The vibrant colors of the flowers, the soothing rustle of the leaves, and the gentle warmth of the sun create an atmosphere of pure serenity. || Beautiful park with many interesting plants in it. Great for spending a few calm moments during sightseeing or for lunch break || Beautiful park with a wide variety of trees and different areas for either working out or doing a picnic, reading and relaxing. Is rather small for a jog yet early mornings or later in the evenings is really peaceful and perfect for a walk. || Probably the best part of Lisbon. Quiet, peaceful, and with a lovely café that has plenty of tables where you can sit, have a bite, and rest. Thankfully, the usual loud and disrespectful tourists haven’t discovered this spot yet (and I hope my review won’t attract them, lol). Surrounded by lots of greenery, it’s such a beautiful, relaxing park — right across from the basilica. Love it! || Im so happy I found this place! Beautiful trees, very dog and children friendly. Banana cafe serves great coffee and pastel da nata ❤️ || I feel so blessed and lucky to be a short walk from this beautiful oasis. The care and thoughtfulness the Portuguese put into public spaces with a care for community is beautiful to experience. || 2€ Banana Bread under quiet Palmtrees in the middle of a bustling Metropolis, what more can one wish for? Fantastic, quiet place to have a beer, run or just have a chat near the pond. Especially beautiful at night! || Lovely park, plenty of benches dotted around to sit and enjoy the greenery and tranquility.  2 cafes with good selection of food and drinks. || I must admit that it is a very very nice park. I liked a tree in particular, they have a liberty-style gazebo, toilets and a couple of cafè, a small artificial lake with ducks, an exhibition building and statues scattered here and there. It is right in front of Estrela cathedral. || A beautiful and well maintained garden. This was built in 1852 as first public park of Lisbon. It has many old and beautiful trees. Worth spending some time and walking when you are free.

Pleasant green space with coffee shops and bars as well as a children’s play area. One of the bars has live entertainment. At one end of the park, stunning view of Lisbon and the river. || One of the best gardens in Lisbon!! Very chill and relatively less crowded than the other famous parks here, so if you’re looking for a serenity, this might be a good spot. Easy to come here by tram or metro after walking a bit. || Great place for a hanging out - beautiful scenery, centrally located near the bairro alto - I can totally recommend || Bistro/restaurant in the park, perfect for a timeout from sightseeing in the shade, there was a singer singing fado, the food was just es expected, warm, tasty, and the whole experience was just perfect || It’s a good place to sit for some time. There is free access to drinking water and also a place where the public can charge their phones for free. However, you need to bring your own charger. || Lovely park to rest the knackered feet after walking up and down hills all day || A wonderful garden with some lovely plants and flowers to view.  On a hot day, this is a great garden to visit. With many trees to provide some shade, you can enjoy the suns rays as well as keeping chilled.  It's quite a small garden, but with a small fee of 5 Euro it is worth a visit (if you like gardens). There are some cool art displays within the gardens also, which fit into the space nicely.  Overall these gardens offer good value fro money and is lovely to walk around and explore new and interesting plants. || Even at afternoon heat a good place to relax. With small cafe and sometimes live music. Nice! || My neighborhood park. It's awesome. Beautiful trees. Farmer's market on Saturdays. Friendly kiosks for a cold beer or fresh pastry. It's golden! || Wonderful spot to relax after walking all day, or go for a stroll and grab a snack and/or drink at one of two kiosks or the small restaurant. Playground is brand new and has something for all ages. Statues and artwork are a treat to discover and contemplate. Plenty of seating and grass around the park for lounging around. || Most favorite park in Lisbon. It's a perfect combination of nature, art, walkways, grass, benches, and cafe in a free space that's easy to get around. Way better than the botanical garden nearby, and it's free! || I would never give up on recommending this spot in Lisbon. For Saturdays market or to meet with you the oldest tree in Lisbon.. 300 yo ceder. That's the truth story of the city.. you just need to listen. || Amazing small. Garden in very beautiful area for pet walk and child play area there are wooden seat to sit down and enjoy. Very old type of trees looks ancient and historic || Beautiful peaceful park in a nice area with a good kids play area, shaded seating and nearby toilet. || Beautiful place to walk around and enjoy the nice views rot he city. There was live music and a truck to buy some drinks, perfect combination! || I loved the old tree the most and the other cluster of trees that make up the garden. A great place to spot and there are enough vendors to get snacks, beer or a cup of coffee.  Once you are here and you are in for a hike, you can walk to Rato or even Estrella. You can catch the tram 28 to Chiado or do a detour to Cais do Sodre. It is not an easy walk, but yeah, some of the random.things you do in Lisbon and get home walking about 8 - 10,000 steps. || Very nice place to relax. Unique huge tree. Nice vibe music from the park kiosk. Clean and calm || One of the most magnificent trees I have ever seen is in this lovely park. Large enough to sit 60 people under this tree is supported by wrought iron scaffold. I was kid again when I first saw it. Well worth the visit if you are near by. Also has a market on weekend and a cafe that is open daily. || A very beautiful place to sit under a special tree that provides the much needed shade. Find an ice cream parlor nearby and this garden is the perfect place to eat your ice cream. || Just a super place to relax and great cafe in under a canopy of wild looking trees. || Nice garden not so big. Trees, grass and shade good enough for a rest. There is also a small restaurant with a terrace - normal prices. Being in a crowded area specially when are turists it might be hard to find a parking spot. Otherwise there is a public parking (with payment) around the park. || Gorgeous place to stroll in the center of Lisbon. || Very nice and clean garden in the Principe Real neighbourhood.  Lots of shady areas and greenery to sit and relax. Playgrounds for the kids and a small kiosk also available. || Small park in a busy part of Lisbon. Has a small organic farming market on a Saturday and playground for children. There are wooden tables and chairs and seems nice enough || We stumbled across this lovely park while visiting Lisbon for the day. It has a beautiful old massive tree in the middle held up with what looks like a iron /steel frame. Nice place to sit and ponder life. We had the famous custard pie with … || We liked the place. You can just sit and relax for a while before you continue discovering beauty of Lisbon. You can buy coffe, wine or beer; the coffe is in the garden. Enjoy! || Renovated and very organized. Just need fence again to stop dogs entering. Had great time there. Very well organized || Gorgeous Gardens, very beautiful at night, lovely for a gentle stroll with some friends or a loved one. Close to some lovely restaurants and some very interesting features of Lisbon. A beautiful view of the city, fantastic at night. Really recommended... a must. || Maybe my most favorite park in Lisbon. It's a perfect combination of nature, art, walkways, grass, benches, and cafe in a free space that's easy to get around. Way better than the botanical garden nearby, and it's free! || A stunning park adorned with majestic trees – a true haven of natural beauty.

place_name: Jardim da Alameda Dom Afonso Henriques
reviews_content: We love this place we spend a lot time here is perfect to run, to picnic, local festivals, or drink a beer. There is so many cafes and restorants near by and some weekends you can watch people dancing kizomba or playing music || This is huge and beautiful fountain. If you spend more time to climb up to the hill, you will have an amazing view too. Local people come here to play Sport, walk with dogs or relax easily. High recommend. || One of the best place in Lisbon. That you come during the day or evening the view is always magic. If you visit this city you must come here. I love this ground very much. Every time I try to spend a few times here. || A very nice place for relaxing and baby playing. Thanks to Arreiro freguesias. :) || Great park! It has a playground. It also has some benchs and tables with chairs. Great to make a picnic. There is also a kiosk that you can get some drinks and food. At the end of the garden there is a big fountain. It is very pretty. It is also great for families since there is a playground for kids. During the summer there are a bunch of events happening here. || One of the best place in Lisbon. That you come during the day or evening the view is always magic. If you visit this city you must come here. || Beautiful big park. It has some food places around the area. In the park you can chill on the grass, walk up the old fortress like building and also enjoy the majestic huge fountain that lights up in the night. A recommended location to go on a relax date with a bonita Portuguesa 😜 … || A nice place especially during sunny days. I loved the fountain and the atmosphere is chill, not a lot of noisy people. You can have your meal there (if you packed one of course) || A very nice park to spend the evening playing ball, having a picnic, watching the sunset, drinking a beer at the kiosk or just walking around with friends or family. It also has an monumental fountain that lights up after the sunset, with stairs to climb up and get an amazing view of the whole park. || Nice park to hold a celebration. It's opposite the science and technology school in Alameda

My fav Lisbon park! Such a wonderful green space full of amazing trees and plants away from busy streets. The park used to be the garden of a wonderful Palace and is littered with beautiful old buildings and statues surrounded by nature and teaming with birds including chickens, geese peacocks and parakeets plus lots of stray cats. Set on a hill looking down to the river this parc is like stepping back in time. Never too busy and space to sit and just connect with nature. || Pretty neglected for the potential it has.  From dry vegetation that amounts, to destroyed/eroded pathways and all the buildings collapsing or ruined.  Among those a beautiful circular building with a greenhouse like glass roof, that by itself is worth the visit.  Just judge it too harshly by its state for it is in my opinion appealing as a rui ed site.  Can’t help to feel like patrimony is being lost without any concern or attempt to save it.  OVERALL IT IS FREE, so can’t really complain on the ticket price 😂  Therefore the relation price to quality of experience is actually juicy better than the Belém Botanical garden.  Also quite awesome if one is into urban ruin exploring! || I really liked this park, it is located a little away from the city center, therefore, there are very few people here and it is clean. There are several picnic tables, peacocks and ducks are walking, a beautiful view of the bridge, a lot of exotic plants and it's just nice to walk here. || A very wonderful and beautiful park.  - Diverse plants, interesting landscape, lots of greenery, and a fairly large area for walking. - There are buildings and fountains. They are partially abandoned but very atmospheric. - There is a lawn where people sunbathe in good weather. - Chickens, geese, peacocks, and cats roam freely around the area. - The park also has a restroom and an enclosed area for dog walking || A beautiful, tranquil space with magnificent cactuses. The chickens run wild, and it feels like a place from a different era. The views of the bay, framed by the plants are something you don't get in many other places either. || It’s a beautiful park with a rare tree that it’s worth spending some time with. Although it’s not for those with walking difficulties as it has elevations and unevenness. Love that there are chickens, peacocks and geese roaming freely. And there are benches for those who wants a place to chill and have their meals. || It has the potential to be the best park in the city if anyone would invest in it.  It has: In the central part is a big lawn, great for picnics and enjoying the peace and quiet (ducks, peacocks, gees and chickens excluded). To the west of the lawn there is a dog or children park, i was not sure, but it is fenced so they don't bother those that are allergic to them. On the other side to the east of the lawn there is a pond with ducks. Further east from the lawn there are staircases that lead to the closed section unfortunately, with a garden done in french style, with a symmetrical pattern of short hedges outlining the flowers planted there. And by looking at it on google maps it is apparent that on the other side of it there are staircases again leading to another similar area that is also closed off. To the north of the lawn there are buildings. First up right next to the lawn there is a glass dome that looks like a theater of some sort, although small and half the glass roof is shattered, then behind it there are buildings that look like maybe they were coops for the birds that are now running around. Coming right behind that is a plato with a big circular water feature that isn't working and half around it is a wall with a (closed) gate that leads into a (overgrown) corridor that leads to some sort of i guess important building. Next to the corridor starts a cactus garden that has been left unchecked for far too long. Even though cactuses are thriving, the paths through it are bit harder to navigate so caution is advised. || Absolutely got surprised by this little park in a quite busy city district. I was expecting an average garden park in the middle of a concrete jungle, but when I entered I got a real different feeling. Being used to Lisbon's buzziness, I am often missing the nature. This park has a very wild feeling to it. Even though it still offers the clean open grass area to lie down and enjoy a picnic with friends and family, you feel like in the middle of untouched nature just a few steps away from the central grass area. The cactus garden offers exactly what you expect and more. There are wild plants and of course 🌵🌵 but there are also free running chicken and even peacocks with beautiful feathers. Feels very untouched, and has even a great view to the bridge. The constant airplane crossing still remind you that you are almost in central Lisbon. Definitely worth a visit if you like wild nature and peace just around the corner. || Very calm space - the perfect get away from the busy touristy areas. Some visitors are sunbathing on the grass. The cactus garden impressed me with the size of the cactuses - some of them were twice my height. There are many happy birds but mostly roosters, crowing non-stop. It’s probably a way to prove their masculinity in front of the chicks… actually I don’t know - it’s not my business :) There are several neglected structures that are still quite beautiful. || What a beautiful, interesting little park! Off the beaten track, loads of ducks, geese, chickens, and pea-fowl. The cactus garden area was where the chickens were plotting to take over the world lol. So glad we happened upon it. || The park could be beautiful as I believe once was, but today it is very poorly maintained with destroyed paths, overgrown bushes and sad abandoned buildings. It probably wouldn't even be expensive to restore it, so I'm confused how they could let this happen. || A nice park to have a picnic. The few features are the peacocks and the geese’s. And the Dragoeiro plant at the south entrance. I read that it’s rare and only a few hundreds left. The park did have a lot of variations of flora, maybe it’s winter time. Oh.. the white roosters seems to monopolised the north entrance. They are cute and naturally roaming. Just an easy part to walk. Nearby is Jardim Estrella which is smaller but probably more family friendly. You could see my other  review there. || This park is extremely underrated!! LOOK AT ALL THESE CHICKENS!!! I was so surprised and tickled to walk through….chickens, cats, many differently types of cactus (and mature too), and a fantastic view of 25 of April Bridge!!! If I lived here I would come often to the park. Peaceful and a jungle of endless exploration. || This a beautiful park that is located off the beaten path. It is quite hilly but there is plenty of shade. The main reason to go is to see all the species of native birds. I saw chickens, geese, pigeons, and peacocks. Just make sure to not step in the animal dung! || We were lucky to find this place. It's very authentic and very beautiful in terms of authentic landscape design. Just have a look at my photos. We could see many photographers that make photo sessions there. There are many white chickens, colorful peacocks, ducks, gooses, etc. There is big walking area and also some field where you can take sun bath or sit at the tables and have a picknick. || There's a hidden gem in the park - a collection of one of the oldest cacti on the planet. It's a free admission to the park except for the restroom, you'll have to pay for adults. There's a water fountain in the park, so you can fill your bottle with it. We visited during Easter holiday, and it was very nice to see that someone was sweet and thoughtful to "hide" some candies in trees and bushes for kids. || I love this garden: feels so wild with all the wonderful animals! Peacocks, chickens, cats, geese and more.  Highly recommend the cactus garden 🌵 the only downside for me is there’s no like little place for refreshments or drinks (I couldn’t find a water tap either). So come prepared!!! || It's the perfect spot for a picnic, to enjoy a sunny day, or simply for a walk. The park offers a calm setting for outdoor activities and relaxation. || Beautiful calm park with a nice cactus garden, free chicken and peacocks. Very nice. || A peaceful park in Lisbon with quiet paths winding around ponds and towering cacti, plus the occasional rooster to hear or peacock to spot. Perfect for a lunchtime break or a change of scenery. It offers ancient trees and impressive views of the Ponte 25 de Abril. A must-see hidden gem.

place_name: José Gomes Ferreira Park / Mata de Alvalade
reviews_content: Parque José Gomes Ferreira, also known as Mata de Alvalade, is a spacious and peaceful green area in Lisbon. The park feels more like a natural forest than a traditional city park, with wide paths, plenty of trees, and a calm atmosphere that makes it ideal for walking, running, or simply enjoying some quiet time.  It’s not as manicured or structured as other parks in Lisbon, but that’s exactly what gives it its charm. A great spot if you’re looking for a more natural, less crowded outdoor space within the city. || Such a beautiful park turned into a dump. I’m not talking cigarette bums or beer cans. There are all kinds of trash here, especially in the sourthern part of the park, from car tyres to broken glass to used condoms. Disgusting!!! Unsafe for children and dogs || Small but very pleasant park, upper part unfortunately a bit trashy, but you can find a nice spots to sit and walk. There is a small bar on the lower part where you can grab a coffee and some small snacks. Very nice trees and call place, you can see the cork trees there 😻 there is also small miradour and you can see outskirts of Lisbon. Very nice area to walk. || You can visit here just to relax for a moment , while you can sip coffee your kids can play in a playground which is so close to you. It's not a crowded area, i can advise vegetarian toast in that coffee, The guys are helpful, you can rest under long trees || Beautiful park to go and feel nature in the heart of Lisbon. As soon as you enter, you can connect with the environment. Jardim da Parada in Campo de Ourique is one of those rare places in Lisbon that feels genuinely local—quiet, shaded, and full of character. The garden is beautifully maintained, surrounded by big, old trees like sequoias and plane trees, with a small pond in the center where ducks and turtles paddle around peacefully. There’s a traditional bandstand, a nice playground for kids, and a charming little kiosk café that serves good coffee, light meals, and has plenty of outdoor seating under the trees. The vibe is calm and neighborly. People of all ages hang out here—seniors playing cards or reading, parents with strollers, kids running around, people walking their dogs, and others just sitting quietly enjoying the shade. One lovely touch is the old red phone booth that’s been turned into a tiny free library. It’s things like this that make the park feel alive and loved. The space isn’t huge, but it’s got everything it needs. Flower beds are always fresh, paths are clean, and there are benches everywhere. There are also two important statues tucked inside the garden—Maria da Fonte and Professor Ferreira de Macedo—which give it a bit of historical personality. But what really stood out this time was the buzz around the new underground development being planned. The city has announced a project to build a large underground parking garage beneath the garden. While I understand the need to ease traffic and create more parking in Campo de Ourique, I can’t help but feel concerned about the long-term impact this might have on such a delicate green space. There’s a real fear among locals that the construction will disturb the ecosystem of the garden—the roots of these beautiful old trees, the peace and quiet, and possibly the safety of the pond and wildlife. Right now, the garden feels timeless and balanced, and people are naturally worried that digging beneath it could change that. It’s a bit of a crossroads moment for Jardim da Parada. As it stands today, it’s one of the most welcoming and peaceful little parks in the city—loved by the neighborhood and full of everyday life. I hope that whatever happens with the development plans, the soul of the garden is preserved. If you're in Lisbon and want to experience a bit of calm, community, and natural charm, this place is well worth a visit. And if you’re a local—keep an eye on what’s planned beneath your feet. || Jardim da Parada is a compact, well-kept square that does the fundamentals right: plenty of shade, ample benches, smooth paths, a small playground, and a kiosk for quick coffee. It’s surrounded by elegant buildings and steeped in historical importance, making it more than just a green space—it’s a cultural landmark. The wide paths are ideal for walking or jogging, and the well-maintained gardens add a peaceful atmosphere away from the busy city streets. One of the highlights is the impressive geometric garden design and the viewpoint at the top of the park, which provides a breathtaking perspective of Lisbon. The park is also very spacious, so it never feels overcrowded, even during busy hours. There are benches throughout the area, perfect for resting and enjoying the surroundings. Eduardo VII Park is great for families, couples, and solo travelers alike. It’s close to the city center and easy to access, making it a must-visit for anyone exploring Lisbon. place_name: National Museum of Science & Natural History
reviews_content: A pretty disappointing museum overall. There was no one else around during my visit, which made the place feel quite eerie, and the clerk at the entrance seemed disinterested, spending most of the time on her phone. She also offered no direction or information about where to go or what to see, which made the visit even more confusing.  The layout was difficult to follow, with several exhibition rooms closed off and others looking unfinished. Having to pay for entry felt disappointing, especially since the Lisboa Card only gives a 10% discount.  The laboratory and amphitheatre were interesting to see but lacked any real information or context about their purpose or history.  The habitats exhibition was oddly arranged and added to the strange, slightly creepy atmosphere. It wasn’t nearly as immersive as expected.  Overall, it was a lukewarm experience.
