place_name: The National Museum of Contemporary Art
reviews_content: This is a really remarkable contemporary art museum currently presenting a couple of women artists, too. For me after getting tired and sensory overloaded by Lisbon‘s Disney-like overtourism this was the perfect place to calm down on my last day in the city. The interior design of the building with steel and glass bridges under brick vaults is worth the visit, too. I especially enjoyed the Petrified Museum show on the floor. || This was included as a part of my Lisboa card! I am glad I didn’t pay for this on its own as it wouldn’t have been worth it unfortunately. The space is beautiful and clearly a historic building being used for a great purpose. I barely had a welcoming upon entering. I had to ask where the exhibitions started as that was not explained. It was hard to navigate and after reading the reviews now it seems I missed a whole back section of the museum :( Not sure if this was a hallway I missed or if it was an area closed off. I shouldn’t have to pre-read through reviews to find out this information though. The garden looks like it would be a really lovely space as well but it was closed and under construction from the looks of it. Even the washrooms lack signage. Could be so worth it with a few tweaks. || This was a very cool exhibit to see. Lots of great artwork. Definitely worth a visit and price was reasonable. If you are into art make the time to check it out. || Disappointing. The exhibition is very small, not too much interesting works. They have a large section with photos and more classic art paintings which does not fall under ‘contemporary art’, from my point of view. With a Lisboa Card, it is worth to visit, but not as a come-in option. || Well worth visiting when there are a good range of exhibitions on. Some of the galleries are a bit hidden away and  so you do need to follow signs and be willing to explore. One badly signed back corridor and stair leads into the old building at the back, which is well worth exploring. || Not a good start when my partner & I got to the museum at 1pm on a Tuesday to find that they were about to close for an hour - it doesn't say this when you look at their hours on google, but have to go into the website for clarity. Overall, an absolute ripoff of a museum. My partner & I paid 10eu each to visit, & it took us a total of half an hour to see the whole thing! It didn't contain any pieces that were particularly interesting, & even when we did want to know more about the piece, the only information the plaques provided were about who owned the pieces. It's also the first museum I've been to where you have to double-back through the whole thing to be able to get back to the lockers & exit?! Really not worth the price; even if it was free, I'd say it's a pretty subpar exhibit. Check out the review where the guy posted 50 photos from inside; that's pretty much everything. || Truly amazing take on the 20th century art ! They were modern then and crazy and unique now .. the museum is in the best location possible, 4 more museums next to it and a waterfront with so many attractions to see || A real waste of what could be a beautiful space. Very poorly curated, especially in the area around the entrance, with works badly illuminated and obscured by shadows, depressing walls of dark, dismal portraits with opera as ambient music for no reason whatsoever, the 'sculpture garden' is closed and abandoned, there is no interesting information about what's on display, and what there is has been translated badly. Add disinterested staff for the complete experience. The only joy I found were some snails on the gallery wall. || The museum did not meet my expectations. It was smaller than I anticipated, and a significant portion was inaccessible during my visit. I found the artwork challenging to comprehend.  The most notable aspect was the Adam and Eve sculptures with belly buttons. While I acknowledge that contemporary art may present unconventional perspectives, I must admit that I am unable to grasp their significance. || Thank you very much for your comment. Your feedback helps us improve everyday, not someday! Thank you! || Interesting collection of portuguese contemporary art pieces, mostly from the 20th century.  Did not find the flow of the museum easy to navigate, and the exit is on the opposite side of the building, so if you left something in the lockers then you would have to walk back or around the outside of the building.  Free as part of the government's 52 day initiative for portuguese residents.

A must see.  A very well curated and documented history of the resistance to and persecution by the fascist regime that dominated much of 20th century Portugal. Important history that can inform our times as authoritarian regimes try and get power in the US and other countries throughout the world.  The conviction, determination and resourcefulness of the men and women that actively participated in resisting the fascist government is a brave example for us all. || Beautiful monastery, with stunning architecture. Whilst I was there I spotted an evening choral concerto and managed to get free tickets - wonderful experience || This was a fantastic little museum. We took about 90 minutes to read everything. It was laid out well, and brought this little known period of history to life (for a 40 year old British person). Tough in places, but a poignant reminder of how easily we could again lose hard-won freedoms as we witness the rise of right-wing politics in our time. || I have visited the museum the last Saturday of May 2025 and I have only said good things about. I chose a guided visit. The guide, Elisabete Araújo know all the historic details and she is an excellent communicator who explains with passion every bend of the Museum. All the building it is very interesting especially the reproduction of the Pide dungeons, the witnesses of the repression and tortures and the April 25th room that is very moving. The Museum has a wide and interesting offer of books. people in reception is very kind and well informed about the books they sell. I am from Barcelona and I was very satisfied with the visit. Thank you very much. || I visited this museum on a Sunday, there wasn't a lot of traffic in the museum so it was a very nice and calm atmosphere where I could explore most of the rooms alone, speaking of which the museum is really impressive and more expansive than I initially thought || This was one of the best museums I have visited anywhere in the world! The information and displays are well-curated, the layout is well-planned, and the photographic and video artifacts are compelling. Outstanding experience that visitors and locals should take time to see. || This was such a moving experience. Well worth the ticket price. We stayed for far longer than we expected.  I never knew how bad it was for people under the fascist regime - and really, it wasn’t very long ago. || The story of Portugal’s repressive past is very well told. There’s not much in the way of exhibits because this is essentially the telling of a story of how the human spirit was crushed by fascism and how its resilience ultimately triumphed. It is compelling, and moving.  Not very engaging for kids and families but an interesting and important museum to ensure we do not forget the very recent past (because as George Santayana reminded us ‘Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it.” || My wife and I visited this museum on our last day in Lisbon without really knowing what to expect, and we were deeply impressed. Neither of us knew much about the history of the Salazar dictatorship and its downfall in the Carnation Revolution, and we learned so much from touring the extremely well done exhibits here. As a visitor, you walk through a chronological timeline starting with events leading up to the fall of the Portuguese monarchy, the brief period of democracy in its aftermath, the rise of Salazar’s fascist regime and the decades-long resistance that eventually led to the regime’s overthrow in 1974. It was every bit as moving as our visit to the Anne Frank House, and the bravery of the resistance was inspiring. Most but not all of the individual exhibits have English captions, but even if we couldn’t read everything we were still very moved by what we saw. || This museum is a must see, not only from the historical context, but the similarities with today's attacks on political enemies, holding prisoners without due process and secret police roaming the streets of Chicago.   The museum was laid out very well, with text, photos and diagrams that clarified the rise and fall of the Salazar regime.  The museum also clarified the relationship between the mid 20th Century dictatorships, and today's events involving trump.  We spent much more time than planned, allow 2 hours to fully experience this museum. || Museu do Aljube Resistência e Liberdade is a poignant and thought-provoking museum that delves into the history of the Portuguese dictatorship and the resistance movements that fought against it. The museum is housed in the former PIDE prison, where political prisoners were tortured and held captive.  The exhibits are expertly curated and offer a comprehensive overview of the regime's oppressive tactics and the sacrifices made by those who opposed it. The museum's interactive displays and multimedia elements bring the stories of the resistance fighters to life.  One of the most powerful aspects of the museum is the way it preserves the memory of the victims of the dictatorship. The cells, torture chambers, and interrogation rooms offer a stark reminder of the horrors that took place within these walls.  If you're interested in learning more about Portuguese history and the struggle for freedom, I highly recommend visiting Museu do Aljube Resistência e Liberdade. It's a powerful and moving experience that will leave a lasting impression. || This museum is a great place to get a glimpse of Portugal's history of the past 100 years. Over three floors, it explains the political major events from the establishment of the dictatorship to the end of its colony war and the countrys transition to democracy. It's right next to the cathedral and definitely worth a visit. || Provides a good overview of the political landscape in Portugal throughout the years. English translations are not great but allows you to understand the intended meaning. Not very interactive and would not recommend for young children. Mostly pictures, videos, and lots of reading. The earlier period seems to start on the first floor and progresses as you climb stairs. (There is an elevator.) || Really good musuem that's great value for money. Really interesting dive into a key part of Porteguese history which is not very well known elsewhere. Good mix of dense information with some slightly more exciting exhibits and in a historic building right next to the cathedral. || A well curated and informative museum. Housed in a historic building in a lovely part of the city. Pity though that I had the museum all to myself. More folks should be stopping by. || The museum has 3 levels that accounts the history of Portugal’s dictatorship. Although there is a lot of reading, I highly recommend checking it out. Entrance fee is €3 and is free for students and professionals in liberal arts (journalism, teaching, etc.). You will definitely leaving with new knowledge and a deeper understanding of Portugal. || This is a brilliant little museum charting the rise of right wing politics in Portugal from the late 1920’s until the 1970’s. As you slowly walk your way through the three floors of displays (many are in English) the parallels with Nazi Germany and the gradual erosion of personal rights as a dictatorship was formed and maintained was frightening to say the least. I cannot say I enjoyed my visit but I most certainly learned a lot and it reinforced my belief that we must be vigilant as the world seems to swing to more towards a right wing ideology. || extraordinary and overwhelming museum in a former fascist prison documenting the repression of the Salazar regime and resistance to it. absolute must see and really opens your eyes to what went down here not so very long ago. || Entrance is a bit off from Google Maps. It’s located a few steps away.  Otherwise, I would say that the museum is a great place for self reflection. It’s not for everyone. This exhibit is a depressing but effective reminder of darker times. || The Aljube Museum in Lisbon is a must-visit for anyone interested in Portugal's history. Once a notorious political prison, it now serves as a powerful reminder of the country’s struggle against the Estado Novo dictatorship.  The museum’s exhibits vividly portray the harsh realities of life under the regime, including torture, and imprisonment of political dissidents. It's a  experience that underscores the importance of freedom and human rights.

Lisbon Story Centre is an excellent place to understand the history of Lisbon and Portugal. The staff were super helpful and welcoming from the start.  You are provided with headphones in your preferred language, and each interactive segment clearly explains different phases of Lisbon’s history in a very engaging way.  This is honestly one of the best ways to learn about Lisbon, especially if you’re visiting for the first time.  The storytelling, visuals, and audio guides make history easy to follow and enjoyable. A big bonus is that it’s free with the Lisboa Card, which makes it even more worth visiting.  The museum also has clean washrooms inside, which is very convenient. Overall, it’s a must-visit museum for first-time visitors and history lovers.  Highly recommended! || It was really interesting to hear all those great stories about Lisbon’s history. The tour was truly informative; however, clearer instructions could have been given about the audio guide. It was an automatic system, meaning that as we walked into different rooms, the guide would start explaining the story. The problem was that sometimes the audio began in the middle, causing some information to be missed. || We returned to Lisbon Story Centre at about 2pm where the crowd had more or less subsided. This is an amazing place to check out if you are into the ruins and history of the sacred sites. Such a cool place. Plus you can buy a ticket that is good for 4 museums in the group. If you are checking out the free ruins across street ensure you pay the fee to check out the museum as it is worth it. || Museu de Lisboa - Teatro Romano: Where Romans Once Roared and Bluegrass Now Echoes  There’s something magical about watching live music in a Roman theatre, especially when it’s tucked into the winding streets of São Mamede and surrounded by the bones of Felicitas Iulia Olisipo, Lisbon’s ancient Roman self.  We arrived on a Thursday evening, just in time for the monthly performance held every last Thursday at 18H00 and were lucky enough to catch Stonebones and Bad Spaghetti, Portugal’s only bluegrass band. Yes, bluegrass. In a Roman ruin. And it worked.  The excavation site itself is awe-inspiring. You sit among the stones, imagining togas and sandals, while banjos and fiddles fill the air. The crowd was a mix of locals and curious wanderers, all drawn in by the music and the magic of the setting. After the show, we joined the happy throng for a glass of wine overlooking the river, because of course there’s wine. It’s Lisbon.  Then we wandered into the museum, where we met the charming Carlota, a bubbly art historian with a passion for living history and history in the making. She walked us through the scale of the original theatre, which could seat 4,000 patrons in the 1st century AD a fact made even more impressive when you see how modest the current excavation is.  The pottery displays are beautifully curated, and the guides know how to spin a story, turning shards and stones into tales of empire, entertainment, and everyday life.  Verdict: The Museu de Lisboa - Teatro Romano is a hidden gem where ancient history meets modern creativity, and where you can sip wine, hear bluegrass, and learn about Roman engineering all in one evening. Highly recommended for history buffs, music lovers, and anyone who enjoys a good story told in stone. || Outstanding indoor and outdoor spaces showing archeological remains, restoration, artifacts and renderings of what the Roman theater looked like. Excellent place to stop, scenic views and learn history || An absolute must see in Lisboa especially more if you happen to be lucky enough to attend a concert there. || We recently visited the Roman Theatre remains in Lisbon and were pleasantly surprised by how well done the site is. Although it’s quite small, it’s incredibly informative and thoughtfully presented, giving a real sense of the history and significance of the area.  One particularly lovely touch is that they host free concerts on Thursdays a beautiful way to keep the spirit of the theatre alive and open it up to the public in a meaningful way. It’s great to see such cultural heritage being celebrated like this.  We do hope there’s still more to be discovered and that future excavations might reveal even more of the site’s past. For now, though, it’s well worth a visit if you’re in Lisbon and interested in its layered history. || I love Ancient Rome. And this was a great little spot to visit. I love how accessible it was, just along the street but covered quite nicely. Loved it! || The remains of this ancient theater are a reminder of how long Lisbon has stood. The exhibit is very large, but does its job well. We get a sense of how much Lisbon has been through under Roman rule.  I walked away from the site wondering how much more history lies buried beneath the city. || This small but incredibly insightful museum reveals a hidden layer of Lisbon's deep past: the ruins of the Roman Theatre of ancient Olisipo. Originally built during the prosperous era under Emperor Augustus in the 1st century AD, the theatre was a major public building in Roman Lisbon. For centuries it lay buried and forgotten. ​Remarkably, its existence came to light following the devastation of the great earthquake of 1755, which unearthed parts of the structure. Excavations continued sporadically, revealing more over time. The museum itself does an excellent job presenting the archaeological finds (columns, pottery, everyday objects) and explaining the theatre's structure, history, and rediscovery through engaging displays. Seeing the actual ruins integrated into the museum space is a powerful experience. A must-visit for anyone interested in Roman history and the origins of Lisbon! || The main site of the theater ruins are viewable, free of charge, via the walkway constructed around the protected site. Like the museum across the lane (3€), the modern preservation and installations are minimal in style and use architectural outlines to provide the former scope and scale for visitors. The museum features excavation of the centuries of building and expansion over this site, while also housing artifacts spanning all the epocs of human settlement on the hills of Lisbon. || They have every last Thursday of every month a free live music show which was very nice. Seats availability subjected to first come first serve system..

A nice open air venue, in the middle of the park, that holds shows (like concerts, theatre and cinema) during spring and summer. In the first two weeks of August, the “Jazz em Agosto Festival” takes place for over 30 years.  When nothing is happening, you can just have a seat and relax. || A magical venue for shows! Huge concert by Hedvig Mollestad and her band yesterday. Thanks to Gulbenkian Jazz in August. Pity there is little use of this beautiful venue. || Do not miss this peaceful park in Lisabon. One of my favorite places. If You get tired and need a  peace in this beautiful city, go there!❤️ || Spent a lot of time reading great books there in the morning 🙂 I trully miss it. … || It's a fantastic place for summer shows.  The cushions in the stands added immense comfort. || Perfect with or without a concert!! Pleasant atmosphere for relaxing and incredible for events. || Today, Tuesday, April 18, 2023, my son, who is in 12th grade K, went there with his class from Camões secondary school and they had a psychology lesson there, and he really enjoyed it because it's a very pleasant place!!! || Gulbenkian has the best garden in Lisbon. || Beautiful and cool place! || Beautiful and wonderful 🤩🤩🤩 …

Great location and amenities. Needs a little freshening up of wood finishes in the room. Photos show views from the rooftop where there is a nice bar. || Amazing location and the best view of the city can be had while swimming in the rooftop pool. I highly recommend staying here when visiting this beautiful city. || It is a super clean super friendly great place to stay. It's in the center of town. || Rooms are a bit dated but clean. Designed by Cassiano Branco and Carlo Florencio Dias and built in 1931. Unfortunately only the facade was left and hides these days a hotel. || There are many things to see and do.  If you have time, this is a great experience.

I had the pleasure of attending a performance at Teatro da Trindade INATEL recently, and it was a fantastic experience. The theater has such a warm, inviting vibe, and you can feel the history in the walls. The intimate setting really made the performance feel special, and the acoustics were spot on, making it even more enjoyable.  The staff were also incredibly friendly, and the whole evening just felt like a seamless celebration of culture. It’s one of those places that really captures the essence of Lisbon’s vibrant arts scene. I’ll definitely be coming back to enjoy more shows here! Highly recommend if you love great theater in a beautiful, historic space. || Opened in 1867, this is one of Lisbon’s oldest and most iconic theaters. It was founded by writer and playwright Francisco Palha and designed in the Italian theatre style, featuring a horseshoe-shaped auditorium and classic stage layout. At the time of its construction, the surrounding Chiado district was already a cultural hotspot filled with theaters and opera houses. Since 1962, the theater has been under the ownership of FNAT (now INATEL), which continues to support its role as a vibrant space for performing arts. || Classic theater with colorful light at night. You are unable to watch a show here to schedule conflict. But we probably will come back. || My favourite theatre in Lisbon, Portugal. Absolutely beautiful venue. The plays on display are usually very good, with some of the very best Portuguese actors. || Very nice theatre and the play was absolutely amazing!😁 … || Nice old theater Very well preserved Very beautiful || Beautiful facades, but the theatre is not open every day. Really, in Lisbon there are many ancient beautiful theaters, but the are every day closed. || We had a good time in the theater. || Beautiful venue, friendly and helpful staff. Would definitely come back again! || Top! Soo cossy that it seams that we are all family on a concert! Top!

Good Teatre, good seats and facilities. Staff also very polite and welcoming || It was amazing. We saw A Mentira and all was fabulous. The actors were simply great. Cast is fantastic. It has good public transport links to reach the venue. || The Novo Grupo de Teatro – Teatro Aberto – was founded in 1982 by theatre professionals João Lourenço, Irene Cruz, Rui Mendes and Morais e Castro (the famous Grupo 4). Since then, it has been a cultural reference in the performing arts. The old space in Praça de Espanha was for decades the ideal place for those who wanted to see a good play. Since 2002, in this new location with magnificent facilities, the public continues to enjoy excellent performances. || The Blue Room has very good acoustics and the play "Mr. Paul" is very well represented. || I had the opportunity to go see the play "The Son" at this wonderful theater. In addition to the play being fantastic, the theater is comfortable and welcoming, has good visibility (considering you sit at one of the ends) and good acoustics. || Renovated theater with good viewing conditions and a great location. || My experience at the Teatro Aberto can be summed up by this magnificent and suffocating play, The Son. I recommend it to parents. Regarding the auditorium, good visibility, excellent sound. || Teatro Aberto is a safe haven. The plays on stage never disappoint. The adaptation of Peter Handke's play, The Tempest Still, was one of the best shows I've ever seen! || To say I really like it is an understatement. Teatro Aberto is a remarkable space for culture and talent. Please come. || A landmark venue for national culture! Spacious halls. An excellent selection of plays to be performed. || This theater is of excellent quality.  All the plays staged have an exceptional cast, good scripts, good acting, good sets... I've seen some very good plays in this space. || A spacious and welcoming place with an interesting cultural offering. || The theater is great, access is easy, there are several rooms with comfortable seats and excellent visibility. A bar makes it easier for those who arrive early to wait. The staff are attentive and efficient. || Comfortable room, good acoustics and visibility. The resident actors are very good, and there's always a good selection of plays. Without a doubt, a cultural space of reference. || The room is great, with good visibility and comfortable. The lobby is nice and the bar has a great atmosphere. || Great atmosphere, friendly and fun staff, spacious and conversational. Fantastic food at reasonable prices. This is my second time and I'll definitely be back! || I've been a fan of Teatro Aberto since the 80s. The productions never disappoint. || Friendly restaurant, good food and inexpensive. || Magnificent theater. Where I've had the pleasure of seeing wonderful plays. The last one yesterday was "The Children". || It has at least two rooms (red and blue) and a restaurant on the 1st floor, with theater-inspired decor and very friendly service. I recommend the hamburgers, which are anything but ordinary. || The theater is one of the newest in Lisbon and has two rooms that can operate simultaneously if necessary. The plays that João Lourenço chooses are always to my liking. I've followed his group since the creation of Grupo 4, when we were all young. The text has meaning, the set is wonderful and incredibly imaginative. The actors are equally good. I ended up having dinner at Pano de Boca, an original and tasty salad with goat cheese and honey in a beautiful setting. We can bring groups. || Excellent cultural offerings, the best plays I've seen at Teatro Aberto...keep giving us quality theatre, always with great actors in a very welcoming space.

On September 7, I visited Jardim Amália Rodrigues and witnessed a partial blood moon eclipse under a cloudy sky. The park, with its wide open spaces and elevated views, was a perfect place to capture the moment in photos. Even with the clouds, the experience was memorable and unique. || Lovely park and bar with a pool to cool your feet after a long day walking..cycling and generally getting about. The drink prices are reasonable. Definitely call in here if your in Lisbon. It's beautiful. || It is a delightful urban oasis at the northern edge of Parque Eduardo VII. Whether you’re after a peaceful retreat, a picturesque spot for photos, or simply want to enjoy sweeping views of Lisbon, this hidden gem is definitely worth a visit. || Somehow hidden from turistic path, a small part of the parc is dedicated to famous singer. || Designed by Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles and opened in 1996, the garden was named in 2000 in tribute to Amália Rodrigues, Portugal’s legendary fado singer. Fans of Amalia Rodrigues must be very disappointed. Like the rest of the area, very poorly maintained and pedestrian access is dreadful. The sun beats down quite mercilessly at around midday. The many benches are a welcome addition for weary travelers. || What a beautiful park. With a nice a cosy bar to hang out and have a drink while enjoying the fresh atmosphere. || This little garden looked like part of the Parque Eduardo VII. The statue at the entrance was interesting. || Good place to relax and meditation... Also your dog will be more than happy to play into the little lake... A coffee on the side also will be great || Amazing views, beautiful gardens, and a perfect place to read a book. || Not to much illumination by night but it’s a cute place || Everywhere I go in the world I always look for a sculptor from the maestro Botero 🫀🫶.  So glad I saw that they have a piece of his in Lisboa.  🇨🇴🇨🇴🫶🫶 … || I love it. You can find fresh corners to cool off in summer while enjoying a green calm environment. A nice pond with fish, turtles and beautiful lilies. Visit it if you are in the area. || Beautiful green space and a lovely photo opportunity || Chilled park that catches the sun perfectly and usually there is a bit of a breeze and if that's not the case you may find some shade from the nearby trees. Close proximity to cafe for some drinks or a nearby lidl that also sells cold drinks. Sunset can be pretty incredible from this place as well if you're lucky || This was very pretty. Worth seeing if you're in the area. My family, though, was under the mistaken impression that this was a fountain that young children could frolic in. To be clear, once we realized it wasn't, we made another plan. People seemed to be letting their dogs run in. So there's that.  Nearby ice cream stand only takes cash. || A great place to stop for a drink, a bite or both. The round, shallow pool is perfect for dogs to play in. || Beautiful clean park. Really loved it. People were jogging, exercising, walking. Very beautiful.

Genuinely, the hidden gem of Lisbon. Worth the climb up from the coast and my word, what an attraction!  We had no queue and a very chill inside experience.  Explore (and I do mean explore) the exotic meandering paths through the foliage, it's great to spend an hour or so.  A really nice bio diversity to look at and enjoy. Particularly enjoyed the banana tree 🍌  Really fairly priced and a fantastic cultural excursion.  HUGE recommend✌️ || Estufa Fria is a true oasis of tranquility in the heart of Lisbon. A wonderful place to escape the hustle and bustle of the city and enjoy the beauty of exotic plants, waterfalls, and cozy paths. The atmosphere is truly peaceful, with everything well-kept and thoughtfully designed down to the last detail. A wonderful place for a leisurely stroll, meditation, or a romantic date. A must-see for anyone who loves nature and wants to see a different, greener side of Lisbon. One of the most pleasant and inspiring places in the city! || Nature, garden, and park lovers will enjoy this spot. It offers about 30–45 minutes of peaceful walking surrounded by greenery and a small artificial lake.  Entrance costs less than €4 per person — a very reasonable price for the experience.  There’s also a café with a lovely terrace nearby, though it’s not directly accessible through the greenhouse area. || Verry beautiful, if you are traveling to Lisbon or just live here, I would recommend coming here. It’s very beautiful nature in the middle of the city come here and relax and enjoy your day. also, if you are a student or a younger person, you can get tickets for way cheaper. You just need to show your student card confirmation that you are a student and we paid our tickets for five euros the two of us so that’s amazing. || Really nice and super cheap. Cool plants and I saw baby ducks! there are so many rooms and pathways, despite it not being the biggest building in the world you really feel like you can get lost in there. Very thoughtfully and beautifully designed. || If you’re in Lisbon on a Sunday and want a peaceful escape from the city buzz, Estufa Fria is absolutely perfect. Hidden inside Parque Eduardo VII, this lush greenhouse feels like stepping into another world — calm, green, and full of life. 🌴  You’ll walk through tropical plants, waterfalls, and quiet pathways where time slows down. It’s beautifully maintained, not crowded, and filled with natural light filtering through the glass roof — ideal for a relaxed stroll or quiet reflection.  💚 Perfect for: •	A slow Sunday morning or afternoon •	Nature lovers, photographers, and couples •	Escaping the heat or city noise  Tip: Grab a coffee nearby afterward and enjoy the view over Avenida da Liberdade — it completes the perfect Sunday in Lisbon. || This is a great area to stroll through while enjoying beautiful flora and fauna. It is located at the far end of Eduardo VII Park. We spent 45 minutes there. || This botanical garden is my favourite hidden gem in Lisbon! Lots of great spots inside for photography and well maintained. Very affordable too! 🌿 || Most beautiful garden i have ever seen. So lush and green with the most monstera i have ever seen. So peaceful and relaxing. Toilets inside. Sat with goslings and ducklings and saw chickens and peacocks as well. Student tickets were €1.80! Highly recommend || This botanical garden is a true gem, offering a diverse collection of plants.  The layout is well-designed, creating a tranquil and relaxing atmosphere.  There are numerous benches and open spaces, perfect for enjoying a picnic lunch.  The affordable 3 euro entrance fee makes it an exceptional value.  A visit here is highly recommended for anyone seeking a peaceful escape.  The variety of flora provides something of interest for every visitor.  It's a wonderful place to spend a few hours immersed in nature. || One of the most beautiful botanical gardens I’ve ever visited, interesting and extensive collection and a landscape curated in every detail. || I loved this area! Completely covered with very high bamboo ceilings, feeling like a whole new dimension covered with beautiful foliage and secret passageways leading to different areas such as the cactus covered greenhouse. You could easily spend a few hours here just exploring! || mucho verde y mucha vida, one of the best botanical gardens but a lot of areas were closed :/ nevertheless its worth checking out 🌿🌱☘️🍀🪴🎋🍃 || Thanks for a wonderful evening at Estufa Fria during a gala dinner and the opportunity to catch some glimpses of the wonderful plants and garden setting in a former basalt quarry! || The place is beautiful, many different types of tree and plants but some area are under maintenance, good to visit and the price is inexpensive. || Fantastic place that just kept going on and on. Beautiful hidden caves, waterways with fish and amazing variety of plants. Well worth a visit || Incredible! Well worth a couple hours exploration, this place is huge and well organized to feel endless - lots of little paths through the plants. The cactus room was crazy! I've been twice and would gladly go again. || Hidden gem! Always calm and relaxing here. My absolutely favorite location in Lissabon 😍 Must visit for urban and garden architects. Unique origin of this project will bring you to the tropics right from city. You may wander around by the small paths into the huge monstrera bush or  chill on the bench observing the tiny habitants of the garden - birds and fish 😌 Truly zen space ✨🌱 || Beautiful park filled with surprises. Makes you feel like you’re roaming around the jungle with secret little passages, various birds and a nice pond. Special thanks to Maria da Graça who presented the different bird species to us 🥰 … || Really worth the money as it very big and a lot of things to explore. A lot of great spot to take picture. Student get 50% discount. However, you may need to use cash if you don't have credit card that issued in Portugal.

place_name: Jardim da Alameda Dom Afonso Henriques
reviews_content: We love this place we spend a lot time here is perfect to run, to picnic, local festivals, or drink a beer. There is so many cafes and restorants near by and some weekends you can watch people dancing kizomba or playing music || This is huge and beautiful fountain. If you spend more time to climb up to the hill, you will have an amazing view too. Local people come here to play Sport, walk with dogs or relax easily. High recommend. || One of the best place in Lisbon. That you come during the day or evening the view is always magic. If you visit this city you must come here. I love this ground very much. Every time I try to spend a few times here. || A very nice place for relaxing and baby playing. Thanks to Arreiro freguesias. :) || Great park! It has a playground. It also has some benchs and tables with chairs. Great to make a picnic. There is also a kiosk that you can get some drinks and food. At the end of the garden there is a big fountain. It is very pretty. It is also great for families since there is a playground for kids. During the summer there are a bunch of events happening here. || One of the best place in Lisbon. That you come during the day or evening the view is always magic. If you visit this city you must come here. || Beautiful big park. It has some food places around the area. In the park you can chill on the grass, walk up the old fortress like building and also enjoy the majestic huge fountain that lights up in the night. A recommended location to go on a relax date with a bonita Portuguesa 😜 … || A nice place especially during sunny days. I loved the fountain and the atmosphere is chill, not a lot of noisy people. You can have your meal there (if you packed one of course) || A very nice park to spend the evening playing ball, having a picnic, watching the sunset, drinking a beer at the kiosk or just walking around with friends or family. It also has an monumental fountain that lights up after the sunset, with stairs to climb up and get an amazing view of the whole park. || Nice park to hold a celebration. It's opposite the science and technology school in Alameda || A large green area in the center of the city.A good walking space and of course you can walk the dog. || Good place in Lisbon to have fun and a amazing time is the spring || Beautiful lawns clean and green stretch surrounded by concrete jungle! Lovely place to relax and spend some time gazing at the greenery! || Amazing place, centre to lots of important places yet peaceful. || Beautiful place to stay, to take a walk, spend time with friends. Close to the subway amd surrounded by different restaurants and fast food option. || Lovely site to visit and wasn't too busy || Nice fountain, not really much to do if you don't want to just sit on the grass. || Very nice place to relax, have a drink at the Cafe or just sit on the grass and have a picnic and enjoy the scenery. || A beautiful fountain like a waterfall. The water stop falling at 8 pm. || Great fountin, great place, a lovely place to hang out with friends || Green space, great to watch the water fountain with lights || Very nice garden in Alameda || It's a beautiful place to hangout with family and friends. Mainly to get some sun. You can play football with your kids as well. || Beautiful when the sunsets 🌇 … || The garden is beautiful and grand. But it's a little dirty. A great hangout point. || Very beautiful place to rest, do some physical activity || Beautiful park ans great views, excellent to bring your dogs || Beautiful and calm open area, with simple but yet interesting view || Really nice park in the center of Lisbon || Really very nice place specially in the evening

A rare find in Lisbon it seems, a quiet shaded park. It had picnic benches with tables, benches in the shade, grass to lie on, a cafe and is very peaceful.  Having said that it does feel like it needs some attention as much of it is run down and the prevailing smell of urine is not so appealing with your lunch || While the view of Lisbon from here is undeniably beautiful, the park itself has sadly declined. It’s often not clean and no longer feels safe, especially after the evening. The presence of homeless people can be unsettling. It's best to visit during the day for the vista and avoid it after dark. No nearby toilets. || Jardim da Cerca da Graça is a hidden gem with an absolutely fabulous view. It’s pretty simple to get there by bus, but just a heads-up, it does involve walking a fair bit downhill after you get off. Still, totally worth it. || It’s the perfect spot to relax, enjoy a picnic, or simply take in the lovely views over Lisbon. The atmosphere is calm, with plenty of shade, open green spaces, and a small café to grab a drink. A wonderful place to unwind and escape the city’s busy streets for a while. || Having just arrived in Lisbon, we dropped off our bags and got our hike on. We ended up at this great park to relax in, and one of the few that had a playground. We thoroughly enjoyed listening to the dogs playing in the wide-open green space above the playground, one even sounded like a turkey gobbling along. || Very cute little park with stunning views. There is a wee cafe/bar in it with a toilet, a children’s play area and plenty of green space to lie down and relax. Also has amazing views || It’s nice to have a park, but the many many dogs leave behind a lot of dog poop. Even if picked up, this makes your clothes and blanket dirty, and I mean really dirty. Even worse, millions of flies. || Nice little park - an oasis in Graca. There’s a big grassy bit where dogs run around. Be careful of the dog poo though! There’s also a little kiosk for drinks and snacks too || One of the best parks in Lisbon. The view is great, the atmosphere is chill and cool. There’s always a lot of cute dogs running around. You can also get a coffee at the small roundy there :) || A bit abandoned park with full of ugly graffitis. City view is nice but we were really disappointed about no way out anywhere except the entrance (don't believe google maps, there is no direct "green" trail). || Nice park. There is open space for doing some sporty activities. I also enjoyed staircase with street art near the park. One of my favorite spots in Lisbon || The day I passed through this park it was all quiet. Nice view all the same. || This park is some what hidden. Most people come here to sun bath, read a book, smoke weed, you play with there dog. Lots of trees around to stay cool. || I got to this park kind of by accident, but it became one of my favorite spots in Lisboa. Surrounded by buildings and unfolding paths, it's a dreamy spatial experience. The great view to the castle doesn't hurt. Ideal for a picnic, beers with friends, play ball, walk the dog, even a date. || It’s a gorgeous place with so much potential. Lots squatters, make sure to watch your children. Suggest the português government gives them a better home! || This guy and his two dogs have lived in the dog park for 4 months straight with all their nasty equipment spread out like they own the place. What is wrong with this city? || DO NOT BRING CHILDREN HERE. While the space is beautiful, unfortunately it’s now full of homeless people and off leash dogs, including in the children’s play equipment. Avoid. || A nice relaxing park where you can enjoy, rest, read, have a picnic or spend time with you friends. Seems to be a dog friendly place 🐕. … || i did not mean to come here, my friend must have sent the wrong location💔💔 … || The garden was well designed for kids and dogs. But unfortunately it has not been maintained and it's now very dangerous for both kids and dogs. People with drug addiction have taken over the dog and kid park and there is litter, ash, and even syringes left about. Whoever is responsible for maintaining the park, you need to step up. Clean this park up and properly maintain it. Get the addicts to move elsewhere. I can't believe anyone would treat a kids playground this way. It's very sad.

Tucked away in Lisbon, Garden Sister Lúcia is a peaceful green retreat named after one of the Fatima visionaries. With quiet paths, shady trees, and benches perfect for reflection, it offers a calm escape from the city buzz — a hidden gem where nature and serenity gently meet. || It's a sufferable little garden with a coffee stand and a very tiny playground with a couple of swings and a rope climber. Meh. || The rose tree is amazing || This garden, located north of the Church of St. John of God in London Square, is well-maintained with grass and trees, and also features various statues that beautify the generally well-kept space. It also has a terrace where you can have a drink or a bite to eat while enjoying the tranquility of the city. It's a very pleasant spot. || The location is excellent. London Square. The small garden is pleasant. The playground is tiny. There are only 2 amusements. There is no public drinking fountain. A 0.33cl plastic bottle of water costs €1.20 without a cup at the kiosk. Lisbon residents have few options for taking children. || Someone will one day explain to me why this garden is called 'Sister Lucia' for some obscure reason. Is it just because it's near a church? Because the statuary has nothing to do with the said Sister, nothing in the garden evokes the theme, nor have they put up, as far as I can see, a single measly plaque with the name.  A well-kept lawn, four statues, one of which depicts girls with a disability, without hands or with their metal prostheses showing. In short, besides the lawn, the trees are the saving grace, always adding some charm to the place. || Relax. Sometimes, a little more cleaning would be great... || Nice garden, but at night people like to paint and vandalize the playground. || A very pleasant garden next to Praça de Espanha. It has a kiosk and a children's playground. || A rather small garden in the center of Lisbon, without much significance. || The church in front is incredible. || The garden was lovely. || Childhood memories 😍 …

Nice place to hang out. Don’t miss the kiosks where it’s easy to grab a drink and a snack, especially in the summer. The vibes are great. On Sundays, there’s a nice flea market with plenty of things to browse and buy. || Downtown Lisbon, amazing atmosphere, gorgeous luxury brand shopping, such as Gucci, Louis Vuitton, Prada, dolce, and Gabbana, Chanel and the list goes on. || This is a very beautiful avenue in the heart of Lisbon where you can find several shops and cafes around and a long walking path for pedestrians in the middle with lots and lots of green area, flowers, small fountains, statues and a good amount of trees. Built in the latter half of the 19th century, between 1879 and 1886, it was designed in the image of the great French boulevards, arising from the need to expand the city to the north, which led to the disappearance of the old Passeio Público, which existed there. Along its 1100 meters in length and 90 meters in width, we find landscaped flowerbeds, rows of trees, statuary, lakes, kiosks, all surrounded by wide sidewalks decorated with Portuguese artistic pavement. The geometry of the flowerbeds, which are symmetrically arranged along the avenue, framed by leafy tree rows, provides a continuous green space that, despite the artificiality of the surroundings, offers an environment conducive to walking and lingering, constituting a fundamental element in the ecological structure that connects the city center to the Monsanto Forest Park. Avenida da Liberdade traditionally hosts the parade of popular marches, associated with the festivities of the city of Lisbon, on the night of Saint Anthony (from June 12th to 13th). You wouldn't expect a bunch of chickens and roosters chilling in tiny garden right in the city center... and yet, here, you do.  It's a gorgeous spot. Come and enjoy! || Small peaceful park with chickens & ducks 🐔 … || Review of Campo dos Mártires da Pátria – 5 Stars  If you’re looking for a peaceful, green escape in the heart of Lisbon that also offers a quirky and heartwarming surprise, Campo dos Mártires da Pátria is an absolute gem. This urban park blends history, nature, and charm in a way that makes you want to stay for hours. It’s one of those rare places that feels alive—quiet yet full of character.  The park is beautifully maintained with wide paths, benches under tall trees, and a calm atmosphere perfect for walking, reading, or simply breathing in the serenity. It’s surrounded by elegant buildings and steeped in historical importance, making it more than just a green space—it’s a cultural landmark.  But what truly stole my heart and made me give this park a glowing 5-star rating were the chickens and roosters. Yes, you read that right. Real, free-roaming gallinas y gallos live here, wandering through the grass and greeting visitors with cheerful clucks and crowing. It’s such a unique and unexpected detail that adds life and magic to the place. They’re charming, friendly, and seem completely at home—bringing joy to kids and adults alike. I absolutely love them. They’re the soul of the park for me.  If you’re in Lisbon and want a quiet spot full of life, history, and the sweet company of feathered friends, don’t miss Campo dos Mártires da Pátria. It’s a small paradise with a big heart. || Great central park in Lisbon that is quite family friendly. With an outdoor beverage place and loads of friendly animals such ducks and chickens about to keep you and your kids eye's busy.  Campo dos Mártires da Pátria, commonly known by its former name Campo de Santana, is a street in the parish of Arroios in Lisbon.  It occupies the upper part of the trough that separates the two converging valleys in the city center, which correspond to Avenida da Liberdade and Avenida Almirante Reis. It is a space full of history, located in the central area of ​​Lisbon, which served as a slaughterhouse in the 16th century and which has known many uses over the last two centuries, such as a bullring, from 1831 to 1889, the realization of the Feira da  From 1835 to 1882 and still a vegetable market in the mid-19th century. || Cutest park with ducks, chickens, roosters, and a little water feature. We love this park for the kids to run around and climb trees.  Great for a stroll with stroller and kids. Safe and clean. I highly recommend visiting. || Jardim do Torel - Where K-Pop Meets Quiet Romance and the Trees Whisper in Harmony  With Dion humming “APT” like it’s the soundtrack to our lives, we made our way to Jardim do Torel, a firm local favourite and, as it turns out, a filming location for NewJeans’ “Super Shy”. If you’re going to chase K-pop vibes in Lisbon, this is the place to do it - with less glitter, more greenery, and a whole lot of charm.  Nestled in a stately, upmarket parish, the garden feels like a secret lookout - overlooking the city and the river, with just enough elevation to make you feel like you’ve earned the view. On the Saturday morning we visited, the park was alive but gentle with older couples sitting romantically on benches, picnic baskets unpacked with care, and the breeze rustling through the trees like nature’s own ballad.  It’s the kind of place where you can slow down, breathe deeply, and let the city hum below you while you hum along to your own tune. Whether you’re chasing K-pop filming locations or just looking for a quiet moment with someone you like, Jardim do Torel delivers.  Verdict: A peaceful perch above Lisbon, perfect for romantic mornings, picnic afternoons, and soft soundtracks. Highly recommended for view seekers, K-pop fans, and anyone who believes a garden should come with a breeze and a bench. || One of my favorite gardens in Lisboa. It looks to other viewpoints and it is chiller than other spots in city due to the trees up here. Good view, chill vibes, only a few people with their dogs and children; lovely atmosphere overall! || Our final stop was Canil Marques where Tom had found that it served up a wide variety of affordable craft beers. Enroute, Kate designed a route that passed by Jardim do Torel with beautiful views over the city of Lisbon. It is said to be one of the best kept secrets of Lisbon with its broad view of the Avenida da Liberdade and São Roque hill – home to the Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara. Jardim do Torel is also surrounded by a garden and grand 18th- and 19th-century houses which makes it a great spot. The wide flat patio a level down provides the best views in our opinion. Could have been better maintained. Originally part of a private estate in the 19th century, it was opened to the public in the 1960s, providing a tranquil retreat amidst the urban landscape. The garden features shaded pathways, a charming pond with an 18th-century mermaid statue, and a terrace café where you can relax and enjoy the scenery. Accessing the garden via the historic Ascensor do Lavra funicular adds a unique touch to the visit. Unfortunately, the furniture is some of the most uncomfortable and least ergonomic imaginable, from chairs made with iron bars to metal grid backrests placed at a height that hurts anyone trying to lean against them. To make matters worse, some of the furniture is fixed to the floor with screws, not allowing any adjustment according to the height or needs of the users. I won't even comment on the aesthetics of the thing. There is another unpleasant surprise. Orders must be placed by cell phone, but the app created for this works very poorly. When customers try to order at the counter, employees use a tablet and also have difficulty registering orders correctly, which causes confusion, errors and a constant accumulation of people who cannot order what they want. The waiting times (over half an hour for a cake and two coffees) are unbelievable. In addition to all this, the service is the worst. The service is entirely provided by persons whose lack of knowledge of product terminology and designations is evident, making the service slow, confusing, and ineffective. They handle the food with their bare hands, without gloves or tongs; and although there are 8 or 9 people behind the counter, the inefficiency and lack of professionalism of the service is shocking.
