Loved the place so much that went twice in a day. || You have to scan a QR code to order which is so complicated ang annoying. The app for ordering is not clear as well. The food was okay but lukewarm. Relatively small portion for the prices. Staff wad friendly though..

place_name: Garden of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation
reviews_content: Such a lovely garden full of paths and little bridges and loads of seating in the shade and great fun to explore and some statues too and we saw a heron and lots of ducks.  The amphitheatre was a real surprise too || Beautiful garden with long bamboo passage ways, a pond with lots of cute ducks, a small area to eat ice cream or coffee and a large area great for dogs. This is a great place to go on a walk with friends or go on a study session. Everything is full of vegetation and butterflies. Like an actual 'secret garden'. If you like fantasy books this is your place to go because it looks like a place in a fairytale. I cannot recommend this garden enough, especially for outdoor lovers. My description doesn't give this place enough justice. || This place is part of a foundation started by Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil tycoon and art lover. You can really feel his belief that “art is for everyone, and beauty means more when it’s shared.”  Right in the middle of the city, there’s this peaceful garden with tall trees, calm ponds, and quiet paths. I could take my time and enjoy the art without any rush. The way nature and art come together here left such a strong impression. || A very lovely garden, located in the center of the city. It’s super convenient to visit either by metro or different bus networks. Here, it’s more like a combination of different gardens, so there are lots of options to enjoy the sun, green, and overall atmosphere. Totally recommended to visit, including the museum inside. || Gorgeous space for all to enjoy for free - lots of areas to picnic, hang with friends, for kids to run around or bike, easy for strollers to get around. There are also two cafes and an ice cream shop - you can spend a whole day enjoying this beautifully maintained space. There must be a mighty team of gardeners tending to all the plants! What a valuable space for residents and visitors alike in this otherwise very densely developed city. || Gulbenkian always had beautiful gardens, around the museums buildings. Landscaping as Portuguese know how ! Now that the renovation of the modern museum is achieved, there is a new setting of this side of the gardens to discover, mix of Japanese zen design, existing garden style and a monumental, yet perfectly integrated awning. Inspiring place where to wander, with cafe and sometimes outdoor activities at the amphitheatre. Just mind the rush hours and some week-end can be crowded, as this place is since long praized by Portuguese and tourists ! || My primary objective was to visit the museum; however, due to renovations, the collection had been relocated.  I was disappointed by the limited number of items, particularly paintings, compared to my expectations. Nonetheless, the collection was aesthetically pleasing and unique.  The garden, however, was unappealing.  Perhaps I mistakenly visited the incorrect park, as signage was inadequate, requiring extensive navigation to locate the proper entrance. || Big enough to wander around. The noise of the city suddenly stops and everything becomes cooler. Part of it is like a jungle. Lots of people either solo or couples and a lot of families with small children. It is a really special place || Designed in the 1960s by Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles and António Viana Barreto, the garden is a beautifully landscaped urban oasis in the heart of Lisbon. The space features a harmonious blend of lakes, streams, terraced lawns, and forested paths—creating a tranquil environment for relaxation and reflection. The garden connects seamlessly with the main Gulbenkian Foundation building and museum, allowing visitors to experience art, architecture, and nature in one integrated setting. || Quiet, cozy park perfect for rest, private conversation with a friend or relaxation! || Best place to hide when it is very hot. There are lots of nice shaded banks to sit and rest under the trees. || Lovely place to escape the bustle of Lisbon for some hours, still in the middle of the city. Grab a picnic towel, a book and sunscreen and lay down for the afternoon. The grass field in the garden is lovely to get some sun light. Even in winter. || one of the most eye-relaxing places seen during my life. An intellectual and thoughtful place , where you can nurture your mind and abandon  everyday tortuosity. the place I’ve been missing the most since my departure from Lisbon. || A really nice place to wander around, there's lots of corners tucked away if you want to sit by yourself or have a conversation. And they have ducks! || Well-known park in Lisbon where people go to just hang-out, relax, create, work and have a love/get out of here relationship with all the ducks! The museum offers a lot of commodities as well and many times have free entry events :) || So relaxing to walk the grounds of the garden. There are shady as well as sunny areas depending on what you prefer and a cafe for your meals. The ducks and the water areas make it even more attractive. Unfortunately a large part of the grounds are under renovation, so we couldn’t walk there. Still, the air is crisp and the garden is well maintained for visitors. || One of the most gorgeous public gardens I've been to with stunning art, landscaping, plants and wildlife. They are doing extensive renovation in a section of it so it's blocked off (and will be incredible once done) but there's still plenty of areas to wander on paths, sit on benches, grab something at cafe and sit outside and enjoy the birds. I brought my camera and had so much fun capturing images of the Spring babies. Truly a remarkable place for all to enjoy. || A perl in the city of Lisbon. Strongly suggested if you have any minimal appreciation for plants and greenery. They have three great greenhouses with a wide variety of plants from all-over the planet. It also looks like a sustainable place to support with a visit. Entrance tickets are cheap and discounts are available. || Beautiful place to go with time on a sunny day to enjoy yourself and/or friends. Lot's of benches to sit or grass to lay down if you want. Different areas to see and walk to. I really loved even though it was drizzling when I went there. I will come back tho. || My favorite park in Lisbon — full of artwork, exotic plants, winding paths, and little ponds. Despite all that, there’s still plenty of open space to sit or lie down and relax. My 10-year-old son loved it, too.

A definite must visit for Lisbon for the views alone as well as the history. Exceptional views across all of Lisbon. Some amazing historical walled artefacts. A beautifully curated museum in the centre with exceptional items through all the ages. The ostentation of peacocks is a lovely little bonus. Nice Ice Cream stand in the middle of the copse of trees near the more ancient ruins. The church right outside the gates is also a lovely little bonus || After visiting other castles in Malta, I personally found this one underwhelming. The castle is relatively small compared to others. The view is nice but you can get lookout spots similar to this one for free around Lisbon. The museum is only filled with old pots which I'm personally not a fan of. The archeological site was closed for some reason and a large part of the parking was all closed due to renovations or it being dangerous. So we didn't end up experiencing all of the site. I personally found more value from 15 Euros in other sites.  Another thing I would have preferred to see is written text throughout the castle. I know they went for a more traditional look and tried to provide an audio on your phone to listen to but this restrains you to follow the audios pace which was too slow for me. I like to go on my own pace and skip what I would like to skip.  I will say if you are a history freak it is a nice historic site, but for me personally it was sub-par.  I will say that the peacocks were very nice here but also you can find them free throughout lisban || This was on our must see list while we were in Lisbon as my friend and I both love touring castles. It wasn’t quite what we were expecting as it was very open and had a lot of courtyards and such but the view from the walls was beautiful. They also had peacocks everywhere which was really cool to see. The museum has a lot of ancient pottery and we learned the history of the tiles we’d been seeing everywhere so we enjoyed that. It does take quite a climb to get there but we were not disappointed! || After visiting the Lisbon cathedral, we walked up to the arch entrance of the castle - it’s walkable but be wary of a steep trek from the cathedral. We were able to use our Lisboa Card for free entry, which was a great bonus. The castle grounds offer incredible views across the city and plenty of historic areas to explore. There are loads of great photo opportunities, and the grounds are home to around two dozen peacocks and peahens. I’ve never seen so many in one place before, and they really add to the atmosphere.  The small museum inside is interesting and gives some insight into the history of the castle, including who built it, what it was used for, and a look at some of the pottery and tiles found on site. It’s also well air-conditioned, which makes it a nice break from the heat outside.  Be warned that the toilets are pretty unpleasant and located down some narrow, slightly sketchy stairs. The main castle area itself is mostly empty, with only the walls open to walk along. The views are fantastic from up there, but it’s definitely not ideal if you’re afraid of heights. The walkways are narrow and can get crowded, and there’s only a railing to hold on to.  We left just before sunset, and as we did, the queue to get in had grown a lot. Leaving early worked out well, as we were able to catch the bus back to the Rua with no hassle || I don’t usually like visiting castles and historic spots, but this castle was breathtaking. I highly recommend visiting it. My teenage boys also liked it. We enjoyed the kastana outside the castle. We took the hop on hop off green line to reach there which stopped exactly opposite to the castle. The area around was beautiful. Beautiful old town 💕 || Castelo de São Jorge is a stunning medieval fortress situated on one of Lisbon’s highest hills, providing visitors with magnificent panoramic views of the city, including the Alfama district, the Baixa area, the Tagus River, and the iconic 25 de Abril Bridge.  The castle itself has a rich history, originally serving as a Moorish citadel before becoming a royal palace and later a military stronghold.  Visitors can explore vast ramparts, eleven towers, archaeological sites, and remnants of the former royal palace, all set within beautiful gardens that are home to roaming peacocks, adding a unique and charming touch to the experience.  The castle's grounds feel like a living museum where one can marvel at medieval defensive architecture, walk along ancient walls, and enjoy peaceful spaces shaded by olive trees and dotted with historical artifacts.  Surrounding the castle, the neighborhood of Alfama offers a vibrant yet authentic atmosphere with narrow, winding streets, traditional tiled houses, cozy cafes, and small shops steeped in local culture.  The area is known for its lively yet intimate vibe, enriched by the sounds of Fado music and the daily rhythms of local residents.  Travelers often find themselves enchanted by the blend of history, culture, and scenic beauty, making the approach to the castle a meaningful journey in itself.  The castle’s elevated position allows for stunning sunrise and sunset views across Lisbon, creating memorable photo opportunities and moments of reflection against the backdrop of terracotta rooftops and the sparkling river below.  Visitors are recommended to arrive early to avoid crowds, as the castle tour, including its museum and archaeological areas, can take one to two hours. The pathway includes some steep climbs, but the well-preserved structures and the sweeping city vistas make the effort worthwhile.  There are also small cafes within the castle grounds where visitors can pause and enjoy refreshments while taking in the scenic surroundings.  Overall, Castelo de São Jorge offers a rich, immersive experience of historical, cultural, and natural heritage, making it a must-visit landmark for anyone exploring Lisbon’s fascinating past and vibrant present.  The castle’s majesty, along with the lively charm of its surroundings, creates an unforgettable visit that reflects both the resilience and spirit of Lisbon. || What an awesome experience this was!  Was there on a Tuesday afternoon and the crowds were light.  Very easy to walk around and explore.  (Although be warmed the steps are pretty steep and some have no handrails....careful!  Sights were amazing and there is a QR Code.at.the entrance that gives you a self guided audio your with anlot of history.  Awesome place and highly recommended! || Castelo de São Jorge in Lisbon is worth a visit for the views alone. Sitting on a hill in the Alfama district, it gives you a clear line of sight across the city and the Tagus River. There is something about seeing the red rooftops stretch out below that makes it easy to understand why Lisbon feels so special.  The castle itself is interesting, even if it is not the most polished attraction. Walking along the ramparts and towers, you can sense the layers of history that have shaped this place. Roman, Moorish, and medieval influences are all visible in the walls and fortifications. The layout is straightforward, but exploring the nooks and stairs gives a sense of how people lived and defended the city centuries ago.  One of the unexpected highlights is the peacocks. They wander freely across the grounds and gardens, adding a bit of life and color to the stone and brick. It is a small detail, but it makes the visit feel a little more playful.  If you are in Lisbon, give yourself an hour or two to explore. Wear comfortable shoes because the paths are cobbled, and take your time to enjoy the history, the views, and the peacocks. Castelo de São Jorge is real, atmospheric, and memorable. || Make sure to sign up for the guided tour which can be done at the ticket office, its free and its the only way to visit the archeological ruins. Our guide was knowledgeable and entertaining. The view from the top is stunning! The history of the area is beyond interesting. Highly recommend if visiting Lisbons historical center || This castle is situated on one of the highest hills and offers stunning panoramic view of lisbon. You can walk over the castle and towers which was fun. The place is overall well maintained and worth a visit. The route to get to the castle is walkable but be aware of the steep path. We visited this place during sunset and it was absolutely lovely and highly recommend visiting around sunset time. No advance booking required and we got the ticket upon arrival. || This 11th-century castle offers a journey into the past, with a great archaeological museum and a wonderful walk around the grounds. It has the best panoramic view of Lisbon from above! You must go! || Amazing view, beautiful ruins, well kept, lots of nature, spacious areas. Unfortunately, this is not all. Multiple areas, view points, terraces were closed off, 2 of the 3 toilets didn't work and it looked and smelled disgusting. For 15 euros I'd hope for better but it's whatever.. However, what's not whatever is the behaviour of the staff. At 5:40 they were aggressively shouting at us that the place is closed, get out. They waved in front of our photos. When we said that the place is not in fact closed and we want to enjoy these 15-20 minutes one of them even more aggressively shouted that "you don't argue with me about this". We were following the signs and wanted to go out through the archeological site (where the official exit was according to the signs) as that was in the end but when we got there they sent us back to the entrance (where it said entrance only). They didn't even tell us why we couldn't. The arrogance and ignorance was mind-blowing. We just wanted to enjoy that beautiful historic sight and the view until we could. || It was a good walk from our hotel. Uphill both ways lol The views from the walls provide excellent photo ops. I recommend a jacket during winter as the wind does pick up and chill you right through at times. || Best views of the city. Museum display was excellent although English descriptions require a darker font yo mage them more easily readable. The lighting was frustratingly dim on many of the exhibits, which minimised the enjoyment. Bonus points for the guy at the ticket office who requested proof of age so I could get my Senior discount. Made my day. || Wonderful castle, very well preserved. It's quite big, so there is a lot to explore and the best, the view over the city of Lisbon is just magnificent. Especially the old town, where you can see the architecture. There is a community of peacocks living in the castle, they are very adorable and not afraid of the tourist. It's really worth the visit, to get a panoramic view of the city. Highly recommended. || Incredible views. Key tip, go later in the afternoon so you can be there for sunset, an incredible vantage point and not nearly as busy as some of the other sunset viewing spots around Lisbon.  The actual castle is really cool and the audio guide was done very well too. || A calm and charming place right in the heart of the city. The atmosphere is very peaceful, and the presence of a good-quality restaurant makes the experience even more enjoyable. The architecture is a beautiful mix of different styles, with strong Andalusian influences that give the space a unique character. What makes this place special is that if it’s not recommended to you in advance, you might easily walk past it without noticing. But once you step inside, you realize it’s a hidden gem well worth stopping for and exploring. || Great views of Lisbon! Very neat to explore the castle itself and get Greta pictures across the entire castle.  Overall, very good price for the value you receive! || Very beautiful castle and lots of places to walk around and take photos. They also have peacocks wandering around which is very pretty. Ample places to sit and I saw two washroom locations.  Incredible views of the city. Also has a small museum to look at (~3 rooms)  Audio tours are available to listen to.  In my opinion, well worth the visit! || We were visiting in lower season and I don't believe there were any cruise rshios in the day we went so pre purchased tickets were unnecessary. However in other times of year they may be. There is an audio tour you can do with this site and the views are truly spectacular. Peacocks were everywhere which was unexpected! There is a lot of uneven ground and narrow paths so it would be tricky to do a lot of this if you have mobility issues

We imagine you are reading this review because of the reviews that have gone before it. And friends, we heartily condone the gusto with which this specimen of planthood has been celebrated.  Is it worth ‘the hype?’ Is it a huge pot plant, escaped from its caging plastic vessel, and now threatening the foundations of the building? Yes. Is it historic? In as much as any single artefact can be deemed a portal to another time, yes. And it is certainly a plant situated in Lisbon. Therefore, its description is true.  We thoroughly recommend this site to anyone for whom the grandeur of the quotidian inspires a good humoured, slightly juvenile giggle. For the more poetic, perhaps Whitman would have praised ‘the play of light and shade on the [plant] as the supple boughs wag.’ Long live the Historic Giant Plant of Lisbon. || The sun glitters through its leaves like a jewel facing the sky. Its roots as deep as Lisboa itself. Tall. Proud. Free.  The Cafe next to it is pretty great too. || This plant, this giant plant, it spoke to me and resonated with me in ways I've never known possible. I grew up with very weak bones and many doctors told me I would not make it to my teenage years and yet I stood strong, I did not, no I could not let that stop me, the fear and dread I felt hearing those words only pushed me forward, pushed me to do more and be more, just like this historic plant. From just a seed, growing out of it's pot and climbing and climbing to heights never imagined by it, all the other trees and vegetation telling it to give up, that is just a plant, that it doesn't need to do any more than it can, and yet it stood strong, and it stood proud, past everything it should be and be what it wanted to be. Just like me. I looked at this giant plant and saw myself, and while others may just see a plant, a fairly big plant, I see a Historic plant, for all my history is laid out in its leaves. Thank you Historic Giant Plant of Lisbon. || This tree is an absolute legend. Perfect shade, great vibes, and zero attitude. The branches are like open arms, the leaves whisper secrets, and I swear it’s the best place to sit and just exist. Highly recommend if you like oxygen. || Incredible plant. The most historic, most giant plant in Lisbon. Probably all Portugal? Possibly the world? Who am I to say? I was humbled before the plant. I was inspired by the way its roots broke the shackles of the plastic pot. The World Tree is not an ash, it is this Historic Giant Plant. Its roots stretch from the primordial wells in the heart of the earth, its branches reach to the heavens themselves, carrying the knowledge and movement of the worlds along the stretches of its growth. I collapsed in ecstasies and am forever changed. || We flew a gruelling 7 hours to see this magnificent tree in Lisbon and it was worth the pain caused by our journey as the sight of it washed away all negativity in our bodies. I could feel it calling to me while we ventured over the treacherous Atlantic Ocean where we experienced turbulence of a near death experience - it helped ease my motion sickness; it was worth the leg cramps caused by Lisbon’s hilly terrain - it said to me “you’re almost there. Keep going.”; it was even worth draining my bank account - i could tell that the wisdom it bestowed on me was more valuable than monetary assets. Once we beheld this tree, we were only left with bliss and an entirely new perspective on the world || Picture this: an ice cold white sangria in one hand. A steaming empanada in the other. And, perhaps even more deliciously, a crystalline tear in your eye as you gaze upon what might be the most dramatic tree on the Iberian peninsula. Is it worth the hype? Every penny, every minute, friend. || Quotes from the crowd: “I’m horny for this tree”, “You can grow wherever you’re planted”, “It’s unlimited”, “Where is the tasty smell?” || The miniscule pot betrays this plant's true nature. Roots burrow deep into the earth, carrying branches that touch the heavens. A tree as old as time itself. In it's gentle presence, past and future meet to become one. Yggdrasil, in the flesh. And the nearby empañada store sells nice smoothies, too. || Firstly, it must be said that this plant isn't just simply giant, it is historic, too. The tree's presence is huge, indomitable, and awe-inspiring, but also reassuring, calming and altogether humbling. Before I made a pilgrimage to the tree, I felt hollow, broken, incomplete, as though my life was without purpose, and I was destined to forever go around in circles. The moment I sighted the tree, I was filled with such vibrant joy, the likes of which I can never equate to, but must be similar to a child on Christmas finding every present they ever wished for under the tree. However, the present this tree gives you is not physical, no, it is a mental, spiritual and psychological aura you shall carry for the rest of your life, that makes you feel you may achieve any goal you set your heart on, in life, love, or labour. It imbues you with the power of self confidence, that you may be whomever you wish to be, and that the tree will guide you to your ultimate destiny, overcoming any obstacle through its sheer power. When I placed my hand on its trunk, and felt its supple, enormous green leaves, I was immediately moved to tears. As I sank to my knees and openly cried in the street, for lack of being able to properly articulate the feeling of glory I was basking in, my body started to glow and hover above the path, as this incredible, omniscient, beautiful tree granted me eternal life and the power of flight, amongst other things. Visit the tree. Let it change your life. || I would like to preface this review with a little quote from Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.  “We must speak with all the humility that is appropriate to our limited vision, but we must speak”  It is with these words in mind that I write this, as I feel so impelled to convey the sheer majesty and fortitude with which this plant stands, and to urge other earthly beings to undertake the same journey. As my friends and I waited for our empanadas, we felt the grandeur emanating in an almost holy energy stream coming from what we learned to be a giant plant nearby. With the greatest humility, we bowed to the plant, and, though I bear no tangible evidence, I do believe the plant forgave us for our past wrongdoings, and imbued in us the greatest sentiments of palpable gratitude and virtue.  In a way, it helped us “turn over a new leaf”.  We strongly encourage any plant-curious brothers and sisters among us to do the same. Thank you Lisbon and plant. || When me and my partner started getting closer and closer to the street where this plant lives, I could start feeling my heart beating faster… and when my eyes finally laid on the mesmerizing beauty of it, my life completely changed. Such an amazing gem in the most random street of Lisbon. I would definitely recommend you all to go visit this beautiful plant || Wow. We came to Lisbon as three cousins looking to reconnect, and honestly we’re leaving with so much more. Mind bending, breathtaking, a learning experience? This tree, rooted firmly into the street next to the aptly named restaurant “Food” was so much more than it appears on the Google link in real life. The time we spent here was special like the first day of spring, like the sun warming your face after a long winter. It felt like being genuinely free for the first time. Not even my widest lens could capture the majesty of this tree (and we were VERY wide). If you’re in Lisbon, see this tree, call your mum, tell your crush you love them. Live every second to the fullest. Thankyou tree. F. || August 8, 2023 14:34. This was the date that changed my life. When I googled things to do in Lisbon there were the typical tourist attractions that you can see anywhere- An old cathedral, a historic fortress on a hill, a marketplace that sells the same 15 things as every other tourist market. Then I saw it. The Historic Giant Plant. What plant species could it be? Why is it Historic? Why is it Giant? There were too many questions and not enough answers, I needed to see it for myself. The pilgrimage from my hostel to the plant was around 20,000 steps but it was all worth it when I laid eyes on the majestic fauna. For some odd reason there were no crowds of people surrounding the plant. Instead it was located in a quaint little area between 2 quiet restaurants; a beautiful area for a plant to grow strong without disturbance. When I approached the plant I noticed some of the branches have been trimmed which may indicate it was growing too powerful which wasn’t hard to imagine. I’m not sure who takes care of the plant but it looked well maintained and was well attached to the surrounding wall and tiny pot. Looking at pictures doesn’t do it justice you need to see the plant in person to get a grasp of the height and girth of this majestic tree. I scanned the leaves with an app that can identify plants however the app came back with nothing. Perhaps this is an undiscovered species. Seeing the Giant plant grow from the base of such a tiny pot seems to defy the laws of nature and physics. From what I saw my best guess for how this plant has grown so large out of such a small pot is due to its roots connecting to the electrical box attached to the building. I asked a local who worked at the shop next to the plant and he said it was magic. The only way to conclude this for yourself is to make the journey and form your own opinion in person. If you don’t see anything else in Lisbon see the Giant Historic Plant. || Single-minded egoists flock to the Plant to enjoy its plentiful gifts. Though the wise man gazes upon said Plant and realizes: the gift of Knowledge, the apple of Life is a double-edged sword.  Be wary of the mesmerizing waving of leaves and wood, as they are hunting you. With no predators left they hide among the trees. Beautiful place to learn, to know, to sacrifice oneself.  Exceptionally beautiful mimic of an unusually large plant, but its sheer size clearly reveals that at its core, something sinister and wicked awaits.  Praise the Plant and its wickedness, praise the Lord for he taketh as he giveth, and praise Nature for bearing fruit and smiting the unholy. || The tree is more than a landmark; it's a pilgrimage site.  Visiting the legendary tree in Lisbon was an experience like no other. We traveled all the way from the Netherlands, fueled by the tales of its grandeur, and it did not disappoint.  We spent the entire day in eager anticipation, and when we finally arrived, it was as if time stood still. The rustling leaves whispered ancient secrets, and the shade it cast provided a sanctuary for our souls. The experience was intense and emotionally stirring, leaving an indelible mark on our hearts. || As I meandered through the mountainous streets of Lisboa, I could hear whispers of the greatness of this plant. A spirit of the plant was calling me, beckoning me to my saviour. The historic giant plant was truly magnificent, a 6 star attraction. Anybody who has never seen the plant should be disappointed, as the one who doesn't see the plant doesn't live -Sun Zu, the art of war. When my gaze met the plant, I was petrified, frozen solid... It took control of my soul. Since I saw it yesterday, my life has changed for the better. Highly reccomended || Not only is this plant historic but also giant! We were really thrown off of our feet by the first glimpse of this marvel of nature. Sadly the locals have lost the appeal for something serene of this calibre. I would definitely recommend this highlight to anyone visiting Portugal for work or vacation. Just be prepared before you lay your eyes on this magnanimous beauty, the place has something divine to it and you suddenly feel small and meaningless in front of the historic and giant nature of the plant. || Behold the Sidewalk Sentinel, a hidden gem of urban charm! This towering tree defies the cityscape, its roots weaving through pavement and its branches offering shade to passersby. A quiet triumph of nature amidst the bustle—unassuming, yet unforgettable. || I first heard the giant plant calling to me the night of my wedding. I heard it in the soft rustling of the leaves of the trees of the venue "Come to me child" it whispered. Naturally I was very confused until that night I dreamt of its leafy visage and it imparted this message onto me. Come to the third level of the seventh hill of Lisbon, then I will share with you the wisdom needed for eternal love. My newly wed wife and I booked the first flight out the next day. We took the first of 23,743 steps from the Aeroporto when Treesus appeared again "Find the nearest cord of wood and profus thine faith for all to see". I couldn't find a cord, but I did find a nice stick. My wife and I passed the stick back and forth performing self flagellation all the way, which we learned was a local custom. It was a long walk, but we finally made it to the tree from my visions. It was even more beautiful in person, and it spoke to us in many tongues, including Fig, Oak, and Willow (if you don't speak those I'm sure they know more). We offered the blood from our backs to the tree and it offered us its final wisdom "Love can be found in many shapes and sizes, many religions and creeds, but at the core of it all is humor, self sacrifice, and long walks to beautiful trees" || Visiting the Historic Giant Plant was an unparalleled marvel that left me utterly speechless! Oh, the sheer grandeur and awe-inspiring beauty of this botanical wonder were unlike anything I had ever witnessed before. But the most astonishing and incredible aspect was the revelation that this magnificent spectacle was nothing more than a normal, ordinary and completely common green plant! A plant with such historic significance, yet so humble in appearance! It was a testament to the extraordinary magic of nature, where simplicity and elegance merge to create a masterpiece beyond imagination. As I stood in its majestic presence, I couldn't help but be in complete awe of this seemingly ordinary plant that had stood the test of time and witnessed the passage of history. The Historic Giant Plant will forever be etched in my memory as a true marvel of nature's artistry, a living testament to the captivating surprises that await us in the world of flora and fauna. 5/5 - would plant my eyes on this behemoth of a wonder again. || As you approach the Historic Giant plant, you can feel the air crackle with energy, it's ancient and mystical magnificence washing over you. I'm not a man of faith but as the tree realigned my being, there was a sense of peace, of oneness with the world, insecurity and doubt replaced with a calm and life affirming knowledge that everything will be what it should be. Absorbing it's lesson's to not be contained and to break the mold as you watch it burst majestically from its tiny pot, you'll leave a better human than you were before. ABSOLUTE must visit. || This plant is THE most historic and culturally significant attraction in all of Europe. My 2 friends and I travelled all the way from Australia to see its majestic beauty. When my hand grazed its rough bark, I instantly felt one with the universe. Everyone in Lisbon makes a pilgrimage to the plant weekly to admire its beauty. Please consider supporting the plant as it has resorted to selling 2 for 1 mojoto advertising space to make ends meet. || Wow! None of Europe’s other endangered Historic Giant Plants come anywhere close.  It’s open 24 hrs and the entry price is free - which is crazy. The aroma, the color, the leafy elegance and the spiritual vigor of this mighty vegetation will guarantee that it is a place you’ll be sure to remember in your dreams and on your deathbed. An ideal spot for a marriage proposal, bris, christening, or graduation. Well done Lisbon, I can die a happy man. || I thought it was a joke, I really did. Wow. 🤯 this Bar is AN EXPERIENCE! It felt like walking into an escape room themed around the 1920s–1930s (the kind that completely pulls you into its story and atmosphere).The effort put into the design and decoration is unmatched! I wanted a Sex on the Beach, but they didn’t have the ingredients, so I asked to be surprised with something similar and it turned out quite yummy.  Music is always important for me when choosing places, and when we were there, they were playing relaxing sort of jazz, super chill and perfectly fitting for the luxurious, slightly historical vibe.  The cocktails were around €13 each, if I’m not mistaken (not cheap, but not too expensive either). Really recommended if this is the vibe you’re looking for it nails it perfectly! || Atmosphere: 8.5/10 The Royal Vessel Bar blends a cozy restaurant-style atmosphere with subtle ship and pirate-inspired design touches. I’ll definitely be coming back, this place is perfect both for special occasions and a chill night out with friends. || The best non-alcoholic cocktails in Lisbon. I loved the atmosphere of the bar and I am definitely going to return! || We had such a great time at the bar, huge thanks to Zhenya from Uzbekistan! He made the evening unforgettable. Every cocktail he suggested was perfect for each of us, like he instantly knew what everyone would love. We ended up chatting in Portuguese, English, Russian, and Ukrainian, it was such a fun mix and the vibe was amazing.  Zhenya even made me a special cocktail, not from the menu, just based on my preferences, and it turned out incredible. 🍸 Definitely one of the bars, we'll come back to and recommend to our friends! || Super sad I discovered it one day before leaving… it is a must! Not only are the cocktails genuinely amazing, but the staff were absolute stars. There was a girl who was clearly very drunk and being bothered by a creepy guy who wouldn’t leave her alone. They handled everything with real care and escalated it to the authorities in exactly the right way. I’d gone over to check on her too, and the staff even thanked me and gave me a drink for helping. Honestly, such a brilliant bar on every front — fantastic drinks, great atmosphere, and a team who genuinely look out for their guests. Couldn’t recommend it more. Five stars. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ || Great cocktail card and lovely staff, the best atmosphere. Besides ordering things from the menu, you can also ask to make a custom cocktail to your liking. One of my favorite places in Lisbon.

This is an amazing place to check out if you are into the ruins and history of the sacred sites. Such a cool place. Plus you can buy a ticket that is good for 4 museums in the group. If you are checking out the free ruins across street ensure you pay the fee to check out the museum as it is worth it. || Museu de Lisboa - Teatro Romano: Where Romans Once Roared and Bluegrass Now Echoes  There’s something magical about watching live music in a Roman theatre, especially when it’s tucked into the winding streets of São Mamede and surrounded by the bones of Felicitas Iulia Olisipo, Lisbon’s ancient Roman self.  We arrived on a Thursday evening, just in time for the monthly performance held every last Thursday at 18H00 and were lucky enough to catch Stonebones and Bad Spaghetti, Portugal’s only bluegrass band. Yes, bluegrass. In a Roman ruin. And it worked.  The excavation site itself is awe-inspiring. You sit among the stones, imagining togas and sandals, while banjos and fiddles fill the air. The crowd was a mix of locals and curious wanderers, all drawn in by the music and the magic of the setting. After the show, we joined the happy throng for a glass of wine overlooking the river, because of course there’s wine. It’s Lisbon.  Then we wandered into the museum, where we met the charming Carlota, a bubbly art historian with a passion for living history and history in the making. She walked us through the scale of the original theatre, which could seat 4,000 patrons in the 1st century AD a fact made even more impressive when you see how modest the current excavation is.  The pottery displays are beautifully curated, and the guides know how to spin a story, turning shards and stones into tales of empire, entertainment, and everyday life.  Verdict: The Museu de Lisboa - Teatro Romano is a hidden gem where ancient history meets modern creativity, and where you can sip wine, hear bluegrass, and learn about Roman engineering all in one evening. Highly recommended for history buffs, music lovers, and anyone who enjoys a good story told in stone. || Outstanding indoor and outdoor spaces showing archeological remains, restoration, artifacts and renderings of what the Roman theater looked like. Excellent place to stop, scenic views and learn history || An absolute must see in Lisboa especially more if you happen to be lucky enough to attend a concert there. || We recently visited the Roman Theatre remains in Lisbon and were pleasantly surprised by how well done the site is. It’s great to see such cultural heritage being celebrated like this.  We do hope there’s still more to be discovered and that future excavations might reveal even more of the site’s past. For now, though, it’s well worth a visit if you’re in Lisbon and interested in its layered history. || I love Ancient Rome. And this was a great little spot to visit. The museum itself does an excellent job presenting the archaeological finds (columns, pottery, everyday objects) and explaining the theatre's structure, history, and rediscovery through engaging displays. place_name: José Gomes Ferreira Park / Mata de Alvalade
reviews_content: Parque José Gomes Ferreira, also known as Mata de Alvalade, is a spacious and peaceful green area in Lisbon. The park feels more like a natural forest than a traditional city park, with wide paths, plenty of trees, and a calm atmosphere that makes it ideal for walking, running, or simply enjoying some quiet time.  It’s not as manicured or structured as other parks in Lisbon, but that’s exactly what gives it its charm. A great spot if you’re looking for a more natural, less crowded outdoor space within the city. || Such a beautiful park turned into a dump. I’m not talking cigarette bums or beer cans. There are all kinds of trash here, especially in the sourthern part of the park, from car tyres to broken glass to used condoms. Disgusting!!! Unsafe for children and dogs || Small but very pleasant park, upper part unfortunately a bit trashy, but you can find a nice spots to sit and walk. There is a small bar on the lower part where you can grab a coffee and some small snacks. Very nice trees and call place, you can see the cork trees there 😻 there is also small miradour and you can see outskirts of Lisbon. Very nice area to walk. || You can visit here just to relax for a moment , while you can sip coffee your kids can play in a playground which is so close to you. It's not a crowded area, i can advise vegetarian toast in that coffee, The guys are helpful, you can rest under long trees || Beautiful park to go and feel nature in the heart of Lisbon. As soon as you enter, you can connect with the environment. Nice place for running, walking, yoga and meditation 🧘🏻‍♀️ … || Although it's a park next to a busy road , once you enter you stop hearing the noise and focus on nature . Beautiful views over Lisbon during sunset . You have picnic areas, a playground and a little cafe. You can also find loads of trails for cycling and exercise. Woman can walk, jog or exercise freely during the day but I don't recommend it at night. If you're planning to walk at night bring a lantern because the park doesn't have any light. Payed parking area. Open 24h everyday. || Beautiful park, you feel like you're in contact with nature even though you're really close to the city centre. Not all places are accessible with baby strollers, but most are. The loud sound of landing airplanes is a downside. || The park is beautiful, but I wouldn't recommend for women to go alone (it was pretty empty and there were only a few very weird guys there). || A quiet place in a bustling city, a natural oxygen bar, peaceful and comfortable. || Amazing park with a kiosk to chill, have a beer or bring your friends and family for a picnic || Nice park. Sport facilities and a nice caffe. Wild trees and nice walking pathways. || A Park that is near an airport and not far from central downtown that is still peaceful, diverse and relaxing || Nice and safe to exercise, walk the dog or take a coffee or beer. || There is no barbecue zone anymore || Could use some updates and it has potential for so much more || It has everything you need to a nice day on the park || Love this park in the city || It should have more lights, you can't see anything at night || Spectacular place to practice sports and be in contact with nature || Very beautiful park in Lisbon. || Huge park away from the hustle-bustle of the city center. || Need more jumps on the trails haha || It's just trees and grass. || A very acceptable urban park for sports, especially in the morning or late afternoon, or simply for spending a few pleasant hours with family and friends. Many of the access paths/paths are in need of maintenance, as are some of the exercise equipment. The trash is not collected as quickly as desired (daily). On weekends there is a large influx of people, especially cyclists, who frequently ride on or off the trails without any respect for pedestrians. Most dog owners are also a problem because they walk their dogs without a leash, muzzle, or because they don't pick up their excrement. More and more scooters are being abandoned in the park. || I visited during a training session, but I loved the space; you don't see any litter on the ground… lots of shade! Good biodiversity on the park's edges… || Nice park with a good picnic area, playground, and some exercise equipment. However, it is quite degraded by time and needs urgent maintenance. || A pleasant spot for a family picnic, a simple walk, or spending time with children in the park. There's a snack bar next to the playground, and for the more athletic, a well-maintained fitness trail. || Very pleasant green space. Several green areas to suit all tastes. Picnic tables. Playground. Viewpoint. Many trees and shady areas. It has a sports circuit. Pedestrian and bicycle paths. Next to the playground there is a small café/bar. || A lovely, calm green space for walking or exercising. Great for children and pets to play in. || Huge space with plenty of tables for socializing. Lots of greenery and peaceful. || A quiet park (Monday noon), where you can go in a few minutes from the airport while waiting for your flight :-) Oh, and look up, you can see green parrots in the crowns, probably an invasive species of Monk Parrots. || José Gomes Ferreira Park, also known as Mata de Alvalade, is a green oasis located in Lisbon, Portugal. This park is a tranquil refuge from the hustle and bustle of the city, offering a variety of outdoor activities for all ages.  The park boasts a large green area with hiking and cycling trails, picnic areas, a children's playground, sports courts, and a picturesque lake. In addition, there are many benches and rest areas for those who wish to relax and appreciate nature.  The park's flora and fauna are diverse, with many species of native birds, plants, and trees. This makes the park a popular spot for birdwatching and nature photography.  The park staff are helpful and friendly, keeping the environment clean and safe for all visitors. Entry is free, and the park is easily accessible by public transport or car.  Overall, José Gomes Ferreira Park / Mata de Alvalade is a popular destination for those who wish to enjoy nature and disconnect from Lisbon's busy urban life. Highly recommended for a relaxing day outdoors. || The park itself and the species that compose it make it a good park without grass or other species that require a lot of water. However, the more natural aspect of the park leads people to let their animals roam without a leash, bothering other users and without worrying about picking up their droppings. It would also be important to have supporting sanitary facilities so that people don't have to resort to the only existing ones belonging to the café located inside the park. || I loved it! Peaceful environment in nature and service from two super, incredibly friendly young people.

Its construction began in 1597-98. In 1601 it was given to the Augustinian hermits. Between 1625 and 1635 a new temple was built to replace the previous one. In the 18th century, the church underwent further renovations, completed in 1754, which were severely damaged by the earthquake the following year, and subsequently rebuilt with the support of the Marquis of Marialva. In the 20th century it became a parish church. The cult of Our Lady of Penha de França originated from a legend about a lizard that spread throughout Brazil and the East through Portuguese navigators. Notable features of the church include the atrium, staircase, octagonal interior, marble cladding in various colors, the altarpiece, images, and the sacristy with its 18th-century tilework. reviews_content: A stunning church, from the outside it looks quite simple, but inside it’s full of gold, marble, and detailed artwork. Each chapel has unique decorations worth seeing. It’s calm and not too crowded, perfect for a quiet visit. Definitely worth stopping by. || Our private tour guide brought us here after learning that I enjoy visiting churches when we travel. He compared it to the Sistine Chapel, which seemed like a stretch—especially given how unassuming the exterior is. Honestly, it’s probably not a church I would have bothered climbing the steps to visit on my own.  Inside, however, it was a different story entirely. The painted ceiling and the opulence of the altar and artwork throughout were the most impressive of any church I visited in Portugal. The craftsmanship is extraordinary.  What made it truly special, though, was the feeling inside. There was a deep sense of goodness and calming peace that I rarely experience in many of the churches I visit. Feeling that kind of holiness is uncommon for me, which made this visit especially meaningful.  Saint Roque, the church’s namesake, is the patron saint against the plague. He devoted his life to caring for plague victims before ultimately contracting the disease himself—adding another layer of depth and reverence to this remarkable place. || One of my favorite churches while living in Lisbon. The Church of Saint Roch is incredibly well-preserved, and the gold detailing from top to bottom, especially across each of the 14 Stations of the Cross, is just breathtaking. It’s truly an amazing experience.  I 100% recommend visiting the museum too. It’s around €8, and they offer a student discount, no proof needed if you look young enough (like me!). Walking through it, you can really imagine how people back then must have felt in awe. The gold, the grandeur, it all ties in with Portugal’s historic campaigns abroad. It just makes sense.  Pro tip: Be respectful and keep quiet while inside. It’s a sacred and peaceful space. || From the outside, the Church of Saint Roch looks quite plain, but once I stepped inside I was amazed. The chapels are beautifully decorated, and the Chapel of St. John the Baptist really stood out for me with its richness and detail. It felt peaceful to walk around and just take it all in. || The Church of Saint Roch (Igreja de São Roque) is one of the most beautiful and decorative churches ever seen. Its humble exterior hides a richly adorned Baroque interior, featuring magnificent chapels with gilded woodcarving, polychrome marbles, and extraordinary mosaics.  The lavish Chapel of St. John the Baptist, made from precious materials, is a masterpiece of European art. This church reflects immense faith, vision, and artistic labor, making it a true gem of Lisbon’s heritage and one of the most impressive religious buildings in Portugal. || The Igreja de São Roque is special because of its stark exterior that contrasts with an incredibly ornate and lavishly decorated interior, housing what is considered one of Europe's most expensive chapels, the Chapel of St. John the Baptist. This chapel was built in Rome with precious materials like gold, marbles, and mosaics, then shipped and reassembled in Lisbon, showcasing impressive Italian Baroque art. || Very nice church, not as know as others in the city but totally worth it. This church is different from most in Lisbon. In 1959, a large fire destroyed the roof and many wooden parts. The heat was so strong that the stone columns cracked and turned black. You can still see the damage today. The church was not fully restored on purpose. The scars were left as a reminder of what happened, instead of being hidden. It is simple, quiet, and very powerful — a place that shows history exactly as it is. || We were walking around Lisbon exploring all the sights for several days while we were waiting to join our cruise. We passed by this church and went inside to explore.  It was very old and very beautiful.  So ornate especially behind the alter. Please note that the base 13th century church has been rebuilt several times over the centuries due to fires and earthquakes. A very peaceful place in the middle of a busy city. || Old church with special legacy but forsaken by caring elites some.time.ago and badly needs renovating - about to start. Very unique style circle within circle. Very spiritual I felt. Had a volunteer lady assisting who was devout and delightful humour. A visit for heartfelt comforting of the soul. || Igreja de São Domingos – Lisbon. - Is a symbol of resilience, uniquely displaying the "scars" of the 1959 fire and earlier earthquakes, which gives its restored interior a haunting and powerful atmosphere. Despite multiple devastating events, it has been repeatedly rebuilt and reopened, preserving its complex history within its architecture and decorative styles. || Fabulous church with an astonishing story. Earthquakes, fire, you name it, this church has gone through a lot over the centuries! A must stop in Lisbon as the architecture of this church is simply amazing. || Very nice Church and place of worship, very old (dedicated in 1241) and damaged by various earthquakes, yet still standing with almost all the original glorious splendor of past centuries. The red ceiling is quite symbolic, together with the stones of the floor. I went early to the 6:00PM Mass and 15 minutes before it began, there were still plenty of tourists taking pictures and speaking loud. But as the Mass time got close, the temple got the silence proper for prayer and recollection of religious people. The liturgy was beautiful, with the proper dignity. The pipe organ makes beautiful sound waves through the old Church walls. Today (Sept. 28, 2025) was the Gospel of the rich man and the poor Lazarus (Luke 16:19-31). The priest delivered a beautiful sermon, balanced between the aspects of social obligations for the rich and wealthy people, and the moral implications for everyone to look around and identify the poor at the gates of their comfort zones, summarizing the message in the line that "often, wealth makes blind." Right in the midst of downtown Lisbon, this is a pearl of a monument since the 13th century and a place where we breathe already a bit of eternal peace if we are able to listen the old stones of the walls and floor, the gospel messages, as well as our own consciences in the hectic of the modern world of social responsibilities towards the poor. || Igreja De S Domingos is a beautiful and peaceful church, I visited when Mass was going on, on Easter Sunday. Definitely one of the most memorable churches I’ve seen in Lisbon || One of the most stunning churches that one can visit in Lisbon. A must-visit place. || Very cool, great history, worth going out of the way for because it is one of the most beautiful churches I've ever been in, the charred stone gives a sense of power greater than any church adorned with art and gilded intricacies || We were amazed by this place! I think that this is the most beuatiful church I’ve ever seen! || Awe-inspiring church, with fascinating story behind it because of various calamities. Outside the church is a memorial and a reminder to a darker side of history and religious persecution. The story is that after the church was severely damaged by fire in 1959 they did not restore it as part of the tribute to its earlier darker past. A very sombre and moving place that is worth a few minutes silence and contemplation. || If you can stomach fighting your way past the many beggars and undesirables that hang around the outside of this building it is well worth a visit . The church itself has survived at least two earthquakes and a devastating fire which the scars can still be seen etched into its internal walls . You are asked not to film inside but hey …. You only live once || This church is one of a kind. It has been barely left standing after the 1531 earthquake, the 1755 Lisbon earthquake and a major fire on August 13, 1959. You can still see the damage left after the fire on the walls and columns. It only reopened in 1994 after so much renovation work was done. It is kind of cool to see how they left the scars of the fire and it adds to the atmosphere of the church.  The church has had a long and mixed history. Obviously there were the terrible natural disasters that occured. On the other hand royal weddings of the Portuguese monarchy were once held here. One other lamentable event was the massacre of Jews, including Jewish concerts to Christianity, that was triggered by an incident at mass in 1506.  Follow here and the IG link in profile for more travel and food and drink tips, ideas and reviews! || Church of Saint Dominic, located next to Praça Dom Pedro IV, which was once one of the most important squares of the city, is one of the important structures in the history of Lisbon, although it seems like a church that only attracts tourists today.  Built in the 13th century, this church was for a long time the largest church in Lisbon and witnessed many events such as the Lisbon massacre and the execution of Gabriel Malagrida. In the Great Lisbon Earthquake of 1755, only the sacristy and altar survived from the church. The rebuilding of the church took more than 50 years.  Maintaining its importance until the 20th century, the church hosted Portuguese royal weddings. It had partially lost its importance with the establishment of the Portuguese Republic. In a fire in 1959, many artifacts were destroyed and the building fell into disrepair. Although the church was reopened in 1994 after the restoration, it is possible to see the traces of the fire on the walls.  The magnificence of the building, the real traces of the fire on the walls and the choice of textures on the places painted in the restoration added a unique atmosphere to the church. From the first moment you enter, you feel like you are in a place that has seen great pain. I recommend it as a structure that should be visited in Lisbon and its history should be studied together with the surrounding region. || Beautiful church, with the particularity of preserving, with minimal concealment, the damage its marbles suffered from a fire in 1959. Its evading architectural and statuary forms provide an added layer of spatial experience and of meaning to the church.  The church suffered several episodes of destruction, having to be rebuilt (and enlarged in the process), in the earthquake of the 16c and another in the 18c. The present form shows traces of late barroque, having had contributions by the architect of the palace of Mafra. By then it was in this church that several national and royal events took place, given its size, faust and centrality. All this magnificence was lost in the fire of 1959. || The church was absolutely beautiful! But I had such a strange encounter with the men selling candles inside. I kindly told the man, “I’m sorry, I don’t have 50 cents in Euros, but I can give you a $10 bill for the two candles and the rest can be a donation to the church.” To my surprise, he seemed bothered that I didn’t have Euros and flatly said no!
