I left feeling both hurt and annoyed. || Remarkable grand 13th century church that’s still standing and intact after a major earthquake over the centuries, and in more recent times, the fire of 1959. Despite it all, the exposure of the existing resilient pillars and refurbished roof give it an immense sense of grandeur and awe.  We sat and attended mass at 6pm one night. We felt blessed to be there. || I love this old church because it is very different from those I saw. It is simple, natural and has traces of the damages from fire and earth quake. I also like those tall stone columns which makes the  church looks very strong. I strongly recommend it.

Wonderful church right in the middle of the old town of Lisboa. Has a really long opening hours, and frequent services.  Visted on the Three Kings Day service. || I really enjoyed visiting the Church of Saint Nicholas. The neoclassical exterior is elegant, and the interior with its colorful marble and ceiling paintings felt peaceful and inspiring || Beautiful church.  We were so happy we experienced a Sunday vigil mass here.  It was at 10pm. Beautiful mass with an amazing cantor and organist.  Music was enchanting. || The Church of Saint Nicholas is a remarkable destination for anyone who appreciates history and architecture. This stunning landmark showcases breathtaking architectural details that reflect centuries of craftsmanship and devotion. From its intricately designed facade to the awe-inspiring interiors, every corner tells a story of heritage and faith.  Whether you’re an architecture enthusiast marveling at its arches, frescoes, and stained glass windows, or a history lover intrigued by its deep cultural and religious significance, this church offers a truly enriching experience. The peaceful atmosphere makes it an ideal spot for quiet reflection and appreciation of artistry. || Definitely worth a visit to check out the architecture and history. || Incredibly majestic church! Nice wall paintings and sculptures. There are some open caskets with what seems like the remains of some saints || Lisbon has many old churches. Some of them are not that interesting from the outside. But, once you get inside, you can see the beautiful architecture and the details which must have taken years to build.  We were staying on Prata Street.  One day while walking down the street, we came across this church.  The exterior was quite ordinary but, beautiful inside with paintings on the walls and dark wood pews.  The ambiance was inviting and peaceful.  The church is still active in the community. || The Church of St. Nicholas is located in the Baixa district of Lisbon and open most of the day so it is convenient to visit if passing through the area.  Historically, the church was originally built in 1280. However, what you see today is a reconstruction that took place after the devastating 1755 Lisbon Earthquake. Rebuilt between the 1760s and 1850s, the church building you see today as both Baroque and Neo-Classical features.  The facade is unassuming while the interior is more ornately decorative. There is a lovely series of beautiful ceiling paintings that depict the live of St. Nicholas. The nave is laid with coloured marble fitted with niche chapels holding sculptures of various saints. There is a gilded sacramental throne in the chancel at the front of the church that is very nice to see as well.  Interestingly, near the back you will see a multi-language monitor screen. You can use to learn about the history of the Church of St. Nicholas including what happened during the 1755 Lisbon Earthquake. There is information about the church reconstructions as well as important artefacts and ceiling paintings that you can see as well. || Wonderful unexpected surprise to discover that there is exposition of the Blessed Sacrament for us to spend quiet time in adoration of Jesus, when we walked past on Saturday, at ~830pm ! Anticipatory Mass at 10pm was also so meaningful. Thank you Lord for the priest and his team, for their love and sacrifice to make this available for us. || There was a meeting of orthodox clergymen in this beautiful church. The Catholic Church was generous to lend us the church for the celebration of Divine Liturgy.

place_name: Basilica of Our Lady of the Martyrs
reviews_content: Beautiful and warm, cosy feel. It's just a stunning basilica (which you can tell by the "umbrella" up at the right in the pulpit). I even ended up attending a portion of a Sunday mass, which was pretty interesting (not that I understand Portuguese).  I don't know what made this basilica feel different than many other churches I've visited, but it just had a very cosy, welcoming feel, and gorgeous ceiling art.  It's deceptive from the outside because you think it'll be kind of "plain", but it isn't. It's really stunning. || Marvellous architecture. Very very pretty. Highly recommend taking a look even if it’s just for a little while. There are also skeletons inside. || A beautiful church in the heart of Lisbon. I was surprised that it was open at 3:00pm in the afternoon and the Blessed Sacrament exposed for a duration. Beautiful! || Beautiful with amazing ceiling paintings. (The floor made my shoes make very loud sqeaky noises though) || Very beautiful church that you can easily visit in the city center. The ceiling is truly wonderful. || A really nice piece of architecture and a stunning site to explore and visit when walking around this area. || Basílica de Nossa Senhora dos Mártires (Basilica of Our Lady of the Martyrs) is located along Rua Serpa Pinto in the Chiado neighbourhood. It is one of several interesting historic church buildings you can visit in the area and according to their website is open from 9am to 6.30pm (Mon to Fri) and 10am to 6.30pm (Sat & Sun). There is a mass schedule on the Basilica website as well if needed.  The Basilica history dates back to the reconquest of Lisbon in 1147, when a chapel was built here to house the image of the Virgin carried by English crusaders. The chapel was given the name Our Lady of the Martyrs in memory of all European soldiers who died in retaking the city and defending the Christian faith.  The present church you can see today dates back to 1784. It was constructed by Portuguese architect Reinaldo Manuel dos Santos to replace the previous building destroyed during the 1755 Earthquake. You'll find subtle Baroque exterior along with a nicely decorated interior. The nave is lined side alters and fronted by an impressive main alter. There is also a delightful ceiling fresco, the work of Pedro Alexandrino de Carvalho, whose work can also be found in Sé (Lisbon Cathedral) and other important historic buildings around the city from that time. || We attended the vigil mass on Saturday evening. The Cantor also played the organ and had a beautiful singing voice. The people were friendly and the interior what's lovely. I wish that I spoke Portuguese. I couldn't understand the homily. || Simply a beautiful Church built-in 1147, check out all the details on their walls. I was shocked by how it was so well preserved and so nice at the same time.  It is amazing how people used to work years ago.  As soon as I walked in I felt so at peace and I loved it. || This is a beautiful house of worship with an ornate interior. Stop by for a few minutes to rest,  relax and admire this church.

place_name: Church of Saint Anthony of Lisbon
reviews_content: The Church of Saint Anthony of Lisbon is a beautiful and historic site dedicated to Saint Anthony, who was born here in 1195. According to tradition, the church was built on the very spot of his birthplace. The architecture is charming, and the altar is especially stunning, showcasing exquisite detail and craftsmanship. It’s a peaceful and inspiring place to visit. I highly recommend it to anyone exploring Lisbon. || Beautiful, historic church right by Lisbon Cathedral! Lovely Baroque-Rococo architecture with elegant details and a peaceful atmosphere. Built on the traditional birthplace of Saint Anthony and after the 1755 earthquake was rebuilt in 1767, it blends history and artistry perfectly. A must-see stop in the Alfama area || Beautiful and peaceful church of Saint Anthony, located in the heart of the downtown Full of history, with a warm and spiritual atmosphere. Downstairs, there’s a small chapel and the place where Saint Anthony was born. Visitors can also write prayer intentions. An ideal place to pause, pray, and fill your heart with peace. Inside the church, there’s a small shop where you can buy souvenirs, prayers, and rosaries. Highly recommended it is a must see, do and visit || The Church of Saint Anthony is a must-visit in Lisbon! I had a truly pleasant and blessed visit. The good architecture is remarkable, and the church has a wonderfully pleasant and serene atmosphere. It is highly recommended for devotion to Saint Anthony and for a moment of peace and reflection. || A beautiful church dedicated to Saint Anthony of Lisbon, known throughout the Cristian world as Saint Anthony of Padua. According to tradition, church was built on the site where the saint was born, in 1195. When you visit Afama, don't forget to visit this church. || St. Anthony Church in Lisbon is a revered religious and historical site closely linked to the life of St. Anthony of Padua, making it a popular pilgrimage destination for visitors and locals alike. This 18th-century baroque church is believed to mark the birthplace of St. Anthony, one of Portugal’s most beloved saints, and offers beautiful architecture, onsite services, and an atmosphere steeped in history just steps away from Lisbon Cathedral. || Beyond being the patron saint of lost items, I was told Saint Anthony was also known as the match maker; regardless, you should definitely visit this beautiful little church if you have the time. || The Church of Saint Anthony of Lisbon (Portuguese: Igreja de Santo António de Lisboa) is a church located in Lisbon, Portugal. It is dedicated to Saint Anthony of Lisbon (also known in the Christian world as Saint Anthony of Padua). According to tradition, the church was built on the site where the saint was born in 1195. The church is classified as a National Monument. || The interior is splendid. The altar is beautiful. The ceiling and floor are colorful. Paintings are fabulous. || Saint Anthony is in the cellar at the underground floor, by walk through his house within the church, just like exploring levels in Dark Souls game. The crying Mary statue looks alive. || A small church (no ticket required), but worth a quick stop before or after visiting the castle and the Cathedral. Make sure to go downstairs to the birthplace and see where Pope John Paul came to pray. || An amazing church to visit—well organised. Entry is €5 per person. I was told there’s a 20% discount with a Lesbian Tourist Card, which you can get from the tourist information centre. || The Church of Saint Anthony of Lisbon is a masterpiece of design and artistry. Its architecture is beautifully crafted, blending lightness with sophistication that captivates the eye. The intricate details throughout the church are complemented by the use of stunning colors, which add warmth and depth to its serene atmosphere.  Walking through this sacred space felt both peaceful and inspiring. || The church stands on the site believed to be the birthplace of Santo António (Saint Anthony, born Fernando de Bulhões). A small chapel was first established here in the 15th century. During the reign of King Manuel I in the 16th century, the church was expanded, but much of it was destroyed in the 1755 earthquake—only the main altar remained. The current building was reconstructed in 1767 by Mateus Vicente de Oliveira in a mix of Baroque and Rococo styles. Beneath the church lies a crypt marking the saint’s birthplace, which preserves the remains of the earlier chapel. Every year on June 13th, the feast day of the saint, a festive parade begins right in front of the church. || I had the opportunity to visit the Church and Museum of Saint Anthony in Lisbon, and it was a deeply enriching experience that offered both spiritual reflection and historical insight. Located near the Lisbon Cathedral in the Alfama district, the Church of Saint Anthony is traditionally believed to be built on the site where the saint was born in 1195. The original structure was destroyed in the 1755 earthquake, but it was rebuilt in 1767 in a late Baroque and Pombaline style under the direction of architect Mateus Vicente de Oliveira. The interior is serene, and the crypt, accessible through the sacristy, is considered to be the exact spot of Saint Anthony's birth.  Adjacent to the church is the Museum of Saint Anthony, which offers a comprehensive look into the life and legacy of one of Lisbon's most revered figures. The museum houses a collection of religious artifacts, including sculptures, paintings, ceramics, and liturgical items, all dedicated to the saint's life and the devotion he inspires. One of the highlights is a 17th-century polychrome tile panel depicting Saint Anthony preaching to the fish. The museum also features multimedia exhibits that delve into the traditions, festivals, and miracles associated with the saint. Admission is affordable, and the museum is open from Tuesday to Sunday, making it accessible for visitors interested in exploring Lisbon's rich cultural and religious heritage. || Now I know why I was automatically dran to the Igreja de Santo António de Lisboa. I tend to lose things and Saint Antonio - born in Lisbon – is th beloved patron “finder of lost things.” Many visitors write small notes (I did not) or prayers for things they’re seeking to find - whether it’s a lost key, a lost purpose, or a lost moment of peace. . The interior of the church is elegant without being overly ornate. I like it very much. || the church of Sant'Antonio stands in the place where, according to legend, the patron saint of both Lisbon and Padua was born. for this reason it is a pilgrimage destination for devotees of the saint and also offers a visit to his presumed birthplace, located below the church. free entrance. || It is unclear whether the chapel below the church, which is dedicated to Saint Anthony of Lisbon (a.k.a. Anthony of Padua) really marks the spot where the birthplace or even the house of the saint stood in the 12th century. In 1495, King João II commissioned the construction of "a lager and more dignified" church or chapel on this site. Simultaneously, history tells us that the meetings of the city council of Lisbon were held in the house of Saint Anthony and continued to do so for several more centuries. This building was situated next to the church but destroyed in the 1755 earthquake, which was followed by a tidal wave that consumed over 80 percent of the city, including the church. A third church, the present one, was built on the site of the old church. The present chapel below the church used to be called the Crypt of Saint Anthony, suggesting he was buried there. He was, as a matter of fact, buried in Padua, Italy. Since Pope John Paul 2nd visited the chapel and prayed there, it is officially called a chapel. The chapel itself is a small hallway with a small niche under an arched construction, in which behind bars is a small 'altar' with a relic of Saint Anthony. Presumably, there is a piece of bone of the saint inside it, but regretfully, there is no text explaining this to visitors. Mostly, the texts inside and outside the chapel relate to the visit of the pope. Besides that, they mention that the chapel is the only remnant of the 2nd church of 1495. That church was built 264 years after the death of the saint. If it truly it had been the exact spot of the birthplace of Saint Anthony, several meters below ground level, you would expect such a sacred place would have been incorporated into that new church. Also, it contradicts the existence of the Saint Anthony House next to the church at that same time.  Another matter is a painting inside the nave of the church. It is advertised to be the most faithful likeness of Saint Anthony, the "true effigy of the Saint," although it was painted somewhere between 350 and 450 years after his death. Apparently, it is of unknown provenance.  On the other side of the nave is a relic of Saint Justina. This could be Saimt Justina of Padua, but regretfully, this is not mentioned. It is a statue of a reclining lady dressed in cloth of real fabric, decorated with golden flowers and jewelry. On her head, a wreath of flowers, and in her hands, she is holding a bouquet of flowers. At her feet, a small vase, covered by a lid, presumably, inside it is a piece of bone or other body part of this saint.  The church itself is quite beautiful. It was designed in a rococo-baroque style.  Set aside all the questions about the originality of spaces and objects under and inside the church, the dedication by believers is what matters most to people of faith. It's arguably that which gives it its strength and makes it unique.  It is to be assumed that during the earthquake and the following tidal flood of 1755, much of the original documentation of the city was lost.  The visit is free of charge.  At the entrance of the church and next to the sacristy are religious gift shops. Also, next to the sacristy are public toilets for visitors. To the side of the front of the church is a Saint Anthony museum. || This is in the Alfama in Lisbon, it's  hard to find a parking spot and if you find one it's only for 2 hours limit.  It's not enough time to walk or explore and have diner. I would leave the vehicle somewhere else parked and just take a Uber to the location. || It was a nice cute little church where they honor Saint Antony, it's free to enter and you can go to the place where they say he was born. You should totally check this church.

On 6 December 2025, as a member of Associaçao São Charbel, we celebrated together with the Parish of São Paulo in Lisbon the arrival of the relics of Saint Charbel from Lebanon. It was a memorial day for many lebanese and portuguese believers. Visits are possible every day except Saturdays. || The church itself is absolutely beautiful definitely worth it to pop in to take a peak of your walking past. The square out the front of it though is absolutely filthy and constant drug dealing and sketchy behaviour happening. 😔 || Visited the Church of Saint Paul on October 29th during a daytime walk around the city of Lisbon and seeing its spectacularly painted ceiling, designed to create an illusion of depth with columns, balconies, and heavenly scenes was absolutely worth it. || Hidden jem of a church. Behind Time Out Market! || This is a Baroque church at the western end of Praça de São Paulo and just a couple minutes walk from Mercado da Ribeira. Like so many churches in Lisbon, it seems it was mostly destroyed during the 1755 Lisbon Earthquake and rebuilt around 1768 by Portuguese architect Francisco Remigio de Abreau.  I liked the simple facade with two bell towers and double niche fitted with statues of St. Paul and St. Peter. Within the church, there is a nave with white marble walls fitted with side chapels. The high altar is very attractive. However, what impressed me the most was the charming ceiling fresco. Stand in back and give it a few minutes to enjoy. There is a remarkable 3D effect to the fresco. || A beautiful square outside the church. || My absolutely favourite church in Lisbon. Blissful place😀 || Check the opening times so you can go in and see the beautiful painting on the ceiling. The altar is also very nice.  This evangelical church/cathedral was destroyed in the 1955 Lisbon earthquake and rebuilt in 1768.  Follow here and on IG for more travel and food and drink tips, ideas and reviews @one.more.step.along.the.world || A gorgeous church with a unique painted wooden ceiling and a very narrow altar that gives it elegant proportions. A comforting respite in the midst of a tourist filled neighbourhood. || Quiet and nice place. With a beautiful ceiling inside. || Very peaceful, beautiful || Magnificent ceiling painting || This church evokes the history of one of Christianity's most important apostles. Its interior is inviting, full of Baroque cultural heritage. It's worth a visit. || Facing a very dirty square with graffiti. Small place but on the tourist route. I didn't like it. || Church of St. Paul Igreja de São Paulo The Church of St. Paul || Splendid in its architecture and Catholic symbols. Besides the main altar, the side altars are beautiful. This magnificent church is located in the city center and is well worth a visit. || In a corner of Lisbon, behind the famous Time Out Market, lies the Church of São Paulo. An intimate atmosphere filled the air as we entered the church; classical music was playing through the loudspeaker system. Everything was very clean, with holy water and options for donations and participation in community events. In short, a church where people feel welcome. There is also a square of the same name with a fountain providing water, number 28. || It's worth a visit. If you walked from the Alcantara Mare train station to Piazza del Commercio or vice versa, you've followed a historical journey through the 18th century, with reconstructions and restorations, as in this case. Be careful not to confuse it with the "Catholic Cathedral of the Evangelicals," which is also located along the route.

place_name: Church of St. Vincent de Fora
reviews_content: A beautiful and tranquil church. Few visitors on a weekday in December. Time and space to appreciate wonderful monastic chanting playing in the background. The multi-lingual signs direct you towards the amazing collection of blue and white tiles (azulejo) which decorate the cloisters, walls, and stairs. These are simply stunning. Many depict rural scenes and the pursuits of the gentry, while others capture funny parables and fables. The latter are very well presented for visitors, with written summaries of each one in Portuguese and English. In total there are over 200 tiled panels so some you might want to study carefully and others you might spend less time on, depending on your schedule. Another highlight for us is the 360 degree panoramic view from the roof, well worth the climb. A fascinating good-value  visit. Seems to be overlooked by many tourists. || Thank you so much for this wonderful and thoughtful review! We’re truly delighted to hear that you enjoyed the calm atmosphere of the church and had the time and space to fully appreciate the monastic chanting and the remarkable azulejo collection.  It’s especially rewarding to know that the multilingual interpretation and the presentation of the tile panels helped bring the stories to life for you. With more than 200 panels, it’s lovely to hear you took the time to explore them at your own pace.  We’re also very glad you enjoyed the panoramic rooftop view, it really is a special perspective over Lisbon and a highlight for many of our visitors.  Thank you for highlighting the tranquility and value of the visit, and for helping bring attention to a place that often remains a hidden gem. We hope to welcome you back again in the future! || A beautiful and peaceful church with impressive architecture and stunning tile work. It’s less crowded than other Lisbon landmarks, which makes it a nice spot to explore in a calm atmosphere. The cloisters and the rooftop view are definitely worth seeing || Thank you so much for your kind words and thoughtful review! We're truly happy to hear that you enjoyed the peaceful atmosphere and took the time to appreciate the architecture and tile work. The cloisters and rooftop views are indeed special, and we're glad they made an impression on you. We always strive to offer a calm and meaningful experience for our visitors—thank you for being part of it! || Such an underrated gem! My friends and I spent nearly two hours exploring the beautiful rooms, the church, cloisters, and vast collection of religious artifacts with great explanations. The rooftop views are stunning, and best of all, it’s not crowded. || Thank you so much for your comment! We're happy to hear that you enjoyed the visit, the explanations, and the views from the terrace. We hope to welcome you back again soon! || Not to be missed, really enjoyed our visit here. Think we got lucky as we arrived quite later but it was open because it was Sunday. Nice place to walk around with loads of interesting large blue and white tiles. Great views at the top too. || Thank you so much for your visit and kind words! We are very happy to know that you enjoyed the monastery, the tiles, and the views. || This is amazing place! Not crowded, cheap entrance tickets. I highly recommend you to visit it. Very underrated, unfortunately. || Thank you so much for your kind review! We’re really happy to hear that you enjoyed the place and appreciated the peaceful atmosphere and affordable tickets. Your recommendation truly means a lot to us. We agree, it’s a hidden gem, and we’re glad you discovered it! || Marvellous.  The complex as a whole is one of the best religious buildings we have visited in Lisbon. The museum is beautifully laid out with some fantastic items. The two cloisters are an oasis of serenity  - plain simple white but with a series of beautiful tiled scenes/panels (65 in total). The actual church is massive with a series of beautifully decorated side chapels. The highlight has to be the views over Lisbon from the roof. We spent well over a hour just wondering around enjoying its serenity and elegant beauty. || Thank you so much for your visit and for your kind words! We are delighted to know that you enjoyed exploring the Monastery of São Vicente de Fora and that you appreciated the serenity of the cloisters, the richness of the museum, and the beauty of the church—especially the view over Lisbon. Comments like yours are a great motivation for us to continue preserving this very special place. We hope to welcome you back soon! || Beautiful and peaceful spot in Alfama. The church is stunning inside and the cloisters with the blue azulejos are incredible. The rooftop view over Lisbon is worth the visit alone.  Quiet, historical, and full of charm. One of Lisbon’s hidden gems. || Thank you so much for your feedback!  We are very pleased to know that you enjoyed the church, the cloisters with their tiles, and the view from the terrace.  It's always a pleasure to welcome those who appreciate the history and tranquility of this special place.  We hope you will visit us again! || What a treasure in the middle of Lisbon.  Not far from the port. Definitely worth the time. Climb the bell tower if you can for amazing views of Lisbon. || Thank you so much for your comment!  We're glad to hear you enjoyed your visit and the view from the terrace. || I absolutely love the Mannerist complex – the simplicity and symmetry are just perfect! It’s also a very quiet spot, so you can really take your time and enjoy every detail. The exhibition offers a thorough look at the history from the medieval period, though most of it is in Portuguese. The architectural elements are definitely worth the visit, especially the cloisters and the rooftop terrace, which offer stunning views of Lisbon. The admission fee for adults is €8, and you get a discount with the Lisboa Card! || Thank you very much for your visit and kind comment about the Monastery. Wow! Fantastic description of the monastery with all essential details and information. Thank you very much for sharing your positive experience and promotion to our monastery. || An absolutely stunning church! The Church of St. Vincent de Fora is a hidden gem in Lisbon, offering breathtaking architecture and rich history. The interior is beautifully adorned, with intricate details and a peaceful atmosphere. The view from the rooftop is also incredible, providing a unique perspective of the city. The staff were welcoming and informative, making the visit even more enjoyable. A must-see for anyone in Lisbon – truly a remarkable experience! || Thank you very much for your visit and kind comment about the monastery. We are very glad to know that you enjoyed your time here and we are grateful for the magnificent description of your very positive experience. It is very rewarding for us that you not only enjoyed the monument itself which is stunning, but also appreciated the assistance provided by our staff. Hope to see you again in the future! || Beyond the beauty and ornateness, it's fun to walk through the halls, and there's also a great 360 degree lookout at the top. || Thank you for your wonderful feedback. We hope to see you again soon to explore even more of this stunning place! || We were spending a few days in Lisbon and saw this from the castle so decided to walk over to it. We thought it was beautiful and well worth the entrance fee. There is plenty to see here from the exhibition of all the old cloaks and artifices to the stunning blue picture tile all around the place. We also went up onto the roof and despite it being wet and grey you still had some nice views. || The team is delighted to know that the visit to the Monastery was a lovely surprise. Thank you! || Religion isn't really my thing, but if it interests you, there's a lot to see. The building itself is very impressive due to its sheer size. The absolute best part is that you can go up to the roof, offering a 360° view over the city for just €8. In good weather, the view is breathtaking (and hot).  The panoramic view allows you to see the entire cityscape, making it a must-visit spot for tourists. The experience of seeing the city from such a height is truly unforgettable and well worth the price. || Indeed, the panoramic view is one of the most beautiful spots in the monastery! Thank you very much! || Definitely worth a visit when in Lisbon. The story of the church of Sao Vicente is extremely interesting. Recommend buying the ticket with the guided tour (only 4€ more). It is possible to access the rooftop of the church which offers a stunning view over Lisbon and the Tago river. Highly recommended. || Thank you very much for your kind comment and for participating in one of our guided tours. We are very happy to hear that you enjoyed the experience and grateful for your feedback. Hope too see you again! || Igreja de São Vicente de Fora is a beautiful place! The church is not that impressive but the monastery is stunning!! I loved the white blue tiles that cover the most of walls! Such a nice exhibition! And not crowded at all!! If you ask is a must! Totally recommend it! || Thank you very much for your visit and kind comment about our monastery. We are glad to know that you enjoyed your time here and appreciated our exhibitions. The peace and serenity within the monastery still take us to ancient times, when it was still inhabited by monks. || We went to this church on a rainy day.  It was so much draft inside some parts of the church. The down pour in the courtyard was very loud.  Because of the pouring rain, we ended up spending more time to walk to all areas of the church, and read through the details, which we don’t do normally. A lot of interesting stuff. It feels more like a museum than an actual church.  Keep your ticket,  you need it to go out or use the washroom. || Sometimes, unexpected situations like the rain make us experience places in a different way. It's nice to know you were able to explore more calmly and discover so many details. || Atmospheric place. There are no crowds of tourists. You can enjoy the exhibits, the atmosphere without the fuss. Beautiful, majestic place. On the  rooftop is a panoramic view of the city. || Thank you very much for your visit and kind comment about the Monastery. We are very glad to know that you enjoyed the experience and very grateful for the beautiful pictures! || Humble, still stunning. Alfama is full of historical gems and this church is one of them without any doubt. The dome is perfect, the building is beautiful both inside and outside. || Thank you very much! Come back anytime! || Very nice place to visit, a lot history. || Incredible, prolific tile work! And marble! Worth paying to self-tour around the complex. There’s a 360-degree viewing terrace in the tower. Fun to take the time to read all the fables that are depicted in tiled panels. || Thank you very much for your visit and kind comment about our monastery. We are glad to know that you enjoyed tour time here, indeed there is a lot of tile inside to appreciate (more than 100.000), being the collection of the Fables of Jean de La Fontaine represented in tile the most unique one.

place_name: Church of Our Lady of Grace
reviews_content: One of the oldest churches in the city, its origins date back to 1271. It was dedicated to a statue of the Virgin Mary miraculously recovered off the coast of Cascais (Portugal, a land of miracles...). Before our eyes unfolds a compendium of Portuguese Baroque religious art: gilded wood, exquisite azulejos (tiles) dating from the 16th, 17th, and 18th centuries, and striking sculptural and trompe-l'œil effects. However, it was damaged, along with the convent, during the 1755 earthquake and subsequently rebuilt. || We visited the church during Christmas holidays. The church is great and tells a lot about Lisbon history. On top, there was a beautiful Christmas crib. Before leaving the church, take time to contemplate one of the most beautiful panorama of the city || Highly recommended. Fantastic view of the city. And the feelings... Sombody play the music in the park behind the temple || We stumbled across this church while strolling around the hills of Lisbon. It’s a little gem with its azulejos and gilded altars,  But the terrace was even better. Breathtaking. No crowds, lots of places to sit, and not overrun with tourists, at least when we were there. || Dear David, we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience. Thank you for your kind comment. It's very important to us. || Beautiful Catholic Church with lots of chandeliers statues, lovely painted ceilings. There is also a plaza out front with beautiful views of the city, places to sit and meet and enjoy a leisurely afternoon. || An amazing and somewhat unexpected stop while touring Lisbon. Beautiful architecture of the church, located on one of the most beautiful viewpoints of the city. Completely unexpected was the offer for 6 EUR per person to tour the gallery of sacred paintings with entrance to the roof/route of the church with a drink. The most beautiful experience in Lisbon, when with a glass of port wine you enjoy panoramic views of the city from the roof terrace, where there are nice and comfortable seating. Pleasant peace (only the sound of bells from the church bell towers) from the hustle and bustle on the viewpoint in front of the church and without crowds of tourists or sellers of various trinkets. || Beautiful medieval former monastery with a church. Really worth walking all the way up to sit with a drink on a rooftop terraceswith stunning panoramic views all over the city. The building itself is very atmospheric and definitely worth coming inside and exploring. || Dear Grzegorz, thank you for your kind comment. place_name: Church of Saint John of God
reviews_content: In the heart of Lisbon, amidst its bustling streets and vibrant culture, lies a sanctuary of serenity and architectural splendour: the Church of Saint John of God (Igreja de São João de Deus). This edifice is not merely a structure; it is a testament to the intertwining of faith, art, and the human condition.  Historical Backdrop  The Church of Saint John of God was erected in the mid-20th century, a period marked by profound social and political changes in Portugal. The architect, responsible for translating faith into concrete and glass, envisioned a space that would reflect the modernist ethos of the era while paying homage to the timeless tenets of spirituality and community. In this endeavour, the church stands as a beacon of modernist architectural principles, eschewing the ornate for the sublime simplicity.  Architectural Marvel  From the outside, the church’s façade may strike one as unassumingly modern, yet it is within its walls that the true grandeur unfolds. The design eschews the traditional Gothic or Baroque styles predominant in Lisbon’s older churches, opting instead for clean lines and an open, airy interior that invites light to dance upon its surfaces. This choice of design creates an atmosphere of tranquillity, a stark contrast to the city’s frenetic pace.  A Sanctuary of Peace  It was on a day, burdened with the weight of personal tribulations, that I found myself drawn to this church’s welcoming embrace. Crossing its threshold, I was immediately enveloped in a calm that seemed almost tangible. The interior, with its subtle play of light and shadow, offered a profound sense of peace and a momentary respite from life’s challenges. It was here, in this unexpected haven, that I found a space for reflection and solace.  Artistic and Spiritual Resonance  The Church of Saint John of God is also a repository of modern sacred art, from its stained glass to the minimalist altar, each piece contributes to a narrative of faith expressed through contemporary aesthetics. This fusion of modern art within a sacred space underscores the church’s role as a bridge between the divine and the everyday, inviting all who enter to find their own meaning within its walls.  Why Visit?  For travellers and explorers of Lisbon’s rich tapestry, the Church of Saint John of God offers a unique detour from the well-trodden path. Here, one can experience the quietude of modernist architecture, contemplate art imbued with spiritual significance, and perhaps find a moment of personal peace. It is a reminder that amidst the rush of modern life, there are spaces designed to soothe the soul and stir the heart.  An Invitation  This church, with its modernist charm and quiet dignity, stands as an open invitation to those traversing Lisbon’s historic streets. Whether you seek solace, an appreciation of modern sacred art, or simply a quiet moment of beauty, the Church of Saint John of God awaits. In my own journey, it offered a sanctuary at a moment of need, and for that, it will always hold a special place in my heart.  In conclusion, the Church of Saint John of God is more than just a point of interest in Lisbon; it is a landmark of faith, art, and the enduring human spirit. || Lovely architecture with a modern and up market touch. Immersing yourself in a barrel full of beer may seem like a nightmare for some, but there are those who consider it a truly relaxing experience. The beer spa concept originated in the Czech Republic and this month arrives in Lisbon, with a new twist. The Beer & Wine SPA Lisbon opened in Chiado at the beginning of August and, like any Portuguese project, has incorporated local tradition. In addition to the beer experiences, the space has added wine to the drinks used. The concept is simple: the spa has several wooden tubs that can be filled with local beers or wines. During the experience, visitors also have unlimited access to drinks. With 340 square meters, the Beer & Wine SPA Lisbon is the result of a venture by Lee Anderson and Pedro Ruiz, two foreign entrepreneurs. The inspiration came from traditional spas in northern and eastern Europe, where beer baths are common. Prices start at €54 for the basic circuit, which includes a bath in a beer tub, access to the spa circuit with sauna and lounge, plus unlimited beer. For greater privacy, all tubs are equipped with curtains and taps specifically for beer and wine. Anybody can come and spend the day enjoying sunbathing, picnic king, talking to friends, enjoying the cafeteria and cafés and the incredibly well designed landscape. If you go to Lisbon, you must come see this place. || Great private collection of art from prehistoric to modern, situated in a beautiful (free) garden. Ticket for the permanent collection was 14€, which is slightly steep but still worth it. For 2€ more I could have gotten access to several additional temp exhibitions that looked nice, just run out of time. Especially nice were the pieces from René lalique. || Petrol money put to good use. It's sad to see so many new structures talking over the once amazing gardens. Still beautiful but the new buildings are not welcome and even the new wood structure is just a waste of money and garden space. Gulbenkian will remain a very special space in Lisbon. || The green area around the museum is very peaceful and well maintained, this is a super nice location to just sit on the bench with friends or family.  The art museum itself is perfect for one day visit, you can see loads of beautiful art pieces in a small museum. I got here on Sunday afternoon, the staff told me that from 2pm in every Sunday is free to visit. || A true gem of a museum that would stand out in any city. It hosts the eclectic art and artefacts collection of a person who was obviously in search of beauty from ancient Egypt up to his own time. I especially enjoyed the architecture of the building itself with its modernist cleanliness and brutalist power. The visit to the cafeteria perfectly wrapped up my visit with good coffee and fresh Portuguese sweets. || One of my favorite museums in Lisbon. The Japanese zen style gardens provide a great source of peace. You can also have coffee, brunch and lunch there. Many options. I loved the Portuguese artists creations. A must do! || What a lovely museum! This hidden gem is nestled in an urban oasis. The entrance fee is affordable, and it wasn’t too crowded. Granted, we visited mid-week, so perhaps the weekends are busier.  The museum houses the private collection of a rich oil guy, and while I think many of the priceless artifacts from around the world should be returned to their places of origin, I must admit that it was incredibly cool to meander through the exquisitely-curated rooms and marvel at the wonders that await.  I appreciated that each object was allowed to shine, and the exhibits weren’t overcrowded. Each item has its own space to breathe. The museum takes about an hour to go through if you take your time, and I think it’s an excellent size.  My favorite parts were the Turkish plates, European impressionist paintings, jewelry room at the end, and the Egyptian room.  The gift shop felt overpriced and underwhelming, but the cafe was very cute. || Such a pretty museum!! Love the current exhibition! It also wasn't busy at all even though I visited at a Saturday. || Even though I only saw the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum from the outside, the experience was still impressive and worthy of five stars. Set within a beautifully landscaped garden, the building blends perfectly into its surroundings with a sleek, modernist design that feels calm and inviting. The low, horizontal lines of the structure, combined with large windows and natural stone, give it a simple elegance that complements the greenery around it.  Walking through the gardens, I enjoyed the peaceful atmosphere—quiet pathways, shaded areas, and small ponds create a sense of relaxation that makes the museum’s exterior feel like an artwork in itself. The way the museum is integrated into this natural setting makes it stand out from other cultural buildings I’ve seen. It feels less like a monumental landmark and more like a thoughtfully designed retreat dedicated to art and culture.  Even without going inside, it’s easy to appreciate the vision behind this place. The architecture and surrounding parkland invite visitors to slow down and enjoy both nature and creativity. For anyone visiting Lisbon, I’d recommend at least passing by the Gulbenkian Museum to admire its beautiful design and gardens—it’s a serene and inspiring part of the city. || Amazing Brazil exhibition, unfortunately the main works exhibition was closed for refurbishment || Fantastic museum with an excellent and varied collection. The exhibits are clearly labelled and very spacious, and when we went mid-week, there weren't any crowds.  There are even a few heavy hitters, with some paintings by Monet and Renoir on display, but even without those, there are many beautiful and interesting pieces.  Sunday after 2pm, entry is free, but if that doesn't work for your schedule as it didn't for us, it was still very much worth the modest entrance fee.

The Museu Militar de Lisboa is an impressive and educational destination for anyone interested in Portugal’s military history. The museum houses a wide range of artifacts, including historic weapons, uniforms, medals, and detailed displays that span several centuries. The exhibitions are well-organized, providing context about Portugal’s military campaigns, strategies, and historical events, which makes the visit both informative and engaging. The building itself has a commanding presence, adding to the sense of history and tradition. While some areas could benefit from updated signage or more interactive elements, the museum remains a valuable cultural experience. Overall, the Museu Militar de Lisboa offers a deep and enriching look into Portugal’s military heritage, appealing to history enthusiasts and curious visitors alike. || Glad I found it thru other views (thank you!). The place looks more like a royal palace than a museum! They mostly cover WW I and before. I personally loved their WW I room where I felt emotional. God bless all fallen ones regardless of their sides. My only wish is they could put more history background timeline for visitors to understand. Overall, very well-spent 3 euros! || We passed this museum everyday whilst staying at the Editory Riverside. We decided to visit on our last day in Lisbon. It’s really a great place to experience the history of Portuguese military history. The staff were very attentive throughout, ensuring we didn’t miss any of the collection. Our visit to the Lisbon Military Museum was an unexpected highlight of our trip. This place is truly awesome not only for history buffs, but for anyone who appreciates beautiful architecture and incredible attention to detail.  The museum is extremely good value for money, offering a rich and immersive experience that far exceeds the modest entry fee. What really surprised us was how spectacularly decorated the building itself is – the interiors are so ornate and impressive that they rival, and in some cases even surpass, many of the city’s palaces.  Beyond the stunning surroundings, the collection of military memorabilia is extensive and clearly labeled in English, which made it easy to appreciate and understand. From ancient cannons to detailed dioramas and uniforms, there’s so much to take in, and it’s all beautifully presented.  I would absolutely put this down as a must-see in Lisbon, even if you’re not particularly into military history. The sheer beauty of the museum’s interior makes it worth the visit on its own.  Highly recommended! || A fascinating museum in a stunning historic building, with beautiful painted walls and ceilings. This hidden gem offers a fascinating glimpse into Portugal's rich military history, and the admission fee of just 3 euros makes it an incredible value.  - A Palace of Military Artifacts  The museum is housed in a beautifully decorated building with ornate ceilings and marble columns. As you wander through the rooms, you'll be surrounded by an impressive collection of weapons, cannons, and armor. The exhibits are well-preserved and thoughtfully arranged, providing a comprehensive overview of Portugal's military evolution.  - From Medieval Swords to Modern Firearms  One of the highlights of the museum is the wide range of historical artifacts on display. You'll find everything from medieval swords and armor to modern firearms and military equipment. The collection showcases the diversity of Portugal's military forces throughout the centuries.  - A Stunning Tribute to Portugal's History  The Museu Militar de Lisboa is more than just a museum; it's a testament to Portugal's rich history. As you explore the exhibits, you'll gain a deeper understanding of the country's role in global events. The museum's informative displays and impressive collection make it a truly unforgettable experience.  - A Must-Visit for History Buffs  Whether you're a history enthusiast or simply looking for something different to do in Lisbon, the Museu Militar de Lisboa is highly recommended. With its affordable admission fee and fascinating exhibits, it's a hidden gem that shouldn't be missed. || For 3eur it's absolute no brainer to spend some time here. The conviction, determination and resourcefulness of the men and women that actively participated in resisting the fascist government is a brave example for us all. || Beautiful monastery, with stunning architecture. Tough in places, but a poignant reminder of how easily we could again lose hard-won freedoms as we witness the rise of right-wing politics in our time. || I have visited the museum the last Saturday of May 2025 and I have only said good things about. I chose a guided visit. The guide, Elisabete Araújo know all the historic details and she is an excellent communicator who explains with passion every bend of the Museum. The information and displays are well-curated, the layout is well-planned, and the photographic and video artifacts are compelling. I never knew how bad it was for people under the fascist regime - and really, it wasn’t very long ago. || The story of Portugal’s repressive past is very well told. There’s not much in the way of exhibits because this is essentially the telling of a story of how the human spirit was crushed by fascism and how its resilience ultimately triumphed. It is compelling, and moving.  Not very engaging for kids and families but an interesting and important museum to ensure we do not forget the very recent past (because as George Santayana reminded us ‘Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it.” || My wife and I visited this museum on our last day in Lisbon without really knowing what to expect, and we were deeply impressed. Neither of us knew much about the history of the Salazar dictatorship and its downfall in the Carnation Revolution, and we learned so much from touring the extremely well done exhibits here. As a visitor, you walk through a chronological timeline starting with events leading up to the fall of the Portuguese monarchy, the brief period of democracy in its aftermath, the rise of Salazar’s fascist regime and the decades-long resistance that eventually led to the regime’s overthrow in 1974. It was every bit as moving as our visit to the Anne Frank House, and the bravery of the resistance was inspiring. Most but not all of the individual exhibits have English captions, but even if we couldn’t read everything we were still very moved by what we saw. || This museum is a must see, not only from the historical context, but the similarities with today's attacks on political enemies, holding prisoners without due process and secret police roaming the streets of Chicago.   The museum was laid out very well, with text, photos and diagrams that clarified the rise and fall of the Salazar regime.  The museum also clarified the relationship between the mid 20th Century dictatorships, and today's events involving trump.  We spent much more time than planned, allow 2 hours to fully experience this museum.

One of the most beautiful exhibitions to see in Lisbon. The building itself is also very good. It has a calming atmosphere. You can see a lot of different exhibitions and the staff is also very nice. Definitely “a must see” if you are visiting Lisbon.  After visiting the exhibitions, you can chill in the beautiful garden which is also very good designed. You feel like you are in another world:) I suggest you to go there a bit early and hang out with the ducks after your visit, there are restaurants/cafes you can sit at too. || Centro de Arte Moderna Gulbenkian - Where Wood, Light, and Art Collide in Quiet Elegance  Tucked into the leafy calm of Rua Marquês de Fronteira, the Centro de Arte Moderna (CAM) is a space that whispers rather than shouts. And the first thing that catches your eye - before the art, before the exhibitions - is that roof. Oh, that roof.  Inspired by Japanese design, the wooden canopy stretches out like a warm embrace, with natural open-grain beams that filter the light and soften the edges of the building. It’s minimalist without being cold, organic without being rustic, and it sets the tone for everything that follows. You feel like you’re entering a space that respects silence, celebrates craftsmanship, and invites reflection.  Inside, the layout is clean and considered, with natural materials and soft lighting that let the artworks breathe. Even without a blockbuster exhibition, it’s a place worth visiting just to experience the architecture, wander the serene spaces, and soak in the Gulbenkian calm.  We were lucky to catch the tail end of “Between Your Teeth”, a powerful exhibition featuring Paula Rego and Adriana Varejão. Though now closed, it left behind a lingering sense of bold storytelling and emotional depth, perfectly matched to the building’s quiet strength.  Verdict: CAM is a masterclass in architectural grace, where wood meets light, and art finds room to speak softly but powerfully. Highly recommended for design lovers, quiet wanderers, and anyone who believes that a roof can be a work of art. || I was out and about in the neighbourhood, they had a nice programme for the day, so i decided to check it out. It's been a while! The 1st time back since the renovation was completed. Highly recommend the guided visit to the exhibition. I enjoyed the creation of small island and the rock and use the headphones for the sound and some background information. Also they usually have different exhibitions going on. They have a cafe or more like a rest pastelaria. Foods I have seen usually around 8 to 10 euros. Also there's some other cafes and restaurants with outdoor sitting. Great for a coffee and cigarette. Don't miss the tv room inside the British gallery collection. It's something I found really amazing. || Great exhibitions from beginning to end. And the facility is an art piece itself. Staff was exceptionally friendly. Go for the art then walk around the beautiful grounds.

An iconic cultural place in Lisboa. You can visit the house museum or attend a fado performance. I recommend the latter as it'll give you more context about the Amália and her legacy. Better to purchase tickets ahead of time, they only accept cash. The performance takes about 2 hours but it's worth it as it allows you to inmerse into the music and learn about Lisboa. Before at the interim you can purchase drinks and food. || This museum/home is a gem. A very real tribute to a beautiful and talented woman. Amalia’s home can only be seen by going on a very well organized tour (in Portuguese or English). Our tour guide was Nuno - who is kind, knowledgeable and very loyal to Amalia and her place in the history of Fado.  Be prepared to be taken on a journey and be surprised to understand her worldwide presence and appeal. Highly recommend this experience.  Plus on Thursdays and Saturdays there are Fado performances in the Garden!  Enjoy! || We had an incredible experience in the garden listening to a Fado performance.  Beautiful secluded location with wine and a great representation of the music made popular by Amalia. Very moving experience!! || We visited Casa Amalia yesterday in Lisbon. It was interesting to discover the life of the Portuguese mist famous twentieth century artist. And we were lucky to attend a fado concert right after the visit. We highly recommend it. || I recently visited the Foundation Amália Rodrigues, and it was an incredibly moving experience. Housed in a charming pre‑Pombaline yellow building on Rua de São Bento, this museum was once the home of the legendary Fado singer Amália Rodrigues, known as the “Queen of Fado” .  Walking through the rooms felt intimate and personal. I admired her original furniture, portraits, stage dresses, and jewelry—every detail seemed frozen in time, offering a genuine glimpse into her life . The guided tour, enriched with fascinating stories about her career and the cultural context of Fado, deepened my appreciation of her legacy. || I enjoyed my tour with a member of staff but they could do with being more friendly. By the end I was being pressured constantly by a different woman by the till to attend a concert, which would have cost me extra. I managed to escape! (They don't have  control over my money!) I was also unsure about that parrot by itself making a huge noise that was unbearable for my ears. Was it a cry for help, a noise showing off, or a lonely depressed animal??? It definitely didn't sound happy. || They preserved all the furniture and the decorations as it was before ad this was amazing to feel that I go through the same way as Amalia did and see the same things. I was quiet interested about the details of her personal life as she grew and the guide  had absolute knowledge in details about her life. It was a pity that I could not take picture of inside the house as they did not allow it but only the reception and the yard was allowed. I highly recommend this museum especially for Fado lovers. The entrance is 6.5 euros and the discount is only for students under 25 years old. || My friend and I passed by on the bus, and I got curious, so we decided to learn more about Amália and visit her house. For €7/each, we got a guided tour of the house, and sat in the lovely garden. It was informative and we could even ask where to see a good Fado concert in the evening. I'd recommend going. It's not allowed to take pictures in the house. || This is a review of the concert in the garden. The concert lasted way too short, maybe 8 songs? It was pretty good, but didn't manage to pull me in because of the length. Somehow I expected it to last 1,5h while it lasted under an hour (including a break). || We went for the fado concert Saturday at 3:30, and is really worth it! Small concert, not crowded, you can also order a coffee, wine, anything while you are watching the performance. It is in the patio of the house so it's really nice, If you have fever you can buy the tickets there but I'm sure you can also buy them in the place. But do it in advance because there isn't a lot of people and it's full! If you don't know Portuguese don't worry about it, they will make you fill part and will do small intersections with the audience saying "now in English" but I don't want to spoiled anything more. Just go! || Excellent place! The house that she was living. There still have her perroquet in her kitchen. Chico (the perroquet name)appel her name with man's voice. So emotional when he call her.. The guide is nice. Take care of my questions. There is the garden, they are going to do the Fado live some time. || The place was full of history, the vibes were really there and Natalia's tour was full of emotions. || Very friendly and interesting displays of Amalia Rodrigues historical paraphernalia from her era. The coffee and cake, famously know as her favourite, was delicious! I am planning to see the Fado show this Saturday which will be nostalgic for me. The music my parents used to listen while growing up in Canada. || One of the best house-museum I have been. Good preserved. Tour guide lady was so nice, answered all questions. Price is 9 euros (for 2025). || Very good experience and nice guided tour. Pity one cannot take photographs. For sure it would increase the interest in visiting de museum. It was an intime visit to the soul of Amália. Congratulations! || It's very nice to see the real house with everything that she had. You can see the house with a guide who explains everything to you. || Genuine and calm, reasonable prices and amazing fado. Better than the touristy ones || Excellent experience with a very well informed guide. Every other day you can experience a fado concert in the garden. || Never visited before but I’m definitely want to . Beautiful house can’t wait to visit inside || Friendly staff, interesting and soulful tour, and fado evenings organised in the nice inner courtyard. Worth a visit.

reviews_content: Fantastic house full of history! Our guide was super lovely and she knew historic and artistic details that made the exhibition even better. 100% recommend if you like painting, furniture and ceramics from the 19th/20th century! ⭐️ || Dr. Anastácio Gonçalves House-Museum is a wonderful place to visit. The individual guided tour was excellent, with 45 minutes of pure enjoyment and plenty of new insights. A beautifully curated home filled with discoveries. Strongly recommended. || Very quiet and beautiful museum located at the centre of the city. No so many visitors so you could enjoy that fantastic paintings and porcelain feel like ur own collecting. The peoples who works there are full of passion and very friendly. The guy at ticket office explained everything to us. And the uncle working upstairs called Paulo, what an awesome person. He lead us visiting the everything and explained everything collection. We enjoy that very much. || Very eccellent experience. The receptionist at the entrance was brilliant, well-trained, and ready to explain and satisfy all  our curiosities about the museum. The Museum is well-kept and historically valid. Worth a visit. || Small house-museum belonging to the late Dr. António Anastácio Gonçalves, whose love for collecting historical artifacts led to the creation of the museum with an interesting number of paintings, oriental artifacts and furniture.  Worth a visit. || Very lovely museum! We went there a couple of weeks ago and had a great time. They have interesting paintings and furniture and a great exhibition on the history of the house itself. What made our stay extra pleasant was Paula, the receptionist who was one of the nicest people we met on our vacation to Portugal. She was very knowledgeable on the exhibition itself and gave us great advice on what to visit in Portugal. I would highly recommend it. || A very interesting, house museum set in a discrete corner of large avenues. A treasure for arts lovers with extraordinary collections of paintings of Dr Goncalves who was the third owner of this house (second was José Malhoa another famous Portuguese painter) : besides paintings (including "Spring" by Alfredo Keil, the composer of Portugal's National Anthem) you may admire religious artworks as well as rare Chinese jars.Visit all floors including the owner's apartment and the large upstairs luminous room where Dr Gonçalves kept his rich collection. A visit to be considered as a lovely step within past times. || Small museum in the former residence of Dr Gonçalves and an adjoining building.  The house dates to 1905 and has a few lovely stained glass windows from the time.  The period Portuguese and French furniture was also interesting, and decorated with a large collection of Chinese ceramics.  The guest experience would be much improved if the museum would simply identify the pieces in the collection with small labels, as a minority of pieces currently have any kind of description/label and very few paintings.  Lighting was also dim.  Additionally, a guide on each floor was assigned to visitors, which many may prefer.  But for a small group of 2, I found very distracting and disruptive when one of the guides kept drawing me away from the piece I was looking at to inspect something else... talking and asking rhetorical questions the whole time.  It prevents the visitor from having any sense of discovery or personal appreciation for the art.  It's obvious that the guides care a lot about the collection, but I wouldn't recommend this museum unless you are interested in something specific to the collection. || The guide/receptionist was incredibly nice and knowledgeable. The introduction was in English, so we were thankful. Also the information about all the art pieces had an English translation. Awesome experience. Beautiful paintings of the Naturalist period, Chinese porcelain/pottery from the 12th century! All displayed in a 'private' home. || Beautiful house, decor, and paintings from the period. It's nice to see how someone lived back then. Wonderful staff. I basically had a private tour and could ask whatever questions I wanted, and I could really take my time looking. || What a collection of Chinese porcelain and art along with furniture. || Unfriendly and very rude staff, especially the old woman at the reception. We booked Lisbon Winery based upon the strong recommendation of travel author Rick Steves. Unfortunately, our experience fell short of what we usually expect from Rick's suggestions. Our disappointment was not with the charcuterie board or the wines poured for us, which were all delicious and generously served. Instead, we felt that the service we received was cool and unfriendly to an unacceptable degree. The food and wine were all presented with a well-rehearsed script, but we found it difficult to ask questions or learn more about what was given to us. Our server seemed disinterested and tried to disengage with us at the earliest opportunity. We believe that we were friendly and relaxed, so I'm not sure why we were treated this way. We simply wanted to learn a little more and expected that the staff would be happy to share their love of Portuguese food and wine. Our visit was in the afternoon and there were only a few other customers present, so it was hardly a busy environment. In fact, our server seemed to enjoy chatting with another couple and he spent far more time with them. We also experienced a woman come into the Winery about half-way through our visit who brought a barking dog with them into the space where we were eating and drinking. The staff seemed to know her, and they chatted with her for about 10 or 15 minutes before the woman and her dog left. By the time we finished, we left feeling that the staff of Lisbon Winery couldn't have cared less about our experience and wishing we had spent our time differently. || Thank you, Kenneth, for taking the time to share your feedback.  My name is Alex, and I am the co-owner of Lisbon Winery. I’m truly sorry that your experience didn’t meet the high expectations you had. If a guest leaves less than delighted, it means we still have room to grow, and I sincerely appreciate the chance to reflect and improve.  That said, I’d like to clarify a few points about your visit:  1. Regarding the presentation and “script”: Our wine and charcuterie selection changes daily — sometimes even during the day — depending on availability, temperature, pairings and guest's preferences. Because of that, no two tastings are ever the same, and there is certainly no pre-established “script.” Our sommeliers speak from knowledge and passion, not memorization. I’m sorry if it felt otherwise during your experience. Sharing the stories of small, independent Portuguese producers is at the heart of what we do and has been the foundation of our more than 2,000 five-star reviews.  2. About the service and attention: I was present during your tasting and observed our sommelier presenting your wines, grapes, wine regions, olive oils, and pairings with his usual enthusiasm and professionalism. From my perspective, he was not unfriendly and was attentive. Of course, every table and tasting is unique — for example, the other couple you mentioned was experiencing a Port tasting, which naturally follows a different rhythm and pacing. Counting minutes of interaction isn’t really the spirit of hospitality we believe in; instead, our focus is on quality, not quantity, of engagement.  3. Regarding the dog: It’s true that a customer briefly came to the deck with a small dog, which is permitted under Portuguese law. The dog remained on the deck, a specific area completely separate from the food and wine area, as per our internal rules. The barking lasted just a few moments, and I personally went to calm the animal. It was me, the owner, and not the staff, that spent some time talking with the lady, who is a customer, like you and came to buy wine. So, once again, not giving more attention to this customer than to you as our sommelier was available in exclusive for both tables in the room.  We understand that every guest has different expectations and sensitivities, and we take all feedback seriously. Our team will keep working hard to offer great experiences. We’ll continue to improve and to stand by the warmth and authenticity that define Lisbon Winery. || Ironically, the low-rated reviews made me want to visit this place. The premium wine tasting costs €85 with an online reservation, but walking in was €95. I assume the extra charge was because I wasn’t part of a group, but paying the additional €10 ended up feeling worth it. They offered three types of local olive oil, a wide range of regional ham and cheese, and small-batch local wines. I hadn’t eaten dinner beforehand, but the amount of food they served was more than enough. The portions of cheese and ham were so generous that I regretted leaving some behind. My companion doesn’t enjoy Port wine, so we asked to switch to red wine, and they kindly accommodated the request. The only minor downside was that English isn’t my first language, and after the third glass, the alcohol made it harder to follow the explanations. Obviously, that’s not the venue’s fault. If you want a solid introduction to premium Portuguese wine, I recommend visiting this place. || Thank you, Luna, for reviewing us. We are really glad you have trusted us.
