The team is awesome too – really welcoming and fun to hang out with. Definitely one of the best drink spot I’ll keep coming back to❤️🙏 || Nastya thank you so much! Great pictures. It was amazing to host you. We agree on the Negroni part || Met some friends at cabal on a Tuesday and we couldn’t have had a better experience. We were looking forward to try the cocktails and treated ourselves with six different options to try.  All of them were honestly great , but if you’d like some ideas, here’s my review of the ones suggested by the barman: - o.f.martini - my favourite; sweat and sour at the same time, perfect taste, served with gummies, 10/10 - old fashioned Portuguese - stronger taste but not overwhelming, definetly try if you’re into “bolder” flavors, - rooibos spritz - if you’re not a fan of aperol spritz like me then this is the perfect alternative, fruity , fresh, not too intense, really liked it  To make it better, the DJ had the perfect set for the occasion, chilled but you could move a little to it if you’d like, and the ambience just feels welcoming overall.  We’ll definitely come back!!  🥰 || Loved the pictures! Thank you so much || I absolutely love this bar! I have been in the city for a while now and this is one of the coolest bars in town. Great environment, spacious, beautiful drinks, easy access and good music. The cocktails are tasty, creative and fun! || Thank you Rafaela! It's an honor || Cabal Cocktail Bar is one of those places that quietly exceeds every expectation. From the moment you walk in, you can tell this isn’t your average cocktail spot — it’s got that perfect blend of sophistication and comfort. The lighting is warm and atmospheric, the music hits that sweet spot where you can still hold a conversation, and the staff immediately make you feel welcome without being intrusive.  The cocktail menu is outstanding — creative without being pretentious. Every drink feels carefully balanced and thoughtfully crafted. I had the whiskey sour. My friend tried the Hugo, and it was easily one of the best floral cocktails I’ve ever tasted (and I’ve tried a lot!). You can tell the bartenders here are true mixologists who take pride in what they do.  What really stood out, though, was the service. Our bartender took time to ask about our flavor preferences and then offered a few off-menu recommendations that were spot on. It felt personal and genuine, not rehearsed. Even when the bar got busy later in the evening, the team stayed attentive and upbeat — you could feel that they actually enjoy what they do.  The ambiance also deserves a mention: stylish decor, a bit of a speakeasy vibe, and a nice mix of people — perfect for date nights, small groups, or anyone who appreciates a good drink in a relaxed setting.  Prices are fair for the quality you get, and honestly, I’d come back just for the experience. If you’re into crafted cocktails, great energy, and a place that treats its guests like regulars from the first visit — Cabal is absolutely worth it. || Wow Dorian, you basically wrote a book here. Thank you so much for such level of detail, and for the amazing review. Come back soon! || We visited Cabal yesterday and really enjoyed this experience. The place has stylish vibe with great attention to detail in the interior and lighting. The cocktails were beautifully made and tasted amazing.  The Coffee Negroni was a real surprise for me – I had never tried anything like this before, and it quickly became my favorite of the night. You should try!! Service was friendly and professional, and the whole experience felt relaxed but special. It’s your sing to visit Cabal if you looking for unique cocktail spot🥰 || Thank you Diana for such an amazing review! Loved the pictures and yeah, the coffee Negroni is quite nice indeed || Excellent bar, well managed and sophisticated, yet casual and friendly. Professional, welcoming staff. Features a spacious elevated patio area to enjoy Lisbon evenings. While they provide nice bar snacks, it’s not a dedicated restaurant as such, but simply a great place to go for a drink or a few drinks. || Thank you for such review, David! Really. We hope to see you soon || This is definitely the best cocktail bar I’ve been to in Lisbon! The drinks were all so delicious, especially the Rooibos Spritz and OF Martini, and it’s super central with a lovely patio. Would recommend going a bit later for more vibes, but overall amazing service and such a fun night out! || Wow Cassidy thank you so much! We're glad you liked our cocktails. We 100% agree with your choice || Super cool vibes with a spacious terrace perfect for chilling! The DJ inside kept the energy just right with great music. Loved their creative cocktails—tried the Panther Martini with pickle (so intriguing 👀) and the Rooibos Spritz, which was my absolute favorite. Everything was delicious and very affordable. Definitely a spot worth visiting! || Such a great review Jade, thanks! We totally agree with you on the Rooibos Spritz! It's a must-have

A wonderful example of a well-maintained and carefully renovated Gothic cathedral. The Sé de Lisboa dates back to 1147, with construction completed around the 13th century, making it the oldest church in Lisbon.  You can really feel the history here, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic elements shaped over centuries. It’s not overly grand or touristy, just authentic and atmospheric.  Definitely worth taking some time to visit when you’re in the city — a quiet, impressive place right in the heart of Lisbon. || Oldest church in the city (1147). Gorgeous catholic cathedral and a must visit. Very cool to be able to go up in the old choir loft  and especially outside by the large stained glass window on the front of the cathedral. There was a short line when I went on a weekday, so you may want to buy tickets in advance for a weekend, cruise ship port day, or high season. I was disappointed that the cloisters were closed when I went. || Beautiful and historic place in the heart of Alfama. The cathedral feels ancient and peaceful inside, with thick stone walls and soft light coming through the windows. I loved seeing the mix of old architecture and history all around. Even from the outside, it’s impressive — especially when the tram passes by. Definitely worth a short visit while exploring Lisbon. || The cathedral was absolutely breathtaking. There is still an admission fee, but you get a discount with the Lisboa Card, which helps. As you enter, you go up the stairs to the treasure room. On the way up, make sure to notice the carved cross on the stairs, said to have been made by Saint Anthony to repel the devil during his studies.  The artifacts in the treasure room are beautifully detailed and very well preserved. From there, you can access the interior balcony, which offers a great view of the main church below and a close look at the stunning stained glass centerpiece. There’s also a small passage leading to an exterior balcony overlooking the front of the cathedral, though it’s quite narrow and can get crowded. It’s a tight squeeze, one-way, and very high up, so just take care if you’re not great with heights.  The main cathedral itself is massive, with chapels dedicated to different saints along the back. The whole place feels grand and full of history.  Overall, an incredible experience and definitely a must-see when visiting Lisbon. || The oldest and most iconic church in Lisbon, full of history and charm. The architecture is impressive, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. Inside it’s peaceful and beautifully lit, offering a quiet break from the busy streets. Climb up to see the cloisters and enjoy the view of Alfama. A must-visit for history and architecture lovers || We took the classic yellow #28 tram and got off at the Se. The area is very cute with many great photo opportunities. We also had brunch at a sidewalk cafe in the small square right before the Se. It’s worth a visit for the views. || ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Lisbon's spiritual heavyweight champion since 1147 ⛪ Plot twist: you absolutely should go inside this magnificent cathedral, and here's the best part - it's completely free! No tickets, no queues, just walk right in like you own the place (which, in a way, we all do). The Sé de Lisboa isn't just "a church like all the churches" - it's THE church, Lisbon's oldest and most historically significant. The Romanesque fortress-like exterior might look a bit stern and businesslike, but step inside and you're hit with centuries of Portuguese history. The Gothic cloisters are genuinely stunning, and if you're lucky enough to catch evening light streaming through those rose windows, you'll understand why people have been coming here to feel something greater for nearly 900 years. The treasury and archaeological remains are worth exploring if you have time, but honestly, just sitting quietly in the main nave for a few minutes costs nothing and gives you everything. The acoustics are incredible if you catch a service or choir practice. Pro tip: Combine with a wander through Alfama afterwards - you're perfectly positioned for the neighbourhood's winding charm. Historic, free, and utterly peaceful. What's not to love? 🕊️✨ || Dear Tom, thank you for visiting, and we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience. We hope you can return one day to visit the museum and other corners of the monument. || The architecture is impressive, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. The treasury upstairs is interesting. Paintings are fabulous. The views from the top are spectacular! || Well worth the ticket price and the time to explore. Don’t miss the area upstairs where the vestments are- I’m fascinated by the detailed stitching even on the shoes! The cathedral is beautiful and there is information on its history available even if you elect not to get the audio guide. || Santa Maria Maior is the kind of place that makes you fall in love with Lisbon almost instantly. It’s the heart of the city — full of charm, history, and little surprises around every corner. Wandering through its narrow streets, you go from lively plazas to quiet alleyways, all wrapped in that classic Lisbon mix of energy and old-world beauty.  You’ve got iconic Lisbon landmarks all within a short walk — the Sé Cathedral, the viewpoints in Alfama, Praça do Comércio, and the buzzing streets of Baixa and Chiado. But what really sticks with you is the atmosphere: the tiled facades, the sound of trams passing by, and the tiny cafés where you can stop for a pastel de nata and just soak it all in.  It’s vibrant without being overwhelming, historic without feeling like a museum, and genuinely one of the best areas to explore if you want to experience Lisbon’s soul up close. || What a gem of a place that I walked into while taking the tram 28 route. Such great architecture inside the church and the tile work was very intricate and unique which truly identifies Lisbon || We went on a Saturday and they happen to be holding a mass, which was a great time to visit. The ticket counter was closed due to the mass so they were not selling tickets but allowed access. Pretty neat to see a full functioning catholic cathedral in action with all of its ornate architecture and items. || The Lisbon Cathedral is the oldest church in the city and a prominent symbol of Portugal's history, showcasing a blend of Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque architectural styles. It's free for the visit of the Cathedral but you need to pay for the museum tour. || The cathedral is a worth seeing part of the historic landmarks in Lisbon. I've been to a lot similar sights all across Europe and I can't say that it is amongst the most spectacular but it is still very interesting, also one of the oldest. It is also sometimes open to the public for free and during the weekend. || Beautiful cathedral with a long history. Also, the turn outside the church is a perfect spot to take pictures of tram 28. || This is an amazing church to check out. I would recommend paying the small entrance fee of $7 euros I believe. You get to see so much more and it is so worth it. I am always memorized by the architecture. I am not religious and I truly enjoyed this powerful place. || The Lisbon Cathedral is absolutely worth a visit. It’s one of the oldest and most important landmarks in the city, with a mix of Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles that really tell the story of Lisbon’s history. The outside is impressive, but the inside feels even more special – calm, quiet, and filled with beautiful details. If you have time, go into the cloisters as well, where you can see layers of history all in one place. It’s right in the Alfama district, so you can easily walk around the old streets after your visit. Definitely recommend stopping by, even if just for a short visit. || A must visit place in Lisbon. You can enter freely as a prayer (stopping by the entrance) or go for a ticket to explore the entire church, including the museum in the first floor and the terrace in front of the plaza. It is a wonderful mixup of different styles, from Romanic to Gothic, with several additions in the following centuries. || The tower was unfortunately closed off, so we could not go up. You can still go outside on a short passageway, just under the central stained glass window, and the views of the city is beautiful. Overall, it was worth paying the entrance fee to go upstairs, see the museum section. More information in English would be helpful for visitors who don't speak Portuguese. By pure coincidence, while visiting the church, two man started playing/practicing the organ, it was beautiful. || Exactly what we expected before coming. We can feel the power of Jesus Christ covering the church. Something reminds us of Dark Souls, the game that we played together, its inspired by ancient Europeans civilization. || Dear Daud, we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience and that it brought back fond memories. Thank you very much for your feedback.

One of the highlights of Estrela. One of the main Lisbon churches due to its size and beauty. You can visit for free but you'll need to pay to go to the rooftop. Beautiful paintings that contribute to the espiritual experience. Parking available just next to the church but it's usually quite full. You can also visit the park just across the street. A metro station is being built which will make it more accessible. || You can pay 5 € to walk up to the roof top. 20% off with Lisboa card and a million steps. The view is amazing. You also get to see inside of the basilica from the top- close to the dome. Also- Jesus dine with the 12 around a round table. || It is an absolute must see! One of the prettiest Basilicas we've visited. And we were able to access the roof and walk around the inside of the church from above and look down into the sanctuary. Absolutely gorgeous! || The interior is splendid. The ceiling, dome and floor are colorful. Paintings are fabulous. The ambience is serene. || The inside of the cathedral is free and breathtaking. there is a core beam of light that shines on you like a spot light for judgement of course.  For the bathroom. You need exact 0.50€ to use it and the post cards are exactly 0.50€ if you need change. I did the €5 climb which was not worth so buy the postcard instead and enjoy a clean private wc. The light goes off automatically but I just used my phone flashlight.  Update: I walked across the street to the Jardin and there is a free bathroom in the “casa de jardin estrella”. Do that. || Very ancient Basilica. It was indeed an Awesome Place, a must visit Place in Lisbon. It is a silent place to be with God. || After years of passing by outside, finally went in and was pleasantly surprised. It is not a giant cathedral, but it has enough of an imposing presence to allow one to appreciate the multiple altars and cruciform architecture. Also a pleasant surprise came in the form of the possibility of climbing to the rooftop from where you can have a look around the area at a very budget friendly price. Just be sure to be away from the belltowers when the full set goes off at, for example, 11:50 on a Sunday morning. || Known for its beautiful dome and interior, the Basílica da Estrela is one of Lisbon's most impressive monuments. The Basílica da Estrela in Lisbon was the first church in the world dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, built by Queen Maria I, and houses her tomb. It is also known for its large dome that dominates the Lisbon skyline, a remarkable baroque nativity scene, and its impressive neoclassical architecture. || I like to recommend everyone to visit this place it’s very peaceful n nice food with handmade dumpling thank u || Very beautiful and peaceful interior to the church. The floor of the church is particularly stunning in its design. We paid the 5 euros each to go to the rooftop. It was pleasant but for us, not worth the price.  Much prefer the pantheon rooftop.  The climb via a narrow spiral staircase is quite steep with just enough room to pass people - it is fun to go up. The view from the rooftop is nice and the dome is beautiful (you can see it close up from access from the rooftop terrace - mind your head going in 🤕)

place_name: Church Nossa Senhora da Conceição Velha
reviews_content: A truly beautiful church tucked away on a quiet side street, yet just a short walk from Praça do Comércio. Nossa Senhora da Conceição has been masterfully renovated. The entrance features wonderful carvings that immediately draw you in, and once inside, you’re greeted by a stunning stucco-decorated ceiling that takes your breath away. A hidden gem worth discovering when exploring the city! || We were in Lisbon na at our cruise for 6 days. Walking back to our ship one day we found this old church which had to be restored after a large fire.  It is quiet and peaceful so stop and say a prayer for the poor people of the world while you rest your feet.  Not too much to see as compared to the larger churches around town. Still, it is very nice and worth a visit. || The Igreja da Conceição Velha has one of the most beautiful examples of Manueline architecture in Portugal. I believe the original interior of the church was destroyed during the Great Earthquake of Lisbon. Even so, admiring its façade alone makes the visit worthwhile. Pay special attention to the intricate carvings on the main doorway — they are truly remarkable. || A beautiful and peaceful church with elegant architecture and a calming atmosphere.  The interior is simple yet charming, offering a quiet break from the busy streets.  A lovely spot to pause and appreciate Lisbon’s history and spiritual charm. || Please visit this beautiful church, especially go the Holy Mass if you are a traditional catholic because the Masses are in Latin. Be aware that the information about the Mass at church is wrong. Just check on the internet. Sundays and holy days of obligation  - 10AM and 6PM,  Tuesdays till Fridays  - 7 p.m. and Saturdays  - 10:30 am. || One of the facades to survive the All Saints Day earth quake of 1755 and the following tsunami; certainly worth a quick stop or, at the very least, a quick walk by. || Tucked away in Lisbon’s Baixa district, the Church of Nossa Senhora da Conceição Velha stuns with its richly carved Manueline façade — a survivor of the 1755 earthquake. Step inside to discover peaceful interiors, gothic arches, and echoes of Portugal’s maritime past in every stone. || Mass is at 10 am on Sundays in a beautiful old church A very interesting mass, very beautiful, but no interaction with the congregation at all. It was almost like watching a play! || Didn’t actually go inside but the architecture outside is a sight worth seeing . || This is truly a magnificent religious space. The Facade could keep you enthralled for a while, and the inside will astound with its very high, ornate ceiling. It was a privilege to look inside || The exterior looks promising, welcoming you to its historical inside warmly.  The Church of Nossa Senhora da Conceição is a church in the civil parish of Madalena, in the municipality of Lisbon. The Church of Conceição dos Freires, or Conceição Velha, was not included in the original plans to reconstruct the Lisbon riverfront, even though it was partially ruined. It was opened in 1834, with a height of 17m. || Nice facade. Humble and not overly complicated on the inside. Only a few minutes walk from the Commerce Plaza. || Beautiful and detailed  architecture on the outside.  The inside has a beautiful roof mural. || Very nice facade from 16th century that survived the earthquake with restored interior in late baroque style. || It is a place where you can find the Manueline style in Baixa. If you don’t have time to go all the way to Belem, check out this place instead not to miss out the unique architecture in the Era of Discovery. || A great place to reverently worship God in accordance with His Will. || I liked this old church, looks a bit Gothic from outside and more traditional inside. The architecture is beautiful. || Recently reopened for visits. Compared to striking outside, inside a little disapointing, but still not to be missed || Very nice church, with beautiful facade. Short walk east of the Praça do Comércio. || the interior may not be of particular interest, but the facade is certainly impressive

place_name: Church of Our Lady of the Rosary of Fatima
reviews_content: Church of Our Lady the Rosary of Fatima in Lisbon was consecrated in 1938. It's a mixture of modern and traditional architecture. Inside are mosaics and colorful stained glass windows. Especially the stained windows behind the choir are quite impressive, with depictions of saints and angels. The church is still in use as such, but respectful visitors are welcomed. There is no charge. Also, at times, there are free concerts in the church. || There is a beautiful painting at the top, showing the Arca Salvifica, but other than that this church isn't very interesting. || Modern church.  Clean lines.  Stained glass that shines we'll inside.  Unique sidewalk tiles. || See it for yourself! Amazing vibe and healing factors mixed up || What a beautiful Church we attended 2 Mass Services Not to be repetitive but so beautiful, very different to back home || Very Beautiful and Religious place to visit. I feel very relaxed and calm at this place. || Lovely church and the choir were absolutely amazing and there were only 4/5 members singing a cappella worth going just to listen to them at 10.30 mass on Sunday. || Nice church for a quick stop if you are in the area. We passed it on our way to a museum close by. Check the opening times first. || November 2024 - Lisbon Sings. I've never felt this way before. I've never been closer to Him. This Church will forever remain a sanctuary to me. || Fabulous catholic church in Lisbon with a shrine of Our Lady of Fatima. It's one of the two Jubilar Churches in Lisbon. || A modern church compared to most Portuguese churches, it was completed in the mid-nineteen thirties. Nonetheless it's very beautiful. I prefer the proper candles over Led ones but it's the thought and prayer that counts. Nice strained glass windows. || The experience was beautiful, I had the opportunity to listen to a choirs concert and it was majestic || Very beautiful church.  I misread the Internet. I thought it said the Sat night mass@1900 was in English. It was in Portuguese 🙏.  All is well. We. Attended mass, we followed along in the Magnificat, and received communion. I am sure the Homily was excruciating. || It's a beautiful church. || Unbelievably beautiful church, despite it being of the brutalist era of architecture. Entirely legible church although modern with amazing stations, lovely altar, beautiful hand carved nativity scene.  Became our spiritual home away from home during our WYD Lisbon 2023 stay. Would love to come back some day! || Beautiful church in Lisbon. Beautiful windows! || For a relatively modern church, it is quite beautiful. || Great moments on Sunday morning with my loved one on the right place. || A beautiful modern church. || Visiting Fatima was a once in a lifetime experience. I’m so happy my group found a day in our WYD schedule to go in visit and explore the area. 10/10 would recommend to anyone visiting Portugal to go and see Our Lady of Fatima.

place_name: Church of Our Lady of the Angels⛪
reviews_content: A beautiful church to visit. There is a terrace at the top (additional cost) for some wonderful views of Lisbon || Evening visit. Very nice church. || Beautiful church. And the community of faithful seemed very close-knit. If I move here, I'd want to be part of this community. I couldn't understand the priest's homily (I have yet to learn the Portuguese language), but he seemed like an eloquent speaker. St John Chrysostom, pray for him!🙂🙏🏼  There was at least a 10am Mass on Sunday. || Very easy to find.  Beautiful gold-edged altar.   Masses held every day at 6.30 pm (including Sunset mass on Saturday). .10.30 am mass on Sunday. I suppose all are in Portuguese.   I attended two evening masses.  Hail Mary or Hymn for Mary sang after each mass. || Incredible beauty! What a sculptors inside!! Thank you for free entry 🙏 … || I attended a Sunday service of the Eucharist.  A truly beautiful church and clearly a very respected & well liked priest || The Catholic Church is located very well. This is the place, you should never miss to visit from inside. I really appreciate the Art. :) || Seems to be closed.  Went to visit after 10am on a Thursday. Only some bums sitting on the front steps. Doors locked. Same situation a few days earlier. || Really enjoyed alot visiting such a wonderful place with great  architecture. || Good old quiet church to sit and review the day and be with the lord. || Worst church-bell-rythm-melody ever! 😈 … || Traditional and Historical. || Old church in Portugal || A small church on the main avenue that passes through Anjos. The Church of Anjos combines simplicity and elegance. With a neoclassical facade and welcoming interior, it is a haven of peace in the city. Highlights include the beautiful stained glass windows and serene atmosphere. A historic site with strong ties to the local community and Marian devotion. || Currently, the Church of Our Lady of the Angels is undergoing exterior renovations. The church is very beautiful! || The Parish Church of Our Lady of the Angels, also known as the "Church of the Angels," was originally a place for parish services and was once located in Regueirão dos Anjos. In 1568, this church existed under the invocation of Our Lady of the Angels, although the ecclesiastical parish had been created in 1563 by Cardinal D. Henrique. In 1758, it underwent restoration and expansion works due to the 1755 earthquake. On January 11, 1908, the "Church of the Angels" was demolished to make way for Avenida D. Amélia (now Avenida Almirante Reis), according to city improvement plans. However, it was rebuilt on the western side of the then Avenida D. Amélia, with the architect José Luís Monteiro respecting the proportions and incorporating the entire interior of the original church, giving it only a more neoclassical character. On March 11, 1910, the Parish Church of Our Lady of the Angels was thus inaugurated in its new and current location. || Initially, the Church of the Angels was located in the Vale de São Jordão, now Regueirão dos Anjos, occupying the space that today faces the Nortel café (formerly Ribatejano café), and the part of the block on Avenida Almirante Reis that goes up to the north. At that time, it was a church dependent on the parish of Santa Justa, which extended from Rossio to the vicinity of Areeiro, encompassing adjacent farms and fields.  This church, which had undergone improvements in 1958, was ruined by the 1755 earthquake and restored in 1758. || It was closed; you need to update the visiting hours because Google said it was open. || The church is beautiful, but I went to the one next door at AIMA.

place_name: Church of Our Lady of the Incarnation
reviews_content: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Encarnação is well worth a visit if you want to see Lisbon beyond the main touristic landmarks. It is in the center and offers a calm space. … || Beautiful church, rebuild after the 1755 earthquake. Classicism/baroque style. Elaborate, colorful decorations painted on the ceiling, arches with statues of saints along both sides of the interior. Accessible for wheelchairs! Open most … || Nice and huge church. Many small altars dedicated to saints and roof paintings. || A calm spiritual place to sit and reflect about life || There are several interesting churches you can visit in the Chiado neighbourhood including the Church of Our Lady of the Incarnation (Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Encarnação) located at Largo de Chiado and Largo Luis de Camões. … || Beautiful peaceful church || Glad.to have 5.30pm.mass sunday here. And its english good for tourist like me || Happened to have found one of the few churches in Lisbon with English mass in the afternoon. Very tranquil atmosphere and connected with friendly faithfuls 🫶🏽 … || It was tagged as the best church in Lisbon. It was a great place of reflection. We arrived there around 12:30 and they were closing. || Yet another outstanding catholic monument, gorgeous oasis above the Praça || Such a peaceful church, just look at the photos of the interior, words alone cannot do it justice. Probably largely unchanged through the generations. The fairly ordinary portico front facade hides a gem within, well worth a visit. Please don't forget to leave a donation. || One of many beautiful churches in the Chiado neighbourhood. || This church has a very profound energy, to the point that I felt a bit uncomfortable. It’s quite beautiful, but I couldn’t stay in there very long. It’s very quiet inside, which is a big contrast to the hustle and bustle of the Chiado outside. Definitely worth going to take a peek. || Super 3D realistic paintings || Big and very busy artwork. Not peaceful and one could wonder how someone prays here || Just Beautiful and Awesome! One of the few reasons of being proud to live in Portugal: our Dedication to The Virgin Mary with our Beautiful Churches. Just sitting inside is Mesmerising! || This is a beautiful church dedicated to Our Lady of the Incarnation, which is the name given to Mary, mother of Jesus, in allusion to the incarnation of her son. It certainly deserves a visit. Inside, over the chancel altarpiece, there's a … || Igreja da Nossa Senhora da Encarnação, like so many other churches in this part of the Portuguese capital, was completely destroyed by the earthquake of 1755. It was subsequently rebuilt under the direction of the architect Manuel Caetano … || Beautiful church. Wish there were labels for each statues || Astonishing baroque interiors. Great ceiling painting by by Simon Caetano Nunes. Don’t forget to visit a little hall to the right side door. Great art works!

This church is different from most in Lisbon. In 1959, a large fire destroyed the roof and many wooden parts. The heat was so strong that the stone columns cracked and turned black. You can still see the damage today. The church was not fully restored on purpose. The scars were left as a reminder of what happened, instead of being hidden. It is simple, quiet, and very powerful — a place that shows history exactly as it is. || We were walking around Lisbon exploring all the sights for several days while we were waiting to join our cruise. We passed by this church and went inside to explore.  It was very old and very beautiful.  So ornate especially behind the alter. Please note that the base 13th century church has been rebuilt several times over the centuries due to fires and earthquakes. Many tourists were there taking pictures along with a lot of worshippers.  A very peaceful place in the middle of a busy city. || Old church with special legacy but forsaken by caring elites some.time.ago and badly needs renovating - about to start. Very unique style circle within circle. Very spiritual I felt. Had a volunteer lady assisting who was devout and delightful humour. A visit for heartfelt comforting of the soul. || Igreja de São Domingos – Lisbon. - Is a symbol of resilience, uniquely displaying the "scars" of the 1959 fire and earlier earthquakes, which gives its restored interior a haunting and powerful atmosphere. Despite multiple devastating events, it has been repeatedly rebuilt and reopened, preserving its complex history within its architecture and decorative styles. || Fabulous church with an astonishing story. Earthquakes, fire, you name it, this church has gone through a lot over the centuries! A must stop in Lisbon as the architecture of this church is simply amazing. || Very nice Church and place of worship, very old (dedicated in 1241) and damaged by various earthquakes, yet still standing with almost all the original glorious splendor of past centuries. The red ceiling is quite symbolic, together with the stones of the floor. I went early to the 6:00PM Mass and 15 minutes before it began, there were still plenty of tourists taking pictures and speaking loud. But as the Mass time got close, the temple got the silence proper for prayer and recollection of religious people. The liturgy was beautiful, with the proper dignity. The Basilica history dates back to the reconquest of Lisbon in 1147, when a chapel was built here to house the image of the Virgin carried by English crusaders. The chapel was given the name Our Lady of the Martyrs in memory of all European soldiers who died in retaking the city and defending the Christian faith. You'll find subtle Baroque exterior along with a nicely decorated interior. The nave is lined side alters and fronted by an impressive main alter. Great gameplay, no glitches, feels like you’re really there in a huge environment. It’s a really fun workout too. Do it!!! || What an experience! Even for my 2, 4, 6 year olds! Super friendly team, accommodating and engaging. He setup my kids perfectly, and as you can imagine, almost impossible to get them out there || Thank you so much Dawid! Your kids were amazing players and we totally get how hard it is to get them to leave. 😄 Hope to see you all again! 🚀  … || Possibly the coolest experience I have ever had!! Staff is super friendly, the games were so much fun (we booked one hour and got to play two games), definitely felt like a real life experience! The games were not only from simple to complex but also have so many different options where you can even play in teams with or against each other! I definitely would do this again!! Most definitely is the highlight of our holiday in Lisbon! || I love virtual games, so I was looking for a place to play in Lisbon. I signed up for a game during happy hour. I liked the location and service. The employee was friendly and kind and he helped me understand rules of games || Everyone should try it! We played 2 games - one was escape room, the other one was with zombies, both were really interesting and brought a lot of fun and suspense! The host was very passionate and kind. I truly recommend it to everyone! || Thank you all so much for making my son's birthday so special! The virtual reality experience was a huge hit—everyone had such a blast, and the kids couldn’t stop talking about it. We even went twice because it was that much fun! || I took my nephew to this experience, and was good fun, we went for half an hour to kill zombies. Nice people on site, tbh the graphics weren’t amazing but they supposed to do some game better, they also provide footage after the game, I will go again. || What an awesome family experience x definitely a great experience for friends and families wanting to have an awesome time together for beginners and experienced players || Thank you so much, Esther! 😊 We’re happy to hear your family had an amazing time. We hope to see you again for more VR fun soon! 🚀  …

reviews_content: Eduardo VII Park is one of the most beautiful and relaxing green spaces in Lisbon. The park offers stunning panoramic views over the city and the Tagus River, making it a perfect spot for photos, walks, or simply enjoying the scenery. The wide paths are ideal for walking or jogging, and the well-maintained gardens add a peaceful atmosphere away from the busy city streets. One of the highlights is the impressive geometric garden design and the viewpoint at the top of the park, which provides a breathtaking perspective of Lisbon. The park is also very spacious, so it never feels overcrowded, even during busy hours. There are benches throughout the area, perfect for resting and enjoying the surroundings. Eduardo VII Park is great for families, couples, and solo travelers alike. It’s close to the city center and easy to access, making it a must-visit for anyone exploring Lisbon. Whether you’re looking for a quiet place to relax, take a walk, or admire the city from above, this park is definitely worth a visit. || We were in Lisbon for several days while waiting to start a cruise with NCL.  We stopped at the north end of this magnificent park and walk all the way to the southern end.  Lots of great views and spots for wonderful pics.  Several monuments along the way. || Parque Eduardo VII is a beautiful park with stunning views of the city and the river. It's beautifully maintained, with plenty of greenery and spacious walkways. It's a great place to escape the hustle and bustle of the city, take beautiful photos, and simply enjoy the atmosphere. A must-see if you're in Lisbon. || It's quite an amazing space. Whether it's chilling, or events, or testing your photographic prowess, it fits the bill. There are usually tourists and residents generally around, and it's more lively during celebrations like Christmas. || It's a very beautiful and large park, perfect for a peaceful walk surrounded by nature. The view from the top of the park is spectacular. Depending on the time of year, there may be more or fewer tourists. On a sunny day with good weather, it's well worth a visit. || A great view of Lisbon from here, you can see the whole layout and scale looking down towards the river. Relaxed and friendly atmosphere as you view the scenery and monuments. You also get an excellent view of the planes coming into Lisbon. || A beautiful public park in Lisbon, Portugal with great views over the city. The top is great for photos. Good for a walk, sit and have lunch or a drink, or have your dog play around. || Wonderful Christmas Atmosphere! We visited Parque Eduardo VII during the Christmas season, and it was a fantastic experience. The Christmas market (Wonderland Lisboa) created such a pleasant and fun atmosphere. It’s a great spot, especially for young people and families, with plenty of amusement park rides, games, and festive food stalls. The park itself is beautiful, and the view from the top is breathtaking. Highly recommended if you are in Lisbon during the holidays! || Parque Eduardo VII is one of the best spots in Lisbon to enjoy a peaceful walk and take in a great view of the city. From the top of the park, you can see all the way down to the river and the Praça Marquês de Pombal. It’s a lovely place to relax, especially at sunset. The park is also very close to El Corte Inglés, so it’s easy to combine a visit with some shopping or a coffee break nearby. || What a great parque / jardim in central Lisbon. Plenty of spaces to walk and sit with many great restaurants, cafes , and quiosques nearby to enjoy the warm Lisbon sun || Iconic park in central Lisbon. You can get the hop on bus at this location or just walk all the way up from the roundabout to get a nice view of the city and take a picture near a Lisboa sign. || A beautiful park! You can exercise, enjoy nature, and relax. It’s very well maintained! || Beautiful lookout over the city towards the water. If you like vistas, definitely a must see. Also check the smaller part of the park across the road (more north), for a super cute cafe near a small pond. || It is a beautiful public park in Lisbon, Portugal. The park occupies an area of 26 hectares (64 acres). The park was built in the first half of the 20th century to restore public green space. The park's central strip, covered with grass, is flanked by long Portuguese paved walkways. The park is at a gradient from the top observation deck you can see it well. Well manicured lawns and hedges. The top of the park is a has the Monument to the Carnation Revolution, flanked by two sets of two obelisks. Car park nearby and easy walk to observation deck. Wear comfy shoes, take water, wear hat, sunscreen. Great place for photography || Very large sloping park mainly put over to trees and grass. Lovely view from the top across the city. Interesting sculpture here too. || Scenic views with many diverse places to sun, shade, relax and explore. Bonus that buildings include the Carlos Lopes Pavilion, restaurants and world class arboretum inside the grounds || Beautiful monument in this lovely park and long Avenue which can be admired from top and bottom.  On a nice day can see far away. || This turned out to be an unexpected city walk.This park is great for a stroll and offers views of much of the Lisbon! There are also orange trees and a small amusement area inside, and it might be even livelier if you come in the evening. || This is the largest park in Lisbon, named in honor of King Edward VII of the United Kingdom following his visit to Portugal in 1903. It features formal gardens, greenhouses, and wide open paths—making it ideal for walking, relaxing, or simply enjoying nature in the city. At the top of the park, a scenic viewpoint offers sweeping views over Lisbon and the Tagus River. The park is also home to the annual Lisbon Book Fair, one of the city’s most popular cultural events. || Super views over Lisbon. Good for a walk around if that’s what you want plus photos at the top of the park. Well looked after.

An amazing amusement park near Lisbon's main landmarks. Easy to find, with great facilities and affordable prices. The staff is friendly and each equipment has its own attendant. There are public restrooms available. The park offers thrilling attractions and food trucks, with visible security guards. I highly recommend it to families, friends, and even those with pets to enjoy together. || Went there for the first time and I really liked it. I went in the afternoon so I did not see much because it’s much better later at night but I enjoyed it . Cool place to go with family and friends and have fun . || Very good experience and the prices is not so bad 😍 … || One of the best places to celebrate Santos Populares in Lisbon || Terrible loud electronic music that disturbs the whole neighbourhood every day Mon -Sun until 5am! They don't even obey the rules and stated schedule. Should be regulated and moved away from the residential area. || A small amusement park mostly for kids but some rides are fit for adults too. There's a candy, farturas, cotton candy, caramel popcorn, etc. Basically everything you would expect. There's also places were you can have something to eat and drink but the prices above average. || It’s a winter Faire of diverting a open space to a play ground for kids and grownups. It will end at the end of February. You must visit || Very nice and entertaining for kids snd teens || There was absolutely nothing there in the address,and it’s state open on google map,I wasted my money going there || Nice place to visit with kids, however, the variety of activities isn't big || annoying trashy electronic music all night.Can hear the annoying music over 1km away. Poor neighbors! || It was a lot of fun during early June. || Nice fair on Portugal day || Interesting. It has the potential to be the amusement park that Lisbon lacks. What's missing is the infrastructure. There's no shortage of space. And the children (and adults too) would appreciate it. If only there were the will. It remains for the City Council and the Port of Lisbon to come to an agreement. Everyone would win. ADDITIONAL NOTE: Days after what I wrote before, the space closed. The carousels, the Ferris wheel, etc., disappeared. And the entertainment at the site ended. It was a shame. Since 2003, the year the Feira Popular in Entrecampos closed, there hasn't been any amusement space in the city, despite the successive promises of the many mayors who have passed through the municipality. The Santos embankment was a good experiment, which in my view deserved to have been continued and cherished. The city's population would have benefited, the children would have benefited from having a place where they could have a good time, the merchants and amusement entrepreneurs would have benefited, and even the tourists could have benefited.  But it seems that once again the local authority's leadership has turned a blind eye and a deaf ear. || An excellent place to leave your car, near Cais do Sodré, where there are good connections to the train, metro, ferry... It's also pleasant for a stroll. || On May 30, 2025, unfortunately, the experience left much to be desired. The DJ seemed to have forgotten that the Popular Saints' festivities, especially at certain times until 9 pm, are family-oriented events. Instead, he chose to play very poor quality funk music and some extremely unpleasant rock tracks. The atmosphere became unsuitable for families, which led many parents with children to leave the venue. Some young women were behaving completely inappropriately, which further contributed to the feeling of discomfort.  The sound was very bad, muffled, without any quality, and without the proper regulation that a Quim Barreiros show requires. To make matters worse, the event started 45 minutes late. Time is time, and it should be respected.  As for Quim Barreiros' show, it was up to par, as always, but impossible to stay until the end.  However, due to the poor sound quality and the unsuitable choice of DJ, I offer this warning: if you intend to go with your family, think twice.  This type of environment is not appropriate for children or for those seeking a more traditional and respectful setting.  If the intention is to listen to more daring music and dance provocatively, there are appropriate venues for that, such as nightclubs. A public and family event is not the suitable place for such behavior.  Therefore, if you go with your family, you are most likely to leave disappointed and bored. || There are no rides, these are temporary carousels, they left, there is just a parking lot here || There's a lot of fun and food and drinks. The downside is that Sagres charges for a glass for beer. To me, it seems like they have a business selling plastic cups, and that's an abuse. I don't recommend buying a glass; I prefer not to drink. Thanks anyway.

Really tasty pastries — I tried 4 different kinds and every single one was amazing! Despite being extremely busy, the staff serve you with big, warm smiles and excellent service. Seating is limited, so expect some waiting time if you want to dine in, otherwise grab it to go and enjoy it on the bench right in front of the church || Excellent place to enjoy good coffee and delicious pastries near São Vicente de Fora. We started every day there early and it was a perfect place to relax over breakfast. Mostly I had a flat white, freshly squeezed orange juice and a croissant however they also offer a more substantial breakfast as well. Highly recommended if you are staying in the area. || The artisanal pastries here are on another level – the Pistachio Roll, Cinnamon Roll, and Raspberry Cruffin are absolute standouts, both stunning and delicious. Drinks like their homemade lemonade and iced tea are refreshing, and the coffee comes with beautiful latte art. Warm atmosphere, friendly staff, and pastries that feel crafted with real passion. Definitely one of the most special pastry shops in Lisbon! || The best pasteleria in Alfama and maybe in all Lisbon. My girlfriend and I had a breakfast every morning there during our vacation. We felt like we didn’t have to try other breakfast place because everything there was amazing- super delicious and beautiful. Artwork!!! The whole staff knows english and is super polite and attentive. Admirations to everyone in the team for the high end service they provide every single day! || Many selection of pastries. The filling of the mortadella pistachio sandwich was nice. Freshly baked bread. The babka was kind of too dry to my liking, the orange peel was kind of too overpowering. || Attentive service and good food ! My husband and I both got the breakfast combo, 8 euros each that included fresh orange juice, coffee of choice and croissant or brioche sandwich, what a good deal ! Environment was good, cute and cozy space, not noisy. Highly recommend ! || We went there for coffee and some dessert and were pleasantly surprised by how cozy the place felt and how friendly the service was. The coffee was excellent, and the pastel de nata was absolutely amazing. || On Monday morning, not crowded at all! Super sweet and lovely staff, we tried a bunch of pastries and the pastel de nata was an absolute standout. So crispy and light, with a just molten center—the best I had on this trip. It was just the right amount of sweetness, absolutely divine. Would definitely recommend ! || Beautiful. Small spot right next to the yellow tram lines. Pastries were excellent, and the pastel de nata was deep and crispy and the right texture - wonderful. Coffee was solid as well. And not expensive! Definitely recommend. || My favorite place in Lisbon with amazing food and great atmosphere. The coffee is excellent and in combination with Paste de nata there is nothing better 😁

Vibe. The owner is BEYOND LOVLEY.  The coffee was good, they also serve ice coffees. The vibe is very homely, gluten free, nasty ingredients free - does that make sense? Some of yall will know what I’m talking about. and try the banana muffin thing. Interesting at first but second bite I was in love. She bakes all the pastries in the morning. It was delicious ! I will be coming back next time I’m in Lisbon || Amazing coffee shop!! Not only is everything homemade and delicious, but the atmosphere inside is really unique. Teresa (the owner) is very caring and makes you feel at home! It’s funny to see how she knows everyone’s name when they come in! A perfect place to have a chat with people from the neighborhood or simply read a book. || Incredible coffeeshop! So cozy, Tereza is the best. So cozy and an amazing vibe! Such a fun local spot- their carrot ginger juice is 10000/10 + their vegan cakes are heaven || really cool hidden gem of lisbon! vegetarian, vegan, gluten free friendly - i think it all might be vegan? plus loads of non-caffeine drinks too.  i got a blueberry iced matcha (i think with oat milk?) which was absolutely superb. i also got a pecan pie cake thing which was delicious too.  the owner is sooooo lovely and friendly and chatty and has curated the coolest, most relaxing and chill vibes in here.  the decor is super cool and interesting. great for catching up with friends or just having a solo coffee.  well worth a visit - im just sad i only found it on my last day!! || This place feels like your family hug after a long trip.  You can get inside and forget about the world for a moment, have some coffee, any of the amazing desserts, all with the cherry on top of a lovely and kind service.  It's a good place to come and recharge your battery. || Such a cute littel cafe, well decorated. The coffee is great and also tbe service. Gluten free&vegan. || Tereza is a very welcoming and positive person, it's always a fun time coming in here to grab my daily coffee, it's delicious and I often sit around having a chat with her. Would recommend anyone in the area to pop in and enjoy this lovely cafe! || One of the best coffee shops in Lisbon! Homemade stuff and good coffee. Cozy vibe! Must visit! || Cute little place with delicious coffee, matcha and some homemade pastries. Today I’m having the apple and pecans (no added sugar) and a flat white. || The cutest cafe in Lisbon! You can tell a lot of care has gone into this cafe and it has a very cozy feel to it. They make freshly-baked goods that change every day and they have "daffee" (caffeine-free coffee alternative made from date seeds). It was truly excellent. || Such friendly staff, cute decor, and a cozy atmosphere! Immediately felt welcomed in. There was a great variety of baked goods. Incredible GF and vegan choices, not to mention everything is only sweetened with maple syrup. Good option to those with a FODMAP intolerance. Coffee was also delicious. 10/10 || I felt like I was sitting at my home in a dining room, such a lovely owner of the shop. She has an amazing aura in her shop. I love the cheese cakes 🍰 Thank you lovely! 🥰 || This place was a bit of a hike to find, but it was worth it. It's sort of hidden in a less frequented sidestreet in a quiet neighbourhood but really brings cozy neighbour vibes. The decor is super cool. It's a big mash up of everything but as a graffiti-loving, skateboarding, sneakerhead photographer, it was so dope to check out all the stuff. Coffee was tasty too! Loved the tiny patio and local dogs :) || A well deserved 5-star-rating. We were welcomed with a warm and happy spirit. Great menu with only a few choices, but everything self-made wirth lots of passion. We enjoyed the avocado sandwich (try the green Tabasco with it as recommended, this one is not too spicy and makes a delicious match), the almond cake and the banana bread, as well as the beauty smoothie. The coffee specialties come in big mugs and the prices - though rather high for Lisbon - are fair. Be aware: everything is sugar-free, and even though I usually don’t like the alternatives, the taste here was really good. Various milk-alternatives are offered as well alongside regular milk. || Passed by Put it on and gave it a try, and i’m so happy i did it. Became my fav cute spot in lisbon, great vegan food and the smoothies are delicious! Tereza that works there is a sweetheart as well! || Cute little place with the nicest energetic barista. Great food! So nice to find delicious gluten free, sugar free options. She had a mango cheesecake that was sooo good. || I spent an hour chilling in this gorgeous little cafe, sipping a super well made coffee and having a delicious vegan cheesecake - and I got such warm and kind service, thank you! || This place had such a cool atmosphere, and the small outside dining area was super cute. We got two lattes and two freshly made pastries, which were a vegan apple maple syrup muffin and a vegan carrot cake with vegan cream cheese on top. Both pastries were super light and delicious and fulfilled the perfect breakfast meal. The lattes were great as well. The barista was very kind and welcoming and she explained to us each of the pastries she had just baked herself. A+ experience, would come again! || Nice café with a relaxed, creative vibe. The cappuccino was smooth and well-balanced, and the croissant was buttery and warm. The staff were welcoming and helpful, and the space had a cozy energy that makes you want to linger. It gets a little busy during the morning rush, but that’s only because the coffee is so good. || Quirky and small cafe tucked away in a side street. I tried a cup of 'daffee' a coffee alternative made from date stones. I chose to add chai spices to it. I was surprised by how similar it was to coffee! I also had a carrot cake which was vegan and gluten free (like all of their desserts). My previous experience of gluten free cakes is that they're fairly dense and slightly tough in texture. To my surprise the carrot cake was light, fluffy and soft! My only tiny criticism is that there was no food menu so I had to wait to be told what the cakes were. I heard other guests order avocado on toast but wouldn't have known this was available otherwise. The cafe is small, with deliberately mis-matched  furnishing and only a small number of tables. Thankfully, they have a few outdoor tables and also offer takeaway. This place is a must-visit for those with dietary requirements and even those without!

Holy moly. Genuinely, the best place in Portugal. I’m from Australia and no cafe there even comes close.  Salmon salad- Silken salmon glows against crisp greens, its richness lifted by juicy mango, cool cucumber, and tangy pickled onions.  Mango and strawberry matcha- The matcha is creamy and layered—earthy green tea softened by tropical sweetness.  “Hygge yoghurt bowl”- The yoghurt bowl is cool, lush, and comforting, crowned with golden mango and gentle crunch. || Hello Titus 🙂  Thank you so much for your incredible and beautifully written review. We’re truly honored by your words and especially touched to hear that Hygge Kaffe stood out so strongly during your time in Portugal — that means a lot to us.  Your descriptions of the salmon salad, the mango & strawberry matcha, and the Hygge yoghurt bowl are simply wonderful and capture exactly what we aim to create: balanced, comforting flavors with a touch of creativity.  We’re grateful you took the time to share such thoughtful feedback and hope to welcome you back again whenever you’re in Lisbon.  Kind regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || The food was delicious! What the reviews say is all true! I got the chicken salad. Tastes so fresh and healthy! The mango’s were so fresh!  Matcha latte with oat milk and cinnamon roll with matcha gnash (delicious and must try)  Space inside or outside (heaters)  Bathroom clean || Hello Fer 😊  Thank you for your wonderful review! We’re so happy to hear you enjoyed the freshness of the chicken salad, mango, and our matcha treats. It’s great to know you felt comfortable both inside and outside, and that everything, including the bathrooms, met your expectations.  We look forward to welcoming you back soon for another delightful visit!  Warm regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || Nicest brunch place I have ever visited. The food was lovely and filling. The drinks were so artfully made and presented. The staff were really friendly and the ambiance was great. I cannot wait to come back. || Hello Corrine 😊  We’re so happy to read such a wonderful review, thank you for your kind words! It truly means a lot to hear that you enjoyed our food, drinks, atmosphere, and the service from our team. We can’t wait to welcome you back for another lovely brunch very soon!   Warm regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || A true gem of best brunch in Lisbon. Its 100% halal and have amazing menu options for vegan and vegetarian as well. Loved each and every item, made with perfection and delicious. Brunch for 2 is huge to share and enjoy . The red velvet pancake is a must try. Sandwich is juicy and flavorful. Juices and coffee hit the right spot . Worth the wait as its usually very busy. || Hi Benish :)  Thank you so much for your amazing review! We’re delighted to hear you enjoyed the variety on our menu, from the vegan and vegetarian options to the halal dishes.   We truly appreciate your kind words and understanding about the wait during busy times, and we look forward to welcoming you back to HyggeKaffe soon!  Warm regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || Fantastic place to get breakfast or brunch. The cinnamon rolls are ridiculously amazing. A must try and I got pistachio frosting on mine which was a 10/10. || Lovely experience ✨ The food was delicious and creative, especially the salmon Benedict highly recommended 👌 The menu is diverse with plenty of great options, and they have the best matcha! I strongly recommend trying the matcha with banana bread 🤍 All the staff were incredibly kind and welcoming, with such positive energy. Special thanks to Caroline for her friendliness. Will definitely be back! || Hello Cylia 🙂  Thank you so much for your wonderful review and for sharing such a lovely experience with us. We’re delighted to hear that you enjoyed the creative food, especially the salmon Benedict, a great choice!  It means a lot to know that you appreciated the variety of our menu and that our matcha stood out as a favorite, particularly paired with banana bread.  We’re also very grateful for your kind words about our team. A special thank you for mentioning Caroline, we’ll be sure to share your compliments with her.  We truly look forward to welcoming you back again soon.  Kind regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || Great vibe matcha was delicious the coconut matcha was very refreshing not sweet, the strawberry was sweet and fluffy. Yoghurt was yummy good size to be able to also try a sweet- the matcha cinnamon roll was lovely very fresh. Savoury waffles also delicious fast and friendly service. || Hi Candyalu :)   Thank you so much for your wonderful and detailed review! We’re thrilled to hear that you enjoyed the matcha drinks — especially the coconut and strawberry, as well as the cinnamon roll and savoury waffles. It’s great to know the balance of flavours and portions hit the mark for you.  We really appreciate your kind words about our team and service, and we can’t wait to welcome you back for another delicious brunch at Hygge Kaffe!   Warm regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || I went to Hygge Kaffe and it was my 1st time there, thanks to Google reviews for that recommendation. The space has a big number of tables and can fit many customers. Staff team were very friendly and helpful. Food was very delicious and good quality products. The price was very good too. I’d definitely recommend and come back to it. || Hello Caio 😊  Thank you so much for your kind review! We’re thrilled to hear that you enjoyed the food, service, and overall atmosphere at Hygge Kaffe. Your recommendation means a lot to us!  We can’t wait to welcome you back for another great experience.  Warm regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || We had the worst experience here, first of all we didn’t make a reservation and we had to wait for a table (which isn’t a problem) but after we were seated we waited around 30 minutes to order and another hour to get the food and drinks (there were about 8 waitresses). Secondly, me and my boyfriend ordered an Eggs and bacon sandwich and the egg white was literally transparent, raw, disgusting. We told the waitress and she said that this is normal (which is funny cause raw egg white causes salmonella) and that we should have asked for a well done egg (we were never asked how we want the egg to be done). She also said that we are the first people to ever complain about this and she turned the conversation into blaming us, not themselves. She also said that when we come back we should order something else so we don’t have problems (we will never come back here) || Hello Zsanette,  Thank you for taking the time to share your experience with us. We are truly sorry to read about what happened during your visit, this is absolutely not the standard of service or food quality we strive to provide.  We sincerely apologize for the excessive waiting times, both to place your order and to receive the food and drinks. We understand how frustrating this must have been, especially after being seated, and this is something we take very seriously.  We are particularly concerned to hear about your experience with the Eggs and Bacon sandwich. Serving an egg that is not properly cooked, as well as how the situation was handled afterward, is unacceptable. Your feedback regarding food safety and the way the conversation was managed is extremely important, and we deeply regret that you felt blamed rather than listened to. That is not how we want our guests to feel.  We will be reviewing this situation internally with both our kitchen and service teams to ensure that food preparation standards, communication, and customer care are clearly reinforced.  While we understand and respect your decision not to return, we truly appreciate you bringing these issues to our attention, as they help us identify where we must improve.  Kind regards Hygge Kaffe Team || Best matcha and brunch place. Loved the drinks and foods. Staff were very nice, would highly recommend. You can also sit by the bar stools if there is a wait for a table. || Hi Eda🙂  Thank you so much for your kind words! We’re thrilled to hear you loved the matcha, food, and drinks, and that our team made your visit even better. Great tip about the bar stools too, we’re glad you enjoyed the experience!  We look forward to welcoming you back soon.  Warm regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || Went twice for weekend breakfast – better to reserve as it gets busy, but during the week no need. Great variety of breakfast options and the staff are warm and friendly. Cozy place to start the day! || Hi Hadi 🙂  Thank you so much for your kind review! We’re so happy to know you enjoyed your breakfasts with us and appreciated both the food variety and our team’s hospitality.  It’s true, weekends can get quite lively, so we’re glad you managed to visit during both busy and calmer moments!  Hope to see you again soon for another cozy start to the day.  Warm regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || Great little brunch spot with delicious food and some seriously yum matchas (tiramisu matcha is incredible). We had a salmon tartar sandwich in brioche toasted bread and turkish eggs, both delicious. There is a bit of wait on the food but understandable considering the place was packed and at peak brunch time. All the staff are lovely. || Hi Tajana :)  Thank you so much for your wonderful review! We’re delighted to hear you enjoyed the menu and as well as the friendly service from our team.  We really appreciate your understanding about the wait during peak brunch hours, and we’re so glad you still had a lovely experience. We look forward to welcoming you back to HyggeKaffe soon!  Warm regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || I stopped by Hygge for a late breakfast and quickly got a table outside (without a reservation). The service was very efficient, though they did seem a bit tired. The food was served surprisingly fast. The scrambled eggs and bread were very tasty – although the eggs were cold. The chai latte was DELICIOUS! The mango smoothie was also good – you could really taste that it was all natural with no added sugar. I recommend it :) || Hi Karolina 🙂  Thank you so much for your detailed review! We’re delighted to hear you enjoyed the chai latte, mango smoothie, and the overall experience with us. We also appreciate your note about the eggs and the service, feedback like this is very helpful for us to keep improving.  We’re glad you’d recommend us, and we look forward to welcoming you back soon for another breakfast or brunch!  Warm regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || I come to Lisbon for work often and stay in the area— this is always one of my “musts”!  The service is great and the food is fresh & filling!  Also I didn’t get a picture but the fresh juice is amazing— recommend the watermelon ginger!  Turkish eggs were perfect || Hello :)  Thank you so much for your wonderful review! We’re delighted to know HyggeKaffe is one of your go-to spots when you’re in Lisbon, and it’s great to hear you enjoyed the menu and our friendly service.  Your kind words mean a lot to us, and we look forward to welcoming you back again soon!  Warm regards, Hygge Kaffe Team || We had a lovely breakfast.
