The pastries were fresh, flaky, and packed with flavor, especially the pastel de nata, which was simply outstanding. While the service is not at the table—you have to place your order at the counter—the staff were friendly and efficient.  For 14.40€, we enjoyed two pastel de nata, one chocolate pastry, two cappuccinos, and a frothy milk. Given the quality and portion sizes, I found this to be great value for money. Compared to similar offerings in the UK, the pricing here is much more reasonable.  Overall, I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for excellent pastries and coffee at a fair price point. Would definitely visit again! || Fábrica Coffee Roasters I’ve had espresso here many times — the coffee is absolutely amazing! Rich, balanced flavor and always freshly brewed. The place is cozy with a relaxed vibe, and the staff are really friendly. Definitely one of the best spots in Lisbon for real coffee lovers. || 💯 The best  This was by far the best brunch we’ve had in Lisbon!  The coffee, the cookies and the avocado toast were incredibly tasty and filled with flavor.  The atmosphere is cozy and squeaky clean.  I think the only thing to be improv would be the service, the guys looked a bit lost and not very organized when delivering the orders. || Nice and cozy place. A lot of room between the tables. Good coffee and excellent cookies. You can bring you furry friend as well. || The coffee is great! I can smell the coffee flavour before drinking it and the sweetness left in my mouth Its definitely worth the price || Lovely quiet spot to grab a decent coffee. Staff were super friendly and efficient and the pastries were delicious! || This plate should have never have been served. Cracked along the edges beyond being ‘hip’ and presentable, great choice in cutlery. Not satisfied with lots of room for improvement but has potential. The egg was far over cooked and tasted very strongly of vinegar. Salad lacked seasoning. Inhospitable staff (those who served the tables didn’t speak Portuguese and their English was incomprehensible), please remember to serve ladies at the table first, get the orders to the right table. Fundamentals of serving tables anywhere. Only gave three stars because it wasn’t expensive and their morning kick drink was quite nice and their decor inside was cosy but didn’t cater to brunch eating. Coffee was excellent, perfect. Was not served with sugar (I don’t have sugar in my coffee but you don’t know that). || Good place for a quick meetup, with coffee and deserts. Or to recharge after a long walk around town. || A perfect lazy coffee morning spot. Coffee was fantastic and the pastries were on point. The decor inside and out both blends into it's surroundings and stands out as a gem of modern coffee brewing in Lisbon.  They also sell t-shirts 👌 || Good shots. Barista pulled a couple of cappuccinos, watched us drink them from the side and asked how they were because he thought he might need to dial the grinder in again.  The shot was balanced and the sweetness of the milk cut through most of the imperfections aside from a slightly sour finish, which he expected.  He then tore down the grinder, cleaned it, adjusted the burrs and pulled us another shot, which was no longer under extracted and had a nice dark chocolatey finish.  The focus on coffee was excellent, and is recommend this place for a good shot in Lisbon. || A small cafe with a special atmosphere. The coffee is delicious, the cake was very tasty, the service is kind and fast. You can also buy packed coffee or tea. || The place is quiet and the service is good.  Ordered the matcha latte and the nata. Both were average.  Others who ordered the V60/drip coffee didn’t enjoy it very much.

I frequently visit different places to explore new experiences, looking for an inspiring atmosphere where I can enjoy trying various types of coffee.  Cafe Expo stands out by offering over 10 types of coffee and more than 40 different drinks, making it a great spot for coffee lovers.  Overall, it has been a great experience.  Free WiFi, laptop-friendly environment 👍 || Very delicious ice coffee! Great alternative to starb**ks if you’re b0yc0tting them🍉 Very reasonably priced. The lady who served us wasn’t so friendly though & it would be nice if they had a dairy alternative besides oat milk. || Thanks Portugirl for you’re feedback. We definitely going to talk to our peoples to pay attention on our service. And we’re trying to add other milks also. || Nice cosy cafe with very friendly barista. Many youngsters here so the vibe is lively. The coffee beans are Brazilian so it’s aromatic for us. The hot chocolate is great too! || Thank you very much for feedback || Nice place to seat for a coffee or a cake. Variety of coffees and sweets. Unfortunately no ice cream. The service is pleasant and there are comfortable tables to seat and work if necessary. There’s also available free WiFi for the customers. || Thanks lukasz for feedback || If you are tight on money but feel like drinking a cappuccino that is of good quality and having a delicious dessert, there is no better place than this café. Would specially recommend to university students. || Thank you Michael Buster || TL;DR - give their drinks a chance, don’t go there for the food or vibe.  I was looking for an alternative to Starbucks in terms of iced lattes etc, the kind that you generally don’t find in Europe. And in that regard, I think this may be a winner because their menu looks promising. Unfortunately I was pressed for time, and was only able to try out the salted caramel latte which, with some luck, you can get at a *few* Portuguese cafes. The SC latte was good, and I was asked if I’d like a different milk, which is good too. However, that is where it ends. I shared a croissant mista and a slice of the chocolate cake with my friend. The croissant was alright, but the cake was somehow very sweet, and bland, at the same time. But what I really found strange is that the server wouldn’t come out from behind the bar at all. I had to get up from my seat 4 times to collect the food, then to pass back the croissant so it could be heated, then to get it back, then because it became apparent to the server that we’d need more than 1 plate between the 2 of us. I’m not sure why they didn’t come to us, and I haven’t experienced this in any other cafe. It’s a different thing if you’re standing at the bar, or if it’s a fast food restaurant, but this was not the case.  Also, the coffee is served in takeaway cups even if you’re dining in, which I found strange as well.  Having said all of this, I will give it another go to try out their fancier offerings, and it won’t be for dine in || Thank you, Cortezia Miranda || Cosy cafe that opens early. Nice local savory samosas and tuna croquettes. Latte art on coffee is so beautiful. Down to earth, friendly staff. || thanks for your feedback || Great new place in the area to enjoy a relaxing coffee with a book. Homely and pleasant atmosphere, friendly people and coffee of amazing quality. Try the espresso and you will know! || thanks for your feedback emily || Frozen pancakes for 3.5€ and the topping isn’t even on the pancakes, the Nutella comes in a container. To much ice in the drinks. Don’t recommend. The music is to loud and there is to much noise. || Amazing coffee and great staff, if you need coffee in the area this is the spot!

Hello, Kristof is where we had a nice and big breakfast on November 1st during our Lisbon trip. The place is spacious, relaxed, and well-kept, even the toilets were spotless. Since we were among the first customers that morning, everything came quickly and smoothly. A very pleasant start to the day. Surely recommended! || Loved the atmosphere, Iordered a smoked salmon toast but the avacado toast came. I went up to tell the waiter that I got a smoked salmon toast and she disagreed and claimed I ordered an avocado toast. The avacado toast itself was okay it was what you could expect from an avacado toast. The second thing that I ordered was a latte but this is the first time when I ordered a latte it came in a clear glass cup? Everyone else in the coffee store had a coffee mug with their drink so I was unsure why mine was different? || There was not a bad café in Lisbon that I found, but hello, kristof is at the top of the good ones! The food was delicious and so were the drinks! It had a very nice laid-back atmosphere and the servers were very friendly! I’d highly recommend checking it out! || Delicious, reasonably priced breakfast with top coffee. Highly recommend. Very accommodating to English speakers but seems to be loved by locals too. Lovely staff. Some of the best scrambled eggs I have ever had in my life. || Hello, Thank you! 💛 We’re thrilled you enjoyed the breakfast, coffee, and especially the scrambled eggs. It makes us happy to know our team made you feel welcome. Hope to see you again soon ☕✨ … || Drinks: The dirty chai latte was well-made, with a sweet chai base and a slightly sour coffee note. It had a Starbucks-like profile, which makes sense considering the other coffee options here don’t really taste like coffee either—more like milk-based drinks with a coffee aftertaste.  The cappuccino was underwhelming. The milk completely overpowered the coffee. It felt more like a generic coffee-flavored milk drink rather than something from a specialty coffee shop.  Pastries: The pistachio soft cookie had a slight crunch on the outside but was mostly soft. Simply adding a few nuts on top doesn’t make it a pistachio cookie—it was filled with chocolate and tasted more like a chocolate chip cookie with pistachios rather than a proper pistachio-based treat.  The vegan brownie was too dry and lacked the gooeyness that makes a brownie enjoyable. It felt like texture was sacrificed just to make it vegan, and honestly, a basic store-bought brownie would have been better.  Overall Impression: The price is unjustified for what was served. The coffee lacks depth, and the drinks cater more to those who enjoy milk-heavy Starbucks-style beverages. If you appreciate actual coffee, there’s nothing for you here. If you prefer milk drinks, Starbucks offers a wider selection for a better experience.  Overpriced and unremarkable. 16.50€ 2 coffees and 2 pastries.  Thank you for the coffee || Thanks for taking the time to share such thoughtful feedback — we’re sorry the experience didn’t meet your expectations. We’ll reflect on your comments as we continue to improve. Wishing you all the best! 💛 … || The breakfasts are delicious — everything is fresh, nicely presented, and the portions are generous. I especially loved the flat white and the toast with salmon. The atmosphere is cozy, and the staff is friendly. The only downside is that the café is quite small. || Our favourite gem that we found exploring Lisbon! Amazing, amazing eggs, smoked salmon and coffee! Everything else looked superb as well. Cozy, cute cafe with good vibes, good wifi, and good views from the patio. Highly recommend! || Great breakfast in a cosy cafe! ☕️  Didn’t see the banana cake on display and found out we were a little early at 9+ in the morning, and decided to wait for it to be ready which took only 15 minutes from the point of ordering - and it turned out great! I believe it’s one of the best banana cakes I have had so far 👍🏻  🥐 the ham and cheese croissant was great, can’t remember if I have a benchmark for this but this was a good one and certainly hard to beat  🥑 avocado toast was good too, a very generous portion and also came with fresh salad on the side too  ☕️ coffee was alright, a 4 stars here - mocha was decent, not milky and had a strong chocolate flavour too, just what we liked  Overall a great experience, beautiful interior design and friendly staff paired with the lovely food 👍🏻 || Hello Kristof should be called hello I’m pissed off -at least that’s the vibe the staff seem to have.  A little smile won’t hurt you, and it’ll make your guests feel welcome. || I loved coming here on my trip to Lisbon! The girls working were sweet and the food presentation was beautiful and coffee AMAZING. I even bought coffee beans to bring home (although this was at the Alfama location). Cool concept with the magazines on the wall and an overall welcoming and warm place! || So happy you loved your visit — and that the coffee made it home with you! 💕 Thanks for the kind words and hope to see you again in Lisbon! … || Amazing place with great tasty food. I took the salty brunch which was 21 euros I beleive and it came with a toast of my choice , fruit bowl, fresh orange juice , chocolate croissant and a hot drink of my choice. The food came very fast as well which was great. The place is aesthetically pleasing and nice atmosphere. Only complaint would be the journals that looked interesting where packaged so we weren’t able to read much. I highly reccomend this place because the food was flavourful , big portions and filling. || Amazing, Thank you Lena! 🖤 ✨ … || Super nice staff and great products! I really enjoyed my breakfast even the place is not big. But the staff was so friendly that we just had to wait a little bit to get a great seat. The music was fantastic and the atmosphere too! The coffee was excellent also the food! I absolutely recommend this place! || If you love vegetables, fresh herbs, spices, delicious bread, you definitely need to visit this place. The portions are large, all the food is very fresh. I ordered smashed avocado with lemon, ricotta, cucumber, crispy onions, chili flakes, chives, seeds, salad & tomatoes. Granola with yogurt fruits and berries was good. My husband chose croissant with smoked salmon, lemon mousse & zest, chives, seeds, salad & tomatoes. Delicious croissant and excellent hot chocolate! || Thank you for your review! 😊 We're thrilled you discovered us and enjoyed our Menu ✨ … || Lovely coffee shop in Lisbon old town. No laptops but magazine to browse and great coffee and food. || Hello,  Thank you! 💛 The photos look amazing!! We’re so glad you enjoyed the coffee, food, and our magazines, the laptop-free vibe is part of what makes the space special.  Hope to see you again soon ☕✨ || The place is very busy all the time. I had a cappuccino and croissant. I love this combo and have had in many places around the world. My conclusion is that in Portugal is that the ratio milk/foam to coffee is even higher than in other places. I like it more strong. Anyways, croissant was superb one of the best I had here! They serve brunch too || It’s a small coffee shop with a simple menu. The v60 here is absolutely amazing. Other coffees such as cappuccino or latte are excellent as well. We tried the cheese and ham croissant, as well as the salmon toast and presunto toast and all was excellent. The croissants are super buttery. The banana bread was amazing, we’ll definitely go back for this. || Really nice breakfast spot. Small menu and we tried the salmon & avo breakfasts. I’d rate the salmon an 8 and the avo an 8 too.  Coffee was an 8.5 (really good score) and matcha was a 7/7.5.  Really recommend if you’re visiting Lisbon! || Hello,  Thanks a lot for the thoughtful review, we love the ratings! So glad you enjoyed the breakfast, coffee, and matcha. Hope your time in Lisbon has been just as delicious.  Hope to see you again soon 💕 || Check out the Santa Clara location. Beautiful view of the pantheon — very relaxing. Must try the panko pork Japanese style sandwich, mouthwatering 🤤 … coffee is excellent too! ☕️ Have always been big fans of this cafe, so excited for the new location this summer! || Amazing, thank you Victoria! 🖤 ✨ … || Very nice for brunch, coffee and refreshing juice. We had goats cheese ricotta cucumber open sandwich, egg mayo sandwich, green juice, coffees. Very nice || Hello, Thank you! 💛 We’re so glad you enjoyed. It means a lot that you shared your experience. Hope to see you again soon ☕✨ || I ordered a chocolate cookie and my friend had the cinnamon roll. I also had the homemade lemonade and my friend had the homemade iced tea. The lemonade was not what I expected it was not fizzy it was more frothy almost like a matcha and had almost a mint flavour. My friend’s iced tea also didn’t have a lot of taste. My cookie was very soft and not very tasty and the cinnamon roll was dry. Staff were friendly and the place was clean just the food and drinks were disappointing. || Hello, Megan  Thank you for your detailed feedback — we're really sorry to hear the food and drinks didn’t meet your expectations. We’re always working to improve and your comments help us do that. Glad to hear you found the team friendly and the space welcoming.  We hope you’ll consider giving us another try in the future. 💛

I ordered a flat white with regular milk ( I was oat milk offered as well ). Good quality, served in ceramic cup. I had avocado and scramble eggs on toast. Pretty good as a breakfast to start your day. Overall great and staff very friendly and enthusiastic. || A great place for some breakfast to start your day. These coffee labs are all a bit quirky , we tried several during our stay. They are staffed by welcoming friendly staff and offer a wide range of food & drinks.  We had scrambled eggs on rye , coffee with pastries or their famous breakfast plate, all good. || Exceptional flavors and presentation. These guys and girls are true masters. Delivering all the quality at super affordable prices and in a comfortable ambiance. Truly AWESOME!!! || This Danish coffee shop chain is the perfect spot for coffee and cake - but not the traditional one full of sugar, the healthier version that is not sacrificing in taste. I had the brownie with walnuts (2.50€) - it was quite petite but boy it was delicious, smooth, moist and creamy. Perfect size for a small little treat. Decaf cappuccino with oat milk was also very tasty, one of the best I’ve had in Lisbon so far. They also have gluten free and vegan alternatives on menu such as the vegan nut bars or mini cheese cake. And of course the traditional Danish cinnamon rolls. They make their own rye bread and it looks delicious. This coffee shop is quite small and has no outside seating but they have 8 different ones spread throughout Lisbon. || I had to take a lot of steep steps from my hotel  to the Cafe but it was worth it!!! Top Coffee quality, great selection of breakfest and the music made my morning start just perfect! Barista was very helpful and Friendly. This is the very best example of how this kind of Business must be run! || We opted for the wrap, and I found the price matched the quality quite well. While there's room for improvement, it was satisfactory. The atmosphere was enjoyable. If you're seeking a contemporary experience within the heart of history, this place is worth a try. || Very nice place with small terrasse, mostly visited by tourists. Great coffee with choice of milk. The food could take a while to arrive but was delicious so well worth the wait. If you get orange juice, it comes from carton and is not freshly pressed. || Excellent range of patries, sandwiches  coffee and juices. Great for breakfast, brunch and lunch. Air conditioned and comfortable. || Stopped in for a quick bite to eat and a coffee. We had the ham and cheese croissant, a smoothie and a yogurt bowl. It was all super quick and tasty. The staff are quick to clean tables and the service is great too. Located really central and not too far from the main attractions. || I visited that café, enjoyed everything, ordered a large breakfast for €12. I'd like to have double eggs in the breakfast, as I've ordered it here before and got scrambled eggs clearly from one egg twice. The staff is very friendly, and the atmosphere could be better; the arrangement of tables in the room is not quite ideal.

place_name: Church of Saint Anthony of Lisbon
reviews_content: The Church of Saint Anthony of Lisbon is a beautiful and historic site dedicated to Saint Anthony, who was born here in 1195. According to tradition, the church was built on the very spot of his birthplace. The architecture is charming, and the altar is especially stunning, showcasing exquisite detail and craftsmanship. It’s a peaceful and inspiring place to visit. I highly recommend it to anyone exploring Lisbon. || Beautiful, historic church right by Lisbon Cathedral! Lovely Baroque-Rococo architecture with elegant details and a peaceful atmosphere. Built on the traditional birthplace of Saint Anthony and after the 1755 earthquake was rebuilt in 1767, it blends history and artistry perfectly. A must-see stop in the Alfama area || Beautiful and peaceful church of Saint Anthony, located in the heart of the downtown Full of history, with a warm and spiritual atmosphere. Downstairs, there’s a small chapel and the place where Saint Anthony was born. Visitors can also write prayer intentions. An ideal place to pause, pray, and fill your heart with peace. Inside the church, there’s a small shop where you can buy souvenirs, prayers, and rosaries. Highly recommended it is a must see, do and visit || The Church of Saint Anthony is a must-visit in Lisbon! I had a truly pleasant and blessed visit. The good architecture is remarkable, and the church has a wonderfully pleasant and serene atmosphere. It is highly recommended for devotion to Saint Anthony and for a moment of peace and reflection. || A beautiful church dedicated to Saint Anthony of Lisbon, known throughout the Cristian world as Saint Anthony of Padua. According to tradition, church was built on the site where the saint was born, in 1195. When you visit Afama, don't forget to visit this church. || St. Anthony Church in Lisbon is a revered religious and historical site closely linked to the life of St. Anthony of Padua, making it a popular pilgrimage destination for visitors and locals alike. This 18th-century baroque church is believed to mark the birthplace of St. Anthony, one of Portugal’s most beloved saints, and offers beautiful architecture, onsite services, and an atmosphere steeped in history just steps away from Lisbon Cathedral. || Beyond being the patron saint of lost items, I was told Saint Anthony was also known as the match maker; regardless, you should definitely visit this beautiful little church if you have the time. || The Church of Saint Anthony of Lisbon (Portuguese: Igreja de Santo António de Lisboa) is a church located in Lisbon, Portugal. It is dedicated to Saint Anthony of Lisbon (also known in the Christian world as Saint Anthony of Padua). According to tradition, the church was built on the site where the saint was born in 1195. The church is classified as a National Monument. || The interior is splendid. The altar is beautiful. The ceiling and floor are colorful. Paintings are fabulous. || Saint Anthony is in the cellar at the underground floor, by walk through his house within the church, just like exploring levels in Dark Souls game. The crying Mary statue looks alive. || A small church (no ticket required), but worth a quick stop before or after visiting the castle and the Cathedral. Make sure to go downstairs to the birthplace and see where Pope John Paul came to pray. || An amazing church to visit—well organised. Entry is €5 per person. I was told there’s a 20% discount with a Lesbian Tourist Card, which you can get from the tourist information centre. || The Church of Saint Anthony of Lisbon is a masterpiece of design and artistry. Its architecture is beautifully crafted, blending lightness with sophistication that captivates the eye. The intricate details throughout the church are complemented by the use of stunning colors, which add warmth and depth to its serene atmosphere.  Walking through this sacred space felt both peaceful and inspiring. || The church stands on the site believed to be the birthplace of Santo António (Saint Anthony, born Fernando de Bulhões). A small chapel was first established here in the 15th century. During the reign of King Manuel I in the 16th century, the church was expanded, but much of it was destroyed in the 1755 earthquake—only the main altar remained. The current building was reconstructed in 1767 by Mateus Vicente de Oliveira in a mix of Baroque and Rococo styles. Beneath the church lies a crypt marking the saint’s birthplace, which preserves the remains of the earlier chapel. Every year on June 13th, the feast day of the saint, a festive parade begins right in front of the church. || I had the opportunity to visit the Church and Museum of Saint Anthony in Lisbon, and it was a deeply enriching experience that offered both spiritual reflection and historical insight. Located near the Lisbon Cathedral in the Alfama district, the Church of Saint Anthony is traditionally believed to be built on the site where the saint was born in 1195. The original structure was destroyed in the 1755 earthquake, but it was rebuilt in 1767 in a late Baroque and Pombaline style under the direction of architect Mateus Vicente de Oliveira. The interior is serene, and the crypt, accessible through the sacristy, is considered to be the exact spot of Saint Anthony's birth.  Adjacent to the church is the Museum of Saint Anthony, which offers a comprehensive look into the life and legacy of one of Lisbon's most revered figures. The museum houses a collection of religious artifacts, including sculptures, paintings, ceramics, and liturgical items, all dedicated to the saint's life and the devotion he inspires. One of the highlights is a 17th-century polychrome tile panel depicting Saint Anthony preaching to the fish. The museum also features multimedia exhibits that delve into the traditions, festivals, and miracles associated with the saint. Admission is affordable, and the museum is open from Tuesday to Sunday, making it accessible for visitors interested in exploring Lisbon's rich cultural and religious heritage. || Now I know why I was automatically dran to the Igreja de Santo António de Lisboa. I tend to lose things and Saint Antonio - born in Lisbon – is th beloved patron “finder of lost things.” Many visitors write small notes (I did not) or prayers for things they’re seeking to find - whether it’s a lost key, a lost purpose, or a lost moment of peace. . The interior of the church is elegant without being overly ornate. I like it very much. || the church of Sant'Antonio stands in the place where, according to legend, the patron saint of both Lisbon and Padua was born. for this reason it is a pilgrimage destination for devotees of the saint and also offers a visit to his presumed birthplace, located below the church. free entrance. || It is unclear whether the chapel below the church, which is dedicated to Saint Anthony of Lisbon (a.k.a. Anthony of Padua) really marks the spot where the birthplace or even the house of the saint stood in the 12th century. In 1495, King João II commissioned the construction of "a lager and more dignified" church or chapel on this site. Simultaneously, history tells us that the meetings of the city council of Lisbon were held in the house of Saint Anthony and continued to do so for several more centuries. This building was situated next to the church but destroyed in the 1755 earthquake, which was followed by a tidal wave that consumed over 80 percent of the city, including the church. A third church, the present one, was built on the site of the old church. The present chapel below the church used to be called the Crypt of Saint Anthony, suggesting he was buried there. He was, as a matter of fact, buried in Padua, Italy. Since Pope John Paul 2nd visited the chapel and prayed there, it is officially called a chapel. The chapel itself is a small hallway with a small niche under an arched construction, in which behind bars is a small 'altar' with a relic of Saint Anthony. Presumably, there is a piece of bone of the saint inside it, but regretfully, there is no text explaining this to visitors. Mostly, the texts inside and outside the chapel relate to the visit of the pope. Besides that, they mention that the chapel is the only remnant of the 2nd church of 1495. That church was built 264 years after the death of the saint. If it truly it had been the exact spot of the birthplace of Saint Anthony, several meters below ground level, you would expect such a sacred place would have been incorporated into that new church. Also, it contradicts the existence of the Saint Anthony House next to the church at that same time.  Another matter is a painting inside the nave of the church. It is advertised to be the most faithful likeness of Saint Anthony, the "true effigy of the Saint," although it was painted somewhere between 350 and 450 years after his death. Apparently, it is of unknown provenance.  On the other side of the nave is a relic of Saint Justina. This could be Saimt Justina of Padua, but regretfully, this is not mentioned. It is a statue of a reclining lady dressed in cloth of real fabric, decorated with golden flowers and jewelry. On her head, a wreath of flowers, and in her hands, she is holding a bouquet of flowers. At her feet, a small vase, covered by a lid, presumably, inside it is a piece of bone or other body part of this saint.  The church itself is quite beautiful. It was designed in a rococo-baroque style.  Set aside all the questions about the originality of spaces and objects under and inside the church, the dedication by believers is what matters most to people of faith. It's arguably that which gives it its strength and makes it unique.  It is to be assumed that during the earthquake and the following tidal flood of 1755, much of the original documentation of the city was lost.  The visit is free of charge.  At the entrance of the church and next to the sacristy are religious gift shops. Also, next to the sacristy are public toilets for visitors. To the side of the front of the church is a Saint Anthony museum. || This is in the Alfama in Lisbon, it's  hard to find a parking spot and if you find one it's only for 2 hours limit.  It's not enough time to walk or explore and have diner. I would leave the vehicle somewhere else parked and just take a Uber to the location. || It was a nice cute little church where they honor Saint Antony, it's free to enter and you can go to the place where they say he was born. You should totally check this church.

A wonderful example of a well-maintained and carefully renovated Gothic cathedral. The Sé de Lisboa dates back to 1147, with construction completed around the 13th century, making it the oldest church in Lisbon.  You can really feel the history here, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic elements shaped over centuries. It’s not overly grand or touristy, just authentic and atmospheric.  Definitely worth taking some time to visit when you’re in the city — a quiet, impressive place right in the heart of Lisbon. || Oldest church in the city (1147). Gorgeous catholic cathedral and a must visit. Very cool to be able to go up in the old choir loft  and especially outside by the large stained glass window on the front of the cathedral. There was a short line when I went on a weekday, so you may want to buy tickets in advance for a weekend, cruise ship port day, or high season. I was disappointed that the cloisters were closed when I went. || Beautiful and historic place in the heart of Alfama. The cathedral feels ancient and peaceful inside, with thick stone walls and soft light coming through the windows. I loved seeing the mix of old architecture and history all around. Even from the outside, it’s impressive — especially when the tram passes by. Definitely worth a short visit while exploring Lisbon. || The cathedral was absolutely breathtaking. There is still an admission fee, but you get a discount with the Lisboa Card, which helps. As you enter, you go up the stairs to the treasure room. On the way up, make sure to notice the carved cross on the stairs, said to have been made by Saint Anthony to repel the devil during his studies.  The artifacts in the treasure room are beautifully detailed and very well preserved. From there, you can access the interior balcony, which offers a great view of the main church below and a close look at the stunning stained glass centerpiece. There’s also a small passage leading to an exterior balcony overlooking the front of the cathedral, though it’s quite narrow and can get crowded. It’s a tight squeeze, one-way, and very high up, so just take care if you’re not great with heights.  The main cathedral itself is massive, with chapels dedicated to different saints along the back. The whole place feels grand and full of history.  Overall, an incredible experience and definitely a must-see when visiting Lisbon. || The oldest and most iconic church in Lisbon, full of history and charm. The architecture is impressive, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. Inside it’s peaceful and beautifully lit, offering a quiet break from the busy streets. Climb up to see the cloisters and enjoy the view of Alfama. A must-visit for history and architecture lovers || We took the classic yellow #28 tram and got off at the Se. The area is very cute with many great photo opportunities. We also had brunch at a sidewalk cafe in the small square right before the Se. It’s worth a visit for the views. || ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Lisbon's spiritual heavyweight champion since 1147 ⛪ Plot twist: you absolutely should go inside this magnificent cathedral, and here's the best part - it's completely free! No tickets, no queues, just walk right in like you own the place (which, in a way, we all do). The Sé de Lisboa isn't just "a church like all the churches" - it's THE church, Lisbon's oldest and most historically significant. The Romanesque fortress-like exterior might look a bit stern and businesslike, but step inside and you're hit with centuries of Portuguese history. The Gothic cloisters are genuinely stunning, and if you're lucky enough to catch evening light streaming through those rose windows, you'll understand why people have been coming here to feel something greater for nearly 900 years. Jardim da Parada in Campo de Ourique is one of those rare places in Lisbon that feels genuinely local—quiet, shaded, and full of character. The garden is beautifully maintained, surrounded by big, old trees like sequoias and plane trees, with a small pond in the center where ducks and turtles paddle around peacefully. There’s a traditional bandstand, a nice playground for kids, and a charming little kiosk café that serves good coffee, light meals, and has plenty of outdoor seating under the trees. The vibe is calm and neighborly. People of all ages hang out here—seniors playing cards or reading, parents with strollers, kids running around, people walking their dogs, and others just sitting quietly enjoying the shade. One lovely touch is the old red phone booth that’s been turned into a tiny free library. It’s things like this that make the park feel alive and loved. The space isn’t huge, but it’s got everything it needs. Flower beds are always fresh, paths are clean, and there are benches everywhere. There are also two important statues tucked inside the garden—Maria da Fonte and Professor Ferreira de Macedo—which give it a bit of historical personality. But what really stood out this time was the buzz around the new underground development being planned. The city has announced a project to build a large underground parking garage beneath the garden. While I understand the need to ease traffic and create more parking in Campo de Ourique, I can’t help but feel concerned about the long-term impact this might have on such a delicate green space. There’s a real fear among locals that the construction will disturb the ecosystem of the garden—the roots of these beautiful old trees, the peace and quiet, and possibly the safety of the pond and wildlife. Right now, the garden feels timeless and balanced, and people are naturally worried that digging beneath it could change that. It’s a bit of a crossroads moment for Jardim da Parada. As it stands today, it’s one of the most welcoming and peaceful little parks in the city—loved by the neighborhood and full of everyday life. I hope that whatever happens with the development plans, the soul of the garden is preserved. If you're in Lisbon and want to experience a bit of calm, community, and natural charm, this place is well worth a visit. And if you’re a local—keep an eye on what’s planned beneath your feet. || Jardim da Parada is a compact, well-kept square that does the fundamentals right: plenty of shade, ample benches, smooth paths, a small playground, and a kiosk for quick coffee.
