However, quality of food is not as good. || This beautiful market is a little farer away from the tourist crowd offering regional products and lots of options for foodies like us. After 11:30 you will find lots of tapas, fish, seafood, meat and pastry dishes as well as a well equipped bar. Highly recommend! || Beautiful market with amazing fruits, vegetables, fresh fish, roasted nuts, artisan bread and plenty of little restaurants. I went for the hummus place, had maybe the best hummus in my life! Super delicious, light and fresh. Spectacular! Overall the market is very chilled, clean, and full of friendly people! || Be prepared to find fresh, fresh, fresh fruits and vegetables, seafood, and artisan breads, olive oils and more inside this covered marketplace. A huge shoutout out to the butcher on the corner, Tahlo do Nuno Félix, who provide first-class customer service. I brought my dog to Lisbon with me and I need to make her dog food from scratch. I work with the same butcher every week and and he de-bones and grinds chicken for me and sets the bones aside to make broth. My Portuguese is limited to "please, thank you, excuse me an see you later" and his English is about on par with my Portuguese, we managed to get my first order done with sign language and Google Translate. Now when I come in he knows just what I want and we have a great rapport. I love Lisbon and its people, I have encountered nothing but friendliness wherever I go. || This place is a great spot for food and produce (when the stalls are open), and fresh seafood (when open). The beauty of all of it is how there's a genuine community feeling that's perfect. || Loved this market. Everything was nice and neat. I tried the steak and sushi. The steak was soo good and the bread that they gave us with it was amazing. The sushi also was fresh and well balanced. The atmosphere and the seats were more than average which gave it a hint of 'luxury' as opposed to basic seating. There were fruit shops, cheese shops, wine, and many different cuisines. Unfortunately some of the places were not open but regardless there were plenty of options to choose from . Highly recommend and loved the food after a tiring day walking through Lisbon's hills. Price also was quite cheaper compared to London markets or Paris || I expected more from this market. There is only one stand that makes Portuguese food. Then there is Japanese, Italian, Mexican. Honestly touristic and it’s not worth the visit!! If you stop here just eat at the hummus bar it’s totally worth it!! || Great place to visit to view fresh food stores, great variety of street food outlets and the central bar offers good service wine of the day was excellent, don’t count on thé E28 tram, as it’s not reaching anywhere near the market for the whole of December 2025 || Thought it was an actual market...it isn't...a few market type stalls but mainly eateries...so if you're hungry or thirsty this is the place to go. On the 25E tram route and some very good antique jewelery shops nearby... || IMHO, the best food and drink market in Lisbon. Great for a family reunion with drinks and “world food”. Don’t forget to pass by honey and fruit jam kiosk. I bought sugar cane “melaço”, traditions em brasil’s northeast, where I was born and raised.

Genuinely, the hidden gem of Lisbon. Worth the climb up from the coast and my word, what an attraction!  We had no queue and a very chill inside experience.  Explore (and I do mean explore) the exotic meandering paths through the foliage, it's great to spend an hour or so.  A really nice bio diversity to look at and enjoy. Particularly enjoyed the banana tree 🍌  Really fairly priced and a fantastic cultural excursion.  HUGE recommend✌️ || Estufa Fria is a true oasis of tranquility in the heart of Lisbon. A wonderful place to escape the hustle and bustle of the city and enjoy the beauty of exotic plants, waterfalls, and cozy paths. The atmosphere is truly peaceful, with everything well-kept and thoughtfully designed down to the last detail. A wonderful place for a leisurely stroll, meditation, or a romantic date. A must-see for anyone who loves nature and wants to see a different, greener side of Lisbon. One of the most pleasant and inspiring places in the city! || Nature, garden, and park lovers will enjoy this spot. It offers about 30–45 minutes of peaceful walking surrounded by greenery and a small artificial lake.  Entrance costs less than €4 per person — a very reasonable price for the experience.  There’s also a café with a lovely terrace nearby, though it’s not directly accessible through the greenhouse area. || Verry beautiful, if you are traveling to Lisbon or just live here, I would recommend coming here. It’s very beautiful nature in the middle of the city come here and relax and enjoy your day. also, if you are a student or a younger person, you can get tickets for way cheaper. You just need to show your student card confirmation that you are a student and we paid our tickets for five euros the two of us so that’s amazing. || Really nice and super cheap. Cool plants and I saw baby ducks! there are so many rooms and pathways, despite it not being the biggest building in the world you really feel like you can get lost in there. Very thoughtfully and beautifully designed. || If you’re in Lisbon on a Sunday and want a peaceful escape from the city buzz, Estufa Fria is absolutely perfect. Hidden inside Parque Eduardo VII, this lush greenhouse feels like stepping into another world — calm, green, and full of life. 🌴  You’ll walk through tropical plants, waterfalls, and quiet pathways where time slows down. It’s beautifully maintained, not crowded, and filled with natural light filtering through the glass roof — ideal for a relaxed stroll or quiet reflection.  💚 Perfect for: •	A slow Sunday morning or afternoon •	Nature lovers, photographers, and couples •	Escaping the heat or city noise  Tip: Grab a coffee nearby afterward and enjoy the view over Avenida da Liberdade — it completes the perfect Sunday in Lisbon. || This is a great area to stroll through while enjoying beautiful flora and fauna. It is located at the far end of Eduardo VII Park. We spent 45 minutes there. || This botanical garden is my favourite hidden gem in Lisbon! Lots of great spots inside for photography and well maintained. Very affordable too! 🌿 || Most beautiful garden i have ever seen. So lush and green with the most monstera i have ever seen. So peaceful and relaxing. Toilets inside. Sat with goslings and ducklings and saw chickens and peacocks as well. Student tickets were €1.80! Highly recommend || This botanical garden is a true gem, offering a diverse collection of plants.  The layout is well-designed, creating a tranquil and relaxing atmosphere.  There are numerous benches and open spaces, perfect for enjoying a picnic lunch.  The affordable 3 euro entrance fee makes it an exceptional value.  A visit here is highly recommended for anyone seeking a peaceful escape.  The variety of flora provides something of interest for every visitor.  It's a wonderful place to spend a few hours immersed in nature. || One of the most beautiful botanical gardens I’ve ever visited, interesting and extensive collection and a landscape curated in every detail. || I loved this area! Completely covered with very high bamboo ceilings, feeling like a whole new dimension covered with beautiful foliage and secret passageways leading to different areas such as the cactus covered greenhouse. You could easily spend a few hours here just exploring! || mucho verde y mucha vida, one of the best botanical gardens but a lot of areas were closed :/ nevertheless its worth checking out 🌿🌱☘️🍀🪴🎋🍃 || Thanks for a wonderful evening at Estufa Fria during a gala dinner and the opportunity to catch some glimpses of the wonderful plants and garden setting in a former basalt quarry! || The place is beautiful, many different types of tree and plants but some area are under maintenance, good to visit and the price is inexpensive. || Fantastic place that just kept going on and on. Beautiful hidden caves, waterways with fish and amazing variety of plants. Well worth a visit || Incredible! Well worth a couple hours exploration, this place is huge and well organized to feel endless - lots of little paths through the plants. The cactus room was crazy! I've been twice and would gladly go again. || Hidden gem! Always calm and relaxing here. My absolutely favorite location in Lissabon 😍 Must visit for urban and garden architects. Unique origin of this project will bring you to the tropics right from city. You may wander around by the small paths into the huge monstrera bush or  chill on the bench observing the tiny habitants of the garden - birds and fish 😌 Truly zen space ✨🌱 || Beautiful park filled with surprises. Makes you feel like you’re roaming around the jungle with secret little passages, various birds and a nice pond. Special thanks to Maria da Graça who presented the different bird species to us 🥰 … || Really worth the money as it very big and a lot of things to explore. A lot of great spot to take picture. Student get 50% discount. However, you may need to use cash if you don't have credit card that issued in Portugal.

reviews_content: Eduardo VII Park is one of the most beautiful and relaxing green spaces in Lisbon. The park offers stunning panoramic views over the city and the Tagus River, making it a perfect spot for photos, walks, or simply enjoying the scenery. The wide paths are ideal for walking or jogging, and the well-maintained gardens add a peaceful atmosphere away from the busy city streets. One of the highlights is the impressive geometric garden design and the viewpoint at the top of the park, which provides a breathtaking perspective of Lisbon. The park is also very spacious, so it never feels overcrowded, even during busy hours. There are benches throughout the area, perfect for resting and enjoying the surroundings. Eduardo VII Park is great for families, couples, and solo travelers alike. It’s close to the city center and easy to access, making it a must-visit for anyone exploring Lisbon. Whether you’re looking for a quiet place to relax, take a walk, or admire the city from above, this park is definitely worth a visit. || We were in Lisbon for several days while waiting to start a cruise with NCL.  We stopped at the north end of this magnificent park and walk all the way to the southern end.  Lots of great views and spots for wonderful pics.  Several monuments along the way. || Parque Eduardo VII is a beautiful park with stunning views of the city and the river. It's beautifully maintained, with plenty of greenery and spacious walkways. It's a great place to escape the hustle and bustle of the city, take beautiful photos, and simply enjoy the atmosphere. A must-see if you're in Lisbon. || It's quite an amazing space. Whether it's chilling, or events, or testing your photographic prowess, it fits the bill. There are usually tourists and residents generally around, and it's more lively during celebrations like Christmas. || It's a very beautiful and large park, perfect for a peaceful walk surrounded by nature. The view from the top of the park is spectacular. Depending on the time of year, there may be more or fewer tourists. On a sunny day with good weather, it's well worth a visit. || A great view of Lisbon from here, you can see the whole layout and scale looking down towards the river. Relaxed and friendly atmosphere as you view the scenery and monuments. You also get an excellent view of the planes coming into Lisbon. || A beautiful public park in Lisbon, Portugal with great views over the city. The top is great for photos. Good for a walk, sit and have lunch or a drink, or have your dog play around. || Wonderful Christmas Atmosphere! We visited Parque Eduardo VII during the Christmas season, and it was a fantastic experience. The Christmas market (Wonderland Lisboa) created such a pleasant and fun atmosphere. It’s a great spot, especially for young people and families, with plenty of amusement park rides, games, and festive food stalls. The park itself is beautiful, and the view from the top is breathtaking. Highly recommended if you are in Lisbon during the holidays! || Parque Eduardo VII is one of the best spots in Lisbon to enjoy a peaceful walk and take in a great view of the city. From the top of the park, you can see all the way down to the river and the Praça Marquês de Pombal. It’s a lovely place to relax, especially at sunset. The park is also very close to El Corte Inglés, so it’s easy to combine a visit with some shopping or a coffee break nearby. || What a great parque / jardim in central Lisbon. Plenty of spaces to walk and sit with many great restaurants, cafes , and quiosques nearby to enjoy the warm Lisbon sun || Iconic park in central Lisbon. You can get the hop on bus at this location or just walk all the way up from the roundabout to get a nice view of the city and take a picture near a Lisboa sign. || A beautiful park! You can exercise, enjoy nature, and relax. It’s very well maintained! || Beautiful lookout over the city towards the water. If you like vistas, definitely a must see. Also check the smaller part of the park across the road (more north), for a super cute cafe near a small pond. || It is a beautiful public park in Lisbon, Portugal. The park occupies an area of 26 hectares (64 acres). The park was built in the first half of the 20th century to restore public green space. The park's central strip, covered with grass, is flanked by long Portuguese paved walkways. The park is at a gradient from the top observation deck you can see it well. Well manicured lawns and hedges. The top of the park is a has the Monument to the Carnation Revolution, flanked by two sets of two obelisks. Car park nearby and easy walk to observation deck. Wear comfy shoes, take water, wear hat, sunscreen. Great place for photography || Very large sloping park mainly put over to trees and grass. Lovely view from the top across the city. Interesting sculpture here too. || Scenic views with many diverse places to sun, shade, relax and explore. Bonus that buildings include the Carlos Lopes Pavilion, restaurants and world class arboretum inside the grounds || Beautiful monument in this lovely park and long Avenue which can be admired from top and bottom.  On a nice day can see far away. || This turned out to be an unexpected city walk.This park is great for a stroll and offers views of much of the Lisbon! There are also orange trees and a small amusement area inside, and it might be even livelier if you come in the evening. || This is the largest park in Lisbon, named in honor of King Edward VII of the United Kingdom following his visit to Portugal in 1903. It features formal gardens, greenhouses, and wide open paths—making it ideal for walking, relaxing, or simply enjoying nature in the city. At the top of the park, a scenic viewpoint offers sweeping views over Lisbon and the Tagus River. The park is also home to the annual Lisbon Book Fair, one of the city’s most popular cultural events. || Super views over Lisbon. Good for a walk around if that’s what you want plus photos at the top of the park. Well looked after.

This is a stunning building. I did not find the tombs nearly as interesting as the building itself. Climbing the stairs (181 to get to the very top) was worth the effort. There are viewing balconies at each level and then you can go outside at the top and look over the city. There was an interesting display on the Mexican custom of Day of the Dead also, though I wasn’t quite sure why it was there. We had no wait to get in on a Wednesday morning. || American Traveler here. We stumbled upon this place as we were at a Saturday flea market. I thought the outside architecture was beautiful. I loved the curves and sharpness. Even on a Saturday the wait time was a little long. They only allowed a certain amount of people in at a time. The gift shop was closed at the time. Absolutely beautiful inside and if you go upstairs you have a great view of the city. A must see! || Lovely building. There are some runs of well known people. . The best views 360 degrees is you go up to around 200 steps. || Even though I have the utmost respect for this place, I cannot shake the feeling that there’s something wrong. It does honor important Portuguese figures who shouldered the foundations of the country and state next to a soccer player. Weren’t there more people to celebrate for their courage against state enemies? Artists that created lasting cultural shifts like fado (there's one)? The history of the place is where it hits home, and I recommend you read about it and visit it for its charm rather than for most of the resting souls it hosts. The terrace is also a thing, if you like stunning views of roofs and the port. || Beautiful! Heads up, if the weather is shitty you can’t go outside on the Terrence. So I would recommended buying tickets when you get there so you know if it is open or not. Still beautiful inside but same price. In November we had no line ups. || Definitely not the most interesting place in Lisbon. The rooftop area is decent, but there’s no particularly beautiful view. || This is a must see in Lisbon. Great views of the city and amazing architecture. Even if your not religious or interested in burial chambers, the views and inside of this building are beautiful. Student discount available and no waiting times || The building itself is magnificent, there are a lot of small rooms, old narrow stairs and tombs, a bit scary. But the rooftop has a great view over the Tagus river || With the Lisboa card, the entrance is free! Go straight up to the top and enjoy the view of the pantheon from the top and also view of Lisbon. || Though smaller than other national pantheons I’ve visited, Lisbon’s National Pantheon is exceptionally well-maintained and offers a distinct charm all its own. What stood out most was the integration of contemporary artistic collaborations, which breathe new life into the space without overshadowing its historical weight.  The structure itself is elegant and serene, and the modern touches serve as a powerful reminder of how history and memory continue to evolve. It’s a quiet, reflective place—less grandiose, but deeply intentional in its presentation.  A meaningful stop for those who appreciate heritage spaces that honour the past while embracing the present. || Honestly, we only went because we had the Lisboa Card, but we ended up having a great time and learning more about the Portugal. The architecture and the views are truly worth seeing. || Included in my lisboa card and well worth it! While not the largest space, it was still interesting and appreciated being able to read the summaries in english. My only complaint is the lack of signage for where to walk (perhaps this is due to only being english speaking) but I only found out I could reach the rooftop from realizing there were people looking down from higher levels. There was also a very small hidden art gallery on the way back down! The 360 degree view at the top makes the whole thing worth it honestly. || Used the lisboa card and came here for free, the ticket machine was easy to use and there was no queue at all! The inside of the pantheon was huge and going to the 4th floor you will see this amazing panoramic view of the city! || The tickets are quite affordable if you compare it with other historical places. The view is just wonderful, even if you don’t go to the terrace of the pantheon, which may take an extra payment. Hence it is located in Alfama, you can keep walking around to visit other touristic attractions in the neighborhood, after here. And it’s very close if you take the metro below. || Arrived 45 minutes before closing but still had enough time to enjoy our visit. Not a huge amount to see but what there is is worth going to, the architecture is cool and nice views from the top out towards the city. || It's on a hill like most places in Lisbon. A collection of graves and memorial coffins for some famous people including Vasco de Gamma who is buried at jeronimos monastery, not here. Maybe you can spend 45 minutes here. || A beautiful structure in the form of a pantheon.   It is now a museum and the place is awesome.   Interestingly enough that this pantheon allows visitors to climb all the way to the top.   One can go outside at the top to get views of Lisbon.   Overall, a must visit in Lisbon. || The National Pantheon in Lisbon is an impressive and beautiful landmark that is well worth visiting. The architecture is grand and elegant, with stunning details inside and out. Climbing to the upper level rewards you with breathtaking panoramic views over the city and the river. The atmosphere inside feels calm and respectful, making it a meaningful place to explore both for its history and its beauty. A must-see spot when discovering Lisbon. || Very beautiful and historical place in Lisbon. Although walking is quite challenging due to steep streets yet it is a must visit place for visitors. You can have a few very scenic view points where you can take a few snaps for your memory. || 🏛️ Where Silence Meets Grandeur — A Monument to Portugal’s Soul ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)  If you're in Lisbon and even remotely interested in architecture, history, or panoramic views — don’t skip the Panteão Nacional (also known as Santa Engrácia Church). It’s far more than just another old building.  Originally designed as a church in the 17th century, this structure took nearly 300 years to complete — and today it serves as Portugal’s National Pantheon, honoring the country’s most iconic figures. It’s where Amália Rodrigues, the queen of Fado, rests — alongside presidents, writers, explorers, and cultural legends.  Inside, the atmosphere is calm and solemn, with towering white marble columns, symmetrical floor patterns, and an incredible sense of scale. The central dome rises above you like a marble sky, and every step echoes — adding to the spiritual stillness of the space.  One of the best parts? You can walk all the way up to the rooftop terrace, which gives you a 360-degree view over Lisbon’s Alfama district and the shimmering Tagus River. The view alone is worth the small entry fee.  Quick Ratings: Historical Significance: 10/10 Interior Architecture: 9.5/10 Rooftop View: 10/10 Atmosphere & Serenity: 9/10 Photo Opportunities: 9.5/10  Tip: Go earlier in the day to avoid crowds, and take your time — this place isn’t meant to be rushed.  📝 If this review helped or inspired your visit, a quick 👍 would be appreciated!  I share real cultural stops across Europe — feel free to explore my other reviews.

Built in the middle of the last century in neo-Gothic style, it is dedicated to Don Nuno Alvares Pereira, a …

One of the highlights of Estrela. One of the main Lisbon churches due to its size and beauty. You can visit for free but you'll need to pay to go to the rooftop. Beautiful paintings that contribute to the espiritual experience. Parking available just next to the church but it's usually quite full. You can also visit the park just across the street. A metro station is being built which will make it more accessible. || You can pay 5 € to walk up to the roof top. 20% off with Lisboa card and a million steps. The view is amazing. You also get to see inside of the basilica from the top- close to the dome. Also- Jesus dine with the 12 around a round table. || It is an absolute must see! One of the prettiest Basilicas we've visited. And we were able to access the roof and walk around the inside of the church from above and look down into the sanctuary. Absolutely gorgeous! || The interior is splendid. The ceiling, dome and floor are colorful. Paintings are fabulous. The ambience is serene. || The inside of the cathedral is free and breathtaking. there is a core beam of light that shines on you like a spot light for judgement of course.  For the bathroom. You need exact 0.50€ to use it and the post cards are exactly 0.50€ if you need change. I did the €5 climb which was not worth so buy the postcard instead and enjoy a clean private wc. The light goes off automatically but I just used my phone flashlight.  Update: I walked across the street to the Jardin and there is a free bathroom in the “casa de jardin estrella”. Do that. || Very ancient Basilica. It was indeed an Awesome Place, a must visit Place in Lisbon. It is a silent place to be with God. || After years of passing by outside, finally went in and was pleasantly surprised. It is not a giant cathedral, but it has enough of an imposing presence to allow one to appreciate the multiple altars and cruciform architecture. Also a pleasant surprise came in the form of the possibility of climbing to the rooftop from where you can have a look around the area at a very budget friendly price. Just be sure to be away from the belltowers when the full set goes off at, for example, 11:50 on a Sunday morning. || Known for its beautiful dome and interior, the Basílica da Estrela is one of Lisbon's most impressive monuments. The Basílica da Estrela in Lisbon was the first church in the world dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, built by Queen Maria I, and houses her tomb. It is also known for its large dome that dominates the Lisbon skyline, a remarkable baroque nativity scene, and its impressive neoclassical architecture. || I like to recommend everyone to visit this place it’s very peaceful n nice food with handmade dumpling thank u || Very beautiful and peaceful interior to the church. The floor of the church is particularly stunning in its design. We paid the 5 euros each to go to the rooftop. It was pleasant but for us, not worth the price.  Much prefer the pantheon rooftop.  The climb via a narrow spiral staircase is quite steep with just enough room to pass people - it is fun to go up. The view from the rooftop is nice and the dome is beautiful (you can see it close up from access from the rooftop terrace - mind your head going in 🤕) || Beautiful building and great to go up to the top to explore the roof and dome. || One of fav places in Lisbon. Very intricate details of the dome and arches. A must-visit spot for the  moment of peace and awe. Highly recommend spending time here to soak in serenity. || Sit down inside and settle your soul or admire the interior. || The beautiful colors of the church all come of different colors of marble. Blue, green, pink, yellow and grey marbles carefully carved for a harmonious result. The polished marbles shine like jewels. The interior is breathtaking. (Today's prices for blue marble is 2000e/m2), The rooftop  was nice, with the bells banging at five  a'clock and sun setting in the Atlantic ocean. || A basilica and a national heritage of Portugal. Built around 1780 this is the first church dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus. It is very good and the dome above the altar is wonderful. || It is a beautiful building inside and out, seen from below and above. Gorgeous decorations, works of art painted and carved in stone. The combination of natural light from the dome and the artificial lighting covers the interior in a special mix of colours. The roof offers great views of Lisbon in all directions. || Impressive creamy white late baroque church with a truly spectacular “terrace” on the roof of the nave, which is like something out of a movie set. Price to climb the spiral stairs is just 3€, and a small door in the dome also gives you a scary view straight down into the church itself—be mindful of the loooooow balustrade and also the electric wires running around the edge of the roof to keep the birds away ⚡️🐥⚡️ || The church, which was built in the Estrela neighborhood as a dedication by Queen Maria I of Portugal, whose wish for an heir was fulfilled, takes its name from this district. Since it is dedicated to the heart of Jesus, it is also known as the Convent of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus.  The church, which we can call the Baroque style, has a remarkable splendor and a beautiful architecture. The entrance is free, but I can say that the Bema section is viewed from a bit of a distance. There was a fee to access the terrace of the church. Since our visit was in the evening, we could not go to the roof, but I think the view is very beautiful with the Estrela park opposite.  I should also point out that the huge dome of the church, located in the hilly part of the neighborhood in the west of Lisbon, can be seen from many points in the surrounding area. If you take a nice route to the church, I think you can enjoy watching this dome until you get close. || Beautiful old church. When we visited the church, on a Monday around 11.30 in the morning, there was a service ongoing which ended around 12.30.  It’s a beautiful church but do not plan a whole afternoon for the visit, it’s not a very big church.  There’s an option to burn a candle for € 0,50.  Make sure to also visit the park behind the church, absolutely worth the visit. || It was a lot of fun to the climb 114 stairs to the roof. Some sections had no barriers 😫

I was particularly struck by the variety of graffiti and the seemingly well-executed work. Graffiti brightens Lisbon, making it much more attractive and freer. || Street art is everywhere in Lisbon! Impressive, fantastic, and surprising, and of truly great artistic value! These pictures show just a few of these gems. || I love street art, so Lisbon in general is a feast for the eyes. During my recent visit to Lisbon, I had the pleasure of exploring the Chafariz das Necessidades, an enchanting historical site nestled in the heart of the city. As I stepped into the meticulously landscaped gardens surrounding the fountain, I was immediately captivated by the serene ambiance and the sense of tranquility that enveloped the area.  The Chafariz das Necessidades, dating back to the 18th century, boasts stunning Baroque architecture and intricate detailing, making it a true gem of Lisbon's cultural heritage. The central fountain, adorned with ornate sculptures and cascading water features, served as a picturesque focal point amidst the lush greenery and vibrant flowers that adorned the gardens.  Exploring the grounds, I couldn't help but feel transported back in time, imagining the aristocrats and nobles who once strolled through these very gardens centuries ago. The meticulously manicured pathways led me through a captivating array of flora, from vibrant azaleas to towering palm trees, creating a delightful sensory experience at every turn.  One of the highlights of my visit was ascending the grand staircase to the upper terrace, where I was treated to breathtaking panoramic views of Lisbon's skyline and the Tagus River beyond. It was the perfect spot to pause and soak in the beauty of the city, while reflecting on the rich history and cultural significance of this remarkable landmark.  Overall, my visit to the Chafariz das Necessidades was a truly memorable experience, offering a delightful blend of history, art, and natural beauty. Whether you're a history buff, a nature enthusiast, or simply seeking a peaceful retreat from the hustle and bustle of city life, this hidden gem is not to be missed during your time in Lisbon. || At the heart of the garden lies the Chafariz das Necessidades, an ornate fountain commissioned by King João V in 1747. This baroque masterpiece features a central obelisk surrounded by sculptures of dolphins and sea creatures, creating a captivating focal point. || I have visited there at night and no water in fountain.  Need more maintenance. Historic place. || Cute spot with a lookout towards the bridge. Interesting museum across the road too; pretty building. || Chafariz das Necessidades is a very beautiful water fountain in a park right in front of a government building. Is empty and it looks like it's a little rundown || Great spot for sunset || A viewpoint, with hidden a park. || Located in Largo das Necessidades, in front of the Palace of the same name, this fountain stands in the center of the Olavo Bilac Garden, named after the Brazilian writer and poet born in 1865.  It dates from 1747 and is part of the Palace complex, having resulted from a vow made by King João V to the Virgin Mary.  Its authorship is attributed to the architect Caetano Tomás de Sousa, author of the execution project of the Palace.  In the middle of a tank that receives water from four gargoyles of Baroque inspiration, rises an obelisk topped by a bronze cross that crowns a monstrance of thorns that accentuates the religious character of the monument.

The Amoreiras 360º Panoramic View is worth checking out if you want to see Lisbon from above. You get a full view of the city, from the Tagus River to the bridges and all the colorful rooftops. It’s not as crowded as some of the other viewpoints, which makes it a nice spot to take your time and enjoy.  The entrance is through the shopping center, so it’s easy to grab a coffee or a snack before or after. The price is fair for the experience, and the staff were helpful. A great way to get a sense of the city’s layout and take some beautiful photos. || Beautiful views. Cost: €5 for adults, tickets can be purchased at the information desk on the first floor. The service was a bit rude. We were watched by security the whole time, the lady just stood in the corner and stared at us, which was a bit awkward. || Very nice views of Lisbon.. staff are also friendly, worth the visit and it is quite affordable || Wow! What a fantastic view! Literally 360 views of Lisbon with helpful maps outlining what you can see. Went on a sunny day so had an amazing view - all the way to the sea in one direction and airport runway in another. Well worth the 5€ entrance. We were the only people up there and it was really clean with lots of seating and fixed binoculars for close up views. Well worth a visit. || Superb. We had the place virtually to ourselves (possibly due to the possibility of dramatic weather). Really liked it here, nice and peaceful with amazing views. || Well worth the entrance fee. Best view of lisbon in the city 😍 could have stayed up there for hours. Was too hot thou.. can see all landmarks for and the telescopes (3) give you an even better view.. || Beautiful view of Lisbon from up high. We were alone, it had recently rained and we could see rainbows. One by one, airplanes were flying over our heads. There are binoculars on the platform and you can watch the planes land at the airport. This observation deck made a cool impression on us. || A view definitely worth coming here and going up with the elevator the 18 stories to the rooftop of the building. Especially when the weather is fine, the sight is clear for kilometers on end and the sky is nothing but blue. I did enjoy it a lot. || Amazing experience! We very highly recommend 😍 you'll have a very beautiful view all over Lisbon. I recommend to came as late as possible for a night view but take care, admissions are not possible 30min before the closure. … || An observation deck placed on the top of a new, modern building. In the same building is a shopping center. The tickets are available in the lobby, at the info point. From here you have to go to the first level of the shopping center and from here you will take an elevator to the top. Nice 360 degrees views from there, worth the visit. I visited it late in the evening, with about 30 minutes before the closing time. It wasn't crowded at all, there were only 3 other people. || It's an observation deck, way above Lisbon as this tall building (in Lisbon standards) sits on a high hill already. In a good day one can see much of the meteopolitan area of Lisbon: Serra da Luz to the North, Arrábida to the South, the Tagus river mouth to the West... It is also unique in that it looks at Lisbon from an unusual west side perspective, where few as tall a building exist.  Access isn't free. Tickets are bought at the information counter on the ground floor (5€), and access to the lifts is on the first floor, up the escalators, at the end of a narrow long corridor, but easy enough to find.  It is not wheelchair accessible and there is a flight of stairs to reach to viewing deck.  The view is spectacular but that's it. There is nothing but the view, some binoculars (coin actioned), marble floor and glass railings. No benches, nor a coffee service, nor souvenir shop. Which can be relaxing in a way, and it guarantees there aren't crowds either. || Took the trip for the sunset viewing- for €5 it’s well worth the value as well to capture glistening views of the city from various points. The staff and security were helpful, accommodating and being solo they were  kind to take photos for me. A worthwhile tip is to get there for 5:00pm as the winter hours are much more reduced now. || After several free of charge panoramic views over Lisbon, we were doubtful of paying 5e for another view, but the view was worth it. Beautiful Lisbon with beautful sky with fast sailing clouds. || One of the best panoramic platforms I have visited. The edge is inset from the building, so you don’t get vertigo. Only 5€ to get up, free for kids, great value. Also, the telescopes are free, no coins needed. You can see all of Lisbon and its beauty in one place. || We were on the 11 floor,wonderful view,  no water pressure, old and needs to be fixed up and brought into the future,  we tried to use the fire escape but the Doors were locked, because floors 10 to 1 are apartment, they need to do something about the breakfast ,very little variety,. || Very nice place to overview the all town and decide where to go. There are 3 binoculars to zoom in to most famous places. || Nice view... after all Lisbon's views are the best! However, as local, I think a little bit expensive (5Euros) just to see the view specially when you have so may places in Lisbon where you can get nice views and for free. Anyway, I got some pictures from my own city! || Extremely recommended this place to visit! Amazing views! Even in the cloudy ⛅ All binoculars are free. Try to make a photo from the ocular - it's cool! || Good viewpoint and that's it. You are far away from all interesting places. Thay are too small for the viewer. In my point of view the viewpoint from the Castelo de S. Jorge is much better. || Amazing for photographers, people who are looking for amazing pics should go on sunrise, not sunset. That way there's less people and less cluster. However the sun isn't in an optional direction if you're looking for better lighting.

If you’re in Lisbon and willing to climb a very steep Alfama hill (yes, your quads will complain), Santo António rewards you with a truly excellent pastel de nata. The custard is silky, the pastry has a satisfying crackle.  This place is absolutely worth the detour, especially if you enjoy pairing your pastries with a scenic cardio workout on the way up. || It was time for my daily dose of Pastel de Nata. Before heading up to the Castle of Saint George in Lisbon, I stopped at this pastelaria for a quick energy boost. The tart was good, flaky, and creamy, though not my personal favorite so far. For my taste, the sugar leaned a little higher than the perfectly balanced ones I’ve had elsewhere. The staff were friendly, which made the visit even nicer. Overall, a sweet little stop before tackling the castle tour. || Authentic pastel de nata at its best. Freshly baked since the place is always crowded. They have good ice cream too! Tried it in Sept 2025. || One of the best [pastel de nata] i had :) Not too sweet or slimy & good filling and pastry.  There are more table and seats on the second floor which had a lovely view. And they have decent toilet. Super recommend! || Amazing pastel de natis, crisp flaky pastry with a warm, creamy, smooth custard filling - include a stop here on your wanders around the area || We were on a walking tour and this was one of the stops! When you come to Portugal, you must try the Pastel De Nata. It is a custard pastry, made with eggs/cream. I am not a custard person , but I have to say, the pastry is delicious! I didn't have one here because I had one the day before and if it's anything like the one I'd tried, it simply melts in your mouth, once you bite into that flaky crust! My goodness 😋 They had other pastries and everything looked good! My daughter opted for the cheesecake. It was cute! The place was busy and the outside of the building was very interesting. Loves the titles ❤️ || Amazing Pastel de Natas and the coffee was also great. Plenty of seating upstairs so you could sit down and relax and enjoy || I'm on a quest to find the very best Pastel de Nata in town, and I've been following the advice of locals to sample these delicious pastries from various renowned bakeries. It's been an incredible culinary adventure, leading me to discover so many amazing places and hidden food gems. And this particular bakery? It's definitely a standout! Their Pastel de Nata is, without a doubt, a must-try.  It's absolutely fantastic. The pastry is perfectly flaky and light, providing a delicate crunch that gives way to the rich, creamy custard filling.  The balance of flavors is spot-on – just the right amount of sweetness with a hint of cinnamon that elevates the whole experience.  It's clear they use high-quality ingredients and time-honored techniques to create a truly exceptional Pastel de Nata. I've been incredibly impressed with the quality and variety of Pastel de Nata I've encountered on this taste-testing journey, and this bakery has earned a top spot on my list.  If you're a fan of these Portuguese treats (and who isn't?), you absolutely have to try the ones here.  You won't be disappointed!  This is definitely one of the best I've had, and I highly recommend it. || Delicious Pastel de Nata, we've tried them in several places, and these are among the best.  The balance of sweetness in the custard and the delicate, crispy pastry is perfect. Additionally, you can watch the desserts being made, which is really fascinating.  The coffee is also quite good.  You can sit by the window on the second floor and enjoy a peaceful atmosphere. || This cafe had a great selection of pastries and the cappuccinos were amazing as well. The staff was very kind. There is spacious upstairs seating and clean restrooms. I would definitely recommend this cafe if you’re wanting a quick bite to eat!

This bakery is AMAZING. Came first thing in the morning and got a pastry and a fresh loaf of bread and both were amazing. They were warm because they were freshly made and the flavors were perfect. It was cheap and the street that this place is on is right next to a street car and overall has a wonderful vibe. 10/10! || I’ve tried many bakeries in Lisbon and this is definitely the best one! The cinnamon roll is a must, so crispy and fresh. The focaccia is also divine. || Super fresh and delicious bread baked just behind the counter. The owner was friendly and told us about each bread and which ones we should get. The breads were very tasty and I would love to visit again for their pizza which they start serving at 6pm! || Best bakery in Portugal fr! This is my partner’s and my fave and we didn’t even have it fresh, but the flavours still held up so well. We honestly wished we bought more! || We walked in by chance while taking photos of the bondinho and found this cozy little gem. Ended up staying longer than planned — the pastries, coffee, and beers were all fantastic. Luis was super welcoming and great to talk to. Such a chill vibe. Definitely recommend stopping by!! || We ordered a baked good relatively late in the day, and, while we expected it to be dry, it was still moist. It'd be far nicer had there been (shaded) seating outside, but it's really just a hole in the wall. || Amazing.  This place is well worth the stars and price. We arrived at 9am the bread was just finishing. Wow. The pao de queijo was incredible. It almost was like mochi consistency. Sooo ono. 10 out of 10 would recommend. || Absolutely amazing bakery! their bread smells amazing and their sundried tomato pastries are phenomenal. then there´s the cinnamon roll  is great too! great and friendly service too! 10/10 should visit! || Impressive- 67 5.0 reviews and here is another. Difficult decisions as to what to choose-everything looks amazing. We took home a delicious chocolate babbcah, two cinnamon rolls because no one wanted to share too much (we are three), two loaves of bread for the week and one more cherry pastry…. Walking to the car we could not resist tasting the bread- super yummy, proper sourdough with a lightness. I would love to learn from them how they do it. We waited to get home for coffee to try the pastries- also delicious. Will definitely return. || I found the bakery by chance, when I was on the walk. I had a nice chat with the owner who told me a story behind his business. But, most of all, he explained to me the process of his bread making. The bread is healthy and tasty. Souredough. I'll try other products when I'll be visiting Lisbon again.

We stumbled upon this place by chance and we’re so happy we did. Serena our host was amazing and explained everything to us (including the story of the shop). We took two types of sweets and 2 cup of coffee. Coffee was amazing as well as the tart. However, our mind was blown by the other sweet (it didn’t have a name so we called it Tropical Happiness). We never had something like this before, each bite brought in a refreshing taste and the whole experience was a delight. We are honored that we are the 1st to review this shop as it opened recently. Highly recommend, will definitely come back again and again. || Adorable place, recently opened. They  bake daily and during the day.So,the pastries available will  be different during the day, freshly baked in the Atelier. Probably the best brownie i've ever had! Also tasty vegan croissants. Beautiful gold china, and a proper good size tea cup and pot. Ann was there today and she's super friendly as well as her staff (Serena). Just go! You won't regret it! || ,A lovely coffee shop The products change daily, so every day is a new surprise. For those looking for a quiet and magical place, go there, you won't regret it.

place_name: Cake Fiesta Portugal (Online Pre Ordered Cake house, Not a Shop)
reviews_content: I planned a surprise birthday trip to Lisbon fpr my wife and tried to get a cake for her. Luckily I found this service located close by. Amazing service, super friendly contact and fair prices. The cakes are just beautiful and most importantly tasty. So glad I stumbled upon this place! Can fully recommend! || thank you so much 🌸 … || I contacted them via Whatsapp to order a birthday cake for my wife. They responded immediately and communicated well throughout. It was a <24h order and I requested a Harry Potter themed cake. The cake turned out beautifully and was delicious as well. Professionally packaged as well, so I had no issues taking it home safely. A very good experience. Will be ordering from them again. || thank you so much 💙 … || I gave the order for birthday cake for my son and the order was ready within very short time. The cake was fantastic. It was exactly the same design which I asked for. I just loved the quick service. The price is completely economical. || Ordered a jungle-themed cake from CakeFiesta for my son's first birthday, and it exceeded all expectations! Beautifully decorated, delicious, and full of flavor: three tiers with three different flavors. Everyone loved it. Highly recommended! || Thank you so much 🙏 … || Fantastic cake .. Respond quickly 5 star. Delicious taste . God bless Best regards SaViOn family || thank you so much 🌸 … || Amazing birthday cake! We ordered a few days before arriving in Lisbon and had a very lovely black forest cake :) the owner was very easy to reach and always kept me updated! Would definitely recommend anyone looking for a cake in Lisbon! || This cake was just perfect not only in the taste but also in the decoration! Rezwana has a talent for baking cakes and with no doubts this was the best birthday cake I tried in Lisbon! I am already suggesting to my friends || Thank you so much 💙 … || I’m from Australia and my friend who lives in Portugal is birthday today, didn’t know anyone from there or even know a cake shop nearby. Luckily this beautiful lady and her business come across when I look up. I ordered personalised cake in such a last minute time, I thought it was impossible but she made it possible. The cake was beautiful and tasted amazing. All have been perfect and beyond delicious. Definitely had a great experience with this business. From the awesome customer service, delivered to town out of Lisbon, to the quality of the cake, I am extremely satisfied. Best experience ever!! || thank you so much 💙 … || I wanted find a good bakery for birthday cake in Lisbon and didn’t want to go to traditional Portuguese bakeries since I don’t like the taste very much. I found this place in Google and the reviews are good, so I ordered one from Facebook page. I did not regret it. From the service to the quality and the taste of cake, price are all wonderful. The lady is also very kind, response messages very quickly. The cake is freshly made on the same day of pick up. I really have nothing bad to say. It was a great experience and I am happy to found this little gem in Lisbon. || thank you so much 💙 … || Oh my god… the cake was fab.. i still remember the taste .. the design was amazing taste was yumm.. wat else u want in a cake.. the owner  is really very kind and understands what u r expecting in a cake .. it was for my husband birthday but i think i finished it 😛 i finally have some goto cake shop.. loved it . Delivery was also at perfect time.

I'm so glad we came to this little bakery to discover such a great variety of local treats, sweet and savory (chicken bun is absolutely amazing). The coffee is also soooo good! The staff is also very kind. Highly recommended this place! || My favorite spot near home is perfect for breakfasts, especially for enjoying an arrufada ou pão de deus, which is definitely my favorite treat there.  The place is small but cozy, and the staff is always friendly. The food is of high quality and reasonably priced. Just a heads up, if you want to pay by card, you need to spend over 5 euros, so be sure to bring some cash as well. || We walked her twice in our stay in Lisbon for the variety of breads, pastries, coffee, and breakfast items. Friendly staff and at least one seems to work daily who speaks English very well. Delicious coffee, pastries, and breakfast and we wish we'd found this place earlier! Lots of locals, but still friendly to the few tourists who also showed up in the morning. || This place was a nice little insight of the real citizens. They take a coffee in a Break or buy there bread for the day. The service was very friendly. The food was delicious. || Lisbon is beautiful and historical but very busy. We often didn’t get good service. But not at Forno de Sapadores. The coffee is the best I had in the town (if you want coffee with milk ask for meia de leite). They sell all sorts of bread but also sweet treats and the staff is always kind and helpful.  For me this was the one remarkable food place in Lisbon. || One of the best bakeries in Lisbon. Bread is excellent. Prices are a bit above average, but if they were to add a hipster vibe to the place - it could have been even higher. Service is slow and it is tiny inside, but the right way to consume products from here is a takeaway - to the nearest park or a bench. || One of the best bakeries I’ve been to. A must when you’re in Lisbon. || Great range of pastry and bread, at least from our non-portuguese perspective. very high standard. || Food is delicious, good coffe and friendly staff. Highly recommend when in the area. || Such a cute local cafe, with the best selection of pastries, bread, sandwiches, sweet treats… people are so friendly and welcoming. || Perfect place to have a breakfast..amazing sweets and cakes, i wish i could taste everything.. || Delicious pastries and really nice service :) || Seriously good bread! And very cheap also. Although i have not much experience with Pastel de Nata, i found them delicious. Very friendly staff. || Superb bakery. Splendid coffee, delicious pastries and most importantly, a wonderful staff. Also popular with locals, making the atmosphere great as well. || This bakery is simply amazing, and it seems to get better and better! Don’t miss the Pão d água — possibly the best bread I’ve ever had! Torrada makes a nice simple breakfast and the pastries and cookies are fantastic. In the winter months the soups are also delicious. I visit every day when I am staying in the area. || A really great bakery. A simple place, with just two tables inside, but delicious food (including some of the best pão de deus I had in Lisbon) and lovely, friendly staff who were patient with my attempts to speak Portuguese. I stayed nearby and went in at least once a day for almost a month. I was sad to leave it behind. || This is an awesome Portuguese bakery with delicious bread, a great variety of pastries and lovely employees. The best thing is that you can try a lot of them, because they offer Pasteis de Nata, Bola de Berlim and other sweet pastries as miniature versions 😍 … || One of my favorite padarias in Lisbon, very recommended. Great bread and food, perfect carcaças And a great service, very kind people. || Such a lovely local bakery where all the sweet grannies and people from neighbourhood get their bread and pastry. People working there are friendly and efficient. And the pasty is very good! So tempting to go there ☺️ || This is such a lovely local bakery. Everything I got there was delicious. I don't speak any Portuguese and they were so incredibly kind and helpful. Makes me wish I lived here.

They’re all over Lisbon, and if you can’t make it to Pastéis de Belém in the Belém district, this bakery is a great alternative for enjoying the famous pastel de nata. The crust was flaky and perfectly complemented the soft, creamy custard filling.  We ended up buying several boxes to take home with us, and they made great gifts. Convenient, delicious, and a solid option when you’re craving a classic Portuguese treat. || The egg tarts were one of the best we had in Lisbon! You can even see the workers making the tarts which was very cool to see. The only issue is that this location doesn’t have much space to stand. But it is worth it since the pastel de natas are soo good || Hi Saloni. Thank you for your feedback. We would be delighted to welcome you to Manteigaria in Rua Augusta, Time Out Market, Alvalade, Belém, Campo de Ourique, Parque das Nações and Saldanha where you can sit and enjoy the pastel de nata on the terrace. We look forward to see you again soon. || Hands down, the best pastel de nata I’ve ever tried in Lisbon! It’s different from the egg tarts I’m used to from Asia, but the custard here is incredibly fresh, creamy, and perfectly balanced. The crust is delightfully crispy, and I love that you can sprinkle cinnamon powder on top or enjoy it as is—both ways are amazing! This is an absolute must-try spot for anyone visiting Lisbon. Highly recommend! || The best Paste de Nata in the whole Lisbon. The bakery is very tiny, but such a mesmerizing. You can watch the pastry chefs prepare these desserts live. The staff is very polite and pleasant – your mood is lifted after visiting. I definitely recommend it. || Really great, rich, custard filling. Could eat it all day. Unfortunately the crust was a bit soft and lacked any crunch.  Really convenient and cute place to stand at the counter and observe the magic happen from being the glass. || Hi Rui. Thank you for your feedback and we're sorry about what happened. Our customers' feedback is very important to us so that we can continually improve our service and provide unique experiences.  We look forward to seeing you again soon. || Such good Pan de Nata! Queue moves super fast, staff is friendly, card payment, practical packaging and multiple presentations (1 pan, 2, 6, etc). Price is €1.50 per Pan, they also have coffee, lemonade, etc. No place to seat, so 100% take away. || Title: Good in Small Doses  Manteigaria is one of those places you *have* to try in Lisbon, and yes—the pastel de nata lives up to the hype… but only to a point. The first one or two are lovely: crisp shell, creamy custard, that iconic warm comfort. But if you overindulge, the charm starts slipping. The more you pay attention to the flavor details, the more it shifts from “wow” to “hmm, maybe not as magical as I thought.”  Coffee was fine, nothing to write home about. I also tried their glühwein, which turned out both pricey and un-drinkable—one sip was more than enough.  The setup is convenient, though. They’ve got a stand where you can grab a pastel on the spot (probably the best way to enjoy it—fresh, hot, and fleeting), or place an order to take away.  Overall: worth trying, especially if you’re in Chiado/Baixa and want that Lisbon pastry experience. Just don’t get carried away—sometimes less really is more. || Hi Manja. We appreciate your feedback and visit. We hope to see you again soon. || Lovely pastel de nata — very creamy and delicious! Definitely worth the hype. As December is off-peak, I assumed there wouldn’t be a queue, but there was one. That said, it moved quickly and there was no real wait time; you go in and they serve you straight away. || Manteigaria is truly a temple of the famous Portuguese pastel de nata, and it’s easy to see why it’s a must-visit in Lisbon. The moment you step in, you’re greeted by the aroma of freshly baked custard tarts wafting from the open kitchen, where trays of golden-brown pastries are pulled straight from the ovens.  The pastel de nata here is perfection — warm, flaky, and buttery on the outside, with a silky custard that’s rich and just the right amount of sweet. The slight caramelized top adds a beautiful touch of bitterness that balances every bite. A light dusting of cinnamon and powdered sugar takes it to another level.  Watching the bakers at work behind the glass and seeing trays of these beauties coming out of the oven makes the experience even more special. The staff are friendly and efficient, ensuring everyone gets their tart fresh and hot.  Whether you’re grabbing one to go or standing at the counter with a bica (espresso), Manteigaria offers a bite of Lisbon’s heart — simple, authentic, and unforgettable. || Some of the tastiest pastéis de nata we had in Lisbon! Located in a lovely spot at the beginning of Bairro Alto, right across from the square. You can enjoy your pastéis de nata at a small stand or take them away with you.

Absolutely incredible spot in the heart of Alfama! 🌟 Padaria Doce Mila is everything you dream of when you imagine authentic Lisbon food. Every single morning the locals are there cooking up fresh food right in front of you — from perfectly made sandwiches to fresh coffee and, of course, the best pastel de nata right out of the oven. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, with some of the nicest locals you’ll meet. The owners, Guedes and Mila, are absolutely amazing — they make you feel right at home and take pride in serving everything fresh and full of flavor. Even the fries are cooked fresh and delicious! I totally recommend Padaria Doce Mila — not only for the food, but for the experience. And the location couldn’t be better: right in the heart of the Alfama district, surrounded by charm and history. A must-visit when in Lisbon! || What a hidden gem (literally). Great service, the owners are very nice and understanding of travellers. Served with a smile. Highly recommend 5*. This place is off the beaten path in a little Courtyard, take a break and visit them. 🤗 || A hidden gem - in house bakery. You can taste the care and tradition in the sweet treats.  Feels quaint and truly authentic. || Sweet Portuguese bakery in a backyard. There are lots of different pastries to choose from. Everything I tried tasted very good and was also very reasonably priced. The waiter was very nice, even if he unfortunately only spoke Portuguese. || Lovely local place to get nata! Espresso was divine so a welcome morning combination upon arriving in Lisbon! Staff were warm and welcoming, definitely an underrated place! Easy to miss the entry on the road so watch out for the shop board sign. || For me the best Pastel de nata in Lisbon. Very good coffee and atmosphere. Very good prices. It is a gem in whole city. Highly recommended. || Delicious food with excellent coffee! Great for breakfast/lunch with reasonable prices :) And in my opinion - best Pastel de Nata in Portugal! ❤️ || We came here for breakfast.  I’m in love with with the Pastéis natas.  They are a good size and after my big breakfast of chicken on toast, I could barely finish it. Which was  a panini with chicken and tomato and cheese. Highly recommend. || Owner and staff were very friendly. Menu is simple, food is good, but nothing to write home about. Very neighborhood vibes which is a nice experience. Coffee is good. || This cafe is such a lovely hidden gem! The owner is so kind and his pastries are delicious. There is a little courtyard with tables in the shade, perfect place to relax and enjoy. I love coming here ❤️❤️

Having recently relocated to Lisbon with my partner, we were looking for something that reminded us of home.  That ended up being a pumpkin pie, and seriously what a pumpkin pie it was!!  We are beyond happy with how it looked and tasted. … || Thank you so much for your kind words, Todd! It makes me happy to hear we gave you a little reminder of home. Hope to see you again soon. :) || Got these Beautiful Beautiful custom cookies for a friend. I dont even live in Lisbon - I live in UAE and I reach out to the page on instagram and Graziella was one of the most attentive, kindest person ever. She understood exactly what I … || Thank you so much, Mehroz, for your kind words and support! I really appreciate that. I hope to see you soon at the bakery when you come to Lisbon :) || Best pies in Lisbon! It’s almost a tradition for us to order from here. We’ve already tried the cherry pie, pumpkin pie, and the amazing Cinnabons. If you love balanced and truly delicious desserts, this is the perfect choice. Totally recommend! || Thank you so much for your support, Rustam! I’m glad to know we’re part of your gatherings. Hope to see you soon! || Got this beauty for a friend’s birthday party and it was ridiculously delicious! place_name: Fábrica da Nata - Pastéis de Nata
reviews_content: Here’s the deal. I saw the line at the famous pastel de nata place in Belém and was like, life is too short for that. A friend recommended this place and it didn’t disappoint. They got super tasty pastel de natas, fresh out the oven along with a bunch of other stuff. Don’t forget to sprinkle some cinnamon on it to really give a kick to the flavor. || There is usually a line of people waiting, which might seem discouraging at first, but it is  worth the wait. The line moves quickly, and you get to enjoy warm pastel de nata. Because they sell so fast, they are always fresh and hot. They were the best pastel de nata we had in Portugal. The place is self-service, and there is also seating available if you want to sit and enjoy them. || We were on a mission to try as many pastéis de nata as possible during our trip to Portugal and stumbled upon Fábrica de Nata. We decided to grab six, and let’s just say I ate five of them myself while my wife had the other one. That pretty much says it all.  They were really good, creamy, flaky, and had that unmistakable custard flavor you don’t forget. If I had to rank all the natas we tried, I’d put these solidly in the B tier. Still delicious and absolutely worth stopping for, especially if you’re nearby.  Very nice box presentation I’d like to add.  So good that I couldn’t stop at one, or two, or three. I ate all five back to back. No regrets. || Wow, I can’t get these pastel de nata out of my mind. They taste incredible, especially when they’re really fresh. It may sound like a cliché, but you really have to try them. If you look around the shop, you can even see trays of them being moved and cooled; that’s when you know they’ll be good. || Honestly, for me that’s the greatest pastel de nata across whole Portugal. And trust me, I’ve tried multiple different pastelarias, even the famous one from Belem. Still, these little stars are absolutely delicious and just one bite sends you to taste paradise 🤭☺️ I could eat them daily and still wouldn’t be enough for me 😁 … || Yummm soooo good. Loads of seating too and decaf options for all coffees. I would say it’s reasonably priced too. The staff are very helpful and speak perfect English as well. You can easily see the bakers making the product. Definitely visit here || The pastéis de nata were exceptional—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly baked. The service was impressively fast and efficient, and the staff were attentive and professional. The space was spotless, beautifully decorated, and created a very pleasant atmosphere. Overall, it was a great experience, and I would definitely visit again. || Best pastel de nata in Portugal, hands down! Tried it in Lisbon, Sept 2025. Egg & ham and spinach were also outstanding. Must-try breakfast spot! || Delicious pastel de natas. Though I wouldn’t say the best but definitely one of the top. Also it’s so busy they’re always making fresh batches including when I went (late at night 10mins before closing) || Egg tart is one of my favorite desserts / pastry, and Fábrica da Nata is one of the best spots (esp. for a chain) is Portugal  Compared to other Portuguese egg tart spots like Pastéis de Belém or Manteigaria, I thought it’s (on average) a lot less charred and custard a bit sweeter and creamier (a key difference in comparison to egg tarts I have had in Hong Kong and across the US)  Not my personal favorite / top 3 but still highly recommend! || It was my first time trying egg tarts, mainly because I’m not a big fan of eggs. Since they’re quite famous I decided to give it a try. I was a bit worried they would have a strong eggy taste - but luckily, that wasn’t the case. They were sweet and surprisingly mild, and in my opinion, you couldn’t really taste the egg much at all.  The place itself was decent in terms of experience and service - it was quick and efficient. However, it didn’t feel very clean. I might have just been unlucky, but the environment could have been better.  That said, the price and taste were both very reasonable, and overall, I was pleasantly surprised. || Thank you for your kind comment and feedback. We're glad you enjoyed it and look forward to your next visit 😊 … || We tried some absolutely fantastic Portuguese tarts—crispy, flaky pastry on the outside and a perfectly creamy, slightly caramelized custard in the center. They were still warm and just melted in the mouth. Honestly, some of the best we’ve ever had. If you're in Portugal, don’t miss out on these heavenly little treats! || Thank you for your kind comment and feedback. We're glad you enjoyed it and look forward to your next visit 😊 … || The best Pastéis de nata in the city, also their quiches and coffee are really good:)  The staff is fast and reliable, ordering is easy and convenient. || Very accessible location. Staff were nice and helpful. Their pasteis de nata were  so good- just the right amount of sweetness! || The pastéis de nata were delicious, fresh, warm, and full of flavor. The service was fast and the place is nice. However, I noticed that the staff handling the pastries were not wearing gloves. It would be great if they improved this for better hygiene. Overall, still a good experience || So worth it. Fresh crispy flakey pastel de nata with delicious custard and also good pastel de bacalhau (codfish pastry)  10/10!! place_name: El Paso Cantina Mexicana y Cocktail Bar
reviews_content: I recently visited EL PASO Mexican restaurant and bar and was really impressed with both the food and the customer service.  The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The tacos were packed with perfectly seasoned meat, and the salsa had just the right amount of heat. Everything tasted homemade and authentic.  The customer service was excellent — the staff were friendly, attentive, and made sure we had everything we needed without being intrusive. Our servers Mumit and Vidal took time to explain the menu and even offered great recommendations.  Overall, the combination of delicious food and outstanding service made for a wonderful dining experience. I’ll definitely be coming back! || Excellent food and service at El Paso Cantina, especially for tourists who are looking for a break from seafood, or taste of home. All the meats and our tacos and burritos were very flavorful, and the margarita does were made from scratch and tasty. Our server Anamika was kind welcoming and friendly, she took great care of us, and added to an excellent meal! || What a lovely place! The food is delicious, the staff is friendly, and the vibes are great. Mumit was very kind and attentive. We had the Nachos El Paso (fully recommend!), beef tacos and vegetarian tacos, and the churros - everything was delicious! Can't wait to come again 🤩 || We had such a great experience at this restaurant. The service was amazing — they constantly checked in on us to make sure everything was okay without being annoying. The food was really good as well, super fresh and full of flavor.  We also loved how the staff took our picture with the hat; it was such a cute and thoughtful touch. Overall, a really warm and enjoyable place. Highly recommended!!! Btw it was Mummit who served us :) || I was really disappointed with this place but I'm not sure if this was down to my menu selections. Some of the items I saw delivered to other tables looked much nicer than mine. I opted for mozzarella sticks as a starter and these were just bland and lacking in flavour.  The texan tacos were also poor. Not what I expected at all..2 hard tacos and what appeared to be chilli on the side. Again, this is probably down to my selection. Service was great though || The best Mexican food we’ve had! Portions are generous, the prices are fair, and everything coming out of the kitchen looked amazing, which made it hard to choose. We went with soft tacos and quesadillas – and wow, they were incredible. The cocktails were just as good, perfectly made and full of flavor. Service was friendly, and the atmosphere was vibrant and fun. Make sure to book a table in advance if you want to be guaranteed a spot. A must-visit if you love Mexican food and great cocktails. || We had dinner here on New Year’s Eve, and we had Mumit as our server. He was very kind and treated us well. We had great food, and had awesome vegetarian options as well. We had the Nachos El Paso, the Vegan Burrito, the Vegan Tacos, and Tacos Alpastor. All were awesome! || Very busy Mexican restaurant in the center of Lisbon, however our waiter Mumit made us feel very welcome and taken care of. The food was amazing. We had the Nachos Mixtos, Tachos texanos and the vegetarian Burrito and everything was very tasty. Also the cocktails were great. There is no marking of gluten or other allergens on the menu but our waiter was super helpful and explained that all Nachos and Tacos are gluten free. Great experience, highly recommend. I would recommend to make a reservation. || We went there as a final dinner in Lisbon because we craved good Mexican food. It’s a simple restaurant but the food was just so delicious and the service was more than attentive and friendly. We’ve ordered our meal throughout the evening because we’ve wanted to try everything on the menu. Not a single dish that disappointed us! Would definitely recommend and obviously visit a second time if I‘ll ever go to Lisbon again. || It was a magnificent experience! Mumit was exceptional!
