Highly recommend to anyone looking for a night full of laughs, drinks, and great company 🍻🎉

Went in August after 2am. No lines, 10€ for females that comes with a drink. Was super sceptical bc of the terrible reviews but music is INCREDIBLE for all Baile Funk lovers (even as a gringa). Partied non-stop till 6 am, best night of my life at a club!!! || Went on a Friday and it felt like a middle school party. No one was on the dance floor and everyone was standing on the edges. I think this club is meant for young kids. 18-20 years old. Good music though. Lots of Portuguese, Spanish and English songs. My friend lost the card that they gave her and had to pay €100. || Absolutely terrible. Please don’t go here. It’s a massive scam, always empty, music is dead and the workers are horrible, they started physically pushing us and don’t clearly explain how the club works. The bouncers make you feel unsafe when it’s literally their jobs to make it safe. Complete scam. Save your coin. || Do not let anyone you know attend this disgusting venue.  The doormen are extortionists why violently attack innocent young people to steal their money.  My friend was violently assaulted by 3 security staff.  He has a broken arm and is physically and mentally shattered.  We will be taking legal and criminal action but we urge you to avoid this place. || Force you to spend 10 euro on a card they give you but then don't tell you how much the drinks are when you swipe your card so you have to ask to even know how much you're spending. The shots are 4 euro. Got there earlier in the night but then it just did not get better throughout the night. Also if you lose the card they give you, you have to pay 100 euro. || Genuinely the worst club I've ever been to. Some random English guy spilled a drink at the bar, the bar staff was so angry and was intentionally refusing to serve other English people. Petty and racist || I was attacked by three bouncers at this club completely unprovoked.  I did not order anything from this club but was charged a Euro fee of 100 via my debit card to leave the club.  I was punched multiple times by security for no reason.  Multiple witnesses who are not affiliated with me can confirm my attack was completely unprovoked.  They are locals who have stated that going to the police will do no good.  AVOID THIS CLUB AT ALL COSTS.  (As an aside, I am in the ER awaiting treatment and a CT Scan….see other reviews:  this club should not be allowed to operate)  Next day update:  One of the three bouncers who attacked me (punching me 10-15 times according to bystanders who tried to intervene and can confirm I did nothing to deserve the attack) took my wallet and stole my credit card.  They charged over $450 to my credit card after I left.  I did not realize they stole my card until this morning.  Thankfully my credit card company declined the charges and is investigating them for fraud.  For your own safety, please stay away from this club. || Got scammed, payed 18 euros for a ticket via ISN, but were'nt allowed to use it. Shots for 4 euros. Bad music. No chill area. You have to spend 20 euros to get out. If you loose your card you have to pay 100. || This is by far the worst club I’ve ever been to. Complicated system with sort of cashless payment where you have to upload money to a card they give you to get the drinks you ordered. This club is the definition of a tourist trap and I regret every cent and second I‘ve spent there. Horrible music and unfriendly staff. It is absolutely not worth your time, nor money. || Horrendous experience. We had to pay €15 each meanwhile we only spent €3,50 on drinks. They want to charge you a minimum amount to spend there but the lady at the cashier didn’t inform us about it. Also the bouncers are not very friendly. || Absolutely horrible experience! We needed to pay 100 euros because the girl checking my cards kept one and said she never did. So basically one if the employees lied just so we can be fined 100 euros! On the question to review the camera I was told to try calling the police hahaaha. Not really sure what that laughter meant but definitely 0 % respect for client. If you are ever in Lisbon - Avoid this place! || Worst club I've ever seen. Someone stole my and my boyfriend's card. We asked them to check the camera but they didn't care. They told us to call the police. We called the police but they couldn't help. We were stuck at the club all night. I had very bad experience. They wanted us to pay 200 €. || Go anywhere else but here. I've been to some dodgy clubs in my time but this takes the crown. They give you these cards (what are we, a hotel?) which you can't misplace under any costs. Luckily I decided to leave at 3am when people were still entering where I find out the costs from your night out are stored on your card. AND THEY DON'T ACCEPT CARD. You have to leave your phone and ID, stumble to the nearest ATM and then queue up again to leave. My total was 14 euros which was no entrance fee but one drink of Redbull and Vodka?? One of my friends was told to pay 100 euros which she negotiated down to 20. Stay at home, have one drink and burn a 20 euro note and I guarantee you'll have a better time. || Son was attacked by three bouncers Concussion and broken arm.  They wanted him to pay them for leaving club || TERRIBLE! TERRIBLE! TERRIBLE! Extremely small club which was full of practically teenagers, (so anyone in their mid-late twenties RUN AWAY) they do not check ID at entrance.. biggest issue I had which is why I left: everyone was SMOKING inside, I was literally coughing and had my throat irritated because of the massive smoke clouds, and the extremely poor ventilation. Especially now with raising covid cases, smoking should be strictly forbidden to reduce spreading in tiny enclosed spaces. On top of that, as far as I know smoking inside is ILLEGAL but they do not seem to care even their staff (bartenders) were smoking and no one was wearing a mask. According to the rules, staff MUST wear mask. Even when I tried to out for some fresh air they wouldn't let me because of their ridiculous card system and queue was insane. Super disappointed with the experience. || Scam. They give you a card to use inside. If you lose you pay 100€. They pickpocket your card inside (bouncers standing around on the dancefloor) || The worst club I’ve ever been. Three friends of mine had to pay to went out 15€. They didn’t order anything on the bar and  the guards didn’t say anything on the entrance about any payment.Scammers!!! Avoid this club!!! || I came here with my girlfriend to dance and a nice time with her. The bodyguards where very rude and some local guys skipped the line to get in. I think they are discriminating at the entrance, locals get in and tourist are not welcome. Such a pity. I do not recover coming here  if you are a tourist, bad way of managing a business. I managed to get in on a Saturday night after 3 hours in the line and many arguments with crazy locals.  Btw they do not pay taxes ;)  What an horrible  place! || I agree with everyone else here, dodgy club with the rude stuff trying to squeeze the money out of you  I had to leave because it was unbearable. Very small place packed full, horrible glitchy choppy music and it seemed impossible to have a good time. They wouldn’t let me leave unless I used the damn card and had to pay 10€ to LEAVE.  Thank god they let me skip the line because I started feeling queasy || The atmosphere was alright (the small space definitely affected it) and the waiters are nice but drinks lack variety and are all very expensive || - 12 euros for women and 20 euros for men - loud and bad bass - unable to hang jackets - 15 euro redbull wodka - locals skipped the line - annoying card system - too busy - long queue || I visited this club as part of a bar crawl and was punched in the face, unprovoked. I was refused water and the security did nothing about this, I would recommend avoiding at all costs. || On a Friday night (2am) || Music was great, and was a great night in general. But when we wanted to leave, we had to wait for 30 minutes because of the stupid card system. Please, PLEASE, get rid of the card system. || Do not go to this place. I asked for a bacardí with redbull and the price was 16€, I complained to the manager and she was really rude and agreed about the price. The drink was in a small glass. Bad people, bad vibes.... || THIS IS FOR YOUNG KIDS-EVERYONE IS AROUND 20 😟 || THEY STOLE MY MONEY!! I HAD TO PAY 15 EURO FOR JUST GETTING OUT OF THE CLUB. THEY DIDNT SAID A THING. DONT GO THERE || They are scammers. You order 2 drinks and you have to pay for 5. Don't go to this club. Seriously. || If you want to stay safe and enjoy your night,don't go there . Completely trap this place . || The club is really small, for the prices you pay its not worth jt.  It you wanr

Went here on a Friday night and was surprised at how empty the club was. A few things stood out to me: 1.	Once you leave, there are no pass-outs, so you can’t come back in. 2.	The club has little to no internet connection, which makes it hard to connect with friends inside. 3.	Drinks are pricey for what you get — small cups at a high cost. 4.	To leave the club, you actually need to ask security to let you out, which feels a bit restrictive. 5.	The staff were friendly enough, though I’ve found warmer and more welcoming teams at other venues in Lisbon.  Overall, not a terrible experience, but there are definitely better nightlife options around the city. || This review is rated one star because I experienced racist behavior here. Google automatically assigns a one-star rating when leaving this kind of feedback. This made me feel very uncomfortable, and it is not acceptable. || If I could give this place zero stars, I would — and even that would feel generous. Going out to a club is supposed to be about music, fun, and good vibes. Instead, this venue delivered one of the most hostile, aggressive, and downright dehumanizing experiences I’ve ever had.  From the second we got to the door, the staff were rude and confrontational for no reason. The security acted like they were guarding a prison, not a nightclub. At the bar, the staff were cold and dismissive, making it clear they had no interest in basic customer service.  In the toilets, things got even more ridiculous — a woman there started making up rules on the fly, with a hostile attitude that felt personal. And get this: the tap water was warm on purpose — a clear tactic to discourage people from drinking water unless they paid. That’s not just greedy, it’s grossly irresponsible, especially in a nightlife setting.  Then came the final straw: we stepped into what we were told was the designated smoking area — a public street — only for security to corner us afterward and demand extra payment, claiming we had “left the premises.” No one warned us about this “rule,” and when we tried to explain, they started arguing and shouting at us, insisting we were lying. It escalated to the point where it honestly felt threatening. Totally unacceptable.  Nightclubs should be safe spaces to enjoy yourself, not places where you’re harassed, intimidated, and disrespected by the very people running the show. This place completely failed that basic standard. There are so many better spots in Lisbon where you’ll be treated like a human being — go to literally any of them instead.  Avoid this nightmare. Seriously. || Rude security. Rude cashier. Drinks are weak, overpriced, and tiny. Dance floor is tiny. The cherry on top is the only exit has the handles removed and you have to wait for security to let you out. This place is a death trap, avoid if you value your life. || If you're a foreigner, be careful! Ask the price and double-check what you're being charged. When I realized it, they'd been overcharging my entire group of friends, taking advantage of my inattention. Even after showing the charge on the bank's app, they refused to refund my money. || A horrible club that many bouncers are hanging out in other gay bars, acting friendly and convincing you to go there. The atmosphere & music inside is totally shit, no smoking room, controversial dark room, you cannot go out with a drink, and many people are fooled to get there. Insanely problematic security, I do not suggest at all. The cloakroom lady & bartender was super nice, likely bouncers are, yet it’s obvious that people on the random street catching you and trying to convince you to get there with being super friendly. One 0.5 beer is 7 euros, 0.33 is 5 euros. Super overpriced for Lisbon. || Very nice place to meet your friends, have a lot of cool drinks. The music is good and you can feel it all around the dancefloor. The staff are very friendly and depending on the night you can watch amazing shows. Very organized with a lot of space for those who wants to dance or just grab some drinks with friends. || Went to step out to smoke and was uncomfortable with the (very minor) confrontation with security. I left instead. || I was in Lisbon on 7 days vacation with my friends and we really enjoyed it. I have been to Construction club 2 times and it was fantastic!! Performances are amazing and everyone is so positive and friendly! I met a lot of nice people and some of them are my friends now, thanks to the place. Never experienced or seen any negative situation. Too many stairs, almost fell few times😂 Bartenders are also nice. Drinks may be a lil bit expensive but it’s worth it because of the atmosphere. I saw a lot of negative reviews, but I’m happy that I had a good time! I also visited another gay night clubs, but for me this is the best one. Thank you for making my trip better, hope to see u soon again!❤️ || Terrible experience. We were promised free entry from their sister bar and they denied it and said my boyfriend’s shorts were too short. The manager came up to check his shorts and then added on an additional 10€ for entry. For an LGBT bar they are NOT gay friendly. I rarely write bad reviews but this place I would avoid for sure. || Incredible space, one of the most spectacular Discos i ever been, Only pretty people, great Djs and performers, Very good drinks iand cocktails as welln an much beautiful space, I stronglly recomend to visit at Lisbon. || The music is good but the big problem here is the drinks, the prices are extremely high for what it is. If you going to charge high prices at least serve the drinks in bigger glasses. The micro glasses they use for gin tonic is ridiculous and very pour choice for other drinks. || It's a good club, music and DJ. Only downside is it is pricey for drinks etc. || Avoid this place! They overcharge us on July 11th and then some acquaintances on July 12th. Total ripoff, go somewhere else || Most expensive bar in Lisbon!! One mini gin-tonic for 9 EUR. Ofenssiv! || I got tonight from the staff of this club a bracelet for entry in the club. Initially the guy didn’t say that are two lines one for those who have the bracelet and one for those who didn’t have. We stayed around 45 minutes in the line and watching how the staff easily passed in front of us over 10 persons. I preferred to leave the line after a short discussion with the members of the staff. I founded this very unprofessional and very rude takeoff into consideration that the bracelet received from himself was null after 2AM because after that time everyone pays the full price. Disgusted of the rudeness and disrespectful staff. I will never return and waiting to be humiliated in such way. || Very expensive, small drinks. Unfriendly security and the whole place smells very bad. Can't recommend at all. || I can't believe people can still smoke inside clubs in Lisbon, this is a big no. The place looks great, but it gets really messy really quick. The dancers were as entertaining as watching paint dry and the music was terrible. Awful remixes of pop songs and underwhelming techno. || I strongly do not recommend that club. Entrance costs 12 euros (one drinks is included). However, they do not include all drinks, only some cheap cocktails. Moreover, I was only  17th visitor of that club at 1:30 on Saturday night. It is just empty hole. || I hoped I would get the chance to dance the night I went there, however that was not the case. You don't get the chance to express yourself on house electronic sh**; you merely repeat the same moves over and over again like a monkey. It wasn't until it got crowded that I realized that the fellows of my community were there HUNTING. Dark room available as well so...you know the rest of the story. Separate, well ventilated area for smokers available.

place_name: The Lisbon Pub Crawl- Discover Lisbon
reviews_content: Leo is the man to do the Pub Crawl in Lisbon with. It was so much fun. Super cool group, stack cup game, dance, karaoke and drinks. Everything was awesome. || Joined the pub crawl twice whilst I was in Lisbon. The MOST fun, such a great way to meet people as I was travelling alone. Leo, Nicholas & Phelps were the BEST 🩷🩷🩷 || Met some cool people I wouldn’t have otherwise. VIP access at the bars. Good times waiting to happen.. Cheers🍻 || First pub crawl experience and definitely a very good one! The bars they brought us to were very nice, good music and space wasn’t a problem since the night was warm so some of us stayed outside. The alcohol included is nice, you get shots and an open bar. I don’t think you can get wasted but a bit tipsy maybe! The guides of the tour, especially Ana and Victoria especially, are nice and organised! I highly recommend 🤘🏻 || Hi Estelle, Thank you very much for  leaving such an amazing review. Lovely that you enjoyed our experiences. We look forward to seeing you again in the near future and party like we never did before.  Best regards, Discover Lisbon team || We had an amazing time with our tour guide Thomas!!! The free shots were trash though from the bars they tasted like juice! It overall was a fantastic time. Highly recommend :) || Phelps he is the best guy ever he is so friendly and funny I think I will try it just because of this. They are friendly and they know how to have fun they are the best || Lovely guide called tiago kept the group together and energetic. Definitely a recommendation. Lots of people and good communication and friendliness! || this was so fun and so safe and all tour guides were amazing!! had fun with us and made sure everyone was having a good time and accounted for. Anna T specifically was amazing and does deserve a raise! please do go on Portugal pub crawl || The pubcrawl was really nice  will sure we will recommend my friends, our tour guide MANNUUUUUU did a great job || Ton was such an amazing guide would definitely recommend if in Portugal for the night.

Been there tonight- Positive: the atmosphere was great and everybody was happy and hyped. The music/DJs were soo good. Also with a stamp you could get in again after leaving :)  Negative: - you can’t close the bathroom doors (at least in the girls bathroom) -decorations were pretty lame -drinks are kinda expensive || Thank you Vic, hope to see you there more times :) || A lot of second-hand smoke will be inhaled but you won't be able to leave without squeezing through people wishing to seek approval from their "friends" by filming themselves dancing with their flash on.  Good sound system paired with some good music.  Only worth the free early entry. || Thanks for your review Shaun, now we have new smoke extractor, give it a try :) || You have to reserve on Instagram to get inside and then make sure you are high n the guest list. 1/5 stars || Hey Sharpie, I think you are not talking about our parties, we never use any Instagram guest list and either not even any guest list, you can just arrive, pay and enter - are you sure you are talking about our parties on Wednesday nights? || Amazing view for the river + beautiful venue = perfect :) || Best venue in Lisbon, great parties and atmosphere. || Went there and everybody knew me even when I was never there before || Thanks Luzzy, hope to see you next Wednesday 🙂 … || Amazing music...and the best party atmosphere || Thanks for the wonderful rating <3 || Best parties in town - love it 💙💙💙 || Very Nice Place for go on wednesdays || The best trance party on Wednesday!! || Thanks for the wonderful rating <3 || Freaky Freaky ! The best club nights in town! || Best Wednesdays in Portugal :) || The best Wednesdays!! 😁😁 … || Thanks for the wonderful rating <3 || Thank you very much :)) || Excellent atmosphere, frequented by beautiful people with good vibes, great sound quality and, of course, always featuring big-name DJs who offer us a night of pure sonic adventure! I love it! ❤️😝 … || Thank you very much :)) || Good atmosphere, good music, I enjoyed the experience and would repeat it. || Thank you very much :)) || I had a great experience there, the event and the venue were fantastic! || Thank you very much :)) || Good music. Excellent atmosphere.  I recommend it. || Thank you very much :)) || I really enjoyed the music and the atmosphere. || Thank you very much :) || Poor service. I do not recommend it. || Hey Thomas what happened? They don't let you in?  I'm asking because you made your review at 1AM, when the party almost didn't start, so I'm wondering which was the bad service at that hour.

Been going there for a while n I am very grateful I found this place. Great environment, two stages (may depend on the day?), performances are great, they got drags and gogo dancers, the sets are fire too. I wanna give a special shout out to the security guard team (Benny, Pina and others) because I ended up loosing my phone and they gave me the support I needed and found my phone. Also shout out to Thais and Afonso, the lovely staff I met at the bar. As long as I’m in Lisbon I’ll def keep coming back. Thank u all for the great memories and service. || Outstanding! One of the best nights i ever had in lisbon! I enjoyed myself a LOT! Music was great.. people fun.. vibe on.. cool! Thanks a lot || This is the place to be! Bernardo the security and bouncer was especially kind, engaging with me and my friend group. Couldn’t feel safer at this establishment! When we needed fresh air it was very easy to socialize in the street right outside the club. If. you need something fun to do while on vacation this is recommended. || A great place to have fun, dance, and meet new people. From the moment you walk into the club, you feel the experience thanks to the excellent service from the hosts and security staff (Benny and Pina are the best!). At the bar, the bartenders are super friendly and always bring good energy to the party. The music always matches the vibe of the night’s theme, and you can dance until 6 a.m., in a very safe neighborhood with a great location. Every time I go, I have an even better time than the last. Totally recommended! || Favorite club in Lisbon!! Super welcoming space for everyone who wants to have a good time in a safe space - the team makes sure of that. Especially Benny at the door makes you feel welcome right away! The entertainers specifically Lexa Black and Rebecca Bunny and staff are absolutely amazing and give ever changing great shows every night! || Well it's young generation's dance club, the door staff, cloakroom and bar-staff  were all very welcoming and friendly. Just too many girls (straight) more than 50%.  😭🤣, and of course I found it rather hard to pretend young again. 🤣 Drinks price were reasonable and it's not a weak drinks. Place got busy after 130am weekend. || I had the best weekend in Lisbon, and TRUMPS was a huge part of why! The club was so inclusive, fun, and welcoming—the atmosphere was electric and everyone inside was friendly, creating a really safe and enjoyable environment.  A special shoutout to Benny (Bernardo), the most incredible security on the door. Coming from London, I’m used to club staff being quite stern and intimidating, but he was the complete opposite—warm, approachable, and genuinely helpful. He guided us, pointed us in the right direction, and made us feel welcome while still being highly professional and attentive to everyone’s safety.  Thank you TRUMPS (and especially Benny!) for such a fantastic experience. I’ll definitely be back! || As a local Drag Queen and performer, I have limited opportunities to enjoy Lisbon's nightlife and local Queens. However, on January 5th, my friend and I spontaneously met up for a few drinks in Bairro Alto and ended up in line to attend Friday night at Trumps Club. Since I prefer to be comfortable on my day off, I was kindly asked by a hostess to change into appropriate attire before entering the club. Luckily, I live just a few minutes away by car, so I quickly took an Uber and returned with a night-ready look.  When I was about to pay the 15 euros entrance fee, a hostess unexpectedly allowed me to enter without charge as a gesture of goodwill to compensate for my time and Uber expenses. I truly appreciated this kind gesture from the staff. Upon entering the venue, I immediately felt a sense of joy and security as the security team diligently checked everyone with metal detectors and wished us a pleasant stay.  However, the real highlight of the night was the presence of the Queens. They truly make each night special by delivering captivating performances and engaging with the crowd. The venue offers two distinct blocks downstairs for different experiences, as well as a comfortable lounge upstairs where guests can take a break. The bathrooms were well-maintained, and there is a hat-check room near the entrance where you can leave your outerwear.  I would like to suggest to the Administration that they encourage all guests to leave their outerwear upon arrival and consider creating a designated spot in the upper bar for tipping. The Queens work hard to make each guest's night at the Club extraordinary, and this would be a small way to show appreciation for their efforts.  Lastly, I would like to request the return of the comedy show, as it added a nice twist to the evening. It would be great if the show could be hosted in English so that everyone can understand and enjoy all the jokes.  Thank you, dear staff, for the wonderful experience, and I look forward to visiting again in the future.  Kind regards, Nikolay a.k.a. Irina Ganache || Trumps is simply the best party from Lisbon. It's a definite stop Everytime I'm in Lisbon. Everyone that works there seems so happy, which makes us happier and enjoy the party even more. || So much fun here and the DJs are so amazing. Must come when you are in Lisbon. Will come back again 💖

NOT RECOMMENDED ! The lady at the entrance told us that we have to pay 10 euros to get in, and that it covers one beer. As tourists, we don't know what to expect. So we asked if … || Hello! reviews_content: I tried to book a spot via WhatsApp starting on December 7, but the team was unable to complete the booking. This was not due to a lack of availability or any other reasonable cause. They simply replied about once a week, repeatedly telling me that I would receive an email to pay the deposit. I never received any email and informed them of this on December 13. They replied again on December 19, and I once more explained that I still had not received any payment email. After that, they stopped responding entirely. On December 23, they contacted me again asking, “Do you still need a spot?” By that time, of course, I did not — on December 7 I was trying to book a spot for December 24. I found a better service instead. I did not visit this place, but I believe this review is necessary, and I hope they improve how they work with potential clients. This is the worst customer service I have experienced in the spa or massage industry. Think twice before considering this company if accuracy and respect for your plans are important to you.  UPD. Please, check photos i uploaded. "Recently exceptionally high volume of contacts" for 9 months ? XD || Dear Madam Maria, thank you for taking the time to share your experience. We sincerely apologize for the frustration and inconvenience you encountered while trying to book with us. During the period you mentioned, we experienced an unusually high volume of contact requests combined with a transition to new booking and payment software, which unfortunately caused significant operational constraints and delays in our responses. This is not the level of service we aim to provide, and we fully understand how disappointing this must have been—especially given the time-sensitive nature of your request. We regret that the payment email did not reach you despite multiple follow-ups, and that communication eventually stopped. That breakdown is entirely on our side, and we take full responsibility for it. Your feedback is important to us, and we are already implementing improvements to ensure faster, clearer, and more reliable communication with all current and potential clients, particularly during peak periods. Once again, we are truly sorry for your experience and appreciate you bringing this to our attention. We wish you all the best and thank you for helping us identify where we need to do better. reviews_content: It was incredibly interesting, very interactive, and extremely well designed. The special effects, the storyline, and the overall atmosphere were impressive and truly immersive. The staff was fantastic: friendly, professional, and very attentive. A special thank you to our guide Luca, who helped us a lot and made the whole experience even more enjoyable. Even compared to escape rooms played abroad, this one undoubtedly had the most diverse and challenging puzzles! We loved all the decoding, and a super positive factor for its success was that, given that we have team members who don't understand Portuguese, Enigmas Land provided both English and Portuguese versions of all the escape room puzzles, allowing everyone to easily understand and focus on solving each one. In addition, Victor was with us in a super fun character who always helped with translations and communication with my friends, as well as putting everyone's reasoning together. He never gives direct clues like in other escape rooms, but rather makes us think through our own reasoning, which makes everything much better and gives us a real feeling of being the ones solving everything, even when we seemed stuck. It was perfect!! I recommend it so much that we've already bought two more escape rooms and even got a free speed game! Thank you so much for everything!! || Thank you very much, and we'll be here to honor those 5 stars in the next games you'll venture into! || As regular customers of this type of game, we were quite disappointed. Anyone who has ever been to an escape room will find this completely different. It's even worse. The game consists only of a table with props on it. The clues are very complex, long, and don't make much sense. And we also have the constant company of a man who is always directing and explaining everything. Which is not expected in an escape game where the group must decipher the clues on their own. || We realized that you didn't read what you were getting into; the game you purchased was an escape game, not an escape room, something that is even in the Odisseias title and present in 3 different places on the voucher.  And as with everything in life, we couldn't all like the same thing, and fortunately, the game you played is our most played and liked game. As you mentioned, the clues are indeed complex, and when you constantly try to read more than one at a time, it becomes more difficult, and this fact was mentioned several times before and during the game by the game master. In Portugal, and especially abroad, this figure (and you can research it) serves exactly as part of the game and to help guide you during the experience. We understand those who prefer to touch a button and immediately get the answer through the intercom; in our case, we prefer to guide the thinking and only assist in how to get the answer to the customers themselves. For your part, you decided to play as 6 in a game meant for 4 people, and despite mentioning that you weren't in the best frame of mind for riddles due to the few hours of sleep you'd had, thankfully at least 2 members still enjoyed it. Our games are all designed for thinking, not just wandering around looking for keys or objects in rooms like in others, but for reading, interpreting, and solving riddles. That's why we're called ENIGMAS LAND. Have a fantastic rest of your birthday and a great week! || The best Escape Game I've ever played! An interesting historical spot in the center of Lisbon. The ruins are atmospheric and give a good sense of the city’s past, especially knowing the monastery was destroyed in the 1755 earthquake and never rebuilt.  The museum itself is quite small, you can walk through everything in about 20 minutes. It’s not a must-see or a top priority if you’re visiting Lisbon for the first time, but it’s still worth a short visit if you’re nearby or interested in history and architecture. || Carmo Archaeological Museum is a beautiful and unique museum in Lisbon that’s definitely worth a visit.  Housed in the stunning ruins of the Carmo Convent, it offers an incredible glimpse into Portugal’s history.  The exhibits are fascinating, covering archaeology, medieval artifacts, and more. Admission is €5, or you can get a 15% discount with the Lisboa Card.  Note that it’s closed on Sundays, so plan accordingly.  Overall, it’s one of the best places to explore Lisbon’s rich past—truly unforgettable! 🏛️✨ || The Convento do Carmo is one of the most impressive places I visited in Lisbon. The partially destroyed convent creates a unique and almost surreal atmosphere, especially with the open roof and the gothic arches framing the sky. The museum inside is small but well curated, with interesting archaeological pieces and a calm, peaceful ambience.  It’s a place where you can really pause for a moment, take in the history, and enjoy the contrast between ruin and preservation. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Lisbon. || This was simply stunning and we went a little before sunset so we had the opportunity to get to see it in the day and the evening making it even more spectacular.  I would plan on spending at least an hour here enjoying the Carmo Archaeological Museum in order to really take it in. || ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Where Gothic drama meets archaeological treasure hunting with killer views 🏛️  If you're going to stumble upon history anywhere in Lisbon, let it be here. The Carmo Archaeological Museum isn't just housed in a "nice historic building" - it's dramatically perched inside the haunting ruins of a 14th-century Gothic convent that the 1755 earthquake couldn't quite finish off. Talk about resilience with style!  The roofless nave creates this absolutely magical open-air cathedral vibe where ancient stones and sky conspire to give you goosebumps. The contrast between delicate archaeological finds and those massive, earthquake-scarred arches is pure poetry. You'll find everything from Roman mosaics to medieval tombs, including some genuinely fascinating Visigothic pieces that most tourists completely miss.  Bonus points for the panoramic views! The elevated position gives you lovely vistas over Lisbon's rooftops and beyond - it's like getting a history lesson with a scenic backdrop thrown in for free.  Pro tip: Visit late afternoon when the light filters through those Gothic arches just right and the city views are at their most golden. The entrance fee is reasonable, staff are knowledgeable without being pushy, and it's mercifully tourist-trap-free.  A perfect gem hiding in plain sight in the heart of Chiado! 📷✨ || Worth visiting. Beautiful old town 💕 || Castelo de São Jorge is a stunning medieval fortress situated on one of Lisbon’s highest hills, providing visitors with magnificent panoramic views of the city, including the Alfama district, the Baixa area, the Tagus River, and the iconic 25 de Abril Bridge.  The castle itself has a rich history, originally serving as a Moorish citadel before becoming a royal palace and later a military stronghold.  Visitors can explore vast ramparts, eleven towers, archaeological sites, and remnants of the former royal palace, all set within beautiful gardens that are home to roaming peacocks, adding a unique and charming touch to the experience.  The castle's grounds feel like a living museum where one can marvel at medieval defensive architecture, walk along ancient walls, and enjoy peaceful spaces shaded by olive trees and dotted with historical artifacts.  Surrounding the castle, the neighborhood of Alfama offers a vibrant yet authentic atmosphere with narrow, winding streets, traditional tiled houses, cozy cafes, and small shops steeped in local culture.  The area is known for its lively yet intimate vibe, enriched by the sounds of Fado music and the daily rhythms of local residents.  Travelers often find themselves enchanted by the blend of history, culture, and scenic beauty, making the approach to the castle a meaningful journey in itself.  The castle’s elevated position allows for stunning sunrise and sunset views across Lisbon, creating memorable photo opportunities and moments of reflection against the backdrop of terracotta rooftops and the sparkling river below.  Visitors are recommended to arrive early to avoid crowds, as the castle tour, including its museum and archaeological areas, can take one to two hours. The pathway includes some steep climbs, but the well-preserved structures and the sweeping city vistas make the effort worthwhile.  There are also small cafes within the castle grounds where visitors can pause and enjoy refreshments while taking in the scenic surroundings.  Overall, Castelo de São Jorge offers a rich, immersive experience of historical, cultural, and natural heritage, making it a must-visit landmark for anyone exploring Lisbon’s fascinating past and vibrant present.  The castle’s majesty, along with the lively charm of its surroundings, creates an unforgettable visit that reflects both the resilience and spirit of Lisbon. || What an awesome experience this was!  Was there on a Tuesday afternoon and the crowds were light.  Very easy to walk around and explore.  (Although be warmed the steps are pretty steep and some have no handrails....careful! Be sure to visit one or more of the wonderful restaurants round the sides.  Nightime is a completely different experience and one not to be missed. || 🌅 Where the City Opens to the River ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)  After walking down Rua Augusta on that bright June 2025 afternoon, we finally reached Praça do Comércio — Lisbon’s great stage by the Tagus River. Still with my friend, I remember stepping out from beneath the arch and feeling the city breathe wider, as if every street had been leading to this one golden moment.  The vast square, once home to Portugal’s royal palace before the 1755 earthquake, now stands as a symbol of rebirth. The yellow arcades glow under the sunlight, and the sound of waves blends with the hum of trams. In the middle, King José I’s bronze statue, mounted on his horse Gentil, looks forever toward the river — the same horizon that launched the Age of Discoveries. Standing there, I could almost imagine ships setting sail again.  We rested on the marble steps facing the Tagus, watching ferries and silhouettes cross the glittering water. It was hot — the kind of radiant, reflective heat only Lisbon can produce — but the breeze from the river made everything slow down, peaceful and cinematic.  Practical Notes  Visit near sunset for cooler air and golden light on the arcades.  Bring water; shade is limited.  Perfect spot for wide-angle photos or time-lapse videos.  Cafés under the arcades are pricier but worth it for the view.  Quick Ratings Historical & Cultural Value: 10/10 Atmosphere & River Views: 9.5/10 Accessibility: 9/10 📸 Photo & Video Potential: 10/10 Café & Rest Spots: 8.5/10  📝 If this glimpse of Lisbon resonated with you, hit 👍 and follow me — I share real impressions from Europe’s most curious corners. || Praça do Comércio is one of Lisbon’s most impressive and iconic squares. The square is lively but not overwhelming, with plenty of cafés and easy access to the surrounding streets of Baixa. A must-see landmark that perfectly captures the elegance and scale of Lisbon’s waterfront. || We were in Lisbon for a few days while waiting to join a cruise. This church is different from most in Lisbon. In 1959, a large fire destroyed the roof and many wooden parts. The heat was so strong that the stone columns cracked and turned black. But as the Mass time got close, the temple got the silence proper for prayer and recollection of religious people. The liturgy was beautiful, with the proper dignity. The pipe organ makes beautiful sound waves through the old Church walls. Today (Sept. 28, 2025) was the Gospel of the rich man and the poor Lazarus (Luke 16:19-31). Right in the midst of downtown Lisbon, this is a pearl of a monument since the 13th century and a place where we breathe already a bit of eternal peace if we are able to listen the old stones of the walls and floor, the gospel messages, as well as our own consciences in the hectic of the modern world of social responsibilities towards the poor. || Igreja De S Domingos is a beautiful and peaceful church, I visited when Mass was going on, on Easter Sunday. place_name: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
reviews_content: You get a fantastic view of the historic centre of this beautiful city from here. You could stay and enjoy the well kept gardens and the views all day. There's so much to look at. Enjoy the full chaos of colours and sounds that envelope your senses. You'll have so many photos when you leave this place, but it is the experience itself that will stay with you. || Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara offers one of the most beautiful panoramic views in Lisbon. The terrace overlooks the historic center, the castle, and the river, making it an ideal place to pause and take in the city’s landscape. The garden is well kept, and the atmosphere is relaxed despite being a popular spot.  It’s especially impressive at sunset, when the light over the city becomes warm and golden. A must-see viewpoint if you want a classic Lisbon panorama in a pleasant, accessible setting. || A nice panoramic view of the city center and part of the coast. It’s adjacent to a busy street and is easy to access locates at the city center. It’s very spacious there currently hosting a Christmas bazaar making it loads of festive feels. There are different direction to arrive the view point, including one very steep pebble street as in the picture. Will recommend if you are nearby, but not necessarily worth to travel across the city for it as there are a number of other Miradouro in the city. || One of the most beautiful viewpoints in Lisbon! It offers a fantastic panoramic view over the city, especially at sunset when the light is golden. There’s a small park with benches, trees, and even a kiosk for coffee or drinks. It can get a bit crowded, but the atmosphere is lively and pleasant. A must-visit spot for anyone exploring Lisbon || We took the funicular up to this little park for the views, and it was not disappointing! The 270 degree views of the city and surrounding mountains were breathtaking. There are two levels to this park, and plenty of park benches to relax on. There is a small cafe here, if you need a drink or a snack. I would definitely recommend visiting here, especially if you want some really great photos! || Great view of the City from the nearby Bairro Alto. We were fortunate to visit during the New Year's market. Excellent choice of Portuguese specialties (think serrano sandwich with sheep cheese) and Porto. || Lisbon is a city that pretends to be humble while casually seducing you at every corner. I left the house planning “just a short walk,” which, in this city, is the most unrealistic expectation you can possibly set. Five minutes in and you’re already climbing some Biblical staircase, questioning gravity, God, and your shoe choices. But then Lisbon apologizes. It always does. Usually with light. I wandered through streets that smelled like roasted chestnuts and mild chaos, past tiled façades that look like somebody finally let a poet design buildings. People spilled into cafés, dogs trotted around like they owned the place, and the whole city glowed in that gentle, old-European way — like a postcard that refuses to retire. Eventually I drifted uphill to Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara, which is the kind of viewpoint that doesn’t just offer a view — it offers perspective. The kind that makes you remember you still have a pulse. Up there, under a tree that had definitely lived through several empires, I found an artist named Anne Laidam, casually painting like she had all the time in the world. Her works were neon daydreams of Lisbon — trams, rooftops, broken sunlight — the whole city filtered through someone’s kindness. I wasn’t planning to buy art. (I never plan to buy art. Art plans to buy me.) But one of her trams looked at me with the exact attitude of a Lisbon cat: unimpressed, slightly judgmental, irresistibly charming. So, of course, I adopted it. And carried it home alongside a copy of Saramago — because every reckless purchase deserves a companion in philosophy. If you ever want a walk that feels like a conversation with a city that knows it’s beautiful but doesn’t brag: just start walking. Lisbon will take care of the rest. || Fantastic views of the city and the boats sailing past on the ocean. Plenty of food and drink stalls. || Amazing view, very nice vibe with bars and good street food around (a bit overpriced). Definitely worth checking if you're is Lisbon, specially near sunset hours. I'd recommend for couples who want a romantic vibe. || Best spot in Lisbon to stop and see the whole city. It has a dog park below and a nice spot in the back with a cat box that was tended by some retirees. Great place for photos, food, music and just relaxing.

Miradouro de Santa Luzia is absolutely worth a visit. The views over Alfama’s rooftops and the Tagus River are genuinely beautiful, and for the price of free, you really can’t complain.  ￼  It was a bit crowded when we went, but that’s expected given how popular this spot is. Even so, it’s still a memorable place to slow down for a few minutes, take photos, and enjoy the scenery. The viewpoint itself is part of the charm too, with a small landscaped terrace, shaded areas, and classic blue-and-white azulejo panels that make it feel distinctly Lisbon.  ￼  One detail I appreciated is that the tile panels aren’t just decorative, they depict historical scenes, including Lisbon’s Praça do Comércio before the 1755 earthquake and the 1147 conquest of the castle (a cool touch if you like history).  ￼  That said, I wouldn’t call the views “to die for.” You can get comparable viewpoints nearby, and this is more of a “quick, classic Lisbon stop” than a once-in-a-lifetime moment. It’s also conveniently located in Alfama at Largo de Santa Luzia, right by the Church of Santa Luzia, making it an easy stop while exploring the neighborhood.  ￼  Overall, crowded or not, it’s still definitely worth a visit and an easy, memorable addition to a Lisbon walking day. || Miradouro de Santa Luzia offers some of the most impressive views in Lisbon. From here you can see the Alfama district and the river in a truly beautiful setting. The terrace is elegantly decorated with plants and traditional blue and white azulejos, making it even more special. It is one of those places you simply cannot miss when visiting the city. || I visited Miradouro de Santa Luzia on a rainy day and the view was absolutely worth it! One of the most beautiful viewpoints in Lisbon. charming tiles, peaceful vibes, and a perfect spot to take in the city from above.  Perched on the hills of Alfama, Lisbon’s oldest district, this viewpoint sits beside the small Igreja de Santa Luzia one of the most breathtaking views in the city. || Miradouro de Santa Luzia is pure magic. The moment you reach the terrace, Lisbon unfolds beneath you — red rooftops tumbling toward the sparkling Tagus River, narrow streets weaving through the Alfama district, and sunlight dancing on every tile. The bougainvillea and azulejos add a splash of color that feels almost unreal. It’s the kind of spot where you just want to sit, breathe, and let the city’s charm wash over you, maybe with a coffee in hand or a camera tucked away, because some moments are just for feeling, not snapping || Beautiful viewpoint. Probably the most beautiful viewpoint of lisbon. Just soak in the surroundings and immerse yourself. The tram to the hill is generally full at the base. Suggest take bolt in case you struggle to do the hike. But don't miss this point. || Miradouro de Santa luzia  Visited around 3 PM and the view was just beautiful — calm, sunny, and full of charm. You can see the red rooftops and the Tagus River stretching into the distance. I only stayed about 10 minutes, but it was completely worth it. Such a peaceful spot in the middle of Lisbon. || Miradouro de Santa Luzia is a beautiful viewpoint with stunning views over Alfama’s rooftops and the Tagus River. The terrace is very charming, with flowers, shaded areas, and traditional Portuguese tiles that add to the atmosphere. It’s a great spot for photos and a short rest while exploring the area. It can get busy with tourists, but the view and vibe make it well worth a visit || A must-see viewpoint in the city. The view is essential, overlooking the sea and the rooftops below, but it is more decorated with azulejos tiles and a very cute little square than its neighbor, Portas do Sol ... and crowded as well most of the time ! || A very lovely patio with a great view! And it is free! Could be a bit crowded but would recommend to take a visit on your way down from the castle, as the view will not disappoint you for sure! || Beautiful view — especially stunning at sunrise or sunset.
