reviews_content: A definite must visit for Lisbon for the views alone as well as the history. Exceptional views across all of Lisbon. Some amazing historical walled artefacts. A beautifully curated museum in the centre with exceptional items through all the ages. The ostentation of peacocks is a lovely little bonus. Nice Ice Cream stand in the middle of the copse of trees near the more ancient ruins. The church right outside the gates is also a lovely little bonus || After visiting other castles in Malta, I personally found this one underwhelming. The castle is relatively small compared to others. The view is nice but you can get lookout spots similar to this one for free around Lisbon. The museum is only filled with old pots which I'm personally not a fan of. The archeological site was closed for some reason and a large part of the parking was all closed due to renovations or it being dangerous. So we didn't end up experiencing all of the site. I personally found more value from 15 Euros in other sites.  Another thing I would have preferred to see is written text throughout the castle. I know they went for a more traditional look and tried to provide an audio on your phone to listen to but this restrains you to follow the audios pace which was too slow for me. I like to go on my own pace and skip what I would like to skip.  I will say if you are a history freak it is a nice historic site, but for me personally it was sub-par.  I will say that the peacocks were very nice here but also you can find them free throughout lisban || This was on our must see list while we were in Lisbon as my friend and I both love touring castles. It wasn’t quite what we were expecting as it was very open and had a lot of courtyards and such but the view from the walls was beautiful. They also had peacocks everywhere which was really cool to see. The museum has a lot of ancient pottery and we learned the history of the tiles we’d been seeing everywhere so we enjoyed that. It does take quite a climb to get there but we were not disappointed! || After visiting the Lisbon cathedral, we walked up to the arch entrance of the castle - it’s walkable but be wary of a steep trek from the cathedral. We were able to use our Lisboa Card for free entry, which was a great bonus. The castle grounds offer incredible views across the city and plenty of historic areas to explore. There are loads of great photo opportunities, and the grounds are home to around two dozen peacocks and peahens. I’ve never seen so many in one place before, and they really add to the atmosphere.  The small museum inside is interesting and gives some insight into the history of the castle, including who built it, what it was used for, and a look at some of the pottery and tiles found on site. It’s also well air-conditioned, which makes it a nice break from the heat outside.  Be warned that the toilets are pretty unpleasant and located down some narrow, slightly sketchy stairs. The main castle area itself is mostly empty, with only the walls open to walk along. The views are fantastic from up there, but it’s definitely not ideal if you’re afraid of heights. The walkways are narrow and can get crowded, and there’s only a railing to hold on to.  We left just before sunset, and as we did, the queue to get in had grown a lot. Leaving early worked out well, as we were able to catch the bus back to the Rua with no hassle || I don’t usually like visiting castles and historic spots, but this castle was breathtaking. I highly recommend visiting it. My teenage boys also liked it. We enjoyed the kastana outside the castle. We took the hop on hop off green line to reach there which stopped exactly opposite to the castle. The area around was beautiful. Beautiful old town 💕 || Castelo de São Jorge is a stunning medieval fortress situated on one of Lisbon’s highest hills, providing visitors with magnificent panoramic views of the city, including the Alfama district, the Baixa area, the Tagus River, and the iconic 25 de Abril Bridge.  The castle itself has a rich history, originally serving as a Moorish citadel before becoming a royal palace and later a military stronghold.  Visitors can explore vast ramparts, eleven towers, archaeological sites, and remnants of the former royal palace, all set within beautiful gardens that are home to roaming peacocks, adding a unique and charming touch to the experience.  The castle's grounds feel like a living museum where one can marvel at medieval defensive architecture, walk along ancient walls, and enjoy peaceful spaces shaded by olive trees and dotted with historical artifacts.  Surrounding the castle, the neighborhood of Alfama offers a vibrant yet authentic atmosphere with narrow, winding streets, traditional tiled houses, cozy cafes, and small shops steeped in local culture.  The area is known for its lively yet intimate vibe, enriched by the sounds of Fado music and the daily rhythms of local residents.  Travelers often find themselves enchanted by the blend of history, culture, and scenic beauty, making the approach to the castle a meaningful journey in itself.  The castle’s elevated position allows for stunning sunrise and sunset views across Lisbon, creating memorable photo opportunities and moments of reflection against the backdrop of terracotta rooftops and the sparkling river below.  Visitors are recommended to arrive early to avoid crowds, as the castle tour, including its museum and archaeological areas, can take one to two hours. The pathway includes some steep climbs, but the well-preserved structures and the sweeping city vistas make the effort worthwhile.  There are also small cafes within the castle grounds where visitors can pause and enjoy refreshments while taking in the scenic surroundings.  Overall, Castelo de São Jorge offers a rich, immersive experience of historical, cultural, and natural heritage, making it a must-visit landmark for anyone exploring Lisbon’s fascinating past and vibrant present.  The castle’s majesty, along with the lively charm of its surroundings, creates an unforgettable visit that reflects both the resilience and spirit of Lisbon. || What an awesome experience this was!  Was there on a Tuesday afternoon and the crowds were light.  Very easy to walk around and explore.  (Although be warmed the steps are pretty steep and some have no handrails....careful!  Sights were amazing and there is a QR Code.at.the entrance that gives you a self guided audio your with anlot of history.  Awesome place and highly recommended! || Castelo de São Jorge in Lisbon is worth a visit for the views alone. Sitting on a hill in the Alfama district, it gives you a clear line of sight across the city and the Tagus River. There is something about seeing the red rooftops stretch out below that makes it easy to understand why Lisbon feels so special.  The castle itself is interesting, even if it is not the most polished attraction. Walking along the ramparts and towers, you can sense the layers of history that have shaped this place. Roman, Moorish, and medieval influences are all visible in the walls and fortifications. The layout is straightforward, but exploring the nooks and stairs gives a sense of how people lived and defended the city centuries ago.  One of the unexpected highlights is the peacocks. They wander freely across the grounds and gardens, adding a bit of life and color to the stone and brick. It is a small detail, but it makes the visit feel a little more playful.  If you are in Lisbon, give yourself an hour or two to explore. Wear comfortable shoes because the paths are cobbled, and take your time to enjoy the history, the views, and the peacocks. Castelo de São Jorge is real, atmospheric, and memorable. || Make sure to sign up for the guided tour which can be done at the ticket office, its free and its the only way to visit the archeological ruins. Our guide was knowledgeable and entertaining. The view from the top is stunning! The history of the area is beyond interesting. Highly recommend if visiting Lisbons historical center || This castle is situated on one of the highest hills and offers stunning panoramic view of lisbon. You can walk over the castle and towers which was fun. The place is overall well maintained and worth a visit. The route to get to the castle is walkable but be aware of the steep path. We visited this place during sunset and it was absolutely lovely and highly recommend visiting around sunset time. No advance booking required and we got the ticket upon arrival.

A wonderful museum in Lisbon located in the port area. The knowledge presented there is accessible yet delivered in a professional manner. Two temporary exhibitions made a strong impression on me. One was about a photography studio in Goa. Since it was a Portuguese colony, it’s always interesting to see how a country deals with such parts of its history. The narrative was excellent and conveyed these complex events very well. It’s certainly an educational value that museums should have. The second exhibition, about Japanese spirituality, is a brilliant introduction to this very complex subject. I highly recommend visiting this museum — it’s a wonderful way to deepen one’s understanding of the world and the history of Portugal. || Thank you Ra for your visit and comment. We hope to see you again soon. Museum of the Orient || Museu do Oriente  -  Where Earth Gods Whisper and Japanese Festivals Dance  Tucked along the Doca de Alcântara Norte, the Museu do Oriente is one of those places that feels like stepping into a quiet reverie - a space of ritual, rhythm, and reflection. We came specifically to catch the temporary exhibition JAPAN: Festivals and Rituals, and it did not disappoint. From vibrant masks to ceremonial garments, it was a fascinating glimpse into the spiritual heartbeat of Japan, where every object seemed to hum with centuries of meaning.  But the real surprise? The Earth Gods Velar Sculpture exhibition - a collection so awe-inspiring it made us pause mid-step. These sculptures don’t just sit in the room - they command it. You can feel the dedication, reverence, and raw craftsmanship in every curve and texture. It’s the kind of art that doesn’t ask for attention - it earns it.  While the museum houses several permanent exhibitions, our visit was laser-focused on these two. Entry gives you access to everything, but we were on a mission of meaning, and we found it.  Verdict: Museu do Oriente is a temple of quiet power, where ritual meets artistry, and where you can wander through spiritual landscapes without leaving Lisbon. Highly recommended for culture seekers, sculpture lovers, and anyone who believes that art should move you - even if it’s carved from stone. || Thank you, Pearl, for your visit and comment.  We are very happy that you found what you were looking for at the Museum of the Orient.  See you soon.  Museum of the Orient || Odd location, but the Museum Book Festival gave me the perfect reason to finally visit. I 1st went for 'Leafing through Japan' themed guided tour which was better than i antecipated. A well-paced guided tour. It was excellent. I went back for the Japan: Festivities and Rites guided tour, but It was different. Different guide, more centered on religion. It felt rushed compared to the other one. || Thank you for your visit and comment.  See you soon, Museum of the Orient || Fascinating museum which illustrates Portugal's historic connections and colonies within the far east. Lovely cafe/restaurant with a view of river at top level. || Thank you Barbara for your visit and comment. We hope to see you again soon. Museum of the Orient || Museu do Oriente  Type: museum Time spent: 40-60 min Price: 10 EUR, Friday 18-20 - free Parking: available, small Bike parking: not available WC: available Path for disabled: elevator  3 floors exhibition of Asian culture and Portuguese discoveries (Japan, China, India). It includes audio and video materials (English/ Portuguese). || Thank you Oleh Shpytko for your visit and comment. We hope to see you soon. Museum of the Orient || I hugely regret not setting aside a day for this! I had to go somewhere else by a certain time so had to rush through but there is so much to see! I really wish I'd had more time to look at everything properly. Absolutely worth the price, if I could I'd go again. || Thank you Rachael for your visit and comment. See you soon, Museum of the Orient || The museum is a good size in that there’s a good bit to see but you won’t be there all day! The collection is quite impressive. I went on a weekday and it was almost completely empty! || Thank you for your visit and comment.  See you soon, Museum of the Orient || I loved the Chinese porcelain collection and the Japanese festivals/rituals exhibit. The food at the fifth-floor restaurant was delightful and reasonably priced. || Thank you for your visit and comment.  See you soon, Museum of the Orient || The first floor of the museum is dedicated to the history of the Portuguese colony in Asia, trade relations between Portugal and Asia in the 15th-18th centuries, a large collection of porcelain. But the most interesting is on the second floor. There are showed religious traditions and holidays of Japan, the exhibition is really interesting. Of the minuses - there is no audio guide, so you need to read everything all the time. It took about 2.5 - 3 hours to visit the museum. || Thank you for your visit and comment. The Museum of the Orient has a mobile application, information about which is available at the Ticket Office, and which is a Digital Guide replacing the traditional audio guides. The APP is called "Discover what you are seeing", which can be accessed via the link - https://www.foriente.pt/detalhe.php?id=52E4D452-F141-4DD2-951B-E0CF623189B0&area=noticias - even outside the museum. It has translations in 7 languages ​​and content in LGP, AD and simplified language. See you soon, Museum of the Orient || Nice museum, quite large and focusing mostly on Portuguese influence in Asia. || Thank you Pedro Heitor for your visit and comment. See you soon. Museum of the Orient

Genuinely, the hidden gem of Lisbon. Worth the climb up from the coast and my word, what an attraction!  We had no queue and a very chill inside experience.  Explore (and I do mean explore) the exotic meandering paths through the foliage, it's great to spend an hour or so.  A really nice bio diversity to look at and enjoy. Particularly enjoyed the banana tree 🍌  Really fairly priced and a fantastic cultural excursion.  HUGE recommend✌️ || Estufa Fria is a true oasis of tranquility in the heart of Lisbon. A wonderful place to escape the hustle and bustle of the city and enjoy the beauty of exotic plants, waterfalls, and cozy paths. The atmosphere is truly peaceful, with everything well-kept and thoughtfully designed down to the last detail. A wonderful place for a leisurely stroll, meditation, or a romantic date. A must-see for anyone who loves nature and wants to see a different, greener side of Lisbon. One of the most pleasant and inspiring places in the city! || Nature, garden, and park lovers will enjoy this spot. It offers about 30–45 minutes of peaceful walking surrounded by greenery and a small artificial lake.  Entrance costs less than €4 per person — a very reasonable price for the experience.  There’s also a café with a lovely terrace nearby, though it’s not directly accessible through the greenhouse area. || Verry beautiful, if you are traveling to Lisbon or just live here, I would recommend coming here. It’s very beautiful nature in the middle of the city come here and relax and enjoy your day. also, if you are a student or a younger person, you can get tickets for way cheaper. You just need to show your student card confirmation that you are a student and we paid our tickets for five euros the two of us so that’s amazing. || Really nice and super cheap. Cool plants and I saw baby ducks! there are so many rooms and pathways, despite it not being the biggest building in the world you really feel like you can get lost in there. Very thoughtfully and beautifully designed. || If you’re in Lisbon on a Sunday and want a peaceful escape from the city buzz, Estufa Fria is absolutely perfect. Hidden inside Parque Eduardo VII, this lush greenhouse feels like stepping into another world — calm, green, and full of life. 🌴  You’ll walk through tropical plants, waterfalls, and quiet pathways where time slows down. It’s beautifully maintained, not crowded, and filled with natural light filtering through the glass roof — ideal for a relaxed stroll or quiet reflection.  💚 Perfect for: •	A slow Sunday morning or afternoon •	Nature lovers, photographers, and couples •	Escaping the heat or city noise  Tip: Grab a coffee nearby afterward and enjoy the view over Avenida da Liberdade — it completes the perfect Sunday in Lisbon. || This is a great area to stroll through while enjoying beautiful flora and fauna. It is located at the far end of Eduardo VII Park. We spent 45 minutes there. || This botanical garden is my favourite hidden gem in Lisbon! Lots of great spots inside for photography and well maintained. Very affordable too! 🌿 || Most beautiful garden i have ever seen. So lush and green with the most monstera i have ever seen. So peaceful and relaxing. Toilets inside. Sat with goslings and ducklings and saw chickens and peacocks as well. Student tickets were €1.80! Highly recommend || This botanical garden is a true gem, offering a diverse collection of plants.  The layout is well-designed, creating a tranquil and relaxing atmosphere.  There are numerous benches and open spaces, perfect for enjoying a picnic lunch.  The affordable 3 euro entrance fee makes it an exceptional value.  A visit here is highly recommended for anyone seeking a peaceful escape.  The variety of flora provides something of interest for every visitor.  It's a wonderful place to spend a few hours immersed in nature.
Clean and safe location. There is paid parking in the area. || A superb pavilion, rich in discoveries. || Pier under construction.

An interesting historical spot in the center of Lisbon. The ruins are atmospheric and give a good sense of the city’s past, especially knowing the monastery was destroyed in the 1755 earthquake and never rebuilt.  The museum itself is quite small, you can walk through everything in about 20 minutes. It’s not a must-see or a top priority if you’re visiting Lisbon for the first time, but it’s still worth a short visit if you’re nearby or interested in history and architecture. || Carmo Archaeological Museum is a beautiful and unique museum in Lisbon that’s definitely worth a visit.  Housed in the stunning ruins of the Carmo Convent, it offers an incredible glimpse into Portugal’s history.  The exhibits are fascinating, covering archaeology, medieval artifacts, and more. Admission is €5, or you can get a 15% discount with the Lisboa Card.  Note that it’s closed on Sundays, so plan accordingly.  Overall, it’s one of the best places to explore Lisbon’s rich past—truly unforgettable! 🏛️✨ || The Convento do Carmo is one of the most impressive places I visited in Lisbon. The partially destroyed convent creates a unique and almost surreal atmosphere, especially with the open roof and the gothic arches framing the sky. The museum inside is small but well curated, with interesting archaeological pieces and a calm, peaceful ambience.  It’s a place where you can really pause for a moment, take in the history, and enjoy the contrast between ruin and preservation. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Lisbon. || This was simply stunning and we went a little before sunset so we had the opportunity to get to see it in the day and the evening making it even more spectacular.  I would plan on spending at least an hour here enjoying the Carmo Archaeological Museum in order to really take it in. || ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Where Gothic drama meets archaeological treasure hunting with killer views 🏛️  If you're going to stumble upon history anywhere in Lisbon, let it be here. The Carmo Archaeological Museum isn't just housed in a "nice historic building" - it's dramatically perched inside the haunting ruins of a 14th-century Gothic convent that the 1755 earthquake couldn't quite finish off. Talk about resilience with style!  The roofless nave creates this absolutely magical open-air cathedral vibe where ancient stones and sky conspire to give you goosebumps. The contrast between delicate archaeological finds and those massive, earthquake-scarred arches is pure poetry. You'll find everything from Roman mosaics to medieval tombs, including some genuinely fascinating Visigothic pieces that most tourists completely miss.  Bonus points for the panoramic views! The elevated position gives you lovely vistas over Lisbon's rooftops and beyond - it's like getting a history lesson with a scenic backdrop thrown in for free.  Pro tip: Visit late afternoon when the light filters through those Gothic arches just right and the city views are at their most golden. The entrance fee is reasonable, staff are knowledgeable without being pushy, and it's mercifully tourist-trap-free.  A perfect gem hiding in plain sight in the heart of Chiado! 📷✨ || Worth visiting. There are some interesting relics and mummies. I do like how the repurposed the building. I wouldn’t make a special trip to see it, but would visit if I was in the area. It is amazing how many of the buildings never recovered from fires, earthquakes, and tsunamis that occurred 500 years ago. || Museum welcomes you with fascinating view of survived pieces of monastery under the open sky, inside there are artifacts that I personally never saw on my own eyes. And even (usually boring) history movie was creative and intersting! Bonus points for a cute cat. || If you love ancient history especially Portuguese history this is a must see. I was astounded by all the artifacts that were uncovered in Portugal alone, including a small mummy. And the ruins of what’s left behind from the 1755 earthquake is very sobering. A trip to Lisbon is not complete without a visit to this area. The history of Carmo Square can’t be ignored. || I walked by this several times over my stay in Lisbon and decided to go in near the end of my trip. I am so glad I did!! This was one of my favorite sites in Lisbon. It literally took my breath away when I walked through its door. It is an absolutely stunning treasure. || Well worth a visit. 7 euros per person takes you inside. It is absolutely stunning. Very clever way of explaining the whole history is a film that runs inside in English and Portuguese. You can just walk in and leave as you please. Displays inside is beautiful and very well marked and description is well put out. We got there around 2pm, and it was busy but not overly busy

A beautiful and peaceful spot right by the Tagus River — perfect for a stroll, watching the sunset. You get a great view of the 25 de Abril Bridge and the passing ferries especially with Sunset.  It’s a simple place, but somehow feels magical — especially in the golden hour. A must-stop if you’re walking around Praça do Comércio. || Its a beautiful square on the beach of the river, with an amazing view and on calm days it is peaceful enough to just sit there or have a walk and enjoy the view of the river and Almada across the river. || We were walking around Lisbon for several days while waiting to join our cruise. By the river in front of Praça do Comercio, we observed two stone columns in the water. We were told by the guide that the columns were installed with a dock in 1755 after the earth quakes. It is a nice quiet spot by the water to relax. || Cais das Colunas is one of those places in Lisbon that just sticks with you. Tucked right next to Praça do Comércio, it’s a peaceful riverside spot with amazing views of the Tagus—especially at sunset. Whether you're passing through or looking for a place to unwind, this is a perfect stop.  The vibe here is really special. It’s calm but still full of life—locals lounging around, tourists soaking it all in, occasional street performers, and sometimes even live music playing in the background. It feels like a snapshot of Lisbon’s soul.  I love grabbing a coffee and just sitting on the stone steps, watching boats go by and the sky change colors as the city lights start to glow. It’s also a great spot for photos—between the water reflections and the beautiful architecture, everything looks picture-perfect.  It’s simple, free, and yet one of the most memorable parts of the city. I’ve been here multiple times and always end up staying longer than I planned.  If you’re visiting Lisbon, definitely carve out a little time to come here. You won’t regret it. || The view of the Tagus River, the 25th of April Bridge, and the view is simply breathtaking, especially at sunset. It’s a great spot to sit, take photos, and soak in the city’s atmosphere. A must-see for anyone exploring the Praça do Comércio area || Great area to visit and hang out with family and friends. A lot of restaurants and cafes,  beautiful view of the city and the river. || The place is amazing for walk at end of the day and or just sit and listen to sound of water and birds flying. I think both locals and tourists come here often just to sit enjoy the sunset views, the vibe and view of the other side of the city.  Best time to go there is when it is sunny at end of the day to get relaxed and enjoy the sunset, or in the morning for sunrise. During the day mostly when it is sunny it is quite crowded. || This is a historic riverside pier in Lisbon, easily recognized by its two marble columns rising from the Tagus River. Designed by Eugénio dos Santos as part of the city’s reconstruction after the 1755 earthquake, the columns are said to be inspired by those of Solomon’s Temple—symbolizing wisdom and devotion. For much of its history, this pier served as a key docking point for ferries and ships, connecting Lisbon with the southern bank of the Tagus and functioning as an important transport hub. The original columns were removed in the late 19th century, later restored in 1929, dismantled again during metro construction in 1997, and finally reinstalled in 2008. || As described, past historic entryway to the city. Some nice musicians, but wouldn’t recommend more then 15min here || It was a lovely day for a walk, and this was a lovely place to visit! There is only a small sandy beach area, but it was fairly clean and our little dog absolutely loved running around on the sand after walking on pavement all day! (we didn't see any signs saying that dogs are not allowed on the beach and we kept her on a leash).

It's a huge and beautiful plaza that has been decorated with a Christmas tree and surrounding lights. You can see a beautiful sunset from here too and musicians like to come around and play to entertain your views and videos with sweet melodies! It's a must see in Lisbon and you can also see a gigantic arch and a middle statue in honor of someone important in Portuguese history. || Praça do Comércio considered a historical symbol of political power and manifestation of capitality in Portugal. It's a beautiful place to spend quality time with family, friends & special person. It's quite and welcome people who really wants to enjoy sunset. After the Revolution of 1910 the buildings were painted pink. However, they have recently returned to their original color, yellow. The south side, with its two square towers, is faced to the Tagus. || Lots of fun activities around. We saw street entertainment, vendors and restaurants and even a 360° video booth! Walk down to the water and sit of the steps to enjoy the waves. As long as you don’t feed the birds you’ll enjoy it || History at its best, even when it's busy it is possible just to stand in your own wee world and admire the architecture.  if you have a Lisbon travel card, you can climb the stairs to the top of the monument for fantastic views all for free.  Be sure to visit one or more of the wonderful restaurants round the sides.  Nightime is a completely different experience and one not to be missed. || 🌅 Where the City Opens to the River ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)  After walking down Rua Augusta on that bright June 2025 afternoon, we finally reached Praça do Comércio — Lisbon’s great stage by the Tagus River. Still with my friend, I remember stepping out from beneath the arch and feeling the city breathe wider, as if every street had been leading to this one golden moment.  The vast square, once home to Portugal’s royal palace before the 1755 earthquake, now stands as a symbol of rebirth. The yellow arcades glow under the sunlight, and the sound of waves blends with the hum of trams. In the middle, King José I’s bronze statue, mounted on his horse Gentil, looks forever toward the river — the same horizon that launched the Age of Discoveries. Standing there, I could almost imagine ships setting sail again.  We rested on the marble steps facing the Tagus, watching ferries and silhouettes cross the glittering water. It was hot — the kind of radiant, reflective heat only Lisbon can produce — but the breeze from the river made everything slow down, peaceful and cinematic.  Practical Notes  Visit near sunset for cooler air and golden light on the arcades.  Bring water; shade is limited.  Perfect spot for wide-angle photos or time-lapse videos.  Cafés under the arcades are pricier but worth it for the view.  Quick Ratings Historical & Cultural Value: 10/10 Atmosphere & River Views: 9.5/10 Accessibility: 9/10 📸 Photo & Video Potential: 10/10 Café & Rest Spots: 8.5/10  📝 If this glimpse of Lisbon resonated with you, hit 👍 and follow me — I share real impressions from Europe’s most curious corners. || Praça do Comércio is one of Lisbon’s most impressive and iconic squares. The wide open space, framed by historic yellow buildings and facing the river, creates a grand and welcoming atmosphere. It’s a beautiful place to walk through, especially in the late afternoon when the light reflects off the water and the arcades.  The square is lively but not overwhelming, with plenty of cafés and easy access to the surrounding streets of Baixa. A must-see landmark that perfectly captures the elegance and scale of Lisbon’s waterfront. || We were in Lisbon for a few days while waiting to join a cruise. We spent a lot of time walking around this area as there is a lot to see here. The plaza is magnificent. Beautiful big arch surrounded by beautiful buildings. Outdoor cafes, statues and lots of tourists all around. A must see if you visit Lisbon. || This is not a destination site but it is worth walking through just for the sheer size of it. It’s also on the water and has one of the Lisboa signs (great for touristy photos!) at the end near the water. You can also see the 25 Abril bridge from here. It was pretty at Christmas with a huge tree. || It’s a nice place, but there are too many touts. First, they will try to sell you sunglasses and then they all move onto other substances. I was bothered here at least five times in an unsolicited way. || Get a leg (or foot!) up and go to the top of the entrance to Lisbon! Beautiful views and we were able to appreciate an aerial view of the beautiful tile on the streets. We also saw the castle we were visiting next!

My fav Lisbon park! Such a wonderful green space full of amazing trees and plants away from busy streets. The park used to be the garden of a wonderful Palace and is littered with beautiful old buildings and statues surrounded by nature and teaming with birds including chickens, geese peacocks and parakeets plus lots of stray cats. Set on a hill looking down to the river this parc is like stepping back in time. Never too busy and space to sit and just connect with nature. || Pretty neglected for the potential it has.  From dry vegetation that amounts, to destroyed/eroded pathways and all the buildings collapsing or ruined.  Among those a beautiful circular building with a greenhouse like glass roof, that by itself is worth the visit.  Just judge it too harshly by its state for it is in my opinion appealing as a rui ed site.  Can’t help to feel like patrimony is being lost without any concern or attempt to save it.  OVERALL IT IS FREE, so can’t really complain on the ticket price 😂  Therefore the relation price to quality of experience is actually juicy better than the Belém Botanical garden.  Also quite awesome if one is into urban ruin exploring! || I really liked this park, it is located a little away from the city center, therefore, there are very few people here and it is clean. There are several picnic tables, peacocks and ducks are walking, a beautiful view of the bridge, a lot of exotic plants and it's just nice to walk here. || A very wonderful and beautiful park.  - Diverse plants, interesting landscape, lots of greenery, and a fairly large area for walking. - There are buildings and fountains. They are partially abandoned but very atmospheric. - There is a lawn where people sunbathe in good weather. - Chickens, geese, peacocks, and cats roam freely around the area. - The park also has a restroom and an enclosed area for dog walking || A beautiful, tranquil space with magnificent cactuses. The chickens run wild, and it feels like a place from a different era. The views of the bay, framed by the plants are something you don't get in many other places either. || It’s a beautiful park with a rare tree that it’s worth spending some time with. Although it’s not for those with walking difficulties as it has elevations and unevenness. Love that there are chickens, peacocks and geese roaming freely. And there are benches for those who wants a place to chill and have their meals. || It has the potential to be the best park in the city if anyone would invest in it.  It has: In the central part is a big lawn, great for picnics and enjoying the peace and quiet (ducks, peacocks, gees and chickens excluded). To the west of the lawn there is a dog or children park, i was not sure, but it is fenced so they don't bother those that are allergic to them. On the other side to the east of the lawn there is a pond with ducks. Further east from the lawn there are staircases that lead to the closed section unfortunately, with a garden done in french style, with a symmetrical pattern of short hedges outlining the flowers planted there. And by looking at it on google maps it is apparent that on the other side of it there are staircases again leading to another similar area that is also closed off. To the north of the lawn there are buildings. First up right next to the lawn there is a glass dome that looks like a theater of some sort, although small and half the glass roof is shattered, then behind it there are buildings that look like maybe they were coops for the birds that are now running around. Coming right behind that is a plato with a big circular water feature that isn't working and half around it is a wall with a (closed) gate that leads into a (overgrown) corridor that leads to some sort of i guess important building. Next to the corridor starts a cactus garden that has been left unchecked for far too long. Even though cactuses are thriving, the paths through it are bit harder to navigate so caution is advised. || Absolutely got surprised by this little park in a quite busy city district. I was expecting an average garden park in the middle of a concrete jungle, but when I entered I got a real different feeling. Being used to Lisbon's buzziness, I am often missing the nature. This park has a very wild feeling to it. Even though it still offers the clean open grass area to lie down and enjoy a picnic with friends and family, you feel like in the middle of untouched nature just a few steps away from the central grass area. The cactus garden offers exactly what you expect and more. There are wild plants and of course 🌵🌵 but there are also free running chicken and even peacocks with beautiful feathers. Feels very untouched, and has even a great view to the bridge. The constant airplane crossing still remind you that you are almost in central Lisbon. Definitely worth a visit if you like wild nature and peace just around the corner. || Very calm space - the perfect get away from the busy touristy areas. Some visitors are sunbathing on the grass. The cactus garden impressed me with the size of the cactuses - some of them were twice my height. There are many happy birds but mostly roosters, crowing non-stop. It’s probably a way to prove their masculinity in front of the chicks… actually I don’t know - it’s not my business :) There are several neglected structures that are still quite beautiful. || What a beautiful, interesting little park! Off the beaten track, loads of ducks, geese, chickens, and pea-fowl. The cactus garden area was where the chickens were plotting to take over the world lol. So glad we happened upon it. || The park could be beautiful as I believe once was, but today it is very poorly maintained with destroyed paths, overgrown bushes and sad abandoned buildings. It probably wouldn't even be expensive to restore it, so I'm confused how they could let this happen. || A nice park to have a picnic. The few features are the peacocks and the geese’s. And the Dragoeiro plant at the south entrance. I read that it’s rare and only a few hundreds left. The park did have a lot of variations of flora, maybe it’s winter time. Oh.. the white roosters seems to monopolised the north entrance. They are cute and naturally roaming. Just an easy part to walk. Nearby is Jardim Estrella which is smaller but probably more family friendly. You could see my other  review there. || This park is extremely underrated!! LOOK AT ALL THESE CHICKENS!!! I was so surprised and tickled to walk through….chickens, cats, many differently types of cactus (and mature too), and a fantastic view of 25 of April Bridge!!! If I lived here I would come often to the park. Peaceful and a jungle of endless exploration. || This a beautiful park that is located off the beaten path. It is quite hilly but there is plenty of shade. The main reason to go is to see all the species of native birds. I saw chickens, geese, pigeons, and peacocks. Just make sure to not step in the animal dung! || We were lucky to find this place. It's very authentic and very beautiful in terms of authentic landscape design. Just have a look at my photos. We could see many photographers that make photo sessions there. There are many white chickens, colorful peacocks, ducks, gooses, etc. There is big walking area and also some field where you can take sun bath or sit at the tables and have a picknick. || There's a hidden gem in the park - a collection of one of the oldest cacti on the planet. It's a free admission to the park except for the restroom, you'll have to pay for adults. There's a water fountain in the park, so you can fill your bottle with it. We visited during Easter holiday, and it was very nice to see that someone was sweet and thoughtful to "hide" some candies in trees and bushes for kids. || I love this garden: feels so wild with all the wonderful animals! Peacocks, chickens, cats, geese and more.  Highly recommend the cactus garden 🌵 the only downside for me is there’s no like little place for refreshments or drinks (I couldn’t find a water tap either). So come prepared!!! || It's the perfect spot for a picnic, to enjoy a sunny day, or simply for a walk. The park offers a calm setting for outdoor activities and relaxation. || Beautiful calm park with a nice cactus garden, free chicken and peacocks. Very nice. || A peaceful park in Lisbon with quiet paths winding around ponds and towering cacti, plus the occasional rooster to hear or peacock to spot. Perfect for a lunchtime break or a change of scenery. It offers ancient trees and impressive views of the Ponte 25 de Abril. A must-see hidden gem.

place_name: Reservatório da Mãe d'Água das Amoreiras

reviews_content: Little bit dirty, but just the homeless You can see some really genius artist || I stumbled upon it by chance while descending from the Miradouro da Senhora do Monte viewpoint. I was particularly struck by the variety of graffiti and the seemingly well-executed work. Graffiti brightens Lisbon, making it much more attractive and freer. || Street art is everywhere in Lisbon! Impressive, fantastic, and surprising, and of truly great artistic value! These pictures show just a few of these gems. || I love street art, so Lisbon in general is a feast for the eyes. Graffiti on the Wall is simply a street with four larger graffiti pieces, which can also be admired throughout the city. It was right on our way, but driving there would have been excessive. || Very nice graffiti that you should definitely visit if it is not too much of a detour

Pleasant green space with coffee shops and bars as well as a children’s play area. One of the bars has live entertainment. At one end of the park, stunning view of Lisbon and the river. || One of the best gardens in Lisbon!! Very chill and relatively less crowded than the other famous parks here, so if you’re looking for a serenity, this might be a good spot. Easy to come here by tram or metro after walking a bit. || Great place for a hanging out - beautiful scenery, centrally located near the bairro alto - I can totally recommend || Bistro/restaurant in the park, perfect for a timeout from sightseeing in the shade, there was a singer singing fado, the food was just es expected, warm, tasty, and the whole experience was just perfect || It’s a good place to sit for some time. There is free access to drinking water and also a place where the public can charge their phones for free. However, you need to bring your own charger. || Lovely park to rest the knackered feet after walking up and down hills all day || A wonderful garden with some lovely plants and flowers to view.  On a hot day, this is a great garden to visit. With many trees to provide some shade, you can enjoy the suns rays as well as keeping chilled.  It's quite a small garden, but with a small fee of 5 Euro it is worth a visit (if you like gardens). There are some cool art displays within the gardens also, which fit into the space nicely.  Overall these gardens offer good value fro money and is lovely to walk around and explore new and interesting plants. || Even at afternoon heat a good place to relax. With small cafe and sometimes live music. Nice! || My neighborhood park. It's awesome. Beautiful trees. Farmer's market on Saturdays. Friendly kiosks for a cold beer or fresh pastry. It's golden! || Wonderful spot to relax after walking all day, or go for a stroll and grab a snack and/or drink at one of two kiosks or the small restaurant. Playground is brand new and has something for all ages. Statues and artwork are a treat to discover and contemplate. Plenty of seating and grass around the park for lounging around. || Most favorite park in Lisbon. It's a perfect combination of nature, art, walkways, grass, benches, and cafe in a free space that's easy to get around. Way better than the botanical garden nearby, and it's free! || I would never give up on recommending this spot in Lisbon. For Saturdays market or to meet with you the oldest tree in Lisbon.. 300 yo ceder. That's the truth story of the city.. you just need to listen. || Amazing small. Garden in very beautiful area for pet walk and child play area there are wooden seat to sit down and enjoy. Very old type of trees looks ancient and historic || Beautiful peaceful park in a nice area with a good kids play area, shaded seating and nearby toilet. || Beautiful place to walk around and enjoy the nice views rot he city. There was live music and a truck to buy some drinks, perfect combination! || I loved the old tree the most and the other cluster of trees that make up the garden. A great place to spot and there are enough vendors to get snacks, beer or a cup of coffee.  Once you are here and you are in for a hike, you can walk to Rato or even Estrella. You can catch the tram 28 to Chiado or do a detour to Cais do Sodre. It is not an easy walk, but yeah, some of the random.things you do in Lisbon and get home walking about 8 - 10,000 steps. || Very nice place to relax. Unique huge tree. Nice vibe music from the park kiosk. Clean and calm || One of the most magnificent trees I have ever seen is in this lovely park. Large enough to sit 60 people under this tree is supported by wrought iron scaffold. I was kid again when I first saw it. Well worth the visit if you are near by. Also has a market on weekend and a cafe that is open daily. || A very beautiful place to sit under a special tree that provides the much needed shade. Find an ice cream parlor nearby and this garden is the perfect place to eat your ice cream. || Just a super place to relax and great cafe in under a canopy of wild looking trees.

Just beautiful, armonic, and calm park right next to Avenida. Surrounded by beautiful trees, vegetation, and colorfoul buildings.  There is a quiosque inside and a fountain, perfect for dates or unwinding sessions. || Being in a beautiful small garden and park,  its concerts, a childrens' playground and a lovely fountain make this a very enjoyable setting for a great cafe with food from the restaurant across the street. A very good Caesar's Salad and a delicious Black Rice were two dishes we thoroughly enjoyed.  Good prices, too! || Small little park, allows dogs on leash. You can relax on a bench and drink a coffee in a little kiosk that’s directly there. Lots of bins a drinking water station for dogs available. || Lovely garden just west of the Avenida de Liberdade.  Beautiful large trees, grassy areas and a central water fountain. Small kiosk and some park benches avaliable. Very clean and well looked after.  Great place to relax after a long day of site seeing. || Cool little park with many couples hanging out even at midnight 😀 … || A great place for a quiet coffee break in the city center. Soothing fountain water splashes, doves looking for food, a nice cafe booth with tables and lots of benches to find a shady place for feet rest. || This park is great. They have spider plants growing OUTSIDE! The place smelt really nice as well || Such a lovely cute park. Nice shade, fountain was flowing. || Praça da Alegria (also called Alfredo Keil Garden) is located just to the west of Ave. da Liberdade. You will also find a nice double chalice water fountain and circular basin, traditional Portuguese style cobblestone surfacing as well as some tall and attractive trees providing significant shade.  There is also a bust monument of Alfredo Keil (1930), composer and author of the National Anthem of Portugal along with children's playground and kiosk selling drinks and light snacks. During our visit, a craft market was being held on the square as well. || Some of the most beautiful trees I’ve ever seen, incredibly well maintained, has a small cute cafe here to sit and enjoy the area and a small playground for children || Beautiful trees, lots of benches to sit and have a break. Gorgeous fountain, and free wifi !! || We sat in front of the fountain with my girlfriend and it was one of my favorite moments of our trip!! || Nice little garden, with a fountain, a "secured" kids play area and an outside restaurant, for quick meals. Very petfriendly.  Please look at the BEAUTIFUL/OLD trees! Simply amazing and unique! ❤️ || Stunning. No words to describe. It's the most beautiful place I ever been in Portugal || Nice park with a fountain.  You can see small shop to buy bags, caps and post card.  This park is surrounded by small hotels. || Nice little square with grass and a quiosk in the middle of Lisbon.  Great way to spend an hour or two, especially if you have a dog! || There was a festival nearby and the vibes are great || Nice outdoor place to have a drink and snack.  Seating with umbrellas. || Lovely park in centre is Lisbon. Beautiful trees, play ground and drinks kiosk. || Praça da Alegria is a small, tranquil park and garden in downtown Lisbon, Portugal just a block up a small incline road from Avenida da Liberdade. The charm of this place is its dominating large stone round pool with bronze fountain spraying water into the pool.  The beautiful garden includes mature trees, greenery, shrubs and flowers, and it seems to have very few visitors, perhaps because it's slightly off the beaten path.  There are several stone benches surounding the fountain area where you can relax and meditate, away from the hustle and bustle of the main roads and squares of Lisbon.  I was very delighted to discover that this park has its own free WiFi, which was both welcome and strong. || A very pleasant place with a terrace and live music. || Beautiful little park with fountains. Great place to rest on the way to the botanical garden. || Great place for a relaxed afternoon just off Avenida Libertad. || It's a cute little park which isn't very crowded. You can go there to walk your pet and if you have children, they can play on the slide and swing. There are benches to sit around the fountain and also Cafe Bagel to enjoy a cup of coffee ☕ :) || Grass, music and good to relax. || Cool little sit down area for beers in the open. No toilets in open but hotel across the road will let you use theirs. Very relaxed vibe and family friendly. Sometimes buskers perform there || The park is surrounded by busy roads and under the flight path for the airport so it isn't quiet. Having said that it still fulfilled the purpose of a city park by providing an escape from the bussel of the city. || Beautiful park. Trees are awesome. I rate with 2 stars only because there is a kiosk with snacks and drinks. Tenants cough and sneeze while preparing food without proper sanitizing , also they do NOT wash the vases, silver, plates,etc. They only rinse with plain water. To my this is highly un acceptable. I do not recommend to have prepared food, ask only for beer on a bottle and packed snacks. || A beautiful praça, but it’s plagued with flies all summer after Santos festival in June, during which there’s a month of grilled sardines and whole roasted pigs being offered here. The best time is spring because plants are green and the flies haven’t arrived yet. || Took there time to prepare food got a funny feeling that they forgot to to cook it when you consider 2 other couples order the same thing and got there before us my wife had to ask again and they said they are waiting for the kitchen in the hotel across the road to say it was really but 10 minutes later they came out of the hotel with the food

place_name: Convento de São Pedro de Alcântara
reviews_content: This is a beautiful church to visit just across the street from the wildly popular Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara (viewpoint) in Bairro Alto.  The Chapel of the Lencastres just outside the main church entrance is very impressive. It is laid with marble and included a lovely altar.  The main church is equally attractive with Baroque features, a nice high altar and walls lined with azulejo (blue and white tile) panels that make for a most beautiful viewing of the church.  Well worth visiting for 10-20 minutes if you plan to spend time at Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara. || Beautiful blue tile work adorn the walls of this beautiful church. It’s quiet and a respite from the busy mirador right across the road. || Around 1:30pm I walked around the entire block twice and couldn't figure out how to get in. There were 2 iron gates but they were locked. I went across the street to a vendor and asked if they knew but they didn't. I went back an hour later and they were still closed. || Small church with huge beautiful paintings on the wall and the always present “azulejos” at eye level.  And the small Chappell  at its side is worth the view: walls, floor, ceiling, wow || A very nice church and chapel,  just beneath the tourist eyes,  and yet so ignored by them... || Special venue full of the typical blue tiles of Lisbon. || An amazing church in the heart of Lisbon. They also offer tours in 4 languages with a modest price around 2 or 3 euros. It was an unforgettable experience as for the first time I could walk straight until the end of the church standing beneath the statue of  Jesus Christ. || Great interior. I guess many people pass it by because the exterior is not so lavish. But it is beautiful inside. I was alone on 24th of december there, around 14h. || Churches and convents have particular visiting hours especially on Mondays, watch them before you go. || We are lucky we are so near to this peaceful heaven so relax inside , everyone should visit to get off the anxiety || If you are in the area, you should stop here for a few moments. || Amazing little church that no one else seem to know about || Superb 😻 Magnificent historic site not demolished by the earthquake … || This convent, despite being relatively recent (17th century), has a fascinating history, and its various constituent elements are fabulous. First of all, the tilework that accompanies us from the entrance door to the end of the visit. The Lencastre chapel, with its walls inlaid with polychrome marble. The church, with its single nave, has, in addition to the tiles alluding to the life of St. Peter of Alcântara, significant paintings and a main altar. A visit to the Sacristy, Upper Choir, and Cloister is also not to be missed. || Beautiful Baroque church with fine gilded wood carvings and lovely blue and white tiles. I attended a very good 16th-century music concert there, the church's acoustics also contributing to the success. || The most popular tourist attraction is the viewpoint, but this place often goes unnoticed by most visitors. However, it's a beautifully preserved gem. Inside the church, you can admire a spectacular tile mural depicting the saint's life. We had no trouble visiting it, and the security guard was very friendly. || The area is beautiful, the Bairro Alto, panoramic, a beautiful building on the outside, reveals a warm and welcoming interior, spectacular, full of valuable artistic details, absolutely not to be missed. || It's not very big, and the visit is quick, but the chapel is very pretty. There's a small square in front (Jardim António Nobre) that's very pleasant, with a lovely view despite the gates that prevent access.

place_name: Mestre da Cerveja | Craft Beer & Sports Bar
reviews_content: I visited this beer bar and had a wonderful experience, thanks to Sergio. His kindness and warm hospitality created such a welcoming atmosphere. With great attention and a friendly approach, he ensured every moment was enjoyable. A fantastic host in a fantastic spot. Variety of beer options. || Dear Adil, thank you so much for your kind words. Yes, Sérgio is a wonderful barman and suits our small family business magnificently. We hope to see you again soon! || Great craft beers and service is excellent. I had a couple amazing IPAs and then a couple more! The Prizm Z was very tasty. || Thanks for your kind words Mike. Welcome back anytime! || I popped in here when I was visiting Lisbon in September of 2023. I chatted with the owner for a while and he had a great selection and knowledge of local and foreign beers. I will definitely return if I find myself back in Lisbon someday! || Came here a few weeks ago with my fellow Estonians right after it opened its doors and we were not left disappointed – the owner was very social and let us know his and his tiny bar's rather exciting history. Selection of beer was pretty good and there's no doubt everyone will find something for their taste buds from sours to belgians. Good luck from Estonia, you're doing the right thing! || Hi Marko, thanks a lot. It was great to meet you. Hope next time you are in Lisbon you visit here again. Best. || Great hole in the wall bar for local/European craft brews || Many thanks for your kind words, and we hope to see you again some day! || Friendly people serving good beer. Can’t ask for much more! || Thanks for your kind words John. Welcome back, any time! || Overall good selection || Thanks for your kind words! || The owner is an absolute legend! Cheers from the guy that locked himself out of his car. 😄 || Hi Hannes, thanks for that and thanks for the beers. Just received them. Hope to see you again. || Excellent, informative and personalized service. Carlo goes above and beyond to provide a pleasant and welcoming environment for any and every client. || Thanks a lot, Rafael. Hope to see you again here to try new beers. || Nice experience during world cup,nice owner,knowing his beers! Cheers || Thanks for your feedback, Emilian. Hope to see you here again soon. Best.

Really delicious food at reasonable prices.  The dumplings, fried rice and the chicken and goat curry were delicious! We Had a great time here it’s a great vibe! The owner and the chef were so friendly and recommended delicious dishes. Place is dog friendly too 🥰 || Thank you very much Vicky, See you next time || Such a lovely gem! From the very first moment, we felt warmly welcomed. The owner creates a relaxed and friendly atmosphere, while the chef prepares each dish with so much love and care. You can truly taste the freshness and passion in every bite – like a little “Nepalese hug for the senses.” He also took the time to recommend dishes we shouldn’t miss, and his suggestions were absolutely perfect.  A wonderful place in Lisbon that makes you feel at home right away – and one we can’t wait to return to. Absolutely worth a visit! || Thank you very much Alena, See you again!! || We recently ate at Nuko for the first time and were instantly greeted by the very friendly owner. For starters we had the Asian cucumber and the spicy fries then followed with Mo-Mos and chicken fried rice. The food was absolutely delicious and would highly recommend eating here. Thank you so much. 😁 || Thank you very much Paul, See you again!! || We were lucky to find Nuko when lots of places were closed in the early evening on a Sunday. Momos were delicious and presented beautifully, chaat was fresh, crunchy and flavorful, Nepalese fries were the best fries i had in Portugal and the spices and sauce they served it with were wonderful. The only drawback is that it's a pretty small and casual location, inside there were about 4 tiny tables that maybe 8-10 people total could fit in and outside there was room for a few more small tables. Overall, a very great experience eating here and i would love to go back. || Thank you very much Mark, See you again!! || We visited Nuko Restaurant & Bar in June and from the very first moment, we felt truly welcomed. The owner personally takes care of everything – from the warm greeting to lovingly preparing each dish himself.  The food was simply outstanding: everything super fresh, cooked with an incredible amount of care and love. Every bite felt like a little “Nepalese massage for the senses.” The atmosphere was relaxed, and the service perfectly attentive.  I still think back to that beautiful moment to this day and regret only now finding the time to write this review, even though I had wanted to do it much earlier. We wish him nothing but the very best – he truly deserves it! We will certainly be back!!  Absolutely recommended! || Thank you so much Ole, You kind review really made my day. See you soon again. !! || Wow! A lovely little hidden gem in Lisbon. The delicious Momo dumplings are a must try! The food here is divine. The chilli levels can be adjusted to your taste buds as the food is cooked fresh with each order. A little taste of Nepal in Portugal!  Thank you to the owner for being so accommodating with our little one. We will be back again. Thank you so much! || Thank you very much J M. See you again!! || Very nice and cozy restaurant. The owners are very kind and welcoming. The chiya is delicious and the jhol momo is amazing: juicy, full of spice and flavour! Perfect for a cold rainy day. || Thank you very much Leah. See you next time... || I usually love exploring different ethnic cuisines, but Nepalese food was still missing from my list. Well, not anymore! I stumbled upon this little gem right in the heart of Campo de Ourique, and it turned out to be a true flavor journey through Nepal. From their delicious MOMo dumplings to the samosas and chicken curry, every single dish was perfectly balanced and a real explosion of taste. And last but definitely not least, Nabin’s kindness and passion for Nepalese cuisine made the whole experience even more special, he truly made us fall in love with it. We’ll definitely be back. 10/10! || Thank you very much Marta, See you again!! || Fantastic food. Fantastic people. Enjoyed the Nepali fries, samosas, chicken curry, and green paneer - every dish, 10/10. Naveen is the man. || Thank you very much Aizhak, See you next time... || The food here is absolutely amazing! Mr. Nabin, the owner, is such a kind and friendly person. He even gave me a discount, which was a really nice surprise. The momos are the best I’ve ever had — soft, juicy, and full of flavor. Everything was 10/10. Highly recommend this place to everyone! || Thank you so much Ravindar, See you again!!
