More on... NOT JUST HIKING (gabifem.es) || The church is wonderful, it brings a lot of peace, the paintings are perfect. || Beautiful church with a unique architectural style! Not very visited, but well worth a trip! || Very beautiful, not to mention that from the entrance of the building there is a wonderful view over Lisbon. It's well worth a visit. || This church is absolutely beautiful. First visit, I loved it. || Beautiful place, beautiful mass, place of peace! || A surprisingly quiet place, just you and the silence. There are absolutely no people around. Beautiful. There's an observation deck nearby. || I really like the water tower-like building behind the church. It is very distinctive and the graffiti is beautiful. || A discreet church on a high point in Lisbon. One of the most beautiful I've ever seen. || Very beautiful church. The woman in the house next door opened the door especially for us and showed us everything. There were no labels, but everything seemed so. A Catholic church, after all. || The church's elevated location offers a panoramic view of almost the entire city of Lisbon. The church's interior, however, reveals its own unique beauty. Beautiful.

A definite must visit for Lisbon for the views alone as well as the history. Exceptional views across all of Lisbon. Some amazing historical walled artefacts. A beautifully curated museum in the centre with exceptional items through all the ages. The ostentation of peacocks is a lovely little bonus. Nice Ice Cream stand in the middle of the copse of trees near the more ancient ruins. The church right outside the gates is also a lovely little bonus || After visiting other castles in Malta, I personally found this one underwhelming. The castle is relatively small compared to others. The view is nice but you can get lookout spots similar to this one for free around Lisbon. The museum is only filled with old pots which I'm personally not a fan of. The archeological site was closed for some reason and a large part of the parking was all closed due to renovations or it being dangerous. So we didn't end up experiencing all of the site. I personally found more value from 15 Euros in other sites.  Another thing I would have preferred to see is written text throughout the castle. I know they went for a more traditional look and tried to provide an audio on your phone to listen to but this restrains you to follow the audios pace which was too slow for me. I like to go on my own pace and skip what I would like to skip.  I will say if you are a history freak it is a nice historic site, but for me personally it was sub-par.  I will say that the peacocks were very nice here but also you can find them free throughout lisban || This was on our must see list while we were in Lisbon as my friend and I both love touring castles. It wasn’t quite what we were expecting as it was very open and had a lot of courtyards and such but the view from the walls was beautiful. They also had peacocks everywhere which was really cool to see. The museum has a lot of ancient pottery and we learned the history of the tiles we’d been seeing everywhere so we enjoyed that. It does take quite a climb to get there but we were not disappointed! || After visiting the Lisbon cathedral, we walked up to the arch entrance of the castle - it’s walkable but be wary of a steep trek from the cathedral. We were able to use our Lisboa Card for free entry, which was a great bonus. The castle grounds offer incredible views across the city and plenty of historic areas to explore. There are loads of great photo opportunities, and the grounds are home to around two dozen peacocks and peahens. I’ve never seen so many in one place before, and they really add to the atmosphere.  The small museum inside is interesting and gives some insight into the history of the castle, including who built it, what it was used for, and a look at some of the pottery and tiles found on site. It’s also well air-conditioned, which makes it a nice break from the heat outside.  Be warned that the toilets are pretty unpleasant and located down some narrow, slightly sketchy stairs. The main castle area itself is mostly empty, with only the walls open to walk along. The views are fantastic from up there, but it’s definitely not ideal if you’re afraid of heights. The walkways are narrow and can get crowded, and there’s only a railing to hold on to.  We left just before sunset, and as we did, the queue to get in had grown a lot. Leaving early worked out well, as we were able to catch the bus back to the Rua with no hassle || I don’t usually like visiting castles and historic spots, but this castle was breathtaking. I highly recommend visiting it. My teenage boys also liked it. We enjoyed the kastana outside the castle. We took the hop on hop off green line to reach there which stopped exactly opposite to the castle. The area around was beautiful. Beautiful old town 💕 || Castelo de São Jorge is a stunning medieval fortress situated on one of Lisbon’s highest hills, providing visitors with magnificent panoramic views of the city, including the Alfama district, the Baixa area, the Tagus River, and the iconic 25 de Abril Bridge.  The castle itself has a rich history, originally serving as a Moorish citadel before becoming a royal palace and later a military stronghold.  Visitors can explore vast ramparts, eleven towers, archaeological sites, and remnants of the former royal palace, all set within beautiful gardens that are home to roaming peacocks, adding a unique and charming touch to the experience.  The castle's grounds feel like a living museum where one can marvel at medieval defensive architecture, walk along ancient walls, and enjoy peaceful spaces shaded by olive trees and dotted with historical artifacts.  Surrounding the castle, the neighborhood of Alfama offers a vibrant yet authentic atmosphere with narrow, winding streets, traditional tiled houses, cozy cafes, and small shops steeped in local culture.  The area is known for its lively yet intimate vibe, enriched by the sounds of Fado music and the daily rhythms of local residents.  Travelers often find themselves enchanted by the blend of history, culture, and scenic beauty, making the approach to the castle a meaningful journey in itself.  The castle’s elevated position allows for stunning sunrise and sunset views across Lisbon, creating memorable photo opportunities and moments of reflection against the backdrop of terracotta rooftops and the sparkling river below.  Visitors are recommended to arrive early to avoid crowds, as the castle tour, including its museum and archaeological areas, can take one to two hours. The pathway includes some steep climbs, but the well-preserved structures and the sweeping city vistas make the effort worthwhile.  There are also small cafes within the castle grounds where visitors can pause and enjoy refreshments while taking in the scenic surroundings.  Overall, Castelo de São Jorge offers a rich, immersive experience of historical, cultural, and natural heritage, making it a must-visit landmark for anyone exploring Lisbon’s fascinating past and vibrant present.  The castle’s majesty, along with the lively charm of its surroundings, creates an unforgettable visit that reflects both the resilience and spirit of Lisbon. || What an awesome experience this was!  Was there on a Tuesday afternoon and the crowds were light.  Very easy to walk around and explore.  (Although be warmed the steps are pretty steep and some have no handrails....careful!  Sights were amazing and there is a QR Code.at.the entrance that gives you a self guided audio your with anlot of history.  Awesome place and highly recommended! || Castelo de São Jorge in Lisbon is worth a visit for the views alone. Sitting on a hill in the Alfama district, it gives you a clear line of sight across the city and the Tagus River. There is something about seeing the red rooftops stretch out below that makes it easy to understand why Lisbon feels so special.  The castle itself is interesting, even if it is not the most polished attraction. Walking along the ramparts and towers, you can sense the layers of history that have shaped this place. Roman, Moorish, and medieval influences are all visible in the walls and fortifications. The layout is straightforward, but exploring the nooks and stairs gives a sense of how people lived and defended the city centuries ago.  One of the unexpected highlights is the peacocks. They wander freely across the grounds and gardens, adding a bit of life and color to the stone and brick. It is a small detail, but it makes the visit feel a little more playful.  If you are in Lisbon, give yourself an hour or two to explore. Wear comfortable shoes because the paths are cobbled, and take your time to enjoy the history, the views, and the peacocks. Castelo de São Jorge is real, atmospheric, and memorable. || Make sure to sign up for the guided tour which can be done at the ticket office, its free and its the only way to visit the archeological ruins. Our guide was knowledgeable and entertaining. The view from the top is stunning! The history of the area is beyond interesting. Highly recommend if visiting Lisbons historical center || This castle is situated on one of the highest hills and offers stunning panoramic view of lisbon. You can walk over the castle and towers which was fun. The place is overall well maintained and worth a visit. The route to get to the castle is walkable but be aware of the steep path. We visited this place during sunset and it was absolutely lovely and highly recommend visiting around sunset time. No advance booking required and we got the ticket upon arrival. || This 11th-century castle offers a journey into the past, with a great archaeological museum and a wonderful walk around the grounds. It has the best panoramic view of Lisbon from above! You must go! || Amazing view, beautiful ruins, well kept, lots of nature, spacious areas. Unfortunately, this is not all. Multiple areas, view points, terraces were closed off, 2 of the 3 toilets didn't work and it looked and smelled disgusting. For 15 euros I'd hope for better but it's whatever.. However, what's not whatever is the behaviour of the staff. At 5:40 they were aggressively shouting at us that the place is closed, get out. They waved in front of our photos. When we said that the place is not in fact closed and we want to enjoy these 15-20 minutes one of them even more aggressively shouted that "you don't argue with me about this". We were following the signs and wanted to go out through the archeological site (where the official exit was according to the signs) as that was in the end but when we got there they sent us back to the entrance (where it said entrance only). They didn't even tell us why we couldn't. The arrogance and ignorance was mind-blowing. We just wanted to enjoy that beautiful historic sight and the view until we could. || It was a good walk from our hotel. Uphill both ways lol The views from the walls provide excellent photo ops. I recommend a jacket during winter as the wind does pick up and chill you right through at times. || Best views of the city. Museum display was excellent although English descriptions require a darker font yo mage them more easily readable. The lighting was frustratingly dim on many of the exhibits, which minimised the enjoyment. Bonus points for the guy at the ticket office who requested proof of age so I could get my Senior discount. Made my day. || Wonderful castle, very well preserved. It's quite big, so there is a lot to explore and the best, the view over the city of Lisbon is just magnificent. Especially the old town, where you can see the architecture. There is a community of peacocks living in the castle, they are very adorable and not afraid of the tourist. It's really worth the visit, to get a panoramic view of the city. Highly recommended. || Incredible views. Key tip, go later in the afternoon so you can be there for sunset, an incredible vantage point and not nearly as busy as some of the other sunset viewing spots around Lisbon.  The actual castle is really cool and the audio guide was done very well too. || A calm and charming place right in the heart of the city. The atmosphere is very peaceful, and the presence of a good-quality restaurant makes the experience even more enjoyable. The architecture is a beautiful mix of different styles, with strong Andalusian influences that give the space a unique character. What makes this place special is that if it’s not recommended to you in advance, you might easily walk past it without noticing. But once you step inside, you realize it’s a hidden gem well worth stopping for and exploring. || Great views of Lisbon! Very neat to explore the castle itself and get Greta pictures across the entire castle.  Overall, very good price for the value you receive! || Very beautiful castle and lots of places to walk around and take photos. They also have peacocks wandering around which is very pretty. Ample places to sit and I saw two washroom locations.  Incredible views of the city. Also has a small museum to look at (~3 rooms)  Audio tours are available to listen to.  In my opinion, well worth the visit! || We were visiting in lower season and I don't believe there were any cruise rshios in the day we went so pre purchased tickets were unnecessary. However in other times of year they may be. There is an audio tour you can do with this site and the views are truly spectacular. Peacocks were everywhere which was unexpected! There is a lot of uneven ground and narrow paths so it would be tricky to do a lot of this if you have mobility issues

It's a huge and beautiful plaza that has been decorated with a Christmas tree and surrounding lights. You can see a beautiful sunset from here too and musicians like to come around and play to entertain your views and videos with sweet melodies! It's a must see in Lisbon and you can also see a gigantic arch and a middle statue in honor of someone important in Portuguese history. || Praça do Comércio considered a historical symbol of political power and manifestation of capitality in Portugal. It's a beautiful place to spend quality time with family, friends & special person. It's quite and welcome people who really wants to enjoy sunset. After the Revolution of 1910 the buildings were painted pink. However, they have recently returned to their original color, yellow. The south side, with its two square towers, is faced to the Tagus. || Lots of fun activities around. We saw street entertainment, vendors and restaurants and even a 360° video booth! Walk down to the water and sit of the steps to enjoy the waves. As long as you don’t feed the birds you’ll enjoy it || History at its best, even when it's busy it is possible just to stand in your own wee world and admire the architecture.  if you have a Lisbon travel card, you can climb the stairs to the top of the monument for fantastic views all for free.  Be sure to visit one or more of the wonderful restaurants round the sides.  Nightime is a completely different experience and one not to be missed. || 🌅 Where the City Opens to the River ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5)  After walking down Rua Augusta on that bright June 2025 afternoon, we finally reached Praça do Comércio — Lisbon’s great stage by the Tagus River. Still with my friend, I remember stepping out from beneath the arch and feeling the city breathe wider, as if every street had been leading to this one golden moment.  The vast square, once home to Portugal’s royal palace before the 1755 earthquake, now stands as a symbol of rebirth. The yellow arcades glow under the sunlight, and the sound of waves blends with the hum of trams. In the middle, King José I’s bronze statue, mounted on his horse Gentil, looks forever toward the river — the same horizon that launched the Age of Discoveries. Standing there, I could almost imagine ships setting sail again.  We rested on the marble steps facing the Tagus, watching ferries and silhouettes cross the glittering water. It was hot — the kind of radiant, reflective heat only Lisbon can produce — but the breeze from the river made everything slow down, peaceful and cinematic.  Practical Notes  Visit near sunset for cooler air and golden light on the arcades.  Bring water; shade is limited.  Perfect spot for wide-angle photos or time-lapse videos.  Cafés under the arcades are pricier but worth it for the view.  Quick Ratings Historical & Cultural Value: 10/10 Atmosphere & River Views: 9.5/10 Accessibility: 9/10 📸 Photo & Video Potential: 10/10 Café & Rest Spots: 8.5/10  📝 If this glimpse of Lisbon resonated with you, hit 👍 and follow me — I share real impressions from Europe’s most curious corners. || Praça do Comércio is one of Lisbon’s most impressive and iconic squares. The wide open space, framed by historic yellow buildings and facing the river, creates a grand and welcoming atmosphere. It’s a beautiful place to walk through, especially in the late afternoon when the light reflects off the water and the arcades.  The square is lively but not overwhelming, with plenty of cafés and easy access to the surrounding streets of Baixa. A must-see landmark that perfectly captures the elegance and scale of Lisbon’s waterfront. || We were in Lisbon for a few days while waiting to join a cruise. We spent a lot of time walking around this area as there is a lot to see here. The plaza is magnificent. Beautiful big arch surrounded by beautiful buildings. Outdoor cafes, statues and lots of tourists all around. A must see if you visit Lisbon. || This is not a destination site but it is worth walking through just for the sheer size of it. It’s also on the water and has one of the Lisboa signs (great for touristy photos!) at the end near the water. You can also see the 25 Abril bridge from here. It was pretty at Christmas with a huge tree. || It’s a nice place, but there are too many touts. First, they will try to sell you sunglasses and then they all move onto other substances. I was bothered here at least five times in an unsolicited way. || Get a leg (or foot!) up and go to the top of the entrance to Lisbon! Beautiful views and we were able to appreciate an aerial view of the beautiful tile on the streets. We also saw the castle we were visiting next! || Praça do Comércio is one of Lisbon’s most open and easygoing places. The square is large, flat, and right next to the river, which makes it feel calm even when there are many people around. The yellow buildings are clean and well maintained, and the Arco da Rua Augusta stands out as the main landmark. It’s a good spot for photos, especially in the late afternoon when the light reflects off the water. There are cafés around the edges, but the square itself is mostly for walking, sitting, or meeting people. It’s not a place where you spend hours doing activities, but it works well as a starting point to explore downtown Lisbon. It’s also convenient, since many trams, buses, and walking routes connect from here. || Definitely a must see for anyone visiting Lisbon. Location is right in the centre close to the river, well maintained and very clean given the amount of tourists that visit here and all round impressive but of Portuguese architecture. Highly recommend. || The Praça do Comércio, or Commerce Square, is a large, historic plaza square. It sits on the Tagus River waterfront and features grand Pombaline architecture, an equestrian statue of King José I, and the majestic Rua Augusta Arch. A landmark of Lisbon, this is a must visit. || So much people waking around. I love the ancient buildings in this place, and environment is so lively. We walked along the road until get to Plaza at evening, very beautiful atmosphere, then went through the huge gate to walking street. || Beautiful and spacious area to explore in Lisbon. The historic architecture and vast open space make it a great spot to stroll and take in the atmosphere. Public transportation and taxis are easily accessible, and the impressive equestrian statue facing the seashore adds a striking touch to the scenery.  Tuk tuks are plentiful and convenient for getting around, but it’s worth negotiating the fare rather than accepting the first price offered. Nearby, you’ll find plenty of restaurants serving delicious meals at fair prices.  A lovely and memorable place to visit! || This is the beautiful please with the largest Christmas tree. It is also near by ocean where you can have a breathtaking view of ocean and waves. There is a small area with a sand that looks like a beach. || Praça do Comércio is one of those places that truly captures the spirit of Lisbon the moment you step into it. This massive, open square sits right by the Tagus River, and there’s something instantly calming about the way the sunlight hits the yellow façades and the arcades that wrap around the plaza.  It’s a spot where you naturally slow down — whether you’re watching the trams roll by, taking in the river breeze, or just enjoying the open space after wandering Lisbon’s narrow streets. The Arco da Rua Augusta frames the city beautifully, and walking through it feels like stepping into the heart of downtown.  There’s always something happening here: people relaxing by the water, street musicians playing, and cafés buzzing with energy. It’s scenic, historic, and surprisingly peaceful for such an iconic landmark. If you want a place that truly feels like Lisbon — bright, welcoming, and full of life — Praça do Comércio is it. || I highly recommend paying a visit to the Praca do Comércio area. It's a great neighbourhood, quite safe and the Christmas tree and Lisbon signs gives character to my photos. || A beautiful public plaza on the river right at the southern edge of the downtown historic district of Lisbon. There are multiple restaurants and bars along the sides of the square, many craftsmen with shopping booths along the sidewalks, bus, train, and trolley stops, and the boat docks for river cruises are close by, too. It is beautiful in the daytime, but be sure to visit here at night, also. It is a very popular place for tourist photos! || ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Where Lisbon flexes its imperial grandeur like an absolute boss 👑  This isn't just a square - it's Lisbon's living room, and what a spectacular one it is! Praça do Comércio (locals call it Terreiro do Paço) is pure architectural theatre on an epic scale. Those imposing yellow arcades stretching endlessly around you, the triumphant Rua Augusta Arch standing guard, and the Tagus River glittering just beyond - it's the kind of place that makes you understand why Portugal once ruled half the world.  The sheer scale is breathtaking, especially when the light hits those baroque facades just right. Perfect for a morning coffee at one of the café terraces or an evening stroll when the crowds thin out. The views across to Almada are stunning, and you're perfectly positioned to explore the rest of Baixa.  Just a heads up: keep your wits about you regarding the persistent street vendors flogging dodgy sunglasses and fake designer gear. A polite "não, obrigado" and keep walking works wonders. Don't let them spoil this magnificent experience!  Absolutely essential Lisbon - pure grandeur! 🏛️✨

But remember it's Lisbon, so be ready to walk uphill. || The best place to smoke a joint and enjoy the sunset 🌅 || I found this viewpoint by lucky and found it quite attractive. Easy access and a small place to have a drink. The day was cloudy but it did not detract from its charm. || Simple neighborhood viewpoint. Enjoy the sunset with the locals. Chairs and benches available as well as a bar serving drinks and snacks. || Absolutely beautiful view! The sunset here is amazing! Very clean and there is a lovely little cafe at your disposal. There is also a little shop not far from this view point. People having the best time! Take some wine, cheese and bread and enjoy the view, or maybe go with some friends and some beer and enjoy the ambiance and your friends company. :) || Nice view, you can get there by Bike or scooter. It's behind the secondary school. There is a free water station || Nice viewpoint/ place to checkt out if you are staying nearby. I went there on a friday evening to check out the view with two friends I made at my hostel nearby and we were surprised by the amount of people being there. The little path up there can be overlooked so definitely check your maps when you try to get there. As I said, there were a lot of people just enjoying the warmer days, drinking and just chatting with friends or other people. There was also a DJ playing some music and a few people dancing. It definitely seems more like a local spot, a place to meet up with your friends on the weekends. Up there, there is also a little café/ kiosk with some food and drinks. The place is quite different to the other places/ miradouros in Lisbon. The spot itself, the people and the atmosphere there reminded me a lot of Berlin. Once up, the view is very nice and there are mainly locals chatting, walking their dogs or playing music. It has a very chill vibe.  Everyone was asked to leave around 8 by the security guard, not sure why as we don't speak Portuguese. || came for a walk on Wednesday around Penha de França area in the afternoon on the 4th week of January. I like that the kiosk have sun lounge chairs to relax on! || Prettiest viewpoint in Lisbon ❤️ || Lovely view across the city you can see the planes coming in and it’s a lovely little coffee shop there as well pity about the graffiti || Good view, not crowded. Perfect place for a beer and a little snack at the kiosk up there. || This Viewpoint was a little bit far away there's no much to see in the area you can have a drink here but there is other viewpoints that are more beautiful however those are very crowded if you make it there early in the morning you should be fine by midday all of them have tourists around it.

reviews_content: Does not worth at the trip or paying the 18 euros. The boat has limited space at the top, and if you happen to get a seat on the right side, you’ll enjoy the view on both rides. The boat goes along one side of Lisbon and comes back from the other. The music that accompanies the trip really puts your nerves on edge, as it doesn’t match the spirit or context of the tour, with a lot of noise and unclear sound. The audio guide, which requires downloading an app, gives only brief explanations of a few monuments, so if you don’t have it, you’ll need to guess or read about them online. In addition, one of the passengers was too tipsy, standing up disturbing around and none of the crew members intervened. The view of Lisbon at the begginning the plaza is beautiful — you can enjoy at the start the beauty of the buildings and their colors. But on the way back, the view is extremely poor as it’s from the other side. Basically, you can do better during the 1h30 than being stuck on the boat and spending at least 20 minutes just to get on. || We got offered a sunset cruise tour and can’t recommend at all. The residents of the residential units located on Rua do Paraíso, Lisbon, hereby notify you of the following:  I. Facts It has been ascertained that this establishment, or a person functionally linked to it, is in possession of a key that allows access to the common door of buildings located on Rua do Paraíso;  The aforementioned door provides access to permanently inhabited private residences;  This key has been given to third parties, namely guests of units operated under the Local Accommodation regime, following instructions given by the respective operators;  The safekeeping and delivery of the aforementioned key occurs without the knowledge or authorization of the residents of the residential units, directly affecting their safety and tranquility.  II. Legal Framework According to Article 1305 of the Civil Code, the right of ownership grants its holder the full and exclusive enjoyment of the property, and interference by third parties without consent is not permitted; Article 1420 of the Civil Code establishes that the common parts of a building under a horizontal property regime belong to all the condominium owners and cannot be used exclusively or instrumentalized for commercial purposes without authorization; Article 1422, paragraph 2, subparagraphs a) and d), of the Civil Code expressly prohibits acts that prejudice the safety, use or tranquility of the other condominium owners, as well as the use of the common parts for purposes other than their intended use; The safekeeping and delivery of a key that allows access to a private residence, without the authorization of the respective occupants, constitutes an illegitimate interference in the legal sphere of third parties, liable to give rise to civil liability for an unlawful act, under the terms of Article 483 of the Civil Code;  The conscious persistence of the conduct, after formal communication of its unlawfulness, may also constitute abuse of rights, under the terms of Article 334 of the Civil Code.  III. Notification and requirements In these terms, you are hereby notified to: a) Immediately cease any form of safekeeping, custody, delivery or intermediation of keys relating to the buildings located on Rua do Paraíso; b) Proceed with the immediate return of the aforementioned key to its rightful holders; c) Refrain, in the future, from any intervention, direct or indirect, in the control of access to the aforementioned buildings. The cactus garden offers exactly what you expect and more. There are wild plants and of course 🌵🌵 but there are also free running chicken and even peacocks with beautiful feathers. Definitely worth a visit if you like wild nature and peace just around the corner. || Very calm space - the perfect get away from the busy touristy areas. Some visitors are sunbathing on the grass. The cactus garden impressed me with the size of the cactuses - some of them were twice my height. There are many happy birds but mostly roosters, crowing non-stop. It’s probably a way to prove their masculinity in front of the chicks… actually I don’t know - it’s not my business :) There are several neglected structures that are still quite beautiful. || What a beautiful, interesting little park! Off the beaten track, loads of ducks, geese, chickens, and pea-fowl. The cactus garden area was where the chickens were plotting to take over the world lol. So glad we happened upon it. || The park could be beautiful as I believe once was, but today it is very poorly maintained with destroyed paths, overgrown bushes and sad abandoned buildings. It probably wouldn't even be expensive to restore it, so I'm confused how they could let this happen. || A nice park to have a picnic. The few features are the peacocks and the geese’s. And the Dragoeiro plant at the south entrance. I read that it’s rare and only a few hundreds left. The park did have a lot of variations of flora, maybe it’s winter time. Oh.. the white roosters seems to monopolised the north entrance. They are cute and naturally roaming. Just an easy part to walk. Nearby is Jardim Estrella which is smaller but probably more family friendly. You could see my other  review there. || This park is extremely underrated!! LOOK AT ALL THESE CHICKENS!!! I was so surprised and tickled to walk through….chickens, cats, many differently types of cactus (and mature too), and a fantastic view of 25 of April Bridge!!! If I lived here I would come often to the park. Peaceful and a jungle of endless exploration. || This a beautiful park that is located off the beaten path. It is quite hilly but there is plenty of shade. The main reason to go is to see all the species of native birds. I saw chickens, geese, pigeons, and peacocks. Just make sure to not step in the animal dung! || We were lucky to find this place. It's very authentic and very beautiful in terms of authentic landscape design. Just have a look at my photos. We could see many photographers that make photo sessions there. There are many white chickens, colorful peacocks, ducks, gooses, etc. There is big walking area and also some field where you can take sun bath or sit at the tables and have a picknick. || There's a hidden gem in the park - a collection of one of the oldest cacti on the planet. It's a free admission to the park except for the restroom, you'll have to pay for adults. There's a water fountain in the park, so you can fill your bottle with it. We visited during Easter holiday, and it was very nice to see that someone was sweet and thoughtful to "hide" some candies in trees and bushes for kids. || I love this garden: feels so wild with all the wonderful animals! Peacocks, chickens, cats, geese and more.  Highly recommend the cactus garden 🌵 the only downside for me is there’s no like little place for refreshments or drinks (I couldn’t find a water tap either). So come prepared!!! || It's the perfect spot for a picnic, to enjoy a sunny day, or simply for a walk. The park offers a calm setting for outdoor activities and relaxation. || Beautiful calm park with a nice cactus garden, free chicken and peacocks. Very nice. || A peaceful park in Lisbon with quiet paths winding around ponds and towering cacti, plus the occasional rooster to hear or peacock to spot. Perfect for a lunchtime break or a change of scenery. It offers ancient trees and impressive views of the Ponte 25 de Abril. A must-see hidden gem.

A rare find in Lisbon it seems, a quiet shaded park. It had picnic benches with tables, benches in the shade, grass to lie on, a cafe and is very peaceful.  Having said that it does feel like it needs some attention as much of it is run down and the prevailing smell of urine is not so appealing with your lunch || While the view of Lisbon from here is undeniably beautiful, the park itself has sadly declined. It’s often not clean and no longer feels safe, especially after the evening. The presence of homeless people can be unsettling. It's best to visit during the day for the vista and avoid it after dark. No nearby toilets. || Jardim da Cerca da Graça is a hidden gem with an absolutely fabulous view. It’s pretty simple to get there by bus, but just a heads-up, it does involve walking a fair bit downhill after you get off. Still, totally worth it. || It’s the perfect spot to relax, enjoy a picnic, or simply take in the lovely views over Lisbon. The atmosphere is calm, with plenty of shade, open green spaces, and a small café to grab a drink. A wonderful place to unwind and escape the city’s busy streets for a while. || Having just arrived in Lisbon, we dropped off our bags and got our hike on. We ended up at this great park to relax in, and one of the few that had a playground. We thoroughly enjoyed listening to the dogs playing in the wide-open green space above the playground, one even sounded like a turkey gobbling along. || Very cute little park with stunning views. There is a wee cafe/bar in it with a toilet, a children’s play area and plenty of green space to lie down and relax. Also has amazing views || It’s nice to have a park, but the many many dogs leave behind a lot of dog poop. Even if picked up, this makes your clothes and blanket dirty, and I mean really dirty. Even worse, millions of flies. || Nice little park - an oasis in Graca. There’s a big grassy bit where dogs run around. Be careful of the dog poo though! There’s also a little kiosk for drinks and snacks too || One of the best parks in Lisbon. The view is great, the atmosphere is chill and cool. There’s always a lot of cute dogs running around. You can also get a coffee at the small roundy there :) || A bit abandoned park with full of ugly graffitis. City view is nice but we were really disappointed about no way out anywhere except the entrance (don't believe google maps, there is no direct "green" trail). || Nice park. There is open space for doing some sporty activities. I also enjoyed staircase with street art near the park. One of my favorite spots in Lisbon || The day I passed through this park it was all quiet. Nice view all the same. || This park is some what hidden. Most people come here to sun bath, read a book, smoke weed, you play with there dog. Lots of trees around to stay cool. || I got to this park kind of by accident, but it became one of my favorite spots in Lisboa. Surrounded by buildings and unfolding paths, it's a dreamy spatial experience. The great view to the castle doesn't hurt. Ideal for a picnic, beers with friends, play ball, walk the dog, even a date. || It’s a gorgeous place with so much potential. Lots squatters, make sure to watch your children. Suggest the português government gives them a better home! || This guy and his two dogs have lived in the dog park for 4 months straight with all their nasty equipment spread out like they own the place. What is wrong with this city? || DO NOT BRING CHILDREN HERE. While the space is beautiful, unfortunately it’s now full of homeless people and off leash dogs, including in the children’s play equipment. Avoid. || A nice relaxing park where you can enjoy, rest, read, have a picnic or spend time with you friends. Seems to be a dog friendly place 🐕. … || i did not mean to come here, my friend must have sent the wrong location💔💔 … || The garden was well designed for kids and dogs. But unfortunately it has not been maintained and it's now very dangerous for both kids and dogs. People with drug addiction have taken over the dog and kid park and there is litter, ash, and even syringes left about. Whoever is responsible for maintaining the park, you need to step up. Clean this park up and properly maintain it. Get the addicts to move elsewhere. I can't believe anyone would treat a kids playground this way. It's very sad. || Very nice place to walk, nice environment, very much famous & amazing area in night time👌here have lots of resturents for tourists👌👌just wow wow👍 … || Cozy park. Perfect place to spend time with your dog or friends. Some people smoke weed there. || Nice little park with view to the Graca church. Ther is a small quiosque where you can have a Snack and drink and rest. || Great garden with super views and plenty of play space for little ones. Highly recommended the wall up the hill through the graffiti lined staircase too || This place was a dreamy hideaway and worth every step up to it, had a ice cold beer, picked some wild rosemary and limes that had fallen off the trees. Such stunning views || Nice spot to take a quick rest after climbing all those hills in Lisbon😂 … || I love this park, it has such a good vibe, and if you are a dog lover this is certainly the place to go! || A shame.  A beautiful park in medieval Lisbon, an incredible green space in an incredibile space, the REALM of homeless people sleeping in children's games and dogs free to fight and leave excrement and urine everywhere.  Please RESPECT Lisbon! || One of the dirtiest park I have ever visited. || Best spot to see a sunset. It doesn’t get any better than this overlook.

On September 7, I visited Jardim Amália Rodrigues and witnessed a partial blood moon eclipse under a cloudy sky. The park, with its wide open spaces and elevated views, was a perfect place to capture the moment in photos. Even with the clouds, the experience was memorable and unique. || Lovely park and bar with a pool to cool your feet after a long day walking..cycling and generally getting about. The drink prices are reasonable. Definitely call in here if your in Lisbon. It's beautiful. || It is a delightful urban oasis at the northern edge of Parque Eduardo VII. Whether you’re after a peaceful retreat, a picturesque spot for photos, or simply want to enjoy sweeping views of Lisbon, this hidden gem is definitely worth a visit. || Somehow hidden from turistic path, a small part of the parc is dedicated to famous singer. || Designed by Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles and opened in 1996, the garden was named in 2000 in tribute to Amália Rodrigues, Portugal’s legendary fado singer. The garden features a variety of trees and plants, with quiet walking paths and benches that make it ideal for rest, reflection, or a peaceful stroll. || Lovely setting, but the garden is boring and very disappointing. Fans of Amalia Rodrigues must be very disappointed. Like the rest of the area, very poorly maintained and pedestrian access is dreadful. A missed opportunity, big time. || Great views and perfect location to see sunset over Lisbon with some live music in the background || Park with a great view of central Lisbon 💚 The shade of the trees makes for a great place to sit down and relax a bit. The sun beats down quite mercilessly at around midday. The many benches are a welcome addition for weary travelers. … || What a beautiful park. With a nice a cosy bar to hang out and have a drink while enjoying the fresh atmosphere. || This little garden looked like part of the Parque Eduardo VII. The statue at the entrance was interesting. || Good place to relax and meditation... Also your dog will be more than happy to play into the little lake... A coffee on the side also will be great || Amazing views, beautiful gardens, and a perfect place to read a book. || Not to much illumination by night but it’s a cute place || Everywhere I go in the world I always look for a sculptor from the maestro Botero 🫀🫶.  So glad I saw that they have a piece of his in Lisboa.  🇨🇴🇨🇴🫶🫶 … || I love it. You can find fresh corners to cool off in summer while enjoying a green calm environment. A nice pond with fish, turtles and beautiful lilies. Visit it if you are in the area. || Beautiful green space and a lovely photo opportunity || Chilled park that catches the sun perfectly and usually there is a bit of a breeze and if that's not the case you may find some shade from the nearby trees. Close proximity to cafe for some drinks or a nearby lidl that also sells cold drinks. Sunset can be pretty incredible from this place as well if you're lucky || This was very pretty. Worth seeing if you're in the area. My family, though, was under the mistaken impression that this was a fountain that young children could frolic in. To be clear, once we realized it wasn't, we made another plan. … || A great place to stop for a drink, a bite or both. The round, shallow pool is perfect for dogs to play in. || Beautiful clean park. Really loved it. People were jogging, exercising, walking. Very beautiful. || The garden was a kaleidoscope of colors and scents, a veritable paradise where the vibrant blooms and lush foliage were in perfect harmony with the gentle trickle of the fountain and the sweet melody of the birdsong. || Probably my favorite park in Lisbon! Full of nature and little cafes! Great place to do some sports or chill ! || One of my  favourite spots in Lisbon, great views, really quiet and dog-friendly. || Very nice park lovely walk there is a casual  cafe and couple of fancy resturants || Beautiful garden with lots space for kids to play nice view.. || Lovely area in the city to relax and connect with nature. || It's worth the hike up with a lovley cafe on top || Beautiful greenery all over the place. A nice spot to relax in a sunny day. || Great green space. Nice place to chill away from the crowds.

A beautiful park where you can spend a few hours. It has a path that goes around it and which I recommend to walk. Beautiful trees and ponds ideal for a pause after a busy day. There's a café which is usually busy and a table is hard to find. On Sundays there's a small marketplace and so you can encounter locals mixed up with tourists. Just across the street you'll find the admirable Basílica da Estrela which is worth the visit. || I met some friends at Jardim da Estrela and it was a very nice experience. The park has lots of trees and open space, so it felt calm and relaxing. We enjoyed walking and sitting by the small lake together. || This is a gorgeous park — perfect for people-watching or for families with kids who just want to escape the hustle and bustle of Lisbon. It’s a peaceful spot to unwind and enjoy a slower pace in the middle of the city, and it even has restrooms (although I wouldn't call them clean but they were free), which is always a plus when exploring! || This place is heaven! One of the most beautiful parks I've seen by far. It's full of nature and also some animals, mostly birds. The place is perfect for a weekend picnic, a chilly eventing, yoga, hangouts and more. Thank you Lisbon for this amazing green gem! || Stunning park in the heart of Lisbon. Absolutely stunning. Full of beautiful plants and flowers, ponds and statues. Benches everywhere and the wonderful Banana Cafe inside which sells burgers and sandwiches, drinks and other refreshments where you can dine alfresco || I recently spent a peaceful afternoon at Jardim da Estrela in Lisbon, and it quickly became one of my favorite spots in the city. Located directly across from the grand Basílica da Estrela, this romantic-style park was inaugurated in 1852 and offers a refreshing blend of history, nature, and community life. The park spans 4.6 hectares and features winding paths shaded by exotic trees like jacarandas and ginkgoes, as well as beautifully maintained flower beds and small lakes with ducks and turtles. One of the standout features is the wrought-iron bandstand, originally built in 1884 and relocated here in 1936, which adds a touch of old-world charm. Families and locals gather here, especially on weekends, to enjoy the playgrounds, picnic areas, and the café with outdoor seating that serves light meals and drinks. The park is free to enter and open daily from 7 am to midnight, making it an accessible and welcoming space for everyone. Whether you're looking to relax, take a leisurely stroll, or immerse yourself in a bit of Lisbon's history, Jardim da Estrela offers a serene and delightful escape from the city's hustle and bustle. || I have a 5 year old and a 2 year old. This is hands down my favorite park to take them to in Lisbon. Great playground. Lots of space to run. A cute little library with little tables the kids can draw and color at. Birds walking about. Cafes for a quick coffee or juice. Plus it’s super safe because it’s all gated. || Definitely one of the most loveliest gardens in Lisbon, if you come here for a few days, I would strongly recommend to see this place. Very cool for pet owners and children hence the park has playgrounds and a huge space  for dogs to enjoy. Also, it’s a very good place just to meet and chill or enjoy your day in serenity. || A beautiful park with ancient trees. Ideal for sitting in peace. || The garden is truly magnificent. For the past several months, we have spent an hour here every afternoon, strolling and unwinding. The vibrant colors of the flowers, the soothing rustle of the leaves, and the gentle warmth of the sun create an atmosphere of pure serenity. || 🌿 A Peaceful Oasis in the Middle of Lisbon ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5) We stumbled upon Jardim da Estrela on a warm afternoon, and it turned out to be one of the most peaceful and refreshing places we visited in Lisbon. It’s more than just a public park — it feels like a little urban sanctuary. The garden is beautifully maintained, filled with exotic plants, huge trees offering generous shade, and winding paths that invite you to slow down. What really stood out for me was the birdsong — there were so many birds, and their constant, melodic chirping made the whole place feel like a live sound bath. It’s incredibly soothing. If you have the time, don’t just walk through. Find a quiet corner, sit down, breathe, and maybe even meditate. This place is perfect for that. It’s not just visually calming, it actually sounds calming too. There are also benches, fountains, a lovely gazebo, and a charming little café nearby if you want to sit and sip something while watching the world go by. Families, joggers, solo readers, and locals chatting on benches all seem to coexist naturally here. It has a very authentic Lisbon energy — not overly touristy, just real life unfolding in a gorgeous setting.  Quick Ratings: Atmosphere: 10/10 Birdsong & Nature Vibe: 10/10 Relaxation Potential: 11/10 Accessibility: 10/10 Instagram View: 8.5/10 Highly recommend making time for it — especially if you’re feeling overstimulated by the city. It’s the kind of place that quietly resets your mood.  If this helped, I’d love a 👍 — and don’t forget to breathe deeply when you visit. 🌿✨ || Beautiful park with many interesting plants in it. Great for spending a few calm moments during sightseeing or for lunch break || Beautiful park with a wide variety of trees and different areas for either working out or doing a picnic, reading and relaxing. Is rather small for a jog yet early mornings or later in the evenings is really peaceful and perfect for a walk. || Probably the best part of Lisbon. Quiet, peaceful, and with a lovely café that has plenty of tables where you can sit, have a bite, and rest. Thankfully, the usual loud and disrespectful tourists haven’t discovered this spot yet (and I hope my review won’t attract them, lol). Surrounded by lots of greenery, it’s such a beautiful, relaxing park — right across from the basilica. Love it! || Im so happy I found this place! Beautiful trees, very dog and children friendly. Banana cafe serves great coffee and pastel da nata ❤️ || I feel so blessed and lucky to be a short walk from this beautiful oasis. The care and thoughtfulness the Portuguese put into public spaces with a care for community is beautiful to experience. || 2€ Banana Bread under quiet Palmtrees in the middle of a bustling Metropolis, what more can one wish for? Fantastic, quiet place to have a beer, run or just have a chat near the pond. Especially beautiful at night! || Lovely park, plenty of benches dotted around to sit and enjoy the greenery and tranquility.  2 cafes with good selection of food and drinks. || I must admit that it is a very very nice park. I liked a tree in particular, they have a liberty-style gazebo, toilets and a couple of cafè, a small artificial lake with ducks, an exhibition building and statues scattered here and there. It is right in front of Estrela cathedral. || A beautiful and well maintained garden. This was built in 1852 as first public park of Lisbon. It has many old and beautiful trees. Worth spending some time and walking when you are free. || A beautiful park in the heart of Lisbon which has a lovely cafe at its southern entrance. Just across the road com the southern entrance is a beautiful church with dome. If you are able to spend 4 euros and climb a narrow staircase with 108 stairs of marble you get a marvellous view of the city of Lisbon || It's a little like walking in a subtropical environment that wraps itself around you and says welcome, stay and just be, while I shade you. There is a mother tree here and you will know it when it finds you. It give beautiful calming energy from its aerial roots and gives a beautiful rustling sound as the breeze kisses its leaves. || A very pretty little city park in a central location in Lisbon. There is a pond, play area and cafe. You can see peacocks and other exotic birds within the park. There are palm trees and other plants and this is a quiet place to relax from the bustle of Lisbon. || Most beautiful garden. Such a magical place! Every time I visit I feel grateful for the experience.  Super cheap for such an amazing time you can get there || A lovely park, very chill, a lovely place to unwind and read a book. A very steep walk to get there but that's to be expected, nice lunch spots around too. There was nice acoustic live music too. || Visiting Portugal and was in the area so we decided to stop by for a walk.  What a hidden gem. Must visit for a laid-back walk. You get to see a beautiful garden and some birds.  The security guard at the front (middle aged man, didn't get his name) was a very pleasant individual. I would visit again just for him. He didn't speak much English but tried his very best to explain everything to us. || It looks nice on the surface, but it’s VERY badly kept (burned lawns, broken glass, dog feces and cigarette buds) literally everywhere. The layout is great, but it is really run down, and good luck finding any table at any of the very mediocre cafes in the park that wouldn’t be engulfed in cigarette smoke. Pro tip: visit after 6pm on weekdays or else be prepared to not only hear an approaching overhead passenger jet every minute or so, but also incredibly intrusive construction work from the (many) huge neighboring building projects that seemingly never get finished and are dragging on since years…  As a sidenote, the public restrooms close to the entrance are appalling; dirty, smelly, not exactly wheelchair accessible and sketchy at night.  Once the first excitement for Lisbon‘s beauty has worn off, this park among many others revels itself to the visitor as a sad example of the state of things in Lisbon. Most invested money seems to go exclusively to gentrification related activities like high (over) priced luxury apartments, and international branded boring stores, and not into much improvement or upkeep of public facilities. || One of the most beautiful gardens in Lisbon. An excellent place to rest and every month you'll find new blossom || Beautiful spacious garden with lots of clean benches you can rest or have a picnic, or just read a book. It’s also a great place to people and dog watch. Lots of interesting dogs walk passed us. The trees are huge and stunning and there are stone sculptures around too. || So soothing place in Lisbon to sit and relax in lush green surrounding. Its facing iconic landmark church. The setup of garden is beautiful with amount of seating. It's pets friendly place. There is a small pond. I saw multiple people doing yoga and training which also add life to this place

place_name: Garden of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation
reviews_content: Such a lovely garden full of paths and little bridges and loads of seating in the shade and great fun to explore and some statues too and we saw a heron and lots of ducks.  The amphitheatre was a real surprise too || Beautiful garden with long bamboo passage ways, a pond with lots of cute ducks, a small area to eat ice cream or coffee and a large area great for dogs. This is a great place to go on a walk with friends or go on a study session. Everything is full of vegetation and butterflies. Like an actual 'secret garden'. If you like fantasy books this is your place to go because it looks like a place in a fairytale. I cannot recommend this garden enough, especially for outdoor lovers. My description doesn't give this place enough justice. || This place is part of a foundation started by Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil tycoon and art lover. You can really feel his belief that “art is for everyone, and beauty means more when it’s shared.”  Right in the middle of the city, there’s this peaceful garden with tall trees, calm ponds, and quiet paths. I could take my time and enjoy the art without any rush. The way nature and art come together here left such a strong impression. || A very lovely garden, located in the center of the city. It’s super convenient to visit either by metro or different bus networks. Here, it’s more like a combination of different gardens, so there are lots of options to enjoy the sun, green, and overall atmosphere. Totally recommended to visit, including the museum inside. || Gorgeous space for all to enjoy for free - lots of areas to picnic, hang with friends, for kids to run around or bike, easy for strollers to get around. There are also two cafes and an ice cream shop - you can spend a whole day enjoying this beautifully maintained space. There must be a mighty team of gardeners tending to all the plants! What a valuable space for residents and visitors alike in this otherwise very densely developed city. || Gulbenkian always had beautiful gardens, around the museums buildings. Landscaping as Portuguese know how ! Now that the renovation of the modern museum is achieved, there is a new setting of this side of the gardens to discover, mix of Japanese zen design, existing garden style and a monumental, yet perfectly integrated awning. Inspiring place where to wander, with cafe and sometimes outdoor activities at the amphitheatre. Just mind the rush hours and some week-end can be crowded, as this place is since long praized by Portuguese and tourists ! || My primary objective was to visit the museum; however, due to renovations, the collection had been relocated.  I was disappointed by the limited number of items, particularly paintings, compared to my expectations. Nonetheless, the collection was aesthetically pleasing and unique.  The garden, however, was unappealing.  Perhaps I mistakenly visited the incorrect park, as signage was inadequate, requiring extensive navigation to locate the proper entrance. || Big enough to wander around. The noise of the city suddenly stops and everything becomes cooler. Part of it is like a jungle. Lots of people either solo or couples and a lot of families with small children. It is a really special place || Designed in the 1960s by Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles and António Viana Barreto, the garden is a beautifully landscaped urban oasis in the heart of Lisbon. The space features a harmonious blend of lakes, streams, terraced lawns, and forested paths—creating a tranquil environment for relaxation and reflection. The garden connects seamlessly with the main Gulbenkian Foundation building and museum, allowing visitors to experience art, architecture, and nature in one integrated setting. || Quiet, cozy park perfect for rest, private conversation with a friend or relaxation! || Best place to hide when it is very hot. There are lots of nice shaded banks to sit and rest under the trees. || Lovely place to escape the bustle of Lisbon for some hours, still in the middle of the city. Grab a picnic towel, a book and sunscreen and lay down for the afternoon. The grass field in the garden is lovely to get some sun light. Even in winter. || A really nice place to wander around, there's lots of corners tucked away if you want to sit by yourself or have a conversation. And they have ducks! || Well-known park in Lisbon where people go to just hang-out, relax, create, work and have a love/get out of here relationship with all the ducks! The museum offers a lot of commodities as well and many times have free entry events :) || So relaxing to walk the grounds of the garden. There are shady as well as sunny areas depending on what you prefer and a cafe for your meals. The ducks and the water areas make it even more attractive. Unfortunately a large part of the grounds are under renovation, so we couldn’t walk there. Still, the air is crisp and the garden is well maintained for visitors. || One of the most gorgeous public gardens I've been to with stunning art, landscaping, plants and wildlife. They are doing extensive renovation in a section of it so it's blocked off (and will be incredible once done) but there's still plenty of areas to wander on paths, sit on benches, grab something at cafe and sit outside and enjoy the birds. I brought my camera and had so much fun capturing images of the Spring babies. Truly a remarkable place for all to enjoy. || A perl in the city of Lisbon. Strongly suggested if you have any minimal appreciation for plants and greenery. They have three great greenhouses with a wide variety of plants from all-over the planet. It also looks like a sustainable place to support with a visit. Entrance tickets are cheap and discounts are available. || Beautiful place to go with time on a sunny day to enjoy yourself and/or friends. Lot's of benches to sit or grass to lay down if you want. Different areas to see and walk to. I really loved even though it was drizzling when I went there. I will come back tho. || My favorite park in Lisbon — full of artwork, exotic plants, winding paths, and little ponds. Despite all that, there’s still plenty of open space to sit or lie down and relax. My 10-year-old son loved it, too. || Beautiful garden at the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum. It is open free of charge. On sunny days, it is quite busy with locals enjoying their time off, yet it's still pleasant, as people respect each other's space. Also, there are several places where you can get a beverage. In the park are sculptures and plants like bridalwreath spirea, Japanese camellia, Rubber tree, Intermediate periwinkle, Common boxwood, Portuguese cherry laurel, and many others. You'll find many benches to sit and enjoy the day. Of course, it is perfect in combination with a visit to the museum of the same name.

Jardim da Parada in Campo de Ourique is one of those rare places in Lisbon that feels genuinely local—quiet, shaded, and full of character. The garden is beautifully maintained, surrounded by big, old trees like sequoias and plane trees, with a small pond in the center where ducks and turtles paddle around peacefully. There’s a traditional bandstand, a nice playground for kids, and a charming little kiosk café that serves good coffee, light meals, and has plenty of outdoor seating under the trees. The vibe is calm and neighborly. People of all ages hang out here—seniors playing cards or reading, parents with strollers, kids running around, people walking their dogs, and others just sitting quietly enjoying the shade. One lovely touch is the old red phone booth that’s been turned into a tiny free library. It’s things like this that make the park feel alive and loved. The space isn’t huge, but it’s got everything it needs. Flower beds are always fresh, paths are clean, and there are benches everywhere. There are also two important statues tucked inside the garden—Maria da Fonte and Professor Ferreira de Macedo—which give it a bit of historical personality. But what really stood out this time was the buzz around the new underground development being planned. The city has announced a project to build a large underground parking garage beneath the garden. While I understand the need to ease traffic and create more parking in Campo de Ourique, I can’t help but feel concerned about the long-term impact this might have on such a delicate green space. There’s a real fear among locals that the construction will disturb the ecosystem of the garden—the roots of these beautiful old trees, the peace and quiet, and possibly the safety of the pond and wildlife. Right now, the garden feels timeless and balanced, and people are naturally worried that digging beneath it could change that. It’s a bit of a crossroads moment for Jardim da Parada. As it stands today, it’s one of the most welcoming and peaceful little parks in the city—loved by the neighborhood and full of everyday life. I hope that whatever happens with the development plans, the soul of the garden is preserved. If you're in Lisbon and want to experience a bit of calm, community, and natural charm, this place is well worth a visit. And if you’re a local—keep an eye on what’s planned beneath your feet. || Jardim da Parada is a compact, well-kept square that does the fundamentals right: plenty of shade, ample benches, smooth paths, a small playground, and a kiosk for quick coffee.
