The restaurant have an outside space for enjoy and smokers, And inside is very friendly  in general recommended and pleas be aware to have to wait on the line, because they area always many people waiting, but in general I say 30m. || The 4 Fingers hotdog is amazing! This is such a gem in Lisbon. The fries and Crispy hotdog ar good too. || Frankie's is a must visit! They offer an assortment of hotdogs (chili dog, cheddar dog, with onion rings, pizza dog, ...) and side dishes. For the hotdog you can choose you type of meat which is nice. As a side dish I would definitely recommend the batatas fritas Frankie, which are thin French fries with pieces of bacon and melted cheese. The daily dessert is great as well.  Frankie's is a very cheap place. I had 2 drinks, a hotdog with side dish and dessert for €11! The portions were perfect for me.  All combined, it makes for a popular place which gets very busy after 7PM. They don't do reservations, so be there early or you'll be in a long line.  UPDATE: we came back today at noon, and tried some other hot dogs. Service was again very friendly. It's really mist visit! || Good quality and tasty food, great presentation and environment, great price! Everything’s good about this place! Fast service even in rush hours. || Nice hot-dog restaurant around the University Campus. || The first place we visited on our trip to Lisboa. The food was AMAZINGLY TASTY. Huge hot dogs with a lot of ingredients, everything home-made.  It's a shame we do not have this kind of "restaurant" in Madrid. I would totally repeat.  10/10 Best hot dog I've ever eaten.

Very good taste, soft and delicious pizza. I love it. || Went here after tile museum. Amazing doner sandwiches and cute little shop. We ate outside with perfect weather and afternoon coffees. 5 of us ordered and all had food in 10 mins. || This is rare find where you least would expect it. Extraordinary food quality, first class service like you'd expect at a fine restaurant and great atmosphere. Friendly, helpful staff. || Thank you so much for your review. Your opinion is our inspiration. We always feel better when our guests enjoy the food. || Unfortunately I was served a raw beef burger here. I cut open the burger and the beef patty was basically only brown out the outside and fully raw in the middle. When I showed them they confirmed it was raw and made me another one.  The second burger was fully cooked and tasted great. If you’re a tourist in Lisbon and happen to be near the tile museum I would recommend this place for a cheap and delicious meal. Combos are all around €5. || Thank you, Yasmine, for your opinion. We are sorry for the first burger.It was unintentional. The second one is our usual making process.  Hope we will follow the usual method for other clients. Thank you. || Good food 😋. Nice service and behaviour. I recommended you. ☺️ || This is a very good restaurant, I often eat here, the taste and service of their food is simply amazing. || Really, the burgers and fries was very good ,friendly staff, and good service ,affordable price, highly recommended for everyone. || Famintos is a casual restaurant with a 4.8-star rating on Google Maps. It is open for lunch and dinner, and offers takeout, delivery, and dine-in options. The restaurant has a relaxed atmosphere and is good for children. It also has paid parking and free street parking available. || The food was very good. Specially the pizza was so good and tasty 😋 || Thank you for your feedback.  Sincerely, Famintos || The food is very good || Food was very delicious and good servis good place to eat and also good environment. || Good burger must come to eat || Good food burger best || Good food and supper cheep price || Wow so beautiful  place and wonderful menu,i like it pizza your shop,thanks for everything || Very good time spend here and enjoyed my meal.  They are very good services. || Nice restaurant,so beautiful Pizza, i like it || Good food , Good service,Good Atmosphere

EXCELLENT samosas. Tastes home made. Friendly service. Highly recommended. || The spicy chatpate pani puri is so delicious, everyone please come and try it once, thank you 😊❤️❤️❤️❤️ || Good chat. Value for money. Quick bite. || Wow it was really good food . Thankyou for the testy panipuri. || Love this place and food || Wow wow wow Pani puri momo chat pate kati mitho Samosa dherai mitho ♥️♥️♥️ thank you so much rossio cafe and momo house lai🙏

One of the nicest, clean, spacious outlets of McD I have seen. Food ordering was quick with the touch screens. Food came nice and freshly made. Toilets are clean. Entry with code on the till slip. It is at the junction of metro and bus routes. The serving staff seemed a bit unfriendly/ bored but I don't know if they were starting or ending a shift... || Still one of the best McDonalds I have been in worldwide. Very fast service.  Sometimes the staff seems little confused, no wonder with that pressure. Only disadvantage was the salad within the menu, is was already kind of rotten n smelled. Maybe left over from 3 days before. Clean place, good for longer stay. || Food and service is fine here, but this has to be the most messy McDonald’s I’ve ever been. I’ve been there on two separate evenings this week and it has trash everywhere on the tables and coming out of the bins. || I rarely eat fast food. When traveling we like to try coffee in other countries (I'm from the US). I'm not sure what it is about coffee drinks in the USA but they are terrible compared to coffee I have had when traveling abroad. I will say when I go to specialty coffee shops they are fantastic but here I'm specifically referring normal coffee not any type of specialty coffee.  Another difference for me was they will deliver your order to you instead of waiting at the counter. And the location itself was much nicer than usual. Very clean and well kept. || Usually, I fancy any McDonald's all over the world (except for the UK's) & I have a pretty low requirement for the food standard at McDonald's. However, we found this branch was pretty bad. First of all, it didn't have our favourites Filet-O-Fish on their menu. So we ordered a Big Arch, a Veggie burger, 9 chicken nuggets, 2 ice creams, a coke & an orange juice. The Big Arch, which looked like a Big Mac, but was tasted a lot worse & nothing liked it. The chicken nuggets were also a bit overcooked & a bit hard to chew. The Veggie burger was also awful. We had to wait for 25 minutes for the food, which was a bit too long for the average McDonald's standard. The seating area was comfy but a bit dirty, as there was no one clearing the rubbish left behind from the previous customers. Inside this McDonald's, there were also pigeons walking underneath each table looking for food as well. || An amazing experience to be able to eat at McDonald's with friends!  I was pleasantly surprised with the amount of gluten-free options available.  What made this experience even better was the customer service from Susana B. She assisted me with making sure my order was correct.  So impressed with being asked to take a seat and they would bring my food to the table.  Susana did amazing, as we dont speak Portuguese, so impressed with her English speaking skills. Thank you for an amazing experience at McDonald's! || Rarely eat fast food, but when it's late and your teenage son is hungry..... Easy to walk in and order on the self-service kiosk. Can easily change the menu to English if need be. Orders were prompt even though they were very busy. Staff spoke both Portuguese and English. Took our food to go but restaurant looked clean with plenty of seating. Cheeseburger was a little dry and over done but nuggets were much better than in the US. Also liked the teriyaki sauce option for the nuggets. || I wish US service and quality like this place. All the employee is so nice and respectful. It is clean. || Mcdonald's here is way better than in Canada 🇨🇦.  It actually tastes like food here in Portugal 🇵🇹  . || I was very disappointed with my visit. This is an international McDonald’s, yet not a single staff member could speak English, which made communication extremely frustrating. I felt like I was in a completely different environment — not a global fast-food chain. For such a large brand, it’s unacceptable not to have at least one English-speaking staff member available. The overall service experience was poor and needs serious improvement. || Solid McDonald BUT:  - very crowded (good for the company) so i had to wait almost 10 minutes. Too much time for fast food  - ordered a special sandwich without the bun, because my wife is allergic, and guess what i get.. the bun :-(  - the monitors where they inform you about your order are very tiny and they only show when they start to prepare your order. When orders are ready you have to listen for your number in portuguese.  To be fair: except the wrong sandwich these are no really bad experiences. || McDonald’s, always crowded with people, mostly is tourist. I stayed at HF Helix hotel, nearby, and came for dinner once. || Typically, I don't review fast food spots unless there is something unique/cool about it. There was nothing unique about this McDonald's except that it's located near Marques de Pombal and it is probably the most chaotic McDonald's I have ever been to in my life. We stopped by on a Sunday at almost 9 pm and the place was still PACKED. I don't know if it's always like this or if it was because of the foot traffic from the nearby Christmas Market (Wonderland Lisboa), but it was truly insane. Ordering is fine - pretty standard. You order at one of the self service kiosks. But it's the waiting for your order part. We waited 30 minutes for our food. 30 MINUTES FOR "FAST FOOD". It's not efficient because the food just sits on the counter until an employee notices it, so by the time we got our food it was cold. If you want to eat there, don't even think about finding a table. Thankfully, we got ours to go and our hotel was nearby. Again, I don't know if it's specific to this location but try to avoid this McDonald's if you can help it. || I love trying out McDonalds when I’m in other countries and this was good! I loved seeing pea soup and chicken wings as options since we don’t have that in the US. I had a McRoyal with cheese, equivalent to the US quarter pounder with cheese. We also got a big tasty burger which had a special sauce and bacon on it. Everything was good! I loved seeing all the mc flurry flavors as well. || A very big branch of McDonalds next to the historical park and avenue of Lisbon. The place is very big which means lots of customers are there. I noticed some of the customers were a bit rude to the staff which was not cool at all. The staff is doing a hard work to prepare all the orders and keeping the toilets clean. It was a well maintained restaurant. || Service staff gave me the"evil eye" because I asked for ketchup after I ordered it. I feel strongly I was profiled and the staff member treater me poorly due to my nationality. I've never experienced this before at a McDonald's. The entire staff defended his aggressive approach. Would NOT go here under any circumstance. I've never felt more unwelcome than at this McDonald's. What a surprise. || A stellar McDonald's restaurant in a top spot in the core of Lisbon's business center.  Visited this McDonald's restaurant right next to the Marquês de Pombal roundabout/statue.  It's gotta be one of the most modern, decorated and well put together McDonald's restaurants in Lisbon.  The atmosphere is very chill and relaxing, and most costumers there were young which helps create a jovial and cool vibe around the place.  The food is what you would expect from a McDonald's restaurant.  The food came well cooked, tender and tasty (the nuggets were delicious), and everything was very 'presentable'.  Benefited from the fact that i went to grab a late lunch after a job interview (around 4 pm) and there weren't many people there, which got me the food on the table in around 5 minutes post ordering it.  In conclusion, if you are in Lisbon and are craving McDonald's, definitely take this one in consideration. || Surprisingly small menu. Burgers were rushed to put together, effectively falling apart as you opened them. Rubbish was overflowing from all the bins. Staff didn’t seem too concerned, shame as the interim is one of the nicest I’ve seen. || If it was possible I would give it less than one star as it's average food at best as to a hot drink personally (I wouldn't bother getting one) as I asked for a cappuccino and it was given to me and in front of the person who gave me it I put my finger in it as it was cold and I did ask for hot water which I didn't get as don't complain as you don't get anywhere || I loved my McDonald's experience here! In Lisboa, they have an espresso shot on the menu and a single serving of vanilla, and together they were divine. McDonald's didn't disappoint with great taste, quality and value. If only we could do this in the states! At least the coffee in the US is decent (in keeping with the standard of where we live).

A wonderful example of a well-maintained and carefully renovated Gothic cathedral. The Sé de Lisboa dates back to 1147, with construction completed around the 13th century, making it the oldest church in Lisbon.  You can really feel the history here, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic elements shaped over centuries. It’s not overly grand or touristy, just authentic and atmospheric.  Definitely worth taking some time to visit when you’re in the city — a quiet, impressive place right in the heart of Lisbon. || Oldest church in the city (1147). Gorgeous catholic cathedral and a must visit. Very cool to be able to go up in the old choir loft  and especially outside by the large stained glass window on the front of the cathedral. There was a short line when I went on a weekday, so you may want to buy tickets in advance for a weekend, cruise ship port day, or high season. I was disappointed that the cloisters were closed when I went. || Beautiful and historic place in the heart of Alfama. The cathedral feels ancient and peaceful inside, with thick stone walls and soft light coming through the windows. I loved seeing the mix of old architecture and history all around. Even from the outside, it’s impressive — especially when the tram passes by. Definitely worth a short visit while exploring Lisbon. || The cathedral was absolutely breathtaking. There is still an admission fee, but you get a discount with the Lisboa Card, which helps. As you enter, you go up the stairs to the treasure room. On the way up, make sure to notice the carved cross on the stairs, said to have been made by Saint Anthony to repel the devil during his studies.  The artifacts in the treasure room are beautifully detailed and very well preserved. From there, you can access the interior balcony, which offers a great view of the main church below and a close look at the stunning stained glass centerpiece. There’s also a small passage leading to an exterior balcony overlooking the front of the cathedral, though it’s quite narrow and can get crowded. It’s a tight squeeze, one-way, and very high up, so just take care if you’re not great with heights.  The main cathedral itself is massive, with chapels dedicated to different saints along the back. The whole place feels grand and full of history.  Overall, an incredible experience and definitely a must-see when visiting Lisbon. || The oldest and most iconic church in Lisbon, full of history and charm. The architecture is impressive, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. Inside it’s peaceful and beautifully lit, offering a quiet break from the busy streets. Climb up to see the cloisters and enjoy the view of Alfama. A must-visit for history and architecture lovers || We took the classic yellow #28 tram and got off at the Se. The area is very cute with many great photo opportunities. We also had brunch at a sidewalk cafe in the small square right before the Se. It’s worth a visit for the views. || ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Lisbon's spiritual heavyweight champion since 1147 ⛪ Plot twist: you absolutely should go inside this magnificent cathedral, and here's the best part - it's completely free! No tickets, no queues, just walk right in like you own the place (which, in a way, we all do). The Sé de Lisboa isn't just "a church like all the churches" - it's THE church, Lisbon's oldest and most historically significant. The Romanesque fortress-like exterior might look a bit stern and businesslike, but step inside and you're hit with centuries of Portuguese history. The Gothic cloisters are genuinely stunning, and if you're lucky enough to catch evening light streaming through those rose windows, you'll understand why people have been coming here to feel something greater for nearly 900 years. The treasury and archaeological remains are worth exploring if you have time, but honestly, just sitting quietly in the main nave for a few minutes costs nothing and gives you everything. The acoustics are incredible if you catch a service or choir practice. Pro tip: Combine with a wander through Alfama afterwards - you're perfectly positioned for the neighbourhood's winding charm. Historic, free, and utterly peaceful. What's not to love? 🕊️✨ || Dear Tom, thank you for visiting, and we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience. We hope you can return one day to visit the museum and other corners of the monument. || The architecture is impressive, with a mix of Romanesque and Gothic styles. The treasury upstairs is interesting. Paintings are fabulous. The views from the top are spectacular! || Well worth the ticket price and the time to explore. Don’t miss the area upstairs where the vestments are- I’m fascinated by the detailed stitching even on the shoes! The cathedral is beautiful and there is information on its history available even if you elect not to get the audio guide. || Santa Maria Maior is the kind of place that makes you fall in love with Lisbon almost instantly. It’s the heart of the city — full of charm, history, and little surprises around every corner. Wandering through its narrow streets, you go from lively plazas to quiet alleyways, all wrapped in that classic Lisbon mix of energy and old-world beauty.  You’ve got iconic Lisbon landmarks all within a short walk — the Sé Cathedral, the viewpoints in Alfama, Praça do Comércio, and the buzzing streets of Baixa and Chiado. But what really sticks with you is the atmosphere: the tiled facades, the sound of trams passing by, and the tiny cafés where you can stop for a pastel de nata and just soak it all in.  It’s vibrant without being overwhelming, historic without feeling like a museum, and genuinely one of the best areas to explore if you want to experience Lisbon’s soul up close. || What a gem of a place that I walked into while taking the tram 28 route. Such great architecture inside the church and the tile work was very intricate and unique which truly identifies Lisbon || We went on a Saturday and they happen to be holding a mass, which was a great time to visit. The ticket counter was closed due to the mass so they were not selling tickets but allowed access. Pretty neat to see a full functioning catholic cathedral in action with all of its ornate architecture and items. || The Lisbon Cathedral is the oldest church in the city and a prominent symbol of Portugal's history, showcasing a blend of Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque architectural styles. It's free for the visit of the Cathedral but you need to pay for the museum tour. || The cathedral is a worth seeing part of the historic landmarks in Lisbon. I've been to a lot similar sights all across Europe and I can't say that it is amongst the most spectacular but it is still very interesting, also one of the oldest. It is also sometimes open to the public for free and during the weekend. || Beautiful cathedral with a long history. Also, the turn outside the church is a perfect spot to take pictures of tram 28. || This is an amazing church to check out. I would recommend paying the small entrance fee of $7 euros I believe. You get to see so much more and it is so worth it. I am always memorized by the architecture. I am not religious and I truly enjoyed this powerful place. || The Lisbon Cathedral is absolutely worth a visit. It’s one of the oldest and most important landmarks in the city, with a mix of Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles that really tell the story of Lisbon’s history. The outside is impressive, but the inside feels even more special – calm, quiet, and filled with beautiful details. If you have time, go into the cloisters as well, where you can see layers of history all in one place. It’s right in the Alfama district, so you can easily walk around the old streets after your visit. Definitely recommend stopping by, even if just for a short visit. || A must visit place in Lisbon. You can enter freely as a prayer (stopping by the entrance) or go for a ticket to explore the entire church, including the museum in the first floor and the terrace in front of the plaza. It is a wonderful mixup of different styles, from Romanic to Gothic, with several additions in the following centuries. || The tower was unfortunately closed off, so we could not go up. You can still go outside on a short passageway, just under the central stained glass window, and the views of the city is beautiful. Overall, it was worth paying the entrance fee to go upstairs, see the museum section. More information in English would be helpful for visitors who don't speak Portuguese. By pure coincidence, while visiting the church, two man started playing/practicing the organ, it was beautiful. || Exactly what we expected before coming. We can feel the power of Jesus Christ covering the church. Something reminds us of Dark Souls, the game that we played together, its inspired by ancient Europeans civilization. || Dear Daud, we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience and that it brought back fond memories. Thank you very much for your feedback.

Cathedral of Saint Paul of the Lusitanian Church (Anglican Church communion), which settled in a former Carmelite Convent built in the 17th century. || Beautiful church with a sweet garden inside. This church though is most of the time close. The rocks used to build this was very beautiful. Relaxing and numbing quiet inside even in the garden area. They have a WC. Lady staff that I met was grumpy and not welcoming || We were only able to see it from the outside on our way to a nearby museum. It was peaceful inside, where we entered the courtyard, and there's something like a dining room, so we respected the location and left. We would have liked to see the inside... || Despite the passing years, this old building remains standing. It's very beautiful from the outside, and upon entering, you find something very beautiful. The entire area is very nice to walk around. || The explanation of the history of this religious community, which we received from a very friendly lady, filled our hearts with joy. Very interesting. The garden behind the left door upstairs is a pleasant surprise. || St. Paul's Cathedral is the seat of the Portuguese Catholic Apostolic Evangelical Church, located in Lisbon. The cathedral stands on the site of a former Discalced Carmelite convent, founded in 1606 and completed in 1611. After the abolition of religious orders and the expulsion of the friars, the building was requisitioned and used from 1835 as barracks for the 17th Battalion of the National Guard, and from the following year also housed the police station. The building was then put up for sale at a public auction in 1872, and the property was purchased by the Scottish Presbyterian Church, a move that sparked considerable controversy. Since 1898, it has been owned by the Portuguese Catholic Apostolic Evangelical Church. || A different style than what I'm used to. Sobriety prevails above all else. It's not a typical Lisbon church. Although it's interesting to learn about other styles. Learn to compare. || I was very well received and the sermon was very edifying! It is a church in communion with the Anglican Church, with a very interesting history in Portugal.  I recommend it to everyone! || A place of prayer with a rich history. || It wasn't the most beautiful cathedral I've ever seen. || Worth a visit! Interesting. || Site of the Portuguese church

place_name: Church of Our Lady of Mercy
reviews_content: It's one of the most beautiful churches in Lisbon. Situated in very antique and premium spot of Lisbon, it's worth a walk away from the city center to find this cute corner. It's a good place to take a group picture and show the typical Lisbon architecture. If you like to visit churches you must go here!! || Beautiful church with big nice square in front. I saw the garden around but the gate was closed. The church is open for visitors. Huge and fine inside, but I didn’t look around for more details - it was time of preaching, so I didn’t want to disturb. || We live few meters form there. This place looks amazing but we never catch it open. || Big church but seems permanently closed || Really beautiful church || Beautiful,  a hidden gem. You can also go upstairs to the organ and the choir cloister || I heared there is mass in English at 5:30 on Sunday || Spectacular, underrated church on a hilltop. Only open on Sundays (mass time and before/after). || Beautiful building at the top of a narrow street. Doesn't seem to be open to the public. || If you are lucky the sacristia will be open...

place_name: Church of Our Lady of the Rosary of Fatima
reviews_content: Church of Our Lady the Rosary of Fatima in Lisbon was consecrated in 1938. It's a mixture of modern and traditional architecture. Inside are mosaics and colorful stained glass windows. Especially the stained windows behind the choir are quite impressive, with depictions of saints and angels. The church is still in use as such, but respectful visitors are welcomed. There is no charge. Also, at times, there are free concerts in the church. || There is a beautiful painting at the top, showing the Arca Salvifica, but other than that this church isn't very interesting. || Modern church.  Clean lines.  Stained glass that shines we'll inside.  Unique sidewalk tiles. || See it for yourself! Amazing vibe and healing factors mixed up || What a beautiful Church we attended 2 Mass Services Not to be repetitive but so beautiful, very different to back home || Very Beautiful and Religious place to visit. I feel very relaxed and calm at this place. || Lovely church and the choir were absolutely amazing and there were only 4/5 members singing a cappella worth going just to listen to them at 10.30 mass on Sunday. || Nice church for a quick stop if you are in the area. We passed it on our way to a museum close by. Check the opening times first. || November 2024 - Lisbon Sings. I've never felt this way before. I've never been closer to Him. This Church will forever remain a sanctuary to me. || Fabulous catholic church in Lisbon with a shrine of Our Lady of Fatima. It's one of the two Jubilar Churches in Lisbon.

place_name: Church of Our Lady of the Conception
reviews_content: Beautiful church in Lisbon. || The beauty of an art. :) || This church, though seemingly a place of worship, doesn't appear so at first glance, as its facade is more like a palace. Inside, however, it's very beautiful. A very peaceful place to be close to God. || A chapel dedicated to Our Lady of the Conception was commissioned by the Marquis of Viana, with construction beginning in 1633 and concluding in 1721. It originally served as the chapel of the former Trinitarian Monastery, with the original invocation of Our Lady of Remedies. The dedication to Our Lady of the Conception only began in 1885, when the building was occupied by the Asylum of Our Lady of the Conception. Its entire facade withstood the 1755 earthquake. Its facade is crafted from stonework. At the end of the 19th century, it underwent remodeling. Inside, we can find panel paintings alluding to the Passion of Christ, located in the chancel, in a Mannerist altarpiece from the Batalha Monastery, crafted in marble. || Linda, I am a devotee of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception. Whenever I turn to her, I am answered. I have great faith in her and I am grateful for everything. || Bonita doesn't need cleaning. || It is currently a church, but until the 18th century it was considered the chapel of the former Trinitarian Monastery, originally dedicated to Our Lady of Remedies, whose construction was only completed in 1721. The entrance to the chapel is through the prominent central section of the elaborate building, executed during the remodeling works of the late 19th century; inside, between the bare walls, the altarpiece of the chancel stands out, originating from the Monastery of Batalha, made of marble with paintings on panels alluding to the Passion of Christ. || I really wanted to schedule a mass. If possible, January 3, 2023. I'm going to Portugal just to pray inside that specific church. It's related to my late father's life story. || From Monday to Friday there is Eucharist at 8:30 am and Adoration until 6 pm. On Sundays Eucharist at 8 pm. Every Wednesday at 5 pm Marian Cenacle followed by Eucharist.

place_name: Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
reviews_content: A good place to visit for brutalism friends. The main room is a well made modern version of historic churches and creates a similar feeling. || Great brutalist building for architecture lovers. Lots of spots to pray.  They also have an architecture book about the church for a price. || Absolutely incredible jewel of a brutalist building. Love the light and the architecture in this place though it is a little hard to spot from the street. If you like churches or brutalist architecture or (gasp) brutalist architecture churches, this is a must go! Then stroll up the hill for an excellent view from the park. || The photos on the internet doesn't make clear how unusual is this church. Geometric and minimal are two adjectives that came to mind spending some minutes here. Also the lighting is particular. Make a stop here if you can, you will see a unique church. || Very different design and architecture and engeneering for a church... but amazingly quiet on the inside... a great place to worship Peace...please visit ! || Beautiful architecture, feels like entering another world in the middle of the city. || Spiritual experience here. I'm glad its not overhyped and crowded, simply a work of art best enjoyed in your own heart. || Large local church with a more stark and modern feel || Very cool inside. I am not a church person but it was worth going to for the architecture alone. It is unlike any other church that I have seen in Europe or elsewhere. It was cold yet cozy.

place_name: Church Nossa Senhora da Conceição Velha
reviews_content: A truly beautiful church tucked away on a quiet side street, yet just a short walk from Praça do Comércio. Nossa Senhora da Conceição has been masterfully renovated. The entrance features wonderful carvings that immediately draw you in, and once inside, you’re greeted by a stunning stucco-decorated ceiling that takes your breath away. A hidden gem worth discovering when exploring the city! || We were in Lisbon na at our cruise for 6 days. Walking back to our ship one day we found this old church which had to be restored after a large fire.  It is quiet and peaceful so stop and say a prayer for the poor people of the world while you rest your feet.  Not too much to see as compared to the larger churches around town. Still, it is very nice and worth a visit. || The Igreja da Conceição Velha has one of the most beautiful examples of Manueline architecture in Portugal. I believe the original interior of the church was destroyed during the Great Earthquake of Lisbon. Even so, admiring its façade alone makes the visit worthwhile. Pay special attention to the intricate carvings on the main doorway — they are truly remarkable. || A beautiful and peaceful church with elegant architecture and a calming atmosphere.  The interior is simple yet charming, offering a quiet break from the busy streets.  A lovely spot to pause and appreciate Lisbon’s history and spiritual charm. || Please visit this beautiful church, especially go the Holy Mass if you are a traditional catholic because the Masses are in Latin. Be aware that the information about the Mass at church is wrong. Just check on the internet. Sundays and holy days of obligation  - 10AM and 6PM,  Tuesdays till Fridays  - 7 p.m. and Saturdays  - 10:30 am. || One of the facades to survive the All Saints Day earth quake of 1755 and the following tsunami; certainly worth a quick stop or, at the very least, a quick walk by. || Tucked away in Lisbon’s Baixa district, the Church of Nossa Senhora da Conceição Velha stuns with its richly carved Manueline façade — a survivor of the 1755 earthquake. Step inside to discover peaceful interiors, gothic arches, and echoes of Portugal’s maritime past in every stone. || Mass is at 10 am on Sundays in a beautiful old church A very interesting mass, very beautiful, but no interaction with the congregation at all. It was almost like watching a play! || Didn’t actually go inside but the architecture outside is a sight worth seeing . || This is truly a magnificent religious space. The carousels, the Ferris wheel, etc., disappeared. And the entertainment at the site ended. It was a shame. Since 2003, the year the Feira Popular in Entrecampos closed, there hasn't been any amusement space in the city, despite the successive promises of the many mayors who have passed through the municipality. Miradouro de Santa Luzia is absolutely worth a visit. The views over Alfama’s rooftops and the Tagus River are genuinely beautiful, and for the price of free, you really can’t complain.  ￼  It was a bit crowded when we went, but that’s expected given how popular this spot is. Even so, it’s still a memorable place to slow down for a few minutes, take photos, and enjoy the scenery. The viewpoint itself is part of the charm too, with a small landscaped terrace, shaded areas, and classic blue-and-white azulejo panels that make it feel distinctly Lisbon.  ￼  One detail I appreciated is that the tile panels aren’t just decorative, they depict historical scenes, including Lisbon’s Praça do Comércio before the 1755 earthquake and the 1147 conquest of the castle (a cool touch if you like history).  ￼  That said, I wouldn’t call the views “to die for.” You can get comparable viewpoints nearby, and this is more of a “quick, classic Lisbon stop” than a once-in-a-lifetime moment. It’s also conveniently located in Alfama at Largo de Santa Luzia, right by the Church of Santa Luzia, making it an easy stop while exploring the neighborhood.  ￼  Overall, crowded or not, it’s still definitely worth a visit and an easy, memorable addition to a Lisbon walking day. || Miradouro de Santa Luzia offers some of the most impressive views in Lisbon. A peaceful spot to take a break from the busy streets below and appreciate Lisbon from above. Definitely worth the walk. || Amazing panoramic view from this beautiful spot. Looks over the city and the coastline with all the infrastructure of the city. Great for sunsets and photos. || A stunning view of the city. It's a bit of a tiring walk uphill but if your prepared for it its nice to explore the area. There's plenty of space for pictures when you reach it. With lots of nice cafe's and restaurants close by if you need a break. I'd definitely recommend checking it out for an atmospheric view and pictures if you have time. || An amazing viewpoint looking over the city and towards the river. Lucky enough to have such a beautiful day, in the middle of December, to see this panorama. Well worth visiting for the WOW factor alone. Plenty of photo opportunities from here. || One of the best few points of Lisbon. Gorgeous photos of a sunset and there’s a beautiful church right next to it so that you can go in at no cost, but you can make donations. I took an electric bike to see the place since it’s very uphill, so I don’t recommend walking.  I suggest taking the tram 28 up. || I arrived there during the sunset moment and lots of people already sit along the railing. It was nice to stay sometime here to oversee this red rooftop buildings and with the light, the city looks astonishing 😃 … || American Traveler here. Our tuktuk guide stopped here and you can see why. It's so gorgeous! You get a good view oh the city. There are restrooms nearby though I didn't try them.

place_name: Chafariz da Rua de O Século
reviews_content: Relaxing fountain, not too busy, kinda a hidden gem || Very quiet when I visited, peaceful sounds of the wall fountains. Beautiful steets around. || Cool place, non-potable water though || It got ruined...you can barely see the design... || An interesting plaza off the beaten tourist track. It features decorative cobblestones and a large wall with a fountain (chafariz) with three spouts and three images. There are a few trees and benches for sitting. It has surely seen better days, but it's still worth a look. || Small, welcoming and charming in the evening, sometimes they organize small free fado shows || Chafariz da Rua Formosa was its former name. It was recently renovated. || One of the city's most charming spots. Very nice, although it could use a bit of a tune-up. || A peaceful and quiet place. || Urban fountain, designed in 1752 by Carlos Mardel, integrated into the Loreto branch. It follows the typology of a wall fountain, with a strong Baroque scenic character, arranged on two levels, connected by lateral staircases, with two spouts in the shape of a rosette. || Somewhere along the climb to the Convento dos Cardaes from Calçada do Combro, you'll come across a rather abandoned plaza. Undoubtedly, what stands out most when illuminated by the afternoon sun is the bright green tiled facade of the building that encloses the plaza on the right. || A must-see attraction on the way to the famous Bairro Alto. 👍👌😃🍻🍹 …

Probably the best public park in Porto. Stunning views, interesting old trees and pathways. The place is really big, and worth spending a whole afternoon exploring it. I highly recommend visiting. || Jardim do Torel - Where K-Pop Meets Quiet Romance and the Trees Whisper in Harmony  With Dion humming “APT” like it’s the soundtrack to our lives, we made our way to Jardim do Torel, a firm local favourite and, as it turns out, a filming location for NewJeans’ “Super Shy”. If you’re going to chase K-pop vibes in Lisbon, this is the place to do it - with less glitter, more greenery, and a whole lot of charm.  Nestled in a stately, upmarket parish, the garden feels like a secret lookout - overlooking the city and the river, with just enough elevation to make you feel like you’ve earned the view. On the Saturday morning we visited, the park was alive but gentle with older couples sitting romantically on benches, picnic baskets unpacked with care, and the breeze rustling through the trees like nature’s own ballad.  It’s the kind of place where you can slow down, breathe deeply, and let the city hum below you while you hum along to your own tune. Whether you’re chasing K-pop filming locations or just looking for a quiet moment with someone you like, Jardim do Torel delivers.  Verdict: A peaceful perch above Lisbon, perfect for romantic mornings, picnic afternoons, and soft soundtracks. Highly recommended for view seekers, K-pop fans, and anyone who believes a garden should come with a breeze and a bench. || One of my favorite gardens in Lisboa. It looks to other viewpoints and it is chiller than other spots in city due to the trees up here. Good view, chill vibes, only a few people with their dogs and children; lovely atmosphere overall! || Our final stop was Canil Marques where Tom had found that it served up a wide variety of affordable craft beers. Enroute, Kate designed a route that passed by Jardim do Torel with beautiful views over the city of Lisbon. It is said to be one of the best kept secrets of Lisbon with its broad view of the Avenida da Liberdade and São Roque hill – home to the Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara. Jardim do Torel is also surrounded by a garden and grand 18th- and 19th-century houses which makes it a great spot. The wide flat patio a level down provides the best views in our opinion. Do note that there’s opening and closing hours of the gardens – check before you head over. A well-hidden gem in Lisbon!  For the full review and details of our 5 months Round The World RTW travels, visit 2bearbear today! || Great place to watch the sunset, grassy areas to sit and picnic, benches, etc. and not too busy either! City views aren’t the best though, and some construction is currently blocking parts but still a nice park. || It is a great view of the city. A rather stunning view to see all the lively bright orange roofs of the city. A bit far from the sea,but it is free. :)  A bit noisy as there are construction work nearby when I visited. The garden is still well maintained though the fountain is not open during my visit.  Could be a good place to have breakfast or a Pinic while enjoying the view. || Great views. Could have been better maintained. Great potential but nevertheless great respite. || I recently discovered Jardim do Torel in Lisbon and it quickly became one of my favorite hidden spots in the city. Perched atop the Santana hill, this peaceful garden offers stunning views over downtown Lisbon and the Tagus River. Originally part of a private estate in the 19th century, it was opened to the public in the 1960s, providing a tranquil retreat amidst the urban landscape. The garden features shaded pathways, a charming pond with an 18th-century mermaid statue, and a terrace café where you can relax and enjoy the scenery. Accessing the garden via the historic Ascensor do Lavra funicular adds a unique touch to the visit. Admission is free, making it an accessible and delightful spot for both locals and tourists seeking a serene escape with panoramic views. || Looks like a secret garden with a cityscape. There is a bar on top, some benches. Great to sit with a drink and enjoy the city || Beautiful hidden spot that can be counted as one of Lisbon‘s beautiful miradouros || Beautiful little park with grant old trees and a fanatic view of the city. Next to the green are stairs going a level down to a fountain pool for public bathing and a good playground for kids! Love the vibe, one of my favorite places in Lisbon! || Amazing plaza where you can enjoy a glass of wine and beer with locals. The neighborhood is beautiful and full of small palaces. A lot of history around. Stunning sunset view from Lisbon without the tourist crowds. || one of my favourite sunset spots in lisbon it’s a shame the fountain is empty || Not the best view at the moment because of the cranes and construction everywhere. I enjoyed sitting on a bench and watching the sunset. It's ridiculous though how much people smoke in this city. It's impossible to escape it. Young men are also very rowdy and cause a lot of disturbance. || One of my favourite viewpoints in Lisbon. Only bad thing is that they come and close it at 20.00. But otherwise it has a very nice vibe, people are getting together ans sitting on the grass, watching the beautiful city below. Perfect for a date or to have some drinks with friends during good weather. || Very cute place to hang out a few minutes during the day. You can sit on the benches and enjoy the view first and later you can go down the stairs and check out the "swimming pool". Some people jump on it when it's very hot. Hence, very charming garden that you should visit if you're in Lisbon! Besides, it's just a few minutes walking from Liberdade Avenue, one of the city's major attractions. || Beautiful view and great vibes. Sometimes some people even play music here , while some watch the sunset …. || A little park with a observation deck that offers wonderful views of the old town. I visited it early in the morning(around 08:00).It was such a nice atmosphere! Quiet, only a few people, the sun gilding the buildings below, the birds singing. Peaceful! At walking distance(less than 10 minutes) you can find the top end of the line of Ascensor do Lavra, a picturesque old funicular. || Jardim do Tourel in Lisbon is a tranquil oasis that should not be missed. With its lush greenery, peaceful atmosphere, and beautiful views, it provides a much-needed respite from the city's hustle and bustle. Whether you're looking for a place to relax, have a picnic, or simply enjoy a leisurely stroll, this park has it all. Don't forget to bring sunscreen and your camera as there are plenty of picturesque spots to capture. Overall Jardim do Torel is a delightful retreat that offers a breath of fresh air in the heart of Lisbon. || charming little hilltop garden with a great view over the city. perfect for solitude reflective time or chilled socializing. also there’s a kiosk for drinks, makes it easy to linger around sunset.

A beautiful and peaceful spot right by the Tagus River — perfect for a stroll, watching the sunset. You get a great view of the 25 de Abril Bridge and the passing ferries especially with Sunset.  It’s a simple place, but somehow feels magical — especially in the golden hour. A must-stop if you’re walking around Praça do Comércio. || Its a beautiful square on the beach of the river, with an amazing view and on calm days it is peaceful enough to just sit there or have a walk and enjoy the view of the river and Almada across the river. || We were walking around Lisbon for several days while waiting to join our cruise. By the river in front of Praça do Comercio, we observed two stone columns in the water. We were told by the guide that the columns were installed with a dock in 1755 after the earth quakes. It is a nice quiet spot by the water to relax. || Cais das Colunas is one of those places in Lisbon that just sticks with you. Tucked right next to Praça do Comércio, it’s a peaceful riverside spot with amazing views of the Tagus—especially at sunset. Whether you're passing through or looking for a place to unwind, this is a perfect stop.  The vibe here is really special. It’s calm but still full of life—locals lounging around, tourists soaking it all in, occasional street performers, and sometimes even live music playing in the background. It feels like a snapshot of Lisbon’s soul.  I love grabbing a coffee and just sitting on the stone steps, watching boats go by and the sky change colors as the city lights start to glow. It’s also a great spot for photos—between the water reflections and the beautiful architecture, everything looks picture-perfect.  It’s simple, free, and yet one of the most memorable parts of the city. I’ve been here multiple times and always end up staying longer than I planned.  If you’re visiting Lisbon, definitely carve out a little time to come here. You won’t regret it. || The view of the Tagus River, the 25th of April Bridge, and the view is simply breathtaking, especially at sunset. It’s a great spot to sit, take photos, and soak in the city’s atmosphere. A must-see for anyone exploring the Praça do Comércio area || Great area to visit and hang out with family and friends. A lot of restaurants and cafes,  beautiful view of the city and the river. || The place is amazing for walk at end of the day and or just sit and listen to sound of water and birds flying. I think both locals and tourists come here often just to sit enjoy the sunset views, the vibe and view of the other side of the city.  Best time to go there is when it is sunny at end of the day to get relaxed and enjoy the sunset, or in the morning for sunrise. During the day mostly when it is sunny it is quite crowded. || This is a historic riverside pier in Lisbon, easily recognized by its two marble columns rising from the Tagus River. Designed by Eugénio dos Santos as part of the city’s reconstruction after the 1755 earthquake, the columns are said to be inspired by those of Solomon’s Temple—symbolizing wisdom and devotion. For much of its history, this pier served as a key docking point for ferries and ships, connecting Lisbon with the southern bank of the Tagus and functioning as an important transport hub. The original columns were removed in the late 19th century, later restored in 1929, dismantled again during metro construction in 1997, and finally reinstalled in 2008. || As described, past historic entryway to the city. Some nice musicians, but wouldn’t recommend more then 15min here || It was a lovely day for a walk, and this was a lovely place to visit! There is only a small sandy beach area, but it was fairly clean and our little dog absolutely loved running around on the sand after walking on pavement all day! (we didn't see any signs saying that dogs are not allowed on the beach and we kept her on a leash). || Just sitting there is beautiful, you can take boat tour of tagus river next to it. || People come here to see the sunset by the river on the shore. You get a nice view of the 25 April Bridge whilst you sit or stand in contemplation. Worth coming down to visit no matter what time of day it might be.  It is next to the Praça do Comércio. Here important figures, including a head of state like Queen Elizabeth II arrived into Lisbon.  Sometimes there are musicians playing.  It gets very windy, so be careful! Watch any loose belongings.  Follow here and the IG link in profile for more travel and food and drink tips, ideas and reviews! || Such a beautiful place to sit and watch the water, with the street musicians creating impeccable vibes! || What a place to hang out before sunset. What I really enjoyed was the view and all the different people of all ethnicity and background just hanging out.  Nice breeze in the evenings and some guy was playing some music. I recommend coming here during your visit to Lisbon. Amazing atmosphere..... must visit places in Lisbon. Every tourist visits this place...❤️❤️❤️❤️ || Next to the main square of Lisbon. Possible to reach here by metro, bus, tram, and also boat. Also possible to sit and chill under the good weather here. || Lovely public square flanked by these massive columns at one end, from which the main street starts. Open 24 hours. We went there at 9 PM and walked around till almost midnight.  There are musicians playing lovely songs and lots of people, young and old, dancing under the columns. Really lovely atmosphere overall. || Loved this area o the centre! || This is a great place to hang out before sunset. What I really enjoyed was the view and all the different people of all ethnicity and background just hanging out.  Nice breeze in the evenings and some guy was playing some music. I recommend coming here during your visit to Lisbon. || A great place to just chill and relax for a bit. Especially on a nice day where you can just watch the waves and look out across the water. Soothing for the soul! || Near the middle and all the fast trouble of Lisboa you find a small place to relax. You will meet young people in mind and body, interpreting their level of art in different styles. They welcome you and you can do same. Enjoy it! Sometimes it’s hard to see a high proportion of homeless people and the coast isn’t that clean as it could be. Don’t find the tourist traps 🪤… there are many… (we know it, well) 😉

place_name: Garden of the Castle of São Jorge
reviews_content: Very clean and moderately maintained. Was nice to walk off the filthy streets into a nice clean garden. The views were immaculate especially during sundown and can get quite windy. The toilets were broken and stinky so go before you come. || A magical place suspended between history and breathtaking views  The gardens of São Jorge Castle are a true oasis in the heart of Lisbon. Walking among ancient trees, native plants, and peaceful paths while enjoying stunning views over the city and the Tagus River is simply unforgettable. The silence, broken only by the calls of peacocks, offers a relaxing escape from the urban buzz.  The gardens are beautifully maintained, and the atmosphere feels authentic—not just a park, but a place rich in history and charm. I highly recommend coming early or around sunset to experience the full magic of the location.  An absolute must-see when visiting Lisbon! || This is a serene garden nestled within the castle walls. Unlike the fortress’s imposing structure, this area offers a calm and romantic atmosphere, perfect for a quiet stroll. At the edge of the garden, you'll be treated to a breathtaking panoramic view of Lisbon and the Tagus River. One of the most delightful surprises is the presence of free-roaming peacocks, which have become a charming symbol of the place. || This park is in the middle of the city and is do beautiful...and out morning walk we encountered beautiful duck 🦆 with their babies going for a swim ..the park is very clean and take you to the stunning building that is the cultural center. You can seat and enjoy the park in different areas and enjoy . The park has also a coffee shop and right beside you can see the castle. || Garden that is definitely worth a visit. Pleasant sitting in the shade of trees, a walk and views of Lisbon. It is also possible to walk on the castle walls in the premises || Loved this spot. Great views of Lisbon and while the castle itself feels empty, you can go up to the ramparts and explore most of the things it has on offer. We got to see the periscope display where a guide points out different parts of the city which was great and I highly recommend. The cost to enter seemed high but I enjoyed it and felt it worth it || Located at one of the highest points of Lisbon, this castle and its surrounding garden are worth seeing. You can both watch the whole city from above and visit the garden. It's great that it also has access to the castle. It's pretty easy to get to the castle as well. It makes sense to go from Lisbon Center by tram. Because a steep road may tire you. You can also capture beautiful pictures with wonderful peacocks in the garden. || Really interesting historical castle on the top of the hill. Definitely worthy to see with good ratio price and experience for visitors. You can enjoy an impressive old architecture as well as beautiful view of the city there. || I loved it. Peacocks are walking around. You can sit and enjoy the view, drink a beer or water...views are amazing. || Wow! What a beautiful place for a sunset! It is quite expensive (10EUR pp) but you get the best sunset view in Lisbon.  When going there make sure to plan some time to buy tickets. The queue gets longer before sunset.  Pick a spot early. In summer there were drinks and food trucks on the premises. But if you want to go low cost, there is a large supermarket just 5min away. Downhill.  Enjoy Lisbon! || Great views, interesting castle and a 360 view of all around the capital with an interesting tour guide. A nice walk up to the castle and reasonable cost to go in. Lots of peacocks too || I think it's worth 10€. The city looks beatiful from up there, peacocks are roaming around freely in the garden, and you can have a seat on many of the windy spots and just enjoy the view. || Beautiful garden, with a majestic view of the city! There are several peacocks roaming around and it's possible to go over the walls of the castle for an even better view || This is part of the Castelo Sao Jorge here you can make as well excellent pictures.  If you bring your children with you, please be aware there are dangerous and too high corners around the Garden where there is really danger for children and adults to fall (too high and areas don’t have protection as I guess they did not want to manage this aged beautiful building).  Bring good shoes 👟 to walk comfortable and safely: rocky floor all over the place. || Great view of the city, the 13 Euro adult entry fee is a little steep, but the view and the castle are worth seeing. || Love this place, you get to see the beautiful town and the sunset, the only bad thing it was very windy, and almost no shades || Stunning 16th century castle. This is not a castle in the British sense but a huge ancient structure on a hill with many stone steps, multiple be levels, and some museum exhibitions. Allow at least two hours to explore the grounds. || Majestic castle in the middle of the city You can see it from around the city standing tall and great. A place that must be in the list of places to visit in Lisbon || A place to have a different stroll and see the views.  Lots of narrow stairways and view points.   Good walking shoes recommended as it's walking on cobble. €8.50 entry about 60mins walking round. || Must visit when in Lisbon, all the history and fantastic views from the Alfama area...

On the way to São Jorge Castle (sometimes known in English as Saint George's Castle), I passed this guy singing on his balcony with the words "The Reverse Serenade". Usually one stands on the ground serenade on on the balcony, but this was truly backwards. He was really entertaining! Glad I had a chance to witness this. || Very original, the guy is sweet and charming. || Refused to pay 15 euro to enter a bunch of old European rocks again. Wandered the surrounding streets and ran across this legend singing and playing guitar and harmonica on his balcony with a hat dangling down for tips. I just couldnt resist the sweet sounds of Stand By Me. Bought a beer from the corner store to get some change to tip him and spent 20 minutes enjoying his medley. It was my highlight of Lisbon. Afro, you truly are a legend brother. Ill try to make it back tomorrow. One love, keep the sweet sounds rolling || Great experience, be sure to visit it! || Magical, songs to transport you back to a simpler time. Thank you for those snatched moments. || It really made my day to walk around and here the guy singing || Walked here in the afternoon around 5ish to check it out however no one was performing. Could be on their break. || I guess he's not always there. He must have a performance time. I came up here eagerly because I wanted to see him, but he wasn't there. (Visit time: 5:50 PM) || Artists playing on the balcony of the house. Nice experience. || A magical moment on my way to São Jorge Castle was when I was lucky enough to witness a unique serenade: a singer perched on a balcony, his voice echoing through the cobbled streets of Alfama. It was a moment of great beauty, blending music and traditional architecture. The singer performed pieces with palpable passion and emotion, offering passersby a poetic and memorable pause. It added a romantic and authentic touch to the stroll. If you happen to be passing by, take a moment to listen and let yourself be transported by this unexpected performance. It's a true gift for lovers of music and the Lisbon atmosphere. || When Portuguese songwriting meets the road, magical things happen. || I thought it was the same old man, but I guess not. The old men sing every day, lol. It's amazing and nice to see.

Lovely architecture. Visited just before Christmas hence the tree. This is the location of Portugals oldest ( continuously open) restaurant. Great service and food at good prices. Definitely worth a stop; even if just for a coffee outdoors || On our last visit to Lisbon, we spent several days touring around the city center including the area around this grand arch and the plaza. Very busy area for the tourists as photo ops in every direction.  Grand beautiful arch and gorgeous buildings all around.  Several restaurants open on the plaza. Maybe the most picturesque spot in Lisbon. || According da Rua Augusta is definitely worth a visit -you can pay a small entrance fee and go up to the top. Once your up there you have a panoramic view of the city of Lisbon. Its a great spot for photos/videos and gives you a birds eye perspective of the city - the praca comercio, tagus river and rooftops of downtown Lisbon. || This magnificent triumphal arch leads you from the city center to the banks of the Tagus River, via the famous Praça do Comércio (Commerce Square). At its summit are sculptures by Célestin Anatole Calmels, a French sculptor who spent much of his life in Portugal, representing Glory and crowning Genius and Valor. Those below, by Vítor Bastos, depict some of the country's most important historical figures: Nuno Álvares Pereira, Viriate, Vasco da Gama, and the Marquis of Pombal. To the left is the Tagus River, and to the right, the Douro River.  These two rivers marked the boundary of the region inhabited by the Lusitanians, and the inscription at the top of the arch refers to the Portuguese colonial empire and the discovery of new peoples and cultures :  “VIRTVTIBVS MAIORVM VT SIT OMNIBVS DOCVMENTO.PPD”, meaning : “The virtues of our elders, to serve as a lesson for all. (Dedication at public spending)”. || It’s a beautiful structure, but it is surrounded by touts selling things you don’t need. It is also a visible human reminder of the economic and housing crisis that exists in this country. || Stunning architecture, well worth taking the time to come and see it. When coming to Lisbon is well worth making sure you include a vist here on your list. It does get very busy, but the street is wide with lots of room so you dont end up bumping into people. I also found it easy to stop and take pictures with out getting in anyone's way, or anyone getting in my way. If you're coming here on a sunny day, make sure you have you're sunglasses. I forgot mine and found it to be extremely bright! || The Rua Augusta Arch is a stone, memorial arch-like, historical building and visitor attraction in Lisbon, Portugal, on the Praça do Comércio. It was built to commemorate the city's reconstruction after the 1755 earthquake. You can take the elevator above the arch for splendid city views || A stunning piece of architecture which is an iconic site to visit when exploring Lisbon. The top of this arch is filled with stunning sculptures and there are so many details you can discover. || The Arco da Rua Augusta is one of Lisbon’s most iconic monuments. Standing between Rua Augusta and Praça do Comércio, it’s beautiful to admire from below, with detailed sculptures and rich history. Even better, you can go up to the top for a small fee. The views are spectacular: Rua Augusta on one side, the vast Praça do Comércio and Tagus River on the other. A must-visit spot that perfectly captures the spirit of Lisbon. || The Arco Da Rua Augusta was first planned in 1759 after the great earthquake of Lisbon in 1755. However, it was only completed more than 100 years later in 1862 due to differing ideas on how the eventual design should be. Inside, you will have to go through a couple of narrow spiral staircases. So narrow that there were green/red traffic lights that you will press before transiting through it...  For the full review and details of our 5 months Round The World RTW travels, visit 2bearbear today! || Amazing people watching! Emerson got tickets to go inside, you can go up the elevator and up the stairs to the top of the arch. Amazing views. || One of the most important and iconic landmarks of Lisbon. A beautiful square right in front of the Tagus River, perfect at any time for a lovely stroll! || The view from the top is fantastic and definitely worth buying a ticket to experience. An elevator takes you up to the top of the Arc, where you can walk around and take great photos of the surroundings. || A lovely walk down the street with the massive arch at the end heralding the entrance to the square. Absolutely loved this area. Fantastic open space with lots of people enjoying being in the fantastic Lisbon. Great place to people watch and just sit and soak up the atmosphere || A vast area close the water that has lots to see, there was a mini market with stalls serving up along the outer sides that sold lots of unique items. The amount of people as guessed is quite a lot and everyone is trying to take nice photos so timing when to come is crucial. A great place to see and walk by if near. || You can see the monument from below and with extra ticket you can visit the top to see the city view. During sunset it is amazing. || Only 4,50€ per person. There was no line or wait to go up. There are a couple of staircases to get up top after the elevator but well worth it once you see the spectacular view. Rode past the "Elevator" lift line on the way down to the Arch and it was very long! This was certainly the better attraction, unless you can't climb stairs. We were able to capture photos from multiple angles showing Christo Rei, the Bay Bridge/sea, downtown and the hills. So very beautiful. || Standing beneath the Arco da Rua Augusta, you feel the heartbeat of Lisbon—where history, tradition, and culture converge with stunning views and wonderful vibes. A timeless icon! || with the Lisboa card, the entrance is free. The view from the top of the arch is amazing. You can see the Comércio and beixa downtown. || The biggest secret in lisbon is the fact that you can go to the top of the arch for less than $5. And it's really empty up there with a gorgeous view of the square and the street. Just look for the little sign on the left when facing the water right next to the arch. It's easy to miss, but it's definitely worth finding.
Also known as Areeiro Square.

Definitely worth the visit and a true highlight of our time in Lisboa. It was a marvellous experience for the both of us and something we’ve never seen before. You even don’t have to wait in line for this, amazing! If you are not going here when you are in Lisboa, then you will regret it for life!!! || This is peak Lisbon. You can cancel visiting the Christmas Markets, the beautiful cobblestone streets, the beach and even the Oceanarium. Nothing beats this.  You will just love this as soon as you come there, the sheer imagination and skill just squeezing out of this point of the tiny streets in Alfama speaks for itself.  I'll probably stay in Lisbon just for this.  Thank me later! || This is the best thing in europe after the leaning tower of pisa. A must. || Silly goofy time in an alley, if you're passing by || I spent the whole day here it was amazing!!! || Dont expect to much. Its more a thing for photoshop. Funny though || The highlight of our Lisboa trip. We woke up extra early and cancelled our Sintra trip just to be able to witness this marvel of entertainment and engineering.  Will definitely be back the next time we visit Lisboa. || Following Google to get there, it was up some very narrow and steep alleyways. Not good for a disability scooter and then we couldn't find it. Not sure how genuine other reviews are... || It’s a railing that when you sit on it gives an illusion that you are floating. Don’t go out of your way to find it, if you are passing by it is ok for a photo op. || Honestly one of the more memorable parts of our trip!  Come check it out or you will never really have lived.

place_name: Jardim da Alameda Dom Afonso Henriques
reviews_content: We love this place we spend a lot time here is perfect to run, to picnic, local festivals, or drink a beer. There is so many cafes and restorants near by and some weekends you can watch people dancing kizomba or playing music || This is huge and beautiful fountain. If you spend more time to climb up to the hill, you will have an amazing view too. Local people come here to play Sport, walk with dogs or relax easily. High recommend. || One of the best place in Lisbon. That you come during the day or evening the view is always magic. If you visit this city you must come here. I love this ground very much. Every time I try to spend a few times here. || A very nice place for relaxing and baby playing. Thanks to Arreiro freguesias. :) || Great park! It has a playground. It also has some benchs and tables with chairs. Great to make a picnic. There is also a kiosk that you can get some drinks and food. At the end of the garden there is a big fountain. It is very pretty. It is also great for families since there is a playground for kids. During the summer there are a bunch of events happening here. || One of the best place in Lisbon. That you come during the day or evening the view is always magic. If you visit this city you must come here. || Beautiful big park. It has some food places around the area. In the park you can chill on the grass, walk up the old fortress like building and also enjoy the majestic huge fountain that lights up in the night. Eduardo VII Park is one of the most beautiful and relaxing green spaces in Lisbon. The park offers stunning panoramic views over the city and the Tagus River, making it a perfect spot for photos, walks, or simply enjoying the scenery. The wide paths are ideal for walking or jogging, and the well-maintained gardens add a peaceful atmosphere away from the busy city streets. One of the highlights is the impressive geometric garden design and the viewpoint at the top of the park, which provides a breathtaking perspective of Lisbon. The park is also very spacious, so it never feels overcrowded, even during busy hours. There are benches throughout the area, perfect for resting and enjoying the surroundings. Eduardo VII Park is great for families, couples, and solo travelers alike. It’s close to the city center and easy to access, making it a must-visit for anyone exploring Lisbon. Whether you’re looking for a quiet place to relax, take a walk, or admire the city from above, this park is definitely worth a visit. || We were in Lisbon for several days while waiting to start a cruise with NCL.  We stopped at the north end of this magnificent park and walk all the way to the southern end.  Lots of great views and spots for wonderful pics.  Several monuments along the way. || Parque Eduardo VII is a beautiful park with stunning views of the city and the river. It's beautifully maintained, with plenty of greenery and spacious walkways. It's a great place to escape the hustle and bustle of the city, take beautiful photos, and simply enjoy the atmosphere. A must-see if you're in Lisbon. || It's quite an amazing space. Whether it's chilling, or events, or testing your photographic prowess, it fits the bill. There are usually tourists and residents generally around, and it's more lively during celebrations like Christmas. || It's a very beautiful and large park, perfect for a peaceful walk surrounded by nature. The view from the top of the park is spectacular. Depending on the time of year, there may be more or fewer tourists. On a sunny day with good weather, it's well worth a visit. || A great view of Lisbon from here, you can see the whole layout and scale looking down towards the river. Relaxed and friendly atmosphere as you view the scenery and monuments. You also get an excellent view of the planes coming into Lisbon. || A beautiful public park in Lisbon, Portugal with great views over the city. The top is great for photos. Good for a walk, sit and have lunch or a drink, or have your dog play around. || Wonderful Christmas Atmosphere! We visited Parque Eduardo VII during the Christmas season, and it was a fantastic experience. The Christmas market (Wonderland Lisboa) created such a pleasant and fun atmosphere. It’s a great spot, especially for young people and families, with plenty of amusement park rides, games, and festive food stalls. The park itself is beautiful, and the view from the top is breathtaking. Highly recommended if you are in Lisbon during the holidays! || Parque Eduardo VII is one of the best spots in Lisbon to enjoy a peaceful walk and take in a great view of the city. From the top of the park, you can see all the way down to the river and the Praça Marquês de Pombal. It’s a lovely place to relax, especially at sunset. The park is also very close to El Corte Inglés, so it’s easy to combine a visit with some shopping or a coffee break nearby. || What a great parque / jardim in central Lisbon. Plenty of spaces to walk and sit with many great restaurants, cafes , and quiosques nearby to enjoy the warm Lisbon sun

4 star, because the japan garden is under conscruction (nobody work on, just closed and write, it's close). Nice, big green place on the city. Lot of peacock and duck. The walk forms a loop that goes downhill and then back up, so be prepared for a bit of a climb. The paths are a bit uneven and gravelly, so comfortable shoes are a good idea.  It’s also a nice place for birdwatching. We spotted a few parakeets and other birds flying around, which added to the charm.  You can use your Lisboa Card here for a small discount, and the same ticket also gives you access to the nearby museum, though that one was unfortunately quite disappointing.  Overall, it’s a relaxing and refreshing break from the noise of the city and a great place to enjoy nature for an hour or two. || We visited on a Sunday before 1pm and the entry was free. I kind of found it astonishing that there was not a gift shop or formal snack bar within the property.  There is a vendor that sells coffee and such on your way in. One of the most beautiful parks I've seen by far. It's full of nature and also some animals, mostly birds. The place is perfect for a weekend picnic, a chilly eventing, yoga, hangouts and more. Thank you Lisbon for this amazing green gem! || Stunning park in the heart of Lisbon. Absolutely stunning. Full of beautiful plants and flowers, ponds and statues. Benches everywhere and the wonderful Banana Cafe inside which sells burgers and sandwiches, drinks and other refreshments where you can dine alfresco || 🌿 A Peaceful Oasis in the Middle of Lisbon ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5) We stumbled upon Jardim da Estrela on a warm afternoon, and it turned out to be one of the most peaceful and refreshing places we visited in Lisbon. It’s more than just a public park — it feels like a little urban sanctuary. The garden is beautifully maintained, filled with exotic plants, huge trees offering generous shade, and winding paths that invite you to slow down. What really stood out for me was the birdsong — there were so many birds, and their constant, melodic chirping made the whole place feel like a live sound bath. It’s incredibly soothing. If you have the time, don’t just walk through. Find a quiet corner, sit down, breathe, and maybe even meditate. This place is perfect for that. It’s not just visually calming, it actually sounds calming too. There are also benches, fountains, a lovely gazebo, and a charming little café nearby if you want to sit and sip something while watching the world go by. Families, joggers, solo readers, and locals chatting on benches all seem to coexist naturally here. It has a very authentic Lisbon energy — not overly touristy, just real life unfolding in a gorgeous setting.  Quick Ratings: Atmosphere: 10/10 Birdsong & Nature Vibe: 10/10 Relaxation Potential: 11/10 Accessibility: 10/10 Instagram View: 8.5/10 Highly recommend making time for it — especially if you’re feeling overstimulated by the city. It’s the kind of place that quietly resets your mood.  If this helped, I’d love a 👍 — and don’t forget to breathe deeply when you visit. 🌿✨ || I recently spent a peaceful afternoon at Jardim da Estrela in Lisbon, and it quickly became one of my favorite spots in the city. Located directly across from the grand Basílica da Estrela, this romantic-style park was inaugurated in 1852 and offers a refreshing blend of history, nature, and community life. The park spans 4.6 hectares and features winding paths shaded by exotic trees like jacarandas and ginkgoes, as well as beautifully maintained flower beds and small lakes with ducks and turtles. One of the standout features is the wrought-iron bandstand, originally built in 1884 and relocated here in 1936, which adds a touch of old-world charm. Families and locals gather here, especially on weekends, to enjoy the playgrounds, picnic areas, and the café with outdoor seating that serves light meals and drinks. The park is free to enter and open daily from 7 am to midnight, making it an accessible and welcoming space for everyone. Whether you're looking to relax, take a leisurely stroll, or immerse yourself in a bit of Lisbon's history, Jardim da Estrela offers a serene and delightful escape from the city's hustle and bustle. || I have a 5 year old and a 2 year old. This is hands down my favorite park to take them to in Lisbon. Great playground. Lots of space to run. A cute little library with little tables the kids can draw and color at. Birds walking about. Cafes for a quick coffee or juice. Plus it’s super safe because it’s all gated. || Definitely one of the most loveliest gardens in Lisbon, if you come here for a few days, I would strongly recommend to see this place. Very cool for pet owners and children hence the park has playgrounds and a huge space  for dogs to enjoy. For the past several months, we have spent an hour here every afternoon, strolling and unwinding. Great for spending a few calm moments during sightseeing or for lunch break || Beautiful park with a wide variety of trees and different areas for either working out or doing a picnic, reading and relaxing. Quiet, peaceful, and with a lovely café that has plenty of tables where you can sit, have a bite, and rest. Surrounded by lots of greenery, it’s such a beautiful, relaxing park — right across from the basilica. Love it! || Im so happy I found this place! Beautiful trees, very dog and children friendly. Banana cafe serves great coffee and pastel da nata ❤️ || I feel so blessed and lucky to be a short walk from this beautiful oasis. The care and thoughtfulness the Portuguese put into public spaces with a care for community is beautiful to experience. || 2€ Banana Bread under quiet Palmtrees in the middle of a bustling Metropolis, what more can one wish for? Worth spending some time and walking when you are free.

reviews_content: The view is *gorgeous*, the drinks are that of a typical bar/pub, but the service can be awkward.
