On a nice day can see far away. || This turned out to be an unexpected city walk.This park is great for a stroll and offers views of much of the Lisbon! There are also orange trees and a small amusement area inside, and it might be even livelier if you come in the evening. || This is the largest park in Lisbon, named in honor of King Edward VII of the United Kingdom following his visit to Portugal in 1903. It features formal gardens, greenhouses, and wide open paths—making it ideal for walking, relaxing, or simply enjoying nature in the city. At the top of the park, a scenic viewpoint offers sweeping views over Lisbon and the Tagus River. The park is also home to the annual Lisbon Book Fair, one of the city’s most popular cultural events. || Super views over Lisbon. Good for a walk around if that’s what you want plus photos at the top of the park. Well looked after.

place_name: Parque Infantil da Praça José Fontana
reviews_content: This is a small playground with two areas: one for younger children and another for older kids. Unfortunately, there are not many suitable play options for toddlers, such as seesaws or swings. There are seating areas for parents, but the play areas have limited shade. The metal slide gets very hot due to direct sunlight all day. The ground is covered with small pebbles, which do a decent job of cushioning falls, but there is still a risk of scraped knees. There are no restrooms available, but there's a café right next door where you can grab drinks and snacks, which is a nice perk. || Great little park and playground. If you have kids and have to wait in the long queues in the nearby city administrative centre, then on a sunny day this is a glorious respite. The atmosphere is slightly cosmopolitan, which again is a pleasant change if you’ve just been dealing with all that bureaucracy has to offer. || Nice outdoor spot. Coffee shop in the middle of the park is convenient. Clean. Lots of places to sit on the park. || Great park for kids located right next to a bar. Win win! || Clean but a bit hard for very young children. No protection from the sun so can get very hot here at times. || Small playground with two play areas. One area is geared toward younger children, and the other toward older children. Unfortunately, there aren't any good play options for very young children. There are no seesaws or swings. There are seating areas for parents. There's little shade in the play areas. The metal slide gets very hot because it's in the sun all day. The ground is made of small pebbles. Overall, the ground cushions children's jumps well. However, there is still a risk of injury, such as scraped knees. Unfortunately, there are no restrooms. It's good that there's a café right next door, so you can stock up on drinks and snacks. || There are two play structures, one suitable for younger children and a second one with more difficulty. There are benches for parents, both inside and outside, and being next to the café is great for relaxing a bit while the children play. We loved it! || It's a nice park, but besides needing repairs, the kids from the school across from it are always there smoking things they shouldn't be smoking... || A nice, pleasant little green park as a refreshment in the surroundings of concrete buildings and busy streets. It has a nice little vaulted and elevated pavilion ideal for summer concerts, if they are held there, otherwise it would be a shame. || a small selection of attractions for children

The Fernando Pessoa Garden, located in the Areeiro district of Lisbon, is a tranquil green space dedicated to one of Portugal’s most celebrated literary figures. Nestled among the urban surroundings, the garden offers a peaceful retreat with neatly landscaped paths, benches, and shaded areas ideal for quiet reflection or reading. Named after the iconic poet and writer, the garden subtly pays homage to Pessoa’s legacy, often drawing locals and tourists alike who are seeking a moment of calm amid the city’s rhythm. Its central location in Areeiro makes it easily accessible, serving both as a community gathering spot and a small cultural landmark. || One of the best playgrounds that I have found so far in Lisbon in terms of amenities, shade, other kids to play with, and safety from streets. We go all of the time. || Nice park. Clean and green. Kid friendly playground. And there is also a football cage. || Very welcoming place. Pleasant. However, the playground only has attractions for children up to 3 or 4 years old. They should do something similar to the Campo Pequeno park, with a lot of variety for different age groups. || This garden, for the long-time residents, is the Roma garden. It was given the name Fernando Peça because he would occasionally go for a bike ride there early in the morning, even though he lived on a different block. || A well-kept garden near our house, where I often go with my grandchildren. It's a very beautiful space. || A beautiful garden, very well laid out, and with the advantage of being suitable for children, dogs, and people of all ages. || A very pleasant place to take children for a walk. place_name: SandCastle – Indoor Playground & Family Café with Nannies
reviews_content: Highly recommended! ❤️✨ The space is treated with so much love and care to all the details. We celebrate my sons  1 year there and we were not disappointed with anything. We rented a celebration room where the owner let us put all the decorations that we wanted, bring a cake and drinks, also  helped us with everything. Kids could explore and play in the kids space with very pleasant and attentive nany :) We passed fantastic time and I was more than happy with everything! Thanks a lot for best service, care and responsibility! 👏👏👏 || A great place for parents and kids! Here you can actually get some work done while your child has fun under supervision. The staff is attentive, the atmosphere is cozy, and the coffee with dessert is delicious. Happy to have it nearby :) || It was really nice experience today … since it was rainy morning we decide to come to this indoor play area … although we thought this place - around 60 m2 is maybe not big enough for my 3.7 years old son … but he absolutely loved it and played 2 hours non- stop and alone ! Give his parents some nice and quiet time at the coffee area … definitely recommend to visit for younger kids family. || My son loved his time in Sandcastle. Really cute environment, lots of fun&toys and super nice girls, both the nanny and the girl at the reception. I could enjoy my coffee quietly while he played. I didnt find any place like this in Lisbon so far. Highly recommended || We liked the space and our kids also had a lot of fun. The place has different types of toys for them to play and the nannies there were very nice and also attentive to the kids. We payed 15 euros for the first hour for 1 kid and the second had 50% of (that was e great surprise). || Outstanding place for families! One of the best places of indoor playgrounds I have ever visited. The owners are kind and caring. The place has plenty of toys and differentiated areas for playing. One of the owners takes constant and active care of the children which makes it perfect for the parents to enjoy nice and healthy food in the meantime. The specialty coffee and the tea quality makes you to enjoy it even more! Both owners are so carefully taking care to ensure we are were having a good time, parents and kids. || We went there on a rainy day after my toddler had skipped a nap, thinking we will spend maybe 30mins up to 1h playing. During the next 2h he had an amazing time running around and exploring the space. There’s a good variety of toys - from balls, blocks, balance play to sensory activities in a sandpit; nice stations for pretend play (tea party, grocery shop, kitchen, workshop) as well as a couple of seated areas for colouring and drawing. The space also has a cafe further down the hall past the rooms where they are planning on having baby/toddler classes. The bathrooms are clean and well equipped with a changing station, diapers and wet wipes. We will definitely return! || Nice place for kids, very tasty pancakes, friendly staff. animator was playing with the kids! Highly recommended. || My daughter loved the playground and the nanny Mathilde! She had so much fun. There is a great selection of toys to play with, a sandbox and a slide. I enjoyed tea and cheesecake while my daughter was playing, then joined her for a bit. We will be back soon! || This was the first time. The caregivers here are wonderful. Lots of toys to play with for littles and a sandpit. 13€ an hour is a bit on the pricey side and the food too. Would love it if there were more affordable options or more like a subscription that we could use for the play area. || My 4 y old daughter and I enjoyed it so much! Super cosy environment, a lot of different toys and activity corners for the kids. Tiny toddler toilets available which is super practical for my kid to go on her own when she needed (hygiene is impeccable). For 2 h we spent there, she played enthusiastically while I managed to work on my stuff in the backroom/workspace(which has a quiet atmosphere looking at the back patio). Coffee is super delicious, cheescake even better. I would only recommend maybe having also some salty pastry like quiche or croissants (which maybe they usually have, didn't ask). Will definitely return when I need to work on some work related tasks while my daughter is playing and enjoying her time. In the workspace,  which is right at the end of a corridor of the playground (and you can see and hear you kid playing) there is a big monitor with extra cameras showing you the playground from all different angles so you can keep an extra eye on your kid if you need/want to. But I was super relaxed as the kids that day were monitored and played with Joana. || Loved it there! Kids didn’t want to leave. Everyone is super nice inside. The nanny playing with the kids is amazing. Clean and cozy! Perfect spot! || We loved the experience so much! My daughter played for 3 hours and didn’t want to leave. While we had brunch and some relaxing time! || Would not be surviving toddlerhood without this place! It’s a lovely bright space that is ideal for rainy days and super hot days.. or just days you are lacking energy as their in house nannies are always happy to entertain the little ones! My daughter absolutely loves it and never gets bored. Thank you for offering this wonderful place, Sandcastle team!! || Great for kids and parents alike 😍 had a great time and will make sure to return, my only issue was that the food was a bit pricey, but otherwise everything and everyone was absolutely perfect, will be returning soon and often 🥰 || Super nice place to spend your time working while your child plays in a safe and cute playground with caring personnel. Highly recommend and will definitely visit this place again ❤️ || My son and I love this place. We are in Lisbon for a month and have gone multiple times. Clean, friendly, great coffee and cheesecake! Recommend to anyone with little ones in Lisbon! || Fantastic space for working parents! The café is modern and comfortable, with great coffee and fast WiFi. The supervised playground and caring childminder kept my child happy and safe while I worked. Price is fair if you think the convenience and peace of mind are absolutely worth it. Highly recommended! Hope this concecp expands! || Lovely place to take your small one to play while you can enjoy some coffee. The  nanny was great, and took the time to let our kid get comfortable playing with her. The location is good and we went for a nice lunch just around the corner. We will definitely come back! ☺️ || Highly recommended! We came here in the afternoon with my son 4 yo. I stayed with him for some time and then went out for about an hour. And thanks to the nanny Mathilde who was able to find an approach to my child, he had a great time and didn't want to leave when I came back. He really loved the playground and we plan to be back soon!

place_name: Parque Infantil do Jardim Teófilo Braga
reviews_content: Better than the Principe Real playground but not impressive. Would not go out of my way for it. || Horror! The children are screaming at midnight. Not only do the parents allow their children to behave like this, but they also don't care that they are disturbing the sleep of a local resident. Total disrespect for others! || Dear visitors to the playground, why do your children scream so loudly in it after 11 PM? Especially teenagers who are left unsupervised. Please respect the right of local residents to peace and sleep! Remember, there is a law in Portugal that prohibits leaving children unsupervised. || Cool, cozy, small. There is a cafe, a swimming pool with animals and everything for relaxing with children. || Always a place to charge batteries.

Although it's small, this place is a lot of fun, especially with tables and chairs, so adults can sit and rest too. || A fun park that is a great stop for letting the kids play before/after some shopping or a meal in the nearby Largo da Graça.  The fence/gate makes it a very safe play space and for a small playground it has a lot of variety in the play equipment.  The only downside is that in the heat of the day there is not much shade. || This is one of the few playgrounds in Lisbon that is good for younger kids (1-2 year old) as well as bigger kids. My daughter likes it. Nice park || You can do better than this || I liked it so much that I'm going to live in this area.

A beautiful park where you can spend a few hours. It has a path that goes around it and which I recommend to walk. Beautiful trees and ponds ideal for a pause after a busy day. There's a café which is usually busy and a table is hard to find. On Sundays there's a small marketplace and so you can encounter locals mixed up with tourists. Just across the street you'll find the admirable Basílica da Estrela which is worth the visit. || I met some friends at Jardim da Estrela and it was a very nice experience. The park has lots of trees and open space, so it felt calm and relaxing. We enjoyed walking and sitting by the small lake together. || This is a gorgeous park — perfect for people-watching or for families with kids who just want to escape the hustle and bustle of Lisbon. It’s a peaceful spot to unwind and enjoy a slower pace in the middle of the city, and it even has restrooms (although I wouldn't call them clean but they were free), which is always a plus when exploring! || This place is heaven! One of the most beautiful parks I've seen by far. It's full of nature and also some animals, mostly birds. The place is perfect for a weekend picnic, a chilly eventing, yoga, hangouts and more. Thank you Lisbon for this amazing green gem! || Stunning park in the heart of Lisbon. Absolutely stunning. Full of beautiful plants and flowers, ponds and statues. Benches everywhere and the wonderful Banana Cafe inside which sells burgers and sandwiches, drinks and other refreshments where you can dine alfresco || 🌿 A Peaceful Oasis in the Middle of Lisbon ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (5/5) We stumbled upon Jardim da Estrela on a warm afternoon, and it turned out to be one of the most peaceful and refreshing places we visited in Lisbon. It’s more than just a public park — it feels like a little urban sanctuary. The garden is beautifully maintained, filled with exotic plants, huge trees offering generous shade, and winding paths that invite you to slow down. What really stood out for me was the birdsong — there were so many birds, and their constant, melodic chirping made the whole place feel like a live sound bath. It’s incredibly soothing. If you have the time, don’t just walk through. Find a quiet corner, sit down, breathe, and maybe even meditate. This place is perfect for that. It’s not just visually calming, it actually sounds calming too. There are also benches, fountains, a lovely gazebo, and a charming little café nearby if you want to sit and sip something while watching the world go by. Families, joggers, solo readers, and locals chatting on benches all seem to coexist naturally here. It has a very authentic Lisbon energy — not overly touristy, just real life unfolding in a gorgeous setting.  Quick Ratings: Atmosphere: 10/10 Birdsong & Nature Vibe: 10/10 Relaxation Potential: 11/10 Accessibility: 10/10 Instagram View: 8.5/10 Highly recommend making time for it — especially if you’re feeling overstimulated by the city. It’s the kind of place that quietly resets your mood.  If this helped, I’d love a 👍 — and don’t forget to breathe deeply when you visit. 🌿✨ || I recently spent a peaceful afternoon at Jardim da Estrela in Lisbon, and it quickly became one of my favorite spots in the city. Located directly across from the grand Basílica da Estrela, this romantic-style park was inaugurated in 1852 and offers a refreshing blend of history, nature, and community life. The park spans 4.6 hectares and features winding paths shaded by exotic trees like jacarandas and ginkgoes, as well as beautifully maintained flower beds and small lakes with ducks and turtles. One of the standout features is the wrought-iron bandstand, originally built in 1884 and relocated here in 1936, which adds a touch of old-world charm. Families and locals gather here, especially on weekends, to enjoy the playgrounds, picnic areas, and the café with outdoor seating that serves light meals and drinks. The park is free to enter and open daily from 7 am to midnight, making it an accessible and welcoming space for everyone. Whether you're looking to relax, take a leisurely stroll, or immerse yourself in a bit of Lisbon's history, Jardim da Estrela offers a serene and delightful escape from the city's hustle and bustle. || I have a 5 year old and a 2 year old. This is hands down my favorite park to take them to in Lisbon. Great playground. Lots of space to run. A cute little library with little tables the kids can draw and color at. Birds walking about. Cafes for a quick coffee or juice. Plus it’s super safe because it’s all gated. || Definitely one of the most loveliest gardens in Lisbon, if you come here for a few days, I would strongly recommend to see this place. Very cool for pet owners and children hence the park has playgrounds and a huge space  for dogs to enjoy. Also, it’s a very good place just to meet and chill or enjoy your day in serenity. || A beautiful park with ancient trees. Ideal for sitting in peace.

Wow. 🤯 this Bar is AN EXPERIENCE! It felt like walking into an escape room themed around the 1920s–1930s (the kind that completely pulls you into its story and atmosphere).The effort put into the design and decoration is unmatched! (You can even catch little sneak peeks of the Halloween elements, so perfectly blended into the space.)  The service was personal and respectful. I wanted a Sex on the Beach, but they didn’t have the ingredients, so I asked to be surprised with something similar and it turned out quite yummy.  Music is always important for me when choosing places, and when we were there, they were playing relaxing sort of jazz, super chill and perfectly fitting for the luxurious, slightly historical vibe.  The cocktails were around €13 each, if I’m not mistaken (not cheap, but not too expensive either). Honestly, I didn’t mind paying that, because it felt like I was paying for the experience as much as the drinks.  Really recommended if this is the vibe you’re looking for it nails it perfectly! || Atmosphere: 8.5/10 The Royal Vessel Bar blends a cozy restaurant-style atmosphere with subtle ship and pirate-inspired design touches. Music is at a good level, the backbar stands out as the focal point, and seating is well arranged with both bar counter spots and group tables.  Drinks: 8/10 Recommendation: Iberica The menu comes in a red book-style format—simple, but stylish. Selection is small, yet the cocktails are well-executed with good flavor balance. Glassware is above average, though presentation overall remains basic with no garnish and no coasters.  Service: 6.5/10 Water isn’t served on arrival. The team is friendly and professional, but attentiveness leaves room for improvement. Reservations aren’t needed. Prices lean slightly above average for Lisbon. || I celebrated my birthday at this bar, and it was absolutely amazing! The atmosphere is incredible - cozy and stylish, with dim lighting that creates the perfect mood for a relaxed evening.  The cocktails are top-notch 🔥 creative, well-balanced, and beautifully presented. I was especially impressed by the wide selection of not only cocktails but also mocktails. the non-alcoholic options are just as flavorful and thoughtfully crafted.  There are also some light snacks available, which pair nicely with the drinks. I’ll definitely be coming back, this place is perfect both for special occasions and a chill night out with friends. || The best non-alcoholic cocktails in Lisbon. I fully recommend to try Virgin porn star and Saint margarita. The bartender was very kind and attentive. I will definitely come back to try the other cocktails || Beautiful, atmospheric bar with décor that feels straight out of a Fitzgerald novel. The Mist of Sintra was fresh and tasty, but the Silk Road was my favorite! || It’s a very classy bar with beautiful authentic interior. Small, but very very cozy. Cocktails were great and the bartenders were friendly, funny and professional. They almost don’t have classic cocktails on the menu but they are happy to make ones if you ask. I loved the atmosphere of the bar and I am definitely going to return! || We had such a great time at the bar, huge thanks to Zhenya from Uzbekistan! He made the evening unforgettable. Every cocktail he suggested was perfect for each of us, like he instantly knew what everyone would love. We ended up chatting in Portuguese, English, Russian, and Ukrainian, it was such a fun mix and the vibe was amazing.  Zhenya even made me a special cocktail, not from the menu, just based on my preferences, and it turned out incredible. 🍸 Definitely one of the bars, we'll come back to and recommend to our friends! || Super sad I discovered it one day before leaving… it is a must! Just share what you want, the atmosphere is beautiful and the cocktails are amazing! Thank you! || I had a fantastic experience at The Royal Vessel Bar. Not only are the cocktails genuinely amazing, but the staff were absolute stars. There was a girl who was clearly very drunk and being bothered by a creepy guy who wouldn’t leave her alone. As soon as the team realised what was happening, they stepped in straight away and were exceptional — calm, professional, and completely on it.  They handled everything with real care and escalated it to the authorities in exactly the right way. I’d gone over to check on her too, and the staff even thanked me and gave me a drink for helping. Honestly, such a brilliant bar on every front — fantastic drinks, great atmosphere, and a team who genuinely look out for their guests. Couldn’t recommend it more. Five stars. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ || Great cocktail card and lovely staff, the best atmosphere. Besides ordering things from the menu, you can also ask to make a custom cocktail to your liking. One of my favorite places in Lisbon.

We had lunch at a restaurant with a beautiful view and a great location. The food was really delicious, and the dessert was just amazing. BUT!!! The white wine was awful — it was literally the cheapest supermarket wine, yet they charged €10 per glass.  Overall though, it’s a great spot for tourists. The staff were courteous, polite, and very pleasant. All in all, I’d recommend it — a great and tasty experience! ❤️ || Only came for drinks but had food as well, glad we did. Amazing view with good food and drinks, can’t beat it. Highlight of my holiday. || Fancy place, high level of service. .Good athmosphere Not a big choice of food, but sushi the i take was amazing. The prices are more then average at Lisbon. || The views here are stunning! Great drinks and food, the staff is wonderful. Highly recommend if you want a great rooftop bar experience in Lisbon. || Francisco made my stay very special with his attentiveness and kindness. I’m grateful he went out of his way to take care of me. He also gave me a wonderful recommendations for my solo trip, which I’m so grateful for. I cannot rave enough about this beautiful human being. 🥹 Amy was also great with her check-ins as my server. Service here is top notch…  …give my man a raise, please…!  View here is beautiful and memorable, music and vibes are very relaxed, and food is sure to be a hit given the way people are ordering and how things look. Happy I stopped by here per the recommendation of a local. || Seen - A Beautiful Rooftop Bar & Restaurant  Discover Seen, a stunning rooftop destination offering breathtaking views and a relaxed yet sophisticated ambiance. Whether you choose to dine indoors or outside under the stars, you'll enjoy an unforgettable experience. Savor delicious, expertly crafted dishes paired with refreshing drinks while taking in the scenic vistas. Perfect for a casual evening, special occasions, or simply unwinding in style.  Highlights: Spectacular rooftop views Stylish indoor and outdoor seating Cozy, inviting ambiance Delicious food and signature cocktails  Come and see why Seen is the perfect spot to elevate your dining experience! || Seen Sky Bar offers stunning views from its rooftop restaurant and bar. If you don’t have a reservation, you won’t be able to sit outside, but we were seated indoors and could still step outside to snap a few photos. I had the beef carpaccio, which was excellent, and my drink—a vodka-based cocktail called Suka—was very good. My girlfriend had the do-it-yourself ice cream sundae, which she just thought was the best thing in the world. From the rooftop, you can see the castle and even a glimpse of the river. It is on the pricier side, and the service was a little slow, but overall it was a very nice experience. || A luxury experience done right — warm, welcoming, and unforgettable  As tourists, we sometimes look for the best spots around town and, admittedly, might overlook certain dress protocols—not out of disrespect, but simply in the spirit of exploring and enjoying our time. That’s what happened when we were turned away at Praia no Parque due to my partner’s dress shorts, despite them being clean and tailored. The interaction there was cold and dismissive.  We then went to Seen by Olivier, which also has a dress code—but what a difference. The staff welcomed us gracefully and with genuine hospitality, making us feel respected rather than judged.  We had four exquisite cocktails, fresh oysters, ceviche tacos, and a beautifully plated dessert. Everything was exceptional—flavorful, refined, and worth every cent. The service was attentive without being overbearing, and the scenic rooftop view over Lisbon made the experience even more memorable.  In total, we spent around €150 and left feeling truly satisfied—not just by the food, but by the atmosphere and the way we were treated.  Seen by Olivier is the standard of elegance and warmth that every upscale restaurant should strive for. || Upscale bar but a great view and atmosphere. Even in the cold weather the heater were actually warm! Drinks were a bit pricey but from the moment you walk in you can tell this place requires a bigger budget. Overall a great experience. || Lovely evening drinking wine and watching the sun go.down. well it went down behind one of the many hills but the light over the city was spectacular. We also had two lunches in the restaurant and the food was delicious.

We love trying cocktail rooms wherever we go, tried this one and it REALLY hit the spot. Best owners, very kind, great vibes - extremely relaxed. The drinks were solid - will hold their own against any cocktail room anywhere. We had the smoky margarita, negroni, a Caribbean inspired drink (forgot the name) and the Black Forest.  Shout out to the Black Forest, that was one VERY well made drink! Completely recommend. Host made us taste her favorite drink - I think it was called the Nikkei Milk Punch and I must say that one was extremely well balanced and beautiful as well.  Best part of the space for us were all the 🐶s visiting, completely made our evening! || Atmosphere: 8/10 Located in Lisbon’s Graça district. Very chill, home-style vibe—cozy, comfortable, music at a good level. Backbar is okay. Seating is limited: no bar counter, a few indoor tables, plus some patio seats.  Drinks: 8.5/10 Recommendation: Black Forrest, Pineapple Express Menu is simple. Selection is decent. Flavors are good. Coasters are nice; glassware is average; garnish is nice. Presentation is okay overall, with unique ice on select serves.  Service: 8.5/10 Water on arrival. Team is friendly, professional, and attentive. Prices are average for Lisbon. Reservations not needed. || Proper crafted cocktails in a small, cozy and we'll appointed space. Joanna and Peter create lovely drinks and provide personal service. I had a lovely milk punch which was perfectly balanced.  Its a good idea to make reservations. We will definitely go again. || Booked Onda to grab a quick pre-dinner drink and we ended up going a bit early and I’m so happy we did!  We got to try four different cocktails and they were so good and so creative! The space was also really cool - loved the decor and the owners were really sweet. || Had an amazing time here and really enjoyed getting to know the owners and hearing their stories and recommendations.  We loved it so much we closed out both of our nights in Lisbon here.  If you are looking for a great cocktail and a relaxing chill atmosphere this is the place to go! || This was hands-down our favorite cocktail bar in the city. It’s a laid back atmosphere where the husband/wife owners attend to the customers with passion and dedication. It’s clear that they love what they do. In my opinion, this establishment is better than Red Frog. The Nikkei Milk Punch was my favorite. You won’t find anything like it elsewhere; it’s one-of-a-kind. Don’t pass up the opportunity to visit, but do make a reservation. || What do you know about cocktails? 🍸✨ Forget everything you think you know! 😎 Because here, a whole new world will open up to you — a world of amazing flavors, aromas, adventures, and people who are truly in love with what they do! 💫🌍💃  Every sip is a little journey 🌴🍹 — through taste, through passion, through creativity! 💥 Whether you’re into something classic, bold, or totally unexpected, they’ll create the perfect cocktail just for you! 🍒🍍🍋  This place isn’t just about drinks — it’s about emotions, art, and pure joy! 💖✨ So dive in, explore, and let yourself be amazed by this ocean of cocktails! 🌊🍸🔥  Cheers to unforgettable moments! 🥂😄🍹 || Thank you so much for your visit and review. We hope you can come by this week for the tasting experience before you go home. 🍸🍸🍸 … || I’ve gone to Onda multiple times, and have always had a nice time.  I lived here as a student (American so do take that into account with my opinions on prices) for about a year and visited multiple times throughout my stay. A few times I went for drinks (sometimes alcoholic and sometimes not, they have amazing options for both) and once for a cocktail making class which was a super fun experience!  It’s a place to go if you want nice cocktails. They’re well made and super unique, so though they aren’t the cheapest, the prices  are by no means unreasonable and are on par with a lot of other places I’ve been to. I loved the smoky margarita, as well as the Thai infused alcohol (I don’t remember the name) which was one of the best cocktails I’ve had.  Would recommend and planning on going again soon as I’m visiting for the holidays! || I can't speak too much to the food but I can speak to the lovely couple who own the place and took us on a journey of many cocktails. Easily a true highlight of Lisbon and something I would recommend anyone who enjoys the finer spirits and what magic they might contain. Do yourself a favor take a friend or six to the cocktail flight, and if you enjoy whiskey talk to Peter the owner into giving you a master class in Whiskeys around the world. || Drinks are crafted with perfection. Flavor explosion balanced with eased shoulders. Cheers for the memorable experience.

All of them were honestly great , but if you’d like some ideas, here’s my review of the ones suggested by the barman: - o.f.martini - my favourite; sweat and sour at the same time, perfect taste, served with gummies, 10/10 - old fashioned Portuguese - stronger taste but not overwhelming, definetly try if you’re into “bolder” flavors, - rooibos spritz - if you’re not a fan of aperol spritz like me then this is the perfect alternative, fruity , fresh, not too intense, really liked it  To make it better, the DJ had the perfect set for the occasion, chilled but you could move a little to it if you’d like, and the ambience just feels welcoming overall.  We’ll definitely come back!!  🥰 || Loved the pictures! Thank you so much || I absolutely love this bar! I have been in the city for a while now and this is one of the coolest bars in town. Great environment, spacious, beautiful drinks, easy access and good music. The cocktails are tasty, creative and fun! || Thank you Rafaela! It's an honor || Cabal Cocktail Bar is one of those places that quietly exceeds every expectation. From the moment you walk in, you can tell this isn’t your average cocktail spot — it’s got that perfect blend of sophistication and comfort. The lighting is warm and atmospheric, the music hits that sweet spot where you can still hold a conversation, and the staff immediately make you feel welcome without being intrusive.  The cocktail menu is outstanding — creative without being pretentious. Every drink feels carefully balanced and thoughtfully crafted. I had the whiskey sour. My friend tried the Hugo, and it was easily one of the best floral cocktails I’ve ever tasted (and I’ve tried a lot!). You can tell the bartenders here are true mixologists who take pride in what they do.  What really stood out, though, was the service. Our bartender took time to ask about our flavor preferences and then offered a few off-menu recommendations that were spot on. It felt personal and genuine, not rehearsed. Even when the bar got busy later in the evening, the team stayed attentive and upbeat — you could feel that they actually enjoy what they do.  The ambiance also deserves a mention: stylish decor, a bit of a speakeasy vibe, and a nice mix of people — perfect for date nights, small groups, or anyone who appreciates a good drink in a relaxed setting.  Prices are fair for the quality you get, and honestly, I’d come back just for the experience. If you’re into crafted cocktails, great energy, and a place that treats its guests like regulars from the first visit — Cabal is absolutely worth it. || Wow Dorian, you basically wrote a book here. The Coffee Negroni was a real surprise for me – I had never tried anything like this before, and it quickly became my favorite of the night. You should try!! The artifacts in the treasure room are beautifully detailed and very well preserved. From there, you can access the interior balcony, which offers a great view of the main church below and a close look at the stunning stained glass centerpiece. There’s also a small passage leading to an exterior balcony overlooking the front of the cathedral, though it’s quite narrow and can get crowded. It’s a tight squeeze, one-way, and very high up, so just take care if you’re not great with heights.  The main cathedral itself is massive, with chapels dedicated to different saints along the back. place_name: Church of Saint John of God
reviews_content: In the heart of Lisbon, amidst its bustling streets and vibrant culture, lies a sanctuary of serenity and architectural splendour: the Church of Saint John of God (Igreja de São João de Deus). This edifice is not merely a structure; it is a testament to the intertwining of faith, art, and the human condition.  Historical Backdrop  The Church of Saint John of God was erected in the mid-20th century, a period marked by profound social and political changes in Portugal. The architect, responsible for translating faith into concrete and glass, envisioned a space that would reflect the modernist ethos of the era while paying homage to the timeless tenets of spirituality and community. In this endeavour, the church stands as a beacon of modernist architectural principles, eschewing the ornate for the sublime simplicity.  Architectural Marvel  From the outside, the church’s façade may strike one as unassumingly modern, yet it is within its walls that the true grandeur unfolds. The design eschews the traditional Gothic or Baroque styles predominant in Lisbon’s older churches, opting instead for clean lines and an open, airy interior that invites light to dance upon its surfaces. This choice of design creates an atmosphere of tranquillity, a stark contrast to the city’s frenetic pace.  A Sanctuary of Peace  It was on a day, burdened with the weight of personal tribulations, that I found myself drawn to this church’s welcoming embrace. Crossing its threshold, I was immediately enveloped in a calm that seemed almost tangible. The interior, with its subtle play of light and shadow, offered a profound sense of peace and a momentary respite from life’s challenges. It was here, in this unexpected haven, that I found a space for reflection and solace.  Artistic and Spiritual Resonance  The Church of Saint John of God is also a repository of modern sacred art, from its stained glass to the minimalist altar, each piece contributes to a narrative of faith expressed through contemporary aesthetics. This fusion of modern art within a sacred space underscores the church’s role as a bridge between the divine and the everyday, inviting all who enter to find their own meaning within its walls.  Why Visit?  For travellers and explorers of Lisbon’s rich tapestry, the Church of Saint John of God offers a unique detour from the well-trodden path. Here, one can experience the quietude of modernist architecture, contemplate art imbued with spiritual significance, and perhaps find a moment of personal peace. It is a reminder that amidst the rush of modern life, there are spaces designed to soothe the soul and stir the heart.  An Invitation  This church, with its modernist charm and quiet dignity, stands as an open invitation to those traversing Lisbon’s historic streets. Whether you seek solace, an appreciation of modern sacred art, or simply a quiet moment of beauty, the Church of Saint John of God awaits. In my own journey, it offered a sanctuary at a moment of need, and for that, it will always hold a special place in my heart.  In conclusion, the Church of Saint John of God is more than just a point of interest in Lisbon; it is a landmark of faith, art, and the enduring human spirit. || Lovely architecture with a modern and up market touch. The pipe organ makes beautiful sound waves through the old Church walls. Today (Sept. 28, 2025) was the Gospel of the rich man and the poor Lazarus (Luke 16:19-31). The priest delivered a beautiful sermon, balanced between the aspects of social obligations for the rich and wealthy people, and the moral implications for everyone to look around and identify the poor at the gates of their comfort zones, summarizing the message in the line that "often, wealth makes blind." Right in the midst of downtown Lisbon, this is a pearl of a monument since the 13th century and a place where we breathe already a bit of eternal peace if we are able to listen the old stones of the walls and floor, the gospel messages, as well as our own consciences in the hectic of the modern world of social responsibilities towards the poor. || Igreja De S Domingos is a beautiful and peaceful church, I visited when Mass was going on, on Easter Sunday. It was completely full! Unfortunately I had an appointment so could not stay, and because it was Mass, I could not go all around the interior as I wished. || Visited the Church of Saint Dominic and was really struck by its burned and worn interior. The atmosphere is intense and dramatic, giving a unique glimpse into its history. Definitely one of the most memorable churches I’ve seen in Lisbon || One of the most stunning churches that one can visit in Lisbon. This church was affected a very big earthquake a few centuries ago, and a fire relatively recently. The renovation and maintenance of some of the remaining seem quite impressive. A must-visit place. || Very cool, great history, worth going out of the way for because it is one of the most beautiful churches I've ever been in, the charred stone gives a sense of power greater than any church adorned with art and gilded intricacies || We were amazed by this place! I think that this is the most beuatiful church I’ve ever seen! || Awe-inspiring church, with fascinating story behind it because of various calamities. Check the blackened walls /columns caused by the fire and how a great part of the church was rebuilt after its destruction. Read the tableaux just before the exit where you can read part of its history. You can visit for free but you can donate some money for its preservation. || Please take your time to visit this church and understand it and the small square it stands on story. Outside the church is a memorial and a reminder to a darker side of history and religious persecution. The story is that after the church was severely damaged by fire in 1959 they did not restore it as part of the tribute to its earlier darker past. A very sombre and moving place that is worth a few minutes silence and contemplation. || If you can stomach fighting your way past the many beggars and undesirables that hang around the outside of this building it is well worth a visit . The church itself has survived at least two earthquakes and a devastating fire which the scars can still be seen etched into its internal walls . You are asked not to film inside but hey …. You only live once || This church is one of a kind. It has been barely left standing after the 1531 earthquake, the 1755 Lisbon earthquake and a major fire on August 13, 1959. You can still see the damage left after the fire on the walls and columns. It only reopened in 1994 after so much renovation work was done. It is kind of cool to see how they left the scars of the fire and it adds to the atmosphere of the church.  The church has had a long and mixed history. Obviously there were the terrible natural disasters that occured. On the other hand royal weddings of the Portuguese monarchy were once held here. One other lamentable event was the massacre of Jews, including Jewish concerts to Christianity, that was triggered by an incident at mass in 1506.  Follow here and the IG link in profile for more travel and food and drink tips, ideas and reviews! || Church of Saint Dominic, located next to Praça Dom Pedro IV, which was once one of the most important squares of the city, is one of the important structures in the history of Lisbon, although it seems like a church that only attracts tourists today.  Built in the 13th century, this church was for a long time the largest church in Lisbon and witnessed many events such as the Lisbon massacre and the execution of Gabriel Malagrida. In the Great Lisbon Earthquake of 1755, only the sacristy and altar survived from the church. The rebuilding of the church took more than 50 years.  Maintaining its importance until the 20th century, the church hosted Portuguese royal weddings. It had partially lost its importance with the establishment of the Portuguese Republic. In a fire in 1959, many artifacts were destroyed and the building fell into disrepair. Although the church was reopened in 1994 after the restoration, it is possible to see the traces of the fire on the walls.  The magnificence of the building, the real traces of the fire on the walls and the choice of textures on the places painted in the restoration added a unique atmosphere to the church. From the first moment you enter, you feel like you are in a place that has seen great pain. I recommend it as a structure that should be visited in Lisbon and its history should be studied together with the surrounding region. || Beautiful church, with the particularity of preserving, with minimal concealment, the damage its marbles suffered from a fire in 1959. Its evading architectural and statuary forms provide an added layer of spatial experience and of meaning to the church.  The church suffered several episodes of destruction, having to be rebuilt (and enlarged in the process), in the earthquake of the 16c and another in the 18c. The present form shows traces of late barroque, having had contributions by the architect of the palace of Mafra. By then it was in this church that several national and royal events took place, given its size, faust and centrality. All this magnificence was lost in the fire of 1959. || The church was absolutely beautiful! But I had such a strange encounter with the men selling candles inside. I went to the candle stand to purchase two candles, which were 50 cents each in Euros. I kindly told the man, “I’m sorry, I don’t have 50 cents in Euros, but I can give you a $10 bill for the two candles and the rest can be a donation to the church.” To my surprise, he seemed bothered that I didn’t have Euros and flatly said no! This really disheartened me—especially because I was trying to give more as a donation. And trust me, he spoke perfect English! I left feeling both hurt and annoyed. || Remarkable grand 13th century church that’s still standing and intact after a major earthquake over the centuries, and in more recent times, the fire of 1959. Despite it all, the exposure of the existing resilient pillars and refurbished roof give it an immense sense of grandeur and awe.  We sat and attended mass at 6pm one night. We felt blessed to be there. || I love this old church because it is very different from those I saw. It is simple, natural and has traces of the damages from fire and earth quake. I also like those tall stone columns which makes the  church looks very strong. I strongly recommend it.

place_name: Church Nossa Senhora da Conceição Velha
reviews_content: A truly beautiful church tucked away on a quiet side street, yet just a short walk from Praça do Comércio. Nossa Senhora da Conceição has been masterfully renovated. The entrance features wonderful carvings that immediately draw you in, and once inside, you’re greeted by a stunning stucco-decorated ceiling that takes your breath away. A hidden gem worth discovering when exploring the city! || We were in Lisbon na at our cruise for 6 days. Walking back to our ship one day we found this old church which had to be restored after a large fire.  It is quiet and peaceful so stop and say a prayer for the poor people of the world while you rest your feet.  Not too much to see as compared to the larger churches around town. Still, it is very nice and worth a visit. || The Igreja da Conceição Velha has one of the most beautiful examples of Manueline architecture in Portugal. I believe the original interior of the church was destroyed during the Great Earthquake of Lisbon. Even so, admiring its façade alone makes the visit worthwhile. Pay special attention to the intricate carvings on the main doorway — they are truly remarkable. || A beautiful and peaceful church with elegant architecture and a calming atmosphere.  The interior is simple yet charming, offering a quiet break from the busy streets.  A lovely spot to pause and appreciate Lisbon’s history and spiritual charm. || Please visit this beautiful church, especially go the Holy Mass if you are a traditional catholic because the Masses are in Latin. Be aware that the information about the Mass at church is wrong. Just check on the internet. Sundays and holy days of obligation  - 10AM and 6PM,  Tuesdays till Fridays  - 7 p.m. and Saturdays  - 10:30 am. || One of the facades to survive the All Saints Day earth quake of 1755 and the following tsunami; certainly worth a quick stop or, at the very least, a quick walk by. || Tucked away in Lisbon’s Baixa district, the Church of Nossa Senhora da Conceição Velha stuns with its richly carved Manueline façade — a survivor of the 1755 earthquake. Step inside to discover peaceful interiors, gothic arches, and echoes of Portugal’s maritime past in every stone. || Mass is at 10 am on Sundays in a beautiful old church A very interesting mass, very beautiful, but no interaction with the congregation at all. It was almost like watching a play! || Didn’t actually go inside but the architecture outside is a sight worth seeing . || This is truly a magnificent religious space. The Facade could keep you enthralled for a while, and the inside will astound with its very high, ornate ceiling. It was a privilege to look inside || The exterior looks promising, welcoming you to its historical inside warmly.  The Church of Nossa Senhora da Conceição is a church in the civil parish of Madalena, in the municipality of Lisbon. The Church of Conceição dos Freires, or Conceição Velha, was not included in the original plans to reconstruct the Lisbon riverfront, even though it was partially ruined. It was opened in 1834, with a height of 17m. || Nice facade. Humble and not overly complicated on the inside. Only a few minutes walk from the Commerce Plaza. || Beautiful and detailed  architecture on the outside.  The inside has a beautiful roof mural. || Very nice facade from 16th century that survived the earthquake with restored interior in late baroque style. || It is a place where you can find the Manueline style in Baixa. If you don’t have time to go all the way to Belem, check out this place instead not to miss out the unique architecture in the Era of Discovery. || A great place to reverently worship God in accordance with His Will. || I liked this old church, looks a bit Gothic from outside and more traditional inside. The architecture is beautiful. || Recently reopened for visits. Compared to striking outside, inside a little disapointing, but still not to be missed || Very nice church, with beautiful facade. Short walk east of the Praça do Comércio. || the interior may not be of particular interest, but the facade is certainly impressive

place_name: Church of Our Lady of Grace
reviews_content: One of the oldest churches in the city, its origins date back to 1271. It was dedicated to a statue of the Virgin Mary miraculously recovered off the coast of Cascais (Portugal, a land of miracles...). Before our eyes unfolds a compendium of Portuguese Baroque religious art: gilded wood, exquisite azulejos (tiles) dating from the 16th, 17th, and 18th centuries, and striking sculptural and trompe-l'œil effects. However, it was damaged, along with the convent, during the 1755 earthquake and subsequently rebuilt. || We visited the church during Christmas holidays. The church is great and tells a lot about Lisbon history. On top, there was a beautiful Christmas crib. Before leaving the church, take time to contemplate one of the most beautiful panorama of the city || Highly recommended. Fantastic view of the city. And the feelings... Sombody play the music in the park behind the temple || We stumbled across this church while strolling around the hills of Lisbon. It’s a little gem with its azulejos and gilded altars,  But the terrace was even better. Breathtaking. No crowds, lots of places to sit, and not overrun with tourists, at least when we were there. || Dear David, we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience. Thank you for your kind comment. It's very important to us. || Beautiful Catholic Church with lots of chandeliers statues, lovely painted ceilings. There is also a plaza out front with beautiful views of the city, places to sit and meet and enjoy a leisurely afternoon. || An amazing and somewhat unexpected stop while touring Lisbon. Beautiful architecture of the church, located on one of the most beautiful viewpoints of the city. Completely unexpected was the offer for 6 EUR per person to tour the gallery of sacred paintings with entrance to the roof/route of the church with a drink. The most beautiful experience in Lisbon, when with a glass of port wine you enjoy panoramic views of the city from the roof terrace, where there are nice and comfortable seating. Pleasant peace (only the sound of bells from the church bell towers) from the hustle and bustle on the viewpoint in front of the church and without crowds of tourists or sellers of various trinkets. || Beautiful medieval former monastery with a church. Really worth walking all the way up to sit with a drink on a rooftop terraceswith stunning panoramic views all over the city. The building itself is very atmospheric and definitely worth coming inside and exploring. || Dear Grzegorz, thank you for your kind comment. We're glad you enjoyed your visit to our viewpoint. || A perfect stop on any tour of Lisbon: beautiful architecture and artworks, a serene church and one of the best views of the city. Small fee for entrance gets you access to all areas, including the rooftop view point where your ticket gets you a complimentary drink to enjoy whilst on the terrace. || Dear Greg, we are delighted that you enjoyed the experience. Thank you for your kind comment. || This convent is a hidden gem in Lisbon! The church and museum-style setting are beautiful, and the rooftop offers some of the best views in the city. The $5 cover is well worth it, especially since it includes a glass of wine or another beverage. I visited in the middle of the day and had the rooftop almost entirely to myself, making for a peaceful and memorable experience. Highly recommend! || dear Megan, we're delighted that you enjoyed the experience. Our viewpoint really is a hidden gem. Thank you. || Gorgeous church next to one of the most popular viewpoints in Lisbon. If you follow the exit, you can also enter monastery-looking courtyard, and then, a long hall of azulejos will be waiting for you! The church is stunning by itself already, yet different azulejos that depict various historical landmarks are just cherry on top! || We definitely agree that our church is stunning and we're glad that you enjoyed your visit. We hope you'll come back one day. || An absolutely stunning church worth visiting. The feeling one gets from being in the church and hearing the Gregorian chants and the likes (see video) is completely different from the hustle and bustle of the city of Lisbon. || Dear Benjamim, we're delighted that you enjoyed the experience. Your opinion is very important to us. We hope you've made good memories of Portugal. || The views from the top of the church are breathtaking! We stumbled on this area by accident while wandering around and it is a must see. Pay the 5€ to go up on the roof. It includes a beverage (we had wine!) and just breathe in the incredible view. The church is free to enter, but the museum and rooftop cost. Absolutely worth it. || We're delighted that you enjoyed the experience. The view from the terrace is truly magnificent. We hope you've kept good memories of Portugal. || You don't need to be religious to enjoy the beautiful church. The entrance is free. For 5 Euro you can access the terrace. Up there the city turns quiet. There are lots of chairs to sit down in the shadows, enjoy the peace, the breeze and the breathtaking panorama. || Dear Matthew, we're glad you enjoyed the experience. We hope you come back onde day. || This charming church, nestled atop a hill in the heart of Lisbon, is a must-visit for those seeking a peaceful and spiritual experience. The Church of Our Lady of Grace offers a beautiful interior with intricate details and a serene atmosphere.  After exploring the church, be sure to head outside to enjoy the breathtaking panoramic views of the city. The location is perfect for taking in the sights and sounds of Lisbon.  If you're looking for a quiet escape from the hustle and bustle of the city, the Church of Our Lady of Grace is a hidden gem that is well worth the visit. || Thank you for your very kind comment. We're delighted that you enjoyed the experience. We look forward to seeing you again. || Graça Church should be high on your list of stops while exploring what Lisbon has to offer. As a spot that many tourists seemingly miss, it'll be unlikely that you have to wait in line for long or struggle to enjoy yourself in a crowd. For €5, you'll be provided a drink and then granted entry to the beautiful church, which you're free to explore at your leisure. Once finished inside, the terrace will grant you access to some of the most captivating views of Lisbon (one of the best in the city, in my opinion!)  It's a peaceful and quiet stop that should make its way onto your itinerary! || We entered the church purely to see the sunset from the roof terrace. A beautiful sunset with views across the city including Castelo de Sao Jorge. The roof area is large but the ‘terrace’ to see the sunset was small and therefore crowded. €5 pp entry fee included a drink. You paid for children too. The staff member serving was extremely miserable and very rude! As part of the entry you can look around other parts of the church including an art exhibition space. Save yourself the fiver and grab a beer on the Miradour de Graça. || We're sorry the experience didn't meet your expectations. We work every day to try to create the best memories for our visitors. We hope you come back one day and that you leave our place happier. || Stunning church on the hill top with beautiful courtyard. || Dear John, thank you very much for visiting the Igreja da Graça and for your kind comment. || We can take a meaningful walk in the area of the beautiful complex of buildings, seeing the majestic church in its simplicity, ornate, tiled corridors, the courtyard and the museum. Connected to the viewingpoint, it is an important stop for a sightseeing tour of Lisbon. || Dear Miklós, we're glad that you enjoyed your visit. Your feedback is very important to us. || Gorgeous church high up on the hill with the most spectacular views of Lisbon.  Very modest exterior architecture, but an exquisite interior. Small monastery with a 5€ entrance fee.  The climb is steep but well worth it. || I finally saw the church from the inside. I was surprised, it's very, very beautiful. A great bonus is that you can go up to the terrace and enjoy the view of the city, with a drink on offer. As the place isn't very popular yet and is priced at 5 euros (which I think is super cheap compared to other cities), I was able to enjoy it and have a moment to myself.

place_name: Church of Our Lady of the Incarnation
reviews_content: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Encarnação is well worth a visit if you want to see Lisbon beyond the main touristic landmarks. It is in the center and offers a calm space. … || Beautiful church, rebuild after the 1755 earthquake. Classicism/baroque style. Elaborate, colorful decorations painted on the ceiling, arches with statues of saints along both sides of the interior. Accessible for wheelchairs! Open most … || Nice and huge church. Many small altars dedicated to saints and roof paintings. || A calm spiritual place to sit and reflect about life || There are several interesting churches you can visit in the Chiado neighbourhood including the Church of Our Lady of the Incarnation (Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Encarnação) located at Largo de Chiado and Largo Luis de Camões. … || Beautiful peaceful church || Glad.to have 5.30pm.mass sunday here. And its english good for tourist like me || Happened to have found one of the few churches in Lisbon with English mass in the afternoon. Very tranquil atmosphere and connected with friendly faithfuls 🫶🏽 … || It was tagged as the best church in Lisbon. It was a great place of reflection. We arrived there around 12:30 and they were closing. || Yet another outstanding catholic monument, gorgeous oasis above the Praça || Such a peaceful church, just look at the photos of the interior, words alone cannot do it justice. Probably largely unchanged through the generations. The fairly ordinary portico front facade hides a gem within, well worth a visit. Please don't forget to leave a donation. || One of many beautiful churches in the Chiado neighbourhood. || This church has a very profound energy, to the point that I felt a bit uncomfortable. It’s quite beautiful, but I couldn’t stay in there very long. It’s very quiet inside, which is a big contrast to the hustle and bustle of the Chiado outside. Definitely worth going to take a peek. || Super 3D realistic paintings || Big and very busy artwork. Not peaceful and one could wonder how someone prays here || Just Beautiful and Awesome! One of the few reasons of being proud to live in Portugal: our Dedication to The Virgin Mary with our Beautiful Churches. Just sitting inside is Mesmerising! || This is a beautiful church dedicated to Our Lady of the Incarnation, which is the name given to Mary, mother of Jesus, in allusion to the incarnation of her son. It certainly deserves a visit. Inside, over the chancel altarpiece, there's a … || Igreja da Nossa Senhora da Encarnação, like so many other churches in this part of the Portuguese capital, was completely destroyed by the earthquake of 1755. It was subsequently rebuilt under the direction of the architect Manuel Caetano … || Beautiful church. Wish there were labels for each statues || Astonishing baroque interiors. Great ceiling painting by by Simon Caetano Nunes. Don’t forget to visit a little hall to the right side door. Great art works!

A stunning church, from the outside it looks quite simple, but inside it’s full of gold, marble, and detailed artwork. Each chapel has unique decorations worth seeing. It’s calm and not too crowded, perfect for a quiet visit. Definitely worth stopping by. || Our private tour guide brought us here after learning that I enjoy visiting churches when we travel. He compared it to the Sistine Chapel, which seemed like a stretch—especially given how unassuming the exterior is. Honestly, it’s probably not a church I would have bothered climbing the steps to visit on my own.  Inside, however, it was a different story entirely. The painted ceiling and the opulence of the altar and artwork throughout were the most impressive of any church I visited in Portugal. The craftsmanship is extraordinary.  What made it truly special, though, was the feeling inside. There was a deep sense of goodness and calming peace that I rarely experience in many of the churches I visit. Feeling that kind of holiness is uncommon for me, which made this visit especially meaningful.  Saint Roque, the church’s namesake, is the patron saint against the plague. He devoted his life to caring for plague victims before ultimately contracting the disease himself—adding another layer of depth and reverence to this remarkable place. || One of my favorite churches while living in Lisbon. The Church of Saint Roch is incredibly well-preserved, and the gold detailing from top to bottom, especially across each of the 14 Stations of the Cross, is just breathtaking. It’s truly an amazing experience.  I 100% recommend visiting the museum too. It’s around €8, and they offer a student discount, no proof needed if you look young enough (like me!). Walking through it, you can really imagine how people back then must have felt in awe. The gold, the grandeur, it all ties in with Portugal’s historic campaigns abroad. It just makes sense.  Pro tip: Be respectful and keep quiet while inside. It’s a sacred and peaceful space. || From the outside, the Church of Saint Roch looks quite plain, but once I stepped inside I was amazed. The chapels are beautifully decorated, and the Chapel of St. John the Baptist really stood out for me with its richness and detail. It felt peaceful to walk around and just take it all in. || The Church of Saint Roch (Igreja de São Roque) is one of the most beautiful and decorative churches ever seen. Its humble exterior hides a richly adorned Baroque interior, featuring magnificent chapels with gilded woodcarving, polychrome marbles, and extraordinary mosaics.  The lavish Chapel of St. John the Baptist, made from precious materials, is a masterpiece of European art. This church reflects immense faith, vision, and artistic labor, making it a true gem of Lisbon’s heritage and one of the most impressive religious buildings in Portugal. || The Igreja de São Roque is special because of its stark exterior that contrasts with an incredibly ornate and lavishly decorated interior, housing what is considered one of Europe's most expensive chapels, the Chapel of St. John the Baptist. This chapel was built in Rome with precious materials like gold, marbles, and mosaics, then shipped and reassembled in Lisbon, showcasing impressive Italian Baroque art. || Very nice church, not as know as others in the city but totally worth it. It is free access (something hard to find in Lisbon) and small but the walls the ceiling and the paintings/sculptures are amazing. I totally recommend visiting this church if you are around. || The interior is splendid. The ceiling is nicely painted. Paintings are fabulous. The chapels are beautifully decorated. || beautiful church. Well worth your time if you are already in the area. || A lovely church that has been well maintained and kept, the scenery is great. It was very quite when we went so we were able to enjoy it all for as long as we wanted. The church is very good in person as photos cant do it justice, a must visit if you are interested in architecture and religious buildings.

place_name: Parque Infantil da Praça António Sardinha
reviews_content: One of the only garden with kids installments in the neighbourhood. Sits inside an adjacent square so no cars passing by speeding. Local kids used to play football in the little ring, but someone thought it was a good idea to put a statue of some unknown guy there, so now the kids have no where to play ball in the area... All around, it's a peaceful Green space in the neighbourhood. || A relatively large playground || Nice playground. Decent amount of shade on sunny days. || Cool spot to sit and chill out- very close to some nice viewpoints overlooking Lisboa. || Unhappy to see facilities for kids are still closed while schools are already open || Great place to play with your kids and toddlers || Beautiful park for babies and children, however, the cleanliness and maintenance leave something to be desired... || It's a place for neighborhood interaction and socializing. At five o'clock, the area begins to invade with children, parents, grandparents, and dog walkers. All languages ​​are spoken, and everyone talks to everyone else. It's a place where it feels good to be. || It's a great place for children to hang out, and now it's open. Whenever I can, I take my son there. I've been going since he was little, and it's one of his favorite places. It's close to home and very calm. My son always finds or makes a friend there. However, something is missing, which should already be there. I suggest that, just like in other squares with a certain number of people frequenting them, a public restroom should be installed, even if it were a symbolic fee, like 0.10 or 0.20 cents.  As I said, the place is great, but I feel it's missing.
